He emphasized the potential of agricultural trade with China, calling for joint ventures in sectors like textiles and leather. DPM Ishaq Dar, accompanied by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, arrived in Beijing to participate in the 2nd Pakistan-China Political Parties Forum and the 4th CPEC Political Parties Joint Consultation Mechanism.  Dar highlighted the economic revival agenda of the Pakistani government and expressed confidence in the success of joint ventures between Pakistani and Chinese companies.

articles.title: Iran war day 86: Trump announces potential deal amid ‘cloud of mistrust’ | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced progress on an agreement with Iran, potentially reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a vital oil chokepoint.  The US president described the memorandum of understanding as a "Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE" and said it would be finalized soon. While Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif of Pakistan, who is mediating the talks, stated that negotiations will happen "very soon," Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expressed skepticism about the agreement, calling some of Trump's claims inconsistent with reality.  The potential deal has been met with mixed reactions from both sides and remains subject to further discussion.

articles.title: Irish gangland figure fails in Dublin byelection bid for seat in parliament | Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gerry “the monk” Hutch, an Irish gangland figure, failed to secure a parliamentary seat in a Dublin byelection. Daniel Ennis of the Social Democrats won the contest with 12,050 first-preference votes, defeating other candidates including Janice Boylan from Sinn Féin and Janet Horner from the Green party.  The election was held to fill the vacancy left by Paschal Donohoe, who resigned as a finance minister for a World Bank position. The victory of Ennis and the Social Democrats marks a shift towards progressive politics, while Hutch's defeat is seen as a relief for establishment candidates.

articles.title: Cooling appliances’ demand surges ahead of Eidul Azha - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Despite rising living costs, appliance sales have increased in the lead-up to Eidul Azha. Sohail Malik, finance secretary of the Karachi Electronic Dealers Association (KEDA), reported a 25-30% increase in refrigerator and deep freezer sales compared to last year.  Pak Elektron (PAEL), a leading appliance manufacturer, attributes this growth to consumers' need for cooling appliances to store Qurbani meat. The company projects strong recovery in appliance sales due to economic stability, easing import restrictions, lower interest rates, and increased consumer financing.

articles.title: Squeals of horror over price caps – but how are we going to fix our broken food system? | Food & drink industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Treasury is asking UK supermarkets to cap price rises on essential foods in response to rising food prices, a move met with criticism from industry figures. The surge in food prices is attributed to global factors like the Iran war and a record-breaking El Niño event, highlighting vulnerabilities in the global food system.  These disruptions, coupled with climate change impacts like drought and extreme weather events, are causing significant challenges for British farmers and increasing the cost of living crisis.  The UK's reliance on imports for key resources like fertilizer and fossil gas further exacerbates these issues. The government acknowledges the need for a more resilient food system but faces resistance from market-driven approaches.

articles.title: Bomb attack in Pakistan’s Balochistan province kills more than 20 people | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A bomb attack in Quetta, the capital of Pakistan's Balochistan province, killed at least 20 people and injured over 50 others. The Balochistan Liberation Army claimed responsibility for the explosion which occurred when a train passed through the city.  The blast caused several carriages to overturn and catch fire, damaging nearby houses and buildings.  Hospitals in Quetta declared a state of emergency as medical staff were ordered to remain on duty.

articles.title: Cricket fandom is already digital. Fan tokens could be the next mov - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Premier League (IPL) is exploring the use of fan tokens to enhance fan engagement.  Chiliz, a blockchain-based sports platform, has partnered with several European football clubs to launch digital fan tokens that offer exclusive experiences like voting on decisions and access to merchandise. The IPL's large and digitally entrenched fanbase makes it an ideal market for this technology. Fan tokens could provide fans with perks such as early access to tickets, signed merchandise, behind-the-scenes content, loyalty rewards, and meet-and-greets.  However, the success of fan token implementation hinges on ensuring that they remain accessible and fun for fans rather than overly financialized.

articles.title: 'Obsession with our country's most cherished structure': Trump reacts to White House shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump reacted to a shooting near the White House, praising Secret Service and law enforcement for their swift action that resulted in the suspect's death. The suspect, identified as Nasire Best, was shot by Secret Service personnel after allegedly firing multiple rounds at officers stationed near a security checkpoint.  The incident occurred while Trump was inside the White House during diplomatic discussions related to Iran and a proposed peace framework involving Middle Eastern nations.

articles.title: 2008 railway exam assault: Raj Thackeray's role in instigating attack not proved, says court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Thane court acquitted Raj Thackeray and five others in a 14-year-old case of alleged assault on Railway Recruitment Board examinees at Kalyan station. The court found the prosecution failed to prove Thackeray's presence or that he incited the attack, as key witnesses could not identify him, and the evidence was deemed inadmissible due to its lack of preservation and production.  The court also noted that injuries sustained by witnesses could have resulted from a stampede.

articles.title: TikToker held in Faisalabad for using obscene language for female tourists in Naran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A TikToker from Faisalabad, Yousuf, was arrested for making a video of female tourists at lake Saif-ul-Muluk using obscene language. The Roshanwala Police registered a case against him after identifying the suspect and he later confessed to profiting from creating such videos. In another incident, a 16-year-old girl suffering from cancer was allegedly kidnapped, gang-raped, and filmed by three individuals including a father and son in Faisalabad. The Saddar Police arrested the accused father and son based on the victim's mother's complaint.

articles.title: ‘AI washing’: firms are scrambling to rebrand themselves as tech-focused | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: UK companies are increasingly using the term "AI" to capitalize on public interest in artificial intelligence, even when their businesses do not utilize generative AI. Public relations firms report that some companies are stretching the definition of AI to describe familiar technologies as such, leading to a rise in "AI washing."  This trend has prompted PR professionals to express concerns about the authenticity and relevance of these claims, as journalists often dismiss them due to their lack of substance.

articles.title: Russian attacks on Ukraine’s Kyiv kill at least four people | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a massive missile and drone attack on Kyiv, Ukraine, killing at least four people and injuring over 60. The attack involved hypersonic missiles, including the Oreshnik, as well as drones and conventional missiles.  The Russian defense ministry claimed the strikes were in response to attacks on Russian-occupied territory. Ukrainian officials reported damage to residential buildings, offices, shops, and a metro station in the capital.

articles.title: RInfra Q4 net profit falls to Rs 918 cr; company appoints Vijesh Babu Thota as CEO - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance Infrastructure reported a net profit of Rs 4,387.08 crore in the same quarter last year, but its total income fell to Rs 4,154.34 crore for the January-March period of FY26 from Rs 4,268.05 crore in the previous fiscal. Expenses increased to Rs 5,419.87 crore, driven by higher power costs, which reached Rs 3,285.68 crore. The company's annual income dropped to Rs 20,862.03 crore from Rs 23,999.29 crore in the previous fiscal year. Reliance Infrastructure appointed Vijesh Babu Thota as CEO effective May 23 and Asheesh Chaturvedi as the new CFO.

articles.title: Taiwan Elections Spark Controversy with 'No Indian Workers' Billboards | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lee Hung-Yi, an independent candidate in Taiwan's upcoming local elections, has sparked controversy with billboards featuring a turbaned man with a "no entry" sign. Joseph Wu, former foreign minister and current National Security Council secretary general, condemned the campaign as "despicable conduct." The billboards have unsettled the small but growing Indian community on the island, who say they are part of an online anti-India sentiment fueled by limited people-to-people contact and political campaigns against a potential influx of Indian workers. Despite attempts to reach him for comment, Lee Hung-Yi could not be reached.

articles.title: Maximum temperatures soar across Telangana, seven Districts cross 46℃ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana Development Planning Society (TGDPS) reported that seven districts in Telangana experienced temperatures exceeding 46°C on Saturday, May 23, 2026.  The hottest locations were Dummugudem and Dharmapuri with readings of 46.3°C and 46.2°C respectively. Other districts experiencing high temperatures included Khammam, Dahegaon, Mothey, Palakurthy, Tandur, Mallampally, and several others within the state.

articles.title: More facts surface ahead of high profile One Constitution project case hearing - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court is set to resume hearing the One Constitution project, with new details emerging regarding a 2012 arbitration award between Abdul Hafeez Sheikh of M BNP and Nadeem Zia Pirzada of M/s Paragon. The agreement stipulated that BNP would hold 75% ownership with Sheikh and 25% with Pirzada, subject to a forensic audit.  The court record also includes a petition concerning a dispute between BNP and the Bank of Punjab, signed by Ejazul Ahsan who later became a judge of the Supreme Court. Notably, Ahsan was part of the IHC bench that restored the controversial lease of the One Constitution Avenue project.

articles.title: East Africa wants to curb imports of used clothes. But it's not easy
articles.rephrased_article: The East African Community (EAC) is grappling with the influx of used clothing, known as "mitumba," which poses a challenge to its burgeoning fashion industry.  Uganda has imposed a 30% environmental levy on imports, while Kenya attempted to simplify its tax system but faced backlash. Despite these efforts, the demand for mitumba persists, prompting concerns about job creation and environmental sustainability. Some argue that the trade supports many jobs, while others believe it hinders local manufacturing growth.  The debate highlights a complex issue with no easy solutions as countries grapple with balancing economic needs and environmental responsibility.

articles.title: £600 for cheese? The Brazilian beach scams that cost visitors dear | Scams | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lisa Selby was charged 4,000 reais (£590) by a beach vendor in Rio de Janeiro after the vendor altered the card reader's display.  The incident highlights a growing problem of tourists being targeted for scams involving fraudulent price alterations at beach vendors. Monzo, her bank, initially denied a refund but later reversed the charge after pressure from the Guardian Money. The Financial Conduct Authority confirmed that pending transactions cannot usually be reversed and that chargebacks are voluntary services offered by card issuers.  Holidaymakers are advised to avoid using contactless payments with vendors and instead pay in cash or insist on holding the card reader themselves.

articles.title: Yemen war sees scramble for scant resources between displaced and locals | Humanitarian Crises News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing Yemen war has exacerbated a dire humanitarian crisis in Maryamah camp and surrounding areas.  Yemen's economic collapse, coupled with reduced aid funding, has led to widespread food insecurity for displaced families and local residents alike. Ali Sagher Shareem, a displaced family member from Hodeidah, described the struggle of his family to find basic necessities like food and medicine. The camp's residents face extreme temperatures, power outages, and dwindling resources, forcing them to make difficult choices such as skipping meals or withdrawing their children from school.  Nadia Saif al-Fakhiri, an official monitoring conditions in government-run IDP camps, reported that the situation is dire with many families struggling to afford two meals a day.

articles.title: LIC emerges as highest profit-making financial company in Jan-Mar quarter - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: LIC reported a 23% increase in net profit to Rs 23,420 crore for the fourth quarter of FY26, making it the top-performing Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE).  State Bank of India (SBI) followed with an annual profit of Rs 80,032 crore, significantly surpassing LIC's Rs 57,419 crore. Other CPSEs like Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) and Coal India also reported strong profits. Meanwhile, Vodafone Idea emerged as the highest quarterly profit earner in the January-March quarter with a record bottomline of Rs 51,970 crore.

articles.title: British Sikh community offers condolences to Henry Nowak family, urges no prejudice during ongoing trial | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sikh organizations across the UK have issued a statement condemning the murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak and urging the public not to associate the Sikh faith with the case. The British Sikh Federation expressed condolences to Nowak's family, stating that the incident does not align with Sikh teachings and values. They called for restraint in public discussion surrounding the case and urged people to allow the legal proceedings to proceed fairly.  The trial of Vickrum Digwa, accused of murdering Nowak, is ongoing.

articles.title: Kurnool police trace missing persons using facial-recognition CCTV network, says SP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kurnool district police are utilizing facial recognition technology (FRS) in over 722 Matrix Smart Technology CCTV cameras to locate missing persons, track criminals, and recover stolen vehicles. The cameras, installed across the state under the Andhra Pradesh FiberNet services, are monitored from a control room in Amaravati and linked to all district control rooms and police stations.  The technology has successfully located missing individuals in Madanapalle and Tirupati, according to Superintendent of Police Vikrant Patil.

articles.title: At least 14 killed in Quetta shuttle train blast: Balochistan govt - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A bomb blast ripped through a shuttle train in Quetta, Balochistan, killing at least 14 people and injuring several others. The explosion near Chaman Phatak derailed three coaches, including the locomotive, and caused significant damage to nearby buildings. Shahid Rind, an aide to the chief minister on media and political affairs, stated that the attack targeted innocent civilians and security forces were investigating the incident.  Shehbaz Sharif, the prime minister, condemned the attack and expressed condolences to the victims' families.

articles.title: Pakistan: Blast targeting train kills at least 24 in Balochistan
articles.rephrased_article: An explosion targeting a train in Pakistan's Balochistan region killed at least 20 people and injured 70 others. The Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) claimed responsibility for the attack, which occurred while the train was traveling through Chaman Phatak station.  Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack and declared an emergency in hospitals treating victims. The incident is not the first time the BLA has targeted trains in Balochistan.

articles.title: UK judge’s decision not to jail boys for rape like a ‘rock in my face’, says victim, 16 | Hampshire | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two teenage boys, aged 15 at the time of the offenses, were sentenced to youth rehabilitation orders for raping two girls in separate incidents. The judge's decision not to jail them has been met with criticism from victims and their families who expressed frustration and shock. Jodie Mittell KC, representing the prosecution, detailed how the boys exploited the victims through manipulation and coercion. Donna Jones, Hampshire police and crime commissioner, also criticized the sentence, stating that a custodial sentence was warranted. The attorney general's office has received multiple requests to review the sentences under the "unduly lenient" scheme.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The lenient sentencing for rape normalizes sexual violence against young girls.

articles.title: Us-Iran Ceasefire Agreement: From Hormuz to nuclear talks - what to expect in the 60-day US-Iran ceasefire proposal - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and Iran are close to signing a proposed agreement that would extend the current ceasefire for 60 days, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and allow Iran to resume oil exports. The draft memorandum of understanding (MOU) would also include talks on curbing Iran’s nuclear program.  Key points of the deal include an end to US sanctions against Iranian ports and a commitment by Iran to never pursue nuclear weapons and negotiate over suspending uranium enrichment. Israel has reportedly raised concerns about certain provisions, while global oil markets remain volatile amid uncertainty surrounding the negotiations.

articles.title: 12 MPs, four Parliamentary panels selected for Sansad Ratna Awards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Prime Point Foundation has selected 12 MPs and four Parliamentary Committees for this year's Sansad Ratna Awards.  Jagdambika Pal, P.P. Chaudhary, Nishikant Dubey, and Shrikant Eknath Shinde are among the individuals recognized, while the Committee on Agriculture, Finance Committee, Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Committee, and Coal and Mines Committee have also been awarded for their performance.

articles.title: Karachi Museum of History to be built by the seaside - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A groundbreaking ceremony was held at Clifton's Beach View Park for the Karachi Museum of History, a landmark cultural and educational space. Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah, Karachi Mayor Barrister Murtaza Wahab, and representatives from the Citizens Archive of Pakistan (CAP) were among those present. The museum aims to preserve and celebrate Sindh's history and the Pakistan independence movement through storytelling, technology, archival material, and interactive experiences.  Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy, CAP Patron-in-Chief, spearheaded the project, envisioning a space that honors Karachi's diverse heritage and resilience.

articles.title: ‘Want equal respect’: Pakistan’s females galloping to glory in tent pegging | Women News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's women are increasingly participating in tent pegging, a traditionally male-dominated sport.  Anum Shakoor, Eshal Ibrahim, and Noor un Nisa Malik, members of the Bint-e-Zahra Club, have been making waves at melas, challenging traditional gender roles and gaining recognition for their skill. Despite facing social pressure and financial barriers, these women are pushing boundaries and demanding respect in a sport that has historically excluded them.  Ayesha Khan is another prominent female rider who has broken down barriers by competing against male riders and leading Pakistan's all-women tent pegging team. Social media has also played a role in raising awareness of women's participation, but some traditionalists remain resistant to their presence.

articles.title: In Japan, divorce splits parents from children. Could a law change end sole custody?
articles.rephrased_article: In Japan, a landmark revision to the Civil Code took effect on April 1, 2026, allowing divorced couples to share custody of their children. This change marks a significant shift from the previous sole custody system that often resulted in one parent losing all contact with their child.  The new law aims to better support families and ensure children maintain relationships with both parents while recognizing the potential risks associated with joint custody arrangements, particularly for victims of domestic violence or abuse. While some families welcome the change, others express concerns about its potential impact on vulnerable individuals and the need for robust legal protections. The law's implementation will be closely watched as it attempts to balance the rights of all parties involved in a family separation.

articles.title: Treasury rejected ministers’ plan to cut VAT on public EV charging to 5% | Electric, hybrid and low-emission cars | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Government officials considered reducing the VAT charged on electricity used at public EV chargers from 20% to 5%, but the Treasury, under chancellor Rachel Reeves, rejected the proposal due to disagreements within departments. The Department for Transport supports lowering the VAT, arguing it would benefit consumers and address perceived unfairness between those with home charging options and those without.  However, the Treasury is concerned about potential lost revenue from reduced VAT, despite a London tax tribunal ruling that the rate should have been 5% all along. The government is reviewing public charging costs and plans to introduce a 3p-a-mile charge for electric cars in 2028.

articles.title: Equity MFs gain over 5% last week with international funds leading. Check top 7 with over 3% return - Weekly performers | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Equity mutual funds saw strong returns last week, with Invesco India Infrastructure Fund leading the pack at 5.70% and Nippon India Taiwan Equity Fund second at 4.36%. Other top performers included Samco Active Momentum Fund, Motilal Oswal Digital India Fund, and two international funds from Mirae Asset.  The returns ranged from 3.25% to 3.08%.

articles.title: France bans Israel minister Ben-Gvir over mocking detained Gaza flotilla activists - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: France banned Israeli national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from entering the country after he released videos appearing to mock and intimidate pro-Palestinian activists detained from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. French Foreign Minister Catherine Barrot condemned Ben-Gvir's actions, stating that they were unacceptable and threatened French nationals who were passengers on the Global Sumud Flotilla.  Barrot called for European Union sanctions against Ben-Gvir and urged the EU to impose bloc-wide sanctions.

articles.title: Bengaluru school headmaster arrested under Pocso Act, after minor student found pregnant - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandraiah, a 59-year-old headmaster of a government higher primary school in Bengaluru, has been arrested under the POCSO Act for allegedly impregnating a minor student. The case came to light after the girl's pregnancy was discovered and police registered an FIR on May 22, 2026.  The girl has been provided medical care and counselling support, while members of the Child Welfare Committee have temporarily relocated her to a government rehabilitation facility. A separate incident involved a minor student escaping an attempted sexual assault by a physical education teacher at a government school in Byatarayanapura. The accused teacher was suspended following a complaint filed by the family and authorities provided support to the student.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power by a school headmaster against a minor is a serious crime.

articles.title: Gunman killed by US Secret Service after opening fire near White House - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A gunman opened fire near the White House on Saturday evening, striking a bystander and killing the assailant after a confrontation with US Secret Service agents. The incident occurred as President Donald Trump was inside the White House, working to finalize a potential peace deal with Iran.  The suspect, identified as Nasire Best, 21, of Maryland, had a history of mental health concerns and multiple prior interactions with Secret Service members. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the shooting.

articles.title: Usyk avoids shock defeat with 11th-round stoppage of Verhoeven | Boxing News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Oleksandr Usyk defeated Rico Verhoeven in a WBC title fight, avoiding a major upset. Despite being the heavier and more experienced fighter, Verhoeven put up a valiant effort, pushing the champion to the 11th round before a decisive right uppercut from Usyk led to the stoppage.  The victory secured Usyk's undefeated record and all three of his world titles. The fight was held at the pyramids of Egypt with Anthony Joshua and Jason Statham in attendance.

articles.title: Man killed in shark attack off Australia's north-east coast
articles.rephrased_article: A 39-year-old man died after being attacked by a shark while swimming off the coast of Queensland, Australia. Queensland Police confirmed the incident occurred near a shoal and that the victim was retrieved from the water but succumbed to his injuries. This is the second fatal shark attack in Australian coastal waters within a week.

articles.title: Shark attack: man dies on Great Barrier Reef in far north Queensland | Queensland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 39-year-old man died after being attacked by a shark while fishing at Kennedy Shoal, south of Cairns, Queensland. Emergency services were called to the Hull River Heads boat ramp just before noon on Sunday and transported the victim ashore where he succumbed to his injuries.  The incident marks another fatal shark attack in Australia's waters, following similar incidents on Rottnest Island and other locations.

articles.title: Dividends, bonus issues: TCS, LIC, Bajaj Auto among 30 stocks turning ex-date this week. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several Indian companies have announced record dates for upcoming corporate actions, including dividends, bonus issues, and stock splits. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) will pay a final dividend of Rs 31 per share on June 12, while Tata Consumer Products will trade ex-dividend on Monday for its Rs 10 dividend.  LTI Mindtree, Siyaram Silk Mills, and Hatsun Agro Product have also set record dates. ITC has fixed May 27 as the record date for its final dividend, while Bajaj Auto will pay a final dividend of Rs 150 per equity share on Friday, May 29.  LIC will issue bonus shares in a 1:1 proportion on May 29, and GSK Pharma has set Friday as the record date for its final dividend.

articles.title: Pakistan train blast: 24 killed, over 50 injured in Quetta explosion near railway track - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: At least 24 people were killed and over 50 injured in a powerful explosion that targeted a train carrying military personnel near Chaman Phatak railway station in Pakistan's Balochistan province. The blast caused partial damage to the train and damaged nearby vehicles, shattering windows and glass panels of buildings. Army servicemen were among those killed, according to authorities.  The incident occurred as the train was traveling from Quetta to Peshawar for Eid holidays.  Following the explosion, emergency services declared a state of emergency in government hospitals across Quetta and security personnel cordoned off the area.

articles.title: Officials check school buses for road worthiness in Kallakurichi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Collector M.S. Prasanth supervised an inspection of 320 school buses in Kallakurichi on Saturday, May 23, 2026.  Officials from the district administration, transport and school education departments found that as many as 20 buses were not roadworthy and instructed school authorities to address the issues. The officials checked for fire extinguishers, first-aid boxes, emergency exits, speed governors, and attendants to assist students. School managements have been given a week to rectify the shortcomings.

articles.title: Several feared killed in Quetta shuttle train blast - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A blast ripped through a shuttle train near Quetta, Pakistan, on Sunday morning, causing significant damage and feared casualties. Pakistan Railways confirmed the explosion derailed three coaches and caused two to overturn.  Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti condemned the attack as a terrorist act by "Fitna al Hindustan" while Railways Minister Hanif Abbasi called it a cowardly act of terrorism sponsored by anti-Pakistan elements operating from India and Afghanistan. Security forces are conducting investigations, including the police, CTD, and bomb disposal squad.

articles.title: Man dies in northeast Australia after shark attack | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A man has died after being bitten by a shark near Kennedy Shoal, Queensland, Australia. The incident occurred on Sunday and the victim was rushed to shore but later passed away. Queensland Police Service are investigating the incident and beaches in the area have been closed. This is the second fatal shark attack in Australia within a week.

articles.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Four dead and dozens injured in wave of strikes on Kyiv
articles.rephrased_article: A wave of Russian missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and surrounding areas resulted in the deaths of four people and over 50 injuries. Vitali Klitschko, Kyiv's mayor, reported damage to residential buildings, schools, and other structures across all districts. The attacks followed Vladimir Putin's vow of retaliation after a deadly attack on a dormitory in Starobilsk, Ukraine, which was claimed by the Ukrainian Armed Forces.  Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukraine's president, warned of potential Russian strikes, citing intelligence suggesting Russia might use the Oreshnik missile.

articles.title: Hunger increasingly used as weapon of war as ‘food-related violence’ surges, analysis shows | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Insecurity Insight and Action Against Hunger analyzed data from 2018 to present, revealing over 21,403 incidents of food-related violence in 15 countries.  The analysis found a marked increase in attacks on markets, farmland, and food distribution systems, with the occupied Palestinian Territory, Yemen, and Sudan experiencing the highest numbers of attacks. The research highlights the weaponization of hunger, where civilians are often targeted while seeking food, resulting in over 10,300 deaths or injuries. Christina Wille, director at Insecurity Insight, urged the international community to implement UN resolution 2417 and prevent these violations.

articles.title: Records of charges against US Capitol rioters removed - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The US Justice Department has removed hundreds of press releases detailing criminal charges related to the January 6th, 2021 attack on the US Capitol from its website. The department claims this action is part of a move to remove "partisan propaganda" and that it's proud to reverse what it calls the "weaponization" of the Justice Department under the Biden administration. This comes after reports that the Trump administration was quietly deleting information about the attack, including press releases detailing the investigation and charges brought against individuals involved.

articles.title: The Enhanced Games: Like the Olympics, but steroids are allowed
articles.rephrased_article: The Enhanced Games, a controversial competition featuring athletes using performance-enhancing drugs to break world records, is being held in Las Vegas.  Aron D'Souza, Maximilian Martin, and their company have attracted backing from prominent investors including Peter Thiel and Donald Trump Jr. Despite warnings from health experts about the risks of anabolic steroids and growth hormones, athletes like Ben Proud are competing with the hope of winning substantial prize money.  The event has been met with criticism from sporting governing bodies who condemn its promotion of doping, while others argue that it is simply a reflection of an existing trend in sports.

articles.title: Taiwan Military Activity: Taiwan detects Chinese military aircraft, naval vessels near island for second straight day - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan's ministry of national defense reported detecting four sorties of Chinese military aircraft and six naval vessels operating around the island until 6 am local time on Sunday. Three of the four aircraft crossed the median line of the Taiwan Strait and entered Taiwan’s southwestern and southeastern Air Defense Identification Zone (ADIZ).  The ROC Armed Forces monitored the situation and responded, following similar activity detected on Saturday involving 16 aircraft sorties and eight naval vessels. The repeated incursions come amid rising tensions between China and Taiwan, with Beijing continuing military operations near the self-ruled island.

articles.title: Kasaragod district administration prepares railway master plan to end travel hardships - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Kasaragod district administration has proposed a comprehensive railway master plan to address travel hardships faced by passengers in the northern Kerala region. The proposals, submitted to Palakkad Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) Madhukar Rawat, include extending eight trains currently terminating at Kannur and Mangaluru Central/Junction to Kasaragod, as well as restoring discontinued passenger services. The administration also seeks stoppages for three major superfast trains that currently bypass Kasaragod station. These proposals aim to benefit passengers travelling for work, education, medical treatment, pilgrimage, and trade.  The district administration has requested the railway authorities to consider these proposals for improved convenience and efficient travel for residents of Kasaragod.

articles.title: Govt toughens airport screening amid Ebola outbreak - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's health ministry has intensified screening measures at airports and directed all provinces to remain on alert following the recent Ebola outbreak in Africa.  The WHO upgraded the risk assessment for the disease, but did not advise any travel restrictions. The Red Cross announced three volunteer deaths in the DRC, while Uganda confirmed three new cases of the virus, bringing the total to five. The African Union's health agency warned that 10 countries are at risk of being affected by the Ebola virus.

articles.title: I survived a missile strike in the Strait of Hormuz, but my friend has not been found
articles.rephrased_article: A missile strike on the oil tanker Skylight in the Strait of Hormuz killed Dalip Rathore, 25, and injured others.  The attack, which occurred on March 1st, was the first commercial vessel to be struck after the US-Israel war with Iran erupted. The ship's owner, Red Sea Ship Management, based in Dubai, is unidentifiable and unresponsive to inquiries. Sunil Puniya, 26, a crew member on the Skylight, lost his friend and remains traumatized by the experience.  The incident highlights the growing dangers faced by seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz due to geopolitical conflicts, with many vessels stranded and facing abandonment by their shipowners. The International Transport Workers' Federation (ITF) reports a surge in abandoned seafarers, highlighting the need for improved maritime regulations and accountability.

articles.title: Dozens feared trapped in Philippines building collapse - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jay Pelayo, the Angeles City information officer, reported that an incident at a construction site resulted in the collapse of a building.  Eight people were rescued and 11 others escaped, including the site foreman. Pelayo stated that approximately 30 to 40 individuals remain missing and search and rescue operations are ongoing. The cause of the collapse is under investigation by the city engineer, who is reviewing the construction history. Rescue efforts are being hindered by the structure's concrete composition.

articles.title: White House shooting: 21-year-old Nasire Best, who identified himself as Jesus Christ, shot dead - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A gunman, identified as Nasire Best, 21, opened fire at a security checkpoint outside the White House on Saturday evening. Secret Service personnel responded with gunfire, killing Best and injuring at least one bystander.  The shooting occurred while President Donald Trump was inside the White House during diplomatic discussions related to Iran and a proposed peace framework involving Middle Eastern nations. The FBI launched an investigation into the incident, which prompted a lockdown of the White House complex for approximately 40 minutes.

articles.title: PM Modi Jhalmuri break: Security stepped up at stall which Modi had visited in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bikram Kumar Sau, a Jhalmuri vendor in Jhargram town, West Bengal, has reported receiving threatening phone calls and messages after Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited his stall during the state assembly election campaign.  The Jhargram police have launched an investigation into the threats, with security personnel posted outside the stall to protect Sau and his family. The incident gained national attention and contributed to the BJP's victory in the district.

articles.title: US-Iran deal in sight as CDF wraps up trip - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Field Marshal Asim Munir, the Chief of Defence Forces, concluded a visit to Tehran after intense negotiations with Iranian officials aimed at ending the conflict.  The discussions focused on de-escalation and achieving a final agreement. While no breakthrough was announced, President Donald Trump claimed significant progress had been made towards a peace deal that would open the Strait of Hormuz. The talks also included proposals from Iran and Pakistan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.  Despite these developments, Iranian officials emphasized their commitment to achieving their goals while maintaining a hardline stance.

articles.title: Rosenberg: Luhansk strike sparks Russian accusations and vow to retaliate
articles.rephrased_article: A five-story building in the Russian-occupied town of Starobilsk, Luhansk region, was destroyed in an attack early Friday. Russia has accused Ukraine of carrying out a drone strike on the college dormitory, claiming 21 lives and 42 injuries.  Vladimir Putin called it a "terrorist strike" while Ukraine's Armed Forces stated they targeted a Russian military unit. The United Nations Security Council convened an emergency session at Russia's request, with some members condemning the attack as a war crime.

articles.title: White House Shooting: Who was Nasire Best? Maryland man who allegedly believed he was ‘Jesus Christ’ killed after gunfire near Donald Trump’s home - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nasire Best, a 21-year-old Maryland man, is the suspect in a shooting near the White House security perimeter. Best had prior encounters with federal security agencies due to mental health struggles and repeated violations of court orders related to his presence near the White House complex.  The incident occurred on July 10, 2025, when Best allegedly bypassed a restricted checkpoint and fired at Secret Service officers. The motive behind the shooting remains under investigation, but reports suggest Best may have believed himself to be "Jesus Christ".

articles.title: Iran refutes Trump's 'largely negotiated' deal, claims to keep Hormuz control - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that the US and Iran have “largely negotiated” a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, potentially ending months of conflict. However, Iran disputes these claims, stating that the Strait will remain under its control according to a draft proposal awaiting approval from supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei.  While Trump expressed optimism about progress and highlighted support from regional leaders, including Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Israel remains cautious about any interim agreement due to concerns over Iran's nuclear program.

articles.title: ITBP officials meet Kanpur top cop seeking action in medical negligence case of jawan’s mother - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) personnel surrounded the Kanpur Police Commissionerate office on Saturday, May 23, 2026, in protest of alleged medical negligence that led to the amputation of a constable's mother. ITBP Commandant and dozens of personnel demanded justice for the incident, accusing doctors at a private hospital of malpractice.  The Kanpur police referred the case to the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) for investigation, which is ongoing.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz hails Trump's 'extraordinary efforts to pursue peace' after phone call with CDF, leaders of other countries - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised President Donald Trump's efforts to pursue peace, stating that a call with multiple countries' leaders, including Field Marshal Asim Munir, the Chief of Defence Forces and Army Chief, was "very useful and productive."  The discussions focused on the current regional situation and how to move forward with ongoing peace efforts. Pakistan hopes to host another round of US-Iran negotiations soon. The latest developments come amidst heightened pressure from the US and its Middle East allies for a peaceful resolution between Washington and Tehran. Secretary of State Marco Rubio commended Field Marshal Asim Munir's visit to Tehran, highlighting the ongoing communication between the US government and Pakistan in facilitating peace talks.

articles.title: Suspect killed after opening fire on Secret Service near White House
articles.rephrased_article: A 21-year-old man, identified as Nasire Best, was fatally shot by Secret Service agents after opening fire near the White House on Saturday evening. The shooting occurred outside the White House at 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue NW, where between 10 and 20 gunshots were fired. One bystander was wounded in the attack but no officers were injured. President Donald Trump was present at the White House at the time of the incident.  The shooting remains under investigation.

articles.title: How has the BCCI resisted RTI scrutiny? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Information Commission (CIC) ruled that the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is not a "public authority" under the Right to Information Act, 2005. This means the BCCI cannot be compelled to provide information requested by a Delhi resident and the appeal was dismissed. The BCCI maintains it is a private entity and does not fall under the definition of a public authority as outlined in the RTI Act.

articles.title: What did the Supreme Court say about bail under UAPA? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court granted six months of interim bail to two accused in the 2020 Delhi riots case, Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad. The court also referred a larger bench to consider whether prolonged incarceration and delays in trials can override stringent bail restrictions under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: fate of strait of Hormuz hangs in balance as Trump claims Iran deal ‘largely negotiated’ | Middle East and north Africa | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced that a peace deal with Iran was "largely negotiated" after calls with various leaders, including Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.  He stated the Strait of Hormuz would be reopened as part of the agreement. However, Fars news agency, close to the Iranian regime, reported that the strait would remain under Iranian control and disputed Trump's claim of a near-final deal. The potential agreement includes an end to the war launched by the US and Israel in February, with negotiations on Iran's nuclear program expected to take place within 30 to 60 days.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship flight hits most targets in pre-IPO test - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX successfully completed a test flight of its next-generation Starship rocket on Friday, deploying mock satellites and splashing down in the Indian Ocean. The uncrewed launch marked the first of its V3 iteration and was a significant milestone for the vehicle designed to enable more frequent Starlink satellite launches and future NASA missions to the moon. This successful test could boost investor confidence ahead of SpaceX's initial public offering next month, which is expected to be the largest in history.

articles.title: West Bengal gained infamy due to recruitment scams, new recruitment policy in next Budget session: CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced a new recruitment policy for the state during the Rojgar Mela in Sealdah. The policy will be introduced in the next Budget session of the assembly, beginning on June 18th.  Adhikari cited previous recruitment scams under the Trinamool Congress regime, including teacher and municipal job scandals, as reasons for the new policy. He also expressed concerns about the lack of transparency in examinations and suggested a carbon copy of the OMR sheet be given to all examinees to prevent nepotism and corruption.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights ongoing recruitment scams and their impact on citizens.

articles.title: US police responding to dozens of shots fired near the White House | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel and President Donald Trump were reportedly inside the White House when shots were fired near the building.  Multiple emergency vehicles cordoned off access to the White House, with police and National Guard troops blocking reporters from entering the area. The Secret Service is working to corroborate reports of gunfire near 17th Street and Pennsylvania Avenue NW. No injuries have been reported at this time.

articles.title: Australia news live: Queensland police shot dead man north of Brisbane; gunshots heard near White House | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Queensland police shot and killed an alleged domestic violence perpetrator who was armed with a firearm at a home north of Brisbane. The incident occurred after midnight on Sunday morning, following reports that the man was making threats. Police Ethical Standards Command, with oversight from the Crime and Corruption Commission, will investigate the shooting. Three people were transported to hospital in stable conditions, while paramedics assessed a patient in a life-threatening condition at the scene.

articles.title: Centre asks Delhi Gymkhana Club to hand over premises by June 5 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Urban Affairs Ministry has ordered the Delhi Gymkhana Club, located adjacent to the Prime Minister's residence, to vacate its premises by June 5th. The club's 27.3-acre plot is needed for "strengthening and securing defense infrastructure" and other vital public security purposes.  The order was issued by the Land & Development Office (L&DO) under the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, citing urgent institutional needs and governance infrastructure projects as reasons. The club has operated from the location since 1913.

articles.title: India is important to the U.S.’s Indo-Pacific policy, says Rubio, invites Modi to Washington - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Secretary of State Marco Rubio began a four-day trip to India, meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other officials.  Rubio emphasized the importance of the Indo-Pacific region and renewed the Quad engagement, highlighting India's role in U.S. policy. The visit included bilateral talks with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, attendance at the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, and a reception hosted by the U.S. Ambassador to India.  The trip also included cultural exchanges and visits to Jaipur and Agra.

articles.title: Heatwave warning in 12 Telangana districts today, warm night conditions in eight districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a heatwave warning for 12 districts in Telangana, with warm night conditions expected in eight more. The IMD predicts very likely heatwave conditions at isolated pockets in several districts, including Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Karimnagar, and Khammam.  Thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds are also forecast for certain areas of the state.

articles.title: Future City will serve as compass for the country: TPCC chief - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahesh Goud, president of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC), criticized T. Harish Rao, a BRS MLA, for his comments on the future development of Hyderabad.  Goud argued that expanding the city's geographical limits was necessary for state development and questioned Harish Rao’s lack of foresight. He also stated that the Congress government is continuing previous schemes and working towards announcing names for working presidents soon.

articles.title: Pinarayi flays crackdown on Cockroach Janta Party - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pinarayi Vijayan, leader of the Opposition, criticized the Union government's withholding of the Cockroach Janta Party’s X handle. He argued that this action reflects intolerance towards democratic protests and suggests fear of the youth movement becoming a political force.  Vijayan stated that the platform has gained significant traction due to its focus on addressing unemployment and inequality, highlighting the deep discontent among young people.

articles.title: Naidu to inaugurate MSME Growth Summit-2026 in Vijayawada on May 25 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will inaugurate the MSME Growth Summit-2026 in Vijayawada on Monday, May 25th. The event, a flagship initiative of the Andhra Pradesh government, aims to accelerate the growth and competitiveness of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across the state.  The summit will feature over 1,500 stakeholders, including entrepreneurs, industry associations, policymakers, financial institutions, and technology partners. It will showcase innovation ecosystems, infrastructure initiatives, digital transformation programs, and success stories of MSMEs from Andhra Pradesh. The summit will also launch key initiatives like the foundation stone laying for Phase III of MSME Parks, the AP Cluster Development Programme, and the SIDBI-RTIH Seed Fund.

articles.title: Congress slams Centre over rising fuel prices, questions PM for not disclosing seriousness of crisis - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders criticized the Prime Minister Narendra Modi government for its handling of rising fuel prices, accusing it of "looting" consumers with high taxes and failing to pass on benefits during periods of low global crude prices.  Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge accused the government of timing fuel price reductions around elections and resuming hikes after polling concluded. Rajeev Gowda, a Congress research department chairman, argued that rising fuel prices and the depreciating rupee reflected broader economic distress and called for greater transparency from the government regarding its energy policies.

articles.title: BMCRI working on setting up a centralised diagnostic hub to ease burden on Victoria Hospital’s Infosys central laboratory - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute (BMCRI) is proposing to centralize its laboratory services, including the Infosys Foundation lab, to address increasing patient load and delays in test results. The plan involves consolidating five other labs under one roof on the top floor of the outpatient department building, streamlining sample collection, and providing digital access to reports.  The project aims to improve efficiency, reduce overcrowding, and enhance quality control while addressing staffing shortages and infrastructure limitations.

articles.title: States to get VB-G RAM G funding based on 16th Finance Commission formula, ‘performance criteria’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre's new rural jobs scheme, Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (VB-G RAM G), will prioritize funding for poorer states using the 16th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution formula. The draft rules also propose allocating a portion of funds based on performance criteria such as timely wage payments and work completion rates.  The scheme, replacing the MGNREGA Act, will have a 60:40 funding split between the Centre and states and includes provisions for grievance redressal mechanisms and administrative frameworks.  Stakeholders have until June 21st to submit their feedback on the draft rules.

articles.title: Telangana proceeds with plan to relocate polluting units outside city, issues HILTP norms - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has released implementation guidelines for the Hyderabad Industrial Lands Transformation Policy (HILTP). The policy aims to relocate polluting industries beyond the Outer Ring Road and convert vacant land into multi-use zones.  Eligible industrial units can submit applications through a dedicated online portal by June 30, 2026, receiving an upfront Development Impact Fee of 10% and consideration of existing market rates. Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) will oversee the policy's implementation.

articles.title: Manipur CM assures NIA probe into abduction of Naga men - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yumnam Khemchand Singh, the Chief Minister of Manipur, promised an investigation by the NIA into the alleged abduction of six Naga men. The Kuki Inpi Manipur extended its shutdown for another 48 hours to pressure the government for the release of 14 Kuki people, including three minors.  The UNC, led by Ng. Lorho, urged the government to intensify efforts to find the missing villagers. The Chief Minister also assured the delegation that the abduction case would be handed over to the NIA and search-and-rescue operations were underway.

articles.title: A.P. continues to grapple with intense heat as 95 mandals record above 42°C - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh continues to experience intense heat, with 95 out of 688 mandals recording temperatures above 42°C.  The highest temperature reached 45.8°C at Kanumolu in Krishna district. While some districts received light to moderate rainfall on Saturday, severe heatwave conditions are expected for 21 mandals and widespread heatwave conditions for 214 mandals on Sunday. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts that weather systems brewing over the Bay of Bengal may bring isolated showers with lightning and thunderstorms in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema next week, but this activity is not expected to be widespread.

articles.title: Nursing student dies during surgery at Tiruchi government hospital; colleagues stage protest - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A third-year nursing student at the K.A.P. Viswanatham Government Medical College in Tiruchi, Seethalakshmi, died after suffering a cardiac arrest during surgery at the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Government Hospital on Saturday (May 23, 2026).  The incident sparked protests by over 300 nursing students who alleged medical negligence. A high-level inquiry committee has been formed to investigate the "adverse medical event." The committee will be led by N. Basker, medical superintendent of the Rajiv Gandhi Government General Hospital. Tamil Nadu BJP president, Nainar Nagendran, demanded a compensation of ₹25 lakh for the student's family and criticized the government's handling of healthcare in the state.

articles.title: Uppal flyover works push traffic into residential lanes in eastern Hyderabad, double commute times for residents - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Traffic diversions for the Uppal–Narapally elevated corridor project are causing significant congestion and delays in residential areas around Uppal X roads. L. Niharika, a commuter, reported heavy traffic even before peak office hours, while Sai Nikhil, an executive at a mobile phone store, noted a drop in walk-in customers due to the extended commute times.  Residents along diversion corridors are experiencing parking issues and increased travel times, impacting their daily lives. G. Nagaraju, Uppal Traffic Inspector, stated that although the diversions have helped prevent major bottlenecks on the main carriageway, they have shifted traffic onto residential roads not designed for sustained vehicular flow.

articles.title: U.P. Congress chief Ajay Rai booked over ‘objectionable’ comment on PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ajay Rai, Uttar Pradesh Congress president, is facing an FIR after a complaint from Neeraj Kumar Rawat, a BJP district working committee member, alleging abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  The complaint claims that Mr. Rai obstructed government work and blocked a public road with his convoy of vehicles and supporters. The police registered the case based on a video circulating online showing Mr. Rai making objectionable statements. Mr. Rai denies the allegations, calling it a tactic to silence him and accusing the BJP government of using state apparatus against opponents.

articles.title: llegal LPG refilling unit busted in Chirayinkeezhu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Acting on a tip-off, officials from the Thiruvananthapuram district supply office raided a godown in Chirayinkeezhu, Kerala. The raid uncovered illegal LPG refilling operations where cylinders were being transferred for resale at inflated prices in the black market.  261 LPG cylinders belonging to various oil companies were seized along with equipment used for the operation. Further investigation is underway and prosecution proceedings will be initiated under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955.

articles.title: Trump says Iran agreement ‘largely negotiated’, awaiting finalisation | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced that a Memorandum of Understanding in ceasefire talks to end the US-Israel war with Iran has been largely negotiated, and will include reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The agreement is subject to finalization by US and Iranian negotiators and various other countries, following a call with Middle East leaders including Benjamin Netanyahu.  The announcement comes after weeks of fluctuating statements from Trump regarding the deal's progress, and a visit by Pakistan’s army chief to Iran that was deemed "highly productive".

articles.title: MHA warns of phishing campaign targeting users of lost or stolen iPhones - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) has warned of a sophisticated phishing campaign targeting Apple iPhone users whose devices have been lost or stolen. Hackers impersonate Apple Support, sending fraudulent SMS messages with phishing links that lead to counterfeit login pages designed to steal Apple ID credentials and One-Time Passwords (OTPs).  The I4C advises users to avoid clicking links from unsolicited messages, carefully check URLs before entering credentials, and utilize the official "Find Devices" service page for tracing lost devices.

articles.title: CPI(M) demands scrapping NTA, seeks Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Communist Party of India (Marxist) demanded the scrapping of the National Testing Agency (NTA) over alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, calling for sweeping changes to the centralized examination system. The party also called for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, alleging repeated failures and loss of credibility by the agency.  The CPI(M) expressed concern over the impact on students' mental health and financial well-being due to the alleged leak, demanding an impartial probe into the matter and strong action against those responsible.

articles.title: Cab driver assaulted on KH Road - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On May 22nd, a gang of armed men assaulted a cab driver on Double Road in Wilson Garden Police Station limits. The incident was captured on CCTV and has since gone viral.  The police are investigating the motive behind the assault and examining footage from nearby areas to identify the attackers. They are also tracing the registration numbers of both the Uber cab and the vehicle used by the assailants.

articles.title: Police constable’s wife found dead; dowry harassment case registered - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lakshmi Priya, a 26-year-old woman, was found dead at her home in Mysuru on Friday. Rajesh Aaradhya, Lakshmi's husband and a police constable, informed her family that she had died.  The police are investigating the incident and suspect it may have been related to an ongoing family dispute. The case is being investigated under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Dowry Prohibition Act.

articles.title: Supreme Court registers suo motu case over death of Twisha Sharma - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has taken suo motu cognisance of the alleged dowry death of Twisha Sharma, a Noida resident, after allegations by her family regarding procedural irregularities and tampering with evidence in the investigation.  A three-judge Bench will hear the case on May 25th. The Sharma family alleges mental harassment and financial demands from her husband, Samarth Singh, and his mother, prompting the family to seek scrutiny of phone records and other material connected to the case.  The Madhya Pradesh High Court ordered a second autopsy by an AIIMS Delhi team following demands by Sharma's parents.

articles.title: Karnataka to soon get India’s second largest international cricket stadium - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Siddaramaiah, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, announced the construction of a new international cricket stadium in Suryanagar, Anekal Taluk. The 80,000-seat stadium will be the second largest in India and is expected to boost sports development, tourism, and economic growth in the area.  The project has faced opposition from some farmers and environmentalists who raised concerns about the impact on wildlife and land value. Siddaramaiah assured that farmers would receive fair compensation and land allocation for their surrendered properties. The CM also launched the 'Namma Mane' housing programme, which will provide affordable housing to residents of Suryanagar.

articles.title: KSRTC driver suspended over defamatory post against Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KSRTC driver S. Sunilkumar has been suspended for posting defamatory content about Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Facebook and circulating his picture in a defamatory manner. The corporation initiated disciplinary action against him, while the police are considering filing an IT Act case.  Further investigation is underway with the assistance of the cyber cell.

articles.title: Cricket betting racket busted, four arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chilakalapudi police arrested four individuals in connection with an online betting operation on IPL cricket matches.  The suspects, P. Dharani Kumar, P. Ravi Kumar, Ch. Ravindra Kumar and I. Satyam, were apprehended during a raid at Edepalli on Friday night. The Krishna district SP, V. Vidyasagar Naidu, confirmed the seizure of ₹36,000 in cash and eight mobile phones from the suspects' possession.

articles.title: `Quality seeds and scientific sowing’ fair on May 26 in Ballari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ballari District Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BDCCI), in collaboration with the district administration and various government departments and farmers' organizations, will host an agriculture fair on "Quality Seeds and Scientific Sowing" at the APMC premises in Ballari on May 26. The event, supported by Minister for Agriculture N. Cheluvarayaswamy, District in-charge Minister B.Z. Zameer Ahmed Khan and Vice-Chancellor of Raichur University of Agricultural Sciences M. Hanumanthappa, will feature a farmers' rally, lectures from agricultural scientists, and the participation of nearly 10,000 farmers.

articles.title: Centre committed to ensuring transparent, corruption-free recruitmentm says Union Minister Joshi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pralhad Joshi, Union Minister for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution,  emphasized the Centre's commitment to transparent recruitment processes during a Rozgar Mela in Hubballi. He urged newly appointed candidates to serve with integrity and dedication, highlighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "Rozgar Parva" initiative which aims to create employment opportunities across India. Over 51,000 candidates received appointment letters from various departments including Railways, banking, and postal services.

articles.title: Hubballi Dharwad Central MLA tells officials to facilitate export of mangoes grown in region - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: MLA Mahesh Tenginakai inaugurated the Dharwad district-level ‘Mango Mela-2026’ to support local mango farmers. The event, organized by Karnataka Agriculture Marketing Board, KCCI, and other organizations, aimed to facilitate mango exports and increase awareness about value addition.  I.G. Sanadi emphasized the importance of planting more saplings for a sustainable future. G.K. Adappagoudar highlighted the need to eliminate middlemen in the mango market.

articles.title: Speakers at leadership summit emphasise on sustained deliberation on role of AI in critical sectors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Shettar, Pro Chancellor of KLE Technological University, emphasized the need for sustained discussions on AI's role in various sectors during the BVB KLE Tech Leadership Summit – 2026.  He also highlighted the importance of bridging the talent gap in the semiconductor sector.  Brahmanand Patil, president of Vector Informatik India Pvt. Ltd., spoke about how AI is driving innovation in the automotive industry.  Ram Kerur, CEO of Sunlux Technovations and chairman of the BVB KLE Tech Alumni Association, stressed the value of alumni engagement and collaboration between academia and industry. The summit focused on technology-driven transformation with panels discussing AI, FinTech, and the semiconductor sector.

articles.title: Driver held for illegal sand mining from Palar River in Tirupattur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: S. Mariappan, a 42-year-old driver from Tirupattur, was arrested by Natrampalli police near Jolarpet town for illegal sand mining from the dry river bed of Palar on Saturday.  The police seized a tipper lorry carrying loads of river sand and registered a case after finding it during a patrol on Chennai - Bengaluru Highway (NH 48). The driver fled the scene before being apprehended using CCTV footage analysis. A probe is ongoing.

articles.title: I don’t think the ruling party has the stomach for sarcasm, says Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led satirical political group, had its website taken down on Saturday, May 23, 2026 at 9 a.m.  Founder Abhijeet Dipke accused the Indian Government of orchestrating the takedown, claiming it was due to the CJP's growing popularity and online movement demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan following the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. The CJP, formed in response to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s controversial “cockroach” remark, rapidly gained traction with over 22 million followers on social media before being blocked by authorities citing national security concerns. Dipke claims his personal accounts were also hacked and he has received death threats.  Despite the takedown, the CJP is not yet a registered political party.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Government censorship of a satirical group raises concerns about free speech.

articles.title: Petrol, diesel prices hiked again in Bengaluru; transport sector warns of ripple effect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Oil marketing companies raised petrol and diesel prices in Bengaluru for the third time this month, increasing prices by an average of 90 paise per litre. This latest increase has added to concerns about rising inflation and its impact on commuters, transport operators, businesses, and consumers.  The president of the Karnataka State Travel Owners’ Association, K. Radhakrishna Holla, called for immediate government intervention to reduce fuel taxes and provide relief measures for the transportation sector. Ride-hailing cab drivers in Bengaluru also expressed concern over the impact on their earnings, while consumers reported that the price hikes were affecting grocery expenses.

articles.title: Is pragmatism replacing ideology in international affairs? | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and India are seeking to mend diplomatic ties after a year of tension, highlighting the increasing complexity and interconnectivity in international relations.  Professor emeritus of strategic studies at the Centre for Policy Research, Brahma Chellaney, argues that pragmatism is replacing ideology in today's diplomatic landscape, while Chief executive officer at Macro-Advisory strategic consultancy, Chris Weafer, suggests that overlapping interests are driving this shift.

articles.title: Power cuts caused by load issues, not shortage, says Minister R. Nirmalkumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for Energy Resources and Law R. Nirmalkumar stated that recent power cuts in Chennai and other districts were due to increased demand during the summer, not a shortage of supply. Mr. Nirmalkumar explained that the Electricity Department is addressing issues with load management, rapid response teams, and call centers to resolve complaints promptly. The department faces financial distress and is implementing reforms to improve efficiency and address outstanding debt.

articles.title: Trump says peace deal with Iran ‘largely negotiated’ with strait of Hormuz to open | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced on Saturday that a peace deal with Iran has been largely negotiated, potentially ending the US-Israel war launched in February. The announcement came after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain, and Turkey participated in indirect talks with Iran.  The deal is expected to include an official declaration of the war's end, two-month negotiations on Iran's nuclear program, the opening of the strait of Hormuz by Iran, and an end to the US blockade of Iranian ports. The details of the agreement remain unclear.

articles.title: ‘Fjord’ by Romania’s Cristian Mungiu wins Cannes top film prize | Cinema News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cristian Mungiu, Romanian director, won the prestigious Palme d’Or for his film "Fjord" at the Cannes Film Festival.  The drama explores a clash of values between a religious family relocating from Romania to Norway and the Norwegian child welfare system. Mungiu becomes just the 10th filmmaker to win the award twice. The Grand Prix went to Andrey Zvyagintsev's Russian war drama "Minotaur," while Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto won best actress and actor awards for their roles in the film "All of a Sudden."

articles.title: ₹350 crore investment to generate 2,300 employment opportunities in Bihar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) approved 20 industrial projects during a meeting chaired by Secretary, Industries Department and MD of BIADA, Kundan Kumar. The projects are expected to attract investments worth ₹350 crore and create employment opportunities for 2,300 people.  Industries Minister Shreyasi Singh highlighted the government's commitment to developing an investor-friendly environment and establishing Bihar as a modern industrial hub.

articles.title: JD Vance makes unplanned return to Washington, claims report triggering speculations over Iran - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump called an emergency meeting of his national security team on Saturday regarding Iran, as Vice President JD Vance, and other top negotiators including Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalifbaf and Jared Kushner have approved a draft peace deal.  Trump skipped his son's wedding in the Bahamas to attend the meeting, prompting speculation about the significance of the event.

articles.title: No refunds for 15,000 Australian ticket holders after Candace Owens’ tour cancelled | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens, a conservative commentator, is out hundreds of thousands of dollars after her Australian tour was cancelled by the company Rocksman, which has declared bankruptcy. The promoter spent all its money and will not refund ticket holders or creditors, according to a liquidator's report.  The company, linked to influential conservative group Turning Point Australia, was unable to cover the costs of the tour due to insufficient funds and insurance. George Zacharia, Rocksman's sole director, has declined to comment on the financial situation.

articles.title: Chennai and surrounding areas to experience cloudy weather - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai experienced cloudy skies on Saturday due to a low-level circulation over the central Bay of Bengal and a north–south trough. V.R. Durai, Director, Regional Weather Forecasting Centre, explained that this interaction caused enhanced moisture incursion and strong onshore winds, leading to widespread low and mid-level clouds. Residents reported a sandstorm at Marina Beach, while Sunday is expected to be cloudy with heavy rain possible in isolated areas of Tamil Nadu and surrounding regions.

articles.title: Twisha Sharma death case: husband Samarth Singh brought to Bhopal, police to seek remand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Samarth Singh, the husband of Twisha Sharma, who was found dead in her marital home on May 12th, 2026, was arrested by Madhya Pradesh police after he surrendered at a Jabalpur district court.  He is being held for questioning regarding his alleged involvement in dowry death and harassment. The case has prompted the State government to recommend a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into Sharma's death.  The investigation is ongoing, with Giribala Singh, former judge and chairperson of the Bhopal Consumer Court, stating she is willing to provide a statement but has not yet been contacted by police.

articles.title: TVK government will fall one day, says M.K. Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, leader of the DMK, criticized the TVK government, led by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, for its dependence on other parties for support and alleged attempts to split the AIADMK.  He compared the public's interest in the new party to a child's fascination with a toy, predicting that it would fade quickly. Stalin also highlighted his government's achievements over the past five years as evidence of improved governance.

articles.title: 68% of flyover on Anna Salai completed despite delays due to war, labour shortage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State Highways Department officials report that nearly 68% of the construction project for a flyover on Anna Salai, connecting Saidapet and Teynampet, has been completed.  The project is expected to be finished by September with 32 out of 131 decks in place. The completion of the flyover will involve placing slabs on girders, completing foundation work for pillars, and installing approach ramps and crash barriers.

articles.title: DMK, Congress trade barbs over the latter’s post-poll alliance with the TVK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin accused the Congress of being responsible for the BJP's victories, claiming they had "shed blood and tears" to ensure Congress wins.  DMK president M.K. Stalin was also present at the meeting where a resolution condemned the Congress for its betrayal and labeled it a "parasite".  The Congress Legislature Party leader S. Rajesh Kumar countered these accusations, stating that the people of Tamil Nadu elected the AIADMK to power based on the promise of sharing power with alliance partners.

articles.title: Coalition government here to stay in Tamil Nadu like Kerala, says Kader Mohideen - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.M. Kader Mohideen, president of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), stated that Tamil Nadu has formed a coalition government similar to Kerala and that it will continue in the future. He attributed this success to the DMK's ability to secure votes from the Muslim community, which he believes was crucial for their victory.  C. Joseph Vijay, the new leader of Tamil Nadu politics, is credited with initiating this change.

articles.title: Half marathon in Bengaluru on May 24 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalki Sports India is organizing the Freedom Bengaluru Half Marathon (FBHM) 2026, a running event expected to draw over 6,000 participants. The race will feature professionally timed categories for 21.1K, 10K, and 5K runs, taking place at NICE Tollgate in Hosakerehalli on Sunday at 5:45 a.m. IST.

articles.title: Public outcry grows louder over power cuts in U.P.; Oppn. parties call it structural failure - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Uttar Pradesh are protesting frequent power cuts, exacerbated by the heat wave.
