The exchange has sparked widespread debate within Twitch, Kick, and X communities.

articles.title: Calcutta HC orders setting up SIT of CBI to probe hushing up charges in R G Kar rape-murder case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court ordered the creation of a three-member special investigation team (SIT) from the CBI to investigate the death of a trainee doctor at the RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. The court's decision follows allegations that evidence was destroyed and attempts were made to downplay the incident. The SIT will focus on the events leading up to the victim's cremation, including potential lapses in the initial investigation by both police and hospital authorities.  The team is expected to file a comprehensive report by June 25th.

articles.title: US Senate pushes back against Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponisation’ fund | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Senate Republicans delayed a vote on immigration enforcement funding, citing concerns about President Donald Trump’s “anti-weaponisation” fund and his request for $1 billion in funds to build a White House ballroom.  The delay comes after Trump sued the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) for leaking his tax refunds, prompting criticism of potential conflicts of interest.  Senator Don Bacon stated that Trump has lost support within the Senate due to these actions, and Senator Thom Tillis called the “anti-weaponisation” fund "stupid on stilts." The Senate will return from its recess in June.

articles.title: Last Australian women and children linked to IS leave Syrian camp before expected return home – report | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australian women and children, the last remaining from the al-Roj detention camp in north-east Syria, have reportedly left for Damascus. The group is expected to return to Australia in the coming days, but the Australian government has not confirmed any flight bookings or official plans.  The group's departure comes after a previous group of Australians was repatriated last month, with some facing charges upon arrival. Tanya Plibersek, federal minister, stated that those returning will face consequences for their actions. The US government is urging Australia to take back its citizens and has offered assistance with repatriation efforts.

articles.title: Historic shift: Vijay’s Cabinet marks Tamil Nadu’s best SC representation till date - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has appointed seven members from the Scheduled Caste (SC) community to his Cabinet. This marks a significant increase in SC representation compared to previous Cabinets.  Political analyst Stalin Rajangam believes this is a positive step towards inclusivity and sets a benchmark for future governments. However, Punitha Pandiyan, former Vice President of the Tamil Nadu SC/ST Commission, argues that celebrating this development trivializes SC politics.

articles.title: Assistant Director of Mines in Ranipet relieved of duties - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Mohan, Director of Geology and Mining, relieved E. Srinivasarao, Assistant Director of the Ranipet office, of his duties due to allegations that he demanded ₹2 lakh in cash from a stone quarry operator to relax mining norms. The incident was reported to the Ministry of Natural Resources, Minerals and Mines, headed by Minister T.K. Prabhu.  A. Arumuganainar, Regional Joint Director of Geology and Mining (Villupuram), will now hold full additional charge of the post of AD of Geology and Mining for Ranipet district.

articles.title: KMRL offers measures to ease traffic snarls as monsoon nears - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) has implemented several measures to improve road safety and traffic management along the Kakkand route ahead of the monsoon season. The company will deploy additional traffic wardens, install reflectors and reflective tapes on barricades, realign barricades for better driver guidance, and gradually remove barricades as construction progresses. KMRL also directed its contractors to undertake comprehensive monsoon preparedness activities at construction sites and ensure drains are cleared to prevent flooding.

articles.title: GCDA market revamp spells tough times for traders ahead of monsoon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Greater Cochin Development Authority (GCDA) market vendors in Kadavanthra are facing hardship due to delayed renovation works.  The project, aimed at replacing floor tiles and improving the roof, is expected to be completed before the monsoon season arrives next week. V.G. Vincent, a fish vendor, expressed concern about the impact of the upcoming monsoon on his business.

articles.title: Summer showers, strong winds damage over 200 houses in Ernakulam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy summer showers in Ernakulam district have caused widespread damage, with 201 houses damaged between March 1 and May 17 this year compared to only 15 houses damaged during the same period last year.  The intense rainfall led to tree uprooting, waterlogging, and damage to agricultural land, causing estimated crop losses of ₹6.92 crore across 2,306.62 hectares. District Collector G. Priyanka stated that village officers are conducting assessments and compensation will be provided to affected parties.

articles.title: Tennessee governor orders stay of execution after doctor can’t find vein | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Bill Lee of Tennessee granted a one-year stay of execution for Tony Carruthers, who was scheduled to be executed on Thursday.  Carruthers's lawyers argued that he is mentally incompetent and there was a lack of physical evidence linking him to the 1994 murders. The reprieve came after Carruthers's legal team filed a last-minute appeal citing difficulties locating his vein during the lethal injection attempt, as well as concerns about the physician contracted by Tennessee’s department of corrections.  Carruthers's case has drawn attention due to ongoing questions about his conviction and mental competency, as well as protests against his execution.

articles.title: 22 Ministers aged below 50: Cabinet signals generational shift in Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government's Cabinet has seen a significant shift in age composition, with the 2026 TVK Cabinet featuring the youngest average age among the three governments examined.  C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of this government, is 51 years old and his cabinet features the youngest Ministers at just 28 and 29 years old. The 2026 TVK Cabinet has nine Ministers in their 30s, followed by a senior tier of seven Ministers in their 50s, three in their 60s, and only one in the 70-80 age bracket.  This contrasts with the 2021 DMK Cabinet which was heavily dominated by older leaders.

articles.title: Lupita Nyong’o responds to rightwing criticism of The Odyssey: ‘Our cast is representative of the world’ | Lupita Nyong'o | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lupita Nyong’o, Oscar-winning actress, defended her casting in Christopher Nolan's adaptation of The Odyssey, stating that the film's diverse cast reflects the world. She acknowledged criticisms from figures like Elon Musk, who accused Nolan of making a "DEI" hire for awards, but emphasized that she supports his vision and believes the cast is representative.  Nyong’o also addressed her experiences with casting roles following her Oscar win, noting the prevalence of enslaved women's roles offered to her.

articles.title: Congress workers clash with police in Jaipur during stir against NEET-UG paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress party workers clashed with police in Rajasthan on Thursday during a protest against the NEET-UG exam paper leak.  Led by State Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra, the protesters demanded the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and the dissolution of the National Testing Agency. The demonstrators, carrying banners and placards, were forcibly dispersed using water cannons. Some protesters suffered minor injuries.

articles.title: Trump says he will ‘try and make’ son’s wedding, but timing is ‘not good’ for him | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed uncertainty about attending his son Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding in the Bahamas over Memorial Day weekend, citing a full schedule of work, including the ongoing war in Iran.  He acknowledged that he might attend but admitted it would be a "small little private affair." The president has been facing declining approval ratings and is reportedly concerned about appearing out of touch with the public's financial struggles.

articles.title: BJP functionary’s request to HR&CE Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinoj Selvam, a BJP functionary, urged newly appointed Ramesh, the Minister for Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments, to only worship at the Srirangam temple if he visits.  Selvam's statement followed social media posts showing Ramesh with images of late social reformer 'Periyar' E.V. Ramasamy.

articles.title: Kyle Busch, two-time Nascar champion, dies aged 41 | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kyle Busch, a two-time Nascar Cup Series champion, has died at the age of 41.  The racing organization announced his passing on Thursday, expressing condolences to his family and the motorsports community. Busch had been hospitalized with a severe illness earlier in the day, and was unable to compete in this weekend's race in Charlotte, North Carolina. He won championships in 2015 and 2019 and is survived by his wife Samantha and children Brexton and Lennix.

articles.title: Ladakh seeks belonging through representation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Ministry of Home Affairs argues that Ladakh needs more districts rather than a legislature due to its sparse population, strategic sensitivity, and financial dependence on the Centre. This argument is criticized as flawed and reflects an impoverished understanding of democracy, echoing historical paternalistic views by the British Empire.

articles.title: British radio Caroline apologises for accidental King Charles III death broadcast | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Radio Caroline, a historic British radio station, apologized after mistakenly broadcasting that King Charles III had died due to a computer error. The incident occurred on Tuesday afternoon and led to the station briefly going off air before resuming normal programming with an apology.  The station's manager, Peter Moore, explained that an internal "Death of a Monarch" procedure was accidentally triggered.

articles.title: Manipur DGP moved to Cabinet Secretariat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Singh, a 1993 batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer of Tripura cadre, has been appointed Secretary (Security) in the Cabinet Secretariat.  He was appointed as Manipur's police chief in June 2023 following ethnic violence between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo people. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved his appointment on Thursday, May 21, 2026. Singh oversaw the recovery of over 4,500 weapons looted from police armouries after the May 2023 violence and led efforts to arrest around 1,000 extortionists during Manipur's state of President's Rule.

articles.title: Single-sex toilets must exclude transgender people, says EHRC | Gender | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) has released a new code of practice for public bodies, businesses, and service providers in England, Wales, and Scotland regarding single-sex facilities. The guidance clarifies that while services must adhere to the supreme court's ruling on sex in the Equality Act 2010, they can offer alternative options like gender-neutral toilets for those who do not wish to use services based on their biological sex.  The document acknowledges potential negative impacts on transgender individuals and encourages a broader conversation about inclusive access to facilities. However, it also emphasizes that excluding trans people from single-sex facilities is not proportionate in healthcare settings where mixed-sex accommodation is unavailable. The code remains in draft form and will be finalized after 40 days of parliamentary review.

articles.title: Trump says he’ll speak to Taiwan’s leader: Why that is significant | South China Sea News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump suggested he may speak with Taiwan’s President William Lai Ching-te, a move that would mark the first direct contact between leaders of the governments since the US switched diplomatic recognition from Taipei to Beijing in 1979.  While Taiwan remains committed to maintaining the status quo in the Taiwan Strait, China opposes any official exchanges between the US and Taiwan, including arms sales. Analysts say Trump's comments could disrupt decades-old diplomatic protocol and trigger a strong response from Beijing. The potential impact of this move on the $14 billion arms deal with Taiwan remains uncertain.

articles.title: Air France and Airbus held guilty over deadly 2009 Atlantic flight disaster - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Air France and Airbus were found guilty of manslaughter by a Paris appeals court for their role in the 2009 crash of Air France Flight 447, which killed all 228 people on board. The court ruled that the companies bore responsibility for the crash, overturning an earlier decision that had cleared them of criminal liability. Both companies were fined €225,000 each and plan to appeal the verdict.  The families of the victims expressed disappointment with the sentence, but Daniele Lamy, president of the AF447 victims’ association, welcomed the ruling as a step towards accountability for the tragedy.

articles.title: Ladakh leaders to meet Home Ministry officials on May 22, Sonam Wangchuk part of delegation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A delegation from Ladakh, including climate activist Sonam Wangchuk, is meeting with Union Home Ministry officials on Friday to discuss demands for constitutional safeguards such as Statehood and inclusion under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution. This meeting follows a previous inconclusive high-powered committee meeting in February and comes after the violence in Leh city in September 2025, which stalled talks.  The delegation will reiterate their demands for Statehood, while officials have offered safeguards under Article 371 of the Constitution.

articles.title: Boys convicted of rape get non-custodial sentences as judge says they should not be criminalised unnecessarily | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Three teenage boys, aged 13 to 14 at the time of their crimes, were sentenced to youth rehabilitation orders ranging from 18 months to three years for their roles in a series of knife-point rapes and sexual assaults against two teenage girls. Judge Nicholas Rowland stated he wanted to support the boys' reintegration into society and avoid criminalising them unnecessarily due to their young age, low intelligence, and limited understanding of consent.  The judge acknowledged the seriousness of the crimes but emphasized that they were "very young" and had not been in any big trouble before. Donna Jones, Hampshire’s police and crime commissioner, expressed concern over the lenient sentences, stating they offer little comfort to the victims.

articles.title: French Open rejects prize money change despite tennis stars’ boycott threat | Tennis News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Coco Gauff and Aryna Sabalenka, top-ranked tennis players, have criticized the French Open for reducing player compensation to 14.3 percent of revenue, compared to 22 percent at other Grand Slams.  Tournament director Amelie Mauresmo stated that prize money will not change this year but is open to dialogue with players and their representatives. A meeting is scheduled for Friday between organizers and players. While the French Open increased its prize money pot by about 10 percent, players argue their share of revenue declined from 15.5 percent in 2024 to 14.9 percent projected in 2026.

articles.title: Zohran Mamdani: Zohran Mamdani enters streamer era with live Twitch series “Talk with the People” - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zohran Mamdani, the mayor of New York City, is launching a new livestream show called "Talk with the People" on Twitch. The first stream will take place on May 21 at 4 PM ET and will feature Mamdani answering questions from viewers about city issues and daily life in NYC.  The show will also be available on YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, X, and Bluesky, but the main platform for direct interaction is Twitch. The aim of the series is to connect younger generations with City Hall by creating a more accessible and understandable dialogue between government officials and citizens.

articles.title: West Asia crisis hurting Indian tea exporters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Tea Association (ITA) officials reported that the West Asia conflict has significantly impacted tea exports, with 87% of India's total exports concentrated in countries around the Gulf of Persia and the Gulf of Oman. The conflict, which began in February, has led to declining export volumes between January and March compared to 2025, as well as increased freight rates and shipping costs. Dinesh Bihani, secretary of the Guwahati Tea Auction Buyers’ Association, stated that the economic uncertainty in West Asia is causing importers to be cautious about buying tea, leading to softer demand and price pressure on both domestic and international markets.  The industry remains hopeful for a recovery in trade flows and consumption once stability returns.

articles.title: Guardian journalists win across categories at Press Awards in London | Newspapers & magazines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Guardian won several awards at the Press Awards in London, including Political Journalist of the Year for Pippa Crerar, Broadsheet Feature Writer of the Year for Simon Hattenstone, and Young Journalist of the Year for Malak A Tantesh.  Her reporting from besieged Gaza provided a vital perspective during a time when international journalists were largely barred. The Guardian's podcast team also took home News Podcast of the Year for their investigation into the disappearance of British journalist Dom Phillips and Brazilian indigenous expert Bruno Pereira, while The Times won Daily Newspaper of the Year.

articles.title: At least 16 people killed in two attacks in northern Honduras | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: At least 16 people were killed in two separate incidents of gun violence in northern Honduras.  Edgardo Barahona, spokesperson for Honduras’s National Police, reported that at least 10 workers were shot dead on a palm farm in Rigores, while six officers from the Anti-Maras, Gangs and Organised Crime Police Directorate (DIPAMPCO) were killed during an anti-gang operation in Omoa.  Hector Benjamin Valerio Ardon, head of Honduras’s Joint Staff of the Armed Forces, pledged to find those responsible for the attacks. The incidents have prompted the National Police to issue a statement promising immediate action to capture suspects and protect vulnerable communities.

articles.title: New govt. hospital, preventing waterlogging are among my priorities, says Katpadi MLA - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Sudhakar, Katpadi MLA, has identified traffic congestion between the railway station and Green Circle roundabout as a top priority for his constituency. He proposes diverting trucks and goods lorries from Andhra Pradesh to reach Ranipet and Kancheepuram via Chittoor limits, aiming to alleviate the heavy traffic flow during rush hour on Old Katpadi Road.  He plans to present this proposal to the State government.

articles.title: Domestic abuse law fails to recognise danger of tech abuse, Lords committee told | Online abuse | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Lords select committee heard that the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, while encompassing physical and psychological abuse, does not fully address technology-facilitated abuse.  Jen Reed, head of policy at University College London’s Gender and Tech Research Lab, emphasized that tech abuse is as devastating as physical abuse, citing examples like stalkerware and AirTags used for tracking. Kaspersky reported 45% of respondents globally experienced tech abuse in the past year. While tech abuse was included in statutory guidance, Reed argued it's often treated as an online safety issue rather than a core aspect of domestic abuse.

articles.title: Poll finds nearly three-quarters of Democratic voters oppose aid to Israel | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A new poll from The New York Times and Siena found that nearly three-quarters of Democratic voters oppose US military aid to Israel. This shift in sentiment comes as support for Israel continues to decline among US voters, with 60% of Democrats expressing greater sympathy for Palestinians than Israel.  Despite this growing opposition within the Democratic Party, led by figures like Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer, Republican President Donald Trump has maintained strong support for Israel, including a joint war on Iran.

articles.title: Imran’s cases will be fixed after Eid, CJP assures PTI - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi assured PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja that the cases concerning access to a personal physician, family members and counsel for former premier Imran Khan would be scheduled after Eidul Azha.  Raja reported that the CJP had issued instructions to senior officers of the Supreme Court to fix these petitions. The PTI general secretary also stated that the appeals regarding Imran's access were pending before the SC since October 2025, and a petition by Imran's sister challenging the IHC ruling was also pending.  The Supreme Court disposed of appeals filed by the Punjab prosecution seeking cancellation of bail granted to Ejaz Ahmed Chaudhry, involved in the May 9 cases.

articles.title: China’s Moon base plans are pushing ahead faster than NASA’s lunar ambitions | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China and Russia, in collaboration, are accelerating their efforts to build a permanent lunar research station (ILRS) by 2035. This initiative aims to establish an operational facility near the Moon's south pole, utilizing resources like ice water for future habitation.  The ILRS program has attracted international partnerships from over 17 nations and numerous research organizations. Meanwhile, NASA is adjusting its Artemis program timeline to focus on building a permanent lunar base on the ground by 2028. The competition between these two spacefaring powers reflects a shift in the moon race from mere exploration to establishing permanent bases for scientific research and future human settlements.

articles.title: Take forward reforms, PM tells Ministers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi convened a full Council of Ministers meeting in New Delhi on Thursday, May 21, 2026. The session focused on the government's reform agenda amidst geopolitical shifts and saw presentations from various ministries including labor, power, commerce, finance, agriculture, railways, and NITI Aayog.  The meetings reviewed past achievements and future plans, outlining targets for each ministry.

articles.title: David Lammy chairs first meeting of board set up to improve diversity among judiciary | Judiciary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Lammy, the first black lord chancellor, and Sue Carr, the lady chief justice, have formed a new judicial and legal diversity board to address underrepresentation of minority ethnic and working-class solicitors in the judiciary. The board aims to fast-track solicitor recruitment from underrepresented backgrounds and improve mentoring schemes for new recruits.  The initiative follows criticism that Lammy's plans to reduce jury trials could exacerbate racial and class bias within the judiciary, a concern echoed by legal professionals like Keir Monteith KC who believe institutional racism hinders progress. The board hopes to work with existing organizations like the UK Association of Black Judges to address these issues.

articles.title: Who are the 10 best FIFA World Cup players of all time? | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zinedine Zidane, Jimmy Greaves, Ferenc Puskas, Lothar Matthaus, Miroslav Klose, Ronaldo, Franz Beckenbauer, Johan Cruyff, Diego Maradona, and Pele are considered among the best FIFA World Cup players of all time.  They have achieved success on the field, both individually and with their national teams. Some, like Zidane, Greaves, and Beckenbauer, have also been recognized for their leadership and contributions to the sport.

articles.title: Radio station mistakenly announces death of King Charles - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Radio Caroline, a former British pirate radio station, apologized for announcing the death of King Charles III on Tuesday afternoon due to a computer error. The station's manager, Peter Moore, stated that the error triggered a "death of a monarch" procedure and led to an on-air apology.  Moore also confirmed that the station plans to continue broadcasting the King's Christmas message in the future.

articles.title: Who is Mohammed Omar, $90-million fraud suspect in Minnesota, who jumped from balcony to evade FBI arrest? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammed Omar, charged with conspiracy to commit health care fraud and four counts of health care fraud, jumped from a fourth-floor balcony during an FBI arrest attempt in Minnesota on Thursday. Colin McDonald, Assistant Attorney General for the National Fraud Enforcement Division, urged the public to help capture Omar, who allegedly operated two companies, North Home Health Care and South Home Health Care, with Ibrahim Bashir Abdi to defraud the government of $90 million through falsified service hours. The scheme involved using disabled individuals as "lottery tickets" to generate millions of dollars for luxury purchases.

articles.title: Himachal urban poll results reflect public confidence in Congress; party united with no groupism, says CM Sukhu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh, attributed the Congress-backed candidates' victory in recent urban local body elections to public approval of the party's governance. He highlighted the sustained popularity despite anti-incumbency pressures and emphasized a unified effort among party workers.  He also criticized the BJP for its perceived lack of support for Himachal Pradesh, particularly regarding issues like the Revenue Deficit Grant and natural disasters. Sukhu asserted that the Congress has fulfilled its promises and exceeded expectations in delivering on commitments such as welfare schemes and reforms in education and healthcare.

articles.title: Record 274 climbers summit Everest from Nepalese side in single day | Mount Everest | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A record-breaking 274 climbers reached the summit of Mount Everest from the Nepalese side on Wednesday, surpassing previous records. Rishi Ram Bhandari, of the Expedition Operators Association Nepal, confirmed this achievement, noting that the number could increase as some climbers haven't yet reported their ascents.  Marcelo Segovia, an Ecuadorian climber, summited independently without oxygen. Mountaineering experts have previously criticized Nepal's high climber numbers for potential safety risks in the "death zone." The climbing season began late due to a serac threat and is expected to conclude by May with 494 climbers and Sherpa guides attempting the climb.

articles.title: UK launches ‘Great British Summer Savings’ to ease family costs | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government launched the “Great British Summer Savings” scheme to help families afford summer activities.  From June 25th to September 1st, 2026, VAT will be temporarily reduced from 20 percent to 5 percent on children’s meals, family tickets for entertainment venues, and admission tickets to attractions like theme parks and museums. The program is estimated to cost £300 million ($403 million). Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Chancellor Rachel Reeves stated the initiative aims to ease pressure on household budgets while supporting struggling businesses.

articles.title: Govt reopens offshore oil frontier - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik witnessed the signing of production sharing agreements (PSAs) and exploration licences (ELs) for 23 offshore blocks awarded in the Offshore Bid Round 2025. The awarding of these blocks, located in the Indus and Makran basins, attracted an initial investment of $82 million and is expected to reach $1 billion if exploration activities progress to the second phase. Mari Energies, a leading participant, emerged as the most active participant with 18 blocks awarded as operator or joint venture partner. The government aims to revitalize offshore exploration, attract foreign and domestic investment, and reduce reliance on imported energy through this initiative.

articles.title: 'At least 3 fewer Indians': Woman's post on Meta layoff affecting H-1B visa holder with wife and kid in Seattle draws flak - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A viral social media post highlighted the impact of Meta's recent layoffs on Indian workers abroad, with many users celebrating the job loss and speculating about the man's immigration status. The post suggested that the engineer was in Bengaluru, India, and had a 30-year plan on a 3-year visa, prompting discussions about the risks associated with working on temporary visas in the US. Social media users expressed varying opinions, some criticizing the man's decision to live in the US while on an H-1B visa and others highlighting the potential consequences for his family.

articles.title: Sedition trials can go on if accused is willing: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has lifted a four-year hold on sedition trials, allowing courts to proceed with cases where the accused do not object. The court clarified that if an accused consents to continued proceedings under Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), courts can decide matters on merits. This decision follows an interim order in 2022, during which the court had requested the government to reconsider the colonial-era provision.  The Supreme Court directed the Madhya Pradesh High Court to hear the petitioner's appeal and related cases.

articles.title: Parody Cockroach Janta political party’s rise reflects youth anger in India | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A satirical online movement, the Cockroach Janta (People's) party, has gained significant traction in India.  Abhijeet Dipke, a political communications strategist and student at Boston University, founded the movement after Surya Kant, the Supreme Court chief justice, sparked backlash with comments comparing unemployed young people to cockroaches. The CJP uses absurdist humor to mock corruption, joblessness, and government dysfunction, attracting millions of followers on social media.  While some dismiss it as a digital gimmick, Dipke believes it reflects mounting frustration among India's youth and could lead to real political change.

articles.title: Do aid flotillas make a difference for Palestinians under Israeli blockade? | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces have faced global condemnation for their violent treatment of activists attempting to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza via flotillas.  Despite two successful deliveries since 2008, Israeli attempts to stop the flotillas have resulted in detentions and violence, with the latest incident drawing protests from various countries.  The abuse of activists has sparked calls for action against Israel, including potential sanctions.

articles.title: MQM-P leader Khalid Maqbool made member of Economic Coordination Committee - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has approved the addition of Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui, leader of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P), as a member of the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC).  The PMO statement noted that this decision follows a meeting between Siddiqui and Shehbaz Sharif where budget proposals were discussed and the overall political situation was reviewed. The ECC is responsible for handling urgent economic decisions and coordinating financial and economic policies across government departments.

articles.title: Jailed Vietnamese tycoon's Birkin bag sells for nearly £400K
articles.rephrased_article: Two Hermès Birkin bags, confiscated from jailed Vietnamese businesswoman Truong My Lan, sold for over $535,000 at a government auction. The larger bag, a size 25 with rhinestones, fetched nearly seven times its starting bid and the smaller bag, a size 30, sold for less. Nicholas Parnell, founder of Agency Parnell, a wholesale luxury fashion agency, noted that Birkin bags have been increasing in value year-on-year due to their exclusivity and rarity.

articles.title: Chudthebuilder: Judge orders ChudTheBuilder to wear GPS monitor and restrict social media use if released on bond - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as ChudTheBuilder, faces strict new bond conditions after a judge ruled on his possible release from custody. The restrictions, imposed due to serious charges including attempted criminal homicide and firearm offenses, include GPS monitoring, weapon surrender, social media bans, and limited communication.  If released on bond, Eatherly will be closely monitored and must strictly adhere to all court orders.

articles.title: Supreme Court declines to interfere with forest clearances for Adani’s Madhya Pradesh coal block project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court declined to intervene in environmental clearances granted to the Adani Group's coal block project in Madhya Pradesh. The court noted a delay in challenging the approvals and observed that the National Green Tribunal (NGT) had relied on a 2025 ruling regarding limitation periods for challenges.  While the petitioner argued for judicial review of the clearances due to environmental concerns, the Adani Group urged dismissal of the plea. The court suggested Mr. Dubey pursue other legal remedies and granted him liberty to do so.

articles.title: The far-right Israeli minister taunting detained Gaza activists – The Latest | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s far-right national security minister, has sparked global condemnation for sharing footage of himself taunting activists detained while attempting to sail to Gaza with aid. Ben-Gvir's actions have been widely criticized by world leaders, including Giorgia Meloni, the Italian prime minister, and Israeli politicians, including Benjamin Netanyahu, the country’s prime minister.

articles.title: Ronaldo scores twice to seal Saudi Pro League at last with Al-Nassr | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cristiano Ronaldo led Al-Nassr to a 4-1 victory over Damac, securing the Saudi Pro League title.  The win marks Ronaldo's first domestic championship since winning Serie A with Juventus in 2020 and adds to his collection of English, Spanish, Italian titles and five Champions League medals. The victory comes after a tumultuous season for Ronaldo, marked by both triumphs and setbacks, including a loss in the King’s Cup final and a protest against Benzema's transfer to Al Hilal.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: Angry crowd sets Rwampara hospital tents on fire
articles.rephrased_article: An angry crowd in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo set fire to hospital tents used for Ebola isolation wards, after the death of a young man who was thought to have died from typhoid fever but whose body was not allowed to be buried. Luc Malembe Malembe, a local politician, witnessed the scene and stated that people did not believe the virus existed. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared it a "public health emergency of international concern," but not at pandemic level.  The outbreak, caused by a rare species of Ebola known as Bundibugyo, has resulted in 139 deaths and two cases in neighboring Uganda.

articles.title: Who is Maurice Shelmon aka Ant Jefe? No Jumper YouTuber and podcaster faces felony murder charge after LAPD arrest - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Maurice Shelmon, better known online as Ant Jefe, was arrested by the Los Angeles Police Department on May 19 in connection with a felony murder case.  Shelmon, a popular podcasting and YouTube personality, had built a large following through his music releases, reaction videos, and appearances on the No Jumper podcast. The arrest has surprised many of his followers, who expressed shock and disbelief during a livestream hosted by No Jumper hosts.

articles.title: From rallies to reels: political catchphrases turn dance anthems in Kolkata - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A new genre of political techno remixes has emerged in Kolkata, using catchy hooks and meme-friendly punchlines to criticize politicians. The trend began with songs like "Khela Hobe" and continues with remixed versions of "Hamba Hamba", "Mach Chor", and "File Chor". These songs often target specific individuals or parties, gaining popularity through social media platforms like Instagram and YouTube Shorts.  The use of crude humor and satirical lyrics reflects a culture of insult-flinging on social media while also expressing anger towards political leaders who abuse power.

articles.title: News live: Australian flotilla activists released by Israel arrive in Istanbul and claim they were denied food and water | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Hillel Newman, Israel's ambassador to Australia, stated that no one from the 400+ people detained on the Global Sumud Flotilla was harmed. Newman also claimed that the interception of the flotilla was done with "great sensitivity" by Israeli security forces.  The Australian delegation aboard the flotilla reported being held for about 80 hours, denied food and water, and said they were treated poorly. The Australians will meet with lawyers before returning to Australia.

articles.title: Board of Peace envoy warns ‘permanent’ Gaza divide under current status quo | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nickolay Mladenov, high representative of the Board of Peace for Gaza, warned that the current status quo in Gaza risks becoming permanent, with Hamas holding control over two million Palestinians.  Mladenov urged the UN Security Council to pressure Hamas for disarmament and for Israel to uphold its ceasefire obligations. He stated that Palestinian obligations alone cannot achieve a lasting peace and called for action from both sides to avoid a permanent division in Gaza.

articles.title: India's 'Cockroach Janta Party' goes viral, spotlights Gen Z worries - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A five-day-old group called the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has gained significant traction in India, surpassing the Instagram followers of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).  The CJP, founded by 30-year-old Abhijeet Dipke, addresses issues like unemployment, inflation, and political representation, resonating with a large segment of young Indians who feel ignored by mainstream politics. The group's rapid growth reflects the anxieties felt by India's youth, as highlighted in a recent Deloitte Global survey that found Gen Z facing financial stress and postponing major life decisions due to economic concerns. Dipke emphasizes the CJP's commitment to democratic and peaceful means of political engagement, while also acknowledging its potential for significant change within Indian politics.

articles.title: Cuba is a national security threat to the US, Rubio says
articles.rephrased_article: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Cuba poses a "national security threat" to the US and diplomatic solutions are unlikely due to Cuba's leadership.  Bruno Rodríguez, Cuba's Foreign Minister, refuted these claims, stating that Cuba has never posed a threat to the US. Rubio also accused Cuba of being a leading sponsor of terrorism and asserted that the US government is seeking to pressure the country into making concessions.  Trump, meanwhile, expressed his desire to help Cuba and remove its communist regime.

articles.title: Trump shifts between diplomacy and threats in Iran standoff | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has exhibited a mixed approach to the Iran standoff, oscillating between expressions of hope for a ceasefire and threats of military escalation.  The US president's unpredictable messaging coincides with renewed diplomacy as Iran reviews Washington's response to Tehran's latest ceasefire proposal. Trump has also indicated an appetite for a prolonged conflict, sharing a pro-Israel think tank article advocating for economic warfare and military action against Iran. This week, Trump threatened renewed attacks but later agreed to give Iran time to return to negotiations.  The US president faces a strategic dilemma as he seeks a convincing victory in the conflict while also navigating potential economic consequences of escalating tensions.

articles.title: Oil markets nearing ‘red zone’ as Iran crisis continues, warns IEA chief | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Fatih Birol, executive director of the International Energy Agency, warned that oil markets will enter a "red zone" by July and August due to dwindling stocks before the summer travel season.  He attributed this to a shortage of fresh oil exports from the Middle East, exacerbated by geopolitical tensions, particularly surrounding Iran's nuclear program. Birol urged the release of more strategic oil reserves and stressed that countries should diversify their energy sources, including renewables, nuclear power, and coal. Pakistan's interior minister, Mohsin Naqvi, is currently in Tehran attempting to mediate between Iran and the United States, while Donald Trump, former US president, has expressed conflicting views on Iran's enriched uranium stockpile.

articles.title: Three children among seven persons rescued from brick kiln near Arakkonam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Revenue officials rescued seven members of the Irular community from a brick kiln in Minnal village near Arakkonam town. The children, aged 13 to 17, were among those rescued and reported suffering inhumane treatment including physical abuse, long working hours, and inadequate living conditions.  The owner of the brick kiln, K. Palani, and his sons, P. Suresh and P. Suman, are facing legal action. The rescued individuals received release certificates enabling them to access government aid programs for bonded laborers.

articles.title: Quote of the day by physicist Wolfgang Pauli: “I do not mind if you think slowly, but I do object when you publish more quickly than you think.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Wolfgang Pauli, a renowned physicist, famously stated, "I do not mind if you think slowly, but I do object when you publish more quickly than you think."  The quote highlights the importance of thoughtful consideration over hasty conclusions. While speed can be beneficial in certain situations, it should not replace careful thinking and analysis. The quote resonates with modern society's fast-paced culture where instant reactions are often prioritized over genuine understanding.

articles.title: Qatar-based British-Pakistani scientist develops AI eye scan for early dementia diagnosis - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Professor Rayaz Malik, a British-Pakistani scientist based in Qatar, has developed an AI-powered eye scan using corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) that can detect dementia and diabetic nerve damage years before symptoms appear.  This technology, traditionally used to diagnose infections and abnormalities in the front surface of the eye, has been shown to identify microscopic nerve fibre damage associated with diseases such as diabetes, chemotherapy, inflammatory disorders, and infectious diseases. Professor Malik believes this could be particularly important for countries facing ageing populations and rising rates of neurological disease.  The technology's ability to detect early-stage cognitive decline could lead to more effective treatments and earlier interventions.

articles.title: Five key takeaways from Democrats’ autopsy report on Kamala Harris’s loss | Kamala Harris News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic National Committee (DNC) released its long-awaited autopsy report on why former Vice President Kamala Harris lost the 2024 presidential election. The report, riddled with factual errors and missing sections, failed to address key issues like the Biden administration's support for Israel during the Gaza war, which some analysts believe contributed to Harris's loss.  The report also criticized the White House for assigning Harris immigration responsibilities without adequate preparation and suggested that the campaign focused too heavily on defeating Trump instead of promoting Harris's own vision. The report was released in its unedited format despite acknowledging its shortcomings and did not include specific recommendations for future elections.

articles.title: Israel deports foreign Gaza-bound flotilla activists after global outcry | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has deported all foreign activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla after global condemnation of their treatment in custody.  The UK, Italy, and the European Council have summoned Israeli diplomats for a formal dressing down, with many condemning the far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, for posting a video depicting activists being humiliated.  Human rights groups have documented widespread abuse of Palestinians in Israeli prisons, prompting criticism from within Israel and even from US officials who typically support Israel's policies. Greece also called for the immediate release of its nationals detained on the flotilla.

articles.title: Bihar midday meal incident: HC asks whether NGO can continue providing meals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Patna High Court has expressed concern over delays in the investigation of a midday meal incident where over 150 students fell ill in Saharsa district. The court questioned whether the NGO supplying meals to over 1,800 students should continue operations during the probe and raised concerns about discrepancies in food sample collection and testing.  The court directed officials to file affidavits explaining the processes involved. The matter will be heard again on June 2nd.

articles.title: Quote of the day by American astronomer Carl Sagan: “The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Carl Sagan's famous quote, "The cosmos is within us. We are made of star-stuff. We are a way for the cosmos to know itself," highlights the scientific reality that human beings are composed of elements forged in stars billions of years ago. This powerful statement transcends mere science, suggesting that humans are intrinsically connected to the universe and carry a piece of its history within them. Sagan's work aimed to make science accessible and relatable, emphasizing the wonder and curiosity inherent in exploring our place within the vast cosmos.  His words continue to resonate with readers today because they remind us that despite our smallness, we possess an extraordinary ability to question and understand the universe around us.

articles.title: Hot weather on the cards during Eid as PMD predicts heatwave from May 25-31 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Meteorological Department (PMD) has issued a heatwave warning for the country from May 25 to May 31, with temperatures expected to reach 47-50°C in some areas. The federal government has declared a three-day public holiday from May 26-28 to allow citizens to stay safe during the extreme weather conditions. The PMD advises the public to take precautions against heatstroke and conserve water and electricity.

articles.title: Ebola tensions rise as treatment centre torched in DR Congo’s Ituri | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Residents in Rwampara, DRC, set fire to a treatment facility after authorities refused to release the body of a man believed to have died from Ebola. The incident highlights deep mistrust and anger surrounding the response to the outbreak, fueled by traditional burial practices that clash with public health measures. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern, warning that violence and community distrust are hampering efforts to contain the disease.

articles.title: Air France and Airbus guilty of corporate manslaughter for 2009 plane crash | France | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Paris appeals court found Airbus and Air France guilty of corporate manslaughter in the 2009 Rio-Paris plane crash that killed 228 people. The verdict, after a 17-year legal battle, resulted in fines of €225,000 each for both companies.  The court's decision, while considered a symbolic victory by some families of the victims, is expected to be challenged further through appeals.

articles.title: Chennithala seeks report on parole granted to Periye murder convicts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following protests from the families of the victims in the Periye twin murder case, Kerala Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has requested a report on the parole granted to five convicts. The parole order was issued during the final phase of the previous Left Democratic Front government's tenure and the jail authorities clarified that prisoners are generally not allowed to leave during elections.  The family members of the victims plan to meet the Chief Minister and the Home Minister to file a formal complaint against the mass parole granted to the convicts.

articles.title: Elon Musk agrees with what Jeff Bezos says on charity: 'If I do my job right...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jeff Bezos, founder of Amazon, stated in an interview that his businesses provide more societal benefit than his charitable donations.  He cited examples like Amazon's essential services during the pandemic and letters from grateful customers as evidence. Elon Musk shared this sentiment, highlighting the value created by for-profit companies. Social media users debated whether Bezos' statement was genuine or a convenient justification for prioritizing profit over philanthropy.

articles.title: Patient tests HIV-positive after surgery, triggering probe at Multan’s Nishtar Hospital - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Nishtar Hospital in Multan, Pakistan, has formed a four-member inquiry committee to investigate allegations of medical negligence following a patient's surgery without mandatory HIV screening. The patient tested positive for the virus after the procedure and raised concerns among staff about potential exposure and lapses in infection control protocols.  The hospital claims that preventive measures were taken immediately, including disinfection of surgical instruments. Dr Riwad Noor, a member of the inquiry committee, stated they will submit their report within two days.

articles.title: Fans create AI-generated team songs ahead of World Cup | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Fans are creating AI-generated football anthems for the upcoming World Cup, generating millions of plays on social media.  The trend has sparked debate about song ownership, artist compensation, and the valuation of human creativity. While some fans prefer these AI-created songs over official FIFA commissions, experts like Jason Palamara, an assistant professor of music technology at Indiana University, raise concerns about copyright and authorship in the use of copyrighted works to train AI models.  Despite these challenges, many listeners appreciate the simplicity and catchy nature of these fan-made anthems.

articles.title: Protests at new US consulate after Trump envoy says time for US ‘to put its footprint back’ on Greenland | Greenland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Greenlandic politicians and protesters gathered in Nuuk to oppose the opening of a new US consulate, citing concerns about increased US presence and potential encroachment on Greenland's sovereignty. Jeff Landry, the US special envoy to Greenland, arrived uninvited and sparked outrage with comments suggesting Greenland needs US intervention for national security.  The protest highlights growing tensions between Greenland and the US over the future of Greenland's autonomy.

articles.title: Sacred hall housing Japan's 'eternal flame' destroyed by fire
articles.rephrased_article: A fire destroyed the Reikado Hall on Miyajima island, causing significant damage to the Daishoin Buddhist temple complex. The Japan Times reports that the hall housed the "eternal flame," which has been burning for nearly 1,200 years and was moved to a different location after the fire. Authorities are investigating whether the blaze may have been caused by the flame itself, as the hall also burned down in 2005.

articles.title: US stocks today: S&P 500 rises on Mideast peace hopes as oil prices dip - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio and Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei have presented contrasting stances on the potential for a diplomatic deal with Iran. While Rubio expressed optimism about positive signs in talks, Khamenei issued a directive prohibiting uranium exports. Despite uncertainty surrounding progress, market sentiment remains sensitive to geopolitical developments, particularly related to Iran's nuclear program and the fragile ceasefire. The S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Jones Industrial Average all experienced gains, while Walmart shares fell after disappointing earnings forecasts.

articles.title: Bangladesh-China talks underway for Tarique Rahman’s first foreign visit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tarique Rahman, Bangladesh's new Prime Minister, is in talks with China to visit the country in late June.  The Chinese government is keen on welcoming him for his first foreign trip since taking office in February. The planned visit will include high-level meetings between Rahman and top Chinese leaders, including President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Li Keqiang.

articles.title: Grammacrackers: 81-year-old Minecraft streamer GrammaCrackers swatted during cancer fundraiser stream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sue Jacquot, better known as GrammaCrackers, a 81-year-old Twitch streamer, was swatted during a Minecraft livestream to raise money for her grandson's cancer treatment.  The incident involved multiple police vehicles and officers who entered her home while she was asleep. Despite the frightening experience, GrammaCrackers remained positive, joking about meeting a "pretty policewoman" and expressing gratitude for the support of her family and viewers. The event sparked anger and concern online, with many people expressing their support for the elderly streamer's fundraiser.

articles.title: Sialkot authorities on alert as India opens spillway gates of dam on Chenab River - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sialkot Deputy Commissioner Saba Asghar issued a high alert for the Chenab River following an advisory from India warning of potential emergency silt flushing at the Indian Salal Dam. The rising water level has prompted restrictions on movement along the river and its banks, with authorities urging citizens to avoid unnecessary visits to rivers and canals.  Asghar also activated the District Emergency Control Room and directed all relevant departments to monitor the situation 24/7.

articles.title: US sanctions elected Hezbollah MPs and Lebanese security officials | Hezbollah News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has imposed sanctions on nine individuals, including members of Lebanon's parliament and an Iranian diplomat, accusing them of aiding Hezbollah and undermining Lebanese sovereignty. The US Department of the Treasury stated these sanctions are intended to deter those who aid Hezbollah's financial networks and obstruct peace efforts in Lebanon.  Hezbollah responded by calling the sanctions a "badge of honor" and stating they would have no effect on its strategic choices. Meanwhile, ongoing Israeli air strikes continue to target southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire that was recently extended for 45 days. The US is also brokering peace talks between Israel and the Lebanese government, with negotiations scheduled for June 2nd and 3rd.

articles.title: Feral horse numbers surge in Kosciuszko national park after pause in aerial culling, survey shows | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: New South Wales government data shows feral horse numbers in Kosciuszko national park surged to between 6,476 and 16,411 in late 2025, a sharp increase from the previous year.  The surge prompted calls for urgent action from conservation advocates who argue that retention zones allowing thousands of horses to remain in the park should be scrapped. Penny Sharpe, NSW environment minister, acknowledged the need for continued management but emphasized the government's commitment to reducing feral horse numbers to 3,000 by mid-2027.  The Invasive Species Council chief executive, Jack Gough, called for amendments to the feral horse management plan and urged the government to eliminate retention zones altogether.

articles.title: Mother arrested after boys abandoned by road in Portugal
articles.rephrased_article: Two French boys, aged under five, were found abandoned by the side of a road in Portugal and their mother and stepfather have been arrested. The children were discovered near Alcacer do Sal on Tuesday with backpacks containing food and water but no identification documents.  The boys' father reported them missing from their home in Colmar, France, on May 11th. Police in Portugal and France are investigating the case.

articles.title: Watch: Moment car explodes into massive fireball in NYC
articles.rephrased_article: A hybrid car exploded in Lower Manhattan on Tuesday afternoon, sending thick black smoke and debris into the air. The incident occurred near Metropolitan Transportation Authority (MTA) headquarters and sent people fleeing for safety. Firefighters extinguished the flames after an hour-long response, with no reported injuries.  The cause of the explosion is believed to be an electrical fault.

articles.title: Hungary to limit PMs to eight years in office, warding off any Orbán comeback | Hungary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, leader of the Tisza party, submitted a constitutional amendment to limit prime ministers to eight years in office. The draft amendment would bar Viktor Orbán, who has served five terms as prime minister since 1998, from returning to the role.  The amendment also aims to dissolve the controversial sovereignty protection office and reclaim control of foundations that were previously controlled by loyalists of the previous government. This move is part of a broader effort by the new government to dismantle the constitution unilaterally rewritten and amended by Orbán's Fidesz party and restore democratic checks and balances. The amendment, expected to pass with the support of the Tisza party’s supermajority in parliament, will be discussed next week.

articles.title: Massive car crash in New Jersey pushes BMW into river; Indian-origin driver arrested after fleeing scene on foot - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A BMW driven by 32-year-old Zorawar S Kohli of Englewood Cliffs crashed into the Hackensack River Bridge on Route 80, causing the vehicle to plunge into the water. The driver escaped and was later found hiding under a train and arrested.  The crash also injured the passenger in the Land Rover, who was taken to a hospital with minor injuries.  State Police investigated the incident, leading to Kohli's arrest on charges of obstruction, resisting arrest, assault by auto, and other motor vehicle offenses.

articles.title: ‘Barring elected representatives, TVK members not to go for inspections’: Minister Arunraj - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) general secretary K.G. Arunraj, Minister for Health and Family Welfare, clarified that only elected representatives are authorized to conduct inspections.  His statement followed criticism of a woman claiming to be from the party's medical wing inspecting the Government Hospital in Sankarankovil, as instructed by TVK president C. Joseph Vijay and general secretary N. Anand.

articles.title: Taliban's new marriage separation decree draws UN criticism - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Afghan Taliban government's new decree on spousal separation has been condemned by the United Nations as it reinforces systemic discrimination against women and girls. The 31-article code sets out various grounds for separation, including "incompatibility" and a husband's disappearance, and suggests child marriage is permitted.  The UN stated that this further erodes the rights of Afghan women and girls, denying them autonomy and access to justice. Zabihullah Mujahid, government spokesperson, defended the decree as coming from people hostile to Islam.

articles.title: Top UN court rules workers’ right to strike ‘protected’ in key treaty | Workers' Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) issued a non-binding advisory opinion stating that workers' right to strike is protected under the 1948 International Labour Organization’s (ILO) Freedom of Association treaty. The ICJ, in a 10-4 ruling, emphasized that this opinion does not determine the exact conditions for exercising this right but is expected to influence labor laws globally. International Trade Union Confederation representatives hailed the decision as a victory for workers' rights and expect it will impact countries that have not recognized employees' right to strike.

articles.title: Trump says he will speak to Taiwan's president in break from protocol
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced he will speak to Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te about a possible arms sale, potentially breaking diplomatic tradition. China strongly opposes such exchanges and US arms sales to Taiwan, urging the US to stop sending "wrong signals" to separatist forces in Taiwan.  The potential conversation comes amidst heightened tensions between the US and China over Taiwan, with President Xi Jinping expressing concern about conflict if handled poorly. The US has a long-standing policy of providing Taiwan with defensive arms, but Trump's decision on the $14 billion arms package is pending.

articles.title: Italian police stop party attended by Mick Jagger over music ban | Mick Jagger | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mick Jagger and other actors from the film "Three Incestuous Sisters" were stopped by police on Stromboli, Italy, for playing music during a Wednesday night celebration. The mayor of Lipari, Riccardo Gullo, enacted a local music ban, which caused confusion but was accepted by the partygoers.  The film crew and actors departed Stromboli on Thursday after the incident, with Jagger leaving via private helicopter.

articles.title: Only 30 people live in this Spanish village which offers cheap land and a peaceful life in the hills to attract new residents | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Olmeda de la Cuesta, a small rural village in Spain, is offering cheap land through public auctions to attract new residents and combat its declining population. The village council hopes affordable living costs and a tranquil countryside lifestyle will reverse the trend of rural depopulation.  While the municipality acknowledges that basic facilities are scarce, it offers a unique alternative for those seeking solitude and a slower pace of life. Spain’s Official State Gazette also listed additional rural land auctions in early 2026.

articles.title: Room for reconciliation within the AIADMK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and the rebel camp of the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) are attempting to reconcile after a recent trust vote where the rebels supported the government while the TVK regime voted against them.  A senior rebel leader claims efforts have been made to bring the two camps together, with mediators involved and petitions filed for disqualification proceedings. The rebel camp insists on an early general council meeting to address electoral setbacks and decision-making processes within the organization, despite not being invited to the swearing-in ceremony of the TVK regime.

articles.title: Seems PTI will now have to 'resort to agitation', says MNA after party leaders yet again denied meeting with Imran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ahad Ali Shah, a member of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), stated that his party would resort to agitation after being denied another meeting with former prime minister Imran Khan.  The Islamabad High Court has granted Khan twice-weekly meetings at Adiala jail, but restrictions have prevented him from meeting visitors for several weeks. The PTI submitted a list of six leaders, including Shah, for a meeting on Thursday but was denied access.  A caravan led by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to meet Khan was stopped in Islamabad and resulted in a sit-in at Chungi No. 26.

articles.title: Shocked Maguire posts on Insta that he is not in England’s World Cup squad | Sport News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Harry Maguire, Manchester United defender, announced on social media that he is not part of Thomas Tuchel’s England World Cup squad. The 33-year-old center back expressed shock and disappointment over the decision, having been a key player for England in previous tournaments.  Maguire's absence comes after a season with Manchester United where he helped revive the team following the departure of former coach Ruben Amorim. He has made 66 appearances for his country and scored seven goals.

articles.title: DR Congo cancels World Cup training camp over Ebola outbreak
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of Congo has cancelled its pre-World Cup training camp in Kinshasa due to an Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the outbreak a "public health emergency of international concern" but not a pandemic.  The team will now train in Belgium, and their pre-tournament games in Europe will proceed as planned. Concerns have been raised about travel restrictions imposed by the US, which is hosting the World Cup this summer.

articles.title: MPs urged to ignore fearmongering and pass Labor’s ‘long overdue’ negative gearing and CGT changes | Housing | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor's proposed changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax are being urged by Australian peak community and housing groups as a way to improve fairness for renters and young homebuyers. The reforms, which include limiting new negative gearing to new-builds and grandfathering existing properties, aim to rebalance the housing market towards first-time buyers.  The changes have been welcomed by social and housing groups who predict they will improve housing stability for renters and encourage long-term investment in housing. However, some economists are concerned about potential impacts on home values and rents, while property lobbyists have raised concerns about misinformation surrounding the reforms.

articles.title: Nykaa Q4 Results: Cons profit surges 286% YoY to Rs 78 crore, revenue rises 28% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nykaa's parent company reported a 28% increase in revenue to Rs 2,648 crore for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026 (Q4FY26), driven by a 26% rise in net revenue to Rs 10,022 crore. The company's gross merchandising value (GMV) grew 28% year-on-year to Rs 5,241 crore, marking the 14th consecutive quarter of growth. Nykaa also saw a significant increase in its EBITDA and PAT, with EBITDA rising 67% YoY to Rs 223 crore and PAT surging 183% to Rs 204 crore for the fiscal year.

articles.title: 'Meta reached out to interview me the same week...': US founder asks what happened to employee retention - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zach Wilson, an American entrepreneur, criticized Meta for its recent layoffs of 8,000 employees following the announcement of a new AI strategy. Wilson expressed his belief that one of those laid-off individuals possesses the necessary qualifications for a principal role offered by Meta.  The company attributed the layoff to "running the company more efficiently" and thanked affected employees for their contributions.

articles.title: IT-based skill training launched for inmates at Visakhapatnam Central Jail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Prisons Department and the Skill Development Institute (SDI), Visakhapatnam, launched an IT-based skill development course for inmates at the Visakhapatnam Central Jail. The "Office Assistant" program, inaugurated by Visakhapatnam District Collector M. Abhishikth Kishore, aims to equip inmates with industry-oriented skills and improve their employability prospects after release.  The two-month course covers computer applications, office administration, digital communication, and employability skills, with successful participants receiving a certification from SDI Visakhapatnam.

articles.title: Educationist who fled occupied Kashmir fights for his life after targeted attack - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Arjumand Gulzar Dar, a Kashmiri educationist and principal of Allama Iqbal Memorial School in Muzaffarabad, was critically wounded in a targeted attack on Thursday. The attacker, apprehended within half an hour, fled the scene after firing three shots at Dar. Police suspect a hostile foreign intelligence service may be involved.  The incident has sparked concerns about security threats faced by Kashmiri migrants in Pakistan.

articles.title: Mayor cuts limited World Cup tickets for New Yorkers to $50 after furore | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York City announced the distribution of 1,000 discounted World Cup tickets costing $50 to city residents. The tickets will be available for seven games at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey and include free transportation to the stadium.  The initiative aims to ensure working-class New Yorkers can afford to attend the tournament, a goal Mamdani has advocated for since his campaign.

articles.title: Nvidia's latest record earnings fail to impress investors
articles.rephrased_article: Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, reported record quarterly earnings with revenue exceeding expectations and a significant increase in net income. Despite strong performance driven by data center growth, shares fell after-hours as investors anticipate slowing growth and increased competition. Nvidia is forecasting continued revenue growth to reach $91 billion in the second quarter, while returning cash to shareholders through dividends and share buybacks.  However, analysts suggest that investor expectations for continued hypergrowth may have led to an early sell-off.

articles.title: Cubans outraged at US charges against Raúl Castro but view military strikes as serious possibility | Cuba | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US has indicted former Cuban president Raúl Castro on charges related to the 1996 shooting down of two unarmed planes belonging to the Brothers to the Rescue group. The indictment, which follows weeks of heightened tensions between the two countries, comes amidst increased surveillance and military activity in the region.  Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, has offered aid to Cuba while also blaming the Cuban government for the ongoing blackouts and economic hardship. Concerns about US attempts to exert control over Cuba have been raised by some, particularly in light of recent reports suggesting a potential deal between Sherritt, a major Cuban nickel miner, and a former Trump advisor.

articles.title: Paytm block deal: SAIF Partners, others likely to sell stake worth Rs 963 crore, says report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SAIF Partners, a global investment bank, is reportedly arranging a block deal sale of shares in One 97 Communications, the parent company of Paytm. The transaction is expected to raise $100 million from existing shareholders.  The move follows a significant stock price recovery for Paytm, driven by improved operational metrics and investor confidence in the digital payments sector.

articles.title: How Kamala Harris sank: Democrats admit 2024 went horribly wrong but have no roadmap for 2028 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Party released a 192-page autopsy of its 2024 presidential campaign, authored by strategist Paul Rivera. The report criticizes the party's disconnect from working-class voters, weak economic messaging, cultural overreach, and organizational complacency.  It also suggests that Democrats failed to connect with Latino voters, men, rural Americans, and younger voters while failing to address issues like immigration, public safety, and inflation. However, the report notably avoids a sustained examination of President Biden's decision to seek re-election despite concerns about his age and stamina. The document was released despite criticism from Democratic National Committee chairman Ken Martin who acknowledged its shortcomings.  The party now faces internal divisions over how to address these issues and regain voter trust.

articles.title: Antarvahini Saraswati ‘Antya Pushkaralu’ begins in Kaleshwaram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla and his wife Janaki Shukla participated in religious ceremonies at the Saraswati Ghat during the start of the 12-day ‘Antya Pushkaralu’ festival.  Devotees from across the region gathered to witness the event, which marks the beginning of the sacred celebrations. Sri Shankara Vijayendra Saraswathi Swami of Kanchi Kamakoti Peetam performed special pujas and rituals at the Triveni Sangamam, where the subterranean Antarvahini Saraswati river joins the Godavari and Pranahita rivers.  D. Sridhar Babu, Minister for IT and Industries, and Konda Surekha, Endowments Minister, were also present.

articles.title: Security forces kill 23 terrorists in multiple Khyber Pakhtunkhwa IBOs: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: ISPR announced the killing of 23 terrorists in intelligence-based operations across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa over the last 48 hours. The military identified the deceased as members of the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), including ring leader Jan Meer alias Toor Saqib, who was wanted for his involvement in terrorist activities.  Security forces discovered and destroyed complex underground tunnels and bunkers used by the terrorists, along with weapons, ammunition, and explosives. The operations are part of a continued counterterrorism campaign against foreign-sponsored terrorism in Pakistan.

articles.title: Net migration to the UK falls by nearly 50 percent amid tighter policies | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) reported that net migration to the UK fell by nearly 50 percent in the year ending December, dropping to 171,000 from 331,000 a year earlier.  This decline reflects stricter immigration policies implemented since 2024, including bans on international student dependents and higher salary thresholds for skilled worker visas. Interior Minister Shabana Mahmood welcomed the progress but emphasized the need to restore border control while acknowledging concerns about labor shortages.

articles.title: Walmart warns US shoppers are cutting spending as higher petrol prices bite
articles.rephrased_article: Walmart has warned that higher petrol prices are causing US consumers to cut spending, leading to a slowdown in sales growth between May and July. The retail giant expects this trend to continue as the effect of tax cuts from President Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) fades away. John David Rainey, Walmart's finance boss, stated that while higher tax returns initially offset pressure from rising fuel costs, they are now diminishing, putting consumers under more strain.  Walmart is closely monitoring petrol prices and expects them to remain high in the coming months, potentially impacting food prices due to supply chain disruptions.

articles.title: Ebola: US ban on travellers from DRC, Uganda or South Sudan ‘not the solution’ | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern due to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with new cases reported in South Kivu province.  Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) criticized travel bans imposed by the US on citizens from the affected countries, arguing that they are ineffective and could exacerbate the situation. Dr Githinji Gitahi, CEO of Amref Health Africa, echoed this sentiment, emphasizing the need for investment in outbreak control at the source rather than isolating affected regions.  Uganda’s information minister, Chris Baryomunsi, countered by stating that his country has experience managing similar outbreaks and possesses the capacity to contain them.

articles.title: Eight cars gutted after carrier truck catches fire on NH-44 in Medak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A container truck carrying new cars caught fire on National Highway 44 near Nagulapally village in Medak district, India.  Police and firefighters battled the blaze for nearly two hours before bringing it under control, preventing any casualties. The fire destroyed eight vehicles inside the truck. Preliminary investigations suggest a mechanical failure may have triggered the incident.

articles.title: LIC announces 1:1 bonus issue, sets May 29 as record date - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: LIC, the State-owned insurance company, announced a 1:1 share swap for existing shareholders.
