The company reported strong Q4 earnings with a 23% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 23,467 crore. LIC's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 10 per share for the financial year 2025-26.  The company also saw significant growth in its net premium income, VNB, and assets under management (AUM).

articles.title: PIA wraps up Haj operations, transports over 53,000 pilgrims: spokesperson - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) successfully completed its pre-Hajj flight operations, transporting over 53,000 pilgrims to Saudi Arabia. The airline achieved a 97% on-time departure rate, exceeding the target by 7%, with direct flights operating from several cities.  The post-Hajj operation is scheduled to begin on May 30 and end on June 30.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists deported from Israel as backlash over treatment grows
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has deported hundreds of pro-Palestinian activists detained after their flotilla attempting to bring aid to Gaza was intercepted.  The move follows international condemnation over a video showing National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir taunting the activists while they were being held.  Poland, Italy, and other countries have also summoned Israeli diplomats in response, expressing outrage at the treatment of their citizens and demanding apologies.

articles.title: One Nation’s rapid national expansion in disarray as ‘significant risks’ force dissolution of new branches | One Nation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: One Nation has been forced to dissolve and re-establish its new branch network less than eight months after its ambitious rollout began due to internal inconsistencies.  The party's general manager, Kelvin Morton, issued a directive requiring all branches to comply with strict vetting processes, including non-disclosure agreements and media silence policies. This move has raised concerns about the party's commitment to free speech, as it attempts to control its grassroots movement ahead of the next election.  The party's headquarters intends to maintain tight control over branch operations and communications.

articles.title: US-Iran diplomacy picks up: What’s the latest? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's visit to Iran is part of ongoing diplomatic efforts to reach a peace deal between the US and Iran.  Naqvi met with his Iranian counterpart, Eskandar Momeni, in Tehran, potentially signaling new diplomatic initiatives. While details of their discussions remain undisclosed, Pakistan has been facilitating talks since a temporary ceasefire was reached in April. The US and Iran continue to exchange proposals for peace, but key issues like Iran's enriched uranium stockpile and its support for proxy groups remain contentious points of disagreement.  The situation remains volatile as both sides are far apart on a number of critical issues.

articles.title: California hit-and-run: Indian man arrested by ICE after state releases him, 4-year-old victim expected to survive - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Aman Kumar, an Indian man, was arrested by ICE after being released from jail in California on charges of felony hit-and-run following a traffic accident that injured a four-year-old boy.  The incident occurred in April 2026 when Kumar ran over the child while attempting to avoid traffic. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) accused California sanctuary politicians of releasing Kumar from jail despite his illegal entry into the US in 2023.

articles.title: Calcutta High Court asks Bengal government to decide on exemption in animal slaughter rules for Eid ul-Adha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court directed the West Bengal government to decide on an exemption request for animal slaughter during Eid al-Adha, citing Section 12 of the West Bengal Animal Slaughter Control Act, 1950. The court emphasized that a decision should be made within 24 hours of receiving the order, considering the potential festival dates of May 27 or 28.  The petitioners argued for an exemption based on religious practices and claimed the Act's provisions allow for such relaxation, while opposing lawyers maintained that the notification issued on May 13th was in accordance with existing laws and previous court rulings. The court also urged the state to assess its capacity to issue necessary certificates and ensure proper infrastructure for animal slaughter.

articles.title: Honasa Consumer Q4 results: Profit more than doubles to Rs 69 cr; co declares Rs 3 dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 682 crore in Q4 FY26, driven by strong growth across key categories and a robust offline distribution network. The company's EBITDA reached Rs 77 crore, marking its highest-ever quarterly operating profit.  Honasa Consumer also announced a maiden final dividend of Rs 3 per equity share, representing 51.2% of FY26 standalone profit after tax. Chairman and CEO Varun Alagh attributed the company's success to investments in AI-led content systems, research and development, product innovation, and distribution infrastructure.

articles.title: Quadcopter attack kills two schoolchildren in KP's Bajaur - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Two schoolchildren were killed in a drone strike in Bajaur district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The incident occurred near Khar and the children were returning home from school when they were struck by the quadcopter. Dr Hamidur Rehman, a PTI MPA, and Sahibzada Haroon Rashid, the chief of the Bajaur Aman Jirga, condemned the attack. Local police launched an investigation into the incident to determine responsibility and motive.

articles.title: Charges dismissed against official at school where 6-year-old shot teacher
articles.rephrased_article: Ebony Parker, former assistant principal at a Virginia elementary school, has been cleared of all charges against her stemming from the shooting incident in January 2023. Judge Rebecca Robinson dismissed eight felony counts, including disregard for life, after the defense argued that the state had not presented sufficient evidence to prove their case. The six-year-old student who fired a single shot at teacher Abigail Zwerner, who suffered injuries requiring surgery, is being cared for by his mother, Deja Taylor.

articles.title: WiseTech begins redundancies – but omits ‘AI’ from emails to Chinese employees, workers say | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: WiseTech, an Australian Stock Exchange-listed company, is laying off approximately 2,000 employees globally due to advancements in artificial intelligence. The redundancies began in South Korea and Mexico and will continue in other countries including Australia next week.  The company's communication regarding the layoffs has been inconsistent, with internal emails referencing "global transformation" instead of "AI" in some cases. Zubin Appoo, CEO of WiseTech, claims that different legal requirements necessitate varying language across jurisdictions. Employees are expressing concern over the lack of transparency and clarity surrounding the layoff process, leading to low morale and anxiety among those awaiting their fate.

articles.title: Arteta ‘built a fire’ instead of watching Arsenal’s Premier League crowning | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mikel Arteta chose to stay home instead of watching Arsenal's Premier League victory over Manchester City on Sunday.  He was at his training center in London Colney but opted for a barbecue and gardening session instead, discovering the news from his eldest son. The team celebrated their first league title in 22 years with dancing and chanting after confirmation of their win. Arteta admitted to doubts about leading them to victory during the challenging season.  He will lead the team to lift the trophy at Crystal Palace on Sunday.

articles.title: I am from India but none of my firm partners is Indian: Attorney Rahul Reddy counters hate on social media - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Reddy, an immigration attorney, and Emily Neumann, a partner at his firm, the Reddy-Neumann Brown PC, addressed concerns about the "Indians only hire Indians" narrative circulating on social media. They emphasized that while fraud exists within the H-1B program, it does not represent the entire process or all individuals involved.  Dr. Sean Wang, a Chinese-American assistant professor, also filed a lawsuit against Southern Methodist University, alleging preferential treatment of Indian employees by head of the department Dr. Hemang Desai.

articles.title: Russia’s Sechenov University assigns ‘Visiting Professor’ status to Basappa Salundi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sechenov First Moscow State Medical (SMSM) University in Russia has appointed Basappa Salundi, chairman of the Department of Organic Chemistry at the University of Mysore, as a 'Visiting Professor'. This honorary title, established in 2025, does not involve formal employment or salary and is awarded to recognized external specialists. The university hopes this will enhance its prestige and competitiveness by attracting leading scientists who can facilitate increased publications and international grants.

articles.title: Sebi proposes changes to pre-open listing session of IPOs for better price discovery - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has released a consultation paper seeking public feedback on proposed changes to the Call Auction Session framework used for relisted stocks. The regulator cited concerns that the current system, which uses dummy price bands and base price calculations, is leading to artificial price suppression and persistent buying pressure once trading begins. Sebi wants to understand if these mechanisms need modification to improve efficiency and reduce distortions in price discovery.  The consultation paper outlines how equilibrium prices are determined during the pre-open session for IPOs and relisted stocks.

articles.title: Israel deports all foreign Gaza flotilla activists - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel deported all foreign activists seized during a Gaza-bound flotilla after global outcry over their treatment. The Israeli government stated it would not allow breaches of the naval blockade on Gaza.  Human rights groups, including Adalah, confirmed the release of detainees from Israeli custody and reported that many were being transferred to Ramon Airport for deportation.  The activists' detention sparked condemnation from governments worldwide, including those of Italy, Spain, Australia, and Canada. The Foreign Office in Islamabad also condemned Israel's interception of the flotilla and the mistreatment of humanitarian workers.

articles.title: Air France and Airbus found guilty of manslaughter over 2009 plane crash
articles.rephrased_article: The Air France and Airbus have been found guilty of manslaughter in the 2009 crash of flight AF447, which killed 228 people. The Paris Appeals Court ruled that the airline and aircraft manufacturer were solely responsible for the incident, citing a combination of technical failure and pilot error.  The companies have been fined €225,000 each but some victims' families criticized the amount as insufficient. Airbus has announced it will appeal the verdict while Air France expressed its acknowledgement of the judgment.

articles.title: ‘It’s broken English’: MP’s attempt to speak Jamaican in parliament sparks language row | Jamaica | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Jamaican MP, Nekeisha Burchell, sparked controversy in parliament when she spoke in Jamaican Patois during her maiden speech. Juliet Holness, the speaker of the house and wife of Jamaica's prime minister, interrupted her, citing parliamentary rules requiring English language use. The incident ignited debate about the legacy of British colonialism and whether Jamaica should embrace its own language in formal settings.  Marlon Morgan, a parliamentary secretary, argued for a more thoughtful approach to any potential change in language usage within parliament, while others like Carolyn Cooper, a literary scholar, supported Burchell's intervention as a symbol of cultural confidence. The issue has sparked public debate about the legitimacy and use of Jamaican Patois in Jamaica.

articles.title: Ecuador’s Disappeared | Crime | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ecuadorian authorities are under scrutiny for the disappearance of at least 50 people detained by security forces since 2024, as investigations into forced disappearances conducted by the military during a drug war intensify.  The Ecuadorian government's crackdown on drug cartels has resulted in record killings and heightened concerns about human rights violations. The film "Disappeared Fault Lines" investigates these cases, including the disappearance of Jonathan Villon, a father of three taken by soldiers in broad daylight in December 2024, and the deaths of four boys known as the “Malvinas 4.

articles.title: Boo of Jobs: Real anger about Artificial Intelligence at US convocations - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Across the United States, commencement speakers who mention artificial intelligence are facing backlash from graduates and communities concerned about job displacement and the uneven distribution of benefits from the AI boom.  At several universities, graduates booed speakers who discussed the future of AI, expressing frustration over potential job losses and concerns about the impact of data centers on their communities. While proponents of AI highlight its potential for economic growth and innovation, critics argue that the gains are not evenly distributed and raise questions about democratic consent in the face of rapid technological change.  This growing public skepticism towards AI reflects a broader societal concern over the impact of technology on employment and social equity.

articles.title: Suo motu case against top Karnataka officials after raids expose illegal sand mining in Bagalkot - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lokayukta Police in Karnataka have registered a suo motu case against several senior government officials, including the Director of the Mines and Geology Department in Bengaluru and the Bagalkot Deputy Commissioner, for alleged large-scale illegal sand mining in the Krishna river bed. The investigation followed complaints about rampant illegal mining activities in Bagalkot district and revealed indiscriminate excavation using heavy machinery in violation of environmental norms.  The Lokayukta Police conducted raids across Bagalkot district on May 21, seizing equipment and uncovering large quantities of illegally extracted sand.  Further investigations are underway to determine the extent of the illegal activity and hold those responsible accountable.

articles.title: Over 15 MF schemes cut exposure to these 10 stocks in April ’26. Do you own any? - Stock Ideas | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mutual funds significantly reduced their holdings in 14 stocks during April 2026, a trend driven by geopolitical uncertainties and market volatility.  The analysis revealed that nearly 15 stocks saw a decrease in mutual fund exposure compared to March 2026. Notably, seven of these stocks have experienced negative returns so far in CY26, with some declines exceeding 60%.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz lauds ‘steadfast’ Pak-China friendship, says Beijing supported Islamabad in ‘unwavering fashion’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari lauded the enduring Pakistan-China friendship, emphasizing its unwavering support during challenging times.  They highlighted the significance of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) as a testament to this partnership. Cai Dafeng, representing the Chinese leadership, underscored the historical bond between the two nations, emphasizing their shared commitment to national rejuvenation and regional stability.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz: Iran steps up claim to control Middle East waterway
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has expanded its claim to control the Strait of Hormuz, asserting military oversight over more than 22,000 square kilometers. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a newly created entity by Iran, claims this authority extends into territorial waters of Oman and the UAE.  However, the US and Gulf allies have rejected these claims and continue to oppose Iranian attempts to control the strait. The US military has boarded an Iran-bound oil tanker suspected of violating the American blockade of Iranian ports. Meanwhile, diplomatic efforts are underway with Pakistan's military chief visiting Tehran to mediate peace between Iran and the US.

articles.title: Macron under pressure over reparatory justice for France’s role in slave trade | Slavery | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron is facing increasing pressure to initiate discussions on reparatory justice for France's role in the transatlantic slave trade.  The French president will mark the 25th anniversary of a 2001 law recognizing slavery as a crime against humanity, but demands are growing for formal dialogue on addressing the legacies of enslavement in French society. This comes amidst political and social unrest over racism and calls for reparations from France's former colonies, including Haiti.  Several organizations and descendants of enslaved Africans have urged Macron to take the lead in this process.

articles.title: Record number of dams dismantled in Europe in effort to help wildlife thrive | Rivers | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Iceland removed its first official dam from a river in 2025, joining other European countries in a growing trend of barrier removals. Dam Removal Europe, an environmental group coalition, found that over 600 barriers were dismantled across the continent last year, with Sweden, Finland, and Spain leading the way. The removal of these structures aims to restore natural river flow and wildlife habitats, but researchers caution about potential risks from invasive species.  The EU's nature restoration law explicitly calls for the removal of obsolete dams, as does a similar effort in the US.

articles.title: How Chinese, Iranian companies profit in Russia-occupied Ukrainian regions | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Chinese and Iranian companies are increasingly involved in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian regions, supplying goods and services despite international sanctions.  Zhongxin Heavy Industrial Machinery and Amma Construction Machinery, two Chinese companies, have supplied equipment for construction projects in occupied areas, including the Azov Sea port of Mariupol.  Moscow has encouraged these ties with Iran, which is buying grain and coal from the occupied regions and integrating its economy into Iranian logistical chains. The presence of these foreign companies underscores the economic integration of the occupied territories with Russia and China.

articles.title: Select SFBs and MFI players positioned for earnings upside: Rajiv Mehta - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rajiv Mehta, from Yes Securities, stated that while the NBFC sector faces external risks, underlying credit performance has remained stable. He highlighted microfinance and select housing finance players as attractive sub-segments within the broader financial space.  He noted strong collections in lending categories, but cautioned that macro risks remain a key monitorable. Mehta believes the strongest cyclical recovery is unfolding in microfinance and microfinance-linked small finance banks, citing renewed growth momentum in affordable housing companies. He also recommended focusing on select lenders with large microfinance portfolios, such as Ujjivan, CreditAccess Grameen, and Fusion.  While acknowledging a positive credit cycle, Mehta cautioned that macro uncertainties could delay the pace of improvement due to inflation and affordability stress.

articles.title: Autoimmune diseases higher than before; long-term effect of pesticides need to be studied: expert - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sougata Bardhan, Associate Professor at Tennessee State University, is investigating the long-term effects of pesticides and genetically modified organisms (GMOs) on human health. His research, which focuses on the "One Health" concept, suggests that existing studies on short-term impacts may not reflect the full picture.  Dr. Bardhan is collaborating with Anirban Chakraborty, Director at Nitte University Centre for Science Education and Research, to study the effects of pesticides and GMOs on zebrafish, a model organism with a four-year life cycle that shares 70% of its genetic makeup with humans.  He emphasizes the importance of sustainable agricultural practices and the use of modern technology in managing food security while advocating for local produce consumption.

articles.title: UK net migration falls below 200,000 as stricter visa rules cut arrivals | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Office for National Statistics reported that UK net migration fell below 200,000 for the first time since the Covid pandemic, reaching 171,000 in the year ending December 2025. The decline was driven by a significant drop in non-EU nationals arriving for work reasons, attributed to stricter immigration rules implemented by the UK government.  The figures also show fewer international students remaining in Britain after completing their studies and a decrease in long-term migrant arrivals.

articles.title: At breakfast meeting hosted by PM, Aga Khan expresses desire to continue cooperation with Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prince Rahim al-Hussaini Aga Khan V, the 50th spiritual leader of the Ismaili community, met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad.  The meeting focused on strengthening cooperation between Pakistan and the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN) in areas like rural development, healthcare, education, and climate adaptation.  Shehbaz Sharif expressed appreciation for AKDN's work in Pakistan, particularly in Gilgit-Baltistan and Chitral, and encouraged further collaboration. Prince Rahim al-Hussaini Aga Khan V thanked the prime minister for the warm welcome and expressed his desire to continue cooperation on human development initiatives.

articles.title: Mali jihadist attack sees dozens of vehicles burnt as Bamako blockade continues
articles.rephrased_article: Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), a jihadist group affiliated with al-Qaeda, has intensified its blockade of Mali's capital, Bamako, setting dozens of vehicles ablaze near the city. The attack, which involved burning fuel tankers, minibuses, and trucks, is aimed at suffocating the country's economy and weakening the legitimacy of the military leaders in power.  The blockade has caused shortages and price hikes for basic commodities, making it difficult for residents to access essential goods.  Gen Assimi Goïta, who seized power in 2020, has struggled to contain the insurgency despite support from Russian mercenaries. The fuel crisis also poses a significant challenge for transportation during the upcoming Islamic holiday of Eid al-Adha.

articles.title: Pauline Hanson announces Norway-inspired gas policy as she decries 25% export tax as ‘economic vandalism’ | One Nation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: One Nation leader Pauline Hanson proposed a new policy to replace the petroleum resource rent tax (PRRT) with a royalty regime and acquire equity stakes in gas ventures.  Hanson’s proposal, which she described as “not socialist”, aims to increase returns for Australian taxpayers by co-owning new projects. The plan drew criticism from industry groups like the Minerals Council of Australia and opposition parties who argue it is not suitable for a mature industry. James Paterson, a Liberal frontbencher, called the policy "borrowed from Venezuela" while Madeleine King, the resources minister, expressed concern about government investment in an already established sector.

articles.title: Canada is using its borders to police Palestine solidarity | Israel-Palestine conflict | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Canada is increasingly scrutinizing individuals critical of Israel's actions in Gaza, including scholars and speakers invited to the Muslim Association of Canada’s annual convention.  These incidents include visa revocations, interrogations at airports, and denials of entry. HonestReporting Canada, B’nai Brith Canada, and other pro-Israel groups have been actively campaigning against these individuals and events. This trend reflects a wider pattern in Western nations where governments are increasingly using immigration law, surveillance powers, and institutional pressure to silence dissent on political issues.  This raises concerns about the erosion of democratic principles and the potential for broader suppression of dissenting voices.

articles.title: GE Vernova T&D emerges as top BSE Power multibagger with 164% returns; should investors buy now? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: GE Vernova T&D India shares have surged following strong Q4FY26 earnings, reporting an 89% year-on-year jump in net profit and a 42% revenue increase. The company's robust operational momentum is attributed to factors like improved margins and healthy order inflows. Analysts at HDFC Securities and PL Capital have revised their EPS estimates upwards, maintaining a "Buy" rating on the stock with target prices of Rs 5,200 and Rs 4,650 respectively.  Despite this positive outlook, some analysts are concerned about the recent share price rally and have downgraded the stock to "Accumulate".

articles.title: CM’s appeal to kids for votes: Plea in Madras High Court seeks an inquiry by Election Commission - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: DMK, AIADMK, Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, Election Commission of India
articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition has been filed in the Madras High Court, seeking an inquiry by the Election Commission of India (ECI) into allegations of electoral malpractice during the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. The petitioner, L. Vasuki, argues that Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's appeal to children to vote for his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), constitutes "exploitation of minor children for electoral propaganda" and falls under the definition of corrupt practice.  The petition also cites a representation by the anti-corruption organization Arappor Iyakkam alleging that DMK and AIADMK members distributed cash to voters in certain constituencies. The court has sought responses from the ECI and CEO by May 29, 2026.

articles.title: Jamsetji Tata: Quote of the day by Jamsetji Tata: “Uncommon thinkers reuse what common thinkers refuse.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jamsetji Tata's quote, "Uncommon thinkers reuse what common thinkers refuse," highlights the importance of perspective in recognizing opportunities. The quote emphasizes that uncommon thinkers notice value where others see limitations and often find success by revisiting discarded ideas or overlooked possibilities. This principle applies to various aspects of life, including business, personal growth, and even societal progress. While many people focus on novelty and immediate gratification, Tata's words encourage a more curious approach, suggesting that staying open to different perspectives can lead to unexpected breakthroughs and success.

articles.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists released from Israeli prison - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Saad Edhi, grandson of late philanthropist Abdul Sattar Edhi, and other activists from around the world detained on a flotilla attempting to break Israel’s blockade of Gaza have been released from Israeli custody.  The activists, who were taken into custody after being intercepted at sea, are being deported from Ramon Airport in Israel. The Israeli government has faced condemnation for its actions, with several governments and organizations calling for the release of the detained activists.

articles.title: Gonorrhoea and syphilis hit record levels in Europe, data shows
articles.rephrased_article: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) reported record levels of gonorrhoea and syphilis in Europe during 2024, with cases surging by 303% and over doubling respectively since 2015.  Bruno Ciancio, head of the agency's Directly Transmitted and Vaccine-Preventable Diseases unit, attributed the surge to widening gaps in testing and prevention efforts. The ECDC called for urgent action to address this public health crisis, emphasizing the potential for severe complications from these infections.

articles.title: Colombia’s climate crossroads: Trumpism casts shadow over presidential battle | Colombia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Susana Muhamad, a prominent environmental activist, urged the crowd in Colombia to win the presidential election on May 31st to prevent the country from becoming aligned with Donald Trump. Gustavo Petro, the current president of Pacto Historico, is constitutionally barred from serving a second term and has selected Iván Cepeda as his successor. The upcoming election will determine whether Colombia continues its progress in environmental protection or reverts to extractivist practices favored by right-wing candidates like Paloma Valencia and Abelardo De La Espriella.  The outcome of the election is significant for Colombia's role in international climate justice, with many countries watching closely.

articles.title: Outrage over Israel’s Ben-Gvir flotilla abuse video: What we know | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s National Security Minister, released a video showing him taunting detained activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla.  The video sparked global condemnation and prompted several countries to summon Israeli ambassadors. Ben-Gvir, who leads the far-right Jewish Power party, has been criticized for his past actions, including convictions for incitement to racism and support of a banned extremist group. The activists were abducted by Israeli forces while attempting to deliver aid to Gaza.  The incident drew comparisons to the 2010 Mavi Marmara incident where Israeli commandos killed ten activists.  Activists have raised concerns about mistreatment during past interceptions, including allegations of sexual abuse and torture.  Israel’s treatment of Palestinian prisoners has also been criticized, with thousands held without charge or trial in harsh conditions.

articles.title: Ola Electric shares can crash up to 35%, warns Emkay after seeing Q4 results - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Ola Electric, led by Bhavish Aggarwal, reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 500 crore for the January-March quarter of the financial year 2026, down 42.5% from the previous year.  While the company saw some sequential volume improvement and market share gains, Emkay analysts believe Ola's recovery will be a long process due to competition from incumbents like Ather Energy and TVS Motor Company. The brokerage firm maintains its 'Sell' call for Ola Electric Mobility shares but raised its target price to Rs 25 from Rs 20.

articles.title: 5 Indians, 2 US businessmen: Inside India's call center operation that FBI shut down for fraud - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The FBI shut down a call center operation in India that defrauded hundreds of elderly victims across the US and elsewhere. Adam Young and Harrison Gevirtz, two former CEOs of a telecommunications company, Ringba, pleaded guilty to misprision of a felony for their role in enabling the scam. The investigation revealed that Indian citizens Sahil Narang, Chirag Sachdeva, Abrar Anjum, Manish Kumar, and Jagmeet Singh Virk were convicted of similar charges. The FBI is urging consumers to be aware of tech support scams and report any suspicious activity.

articles.title: Fight against terrorism will continue with 'full national resolve', asserts CDF Munir - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Asim Munir reaffirmed that Pakistan's fight against terrorism will continue until enduring peace and stability are achieved.  He made this statement at an investiture ceremony in Rawalpindi, where he conferred awards on officers and soldiers for their gallantry and service to the nation. The CDF also praised the resilience of shuhada families and the operational preparedness of Pakistan's armed forces and law enforcement agencies.

articles.title: China says US should stop 'threats' against Cuba after ex-leader charged
articles.rephrased_article: China has called on the US to cease threats against its ally, Cuba, after former Cuban leader Raúl Castro was indicted on murder charges related to the 1996 downing of two planes.  The US accuses Castro of conspiracy to kill US nationals and is seeking his extradition. China has expressed strong support for Cuba and opposes any external pressure on the island, urging the US to stop using sanctions and threats against it.

articles.title: US is ‘simply choosing not to stop’ Ebola outbreak after massive public health cuts, experts say | Ebola | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A previously undetected outbreak of the Bundibugyo variant of Ebola is spreading through parts of central Africa, with the World Health Organization (WHO) declaring a public health emergency of international concern. The US has been criticized for its withdrawal of funding and personnel from global health programs, leaving key countries like the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) vulnerable to the outbreak.  The US has also announced travel bans for noncitizens who have recently traveled to the region, but experts argue these measures are ineffective and do not address the root causes of the outbreak. The situation highlights the need for increased investment in global public health efforts to prevent and contain outbreaks like this one.

articles.title: Apollo Micro Systems shares rally 22% in 3 days after strong Q4 results. Should you buy? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Apollo Micro Systems shares surged nearly 6% to a new 52-week high on Thursday, driven by strong quarterly and annual financial performance. The defense player reported a 163% year-on-year increase in net profit for the fourth quarter of FY26, alongside a significant rise in revenue.  The company attributed its success to acquisitions, licensing agreements, and record order bookings. Analysts predict continued upward momentum for the stock, recommending fresh buying with a stop loss at Rs 340.

articles.title: Scientists turn sheep wool into a bone-healing material in a major medical breakthrough | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: King's College London scientists have developed an experimental bone-healing material made from sheep wool that could offer a sustainable alternative to collagen. The research focused on keratin, a structural protein found in wool, hair, and nails. Laboratory and animal tests showed the wool-derived material successfully supported bone regeneration and produced tissue more closely resembling healthy natural bone than conventional collagen-based scaffolds. While further testing is needed before human trials, researchers believe this sustainable source of biomaterials could revolutionize bone repair and dental reconstruction.

articles.title: Major fire at hosiery shop in Hyderabad’s Pathergatti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A major fire broke out at the Younus Hosiery Shop in the SYJ Complex, Pathergatti, Hyderabad on Thursday (May 21, 2026), prompting an extensive emergency response from the Telangana Fire Services Department.  The fire originated in the hosiery shop and spread rapidly within the commercial complex, causing panic among shop owners and nearby establishments.  Firefighters managed to contain the blaze after several hours of firefighting operations, preventing further damage. The cause of the fire is currently under investigation.

articles.title: Punjab govt imposes Section 144 around airports, PAF bases for 30 days - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab's government has implemented a 30-day ban on pigeon homing, laser light usage by businesses, and meat disposal near airports and Pakistan Air Force bases. The order, issued under Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), aims to prevent disruptions to public peace, safety, and tranquility.  The ban is effective immediately and applies within a 13km radius around all PAF bases and commercial airports in the province.

articles.title: Dublin gangland figure brings extremist views to Irish mainstream on campaign trail | Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gerry "the monk" Hutch, a prominent gangland figure, is running as an independent candidate in the Dublin Central byelection.  His campaign has been fueled by xenophobic rhetoric and hostility towards immigrants, particularly Black immigrants and Muslims. While mainstream parties disavow racism, they have adopted tougher immigration policies. Mary Lou McDonald of Sinn Féin and Micheal Martin, the current taoiseach, have both condemned Hutch's comments on immigration. The election is being held amidst a backdrop of rising prices, housing shortages, and public discontent with the government's handling of these issues.

articles.title: Watch: BBC on the ground in Cuba after US announces criminal charges against Raúl Castro
articles.rephrased_article: Raúl Castro, former Cuban leader, has been charged by the US with conspiracy to kill US nationals and other crimes related to the 1996 downing of two planes belonging to Brothers to the Rescue. The charges were announced on Wednesday, prompting condemnation from Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel, who called them "a political manoeuvre, devoid of any legal foundation."  Castro, now nearly 95 years old and a significant figure in Cuban politics, remains influential despite his age.

articles.title: DR Congo cancel World Cup training camp in Kinshasa over Ebola outbreak | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) football team has canceled a training camp and public farewell in Kinshasa due to an Ebola outbreak. The team will now proceed with their pre-tournament preparations elsewhere, as per FIFA guidance.  The World Health Organization has declared this a public health emergency of international concern, and the US CDC has issued a 30-day ban on entry for nationals from DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. Despite these restrictions, the DRC team will not be affected by the ban because they have been training in Europe. The team is scheduled to play their first World Cup game against Portugal on June 17th in Houston.

articles.title: Jubilant Foodworks shares crash 8% after Domino's India operator's Q4 results. What spooked investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jubilant FoodWorks, the operator of Domino's Pizza, reported a 66% year-on-year increase in net profit for the January-March quarter of the financial year 2026. Revenue from operations grew 19% YoY to Rs 2,499 crore during the quarter. The company recommended a dividend of Rs 1.2 per share (60%) with a face value of Rs 2 each for the financial year that ended on March 31, 2026, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. Despite temporary LPG supply constraints impacting operations, Jubilant FoodWorks managed the situation effectively and expects normalized supply in Q1FY27.  Analysts from various brokerage firms have varying opinions on the company's performance, with some maintaining a "Buy" rating while others express concerns about near-term margin pressures.

articles.title: England Free Bus Travel Scheme: Children across England to get free bus travel this August under £100 million Government Scheme | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chancellor Rachel Reeves announced a new government-backed scheme offering free bus travel for children aged five to 15 throughout England during August. The initiative, part of the "Great British Summer Savings" package, aims to ease pressure on household budgets and is estimated to cost over £100 million. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander stated that the program will allow children unlimited journeys without paying fares or registering in advance.  The scheme applies only to participating local bus operators and excludes long-distance coach services and rail travel.

articles.title: West Bengal government to detect, delete and deport illegal infiltrators, says CM Adhikari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister, announced a new policy of "detect, delete, and deport" for illegal infiltrators.  He stated that the state police will arrest those not covered under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and hand them over to the Border Security Force (BSF) for deportation. The announcement was made during an event where land was handed over to the BSF for border fencing along 27 km of the India-Bangladesh border.  The Chief Minister also emphasized the revival of district-level coordination mechanisms between the BSF, state police, and administration in bordering areas.

articles.title: Wanted terrorist ringleader among 5 militants killed in North Waziristan operation: security sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi lauded the elimination of a wanted terrorist ringleader, Kharji Umar alias Jan Mir alias Tor Saqib, in an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in North Waziristan's Spinwam area.  The operation resulted in the death of five militants, including the ringleader, who was linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and responsible for attacks on security forces and civilians. The ISPR reported a previous operation that killed 22 India-sponsored terrorists in North Waziristan.  The government has intensified counter-terrorism operations in response to a resurgence of terrorism in Pakistan, particularly in KP and Balochistan.

articles.title: EasyJet summer holiday bookings down on last year amid Iran war uncertainty | easyJet | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: easyJet, the budget airline, reported lagging summer holiday bookings due to consumer uncertainty caused by the Iran war. Kenton Jarvis, easyJet's chief executive, stated that despite fuel price increases and potential disruptions, the airline is well-positioned to manage the current environment and operate normally.  The company has hedged 72% of its fuel needs for the next six months but temporarily suspended short-term hedging due to elevated near-term fuel prices. easyJet also reported a £552m pre-tax loss for the six months to March, compared with a loss of £394m in the same period last year.

articles.title: From AI to shotguns and cheap interceptors, Ukraine is trying to drone-proof its skies
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine is intensifying its efforts to defend against Russian aerial attacks, employing a layered defense system that includes both sophisticated Western-supplied systems and homegrown solutions. The country's air defenses have been successful in intercepting a significant portion of the incoming drones and missiles, with the help of software like Sky Map, which tracks threats using radars, sensors, and AI. Ukraine has also developed its own interceptor drones, along with private companies providing additional support. Despite these advancements, challenges remain, including gaps in sophisticated missile interceptors and the persistent threat of small FPV drones. The ongoing battle for air superiority highlights the constant need for innovation and adaptation as both sides strive to gain an advantage.

articles.title: Israel pushes for war amid US ceasefire, but its options may be limited | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's political establishment is reportedly eager to restart hostilities with Iran, despite a US ceasefire.  While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces pressure from both the public and opposition leaders to resume the conflict, it is unlikely he can do so without US permission.  The recent ceasefire has proven politically costly for Netanyahu, who is facing criticism for his handling of the situation.  However, some analysts believe that Netanyahu may be motivated by a desire to secure a strategic victory and boost his chances in upcoming elections.  Ultimately, the decision to resume conflict will likely hinge on US approval.

articles.title: Mega merger incoming: Should you buy PFC, REC shares ahead of merger? Here's what analysts say - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nirmala Sitharaman, the Union Finance Minister, announced plans to restructure Power Finance Corporation (PFC) and Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) for streamlined operations. The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved a proposal where PFC acquired 52.63% of the government's holding in REC, consolidating them into a single balance sheet.  Analysts suggest investors consider staggered exposure to PFC and REC as the merger process is subject to regulatory approvals and structural adjustments. While PFC offers better visibility due to its parent status, REC presents a merger-arbitrage opportunity with higher event risk depending on the swap ratio.

articles.title: ‘Beautiful light of our family’: Three women found dead off UK Brighton Beach identified as sisters | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sussex Police have identified the three women found dead in the sea near Brighton beach on May 13 as sisters Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, from Uxbridge.  The cause of their death is currently unknown, but police are continuing to investigate. Sussex Police Chief Superintendent Adam Hays stated that officers will leave no stone unturned in the investigation.

articles.title: After State-run schools, Vande Mataram now compulsory in all Bengal madrasas - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal Directorate of Madrasa Education has mandated the singing of "Vande Mataram" during assembly prayers in all government, aided, and recognized madrasas across the state. The order, issued by the Director of Madrasa Education, states that this is effective immediately and supersedes previous practices.  This decision follows a similar mandate for state-run schools announced earlier in May.

articles.title: FO condemns mistreatment of Gaza flotilla activists following global outcry over video posted by Israeli minister - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Foreign Office of Pakistan condemned the interception and mistreatment of the Global Sumud Flotilla by Israeli occupying forces in international waters. The statement also demanded the immediate release of all detained activists, including humanitarian activist Saad Edhi, son of prominent social worker Faisal Edhi.  Pakistan called on the international community to ensure the safety and dignity of those detained and pledged to work with diplomatic missions to secure their safe return.

articles.title: ‘Peace in Europe no longer default situation’, warns Czech president Petr Pavel – Europe live | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Retired NATO general Pavel warned that peace in Europe cannot be taken for granted and called for increased European defense capabilities. He emphasized the need for faster response times, greater technological innovation, and closer collaboration between the EU and NATO to address security threats from Russia and China.  Ukraine is bolstering its defenses along its northern border with Belarus following warnings of a potential attack. Meanwhile, Poland's defense minister urged precision in drone usage by Ukraine to avoid Russian interference. Pavel also stressed the need for Europe to assume greater responsibility for its own defense, independent of US involvement.

articles.title: Sierra Leone becomes latest African country to receive deportees from US
articles.rephrased_article: Sierra Leone has become the latest African country to receive deportees from the United States, following a deal with the US government. A Boeing charter flight carrying nine West African migrants landed at Sierra Leone's international airport on Wednesday morning. The group consisted of seven men and two women, all of whom were deported from the US under President Trump's crackdown on illegal immigration.  The migrants will be housed for two weeks before being sent to their home countries in accordance with Ecowas agreements.

articles.title: Ketan Parekh Case: Sebi sends show cause notice to 6 Capital Group FPIs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi has initiated legal proceedings against Capital Group, alleging that its traders, James Vincent Cheng and Terence Tsai, leaked sensitive information about impending trades to Salgaocar, who then shared it with Ketan Parekh for front-running the market. The regulator claims that this resulted in illicit gains for those involved.  The investigation covers a period from January 1, 2021, to June 20, 2023, and Sebi alleges that Capital Group failed to maintain confidentiality regarding its trading intentions.

articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar challenges BJP leaders to travel by public transport daily - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D.K. Shivakumar, Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka, criticized BJP leaders for using public transport only for photoshoots in response to the Prime Minister's call for austerity measures. He challenged them to travel by public transport daily, questioning the sincerity of their actions.  He also addressed the Prime Minister's call to abstain from buying gold and expressed his commitment to visit Delhi when called upon by Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Charlie was about to update his will": Candace Owens sparks backlash after explosive Charlie Kirk conspiracy claims on livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens sparked controversy during a recent broadcast with accusations and conspiracy claims surrounding the late Charlie Kirk, his inner circle, and other public figures.  She repeatedly questioned the circumstances of Kirk's death and suggested hidden motives, alleging changes to end-of-life documents and possible monitoring of his communications. Owens also criticized Victor Marx, calling him "unstable" and suggesting a broader effort to divide Christians and Muslims. The episode drew criticism for lacking hard proof and fueling online debates about the validity of her claims.

articles.title: Pakistan races to prevent US-Iran escalation - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi traveled to Tehran for the second time in a week to mediate between US and Iran, hoping to revive stalled negotiations.  Trump claimed talks were in the final stages, threatening renewed hostilities if no deal is reached. Iran warned of confrontation beyond the Middle East if war resumes but insisted all paths remain open for negotiation.  Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud praised Pakistan's efforts and expressed hope for a peaceful resolution to the conflict.

articles.title: Reeves to promise free summer bus rides for children and food tariff cuts in living costs package | Economics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the chancellor, will announce a package of measures to address rising inflation caused by the Iran conflict. These include free bus rides for children aged 15 and under during August as part of the "Great British summer savings scheme" and the removal of tariffs on certain food imports. The Treasury estimates the cost of these measures at £400 million, with details about funding to be outlined on Thursday. Keir Starmer has also announced postponements to fuel duty increases and a vehicle tax holiday for lorry drivers.

articles.title: Iran war live: Tehran says no surrender to US, diplomacy ‘wiser’ than war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that diplomatic solutions remain open, while warning against coercion. Israel's far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, has faced condemnation for posting a video of himself taunting abducted Gaza aid flotilla activists. The Lebanese Health Ministry reports 3,073 deaths in Lebanon since March due to Israeli attacks.

articles.title: RBI proposes rules to let lenders disable phones for loan defaults - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed amendments to its Responsible Business Conduct Directions that would allow banks to restrict functionalities of borrowers' mobile devices only under tightly regulated conditions. The draft guidelines, effective from October 1, 2026, specify that restrictions can be imposed only after a loan becomes 90 days past due and following multiple notices to the borrower.  The RBI has also introduced stricter rules for loan recovery, including mandatory certification for recovery agents, public disclosure of empanelled agencies, and prohibitions on assigning cases while grievances remain unresolved. The draft norms also prohibit banks from accessing or storing data on borrowers' phones and impose restrictions on recovery staff conduct.

articles.title: Stray dog euthanasia: Bengaluru examining legally permissible options for ‘rabid, ill, or aggressive dogs’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru’s corporations are grappling with the Supreme Court's ruling that allows for euthanasia of "rabid, incurably ill or demonstrably dangerous" dogs. The court emphasized qualified veterinary assessments and adherence to existing animal welfare laws.  However, a lack of clear guidelines on aggression levels has raised concerns about potential misuse by civic officials. Animal rights activist Arun Prasad warns this could lead to unnecessary dog killings. Meanwhile, Nevina Kamath, a co-petitioner in a previous case regarding stray dog euthanasia, plans to file a review petition against the new ruling.

articles.title: Donald Trump Iran Strategy: 'PM's hair was on fire': Donald Trump & Netanyahu spar over Iran war's next steps in heated phone call - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu engaged in a tense phone call on Tuesday regarding efforts to revive diplomacy with Iran.  The call centered around a revised peace proposal drafted by Qatar, Pakistan, and other regional mediators, aimed at bridging gaps between Washington and Tehran. While Trump expressed hope for a deal, he also warned of potential military action if negotiations fail. Netanyahu, however, remained skeptical of negotiations and urged continued military operations against Iran to weaken its infrastructure.  Despite ongoing talks, Trump cautioned that the window for diplomacy could close quickly, leaving both sides prepared for any development.

articles.title: Pakistan responds to India at UNSC debate, says it stands exposed by terrorism and disregard for international law - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: During a UN Security Council debate on civilian protection, Pakistan responded to India’s accusations of terrorism and human rights violations by stating that India is the aggressor.  Pakistan’s representative Saima Saleem accused India of exporting terrorism, occupying Kashmir, persecuting minorities, and weaponizing water. She also refuted claims made by the Afghan Taliban, asserting that Pakistan's counter-terrorism operations targeted terrorists and their infrastructure, not civilians in Afghanistan or Pakistan. Pakistan emphasized its commitment to peace and dialogue while calling out India’s disregard for international law.

articles.title: AI will help make a Nobel prize-winning discovery within a year, says Anthropic co-founder | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic, predicts significant advancements in AI within the next few years, including a Nobel Prize-winning discovery and companies run solely by AIs generating millions in revenue. He acknowledges the potential dangers of advanced AI but believes that its development is unstoppable due to fierce competition between countries and commercial interests.  Clark urges humanity to prepare for the transformative power of AI, comparing it to the need for pandemic preparedness. Critics warn that over-reliance on current AI models could lead to "cognitive atrophy" and a weakening of human decision-making.

articles.title: US lifts sanctions on Francesca Albanese, UN expert on Palestinian rights | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of the Treasury removed sanctions against Francesca Albanese, a UN special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territory, after a federal judge ruled that the measures restricted her freedom of speech.  The decision followed a lawsuit filed by Albanese's husband and daughter who argued the sanctions were imposed as punishment for her advocacy against Israel’s human rights abuses in Gaza. President Donald Trump’s administration had accused Albanese of "biased and malicious activities" and "lawfare," including recommending arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant, but a judge found the sanctions were based on the “idea or message expressed”.

articles.title: Sensex gains 560 points, Nifty above 23,800. Key factors behind today's Dalal Street rally - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 gained significantly on Thursday, driven by a combination of factors including cooled bond yields, declining oil prices, and hopes for an Iran-US peace deal.  The Rupee strengthened against the US dollar, while global markets rallied as some vessels resumed passage through the Strait of Hormuz. However, foreign investors remained net sellers in Indian equities, raising concerns about sustained market strength.

articles.title: After High Court verdict, Hindu petitioners seek free entry for devotees at Bhojshala in Madhya Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hindu petitioners have filed applications with the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Union Culture Ministry, demanding free entry to the Bhojshala complex and the removal of "unauthorised Islamic symbols". They also requested that idols of Lord Hanuman and other Hindu deities be retrieved through a scientific excavation. The Madhya Pradesh High Court had declared the site a Vagdevi temple on May 15, quashing an earlier order allowing Muslims to offer namaz there.

articles.title: Uss Nimitz: Another military operation on cards? USS Nimitz enters Caribbean amid US-Cuba tensions - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US aircraft carrier USS Nimitz and its strike group have entered the Caribbean Sea amid escalating tensions between Washington and Havana. The deployment comes as President Donald Trump has intensified rhetoric against Cuba, hinting at possible action against the island nation. The strike group includes the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, Carrier Air Wing 17 equipped with F/A-18E Super Hornets, EA-18G Growlers and C-2A Greyhounds, along with the destroyer USS Gridley and the replenishment oiler USNS Patuxent.  The deployment follows a formal indictment of former Cuban President Raul Castro for the 1996 downing of two civilian aircraft by the exile group Brothers to the Rescue.

articles.title: Trump administration pressures Palestinian UN envoy to drop General Assembly vice presidency bid - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States threatened to revoke the visas of the Palestinian delegation to the United Nations if the Palestinian ambassador, Riyad Mansour, does not withdraw his candidacy for the vice presidency of the UN General Assembly. The State Department cable instructed US diplomats in Jerusalem to deliver this message, stating that Mansour's bid "fuels tensions" and risks undermining Trump’s Gaza peace plan. The cable also noted a previous decision by the US to waive visa sanctions for Palestinian officials assigned to the Palestinian UN mission in New York.  The State Department spokesperson declined to comment on specific cases but emphasized their commitment to obligations under the UN Headquarters Agreement.

articles.title: Australia’s unemployment rate jumps to 4.5% in ‘tentative signs labour market is buckling’ | Unemployment | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australia’s unemployment rate surged to 4.5% in April, marking the highest level in nearly four-and-a-half years, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The unexpected decline in employed individuals contributed to this increase, prompting economists to question whether the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates again.  The jobless rate remains below pre-pandemic levels but has been on an upward trajectory since late 2022, and financial markets are now factoring in a smaller chance of future interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Nvidia posts record profit of $58.3bn amid AI chip boom | Technology | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nvidia, the chip giant, reported record quarterly profit of $58.3 billion for the February-April period, driven by explosive demand for its advanced AI chips. The company's revenue surged to $81.6 billion, exceeding analysts' estimates and fueled by growth in its data-center business. Nvidia announced a $80 billion stock buyback scheme and a dividend hike, rewarding shareholders. Despite the record results, shares fell slightly after hours, reflecting high expectations for continued growth.

articles.title: Lenskart shares rise 2% after Q4 profit slips; revenue jumps 46% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Lenskart, despite a profit decline, reported strong operational growth in FY26. Revenue increased 32% to Rs 9,002 crore, driven by a 46% year-on-year rise in revenue from operations to Rs 2,516 crore.  The company conducted 23.8 million eye tests globally, with India experiencing strong same-store sales growth (SSSG) and expanding its footprint to 157 new cities. International operations also performed well, with international revenue growing 30% and EBITDA margin improving to 7%.

articles.title: T.N. Cabinet expansion LIVE: Congress set to join Tamil Nadu’s first coalition government in decades - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay is set to expand his Cabinet with the oath of office for 23 new ministers scheduled for Thursday, May 21, 2026.  The ceremony will take place at Lok Bhavan. The Congress party, which won five seats in the alliance led by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), is joining the coalition government. Thol. Thirumavalavan, leader of the VCK, and the IUML have been invited to join the Council of Ministers.

articles.title: New Mexico Substance Exposure: Mystery substance scare in New Mexico: 3 dead, first responders quarantined over toxic exposure - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Three people died and over a dozen first responders were exposed to an unidentified substance at a rural home in New Mexico. Mountainair Mayor Peter Nieto stated that authorities are investigating the substance's nature, ruling out carbon monoxide and natural gas but not yet identifying it.  The incident prompted several firefighters and EMTs to experience symptoms like nausea, vomiting, and dizziness after contact with the substance. University of New Mexico Hospital officials assessed 23 exposed individuals, most of whom were first responders who showed no symptoms. While authorities believe the substance may be transmitted through contact and not airborne, the investigation continues.

articles.title: IMF wraps up Pakistan visit following talks with authorities on reforms, budget - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) mission concluded talks with Pakistan authorities, focusing on economic developments, fiscal plans for the next financial year, and progress on reforms under its IMF-supported programs. The mission, led by Iva Petrova, discussed disruptions from the Middle East conflict, budget formulation, and ongoing reform efforts in areas like energy, state-owned enterprises, and financial sector reforms.  The authorities reaffirmed their commitment to a primary surplus target of two percent of GDP and emphasized efforts to broaden the tax base and improve fiscal management. The IMF mission also highlighted the importance of maintaining an appropriately tight monetary policy stance and building a deeper foreign exchange market.  Discussions on structural reforms and progress under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF) were also covered, with the next mission expected in the second half of 2026.

articles.title: Samsung strike on hold as workers push for AI bonus
articles.rephrased_article: Samsung Electronics reached a tentative pay agreement with its largest union, averting a planned strike that could have disrupted the global technology industry. The deal will be voted on by union members from May 22nd to 27th and includes bonuses for memory chip workers at least six times higher than those received by employees in other units. Samsung had proposed bonuses of 607% of annual salary for memory chip workers, while other employees would receive only 50% to 100%. The company's stock price rose after the agreement was reached, and the South Korean court granted an injunction to prevent a strike from disrupting operations.

articles.title: Papua New Guinea warns against fishing in New Ireland after mystery deaths of marine life | Papua New Guinea | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Papua New Guinea’s government has issued warnings to communities along the New Ireland coastline not to fish due to preliminary metal contamination in water samples. Jelta Wong, the fisheries minister, stated that initial tests detected poisonous minerals and investigations are ongoing.  The issue began in December 2025 when residents reported dead marine life, with at least 11 villages and over 1,250 people affected by illness or contaminated food and water. The seawater has a strong sulfur-like smell and appears cloudy. Ailan Awareness, an environmental organization, documented over 3,400 dead marine organisms across several species, prompting calls for urgent action from the national government.

articles.title: Ponraj seeks anticipatory bail in two cases booked for derogatory speech against TVK women wing members - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a distinguished scientist and former advisor to the President, has filed two anticipatory bail petitions in the Madras High Court, fearing arrest by Chennai and Cuddalore police for alleged derogatory speech against women supporting C. Joseph Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  He claims the allegations are false and politically motivated, arguing that he is a senior scientist with no flight risk and willing to cooperate with any investigation. The petitions will be heard by Justice R. Sakthivel on Thursday (May 21, 2026).

articles.title: Incoming Ofcom chair vows to take on ‘tech bros’ | Ofcom | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ofcom's incoming chair, Ian Cheshire, has pledged to address concerns about the regulator's perceived complacency and slowness in enforcing online safety regulations.  Cheshire emphasized his intention to scrutinize tech companies, particularly social media platforms like TikTok and YouTube, for their efforts to protect children from harmful content. He also acknowledged personal concerns about the impact of social media on under-16s and suggested Ofcom needs to be clear about its limitations in policing these platforms.  Cheshire's comments were welcomed by safety campaigners who believe this signifies a necessary shift towards more robust enforcement.

articles.title: Iran claims it coordinated passage of 26 vessels out of Hormuz in 24 hours | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claims to have coordinated the passage of 26 vessels through the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours, despite ongoing US sanctions on Iranian ports. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) has published a new map outlining a controlled maritime zone within the strait, restricting vessel transit without authorization.  The standoff between Iran and the United States over the Strait of Hormuz has significantly disrupted global energy markets and raised concerns about a potential food crisis.

articles.title: Ponraj seeks anticipatory bail in two cases booked for derogatory speech against TVK women wing members - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Ponraj, a distinguished scientist and former advisor to the President, has filed two anticipatory bail petitions in the Madras High Court against arrest by Chennai and Cuddalore police for alleged derogatory speech against women supporting C. Joseph Vijay and his party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).  He claims the allegations are false and politically motivated, asserting that he is a senior scientist with no intention of interfering with the investigation. The petitions will be heard by Justice R. Sakthivel on Thursday (May 21, 2026).

articles.title: Fed Minutes: More officials warned of rate hike scenario - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Many officials at the Federal Open Market Committee meeting last month expressed concerns about persistent inflation, prompting a debate over whether to signal an interest-rate increase.  The minutes of the April 28-29 meeting show that while some participants believed rate cuts would eventually be warranted, most favored firming up policy if inflation remained above 2%. The decision to retain the easing bias in the post-meeting statement was a closer call than at the previous meeting and could potentially be revisited.  Incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will face this challenge as he takes over from outgoing Chair Jerome Powell.

articles.title: Voters across parties believe UK net migration is rising despite sharp drop | Migration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A leading thinktank, British Future, has found that public perception of net migration in Britain is significantly misaligned with actual figures.  While government data shows a sharp decline in net migration from 944,000 to 204,000 between March 2023 and June 2025, a majority of the public believe it has increased. This gap in perception is attributed to media coverage focusing on asylum seekers and unauthorized crossings, which creates a more visceral reaction than official figures. The research highlights the political polarization surrounding immigration and suggests that addressing concerns about migration's impact on local communities may be crucial for managing public opinion.

articles.title: Chris Rabb win in Pennsylvania energises Democrats’ progressive flank | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Chris Rabb won the Pennsylvania US House primary, securing a victory that bolsters Democrats' progressive flank.  The win signifies a shift in party dynamics as Rabb, who ran on a platform of bold working-class leadership and an end to the status quo, defeated his opponents, including State Senator Sharif Street and paediatric surgeon Ala Stanford. The race is seen as a sign of hope for progressives facing challenges in primary races, particularly those critical of Washington's support for Israel.  The outcome also reflects internal strife within the Democratic party following their 2024 election loss. Rabb will likely face little opposition in the general election and represents a potential boost to Democrats' progressive wing.

articles.title: PIL plea filed against deposit of temple funds in State-owned non banking finance corporations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A public interest litigation petition challenging the previous DMK government's decision to deposit temple funds in non-banking finance corporations has been filed in the Madras High Court.  The petitioner, T.R. Ramesh of Indic Collective Trust, argues that these corporations are unsafe and unsuitable for holding temple surplus funds. The court has directed the HR&CE department to file a counter affidavit by May 27th and will hear the case for final hearing next week.

articles.title: Pakistan can buy Russian oil - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of the Treasury has issued a 30-day general licence allowing selected energy-importing nations to access Russian oil. This move aims to ease immediate supply pressures in global crude markets and provide relief to energy-vulnerable countries, including Pakistan.  However, diplomatic sources caution that Pakistan's limited technical capacity may hinder its ability to fully utilize the concession.

articles.title: Parle Industries hits upper circuit amid ‘Melody’ confusion - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parle Industries shares surged 5% on Wednesday after a social media video showed Prime Minister Narendra Modi giving a 'Melody' toffee to his Italian counterpart, Giorgia Meloni. The stock's trading volume spiked significantly, exceeding its two-week average. This is not an isolated incident; similar mix-ups have occurred in the past with companies like LG Electronics India and Tata Motors, highlighting the potential for confusion among retail investors during market volatility.

articles.title: Manchester shows biggest fall in inner-city deprivation in boost for Burnham | Economics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester has experienced the largest decline in inner-city deprivation among UK towns and cities, according to a report by the Centre for Cities.  Between 2010 and 2025, Manchester saw a 17 percentage point fall in deprivation rates, exceeding other major cities like London and Liverpool. This success is attributed to the city's devolved powers and interventionist economic policies championed by Andy Burnham, who is vying for leadership of the Labour Party.

articles.title: UK grooming case: 20 jailed for 277 years over rape and abuse of girls between 1995 and 2003 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty individuals have been sentenced to a combined 277 years in prison for their roles in a child sexual abuse investigation spanning from 1995 to 2003. Sajid Majid, Manaf Hussain, and Tariq Azam received the longest sentences, with Majid receiving 28 years for five counts of rape and three counts of indecent assault.  The Kirklees District Police described the investigation as exposing "truly appalling sexual abuse" carried out by "a large number of sexual predators." Detective Chief Inspector Rob Stevens praised the victims' courage in enduring lengthy trials.

articles.title: Boosting climate action in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The recent political mandate in Tamil Nadu arrives amidst growing climate risks, including rising heat and coastal vulnerability.  Tamil Nadu, one of India's most vulnerable states, faces challenges like sea-level rise, cyclones, heatwaves, water stress, and rapid urbanization. This transition presents an opportunity to accelerate the state's climate action response.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX unveils filing for blockbuster IPO | Elon Musk News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX, the rocket technology company founded by Elon Musk, has filed for a blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) that could value it at a record-setting $1.75 trillion.  This would make Musk the first trillionaire in history and cement SpaceX as one of the world's most valuable publicly traded companies. The IPO, expected as early as June 11th, is part of a larger trend of monumental IPOs in the technology sector, including potential offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic.  The sale would allow Musk to pursue ambitious goals like colonizing Mars and building AI data centers in space.

articles.title: Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub ruled out of upcoming ODI series against Australia - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced that opening batters Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub have been ruled out of the upcoming ODI series against Australia due to injuries. Both players are currently recovering under PCB medical supervision and will not be available for selection. The PCB wishes them a speedy recovery and looks forward to their return to competitive cricket.

articles.title: Long-term SIPs deliver consistent gains as market volatility eases over time - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A study by Whiteoak Capital found that SIP returns diverged in shorter holding periods, narrowing over longer durations.  For a three-year horizon, returns ranged from 55.6% gains to 24.6% losses, but for investments of eight years or more, all SIPs made gains and did not experience losses. Madhu Nair, CEO of Union Mutual Fund, recommends a minimum investment period of 10 years to benefit from rupee cost averaging and navigate market cycles.

articles.title: US puts pressure on Palestinian leaders to withdraw bid for UN vice-presidency role | United Nations | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US embassy in Jerusalem has issued a demarche to the Palestinian Authority, urging them to withdraw their bid for a vice-presidency position at the UN general assembly. The US government is concerned that the candidacy could allow Palestinians to chair high-profile debates on the Middle East and undermine President Trump's Comprehensive Plan for Gaza reconstruction.  The US has threatened consequences if the Palestinian delegation does not comply, including potential visa revocation and withholding of tax revenue owed by Israel to the Palestinian Authority.

articles.title: Was Nina Lin arrested? Twitch streamer claims missed $4 scissors scan led to night in jail - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nina Lin, a controversial Twitch streamer, claimed she was arrested for failing to scan a pair of scissors worth $4 at a checkout.  She stated the incident occurred during a rushed checkout process and that security footage showed her missing one barcode. Lin has been accused of shoplifting in the past and faces criticism from viewers who believe this latest incident is part of a pattern of behavior. Legal commentator Andre Esquire questioned whether the situation was truly accidental, given Lin's history of similar incidents.
