articles.title: New USCIS signature rule for H-1B, Green Card: Dos and don'ts for your next immigration application
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Homeland Security has issued an interim rule that expands the authority to reject immigration benefit requests due to signature issues. The rule, effective July 10, 2026, clarifies acceptable signature formats and outlines what constitutes a deficient signature.  Immigration experts warn that even minor signature errors can lead to case delays and potential loss of filing fees. This new rule applies to all individuals seeking immigration benefits under the US framework.

articles.title: Push for public transport exposes structural gaps - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's push for public transport, particularly metro rail, has prompted politicians and bureaucrats to use such systems. However, the renewed spotlight on public transit highlights a gap between policy intent and on-ground delivery.  Years of underinvestment in mass rapid transit systems have led to stalled projects like the Hyderabad Metro’s second phase and the Multi-Modal Transport System (MMTS) network. While efforts are underway to improve connectivity and funding, challenges remain, including securing approvals for expansion and procuring new train sets. The State government is also exploring a Rapid Rail Transit System (RRTS), but its suitability for urban settings remains questioned.

articles.title: UK police brace for far-right rally and counter-demonstration - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of people gathered in London for two opposing demonstrations: a far-right rally organized by Tommy Robinson and a counter-demonstration combining pro-Palestinian and anti-fascist sentiments. The Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers to manage the events, citing concerns about potential violence and clashes between rival groups.  The Met has imposed strict conditions on both rallies, including restrictions on routes and timings, in an effort to keep attendees separated. Elon Musk, owner of X (formerly Twitter), addressed a similar rally organized by Robinson last year, drawing large crowds and sparking controversy.

articles.title: Zimbabwe’s diaspora reshapes real estate and farming investment trends | Features | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zimbabwean digital influencers, Kundai Chitima and Kelvin Birioti, are influencing diaspora investment decisions through their social media content.  Their videos highlight opportunities in real estate, farming, and market trends, prompting some diaspora members to reconsider returning or investing in Zimbabwe. Nyashadzashe Nguwo, an Africa market entry advisor based in the UK, states that many individuals are relocating due to a combination of emotional and lifestyle-driven factors, including a desire to reconnect with their roots and contribute to national development.  Catherine Mutisi, a diaspora member who had previously invested in Zimbabwe, credits social media content for shifting her perspective on returning permanently. Economic pressures, such as high unemployment rates and rising living costs, continue to influence migration decisions, but the strong economic link between Zimbabwe and its diaspora remains significant, with diaspora investment playing a crucial role in various sectors.

articles.title: Toddlers among more than 50 schoolchildren kidnapped in Nigeria
articles.rephrased_article: Over 50 children, mostly toddlers aged two to five, were kidnapped from three schools in Mussa, Borno state, Nigeria. Gunmen used the children as human shields while fleeing on motorbikes, preventing security forces from responding. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and government officials have not responded to requests for comment. The incident has prompted residents to flee the area, leaving traumatized parents waiting anxiously for news about their children.

articles.title: Soldier dies after falling from horse at Royal Windsor Horse Show | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A soldier from the King’s Troop, Royal Horse Artillery died after falling from their horse at the Royal Windsor Horse Show on Friday evening.  The incident occurred after a display and despite receiving immediate medical treatment, the soldier was pronounced dead at the scene. Police are investigating the cause of death but consider it to be unexplained. The show is continuing as planned with the omission of the King’s Troop’s display.

articles.title: Israel says Hamas military chief, involved in planning October 7 attacks, killed in Gaza
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces targeted and killed Izz al-Din al-Haddad, the head of Hamas' military wing, in a Gaza City airstrike.  The IDF stated that Haddad assumed leadership after the death of Mohammed Sinwar and was involved in planning attacks against Israeli civilians and troops. The IDF also claimed to have killed two other Hamas operatives, Hamer Iyad Muhammad Almatouk and Khaled Muhammad Salem Joudeh, who were accused of infiltrating Israel during the October 7th attacks.  Haddad's death follows a series of airstrikes targeting Hamas leaders in Gaza, as both sides continue to accuse each other of ceasefire violations.

articles.title: Kamal meets Vijay, submits 6 demands Tamil film industry’s development - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kamal Haasan, founder of Makkal Needhi Maiam, met with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to discuss the development of the Tamil film industry.  Haasan presented six demands, including eliminating manual scavenging through technology and establishing village libraries and skill development centers. He also requested the abolition of local body entertain taxes on movie tickets, a strong anti-piracy team, and a state-owned OTT platform for Tamil cinema.

articles.title: Alleged drug queenpin Anmol remanded into police custody till May 22 in narcotics case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A judicial magistrate in Karachi remanded alleged drug queenpin Anmol alias Pinky into police custody until May 22nd.  She was arrested earlier this week for possession of narcotics and an unlicensed weapon, and is already facing multiple criminal charges. The police sought her physical custody in a total of 15 cases but were denied in most instances, with some being sent to judicial remand. Anmol claimed she was tortured during custody and that the police are trying to harass her in court.  The investigation into her alleged drug network is ongoing.

articles.title: Tens of thousands march in London in far-right and pro-Palestine protests | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands of people marched in central London for two separate protests on Saturday: a pro-Palestine demonstration and a far-right rally organized by Tommy Robinson.  The Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers, including reinforcements from outside the city, to manage the events. The police warned that they would adopt a "zero-tolerance approach" to hate crime and said organizers would be legally responsible for ensuring invited speakers do not break hate speech laws. Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the far-right rally as peddling hatred and division.

articles.title: Rescue diver dies during search for bodies of Italians who drowned in Maldives caves
articles.rephrased_article: Rescue diver Staff Sgt Mohamed Mahdhee died while searching for the bodies of four Italians who drowned in Maldivian caves. The five divers, part of a University of Genoa team and a boat operations manager/diving instructor, were exploring a depth of around 60m when they disappeared on Thursday. Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu visited the area to observe the search efforts.  The incident is believed to be the worst single diving accident in the nation's history. The other divers have been accounted for and are receiving assistance from the Italian Embassy in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

articles.title: Two men arrested in London after man run over by van in Birmingham | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two men were arrested in London after arriving for a protest in the capital. The arrests are related to an incident in Birmingham where a man was run over by a van on Thursday evening. West Midlands police are investigating the incident, which left a man in his 30s with a broken leg that required surgery.  The van involved in the incident has been recovered and is being examined.

articles.title: Israel’s Image Crisis: Becoming Too Big to Spin? | TV Shows | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel is intensifying its public relations efforts to counter criticism of its actions in Gaza, Lebanon, Iran, and the West Bank. The push includes a major expansion of Hasbara, digital campaigns, and media messaging aimed at reversing declining support for Israel, particularly in the US.  However, critics argue that these efforts cannot erase the reality of ongoing violence and human rights concerns.

articles.title: 'He couldn’t stop blushing': When Queen Elizabeth II smiled at Prince Harry, his reaction said everything
articles.rephrased_article: A photograph of Queen Elizabeth II smiling at Prince Harry during his military training graduation in 2006 has resurfaced, capturing the warmth of their relationship.  Royal enthusiasts have praised the image for its genuine connection between the Queen and her grandson. The photo is a reminder of the Queen's supportive nature towards her grandchildren, including encouraging them to serve the public. Prince Harry served ten years in the British Army, including two tours to Afghanistan, and founded the Invictus Games to support injured veterans.

articles.title: CJI Surya Kant clarifies ‘parasites’ remarks, says youth are pillars of country - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant issued a statement clarifying that his remarks about "attacks" on institutions were not directed at the youth but at individuals with fake or bogus degrees in professions like law and media. He stated that these individuals act as parasites by attacking institutions without any legitimate standing. The CJI maintained that he holds immense respect for India's youth and expressed pride in their potential to contribute to a developed nation.

articles.title: Andalucíans to vote in election seen as gauge of Spain’s wider political change | Spain | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming election in Andalucía, Spain's most populous region, is expected to deliver an absolute majority for the conservative People’s Party (PP) and further weaken the Socialists. Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla, the PP regional president, seeks to capitalize on scandals surrounding Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his administration.  The PP aims to portray the election as a referendum on Sánchez's leadership, while Vox is expected to gain seats. The outcome will have implications for Spain's upcoming general election next year.

articles.title: Robert Lewandowski to leave Barcelona with his ‘mission complete’ | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Robert Lewandowski announced his departure from Barcelona at the end of his contract this summer. The veteran Polish striker, who joined from Bayern Munich in 2022, helped the club to three La Liga titles, including this season's trophy, and the Copa del Rey in 2025.  He expressed gratitude for the support he received from fans and described leaving with a sense of mission accomplished. Lewandowski will play his final game at Camp Nou on Sunday against Real Betis.

articles.title: The surprising reason Joan Kroc’s record-breaking Salvation Army gift still changes lives today
articles.rephrased_article: Joan Kroc's massive donation to the Salvation Army, totaling several billion dollars, resulted in the construction of a network of community centers known as Kroc Centers across the United States.  These centers provide a wide range of services including swimming instruction, fitness classes, youth sports activities, and educational programs, fostering social interaction and community engagement. The donation transformed the Salvation Army's strategy for community engagement by enabling the construction of sustainable facilities that could operate independently from traditional charity events. This tangible legacy has had a lasting impact on communities nationwide.

articles.title: BRICS is evolving with new members; differences will take time to resolve: Brazil FM Mauro Vieira - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BRICS Foreign Ministers meeting in Delhi concluded with a detailed Chair Statement supporting Indian initiatives and the Palestinian cause, but failed to reach consensus on positions regarding the war in West Asia.  Despite disagreements, Mauro Vieira, Brazilian Foreign Minister, emphasized the continued importance of BRICS.

articles.title: Divers in Maldives resume search for Italian scuba divers who drowned in cave | Maldives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Divers in the Maldives resumed their search for the bodies of four Italian scuba divers who drowned while exploring a deep underwater cave on Friday. The Maldives presidential spokesperson, Mohamed Hussain Shareef, said eight divers took part in the operation, working in pairs, with plans to continue the mission on Saturday.  The five Italians died in the accident in Vaavu Atoll on Thursday, and their bodies were recovered except for the remaining four divers who are believed to be inside the same cave. The Italian foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, said the Italian government will do everything possible to recover the bodies of the deceased.

articles.title: Amid the fertiliser crisis, Africa has a chemical-free option: Agroecology | Agriculture | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Amidst a looming global food crisis exacerbated by the US-Israel war on Iran, African states are urged to invest in sustainable agriculture through agroecology.  International agencies are concerned about the implications for Africa, where hundreds of millions face food shortages and many countries rely heavily on food imports. The reliance on chemical fertilizers has led to high costs, debt burdens, and environmental damage.  Experts propose shifting subsidies and policy initiatives towards supporting agroecological methods that increase food production, strengthen farmer livelihoods, and provide ecosystem benefits while reducing dependence on fossil fuel-based fertilizers.

articles.title: Why Robert F. Smith’s Morehouse surprise donation mattered even more after graduation day
articles.rephrased_article: Robert F. Smith, an entrepreneur, made a significant donation of $34 million to Morehouse College in 2019, covering the student debt for the graduating class and that of their parents. The gesture resonated widely due to its impact on both students' immediate financial burdens and the broader issue of educational debt in African-American communities.  This event highlighted the significant role family debt plays in college expenses and sparked a conversation about educational equality and financial empowerment within historically black colleges and universities (HBCUs).

articles.title: KTR asks party leaders and BLAs to be alert during SIR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.T. Rama Rao, working president of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), met with Assembly Constituency in-charges to discuss electoral roll revisions and membership drives. He cautioned against potential voter suppression by Congress and BJP.  He urged party members to protect voters' rights and expose the opposing parties' policies. At a separate meeting with Sanathnagar constituency activists, KTR stated that the BJP has minimal presence in the state and their Lok Sabha election performance was an anomaly.

articles.title: Peacock ‘invasion’ of Italian seaside town ruffles feathers | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Federico Bruni, a resident of Punta Marina, Italy, finds the town's peacock population to be a charming addition.  However, some residents like Francesco and Marco are unhappy with the birds' presence due to their droppings and mating calls disrupting the peace. The peacocks have become increasingly numerous in recent years, likely due to supplementary feeding by locals during the Covid-19 pandemic.  The Ravenna city council is struggling to manage the situation, attempting to find a balance between respecting the birds' natural behavior and maintaining public order.

articles.title: Hamas confirms killing of military chief after Israeli strike - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Hamas’s armed wing chief, Ezzedine Al-Haddad, was killed in an Israeli airstrike in Gaza on Friday. The Israeli military and its intelligence agency, the Shin Bet, confirmed his death, stating he directed the planning of the October 7th massacre.  The Israeli military also claimed this is a significant operational achievement, following previous assassinations of Hamas leaders like Yahya Sinwar and Mohammed Deif. The conflict in Gaza continues with over 72,700 civilian deaths attributed to Israeli strikes since the ceasefire began in October.

articles.title: Ultra-Orthodox conscription dispute pushes Israeli government to brink | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Israeli government is facing a crisis due to the withdrawal of support from ultra-Orthodox parties, who are demanding an exemption from military conscription. The coalition has called for an early election following continued fractures over the issue.  Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government is struggling to address the demands of the ultra-Orthodox parties, with their spiritual leader calling for the dissolution of the Knesset. This situation has prompted calls for sanctions on those who refuse conscription and a potential end to benefits for religious students whose families rely on them. The Israeli military argues that recruiting ultra-Orthodox men is crucial for sustaining its operations in the region.

articles.title: Video: 8 killed, over 20 injured as freight train crashes into bus in Bangkok
articles.rephrased_article: At least eight people were killed and over 20 injured in a freight train collision with a public bus at a railway crossing in Bangkok, Thailand. Siripong Angkasakulkiat, Thailand's deputy transport minister, confirmed the deaths and said all bodies recovered were found inside the bus. The accident occurred near an airport rail link station late Saturday afternoon, with videos showing vehicles halted at the crossing before the collision.  Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

articles.title: T.N. Cabinet portfolios: CM Vijay to hold Home; Finance for Sengottaiyan; Aadhav Arjuna gets PWD - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, has announced the portfolios for his cabinet members. Vijay will oversee key departments including Home, Police, and IAS/IPS officers.  N. Anand, the deputy chief minister, will handle Rural Development and Water Resources. Other ministers have been assigned specific responsibilities in areas such as health, education, finance, and energy. The Governor has approved the recommendations.

articles.title: Freight train and bus crash kills at least eight in Bangkok
articles.rephrased_article: An accident involving a freight train and a public bus in Bangkok has resulted in the deaths of at least eight people and injuries to 25 others. The collision, which triggered a fire that engulfed the bus, prompted emergency services to respond with firefighters and rescue crews.  The fire has been contained, but teams continue to search for victims and investigate the cause of the accident.

articles.title: Arrest of Iraqi terror suspect with alleged links to Iran’s Quds Force is astonishing but not surprising | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An alleged Iraqi commander of an Iranian-backed militia group, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, has been arrested in the US on charges of orchestrating 18 terrorist attacks across Europe and Canada since the beginning of the Iran war. The complaint alleges that al-Saadi is responsible for a string of recent firebombings, an arson attack on a synagogue, and a shooting at the US consulate in Toronto, as well as a wave of attacks on Jewish targets in the UK.  Al-Saadi allegedly posted claims of responsibility for attacks on social media platforms under the name of Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia (HAYI), a group believed to be linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The arrest comes as no surprise to investigators and analysts who have long suspected Iranian involvement in these attacks.

articles.title: SIR in Telangana: Draft electoral rolls to have names of electors whose Enumeration Forms are received - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Electoral Registration Officers (ERO) in Telangana will publish draft electoral rolls on July 31, 2026, including names of all electors whose Enumeration Forms were received.  Following this, EROs will issue notices to individuals who cannot be linked or have discrepancies in their linking with the previous revision's electoral rolls. This is part of a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted for the first time since 2002 when Telangana was part of united Andhra Pradesh.

articles.title: Wembanyama’s Spurs reach Western finals, Pistons stay alive in NBA playoffs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Antonio Spurs advanced to the Western Conference Finals with a 139-109 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves, while the Detroit Pistons defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 115-94 to level their Eastern Conference semifinal series at 3-3.  Victor Wembanyama, who was ejected from game four for an elbow incident with Naz Reid, led the Spurs with 21 points and 19 rebounds. The Pistons, led by Cade Cunningham's 21 points, will face a decisive Game Seven in Detroit to advance to the next round.

articles.title: Bhojshala Case: What did the High Court decide? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh High Court ruled that the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula site is a Hindu temple, granting full worship rights. The verdict has sparked reactions from both sides and may now be appealed to the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Trump says ISIL second-in-command Abu-Bilal al-Minuki killed | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced that Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, the second-in-command of ISIL (ISIS), was killed in a joint operation by US and Nigerian forces.  The operation, which involved a meticulously planned mission, eliminated the "most active terrorist in the world" according to Trump. The US State Department designated al-Minuki as a global terrorist in 2023 for his links to ISIL, highlighting his role as a Sahel-based ISIL senior leader and part of its General Directorate of Provinces.

articles.title: Cyberabad police begin search for Bandi Bageerath in Hyderabad and Karimnagar after HC rejects pre-arrest bail plea - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyberabad police intensified their search for Bandi Bageerath, accused of sexually assaulting and emotionally manipulating a 17-year-old girl, by conducting searches at his residences in Hyderabad and Karimnagar.  Five police teams were involved in the operation, which included physical checks and surveillance efforts to track his whereabouts. The investigation is ongoing, with discussions about Bageerath surrendering to authorities before being subjected to medical examination and remanded.

articles.title: US charges alleged Iran-backed ⁠Kataib Hezbollah suspect – What we know | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Justice has arrested and charged an Iraqi national, Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, with involvement in at least 18 attacks and attempted attacks spanning the US, Canada, and Europe. The charges against al-Saadi, a senior commander of the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah, include conspiracy to provide material support to foreign terrorist organizations, conspiracy to provide material support for acts of terrorism, and provision of material support for acts of terrorism.  Al-Saadi is accused of coordinating international retaliation following the US, Israel, and Iran's military conflict in late February 2026. He appeared in a Manhattan federal court on Friday where he was hit with a six-count criminal complaint. Al-Saadi smiled throughout the hearing but did not speak and will remain jailed for the time being.

articles.title: Submerged temple emerges as Bhavanisagar Dam level drops - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bhavanisagar Dam's water level dropping to 59 ft. has revealed the dilapidated Sri Madhava Perumal Temple, which was submerged during construction in the 1940s and 1950s.  A study of inscriptions on the temple premises found it to be located at the confluence of the Bhavani and Moyar rivers, once a significant trade route connecting Kongu with Karnataka and Kerala. The site is believed to have been ruled by the Hoysalas and served as the location for a fort built by Madhava Perumal Dhandanayaka, a general appointed by King Veera Ballala III.  The temple was last visible in 2024 when the water level dropped, and fishermen report that portions of the structure become visible again at lower water levels.

articles.title: Gunmen kidnap dozens of students in Nigeria’s Borno State | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gunmen stormed a school in Borno State, Nigeria, kidnapping dozens of students. The attack, which bore the hallmark of the Boko Haram group, occurred at Mussa Primary and Junior Secondary School while classes were in session.  Local lawmaker Midala Usman Balami called the attack "heartbreaking" and urged authorities to act swiftly. This incident follows a string of similar kidnappings across Nigeria, highlighting the ongoing security challenges in the country's northeast. The community of Mussa lies near the Sambisa Forest, a longstanding stronghold of rebel fighters who have waged a campaign of violence in northeast Nigeria for over a decade.

articles.title: Manoj Jarange warns of fresh agitation over Maratha quota issue from May 30 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Manoj Jarange, a Maratha quota activist, announced an indefinite hunger strike beginning May 30th over the Maharashtra government's failure to distribute Kunbi caste certificates and implement other demands.  Jarange demanded the dissolution of the Maratha quota sub-committee and urged for a separate ministry for the Maratha and Kunbi communities. He also criticized the state government for halting the issuance of Kunbi caste certificates, claiming that officials have been instructed not to issue them. Devendra Fadnavis, the Chief Minister of Maharashtra, has been accused by Jarange of being responsible for these actions.

articles.title: Iran war day 78: Trump, Tehran signal talks as Lebanon truce extended | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that the US administration has signaled openness to new negotiations aimed at ending the war.  He also said Tehran received communication from Trump's administration indicating willingness to continue talks, and that he was open to any support – including from China. Meanwhile, Lebanon extended a ceasefire with Israel for 45 days despite renewed violence. The truce extension was facilitated by US mediation after talks in Washington.  At least 12 people were killed on Friday, including three paramedics, according to Lebanese authorities.

articles.title: PM Modi arrives in Netherlands on second leg of five-nation tour - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in the Netherlands on Friday, May 15, 2026, for a two-day visit to further strengthen bilateral cooperation. Modi met with Dutch counterpart Rob Jetten, and will also meet with King Willem-Alexander and Queen Maxima. The visit is part of a five-nation tour that includes stops in Sweden, Norway, and Italy.  The trip comes as the India-EU Free Trade Agreement has been finalized, and the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement was signed in 2025.

articles.title: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon continue despite ‘ceasefire’ extension | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a 45-day ceasefire extension agreed upon in Washington, Israel continued to bomb southern Lebanon on Saturday.  The Israeli army issued forced displacement orders for nine villages near Sidon and Nabatieh, while air strikes targeted at least five villages in the south.  Hezbollah opposes these negotiations and continues to oppose Israeli occupation of parts of Lebanon since the ceasefire took effect. The Lebanese presidency welcomed the extension but expressed concern over continued Israeli attacks.

articles.title: Rising diesel costs from Iran war strain US school budgets - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: US school districts are struggling to afford fuel costs due to soaring diesel prices since the start of the Iran war.  The price increase has forced many districts to tap emergency funds, consolidate routes, and reduce other programs. The situation is particularly challenging for districts in remote areas like Alaska and those with tight budgets, such as Yakima, Washington, where officials are facing a $213,000 annual fuel cost burden.  Some districts have found ways to mitigate the impact through alternative fuels or outsourcing transportation services, while others are grappling with the pressure of rising costs and potential service cuts.

articles.title: CBI arrests ‘mastermind’ linked to NEET-UG 2026 biology paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested a biology lecturer, Manisha Gurunath Mandhare, for her involvement in the 2026 NEET-UG paper leak case.  Mandhare, appointed by the National Testing Agency (NTA) as an expert, allegedly disclosed questions and answers from botany and zoology subjects to students through special coaching classes at her residence. The agency has arrested nine individuals in connection with the case, including a chemistry lecturer, P.V. Kulkarni, who allegedly leaked chemistry questions.  The CBI is conducting searches across the country and investigating leads related to the distribution of a "guess" paper that closely matched the actual exam paper.

articles.title: How Kansas City became unlikely 2026 World Cup hosts for the US | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kansas City, Missouri overcame significant odds to become one of 11 US venues for the 2026 World Cup. The city invested heavily in stadiums and facilities, including a "Soccer Capital of America" designation, and leveraged its unique charm to impress FIFA officials during visits.  The Kansas City Current women's team and Sporting Kansas City MLS club played key roles in promoting the sport within the region. The city also tailored its pitch to specific teams like Argentina, England, Algeria, and the Netherlands, demonstrating a deep understanding of their needs and cultural preferences.

articles.title: US CEOs follow Trump's footsteps with diplomacy in Beijing - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met in Beijing, with several US CEOs accompanying the President. These executives, including representatives from Boeing, GE Aerospace, Qualcomm, Cargill, Visa, Goldman Sachs, and Citigroup, held meetings with Chinese government officials to advance business interests. The CEOs sought regulatory approvals, lucrative purchase deals, and solutions to economic challenges in China.  Post-summit discussions included meetings between Jane Fraser of Citigroup and the chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, as well as a meeting between David Solomon of Goldman Sachs and the vice governor of the People's Bank of China.

articles.title: At least five people pardoned by Trump for Capitol attack accused of new crimes | US Capitol attack | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ryan Nichols, a former Capitol rioter pardoned by Donald Trump in January 2025, was arrested on May 11th in Texas for brandishing a handgun during a dispute.  Nichols had previously pleaded guilty to his role in the January 6th insurrection and received a prison sentence. He later announced his withdrawal from a congressional race after facing new criminal charges. Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) has documented over 30 individuals pardoned by Trump who are now accused of committing crimes after their pardons.

articles.title: ASHAs meet Kerala CM-designate V.D. Satheesan, urge him to honour pre-poll promises - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala ASHA Health Workers’ Association (KAHWA) met with V.D. Satheesan, the new Chief Minister-designate, to reiterate their demands for an increase in honorarium and retirement benefits. They expressed hope that the new government would prioritize addressing their concerns.  Satheesan assured them that he would not forget his pre-election promise of resolving their grievances.

articles.title: ‘Within hours, he was gone’: Berkshire father shares pain after son dies in meningitis outbreak
articles.rephrased_article: Lewis Waters, a 17-year-old student at The Henley College, tragically died from sepsis after contracting meningitis. His father, Sean Waters, described his son as "funny, sociable, kind-hearted" and deeply devoted to his family and friends. Two other students in Berkshire are also being treated for meningitis, prompting concerns about the disease's rapid progression and a call for wider vaccination programs among young adults. The UK Health Security Agency is investigating the cases and offering antibiotics to close contacts as a precautionary measure.

articles.title: At least eight killed, 25 injured as train hits bus in Bangkok | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: At least eight people were killed and 25 others injured when a train collided with a public bus near an airport rail link station in Bangkok. The incident occurred on Saturday afternoon, causing flames to engulf the bus and nearby vehicles. Firefighters and rescue crews responded to the scene, attempting to extricate victims from the wreckage and combat the blaze.

articles.title: At Samsung, the global AI boom has spurred a looming strike and deep divisions - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A 18-day strike at Samsung Electronics, Korea's largest chipmaker, is threatening global supply chains due to a dispute over bonus payouts.  Samsung wants to give its memory chip workers significantly higher bonuses than those in its logic chip division, which has suffered losses. The union argues that all employees should receive equal compensation and are concerned about talent drain from the foundry division. Samsung, however, maintains it needs to prioritize the memory business due to its profitability while also investing heavily in the logic chip division.  The strike could impact Samsung's operating profit by a significant amount.

articles.title: Florida tightens rules on capturing giant manta rays but stops short of full ban | Florida | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Florida's Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) voted to amend its rules, allowing the capture of threatened giant manta rays for "responsible exhibition" in the US.  The commission approved a rule that restricts the export of manta rays for international display while requiring entities seeking to exhibit them to prove an educational reason. The move comes after a viral video sparked outrage and calls for an outright ban on capturing these species. Republican Congressman Brian Mast and Democratic State Senator Jason Pizzo, along with other politicians, expressed concerns about prioritizing the captive marine animal entertainment industry over the protection of threatened species.  The FWC's decision was met with mixed reactions, with some praising it as a step forward in protecting Florida's marine wildlife while others expressed continued concern about the potential impact on these vulnerable creatures.

articles.title: Alleged murder of Aboriginal girl highlights Australia's deep inequalities
articles.rephrased_article: The death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, an Aboriginal girl from Alice Springs, has sparked national grief and outrage. The circumstances surrounding her alleged murder have brought to light deep inequalities within Australia's child protection system, particularly in remote Aboriginal communities.  Asta Hill, the mayor of Alice Springs, and Catherine Liddle, CEO of SNAICC, a peak body representing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and their families, have both acknowledged the need for systemic change.  The Northern Territory government has announced a review into its child protection system, but some Aboriginal organizations are critical of this approach, arguing that it could further marginalize already vulnerable communities. Jacinta Nampijinpa Price, Liberal Party Senator, expressed her grief and called for an "honest conversation" about the failures in child protection.  Experts suggest addressing the complex social inequalities that have been present for generations is crucial to preventing similar tragedies from occurring.

articles.title: Reble's Praying Mantis: The female rapper reshaping Indian hip-hop
articles.rephrased_article: Reble, a rapper from Meghalaya, India, has gained significant popularity with her unique blend of English and indigenous languages. Her breakout moment came with the Bollywood film *Dhurandhar*, where her music resonated with audiences.  Her latest single, "Praying Mantis," continues to generate discussion online. Reble's rise reflects a broader shift in Indian pop culture towards embracing regional artists. Despite facing criticism for her style and lyrics, she remains committed to her artistic vision and believes consistency is key to success.

articles.title: FDA turmoil deepens as top drug chief departs claiming she was fired | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) experienced a series of high-profile departures this week, including the acting drug chief, Tracy Beth Høeg, and the acting vaccines chief, Katherine Szarama. Marty Makary, who resigned on Tuesday, has been replaced by Kyle Diamantas as acting commissioner, while Michael Davis will serve as acting director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER).  The departures come amid controversy surrounding FDA decisions on vaccines, rare disease medications, staff layoffs, and low morale.

articles.title: Russia’s Putin to visit China following Trump’s trip | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin will visit China from May 19 to 20, the Kremlin announced. The trip is timed to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation signed in 2001 between the two countries.  Putin will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and discuss economic and trade cooperation. This visit follows Donald Trump’s departure from China after his first presidential trip to Beijing in almost a decade, during which he and Xi Jinping discussed several broad trade deals but made little public progress on key sticking points related to Taiwan or the US-Israel war on Iran.

articles.title: Multibaggers, mirages and market math - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: A study analyzing stock market performance found that while multi-baggers are possible, they are not a guarantee of long-term success. The probability of finding such stocks is influenced by various factors like the starting valuation and prior drawdowns. While some investors may achieve exceptional returns through skill or luck, relying solely on hunting for these rare opportunities can lead to significant losses. A more practical approach involves understanding market cycles and identifying periods where the odds are in your favor.

articles.title: PM Modi in Netherlands LIVE: Prime Minister lauds Dutch coach’s role in Indian women’s hockey success - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in the Netherlands on Friday, May 15, 2026, for a two-day visit to further strengthen bilateral ties. Mr. Modi met with his Dutch counterpart, Rob Jetten, and was welcomed by senior officials from both countries, including Rear Admiral Ludger Brummelaar. The visit marks an important juncture in the India-Netherlands relationship, which has expanded beyond traditional sectors into areas like technology, defense, and renewable energy.

articles.title: Trump's geopolitical brinkmanship has hit a wall with Iran - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's aggressive diplomatic approach toward Iran has failed to yield a negotiated settlement, despite his insistence on framing the conflict as an American victory.  Analysts suggest that Trump's blustery rhetoric and demands for unconditional surrender are undermining efforts to end the 11-week-old crisis and may even embolden Iranian leaders who view him as desperate. Trump has repeatedly threatened Iran with devastating consequences, including wiping out its civilization, while also insisting on a quick resolution despite evidence that Iran is not willing to concede. This approach, coupled with his unpredictable nature, has fueled fears of an indefinite standoff and prolonged economic disruption.  Some experts believe Trump's actions may backfire by emboldening Iran to pursue nuclear weapons development as a means of self-preservation.

articles.title: What is a 'safe death'? Mentally ill woman asks for assisted dying in Canada
articles.rephrased_article: Claire Brosseau, a 49-year-old woman with debilitating mental illness from bipolar disorder and PTSD, is seeking medically assisted dying (MAID) in Canada.  She argues that current laws are exclusionary to those with mental illness and unconstitutional. Prime Minister Mark Carney is awaiting a report from a parliamentary committee reviewing the expansion of MAID to include patients with severe, treatment-resistant mental illness. The committee has faced criticism for its composition and process, with Brosseau expressing concerns about being excluded from testifying.  The Canadian government's response to her legal challenge remains pending.

articles.title: Stateside with Kai and Carter: Stacey Abrams on why gutting of the US Voting Rights Act is ‘evil’ – podcast | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court ruled in *Louisiana v. Callais* that states cannot consider race when drawing electoral districts, sparking concerns about voter suppression and the erosion of voting rights.  Stacey Abrams, a voting rights activist and former Georgia House minority leader, discusses the impact of this decision on the upcoming midterm elections with Kai Wright on the podcast "Stateside with Kai and Carter."

articles.title: From the Nakba to Gaza’s ruins: One man’s lifetime of displacement | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Abdel Mahdi al-Wuheidi, an 85-year-old Palestinian, recounts his lifetime of displacement.  He has experienced two Nakba's: one in 1948 and another in 2023. He was forced to flee his home in Jabalia refugee camp during the latest Israeli war on Gaza, enduring multiple displacements and witnessing unprecedented destruction. Despite losing everything, he remains determined to stay in Gaza, clinging to his homeland and refusing offers of relocation.  The United Nations and other organizations have provided humanitarian aid but Abdel Mahdi al-Wuheidi believes that more needs to be done to address the ongoing crisis.

articles.title: SpaceX shareholders approve 5-for-1 stock split ahead of much-awaited IPO: Report - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX shareholders were notified of a stock value adjustment following a recent split. The company plans to list its shares on the Nasdaq as early as June 12th, aiming for a valuation of approximately $1.75 trillion and raising about $75 billion.  The stock split is expected to be completed by May 22nd.

articles.title: Meningitis outbreak sparks alarm after student dies and 2 others fall ill in Reading Area
articles.rephrased_article: UKHSA officials are investigating a meningitis outbreak in the Reading and Oxfordshire area after one student's death and two hospitalizations. The Henley College student who died, Lewis Waters, was found to have tested positive for MenB.  Authorities are working with schools and families, offering precautionary antibiotics to prevent further spread. Public health officials are urging parents, students, and schools to stay alert for symptoms such as high fever, headache, vomiting, and stiff neck, which can appear in any order and worsen rapidly. The UKHSA has reassured the public that large outbreaks remain rare but acknowledges recent clusters have raised concerns about meningitis transmission among young people.

articles.title: Census 2027: Field visits for house-listing, household data collection begin in Jharkhand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jharkhand began the first phase of its 2027 Census on May 16, 2026.  Trained enumerators will visit homes across the state's 24 districts and 32,459 villages to collect data on housing conditions, family details, and assets. The exercise, which runs until June 14, 2026, has deployed over 76,000 government officers and employees, including field trainers, enumerators, and supervisors.  Jharkhand's Directorate of Census Operations is overseeing the process.

articles.title: Karachi roads paved with good intentions but potholed with reality - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi's use of paver blocks to address its pothole problem has been met with mixed reactions. While the city government promotes them as a sustainable solution, some experts argue that they are not a long-term fix and may require more frequent maintenance than asphalt roads. The effectiveness of pavers is debated, with some residents praising their ability to withstand heavy traffic while others complain about uneven surfaces and potential safety hazards. Concerns have also been raised about the quality control of these blocks, with reports of inconsistent strength and substandard materials. While pavers offer a temporary solution for specific areas, experts suggest that reviving Pakistan's asphalt production capacity could provide a more sustainable and long-lasting alternative.

articles.title: Palestinian leaders hold rare party meeting as polls show rising discontent
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Abbas, the 90-year-old Palestinian President, was re-elected as head of Fatah at its first major conference in a decade.  The meeting comes amid rising discontent among Palestinians, with polls indicating widespread dissatisfaction and calls for Abbas' resignation. The conference aims to address these concerns and implement reforms, but critics point out internal divisions and nepotism within the party.  Despite promises of elections and unity, many Palestinians feel that Fatah has lost its way and is prioritizing its own interests over those of the Palestinian people.

articles.title: A third of Britons believe they have changed social class, survey finds | Class issues | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A survey by Attest found that over a third of Britons identify as belonging to more than one social class, with millennials most likely to do so.  The research also revealed an entrenched sensitivity about class in Britain, with nearly half of respondents feeling judged for their social standing.  Professor Dominic Abrams, director of the Centre for the Study of Group Processes at the University of Kent, believes that traditional class categorizations are less relevant now as people can move between social groups more easily. Nick Harrison, chief executive of the Sutton Trust, highlighted the link between social mobility and happiness, noting that even those who climb the social ladder may not experience equal levels of wellbeing due to factors beyond income.

articles.title: Britain is losing the ability to tell anti-Semitism from dissent | Protests | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sir Mark Rowley, the Metropolitan Police commissioner, has suggested that some pro-Palestinian demonstrations in London send a message “that feels like anti-Semitism,” raising concerns about the increasing conflation of anti-Semitism with criticism of Israel.  This trend is causing concern among Jewish communities and experts who argue that Britain needs to distinguish between hatred of Jews and political dissent. The article highlights how Palestinians are increasingly facing suppression for expressing grief and anger over the destruction of Gaza, while critics of Israeli actions face suspicion and accusations of anti-Semitism. This conflation risks reinforcing harmful stereotypes and silencing legitimate criticism of Israel's policies.

articles.title: Bitcoin slips towards $79K as higher Treasury yields and oil prices pressure trigger risk-off sentiment - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced slight declines in value over the past 24 hours, with Bitcoin falling to $79,000-$81,000 and Ethereum remaining near $2,250-$2,345.  Riya Sehgal, a research analyst at Delta Exchange, attributed the dip to broader macro-economic risk aversion. While some analysts see this as consolidation after recent gains, others believe it could signal a shift in market sentiment. Institutional activity and positive regulatory developments, including the advancement of the Clarity Act by the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, are seen as supporting factors for crypto markets.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: Over 80 dead, 246 cases reported in Ituri province; health emergency declared
articles.rephrased_article: Africa CDC has declared an Ebola outbreak in the eastern Ituri province of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with 246 cases and 80 deaths reported. The virus, confirmed in 13 of 20 samples, is believed to have originated in bats and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids. Health officials warn of a high risk of further spread due to population movement and mining activity. Africa CDC has called for joint action with neighboring countries to strengthen surveillance and response measures.

articles.title: Adhikari aide killing: CBI conducts searches at multiple locations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The CBI conducted searches at multiple locations in connection with the murder of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandrakant Rath. The agency took over the investigation from the West Bengal Police, forming a seven-member special investigation team under a DIG of Special Crime from Delhi.  Rath was shot dead on May 6th, two days after the West Bengal Assembly election results were declared. Three individuals have been arrested in connection with the case, while police believe at least eight people were involved.

articles.title: Fatima Sana to lead women’s side as PCB announces squad for T20 World Cup, Ireland tri-series - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced a 15-member squad for the upcoming ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026, including captain Fatima Sana, who will lead the team for the second consecutive tournament. The squad will participate in a tri-series featuring Ireland and the West Indies from May 28 to June 4 before traveling to England and Wales for the main event.  The Pakistan women's team will play warm-up matches against Sri Lanka and Scotland before beginning their campaign against India on June 14.

articles.title: US planning to criminally indict former Cuban leader Raúl Castro
articles.rephrased_article: The US justice department is reportedly preparing to criminally indict former Cuban leader Raúl Castro over the shooting down of two aircraft in 1996. The charges, which would need approval from a US grand jury, center on an attack by Cuban forces on planes operated by the activist-humanitarian group Brothers to the Rescue.  The potential indictment comes as part of a broader US pressure campaign against Cuba that includes sanctions and an oil blockade. While Raúl Castro, 94, stepped down as Cuban Communist Party leader in 2021, he remains a target for US officials seeking to change Cuba's communist leadership. The charges are unclear but are said to be related to the incident which occurred while Fidel Castro was president.  The potential indictment is seen as part of a pressure campaign by the US government and could have significant implications for Cuba's political landscape.

articles.title: Extra 4,000 officers in London as police brace for far-right and pro-Palestine marches – live | London | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Metropolitan police is preparing for a potentially "unprecedented" security operation with 4,000 officers deployed to manage two major demonstrations in central London. The far-right Unite the Kingdom (UTK) rally organized by Stephen Yaxley Lennon, otherwise known as Tommy Robinson, will be met with strict conditions on timings and routes, while the pro-Palestine Nakba Day march is expected to draw between 15,000 and 40,000 people.  Police have granted officers extra powers to conduct stop and search without suspicion of an offense, which will also apply to the pro-Palestine rally. The prime minister has condemned both rallies, warning that they are seeking to inflame and divide while British Jews feel unsafe in their own streets.

articles.title: Where did Eurovision go wrong? | Music News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Eurovision Song Contest, a major global entertainment event, is facing controversy due to Israel's participation.  Israel’s President Isaac Herzog, and the Israeli Broadcasting Authority (Kan) have spent significant resources promoting Israel's presence in the contest, while artists and broadcasters are boycotting it. Critics argue that Israel's actions in Gaza constitute a genocide and question the event's ability to remain apolitical.  The EBU has defended its decision, citing Kan's independence from the Israeli government, but critics point out a perceived double standard compared to Russia's ban following its invasion of Ukraine. The controversy has led to boycotts by broadcasters in several countries, including the Netherlands, Slovenia, Spain, Iceland, and Ireland, while artists like Molly Nilsson have called for a boycott until Israel is removed.  The financial impact of these boycotts is significant, with some estimates suggesting that it could remove millions of euros from the contest's funding pool.

articles.title: NEET paper leak row: Youth Congress protests in Delhi, chief Uday Bhanu Chib detained - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) staged a protest in New Delhi demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged NEET-UG question paper leaks.  Protesters, including IYC president Uday Bhanu Chib, were detained by police as they marched towards Pradhan's residence. The examination was cancelled on May 3rd and a re-test is scheduled for June 21st. The IYC accused the BJP-led government of creating a corrupt system that favors wealthy students while disadvantaging those from poor backgrounds.

articles.title: India’s gold import duty hike: A double-edged sword - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Prime Minister of India has urged citizens to voluntarily reduce gold consumption to alleviate pressure on foreign reserves and stabilize the rupee. This appeal is driven by a widening current account deficit, partly fueled by high gold imports, which surged to nearly $72 billion in FY26 despite lower volumes. While higher customs duties on gold aim to curb imports, they are unlikely to fully address India's persistent gold demand, deeply rooted in cultural traditions and festivals.  The government is exploring alternative strategies such as expanding the Gold Monetization Scheme and promoting Sovereign Gold Bonds to channel investment into formal avenues.

articles.title: Putin to visit China on May 19-20 to further strengthen 'comprehensive partnership' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin will visit China on May 19th for a two-day meeting with Xi Jinping, focusing on strengthening their strategic partnership. The trip follows Donald Trump's recent visit to Beijing, during which the two leaders discussed the Ukraine-Russia conflict and US-Iran tensions without securing breakthroughs.  The discussions will also include economic cooperation between Putin and Li Qiang.

articles.title: Josef Mengele: Switzerland finally to open secret files on Nazis' Auschwitz 'Angel of Death'
articles.rephrased_article: The Swiss Federal Intelligence Service has agreed to release long-sealed files on Josef Mengele, the notorious Nazi war criminal. The files will be released subject to conditions and requirements yet to be defined.  Historians have long sought access to the files, which contain information about Mengele's possible presence in Switzerland after World War Two, but the Swiss authorities have previously refused requests for their release.  The decision comes after years of debate and legal challenges from historians who argue that the secrecy surrounding the files fuels conspiracy theories. The files are expected to shed light on Mengele's activities during his time in Switzerland, but it remains unclear if they will reveal anything concrete about his presence or actions.

articles.title: British Palestinians feel ‘gaslit’ and unable to speak out, says leading activist | Communities | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Husseini, director of the British Palestinian Committee, expressed concern that Palestinians in the UK are facing growing hostility and fear due to a climate of anti-Palestinian sentiment. Husseini said many Palestinians feel silenced or punished for expressing their identity and activism, citing incidents of colleagues being gaslighted and families being subjected to violence in Gaza. Despite this, she highlighted the strong support from British citizens who participate in pro-Palestine marches and demonstrate against Israeli war crimes.  However, some Jewish groups are calling for stricter restrictions on these demonstrations, which Husseini rejects as a misrepresentation of peaceful protests against war and genocide.

articles.title: Aston Villa trounce Liverpool 4-2 to seal Champions League place | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Aston Villa secured a 4-2 victory over Liverpool at Villa Park, securing their place in the Champions League for next season.  Ollie Watkins scored two goals for Villa, while Virgil van Dijk netted twice for Liverpool.  The win moves Villa into fourth place with 62 points, leaving Liverpool vulnerable to being overtaken by other teams vying for a Champions League spot.

articles.title: After Donald Trump, Putin to visit China's Xi Jinping on May 19 for two days
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin will travel to China on May 19 for a two-day visit, following Donald Trump's high-profile trip to Beijing. The Kremlin stated that the meeting between Putin and Xi Jinping will focus on strengthening their comprehensive partnership and strategic cooperation, as well as discussing key international and regional issues.  The visit comes amid ongoing tensions over Taiwan, trade ties, and the Ukraine conflict, with both sides seeking a more stable relationship despite major differences.

articles.title: Kerala politics LIVE: All eyes on Congress equations in Satheesan’s home turf ahead of Cabinet formation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, the newly designated Chief Minister-designate of the United Democratic Front (UDF), has sparked speculation about potential Cabinet appointments in his stronghold of Ernakulam.  The UDF leadership met in Thiruvananthapuram on May 15th to discuss the new government's formation but did not make any final decisions regarding ministerial positions. The AICC general secretary K.C. Venugopal assured that differences among senior Congress leaders would be resolved amicably, paving the way for a smooth Cabinet selection process.

articles.title: Eternal, HDFC Bank among 10 stocks which saw highest DII buying in Q4. How many do you own? - DII Buying | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) significantly increased their holdings in several large-cap stocks during the March 2026 quarter, despite market pressure. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Infosys, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bharti Airtel, Reliance Industries, Maruti Suzuki India, Tata Consultancy Services and InterGlobe Aviation were among the top stocks purchased by DIIs.  The cumulative buying value reached thousands of crores, with some stocks experiencing significant declines in share prices during the quarter.

articles.title: Naqvi discusses cooperation in counter-terrorism, cybercrime with delegation from Egypt - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mohsin Naqvi, Pakistan's Interior Minister, met with a delegation from Egypt's Ministry of the Interior, led by Major General Magdy Helal, to discuss enhancing cooperation in security and counter-terrorism. The two sides agreed to strengthen collaboration between their interior ministries, including joint training programs at police academies.  Naqvi stated that practical steps would be taken to further strengthen bilateral relations, with a Pakistani delegation visiting Egypt soon to explore new opportunities for cooperation.

articles.title: Man killed by 13ft great white shark in Western Australia
articles.rephrased_article: A 38-year-old man was killed by a 13ft great white shark at Horseshoe Reef near Perth, Western Australia. The Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development urged the public to take additional caution in the area following the attack. This is the first fatal incident in Western Australia since March 2022.

articles.title: Record numbers of UK renters crowdfunding to cover bills | Social exclusion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: GoFundMe reported a record number of rent-related fundraisers in April, with donations increasing by 60% since 2022.  People like Andrew Foster, who was forced to move due to rising rent costs, and Nick Jardine, whose family faced eviction, turned to crowdfunding for financial assistance. These individuals are part of a growing trend of people seeking help from the platform as housing costs continue to rise, leading to record numbers of families applying for discretionary housing payments.  The surge in fundraising highlights the challenges many face in meeting their rent and household bills.

articles.title: Man killed in great white shark attack in western Australia | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A 38-year-old man was killed in a shark attack near Horseshoe Reef, a popular diving and fishing spot off Rottnest Island, western Australia.  The Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development confirmed the shark was a long great white measuring four meters. This marks the first fatal shark attack in Western Australia since last March.

articles.title: BBC’s 72-year Commonwealth Games era ends as Channel 5 secures Glasgow 2026 highlights deal
articles.rephrased_article: Channel 5 has secured the rights to air daily highlights from the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games after a sublicensing agreement with TNT Sports. This decision marks the end of the BBC's 72-year relationship with the multi-sport event, reflecting a shift in UK sports media and the broadcaster's financial struggles.  The move comes as Channel 5 expands its sports portfolio and TNT Sports secures major Olympic and multi-sport properties. The Glasgow Games are facing uncertainty but organizers hope to revive interest after years of challenges.

articles.title: UN event highlights India-Oman maritime ties through maiden voyage of stitched sail vessel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Navy's traditional stitched sail vessel, INSV Kaundinya, embarked on its maiden voyage from Porbandar to Muscat. The event, organized by the Permanent Mission of India to the UN and the Oman Mission to the UN, highlighted centuries-old maritime traditions and cooperation amidst global shipping disruptions.  Indian Navy Commodore Amit Srivastava, Commander Vikas Sheoran who skippered the vessel, and Expedition Officer Commander Y. Hemant Kumar attended the event. The voyage underscores India's ancient maritime trade routes connecting India with the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa, while Oman's Permanent Representative to the UN Omar Said Omar Alkathiri emphasized the shared history and the importance of cooperation in ocean governance.

articles.title: 10 equity mutual funds cross Rs 60,000 crore AUM; top 3 manage over Rs 1 lakh crore each - Prestigious list | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parag Parikh Flexi Cap Fund, the largest active fund and flexi cap fund based on assets managed, held over Rs 1.40 lakh crore in AUM as of April 30, 2026.  HDFC Mutual Fund's HDFC Balanced Advantage Fund, HDFC Flexi Cap Fund, and HDFC Mid Cap Fund also saw significant growth, with their AUM reaching Rs 1.05 lakh crore, Rs 1 lakh crore, and Rs 94,744 crore respectively.  Other notable funds included SBI Equity Hybrid Fund, ICICI Pru Large Cap Fund, Nippon India Small Cap Fund, ICICI Pru Balanced Advantage Fund, and Kotak Mutual Fund's Kotak Arbitrage Fund and Kotak Midcap Fund.

articles.title: Sindh lifts curbs on market timings; minister says step taken to facilitate businesses, citizens - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sharjeel Memon, Sindh Senior Minister, announced the exemption of shops, markets, malls, hotels, restaurants, wedding halls and marquees from fixed closing timings to support businesses and citizens.  The decision comes after the Sindh government previously enforced a 9pm closing time last month as part of austerity measures amid the Middle East conflict. This follows similar decisions by Punjab and federal governments to adjust market closure times in response to energy conservation concerns.

articles.title: Senior IS leader killed by US and Nigerian forces
articles.rephrased_article: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria confirmed the death of a senior Islamic State (IS) leader, Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, in a joint operation with the US.  The operation was announced by US President Donald Trump, who described al-Minuki as the "second in command of ISIS globally". The killing is considered a significant setback for IS following the death of its leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi in 2019.  Nigerian Military officials stated that al-Minuki was killed along with several lieutenants during a strike on his compound in the Lake Chad Basin, and linked him to various terrorist activities including the 2018 Dapchi schoolgirls kidnapping. Trump praised the partnership between the US and Nigeria, emphasizing that al-Minuki will no longer terrorize Africa or target Americans.

articles.title: ‘Why are we even doing this?’ The week that left Britain’s PM looking like an interim leader | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following a tumultuous week, Keir Starmer remains in office as the Labour Party grapples with internal challenges.  While some MPs have called for his resignation, including Steve Reed, and others have expressed support for potential successors like Andy Burnham, no formal challenge has been launched. The party's national executive committee is expected to allow Burnham to stand in a byelection, potentially paving the way for him to challenge Starmer.  Despite calls for his departure, Starmer insists he will contest any challenge and remains confident in the party's ability to win the next election.

articles.title: LHC upholds widows’ right to interest on delayed insurance payments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.sentiment_target: State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court upheld the right of widows and legal heirs of deceased policyholders to receive statutory interest on delayed group insurance payments from State Life Insurance Corporation of Pakistan. The court rejected the corporation's arguments that Section 47B of the Insurance Act, 1938 was no longer enforceable due to Islamic injunctions. Justice Raheel Kamran dismissed all four appeals filed by the corporation and ordered the payment of statutory interest at a rate five percent higher than the prevailing bank rate from the date of death of each insured person until realization of the amount.  The court also rejected objections regarding limitation and maintainability, noting that the claimants had pursued remedies in good faith despite confusion regarding the proper legal forum for insurance disputes.

articles.title: ‘An hour of abuse thrown at me’: Jeremy Corbyn on being the target of a Labour coup | Labour party leadership | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jeremy Corbyn experienced a Labour Party coup in 2016, resulting from resignations and condemnatory statements from party colleagues.  The event was fueled by a mass walkout orchestrated by Hilary Benn, his shadow foreign secretary, which led to an unprecedented 21 resignations from his shadow team. The parliamentary Labour party passed a motion of no confidence against Corbyn, but he remained defiant, stating that the decision did not change his stance as leader.  Keir Starmer has faced criticism for his handling of the situation, with some members claiming he lacks political touch and courage.

articles.title: Oil prices climb more than 3% on fears of new US-Iran combat - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brent and WTI crude oil futures surged on Friday, driven by uncertainty surrounding the fragile ceasefire in the Iran war.  Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi stated that Iran has "no trust" in the United States and is only willing to negotiate if Washington demonstrates seriousness. The U.S.-China summit failed to resolve the situation, with both sides expressing conflicting views on the future of the Strait of Hormuz.  Analysts warn of potential disruptions to oil supply as a result of the ongoing conflict and geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: Mumbai water cut: BMC warns of criminal action against electric pump users - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) in Mumbai has implemented a 10% water cut starting Friday, May 15, 2026, due to dwindling reservoir levels and potential below-normal monsoon conditions. The civic body warned of criminal action against individuals illegally using electric pumps to siphon water from pipelines.  The move is intended as a precautionary measure.

articles.title: Trump–Xi summit highlights limits of transactional diplomacy - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump’s visit to Beijing ended without a major breakthrough, highlighting the widening strategic gap between the two superpowers.  Both sides projected warmth and stability during the summit, but discussions on Iran, Taiwan, and technology revealed limited cooperation. Xi Jinping emphasized China's core national interest in Taiwan while Trump suggested easing sanctions on Chinese companies purchasing Iranian oil. Despite optimistic rhetoric, no concrete agreements were reached on trade or technology, leaving a sense of ambiguity surrounding future US-China relations.

articles.title: Down and then out in Paris and London? Why Starmer isn’t the only one with a popularity problem | Europe | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: Keir Starmer, Emmanuel Macron, Friedrich Merz
articles.rephrased_article: The popularity of Keir Starmer, Emmanuel Macron, and Friedrich Merz is low, with their approval ratings mirroring the trend seen across Europe.  Starmer, Merz, and Macron face similar challenges in terms of public perception, despite some differences in their specific circumstances. The article suggests that these leaders are struggling to navigate a complex geopolitical landscape marked by economic uncertainty, energy crises, and global turmoil. While some European leaders like Mette Frederiksen have managed to maintain popularity through strong leadership and effective policies, others face significant challenges in maintaining public support.

articles.title: Gold at over one-week low as dollar, yields climb, Middle East tensions stoke inflation - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Spot gold prices fell 2.6% to $4,527.80 per ounce on Friday, marking their lowest point since May 5th and continuing a downward trend for the week.  The dollar's strength, rising U.S. Treasury yields, and increased crude oil prices contributed to the decline. President Trump expressed frustration with Iran and China's lack of progress in resolving the conflict, further impacting gold prices.  Overall, precious metals experienced losses across the board, with silver falling 8.7% and platinum and palladium also declining.

articles.title: Vijay opposes hike in fuel prices; seeks immediate rollback - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay criticized the recent fuel price hike, arguing that it disproportionately impacts low-income individuals and businesses.  He called for an immediate rollback of the increase, citing its negative effects on vehicle rentals, inflation, and manufacturing costs in the MSME sector. Vijay emphasized the hardship this will cause for those reliant on two-wheelers and mini buses, as well as those with loans tied to vehicle operation.

articles.title: Paved with good intentions but potholed with reality - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Karachi's reliance on paver blocks for road repair is a response to chronic drainage failures, but its effectiveness remains debated. While pavers offer a temporary fix for potholes and waterlogging, their long-term viability is questioned. Concerns about uneven surfaces, durability, and maintenance costs persist despite the city government's investment in paver projects. Some residents report negative experiences with paver blocks, citing damage to vehicles and instability on motorcycles.  Experts argue that while pavers may be cheaper initially, they require frequent repairs and their lifespan can be shorter than asphalt roads. The debate over the best solution for Karachi's road infrastructure highlights the city's need for a comprehensive approach that addresses drainage issues alongside construction materials.

articles.title: UK drivers struggle to get insurance for Chinese EVs such as Jaecoo | Car insurance | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: UK insurers are hesitant to cover some Chinese-made hybrid and electric vehicles (EVs) due to limited repair data, parts supply chains, and long-term claims histories.  A study by Carwow found that half of the requests for quotes were declined, with insurance costs often being almost twice as much as similar petrol vehicles from other countries. While some insurers like Aviva offer coverage for certain models, others such as Axa and Hastings Direct have limited options or decline to provide quotes altogether.  Insurers are working to build up data on these newer models but acknowledge that insurance availability and pricing may improve as Chinese manufacturers become more established in the UK market.

articles.title: European shares log weekly losses on Iran war-linked inflation woesdrop - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The European stock market closed down 1.5% on Friday, with the DAX index in Germany experiencing the largest decline.  Rising energy prices and concerns about inflation prompted investors to price in at least two rate hikes by the end of the year from the European Central Bank. The materials sector led declines, dropping 5.1%, while semiconductor shares paused their recent rally. Political uncertainty in the UK also weighed on market sentiment.

articles.title: Fuel price hike negatively impacts economy, triggers rise in essential commodity prices: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Revanth Reddy, Telangana Chief Minister, criticized the Union Government’s decision to increase petrol and diesel prices, arguing it would negatively impact the economy and ordinary citizens. He accused the government of mismanaging the economy through “inefficient governance” and “ill-conceived policies,” claiming that the fuel price hike was a breach of public trust and a misleading tactic for electoral gains.  He demanded the immediate withdrawal of the increase.

articles.title: Bahawalpur police look for suspect linked to ‘cocaine queen’ network - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bahawalpur district and regional police are investigating Tahir Saleem, a drug trafficker allegedly linked to the cocaine trafficking ring run by Ms Anmol alias Pinki.  Police confirmed that Tahir Saleem is from Hasilpur, Bahawalpur district. He was previously arrested in Lahore for supplying narcotics to students and is suspected of working with Ms Anmol alias Pinki. The police are currently reviewing his criminal records. In a separate incident, the bodies of a mother and her three children were found axed to death in Fatehpur, Vehari district.  The husband of the deceased has been taken into custody for questioning.

articles.title: Stafford byelection tipped to swing towards LNP as danger looms for Steven Miles’ leadership of Queensland Labor | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A byelection in the Brisbane seat of Stafford is expected to favor the LNP Queensland government, potentially dealing a significant blow to former premier Steven Miles' leadership.  Political experts predict that Fiona Hammond will likely win the seat for the LNP with a predicted vote of 51-52%, despite Labor candidate Luke Richmond holding onto a narrow two-party preferred margin. The byelection outcome is considered consequential, with potential ramifications for both the Labor opposition and federal politics.

articles.title: Buyback alert! 4 stocks turning ex-record dates for share buybacks in next two weeks. Check details - Buyback Clock Ticks | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several Indian companies have announced share buyback plans, with Onward Technologies, Garware Technical Fibres, CMS Info Systems, and CyberTech Systems leading the way.  These companies will repurchase shares through tender routes on a proportionate basis, with record dates set for May 18th, May 20th, May 22nd, and May 29th respectively. The buybacks are expected to be worth a combined Rs 18 crore, Rs 110 crore, Rs 168 crore, and Rs 14.45 crore, respectively.
