articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held bilateral talks in Beijing on Thursday and Friday, marking a significant diplomatic event. The US leader was greeted with pomp and circumstance upon arrival, including a gun salute and cheering crowds.  Joining Trump were tech leaders such as Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, and Tim Cook.  The two leaders met at the Great Hall of the People, where they discussed global challenges and their ongoing relationship. Following the talks, they visited the Temple of Heaven, an ancient complex significant to Chinese history.

articles.title: One dead and two fighting for their lives after bus rolled off road in Whitsundays region | Queensland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A coach carrying 29 people rolled on the Bruce Highway in Gumlu, Queensland, resulting in one fatality and multiple critical injuries.  Emergency services responded to the scene, with eleven ambulances, two helicopters, and a Royal Flying Doctor Service plane attending. The driver escaped with minor injuries, and the road was closed in both directions. Queensland police are investigating how the crash occurred.

articles.title: HAL Q4 Results: Net profit rises 6% YoY to Rs 4,196 crore; revenue up 2% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) reported a 2% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 13,942 crore for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026.  The PSU's net profit more than doubled from the previous quarter and reached Rs 1,867 crore. HAL also saw a 7% revenue growth to Rs 33,089 crore in FY26. The company's earnings per share rose nearly 6% for the fourth quarter and over 9% for the full year. HAL shares surged after the announcement but later pared some gains.

articles.title: What is the ‘Thucydides Trap’? Why Xi Jinping brought it up during talks with Donald Trump in Beijing
articles.rephrased_article: During a meeting in Beijing, Xi Jinping of China and Donald Trump of the United States discussed the "Thucydides Trap," a theory suggesting that rising powers can lead to conflict with established ones. The phrase reflects growing concerns about the rivalry between the two countries, particularly in areas like trade, technology, and military positioning.  While some argue that the concept is outdated and overly simplistic, it highlights the anxiety surrounding the potential for escalation in US-China relations.

articles.title: India no longer a country that suffers, will strike back if Pakistan provokes us again: Rajnath Singh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh warned Pakistan against terrorism, stating that India would respond decisively if provoked again.  He highlighted the "Operation Sindoor" campaign as a strong message to Pakistan and emphasized India's zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism, citing past military actions like the 2016 surgical strikes and 2019 Balakot airstrikes. Singh also condemned the Pahalgam terror attack last year, stating that India would not tolerate attacks on its citizens.

articles.title: Russia launches hundreds more drones at Ukraine, killing three people | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a massive drone and missile attack on Ukraine, targeting Kyiv, Odesa, and surrounding areas. The attacks killed at least three people and wounded 40 others, according to Ukrainian authorities. President Zelenskyy condemned the strikes as an attempt to prolong the war and called for international support in protecting Ukraine's airspace.  Rescue operations are ongoing following a nine-storey building attack in Kyiv.  The attack comes despite efforts by US President Trump to broker a ceasefire last week, which was quickly followed by renewed drone attacks from both sides.

articles.title: Finance ministry terms report on Dar being 'handed' budget-making process 'misleading, incorrect' - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Finance refuted a report by The Express Tribune claiming that Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar had been handed the budget-making process. The ministry clarified that the prime minister formed a committee to review tax policy proposals, but this did not constitute a handover of responsibility from the Finance Division or a "sidelining" of the finance minister.  The ministry emphasized that the preparation of the federal budget remains under the leadership of the finance minister and that the committee was formed for consultation purposes on specific aspects of the budget.

articles.title: Cuba has run out of diesel and oil, energy minister says
articles.rephrased_article: Cuba's Energy Minister Vicente de la O Levy announced the country has completely run out of diesel and fuel oil, citing a US-led blockade as the primary cause for the energy crisis.  This shortage has led to widespread power outages, impacting hospitals, schools, government offices, and tourism. Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel blamed the US for the shortages while hundreds of Cubans protested against the government in Havana. The US State Department reiterated its offer of $100 million in humanitarian aid but Cuba has yet to accept it.

articles.title: Brazil’s Atlantic forest records lowest deforestation in 40 years | Brazil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Brazil’s Atlantic forest, the country's most threatened biome, recorded its lowest level of deforestation since monitoring began in 1985, with 8,658 hectares of deforestation in 2025. Environmentalists attribute this decline to a combination of public pressure, civil society mobilization, environmental policies and enforcement actions. However, the recent approval of the "devastation bill" in Brazil's congress, which weakens environmental law, poses a significant threat to this progress.  This legislation could lead to a return of deforestation levels seen under Jair Bolsonaro, who led the country to record-high deforestation rates during his 2019–2023 presidency.

articles.title: Modern antisemitism built on old Jewish stereotypes and tropes, royal commission told | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Dave Rich, the Community Security Trust’s policy director, testified before the royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion that modern-day antisemitism has evolved from traditional tropes found in documents like the Protocols of the Elders of Zion. Rich explained that these negative stereotypes about Jewish people, often rooted in historical accusations such as blood libel or claims of being Christ killers, persist today and are frequently used to justify violence against Jews. He emphasized the need for governments to define antisemitism to combat it effectively while acknowledging the complexities of determining when criticism of Israel crosses into antisemitic territory.

articles.title: Australia Lizard Population: Why Australia became home to one of the world’s largest lizard populations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Australia's long environmental history, including periods of climatic change and geographic isolation, has contributed to its high concentration of reptile species, particularly skinks.  The continent's gradual shifts between wetter and drier conditions allowed reptiles to adapt and evolve into distinct species over millions of years. This process was further enhanced by the continent's isolation from other landmasses, leading to the evolution of specialized ecological niches within diverse microhabitats. The resulting diversity is reflected in Australia's well over a thousand lizard species, with skinks forming one of the largest components of that diversity.

articles.title: Kerala CM announcement LIVE: Congress names V.D. Satheesan as Kerala CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AICC announced V.D. Satheesan as the Chief Minister designate of Kerala, ending a ten-day period of uncertainty following the May 4th election results. The announcement was made by Ajay Maken, Mukul Wasnik, and Deepa Dasmunshi at the AICC Office.  The Congress will now proceed to form the government in the state after securing the majority.

articles.title: HRCP 'deeply alarmed' at continued captivity of seafarers onboard tanker seized by Somali pirates - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) expressed alarm over the continued captivity of 10 Pakistani crew members aboard a seized oil tanker, MT Honour 25, by Somali pirates.  The HRCP demanded urgent action from the Pakistan government and international authorities to secure their release, highlighting concerns about the hostages' living conditions and expressing solidarity with families protesting for their return. The Foreign Office confirmed contact with the Somali government and stated that the ship was anchored in Puntland, a semi-autonomous region of Somalia.

articles.title: Iran’s US-bound World Cup squad given public sendoff in Tehran | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Football Federation Islamic Republic of Iran (FFIRI) organized a public send-off for its World Cup squad in Tehran, with thousands of fans cheering as the team unveiled their 2026 kit. The players made patriotic statements from a stage before departing for their training camp in Turkey, where they will prepare for their upcoming matches.  Iran’s participation in the World Cup has been challenged by concerns over potential visa issues due to the US and Israel's attacks on Iran and the IRGC's designation as a terrorist organization in both countries. FIFA is responsible for securing visas for the team, with hopes that arrangements will be made within the given timeframe.

articles.title: Hezbollah support endures in south Lebanon as ceasefire fails to stop war with Israel
articles.rephrased_article: The Israeli military continues to target Hezbollah in southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire agreement.  A recent airstrike destroyed a building where a family was sheltering, killing nine people. The attack is part of a larger conflict between Israel and Hezbollah, which began after the death of Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. While many Lebanese residents support Hezbollah as their only defense against Israeli aggression, others are critical of the group's role in the ongoing conflict and its continued possession of weapons.  The war has displaced over a million people across Lebanon, with most concentrated in southern Lebanon.

articles.title: Victorian Labor signals tougher stance on young offenders after 109 charges against 14-year-old dropped | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victorian Labor government officials stated they will "toughen consequences" for young offenders after 109 charges against a 14-year-old girl were dropped due to concerns regarding the doli incapax rule. The girl was accused of multiple offenses, including reckless conduct endangering serious injury and burglary, following a two-month crime spree earlier this year. Liberal MP David Southwick criticized the justice system's failure to hold the girl accountable for her actions, while Premier Jacinta Allan acknowledged the unacceptable behavior but did not comment on specific details of the case.

articles.title: Manufacturing exports, earnings revival and AI: Why Mukul Kochhar sees Indian market staying resilient - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kochhar, a prominent financial analyst, believes that India's fourth-quarter earnings have been strong and may signal a bottoming out of corporate profitability. He anticipates FY27 earnings estimates to remain stable or increase once the temporary impact of rising commodity prices fades.  He sees manufacturing exports as a key investment theme for the next five years, citing India's improved trade agreements and growing export competitiveness in sectors like electronics and defense manufacturing. While acknowledging concerns about AI disrupting the IT sector, Kochhar believes that India's services market will remain strong in the medium term, particularly in application-layer AI services. He advises investors to be selective in their purchases of IT stocks, favoring companies working on AI-driven solutions.

articles.title: Rhode Island: 6 lakes larger than Rhode Island in the US: Lake Huron and Lake Michigan are nearly 15 times larger | World News - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario, Lake Erie, Lake Superior
articles.rephrased_article: Rhode Island, despite being the smallest state in the US by area, is dwarfed by several freshwater lakes within North America.  Lakes like Lake of the Woods, Lake Ontario, Lake Erie, Lake Michigan, Lake Huron, and Lake Superior are significantly larger than Rhode Island, each boasting unique characteristics and ecological importance. These lakes, with their vast size and diverse wildlife, contribute to the remarkable freshwater geography of North America.

articles.title: Vijay govt. says it needs time to ‘restructure’ Magalir Urimai Thogai programme; funds to be disbursed soon - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government announced it needs time to restructure the 'Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai' program, which provides a monthly grant of ₹1,000 to eligible women heads of families.  Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay had previously promised an increase to ₹2,500 per month under the new "Madhippumigu Magalir Thittam" program for women over 21 years old with family incomes below ₹2.5 lakh. The government stated that the May grant will be credited into beneficiaries' bank accounts soon.

articles.title: Former Indian army chief backs RSS leader's call for engaging in dialogue with Pakistan - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Gen (retired) Manoj Naravane and Dattatreya Hosabale, the secretary general of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), have both called for maintaining dialogue between India and Pakistan.  Hosabale emphasized the importance of people-to-people connections and suggested that diplomatic relations, trade, and visas should continue despite tensions. Naravane agreed, highlighting the significance of cultural ties and shared concerns among ordinary citizens. The Congress party criticized the RSS's stance, accusing it of promoting a divisive ideology and suggesting that Hosabale's remarks were influenced by his recent trip to the United States.

articles.title: Trump in China for talks with Xi Jinping | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump visited Beijing for a summit with Xi Jinping, aiming to ease tensions between the US and China. The meeting comes amid strained relations over Iran, trade, and Taiwan.  Trump expressed confidence in reaching an agreement on the Iranian issue, stating that he doesn't believe China needs to be involved. The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs welcomed Trump's visit and emphasized their commitment to cooperation with the United States.

articles.title: Rescuers search rubble of Kyiv flats after massive Russian strikes kill two
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a massive wave of strikes against Ukraine, killing two and injuring 40 in Kyiv, where rescuers are searching through the rubble of a nine-storey apartment block.  The attack followed a major assault on Wednesday, marking the third consecutive day of Ukrainian deaths as Moscow ramps up its offensive after a three-day ceasefire expired. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged allies to pressure Russia, while Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko called for strengthened air defense.  The attacks also targeted other regions including Kremenchuk, Bila Tserkva, Kharkiv, Sumy, and Odesa.  Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha condemned the attack as "barbaric" and urged US President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping to exert pressure on Putin.

articles.title: Philippines authorities investigating reports lawmaker wanted by ICC has fled after taking refuge in senate | Philippines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Philippine authorities are investigating reports that Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for his role in the "war on drugs", has left the Senate premises.  Dela Rosa had evaded arrest after dramatically outrunning government agents earlier this week and was offered protective custody by allies. The incident involved gunshots fired inside the Senate building, prompting an investigation into the shooting.  A person has been detained in connection with the incident, while Dela Rosa's lawyer claims he is still inside the Senate.

articles.title: Rohit Singhania bets on financials, telecom and healthcare for alpha generation - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rohit Singhania, fund manager at DSP Mutual Fund, advises investors to adopt a "wait and watch" approach due to rising geopolitical risks. While valuations are not yet attractive enough for aggressive investment, he believes largecaps like financials, telecom, and healthcare sectors offer potential opportunities.  However, he remains cautious on the IT sector, citing concerns over slowing demand and margin pressures. DSP Mutual Fund has revised down earnings assumptions and valuation expectations across several holdings but is not rushing to deploy capital aggressively.

articles.title: He started Dave’s Hot Chicken with $900: Years later, 19 employees became millionaires after a $1 billion deal | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Graham Walker, founder of Fibrebond Corp., reportedly shared $240 million with 540 employees following the sale to Eaton. Similarly,  Dave's Hot Chicken CEO Bill Phelps rewarded 19 employees with millions after a $1 billion investment deal by Roark Capital. This move sparked conversations about employee loyalty and how companies reward their workforce. These examples challenge traditional corporate practices that often prioritize shareholder returns over employee compensation.

articles.title: Blaze erupts after explosion at firecracker factory in M.P.'s Dewas; casualties feared - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire and explosion at an alleged illegal firecracker factory in Dewas district, Madhya Pradesh, resulted in multiple casualties. Police and administration personnel launched rescue operations after the incident, which occurred in Tonk Kalan area.  Local residents reported the factory was producing illegal fireworks.

articles.title: Xi warns Trump Taiwan issue could lead to 'conflict' as US-China summit starts - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Xi Jinping and Donald Trump met in Beijing for a superpower summit, with Xi warning of potential conflict if the Taiwan issue is mishandled.  Trump, who arrived in China calling Xi a "great leader", expressed optimism about the future of US-China relations. The two leaders discussed trade tensions, including the possibility of extending a tariff truce and addressing issues like rare earth exports, AI rivalry, and the countries' complex trade relationship.  While both sides aim to achieve positive outcomes from the summit, Trump hopes for a reciprocal visit by Xi to the US in 2026.

articles.title: Iran war day 76: Vance says progress made in talks; Israel pounds Lebanon | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Vice President JD Vance believes progress is being made in negotiations with Iran, despite President Donald Trump rejecting Tehran's latest proposal.  Meanwhile, Iran warns countries working with Israel against them will face consequences, while the UAE denies a secret visit by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.  The war continues to cast a shadow over diplomatic efforts, including a BRICS meeting and talks between Lebanon and Israel.

articles.title: DR Congo conflict: M23 and Rwanda accused of atrocities in Uvira
articles.rephrased_article: Human Rights Watch (HRW) investigators have documented widespread atrocities committed by the M23 rebel group and Rwandan soldiers during their occupation of Uvira, Democratic Republic of Congo. The report details the execution of 53 civilians, including children, through door-to-door raids, as well as eight cases of rape allegedly perpetrated by both groups. HRW also found evidence of forced recruitment, abductions, and enforced disappearances.  The organization believes these acts constitute war crimes and has called for accountability from the Rwandan government and the M23.

articles.title: Trump and Xi meet in Beijing for key summit, with trade, Iran and AI on table | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping met for a summit in Beijing, focusing on global conflict, trade, and artificial intelligence. The two leaders discussed the Middle East war, Ukraine, and the Korean peninsula during their bilateral talks.  Xi Jinping emphasized the importance of handling the Taiwan issue carefully to avoid conflicts with the US. Despite hopes for a stable trade relationship, Trump's Iran strike has cast a shadow over the summit. Both sides are expected to continue discussions on trade and other issues throughout the year.

articles.title: Last date to buy these 12 stocks for dividends, bonus issues and more. Do you own any? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SEBI’s T+1 settlement rule means investors must buy shares by today to be eligible for corporate actions. SBI, the largest lender in India, will pay a dividend of Rs 17.35 per share tomorrow. Other companies with ex-dividend dates include Anand Rathi Wealth, IEX, and several others that have set May 15 as their record date for dividends. Biogen Pharmachem Industries will issue a 1:6 bonus, while Dev Labtech Venture will go ex-record date for its 1:1 bonus and stock split.  Stocks like Steelco Gujarat and Onix Solar Energy will turn ex-record date for their rights issues tomorrow.

articles.title: J D Vance: 'Home Alone' at White House: Vance jokes as Trump visits China for key talks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vice President J D Vance compared his current situation at the White House to Macaulay Culkin in "Home Alone" due to US Secret Service protocols that prevent him from traveling abroad with President Donald Trump.  Vance, who leads the Anti-Fraud Taskforce, warned of potential federal funding cuts for state health insurance programs if states do not cooperate with the Trump administration's crackdown on fraud. President Trump is currently in China and expected to return this Saturday.

articles.title: Henley places Pakistani passport on 100th spot - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's passport has fallen to 100th place in the Henley Passport Index, with access to 30 destinations.  The ranking improved from 2021 but recently decreased due to adjustments in global visa policies. Singapore, Japan, South Korea, and the United Arab Emirates are among the top-ranked passports. The United States ranks at No 10.

articles.title: Wife of Briton pleads for Saudi Arabia to release him from ‘arbitrary detention’ | Saudi Arabia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The wife of a British national imprisoned in Saudi Arabia since 2024 for social media posts, Amaher Nour, has pleaded for his release.  The UN working group on arbitrary detention found his detention to be arbitrary and recommended his immediate release. The UK Foreign Office is supporting the man, whose health has declined, and has raised the case with Saudi counterparts. Amnesty International supports Nour's plea, highlighting the impact of the imprisonment on the family.  The UN working group concluded that al-Doush was arrested solely for social media posts and his association with a critic of the Saudi government.

articles.title: Adani Enterprises shares jump 5% after nearly 60 lakh shares worth Rs 1,435 crore change hands in block deal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Enterprises reported a net loss of Rs 221 crore for the fourth quarter, but revenue rose 20% year-on-year to Rs 32,439 crore. The company attributed this to higher depreciation charges related to newly commissioned assets, impacting profitability.  However, Adani Enterprises' core infrastructure businesses remained resilient, with EBITDA rising 3% year-on-year and a majority of its earnings now coming from mature and long-term contracted assets. Chairman Gautam Adani highlighted the company's transition into a more stable infrastructure-led business model, which positions it well for sustained cash generation and long-term value creation.

articles.title: Us Cuba Aid: US renews $100m Cuba aid offer; alleges Havana blocking ‘critical life-saving aid’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States renewed its offer of $100 million in humanitarian aid to Cuba, contingent on Havana's cooperation. The proposed package includes direct assistance and funding for internet access. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez dismissed the offer as a "lie," while Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel blamed US sanctions for the worsening energy crisis.  The diplomatic exchange comes amid severe blackouts and fuel shortages in Cuba, exacerbated by disruptions to fuel shipments following the US's actions against Venezuela.

articles.title: Punjab to include Marka-i-Haq in textbooks - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab has decided to include the four-day war between Pakistan and India, known as Marka-i-Haq, in its national curriculum and produce films about it. The decision was made during a meeting of the Information Steering Committee, chaired by Punjab Information and Culture Minister Azma Bokhari.  The meeting also requested the DG ISPR to continue visiting educational institutions for "intellectual and ideological guidance" of students.

articles.title: 50 years of Annakili: The film that launched Ilaiyaraaja’s career
articles.rephrased_article: Ilaiyaraaja, whose career was launched by the film "Annakili,"  shared a close bond with Gangai Amaran, who worked on the soundtrack and provided rhythm guitar for the movie. Amaran recalled how the high notes in the song "Annakili Unnai Theduthey" foreshadowed Ilaiyaraaja's future success.

articles.title: The secret mission to rescue the UN’s vital Palestinian refugee archive | Refugees | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (Unrwa), tasked with safeguarding historical records of Palestinian refugees, faced a complex challenge in rescuing vital archival documents from Gaza during the 2023 conflict.  After Israel's invasion, Unrwa staff risked their lives to transport archives out of Gaza, eventually reaching Jordan and then Amman for digitization. The agency now faces new challenges with Israeli restrictions on its operations in Israel and occupied Palestinian territories. Despite these obstacles, Unrwa continues efforts to digitize the documents, aiming to provide a comprehensive record of Palestinian history and displacement during the 1948 Arab-Israeli war.

articles.title: Preparing for Rupee at 100: What does it mean for the economy and your stock market investments? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian rupee reached a record low of 95.74 against the US dollar on Wednesday, driven by surging crude oil prices, foreign investor outflows, and concerns about India's external balances. VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, highlighted the worrying pace of depreciation and attributed it to sustained selling by foreign portfolio investors seeking better returns in other markets. The weakening rupee is expected to fuel imported inflation, impacting sectors like aviation, oil marketing companies, automobiles, and consumer durables. However, export-oriented businesses such as IT services, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and selected manufacturing exporters are anticipated to benefit from the currency depreciation. Analysts advise investors to focus on strong balance sheets, pricing power, and global revenue exposure while avoiding highly leveraged and import-dependent companies. The direction of crude oil prices and foreign capital flows will remain crucial in determining whether the rupee breaches the Rs 100 mark.

articles.title: Trump China Visit: 'US, China should be partners not rivals': Key takeaways from Trump and Xi's much-watched summit - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held a high-stakes meeting at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, marking Trump's first visit to China during his second presidency. Both leaders emphasized cooperation over confrontation despite tensions on trade, technology, and regional security.  Xi highlighted the importance of global stability and called for stronger bilateral ties between the two countries. Trump praised Xi's leadership and expressed optimism about a brighter future for US-China relations.

articles.title: IMF funds arrive as govt opens pre-budget talks - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has provided Pakistan with $1.3 billion in fresh inflows, boosting the country's foreign exchange reserves to near its target of $18 billion.  A visiting IMF mission began a pre-budget review focusing on revenue targets, tax measures, reforms and fiscal strategy for 2026-27. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb briefed the IMF delegation on Pakistan's macroeconomic outlook and reform priorities, emphasizing positive trends in remittances and exports while acknowledging structural economic challenges.  He also met with US Assistant Secretary of State S. Paul Kapur to discuss investment opportunities and trade relations. Aurangzeb will participate in the issuance ceremony of Pakistan's inaugural Panda bond in Beijing.

articles.title: Who is Tammy Tyrrell, the former Jacqui Lambie senator who just defected to Labor? | Tasmania | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tammy Tyrrell, the Tasmanian senator who had a falling out with Jacqui Lambie, has joined the ALP.  Tyrrell, who previously served as an independent, will now serve out her term as a government member.  Prime Minister Anthony Albanese welcomed Tyrrell's decision, praising her advocacy for Tasmanians and commitment to helping others. The move sees the Labor government increase its numbers in the Senate from 29 to 30 but still falls short of an overall majority.

articles.title: Explained: Why Balrampur Chini, Dhampur Sugar, other stocks tumbled up to 4% on Thursday - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: India's government has imposed a ban on sugar exports, effective immediately and lasting until September 30th. The restriction applies to all forms of sugar, including raw, white, and refined, and affects shipments under the ITC (HS) codes 1701 14 90 and 1701 99 90. This decision comes as domestic sugar production is expected to remain below consumption for a second consecutive year due to declining cane yields. The ban also covers exports to the European Union and the United States under tariff rate quota agreements, with shipments already in progress allowed under certain conditions.

articles.title: Hantavirus outbreak: Deadly Andes strain detected in cruise ship cases; eight cases confirmed - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organisation (WHO) reported eight confirmed cases of Andes virus infection among the passengers and crew of the cruise ship MV Hondius, with three deaths linked to the outbreak.  Two deceased individuals had confirmed Andes virus infections, while the third was classified as a probable case. The WHO stated that the public health risk remains moderate for those who were on board but low for the rest of the world. The American passenger involved in an inconclusive case is currently asymptomatic and undergoing further testing after initial positive and negative results.  Dr Stephen Kornfeld, an oncologist, was placed in a biocontainment unit at the University of Nebraska Medical Center after an inconclusive nasal swab result but has since been cleared to leave quarantine.

articles.title: UAE 'denies reports' of secret Netanyahu visit - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) denied reports of an unannounced visit by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to the country, despite Netanyahu's office claiming he met with Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE president. The UAE stated that its relations with Israel are public and not based on unofficial arrangements.  Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi criticized any collaboration between Israel and the UAE, stating it is unforgivable.

articles.title: Australians from hantavirus cruise ship to fly out of Netherlands in full PPE after plane and crew secured | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australian citizens and a New Zealand citizen aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, which is currently in the Netherlands, will be returning home after a complex international effort.  The Australian government secured an aircraft and crew for their safe transport from the Netherlands to Perth, where they will undergo a three-week quarantine at Bullsbrook facility. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade worked with national and international partners to ensure the safe return of all passengers and crew members. The outbreak has now reached 11 reported cases, with nine confirmed, and has resulted in three deaths.  The World Health Organization maintains that the threat to the general public remains low but urges caution as the virus can be serious.

articles.title: Iran war: Why the BRICS foreign ministers meeting in India matters | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The BRICS foreign ministers meeting in New Delhi, India, from May 14-15 is taking place ahead of the upcoming 18th BRICS summit. The meeting, which focuses on "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability", will discuss economic cooperation and coordinate positions on global issues, including the ongoing war on Iran. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is attending the meeting, alongside foreign ministers from Russia, South Africa, Brazil, China, and India.  The meeting comes amid an energy crisis triggered by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the US-Israel war on Iran, which has impacted BRICS members like India, China, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. The meeting is expected to set the agenda for the upcoming BRICS summit in September.

articles.title: Kaynes Technology shares plunge 19%. Why JPMorgan, Nuvama downgraded the EMS stock - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JPMorgan, Nuvama, and Morgan Stanley downgraded their ratings on Kaynes Technology after the company's Q4 results fell short of expectations. The brokerage firms cited a miss in revenue guidance, rising working capital days, and negative operating cash flow as reasons for the downgrades.  JPMorgan lowered its target price to Rs 4,000 while Nuvama cut its target to Rs 3,550, both reflecting a significant reduction from previous estimates. The analysts also noted concerns about Kaynes's working capital trajectory and profitability outlook.

articles.title: NEET-UG, 2026 paper leak: Experts call for reforms in exam process, exemption of State-government seats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors’ Association for Social Equality (DASE) general secretary G.R. Ravindranath and Indian Medical Association (IMA) former president Rajeev Jayadevan have called for compulsory registration of all medical entrance exam coaching centers, a computerised NEET exam, and exemption of state-government controlled medical seats from the single-window national system to prevent malpractices in the exam.  They also suggested free coaching centers with boarding facilities for poor students and the use of technology like encrypted questions and multi-session testing to ensure a fair and merit-based process.

articles.title: Hantavirus: After hantavirus, now norovirus? How a gut bug forced a France cruise ship into lockdown - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: French authorities lifted restrictions on the British cruise ship Ambition, after tests confirmed a gastrointestinal virus, likely norovirus, was behind an outbreak that sickened dozens of passengers. The ship, operated by Ambassador Cruise Line, had been placed under temporary lockdown in Bordeaux following concerns over a possible link to a hantavirus outbreak aboard another vessel. While the outbreak initially raised global concern due to the recent hantavirus case on the Dutch-flagged MV Hondius, health officials stated there was “no reason” to connect the two incidents.  The ship's passengers were largely from Britain and Ireland, with 1,233 people onboard.

articles.title: Xi calls for China, US to be 'partners not rivals' as high-stakes talks with Trump begin in Beijing - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met for two days of talks in Beijing.  The leaders agreed to be "partners not rivals" and emphasized the importance of a stable China-US relationship, but also discussed contentious issues like Taiwan, trade, and Iran.  Trump hopes to secure business deals with Chinese companies while addressing concerns about US sanctions on Iran and China's control over rare earth exports.  Both sides aim to stabilize their often tense relationship.

articles.title: ‘Stunned and shocked’: Ingrid Horrocks wins top prize at New Zealand’s Ockham awards for her fiction debut | New Zealand | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ingrid Horrocks, a Wellington-based poet and memoirist, won the prestigious Jann Medlicott Acorn prize for fiction at the 2026 Ockham New Zealand book awards for her debut short story collection, "All Her Lives." The book follows nine women across different life stages and generations as they navigate politics, gender, and motherhood.  Horrocks' win marks only the fifth time a short story collection has won the top prize since the awards began 58 years ago. Craig Cliff, a fiction judge, praised Horrocks' "crisp, clear, and unencumbered" writing style and her ability to tackle different perspectives of womanhood.

articles.title: NHS drugs go-ahead offers lifeline to children with rare muscle-wasting disease | Children | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) has published final draft guidance recommending that any patient with spinal muscular atrophy can receive either nusinersen or risdiplam from the NHS. Prof James Palmer, NHS England’s national medical director for specialized services, stated that these treatments offer a "phenomenal step forward" in care for children and families affected by SMA.  The drugs have been available in a limited way since 2019 and 2021 respectively. Portia Thorman, whose nine-year-old son Ezra received nusinersen, said the drug has transformed his life, allowing him to attend primary school. The NHS plans to start an "in-service evaluation" of newborn screening for SMA in October, which may pave the way for it to become part of routine care.

articles.title: Sebi plans broader use for intraday borrowing by MFs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the Securities and Exchange Board of India, has highlighted the necessity of intraday borrowing by mutual funds to address timing mismatches between outflows and receivables. This arises from the requirement to meet redemptions and other obligations before specific cut-off times, impacting fund management flexibility and potentially affecting returns.  The regulator emphasizes that without intraday borrowing, fund managers would face limitations in executing trades during the same day.

articles.title: Bengaluru: Nearly 80% land acquisition done for PRR Package 1, work order to be issued in June - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru Business Corridor Ltd. (BBC), a Special Purpose Vehicle formed to oversee the Peripheral Ring Road (PRR) project, is set to issue work orders for Package 1 between Tumakuru Road and Ballari Road in June. Civil works are anticipated to commence three months after that.  The first on-ground construction for the PRR, which has been delayed for over two decades, will begin with this package.

articles.title: Housing market in England and Wales weakening due to Iran war, say estate agents | Housing market | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Fears of rising mortgage rates and inflation due to the Middle East conflict are causing a subdued housing market in England and Wales. Estate agents report a decline in buyer inquiries and fewer homes being listed for sale, with many citing concerns about affordability and interest rate increases. The Bank of England has warned that interest rates may need to rise further as a result of inflation caused by the war.  The RICS survey also found a widening regional divide in house price growth, with stronger falls in London and the south-east while the north continues to see positive readings.

articles.title: RBI expected to hold rates in June despite rising inflation, H2 rate hike bets emerge - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: RBI economists expect the consumer price index (CPI) to rise above its forecast of 4.6% for FY27, with some predicting two rate hikes in the second half of 2026. However, most economists anticipate the central bank will maintain the status quo on rates at its June 5th meeting.  RBI has maintained a status quo since February and is expected to continue this policy until inflationary pressures rise significantly.

articles.title: Ilaiyaraaja’s trendsetter movie Annakili turns 50 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Annakili, a Tamil film released in 1975, celebrated its 50th anniversary on May 14th. The film, starring Sujatha as Annam and featuring the musical talents of Ilaiyaraaja and his brothers, was praised by poet Kannadasan.  The cast included Sivakumar, Thyagarajan, R. Muthuraman, Padmapriya, and others. The film's 50-day celebration took place at Shanmuga Theatre on September 6th, 1975.

articles.title: Typical English roast dinner potentially ‘drenched’ in 102 pesticides, says report | Pesticides | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Greenpeace has released a report revealing that the traditional Sunday roast, often considered a rustic meal, may contain pesticides. The report found over 100 pesticides used on vegetables and fruits, including some banned in the EU due to health concerns. Greenpeace UK's senior campaigner, Nina Schrank, stated that this widespread pesticide use is harming wildlife and ecosystems.  The UK government has a national action plan aimed at reducing pesticide use by 2030, while Greenpeace calls for stricter regulations and increased organic agriculture.

articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks, US futures climb on tech optimism - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: US stocks closed at record highs on Wednesday, boosted by strong corporate earnings and expectations of sustained growth fueled by AI spending. Cisco Systems Inc.'s strong outlook lifted Nasdaq 100 futures contracts.  Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and Tencent Holdings Ltd. missed revenue estimates, while the offshore yuan is experiencing its best winning streak since 2017. Investors are closely watching geopolitical developments in Iran and the summit between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping for potential market impacts. The yield on benchmark 10-year Treasuries rose to the highest since July due to mounting price pressures from US inflation reports.

articles.title: DMK boycotts floor test; urges CM to continue with Dravidian model welfare schemes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhayanidhi Stalin, leader of the Tamil Nadu opposition, led his party members in a boycott of a confidence motion presented by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay.  The walkout occurred after Stalin stated that the majority did not vote for the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK).

articles.title: Memphis residents file lawsuit alleging abuses by Trump-backed task force | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Four residents from Memphis, Tennessee have filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration alleging harassment by members of the Memphis Safe Task Force, a law enforcement initiative launched by President Donald Trump. The complaint claims that agents retaliated against bystanders who recorded the task force's activities, citing instances of hostility and threats of arrest.  The plaintiffs allege that the task force has conducted over 120,000 traffic stops in Memphis, a majority-Black city, with the involvement of state and federal agencies including the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The lawsuit also names acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche as a defendant alongside state officials like the leader of the Tennessee Highway Patrol.  The Department of Justice has denied any wrongdoing, while the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) is representing the plaintiffs in this case.

articles.title: Labor accused of ‘robbing Peter to pay Paul’ for axing $760m research program to fund other science measures | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government has announced a budget that includes funding for the CSIRO and National Measurement Institute, but at the expense of the $760 million Australia’s Economic Accelerator program. The axing of the program, established in 2023 to commercialize research, has angered researchers who argue it undermines the government's own priorities. Universities Australia and the Australian Academy of Science have expressed disappointment with the decision, stating that while they welcome increased investment in science, the repurposing of funds from one program to another is a disservice to both universities and the research community.

articles.title: Pharma, NBFCs see fresh mutual fund buying in April - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian drugmakers are benefiting from the impending patent expiry of semaglutide, a weight-loss drug.  This has led to increased buying in companies like Aurobindo Pharma, Torrent Pharma, and Sun Pharma.  Meanwhile, mutual funds have allocated more to asset management firms such as Nippon Life and Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC due to attractive valuations. Additionally, funds are increasing exposure to PNB Housing Finance in the retail lending and affordable housing sectors.

articles.title: ‘Limited’ religious symbols to be allowed with uniforms in Karnataka schools and colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government withdrew its 2022 order requiring prescribed uniforms in educational institutions and replaced it with a new order allowing students to wear “limited” traditional and faith-based symbols alongside their uniforms.  Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa stated that the decision aims to promote secular values and equal respect for all religions and traditions within schools, while maintaining institutional discipline.

articles.title: Trump administration offers $100m in aid to Cuba in exchange for reform | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has offered $100 million in humanitarian aid to Cuba, contingent on the Cuban government agreeing to "meaningful reforms". The offer was made public by the State Department and follows a period of escalating pressure from the Trump administration, which blames Cuba's communist leadership for hindering aid delivery. This comes amid an ongoing oil blockade imposed by President Donald Trump in response to the island's reliance on foreign imports for energy.  The US has accused the Cuban government of enriching elites while condemning its people to poverty.

articles.title: Court rules Coles misled shoppers with its ‘Down Down’ discount campaign | Coles | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) successfully sued Coles for misleading shoppers with "Down Down" discounts on everyday grocery products.  Justice Michael O'Bryan ruled that the supermarket giant falsely promoted these discounts by advertising prices as discounted when they had only been available at a lower price for a short period. The judge found that Coles misled consumers about the duration of the price increases, despite arguing that the promotions were genuine discounts in response to rising wholesale costs.  The decision sets a precedent for how long price increases must apply before a discount can be promoted without legal consequences.

articles.title: Trading volumes in unlisted shares plunge up to 70% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Trading activity in the unlisted market has significantly slowed down, with trading volumes declining by nearly 40% from last year.  Hitesh Dharawat, founder of Dharawat Securities, attributes this slowdown to a lack of quality companies, elevated valuations, and concerns about recent IPO underperformance.  Metropolitan Stock Exchange of India, Chennai Super Kings, SBI Funds Management, and Parag Parikh Financial Advisory Services are among the few stocks experiencing growth in 2026.  The decline in demand has also impacted share prices for companies such as Oravel Stays (Oyo), Hero FinCorp, Imagine Marketing (Boat), Nayara Energy, and Zepto.

articles.title: Women’s coalition urges speedy implementation of 33% reservation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the National Coalition for Women’s Reservation-Karnataka have called on the government to immediately implement the women's reservation Act, arguing that linking it to future Census and delimitation exercises is delaying progress. They criticized the delay in delivering equal political representation for women, who constitute 50% of the population, and questioned the need to link implementation with these processes.  The coalition has been advocating for the Act's implementation since 1996 and has intensified nationwide mobilization efforts to achieve this goal.

articles.title: Iran war live: Tehran slams ‘collusion’ as Netanyahu ‘secretly’ visits UAE | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref stated that Tehran's right to the Strait of Hormuz is established and closed. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the United Arab Emirates (UAE) amid attacks by the US and Israel, a visit his office described as "historic." The UAE's Foreign Ministry denied the visit was historic. Iran’s foreign minister condemned the trip, calling it evidence of collusion with Israel and warning that those involved will be held accountable.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit live: US president preparing to meet China’s leader with trade, Taiwan and the Iran war set to dominate talks | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump arrived in Beijing on Wednesday and is set to begin a summit with Xi Jinping on Thursday.  Air quality in the capital remains poor, with an air quality index exceeding 150, despite China's past efforts to improve air quality for important events. The visit comes amid geopolitical tensions, including the ongoing Iran war and trade disputes between the two countries. Trump is expected to discuss topics such as Iran, trade, Taiwan, and artificial intelligence during his summit with Xi Jinping.

articles.title: Margin revival, Semaglutide launch to drive Dr Reddy’s growth momentum in FY27 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Reddy's Laboratories experienced a decline in US revenue during the March quarter due to the loss of exclusivity for Revlimid. However, the company anticipates its base generics business, excluding Revlimid, to return to double-digit growth in fiscal year 2027.  The company expects Abatacept, an arthritis drug, to be a key growth driver following its launch around FY28. Dr Reddy's also reported a decrease in research and development (R&D) costs, which are expected to remain in the 7-8% range going forward.

articles.title: NSUI holds protest outside Education Minister’s residence over NEET paper leak - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the National Students’ Union of India (NSUI) protested outside Dharmendra Pradhan's residence in Delhi, demanding his resignation following allegations of a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination. The protesters accused the Education Minister of failing to protect students and demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into the incident, along with action against those involved. The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the exam and announced it would be retaken at a later date.

articles.title: Why was Tyler Oliveira deported and banned from Israel? YouTuber’s airport ordeal sparks backlash and debate | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tyler Oliveira, a YouTuber and documentary filmmaker, was denied entry into Israel after arriving in Tel Aviv on May 12, 2026.  He claims the reason for his deportation was due to accusations that some of his videos promoted anti-Semitic narratives, but Israeli authorities cited "illegal immigration considerations" in their refusal. The incident sparked controversy online and drew attention from controversial streamer Sneako, who compared Oliveira's situation to his own travel ban from Australia.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit live: US, China leaders to hold talks on trade, tech, Iran | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is in Beijing for talks with Xi Jinping, seeking to resolve trade disputes and bolster economic cooperation. The summit, occurring amidst ongoing tensions over the war in Iran, aims to address issues like market access, investment, and agricultural trade between the two countries.

articles.title: Remains of second US soldier who went missing during military exercises in Morocco have been recovered | Morocco | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Army announced the recovery of the remains of Spc Mariyah Symone Collington, a 19-year-old air and missile defense crew member who went missing during military exercises in Morocco. Collington, assigned to Charlie battery, fifth battalion, fourth air defense artillery regiment, was part of an ongoing multinational search operation that involved air, naval, and artificial intelligence assets. The remains were transported by a Moroccan helicopter to the morgue of Moulay El Hassan military hospital in Guelmim, Morocco.  The circumstances surrounding Collington's disappearance are under investigation.

articles.title: Republican redistricting effort is ‘evil incarnate’, Stacey Abrams tells new Guardian podcast | Stacey Abrams | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stacey Abrams, former Georgia gubernatorial candidate, criticized Republican-led states' efforts to redraw congressional maps to favor their party as "evil incarnate," arguing that it is a form of voter suppression.  She stated that these actions are not just cheating but also kneecapping the players and dismantling democratic systems. Abrams emphasized that this redistricting drive is part of a larger trend towards authoritarianism, urging voters to fight back in court even if they lose. She believes that building voter registration and turnout is crucial to counter Republican gains and build momentum for future elections.

articles.title: Vijay Narayan earns rare distinction of being Advocate General under two different governments - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's government appointed senior counsel Vijay Narayan as its Advocate General. This marks a rare distinction for Mr. Narayan, who previously served in this role under the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam regime from 2017 to 2021.  Mr. Narayan is the nephew of former Attorney General K.K. Venugopal and grandson of M.K. Nambyar, a renowned lawyer. He has extensive experience in various legal fields, including service law, labor law, and constitutional law, having argued cases at both the Supreme Court and several High Courts.

articles.title: JD Vance threatens health funding to states that don’t comply with White House anti-fraud effort | US healthcare | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: JD Vance, the US vice-president, threatened to withhold federal funding for government health insurance programs in states that fail to comply with a crackdown on suspected fraud. CMS, the agency responsible for Medicaid and Medicare, announced a six-month halt on new Medicare enrollment for hospices and home health agencies while investigating potential fraud alongside Vance's taskforce.  The administration will review anti-fraud funding for states deemed non-compliant, but it is unclear how extensive these actions will be or what impact they will have on access to care.

articles.title: Scrap NEET-based admissions, allow States to fill up medical seats, Vijay appeals to Centre - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay urged the Union government to cancel the NEET-based admissions in medical courses and allow states to fill seats based on Class 12 marks.  Vijay cited multiple instances of NEET paper leaks, including a recent cancellation following investigations by law enforcement agencies, as evidence of the exam's flaws. He emphasized that the introduction of NEET has disadvantaged students from rural areas and socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds. The NEET-UG 2026 was conducted on May 3, 2026, with over 22 million candidates appearing nationwide, including 140,000 from Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: Influencer detained in Tennessee over alleged confrontation involving gunfire | Tennessee | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as Chud the Builder, was detained in Tennessee following a shooting incident outside the Montgomery county courthouse.  Eatherly allegedly opened fire during a confrontation with another man, sustaining a gunshot wound to his arm and injuring the other individual who was transported by Lifeflight to Vanderbilt University Medical Center. The Montgomery County Sheriff’s Office praised their deputies for preventing further escalation of the situation. The District Attorney General's office is reviewing the facts of the investigation for formal criminal charges.

articles.title: 24x7 control rooms for disaster management to be set up in Ernakulam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector G. Priyanka announced the activation of Taluk Emergency Operation Centres (TEOCs) by May 20th to prepare for the monsoon season. The district has received a ₹5 crore disaster relief fund from the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) and additional funds for desilting rivers, cleaning canals, and installing geobags along the Chellanam coast.  Local bodies have been tasked with identifying potential relief camps and furnishing equipment for emergency response.

articles.title: Howard Lutnick said he had three ‘inconsequential’ meetings with Epstein | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Howard Lutnick, US commerce secretary, testified before the House oversight and reform committee about his interactions with Jeffrey Epstein. Lutnick stated he met Epstein only three times, in 2005, 2011, and 2012. He claimed these encounters were "meaningless and inconsequential" and that he had no personal or professional relationship with the disgraced financier.  Lutnick's testimony contradicted previous statements he made about their interactions on a podcast last year. The committee questioned Lutnick's account, with some Democrats calling his performance "contortions and lies."

articles.title: Odisha CM reduces number of vehicles in his convoy by half - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has ordered a reduction of half the vehicles in his personal security convoy, following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal for citizens to adopt cost-cutting measures due to global oil crisis.  Majhi also urged the public to minimize private vehicle use and prioritize public transport, advising against unnecessary travel and gold purchases.

articles.title: Drug overdose deaths drop in United States for third year in a row | Drugs News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) released data showing a nearly 14 percent decline in drug overdose deaths in 2025, reaching nearly 70,000. This marks the third consecutive year of declining overdose deaths, attributed to factors such as increased availability of naloxone, fentanyl testing strips, and regulatory changes in China limiting access to fentanyl-making chemicals. While the trend is positive, seven states saw increases in overdose deaths.  President Donald Trump's administration has highlighted the decrease as a sign of success for its crackdown on drug trafficking, while experts have criticized such claims as exaggerated.

articles.title: The south London community where ‘pioneering’ scholarship choristers are made | London | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: St John the Divine, Kennington (SJDK), a church in south London, has produced several young choristers who have secured scholarships to prestigious music institutions.  The church's youth choral program, which began in 2013, aims to remove barriers that keep working-class children from classical music. The program provides transportation and snacks for rehearsals, making it accessible for families with limited resources. Ed Picton-Turbervill, an award-winning composer and organist, credits the program's success in fostering musical talent and breaking down racial prejudice within the community.  N’raeah, a four-year-old chorister from south London, has been accepted into St Paul's Cathedral school, a testament to the impact of the program.

articles.title: Three held; security beefed up in Bhopal as Muslim community protests assault on man over ‘love jihad’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three men were arrested in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh, following a protest by members of the Muslim community who demonstrated against an assault on a man by Bajrang Dal activists. The incident occurred after several videos of the assault, which allegedly involved derogatory language and insults to Islam, went viral online.  The Muslim community demanded that the accused be arrested within 24 hours.  Ayush Gupta, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Bhopal zone 1, confirmed searches for more suspects and stated that adequate security has been implemented in sensitive areas. Bittu Sharma, Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), Jahangirabad, reported increased police presence in these locations to maintain peace. The incident followed a previous attack on Arif Khan, a 27-year-old man from the Muslim community, by right-wing activists who accused him of "love jihad."

articles.title: Top 10 countries with the most gold in 2026: USA tops, China and India lead the global rankings | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States, with over 8,000 tonnes of gold reserves, maintains the largest holdings globally.  Second is Italy with more than 2,400 tonnes, followed by China at over 2,300 tonnes. Other countries with significant gold reserves include India, Japan, Poland, Turkey, and Uzbekistan. These nations utilize gold as a strategic asset for economic stability and diversification of their foreign exchange reserves.

articles.title: US Senator Cassidy’s vote to convict Trump looms over Louisiana primary | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bill Cassidy, a US Senator who voted to convict Donald Trump in his first impeachment trial, faces a primary challenge from Julia Letlow and John Fleming.  The race is seen as a barometer of Trump's influence within the Republican Party despite declining national approval ratings. The winner will likely secure victory in the general election in the deep-red state. Cassidy has walked a fine line between supporting Trump's policies and clashing with his administration, including a contentious vote on Robert F Kennedy Jr.'s nomination for health and human services secretary.  The primary is taking place amid ongoing redistricting battles and concerns about voting rights.

articles.title: Wes Streeting: PM-in-waiting or ‘this generation’s David Miliband’? | Labour party leadership | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: As the king's speech approached, Wes Streeting, the health secretary, was expected to remain a contender for the Labour leadership. However, after a series of events, including Keir Starmer's resilience and Downing Street's public statements, Streeting announced his resignation plans, potentially triggering a leadership contest. While some allies believe Streeting has the support he needs to launch a bid, others are skeptical about his chances. The outcome remains uncertain, with potential contenders on the left of the party like Ed Miliband or Angela Rayner also in the mix.

articles.title: How the anti-defection law is going to operate in the AIADMK case? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, the general secretary of the AIADMK, removed 26 rebel district secretaries, including former Ministers C.Ve. Shanmugam and S.P. Velumani, from their positions on Wednesday night (May 13, 2026).  This action followed a division within the party's Assembly members, with 22 supporting Palaniswami and 25 opposing the trust motion moved by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam. The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution and the Members of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly (Disqualification Ground of Defection) Rules, 1986, outline grounds for disqualification in cases of defection.

articles.title: Alien smuggling and child sexual abuse material: Iranian national pleads guilty in New York court to two serious federal crimes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Sharon Gohari, a naturalized US citizen of Iranian descent, pleaded guilty to charges of alien smuggling and receiving child sexual abuse material in federal court.  Gohari operated a scheme from at least December 2020 until May 2025, facilitating travel for Iranian nationals seeking entry into the US for thousands of dollars per client. Authorities discovered child sexual abuse material on Gohari's phone, including videos depicting the rape of children as young as five years old, and he shared some with overseas accounts in Iran.  Sentencing is scheduled for a later date.

articles.title: How US donor bodies were sold for Israeli military training | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The University of Southern California (USC) is selling donated human cadavers to the U.S. Navy, which are then being used by Israeli military surgical teams for training in Los Angeles without the donors' consent. This practice has been highlighted in an AJ+ documentary, prompting concerns about ethical implications and donor rights.

articles.title: Wes Streeting prepares to launch leadership challenge against Keir Starmer | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting is preparing to launch a leadership challenge against Keir Starmer on Thursday if he can secure enough support.  Ed Miliband, Angela Rayner, and other potential contenders are scrambling to find a candidate to oppose him. Starmer is urging MPs to avoid a contest, arguing it would cause chaos. The situation has sparked concerns about the future of the Labour party as some MPs believe Streeting's challenge could destabilize the party further.

articles.title: Assam ships first legal agarwood chips to West Asia - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Assam marked a significant milestone in its agro-forest economy by exporting the first legally approved consignment of agarwood chips to Saudi Arabia and the UAE. The shipment, valued at ₹2.35 crore, was flagged off by Jehirul Islam, chairman of the All Assam Agarwood Planters and Traders’ Association, after securing all necessary permits including a CITES permit and a restricted export license from the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.  Dr. Islam expressed gratitude to Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma for supporting the Assam Agarwood Promotion Policy, 2020, which aims to regulate agarwood cultivation, processing, and exports. The policy is expected to curb illegal trade and generate substantial revenue for the state.

articles.title: Man arrested on suspicion of rape after woman alleges assault near church in Maidstone - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kent Police arrested a 50-year-old man on suspicion of rape following an alleged assault near a church in Maidstone. The incident occurred between 7 pm and 10 pm on Saturday, with the woman reporting the attack to police late that evening.  The suspect remains in custody while police continue their investigation, cordoning off the area and urging residents with CCTV or dashcams to check for footage.

articles.title: Trump taps David Venturella, former private prison executive, to lead ICE | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's administration has appointed David Venturella, a former executive at the private prison company GEO Group, as acting director of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Venturella will replace Todd Lyons, who is leaving the agency on May 31st.  Venturella previously served at ICE under both Democratic and Republican administrations and has been involved in the Trump administration's mass deportation campaign, which has benefited private contractors like GEO Group. Rights groups have criticized the hiring of Venturella as a "revolving-door phenomenon" due to his past experience with ICE and GEO Group.

articles.title: Valdo Calocane brother tells inquiry he felt powerless over killer’s mental ill health | Nottingham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020, stabbed to death three people and injured others in Nottingham on June 13, 2023. His younger brother, Elias, testified at an inquiry into the events leading up to the attacks, stating he believed his brother's violent messages concerned suicidal thoughts.  Elias said he had a "belief" that Calocane would take his own life and saw him as having "darkest thoughts". The inquiry heard that Calocane had called his brother on the day before the attacks, asking him to take their parents out of the country.

articles.title: Kashmir MLA ‘boycotts’ L-G’s drug campaign after demolition drive in his constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sheikh Khursheed, an MLA from north Kashmir, boycotted a campaign led by Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha after the police demolished a house in Langate.  Khursheed criticized the demolition as arbitrary and violating Supreme Court directives, arguing it targeted innocent families based on past accusations. He also questioned the government's focus on drug eradication while ignoring other issues like liquor ban. The LG Sinha, meanwhile, launched a campaign to curb drug use in the region, highlighting its connection with terrorism.  The police conducted a demolition drive targeting properties linked to alleged drug traffickers.

articles.title: By day a priest, by night a wrestler: Meet the Mexican hero who raised money for an orphanage by fighting in wrestling rings | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Fray Tormenta, a Catholic priest known for his work at an orphanage in Mexico, secretly competed as a masked wrestler to support the children.  He began wrestling after struggling financially and found that it provided a way to raise funds for the orphanage. His unusual double life made him a national hero and inspired films like "Nacho Libre". Fray Tormenta's story highlights the power of compassion and the unconventional paths people take to help others, blending faith, charity, and professional wrestling in a unique way.

articles.title: Man City beat Palace to close gap with Arsenal to 2, with two games to play | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester City defeated Crystal Palace 3-0 to close the gap with Arsenal to two points.  Goals from Antoine Semenyo, Omar Marmoush, and Savinho secured the victory for City, who now have a superior goal difference and are looking to secure a domestic cup double. The win puts City at 77 points, while Arsenal needs to beat relegated Burnley next Monday to keep their title hopes alive.  The final day of the season will see both teams in action.

articles.title: Israel’s ruling coalition proposes early elections amid ultra-Orthodox anger at Netanyahu | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli prime minister, has proposed dissolving parliament to trigger early elections. The move comes after mounting pressure from ultra-Orthodox parties and follows a possible collapse of his coalition.  The bill, signed by leaders of the governing coalition, could be put to a vote on May 20th. Yair Lapid, leader of the opposition, has responded with his own proposal to dissolve parliament. The upcoming elections are expected to take place in August, potentially two months before the original end of the legislative term.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh confirmed as new US Federal Reserve chair amid controversy | Banks News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the new chair of the Federal Reserve’s Board of Governors, succeeding Jerome Powell, in a 54-45 vote.  Warsh's confirmation comes amid concerns about independence at the central bank and rising inflation. He was previously on the board from 2006 to 2011 and has advocated for rate cuts under Donald Trump. Warsh’s swearing-in awaits final White House signatures.

articles.title: OPT faces fresh political heat in US amid fraud allegations; Intl students will face the brunt - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Acting Director Todd Lyons announced the identification of over 10,000 foreign students linked to “highly suspect employers” in a crackdown on fraud within the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program.  Lyons described the OPT program as a "magnet for fraud" and warned of potential criminal, civil, and immigration consequences. Immigration lawyers and education experts have long cautioned against fraudulent consultancies and fake staffing arrangements within the OPT ecosystem, but this latest crackdown is expected to fuel ongoing political efforts by conservative groups to scale back or eliminate the program.  The recent briefing has caused anxiety among international students, particularly Indian students, who are the largest cohort in the OPT program.

articles.title: Keir Starmer sets out changes to education, health and courts in king’s speech | King's speech | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the prime minister, unveiled his second king’s speech on Wednesday, outlining a legislative agenda focused on economic growth and public service reform. Starmer promised measures to curb social housing purchases, overhaul special educational needs provision, limit jury trials, introduce digital ID, and abolish NHS England. However, these plans face potential challenges as health secretary Wes Streeting is expected to resign, potentially triggering a leadership contest.  Despite the proposed reforms, some MPs criticized the lack of urgency and radical transformation in the package.

articles.title: West Bengal CM gives sanction to CBI to prosecute officials in several scams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, West Bengal Chief Minister, granted permission to the CBI to prosecute officials involved in teacher's recruitment, municipality recruitment, and cooperative scams.  He stated that these investigations were previously withheld by the previous Trinamool Congress government due to corruption concerns. The move is part of a "zero tolerance" policy against corruption adopted by his BJP-led administration.  The Chief Minister also lifted a ban on potato sales to other states, citing a bumper crop and falling prices.

articles.title: US waives visa bonds of up to $15,000 for FIFA World Cup ticket holders | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US is waiving costly visa bonds for World Cup ticket holders, a move aimed at addressing concerns about the impact of previous policies on international travel.  This decision follows criticism that the Trump administration's visa bond program was burdensome and raised questions about the inclusivity of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The US Department of State confirmed that visitors with tickets will still undergo regular visa vetting, while FIFA President Gianni Infantino has pledged to make the tournament the most inclusive in history.

articles.title: Quote of the day by David Lloyd George: “Don't be afraid to take a big step if one is indicated. You can't cross a chasm in two small jumps.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: David Lloyd George, a prominent British political leader, famously stated that "Don't be afraid to take a big step if one is indicated. You can't cross a chasm in two small jumps." This quote resonates with modern-day individuals facing uncertainty and navigating rapidly changing landscapes. While fear of failure or embarrassment may contribute to delaying major decisions, the underlying message emphasizes the need for decisive action when a significant gap exists between current circumstances and desired outcomes.  This timeless wisdom highlights that incremental adjustments often fail to address fundamental issues, urging readers to acknowledge when it's time for a bolder leap.

articles.title: India hikes gold, silver duties to protect sliding rupee - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India has increased import tariffs on gold and silver to about 15 percent, aiming to bolster its sagging rupee and replenish depleted foreign currency reserves. This move comes amid a worsening rupee slide against the dollar due to the ongoing war in the Middle East, which has disrupted oil supplies and driven up crude oil prices.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi previously urged citizens to avoid gold purchases to alleviate pressure on the country's balance of payments.

articles.title: Family of British couple jailed in Iran say they have lost contact | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Foreman family of British couple Lindsay and Craig Foreman, jailed in Iran for 10 years on espionage charges, have reported losing all contact with them.  Their son, Joe Bennett, expressed fears for their safety after the family's telephone access was cut off following a media interview where they voiced concerns about their detention conditions. The Foreign Office has previously condemned the sentences and emphasized the risk of arrest for British nationals in Iran.

articles.title: Nicobarese oppose proposal for three wildlife sanctuaries - The Hindu
