articles.rephrased_article: SAIL's stock experienced a sharp rally on Tuesday due to unusually high activity among traders covering short positions.  Apurva Sheth, Head of Market Perspectives and Research at Samco Securities, noted that the stock was nearing its market-wide position limit (MWPL), which indicates concentrated bearish trading. This surge in MWPL usage, coupled with stop losses triggered by a price rise, forced traders to buy back shares and futures contracts, creating a feedback loop that accelerated the rally.  The incident highlights concerns about concentrated positioning in the derivatives market, particularly in highly liquid PSU and commodity-linked stocks.

articles.title: The $1.8 billion pivot: How Michael Bloomberg’s historic gift rewrote the rules of college access | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Bloomberg donated $1.8 billion to Johns Hopkins University, the largest donation in American history, to fund undergraduate scholarships and eliminate financial barriers for prospective students. This move aims to address a psychological obstacle preventing talented individuals from low-income backgrounds from pursuing higher education due to high tuition fees. The endowment will ensure that all accepted students can attend without incurring debt, fostering an environment where merit is prioritized over wealth.  This historic gift signifies a shift in the focus of philanthropy towards creating opportunities for excellence and dismantling financial barriers in higher education.

articles.title: School education index: Kerala betters grade, score - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Despite the denial of funds by the Union government, Kerala has improved its performance in the Union Ministry of Education’s Performance Grading Index 2.0 for States/Union Territories (UT) for the year 2024-25. The state received a Prachesta-2 grade, an improvement from Prachesta-3 in 2023-24, with scores rising from 594.2 to 687.7.  Kerala achieved the topmost Utkarsh grade (72.8-80) in access and the Uttam-1 grade (81-90.9) in teacher education and training, among other achievements. The report highlights Kerala's progress despite challenges, including a lack of funding from the Union government.

articles.title: Why Trump decided to back Iraq’s prime minister-designate, Ali al-Zaidi | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump publicly supported Ali al-Zaidi, a pro-Iran Iraqi politician, as the country's next prime minister after pressure from Washington to avoid an Iran-aligned government.  The US suspended aid and security assistance to Iraq in order to prevent the nomination of former Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki, who was backed by the Coordination Framework, a Shia party coalition aligned with Iran. The US Secretary of Treasury, Scott Bessent, warned that those enabling militia violence would be held accountable. Al-Zaidi's appointment is conditional on progress in curbing pro-Iran militia activity and removing them from Iraqi institutions.

articles.title: Khawaja Asif says KP now on 'same page' as Centre in fight against terrorism - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif acknowledged that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government is now cooperating with the federal government in combating terrorism. He stated that despite past disagreements, the two governments are united in their efforts to address the issue and emphasized Pakistan's attempts to engage with the Afghan Taliban for a peaceful resolution.  Asif also addressed concerns about terrorist activities originating from Afghanistan, highlighting the need for cooperation from all provinces and the ongoing challenges faced by Pakistani forces. Following a heated exchange between Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl leader Noor Alam Khan and Asif during a parliamentary session, Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah adjourned the session due to unruly behavior from PTI members.

articles.title: Trump China trip: What to know as president meets Xi Jinping
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump, accompanied by CEOs of major US businesses and tech companies, arrived in Beijing for his first trip to China since 2017. The main focus of the talks is expected to be the current tense trade relationship between the two superpowers, with Trump seeking to open up China's economy to major tech companies and pressuring Xi Jinping to end US arms sales to Taiwan and extend the trade truce agreed in October.  The visit also includes discussions about Iran and artificial intelligence, with both sides hoping for a "better future" and increased stability between them.

articles.title: Official marking of land for Brazil’s uncontacted Kawahiva people begins after 27-year wait | Brazil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Brazilian government has begun the demarcation of the 410,000-hectare Pardo River Kawahiva Indigenous territory in Mato Grosso and Amazonas states. This decision comes after 27 years of efforts to protect the uncontacted people living there, with support from organizations like the National Indigenous Peoples’ Foundation (Funai) and campaigners.  However, legal challenges from groups linked to agribusiness have delayed progress, highlighting ongoing threats to the Kawahiva's survival. Despite these obstacles, Funai is planning buffer zones to protect the territory from deforestation and advocates for increased resources to ensure the safety of isolated Indigenous peoples.

articles.title: In a major reshuffle, 72 IAS officers transferred by Gujarat government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Gujarat government transferred 72 Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officers on Wednesday, May 13, 2026.  D.N. Modi, the Municipal Commissioner of Jamnagar, was appointed Development Commissioner in Gandhinagar, while Anand Patel, Collector of Kutch-Bhuj, became Commissioner of Schools and also took charge as Director of the Gujarat Council of Education Research and Training (GCERT). Other notable transfers included Sujeet Kumar to Special Commissioner of State Tax, Ahmedabad.

articles.title: Karachi police get 3-day physical remand of alleged cocaine queenpin Anmol alias Pinky - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Anmol alias Pinky, an alleged drug supplier, was granted a three-day physical remand by a Karachi court after her arrest in connection with two narcotics cases. The incident sparked controversy when a video surfaced of her being escorted to court without handcuffs.  The investigating officer (IO) filed a revision application against the judicial magistrate's order, arguing that proper interrogation was needed for the investigation. The Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar expressed satisfaction with the police's re-examination of the legal aspects and directed a fair and transparent investigation into the case.

articles.title: Jason Collins, first openly gay active NBA player, dies after cancer battle | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jason Collins, the first openly gay active NBA player, died at age 47 after a battle with glioblastoma.  Collins revealed his diagnosis of stage four glioblastoma in September and had been battling cancer since then. The former NBA center played for several teams including the Houston Rockets, New Jersey Nets, and Memphis Grizzlies. His family said he will be deeply missed, adding that his legacy was one of tolerance and understanding.

articles.title: Australian military plane to join efforts to reopen strait of Hormuz as Marles considers ‘how else we can contribute’ | Australian military | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australia will send its world-leading E-7A Wedgetail surveillance plane to join an international mission to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The defence minister, Richard Marles, stated that Australia is prepared to contribute further assets to the effort, potentially including additional military personnel and equipment.  The decision follows a meeting of defense ministers from 40 countries who agreed to support freedom of navigation through the strait.

articles.title: SBI shares extend fall to 20% from peak after Q4 NIMs contraction rattles investors. What's ahead for investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SBI's stock price has declined since hitting a 52-week high due to concerns about margin pressure and slower earnings growth. The bank reported a decline in operating profit for Q4FY26, with net interest margins (NIMs) contracting both year-on-year and sequentially. Despite this, analysts remain optimistic about SBI's long-term prospects, citing strong fundamentals, healthy loan growth, and improving asset quality.  However, the stock has broken below key support levels, indicating bearish momentum.

articles.title: Uk Women Lottery Prize: ‘She’s luckier than me’: UK woman wins £333,000 lottery prize after husband secretly put her namec | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nancy Barkley, an 80-year-old woman from Cheshire, UK, won £333,333 in the People’s Postcode Lottery after her husband secretly registered the ticket in her name. Colin Barkley, her 69-year-old husband, believed she was the lucky one in the family. The couple plans to purchase a home and enjoy quieter pleasures like lunches out and short trips away.  The win comes as a significant change for the retired factory worker and her family after years of modest living and health challenges.

articles.title: NIA arrests Hizb-ul-Mujahideen linked ‘narco-terrorist’ after extradition from Portugal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested Iqbal Singh, also known as Shera, in Delhi after securing his extradition from Portugal. Singh, a mastermind in a major Hizb-ul-Mujahideen (HM) terror-financing case, had fled to Portugal in 2020 and was wanted for a non-bailable arrest warrant issued in October 2020 and an Interpol Red Notice opened in June 2021. The NIA alleges that Singh coordinated the smuggling of heroin from Pakistan into India and channeled proceeds through "hawala" networks to HM operatives in Pakistan and Kashmir, facilitating terror activities.

articles.title: Indian arrogance shot down alongside planes during last year's military conflict, Tarar says - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Information Minister Attaullah Tarar addressed a ceremony in Islamabad, commemorating the "Marka-i-Haq" (Battle of Truth) conflict with India. He stated that the downing of eight Indian planes during the May 2022 conflict, including several Rafale jets, demonstrated Pakistan's aerial dominance and exposed India's false flag operation in Pahalgam.  Tarar emphasized Pakistan's narrative strength due to its timely and accurate communication about the incident, highlighting the country’s role as a frontline state against terrorism. He also praised the Pakistani media and public for their support during the conflict.

articles.title: Series of tremors near Tehran renews concerns over major quake risk | Earthquakes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran experienced a series of nine small earthquakes near Tehran overnight, renewing concerns about the potential for a major seismic event. The tremors occurred near the Mosha fault, one of the country's most active seismic zones, and were felt in an area close to the capital.  Seismologist Mehdi Zare warned that while the recent activity may not indicate a future earthquake, Tehran's vulnerability due to its dense urban development and proximity to active faults remains a significant concern.

articles.title: Stella prize 2026: Lee Lai becomes first non-binary person and first graphic novelist to win with Cannon | Stella prize | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lee Lai, the first non-binary winner of the Stella Prize, has won with her graphic novel "Cannon". The book follows a queer Chinese woman living in Montreal and explores themes of responsibility, communication, and exploitation.  Lai's win marks a significant milestone for the graphic novel community, as it is the first time a comic book has taken home the prestigious award. The Stella Prize was first opened to non-binary writers in 2021. Lai hopes this victory will encourage more readers to explore comics.

articles.title: Manappuram Finance, IIFL Finance, other stocks rally up to 11% as gold prices soar after import duty hike - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to reduce non-essential gold purchases, citing the need to stabilize the rupee and reduce imports. India's government implemented a hike in import duties on gold to address these concerns. This move is expected to decrease precious metal imports, support the rupee, and narrow the trade deficit.  The rise in gold prices has positively impacted gold financing firms like Muthoot Finance, Manappuram Finance, and IIFL Finance as their loans are secured by gold.

articles.title: Hantavirus outbreak: Passengers evacuated from cruise ship to leave hospital after 72-hour quarantine - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Passengers evacuated from the virus-hit Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius are set to begin leaving a specialist isolation facility in the UK after completing an initial 72-hour quarantine period.  All passengers remain healthy and asymptomatic, but will continue self-isolation at home for another 42 days as a precaution. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) stated that public health specialists will assess whether individuals can safely isolate at home or if alternative accommodation arrangements are necessary. The outbreak aboard the expedition cruise ship has so far been linked to three deaths, including two confirmed hantavirus cases.  The WHO has confirmed six infections linked to the outbreak, with more potential cases still possible.

articles.title: AIADMK legislature party splits vertically during trust vote in Tamil Nadu Assembly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) legislature party in Tamil Nadu experienced a significant split during a trust vote.  25 MLAs, led by rebel leader S.P. Velumani, voted in favor of the motion moved by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay while 22 MLAs, led by AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami, voted against it. The division within the party highlights a growing rift between factions within the AIADMK.

articles.title: Finance minister discusses budget preparations with visiting IMF mission - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) delegation in Islamabad to discuss preparations for the upcoming federal budget and the country's broader reform agenda.  The discussions focused on macroeconomic stabilization efforts, fiscal strategy, and structural reforms aimed at promoting investment, productivity, and export-led growth. The IMF mission acknowledged Pakistan's progress in maintaining economic stability despite global challenges, while emphasizing the need for continued reform momentum to manage risks from the war in the Middle East. Aurangzeb stressed the government's commitment to deepening reforms and strengthening macroeconomic stability without compromising long-term growth prospects.

articles.title: The class politics of modern outbreaks | Health | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A recent hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius, a luxury cruise ship, highlights concerns about elite mobility and its impact on global health. The outbreak, which has led to confirmed cases and deaths, underscores the unequal distribution of risks associated with disease transmission during pandemics.  While wealthy passengers often travel freely and experience minimal consequences, poorer populations in regions where outbreaks occur bear the brunt of the risk. This pattern reflects a larger issue of inequality within globalization, where wealthier individuals contribute disproportionately to the spread of diseases while those with fewer resources are most vulnerable to their effects.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang joins Trump as tech dominates China trip | Nvidia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, joined a delegation led by Donald Trump to China for a 36-hour meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The summit, the first overseas trip for Trump since the US and Israel launched attacks on Iran, is expected to cover topics including the conflict, tariffs, and China's relationship with Taiwan. Huang was invited by Trump, who confirmed his participation on social media, and aims to support American goals in the Chinese market.

articles.title: PFC Q4 Results: Profit rises 24% to Rs 6,325 crore as interest income grows - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: PFC's profit before tax increased 27% year-over-year to Rs 7,764 crore in the quarter ending March 2023. Total income rose 3% to Rs 15,348.23 crore during the same period. The company experienced a significant reversal of impairment on financial instruments, contributing significantly to its profitability. PFC reported a net profit of Rs 20,051 crore for FY26, an increase of 16% from the previous year.

articles.title: Ukraine Spying Case: Scottish ex-military instructor jailed for over eight years in Ukraine for spying for Russia | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ross David Cutmore, a Scottish man who traveled to Ukraine as a military instructor, was sentenced to eight-and-a-half years in prison for working as a Russian spy.  Cutmore admitted to passing sensitive military information to Russia while Ukraine remained under martial law and was recruited by an officer linked to the Federal Security Service (FSB). He provided coordinates of Ukrainian military positions, details about foreign trainers, photographs of training sites, and information on facilities in Odesa. Cutmore also received guidance on assembling an improvised bomb and obtaining weapons from a hidden stash.

articles.title: SC asks Centre to consider States’ pleas for funds for CCTVs in police stations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court urged the Union government to fully implement the Assistance to States and Union Territories for Modernisation of Police (ASUMP) scheme, which provides funds for installing CCTV cameras in police stations and a centralized monitoring dashboard. The court expressed concerns over non-functional CCTV cameras in Udaipur police stations and directed the Centre to consider requests from states for funding.  The ASUMP scheme has been extended until September 30, 2026, with most states initiating steps towards compliance. However, Jharkhand was criticized for not installing any CCTV cameras, despite receiving funds under the scheme. The court also cautioned against releasing funds without due diligence to prevent misappropriation.

articles.title: Khawaja Asif says KP on 'same page' as Centre in fight against terrorism - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif acknowledged that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government is now cooperating with the federal government in combating terrorism.  He stated that despite previous lack of cooperation, the two governments are now on the same page and have made efforts to address the issue through dialogue with the Afghan Taliban government.  Asif also addressed concerns about Pakistan's security by emphasizing that Afghanistan was acting as a proxy for India and facilitating terrorist activities in Pakistan. He warned that if communication efforts fail, open war may be inevitable.

articles.title: At least eight killed in Israeli drone strikes on highway south of Beirut | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel carried out three drone strikes on cars on a major highway in Jiyeh, south of Beirut, killing at least eight people, including two children. The Lebanese Ministry of Health reported the attacks, which have been escalating since the beginning of the war in March.  The Israeli military issued forced displacement orders for six southern Lebanese villages, warning residents to move away from their homes.  Hezbollah, a Lebanese militant group, opposes these negotiations and continues its attacks on northern Israel and Israeli troops.

articles.title: 1MDB financier Jho Low seeks pardon from Donald Trump | 1MDB | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jho Low, a fugitive Malaysian financier, has reportedly requested a pardon from President Donald Trump.  Low faces multiple charges in the US and Malaysia related to his alleged role in the misappropriation of at least $4.5 billion from 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB). The scandal is one of the world’s biggest financial frauds, with billions plundered from the now defunct sovereign wealth fund. Johari Abdul Ghani, chair of a Malaysian taskforce seeking to recover funds and assets linked to 1MDB, opposes Low's request for a pardon and urges the US to assist Malaysia in locating him.

articles.title: Ghana to evacuate 300 citizens from South Africa over anti-immigrant protests
articles.rephrased_article: Ghana will evacuate 300 citizens from South Africa following a wave of anti-immigrant protests.  The Ghanaian government, citing "distressed" citizens and an advisory by the foreign ministry, has granted approval for their immediate evacuation.  President Cyril Ramaphosa of South Africa stated that the recent protests were isolated acts of criminality and that the government will regulate migration and enforce its laws. The situation has prompted other African nations like Kenya, Malawi, Lesotho, and Zimbabwe to issue warnings to their citizens in South Africa.

articles.title: U.S. to impose visa curbs on 13 people linked to Indian firm over fentanyl - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The United States imposed visa restrictions on 13 individuals linked to K.S. International Traders, an Indian online pharmacy accused of selling counterfeit prescription pills laced with fentanyl. The U.S. State Department stated that the company generated revenue through trafficking in fentanyl, which President Trump designated as a “weapon of mass destruction.” This action follows previous sanctions against KS International Traders last year for similar activities.

articles.title: Tens of thousands protest in Argentina over Milei university cuts | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands of Argentines protested in cities across the country against Javier Milei's government's cuts to public university funding. The demonstrations, fueled by concerns over staff wages and a stalled funding law, highlight growing discontent with Milei's policies, which have led to declining real salaries for professors and accusations of corruption within his administration.  The protesters argue that the cuts undermine the foundations of higher education in Argentina, a country known for its public universities' history of producing Nobel laureates.

articles.title: US to impose visa curbs on 13 people linked to Indian firm over prescription pills laced with fentanyl - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has imposed visa restrictions on 13 individuals associated with KS International Traders, an Indian online pharmacy accused of selling counterfeit prescription pills laced with fentanyl. The company, based in Mumbai, generated revenue through trafficking fentanyl, a powerful synthetic opioid that the US government has designated as a "weapon of mass destruction."  This action follows previous sanctions against KS International Traders last year for similar illicit activities.

articles.title: London prisoner with muscle-wasting condition claims he has to crawl on floor | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Umer Khalid, a prisoner at Wormwood Scrubs awaiting trial for alleged involvement in a break-in at RAF Brize Norton, claims he has been forced to crawl due to inadequate medical care and lack of a wheelchair. Khalid, who suffers from limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, alleges that prison officials have ignored his needs, including missed appointments with healthcare professionals and insufficient access to medication and high protein food. He also claims to have been left in his cell during a fire alarm evacuation and denied proper treatment for his condition despite being diagnosed with muscular dystrophy in 2014. Shabana Khalid, his mother, expressed outrage at the prison's response, stating that her son is suffering from severe physical deterioration.

articles.title: Hindustan Zinc shares surge 5% as silver prices near Rs 3 lakh/kg after import duty hike; Vedanta shares jump 4% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged citizens to reduce purchases of non-essential gold and silver over the next year to alleviate pressure on foreign exchange reserves and imports. This policy measure led to a surge in import duty on silver, resulting in a 6% jump in MCX silver futures prices and a 6% rise in gold futures prices. Hindustan Zinc, India's largest silver producer, saw its share price climb over 5%, while Vedanta shares also rose significantly.  The government's push for infrastructure development is expected to boost steel demand, benefiting companies like Hindustan Zinc.

articles.title: PM austerity appeal: State leaders take steps to limit their fuel use - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and several other state chief ministers have implemented measures to reduce fuel consumption in response to the West Asia crisis.  These include reducing convoy sizes, promoting electric vehicles, and encouraging public transport use. Yogi Adityanath, Rekha Gupta, Mohan Yadav, and others have also taken steps to promote sustainability within their respective states.  Devendra Fadnavis, Harsh Sanghavi, and Acharya Devvrat have implemented similar measures in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Bihar respectively.

articles.title: Trump and Xi to meet in Beijing: The key issues shaping the China summit | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are meeting in Beijing for a high-stakes summit focused on trade, Taiwan, artificial intelligence, and the Iran war.  The summit comes amid growing tensions between the two superpowers over technology, rare earth minerals, and economic competition.  Trump is seeking to secure concessions from Xi, including increased purchases of American goods and easing restrictions on advanced chip exports. Xi aims to maintain stability while asserting China's economic dominance and pushing back against US attempts to restrict its access to critical resources. The summit will likely result in a limited agreement, with both sides acknowledging the need for continued dialogue despite their deep-seated rivalry.

articles.title: Ahead of high-stakes visit to Beijing, Trump vows to push Xi to 'open up' China - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump is traveling to Beijing for a high-stakes summit with Xi Jinping, aiming to "open up" China to American businesses. The trip, delayed from March due to political frictions over Taiwan and the Middle East war, will also involve discussions on trade, arms sales to Taiwan, and Iran.  The two leaders are expected to extend a one-year truce in their tariff war while navigating tensions over rare earth exports, AI rivalry, and China's growing assertiveness. The visit is being closely watched by Taiwan and allies for any sign of weakening US support for the island.

articles.title: One Nation senator Malcolm Roberts again fails to rule out Bondi beach terror attack being ‘false flag’ | One Nation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Malcolm Roberts, senator from One Nation, sparked controversy by claiming the Bondi beach antisemitic terror attack was an "absurd proposition" and that he didn't have data to rule it out.  He made these comments during a YouTube interview, despite police and investigators treating the incident as terrorism allegedly inspired by Islamic State. Pauline Hanson, his fellow senator from Queensland, defended him, claiming his statements were taken out of context. The federal government has convened a royal commission into the attack and broader issues of antisemitism in Australia.

articles.title: Thief jailed after stealing unreleased Beyoncé music from car
articles.rephrased_article: A man named Kelvin Evans, 41, was sentenced to two years in prison for stealing unreleased Beyoncé music from a car.  Evans pleaded guilty to charges including entering an automobile and criminal trespass last year in Atlanta, Georgia. The theft occurred on July 8, 2025, as the singer's Beyoncé tour was in town.  The stolen hard drives containing unreleased material have not been recovered.

articles.title: Vodafone Idea shares jump 7% as telco set to consider fundraise on May 16. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone Idea's board of directors will meet on May 16th to consider its fourth quarter earnings and a proposal for raising funds through equity issuance. The company recently received a significant reduction in adjusted gross revenue (AGR) dues from the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), leading to an increase in investor confidence and stock price.  The move comes after the DoT finalized AGR dues at Rs 64,046 crore as of December 31, 2025, a significant relief for the telecom company.

articles.title: What you need to know about Karnataka’s Rohith Vemula Bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government has approved the revised Rohith Vemula Bill, 2026. The bill aims to prevent discrimination and injustice for students, faculty, and staff from scheduled castes and tribes (SC/ST) by guaranteeing equal access to education in all higher educational institutions across the state.

articles.title: UK PM Starmer set to meet rival Streeting amid pledge to carry on governing | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, facing pressure to resign after a string of ministerial resignations, is expected to meet with potential leadership rival Wes Streeting. The meeting comes ahead of King Charles' speech at the opening of parliament, where Starmer will outline his government's plans for reform.  Despite calls for his resignation from over 80 MPs, Starmer insists on pressing forward with his agenda to build a stronger and fairer country.

articles.title: President Zaradari approves Sitara-i-Shujaat for citizen who sacrified his life while averting suicide attack - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari approved the award of the Sitara-i-Shujaat to Liaqat, a local shepherd who was killed while foiling a suicide attack in Attock's Jand tehsil.  The incident occurred on Monday near a security post, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised Liaqat’s bravery in confronting the suspect. The president echoed these sentiments, highlighting the importance of national resilience against terrorism.

articles.title: Targeted promotions ‘influential’ in luring Melbourne man who gambled $895,000 back to betting apps, inquest hears | Gambling | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Victorian inquest is investigating the death of 22-year-old Kyle Hudson, who lost over $895,000 gambling over four years. Forensic accountant Cameron Gray testified that Kyle Hudson received hundreds of inducements from betting companies like Sportsbet, Entain, and bet365, which he used to repeatedly deposit funds into his accounts and place high-value bets.  The inquest heard that Hudson experienced a brief period of net financial gain but ultimately incurred a significant loss before his death in July 2021. Representatives from Sportsbet, Entain, and Bet365 were questioned about their responses to Hudson's betting activity and the inducements offered to him, with one representative stating that it was not ideal for customers to bet cleverly using free money. The inquest continues.

articles.title: Trump's 'Golden Dome' will cost $1.2tn and might not stop all-out missile attack
articles.rephrased_article: The Congressional Budget Office estimates that the proposed "Golden Dome" missile defense system, designed to shield the US against ballistic and cruise missiles, will cost approximately $1.2 trillion over two decades. This figure is significantly higher than the initial $175 billion estimate and raises concerns about its effectiveness, as it might not be able to withstand a full-scale attack from Russia or China. The system's high cost has drawn criticism from Democratic Senator Jeff Merkley, who argues that it benefits defense contractors at the expense of working Americans.

articles.title: Berger Paints shares soar over 9% after Q4 net profit jumps 27% to Rs 335 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Berger Paints India reported a 6.1% increase in consolidated revenue for the March quarter, driven by healthy volume growth and favorable product mix. The company's gross margin reached its highest level in three years, aided by lower raw material prices and partial benefits from anti-dumping duty removal on titanium dioxide. Despite this positive performance, Berger Paints India saw a 4.6% decline in net profit for the fiscal year due to implementation of new labor codes and a warehouse fire. The company expects staggered price hikes to support gross margins and ongoing cost optimization efforts to maintain operating margins within their guided range.

articles.title: Man booked for using fake number plate on car to evade traffic challans in Hyderabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad Traffic Police and Attapur police arrested a 28-year-old man, Syed Rizwan Ali, for using a fake vehicle registration plate to evade traffic fines.  Ali affixed the fake plate on his car and used it to avoid generating challans against him. The case was registered under relevant provisions of the e Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Motor Vehicles Act. Police issued a notice to Ali under Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).

articles.title: Wembanyama returns, Spurs rout Wolves for 3-2 lead in NBA Playoff series | Basketball | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The San Antonio Spurs defeated the Minnesota Timberwolves 126-97 in Game 5 of their Western Conference semifinal series, taking a 3-2 lead.  Victor Wembanyama, who returned after being ejected in Game 4, led the Spurs with 27 points and 17 rebounds. The Spurs built a large lead in the second quarter before Minnesota rallied to tie the game in the third. However, San Antonio regained control in the fourth quarter and secured the victory.  The series continues Friday in Minneapolis.

articles.title: SBP says it has received $1.3bn tranche from IMF - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) approved $1.3 billion in disbursements to Pakistan on May 12, including SDR 760 million from the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and SDR 154 million from the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF). This brings the total amount disbursed under these arrangements to roughly $4.8 billion. The IMF acknowledged Pakistan's economic stability improvements but cautioned against heightened global volatility, particularly from the Middle East war.  IMF Deputy Managing Director and Acting Chair Nigel Clarke emphasized the need for continued macroeconomic discipline and accelerated reforms to mitigate future shocks and foster sustainable growth.

articles.title: Police drop charges against Palestinian Australian protester arrested at Isaac Herzog rally as more set to be withdrawn | Sydney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police withdrew charges against Eyad Shadid, a 25-year-old Palestinian Australian man, who was arrested during an anti-Isaac Herzog protest in Sydney. The withdrawal followed the decision by New South Wales police commissioner Mal Lanyon to drop charges laid under the now-defunct public assembly restriction declaration (Pard) law.  The Pard law, which restricted protests for 90 days after a terrorist attack, was struck down by the court of appeal, and lawyers are exploring whether other charges will be affected. The decision could have implications for future attempts by the government to control speech and protests on the basis of "social cohesion".

articles.title: Jason Collins: NBA's first openly gay player dies aged 47
articles.rephrased_article: Jason Collins, the first openly gay athlete in a major American professional team sport, died at age 47 after a valiant fight with glioblastoma. Adam Silver, NBA Commissioner, described Collins as an "inspiration" who helped make sports more inclusive.  Collins played for six teams over his 13-year career and was the first openly gay athlete to play in any of the four major US leagues. The New Jersey Nets expressed their heartbreak at his passing, noting his contributions to their franchise and his impact on the game. Former Stanford University coach Mike Montgomery also praised Collins's impact on the school.

articles.title: Silver jumps Rs 17,000/kg, gold soars to Rs 1.62 lakh/10g after centre hikes import duty. What should investors do? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX silver futures surged 6% to Rs 2,95,805 per kg on July 2026 delivery, while gold futures rose 6% to Rs 1,62,648 per 10 grams. The Indian government raised the customs duty on gold and silver imports to 15%, impacting international markets where spot gold fell slightly and silver rose.  Experts suggest traders book profits near target levels for both precious metals based on current volatility.

articles.title: Maya Higa: Who is Maya Higa? Twitch streamer makes history with first-ever TED Talk and standing ovation - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Maya Higa, a popular Twitch streamer and wildlife conservation advocate, delivered the first official TED Talk by a Twitch streamer.  During her speech in Vancouver, Canada, she discussed how her online platform has evolved into a mission-driven organization focused on animal education. Higa explained that livestreaming allows her to reach a global audience passionate about conservation, leading to the creation of Alveus Animal Sanctuary, which combines wildlife rescue with online broadcasting and educational outreach.  Her TED Talk received a standing ovation from the audience, highlighting the impact of online communities in driving real-world change.

articles.title: Prateek Yadav, Mulayam Singh Yadav’s younger son, passes away in Lucknow - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prateek Yadav, the son of former Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav and husband of BJP leader Aparna Bisht Yadav, passed away on Wednesday morning at the age of 38.  He was pronounced dead after being rushed to a hospital in Lucknow where doctors could not determine the cause of death.  Yogi Adityanath, the current Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, expressed condolences and offered prayers for the departed soul.

articles.title: Man who averted suicide attack nominated for ‘highest civil award’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Maryam Nawaz, Punjab Chief Minister, nominated Muhammad Liaqat Ali, a railway employee, for the country's highest civil award after he thwarted a potential suicide attack.  Liaqat Ali was grazing his livestock near a checkpost when he intercepted the attacker, preventing potential loss of life. Shehbaz Sharif, Prime Minister, and Hanif Abbasi, Federal Minister for Railways, also paid tribute to Liaqat Ali's bravery and sacrifice.

articles.title: Air India: Crisis deepens ahead of final Ahmedabad crash report
articles.rephrased_article: The Air India crisis deepens as the final report on the June 2025 crash of flight AI-171 is expected in a month.  With mounting losses, operational challenges, and airspace closures, the airline's ambitious turnaround plan faces significant hurdles. The recent resignation of CEO Campbell Wilson adds to the uncertainty, while concerns about safety and financial stability persist. Singapore Airlines, a 25.1% shareholder, has been linked to increased involvement in the carrier's future. Experts suggest that further financial support from the Tata Group and innovative financing arrangements are needed to address the airline's mounting losses.  The investigation into the crash is expected to reveal potential liabilities and reputational damage for Air India.

articles.title: A Zara dress, the Jim Reaper and a communist state: how Australia’s media interpreted the budget | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jim Chalmers, the Australian Treasurer, delivered his fifth budget on Wednesday, prompting a wave of negative reactions from Murdoch-owned tabloids. The Daily Telegraph and Herald Sun depicted him as a communist figure, while the Courier-Mail accused him of lying.  The Sydney Morning Herald offered a more balanced perspective, highlighting Labor's positive impacts on first home buyers and workers.  Meanwhile, Sky News Australia, The Daily Mail, and other outlets focused on Laura Chalmers' budget night outfit, with Daily Mail reporting that she chose a modest Zara dress.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump travels to China as conflict with Tehran looms large | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump departed for Beijing on Tuesday to meet with President Xi Jinping, stating the meeting would focus on trade and a "long talk" about Iran.  Esmaeil Baghaei, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman, criticized the US-Israel conflict as a war between a proud people and professional liars who fabricated justifications for atrocity.

articles.title: Kalyan Jewellers, Titan, other jewellery stocks crash up to 6% as Centre hikes gold customs duty to 15% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government has significantly increased customs duty on gold and silver imports, raising the effective import tax to 15% from 6%.  This move is expected to dampen demand in the jewelry sector, potentially leading to higher domestic prices and reduced consumer spending.  While organized players may fare better than smaller unorganized jewellers due to their stronger brands and inventory management, the increase could still negatively impact sales. The decision comes after Prime Minister Modi urged citizens to reduce gold purchases and curb imports, which have already fallen significantly in recent weeks.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth: Hegseth pushes Trump’s $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027 as Congress presses Pentagon over Iran war costs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, US defense secretary, defended President Donald Trump's proposed $1.5 trillion military budget before Congress, facing questions about the rising cost of the Iran war and its impact on military readiness.  Lawmakers expressed concerns about the conflict's expanding cost, with Pentagon officials reporting that it has now reached nearly $29 billion. Hegseth acknowledged efforts to increase weapons production but maintained that the administration is not straining US weapon supplies. The proposed budget includes significant funding for missile defense, aircraft procurement, drone technologies, and shipbuilding.

articles.title: Jammu and Kashmir leaders ask Omar Abdullah government to follow steps of Tamil Nadu CM Vijay on liquor ban - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Farooq Abdullah, president of the National Conference, stated that a complete ban on liquor sales in Jammu and Kashmir is not feasible due to revenue loss concerns, while opposition parties like the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and J&K Apni Party urged the government to follow Tamil Nadu's example by closing down liquor shops.  Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, the Kashmir chief cleric, argued that alcohol consumption is socially and religiously discouraged in the region and called for a complete ban on liquor sales to combat drug networks and societal harm.

articles.title: Iran war costs soar past $29bn as truce teeters - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump departed for China, vowing to "win peacefully or otherwise" in the ongoing conflict with Iran. The Pentagon reported that the war has cost over $29 billion since February, while Iran expanded its control of the Strait of Hormuz and held military exercises in Tehran.  The US welcomed UAE attacks on Iranian energy facilities last month, according to the Wall Street Journal. Meanwhile, Pakistan continued diplomatic efforts to mediate a ceasefire between Iran and the US.

articles.title: Australia has some of the world's costliest homes. Will scrapping tax breaks help?
articles.rephrased_article: Australia's housing crisis is a growing concern, with young people like Sebastian Muñoz-Najar expressing worry about the future affordability of homes. The government has proposed tax reforms to address intergenerational inequality in the housing market by scrapping lucrative tax breaks for investors. While some homeowners argue these changes will stifle investment and worsen the situation, critics believe they are necessary to bring housing back to being places to live rather than investments.  Experts suggest that addressing supply constraints through faster construction approvals is crucial alongside the proposed reforms. However, many young Australians feel let down by policymakers who prioritize the interests of existing homeowners over their own future housing security.

articles.title: Inquest into death of Clare Nowland after Tasering by NSW police aims to answer ‘outstanding questions’ | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An inquest into the death of 95-year-old Clare Nowland, who died after being Tasered by Constable Kristian James Samuel White at Yallambee Lodge nursing home in Cooma, is expected to focus on improving training for first responders dealing with aggressive dementia patients. The three-day inquest will examine systemic issues related to dementia care and training for aged care staff, police, and ambulance officers, as well as the communication between these groups.  State coroner Teresa O’Sullivan will examine whether Nowland's care was reasonable and if there were any contributing factors that led to her death.

articles.title: Peru presidential candidate Roberto Sanchez charged with financial crimes | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Roberto Sanchez, a presidential candidate for the Juntos por el Peru party, has been charged with financial crimes by the Peruvian public prosecutor’s office. The charges allege that Sanchez filed false financial disclosures related to campaign contributions between 2018 and 2020, receiving over 280,000 Peruvian soles in funds that were never disclosed. Prosecutors are seeking a five-year and four-month jail term for Sanchez and his permanent disqualification from holding the office of president for the Juntos por el Peru party. Sanchez's lawyer denies responsibility, claiming the party's treasurer was responsible for financial filings.

articles.title: Tata Power shares crash 7% after Q4. What are Goldman Sachs and Motilal Oswal saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Power's revenue for the March quarter declined 13% year-on-year to Rs 14,900 crore. However, EBITDA rose 10% to Rs 4,216 crore. The renewable energy segment contributed significantly to growth, with profit after tax before exceptional items rising 59% year-on-year.  Brokerage firms like Goldman Sachs and Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintain "Sell" and "Buy" ratings respectively on Tata Power, highlighting the company's strong long-term growth potential in rooftop solar and distribution, while acknowledging challenges with renewable energy generation execution.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Airstrikes: Saudi Arabia launched secret retaliatory airstrikes on Iran during regional war: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia carried out unpublicized airstrikes on Iran in late March as retaliation for attacks within the kingdom, marking a significant shift in its approach to the regional conflict. The strikes followed a series of Iranian missile and drone attacks targeting US military bases, civilian sites, airports, and oil infrastructure across the Gulf Cooperation Council states.  The actions were seen as a response to the escalating tensions between Iran and the United States, which had begun after US and Israel launched airstrikes on Iran in February.  These strikes, along with similar actions by the United Arab Emirates, demonstrated a regional confrontation that remained largely out of public view.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly session LIVE: CM Vijay moves resolution seeking confidence vote - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, faces a floor test in the state assembly on May 13, 2026.  The test will require him to prove his alliance's majority after rebel AIADMK leaders led by former Ministers S.P. Velumani and C.Ve. Shanmugam announced support for his ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). The floor test comes as AIADMK MLAs from the faction supporting Edappadi K. Palaniswami have declared their intention to vote against the confidence motion.

articles.title: Fuel levy yields lowest fiscal deficit in nearly three decades - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan recorded its lowest fiscal deficit in at least 27 years, reaching 0.7 percent of GDP during the July-March period.  The improvement was driven by higher provincial contributions, strong petroleum levy collections, and lower interest payments. Revenue-to-GDP ratio fell to 11.4 percent, while expenditure increased across most categories, particularly defense and subsidies. The State Bank of Pakistan also continued to post healthy profits due to high interest rates.

articles.title: Trump-Xi summit: A decade on, the US president returns to a stronger and more assertive China
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump returns to China this week for a meeting with Xi Jinping, where the agenda will include trade, technology and Taiwan.  The Chinese economy has undergone significant changes in recent years, including investments in renewable energy, robotics, and artificial intelligence. Trump's visit comes amid strained relations between the two superpowers, with concerns about China's rise as a competitor and its potential for technological dominance. The meeting will likely focus on trade tensions, but also on issues such as Iran and the global economy.  China has been actively promoting itself as a leader in innovation and technology, while Trump seeks to secure commitments from Beijing to increase US exports.   The visit is seen by some as a sign of China's growing influence and its ability to navigate international relations.

articles.title: ‘Blatant disregard for rights’: concern grows over Gabon’s social media clampdown | Gabon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gabon’s government indefinitely suspended major social media platforms in February, citing security concerns and the spread of misinformation.  This action led to a surge in VPN usage but also resulted in arrests and account suspensions for activists and opposition members. Nelly Ngabima, a controversial activist, reported threats from government officials who accused her of identity theft. Rights groups have condemned the restrictions as a violation of freedom of expression. Despite temporary lifting of the ban in April, new regulations mandate verified information from social media users or face fines and imprisonment.  The crackdown on dissent has been criticized by opposition figures and human rights organizations.

articles.title: Opposition parties are spreading panic over PM’s voluntary, precautionary appeal: BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) criticized opposition parties, accusing them of spreading misinformation about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for voluntary gold purchases and foreign travel restrictions.  BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia stated that the government has taken measures to protect India's economy and there is no shortage of essential commodities.

articles.title: Supreme Court to hear ED plea against bail granted to accused in West Bengal coal scam case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court agreed to hear the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED) appeal against the grant of anticipatory bail to Anup Majee, accused of leading a coal mining scam in West Bengal. The ED claims that Mr. Majee operated with the “active” assistance of several leaders from the All India Trinamool Congress.  The court sought Mr. Majee’s response to the agency's plea challenging a June 2025 order granting him bail in a money laundering case registered in 2020.

articles.title: Cong MLCs meet Surjewala, seeks clarity on leadership issue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: MLCs from the Congress government in Karnataka met with Randeep Singh Surjewala, a Congress general secretary, in New Delhi to discuss potential leadership changes. The MLCs requested an early clarification on the issue and also demanded that at least five members be included in the state cabinet if there is a reshuffle.

articles.title: Over ₹1 crore cash, AK-47 rifles recovered from Maoist hideouts, say police - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Narayanpur district, Chhattisgarh, have recovered over ₹1.01 crore in cash and a significant amount of arms and ammunition, including AK-47 and SLR rifles, from former Maoist hideouts or dumps in the past month.  The largest recovery was made on May 9th at Nelangur village near the Chhattisgarh-Maharashtra border, where ₹84 lakh in cash was found alongside two AK-47 rifles.

articles.title: A nearly 40-year-old pending case spurs Supreme Court to declare speedy trial a ‘human right’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that the right to a speedy trial is a human right, while also directing an investigation into judicial backlog and bail pleas in Uttar Pradesh. The case involves five police constables who brawled over their canteen cook's food choices in 1989.  This decision comes after a nearly four-decade-long legal battle.

articles.title: Free vaccination for cervical cancer until May 31 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector G. Priyanka announced the final phase of the HPV vaccination campaign against cervical cancer in the district, urging all eligible girls to receive the vaccine before May 31, 2026.  The campaign aims to vaccinate a total of 22,358 girls aged 14 and under, with only 34% currently vaccinated as of the current date. The vaccination facility will cease operation after this deadline.

articles.title: Summer showers, strong winds lash district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Strong summer showers with accompanying strong winds caused widespread damage across the district on Tuesday evening, May 12, 2026.  Ten houses sustained damage in various taluks, including Kothamangalam, Muvattupuzha, Kochi, and Thripunithura. Tree branches fell on vehicles and disrupted traffic, while a roof collapse at an automobile company building caused further damage. Fire and Rescue Services cleared fallen trees and restored traffic flow.  Authorities warned of continued strong summer showers in the coming days.

articles.title: Vijay urges Union Minister to secure the release of six T.N. fisherfolk arrested by Lankan Navy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay requested the Union Minister for External Affairs S. Jaishankar to use diplomatic channels to secure the early release and safe repatriation of six Tamil Nadu fishermen arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy on May 10th for allegedly crossing the International Maritime Boundary Line while fishing. The fishermen, identified as Alex, Anthoni Rajan, Santhana Alocias, Arul They Britto, Albert, and Sahaya Selvashanu, were apprehended along with their fishing boat.

articles.title: Meeting to review progress of literary corridor project in Kozhikode city - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kozhikode Mayor O. Sadasivan and other civic body members will meet with officials from Impact Kerala, a special purpose vehicle for the Kerala Infrastructure Investment Fund Board (KIIFB), on Wednesday to discuss the development of literary corridors. The initiative aims to uphold the city's UNESCO 'City of Literature' title, which was announced in late 2024 but has yet to materialize despite receiving funding from the KIIFB.  The meeting will review the project's progress and address the allocation of ₹3 crore for UNESCO-branded activities and international literary summits within the Corporation Budget.

articles.title: Kash Patel denies excessive drinking allegations as ‘total farce’ in Senate hearing | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kash Patel, the embattled FBI director, denied allegations of excessive drinking and unexplained absences during a congressional hearing. Democrats challenged him over reports in the Atlantic that described his behavior as "extremely alarming" and argued it constituted a "gross dereliction of duty."  Patel sued the magazine and its author, seeking $250 million in damages. He accused the senator who raised the issue, Chris Van Hollen, of engaging in similar misconduct while on taxpayer dollars. The FBI director denied ordering polygraph tests to identify leaks and stated that no resources were used to investigate negative press about him or his leadership.

articles.title: Kozhikode Corporation’s official website to be relaunched - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Information Kerala Mission (IKM) will relaunch the Kozhikode Corporation's official website in two months. The project aims to modernize the platform, which has been criticized for its outdated design and lack of updates.  The redesigned website will feature regular updates on council meetings, financial statements, and administrative sections, as well as separate sections for hearing committees, water committees, health offices, and health circles. It will also include an RTI section, e-governance services like e-payment for property tax and building permits, and access to e-services such as birth and death certificates, marriage certificates, and government orders. The website will also incorporate a GIS system for interactive mapping of municipal infrastructure and service locations.

articles.title: Three-quarters of UK millionaires would be happy to pay more tax, research finds | The super-rich | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Patriotic Millionaires UK, a nonpartisan network of wealthy individuals, conducted a survey of 501 millionaires in the UK. The research found that nine out of ten millionaires are proud to live in Britain and would be willing to pay more taxes to fund public assets. While concerns exist about high net worth individuals leaving the country due to rising taxes, the survey suggests these fears are largely unfounded.  The findings indicate that millionaires prioritize healthcare workers' departures over their own emigration, highlighting a strong sense of national pride among this demographic.

articles.title: Elephant dies after fall near Nadugani ghat road - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A young female elephant died after falling from a steep cliff near Nilambur, India.  Forest officials confirmed the presence of fresh tiger pugmarks near the carcass, but concluded that the elephant's death was likely caused by the fall itself. The elephant's trunk had been partially eaten by a tiger after it died two days prior. Forest officials moved the carcass to a convenient location and buried it.

articles.title: Older people risk mental decline if they do long hours of caring, UK study shows | Carers | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Carers UK and researchers at University College London have found that providing care for 5 to 9 hours a week can boost brain health, while long hours of care lead to accelerated cognitive decline. The study compared the cognitive health of 2,765 carers aged 50 or over with 2,765 non-carers and found that those providing more than 50 hours of care experienced faster mental decline.  The researchers suggest that the government should provide more support for "intensive" carers through better access to funded formal and replacement care. The findings highlight the need for increased support for family caregivers who often face significant stress and burnout.

articles.title: BJP targets DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin over Sanatana Dharma remarks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) condemned Udhayanidhi Stalin, a DMK leader, for his remarks on Sanatana Dharma in the Tamil Nadu Assembly.  G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister for Coal and Mines, accused the DMK of "poisonous politics" and "anti-Hindu rhetoric." The BJP also criticized the Congress party's support for Stalin's comments and questioned Vijay, the newly elected Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, on his silence regarding the issue.

articles.title: Labour must fulfil promise to introduce clean air act, charities urge | Air pollution | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 60 charities have urged Ministers to introduce a new clean air act that would ban wood burning, clear diesel vehicles from the roads, and force councils to reduce pollution. The call comes after the government has made no move to reinstate a proposed clean air act dropped from its election manifesto in 2023.  The charities point out that dirty air is costing the country billions of pounds annually and harming public health. They also criticize the government for failing to enforce existing regulations against wood burning despite thousands of complaints, while acknowledging efforts by the Scottish government to address concerns about rural communities' reliance on wood-burning stoves.

articles.title: India's global market cap share falls after D-Street's slide this year - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a weakening global market, Indian benchmarks maintain a high price-earnings (P/E) multiple of around 20.6, exceeding some emerging markets but lagging behind developed indices like the US's Dow Jones and S&P 500.  While India retains fifth place in global market cap rankings, Taiwan and South Korea are closing the gap, fueled by semiconductor company rallies. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have been selling Indian equities significantly, contributing to a record outflow of $18.9 billion in 2025.

articles.title: Honduras mayor arrested for masterminding environmentalist’s killing | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Honduran authorities arrested Adan Funez, former mayor of Tocoa, for allegedly orchestrating the 2024 assassination of environmental activist Juan Lopez.  F Nunez was captured at his home on Tuesday and joins two other suspects, businessman Hector Eduardo Méndez and Juan Angel Ramos Gallegos, who are accused of criminal association to the detriment of fundamental rights. The arrests follow years of accusations against Funez by religious and environmental leaders and come after a string of prior arrests related to Lopez's death.  The trial is set for next June.

articles.title: What happened between Trevv and ChudTheBuilder? Nashville confrontation turns into aggravated robbery controversy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ChudTheBuilder and internet personality Trevv are embroiled in a public feud following an incident in Nashville on May 10, 2026.  Trevv was filmed grabbing ChudTheBuilder’s hat and running away while mocking him. ChudTheBuilder accused Trevv of assault and robbery, claiming the hat was part of his person and that Trevv admitted to carrying a weapon. The situation has gained attention due to both creators' controversial online behavior earlier this year.  Neither the FBI nor Nashville police have confirmed any investigation or charges related to the incident.

articles.title: AIADMK rebel MLAs to back TVK in Tamil Nadu floor test - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, called on rebel AIADMK leaders S.P. Velumani and C.Ve. Shanmugam ahead of a floor test in the state Assembly. The rebels declared Velumani as the "AIADMK Legislature Party leader" but Edappadi K. Palaniswami, the AIADMK general secretary, claimed he was the leader.  O.S. Manian, a senior leader supporting Palaniswami, stated that all 47 AIADMK legislators had signed a letter electing Palaniswami as the Legislature Party leader and that the rebels were attempting to lure MLAs. The rebels, who have accused Palaniswami of collaborating with the DMK, are seeking ministerial positions.

articles.title: Don’t reach for the bug spray: scientists find insects may feel pain after crickets nurse sore antenna | Animal behaviour | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Associate Prof Thomas White, an entomologist from the University of Sydney, and Associate Prof Kate Umbers from Western Sydney University, studied crickets to determine if they experience pain.  The study found that crickets exposed to a heated soldering iron on their antenna groomed it more frequently and for longer periods than those who received a non-heated probe or no treatment. This suggests the crickets were directing attention to the affected area, indicating a response similar to what humans would observe in animals experiencing pain. The research highlights the potential for insects to feel pain and challenges human perception of insect sentience.

articles.title: Work on 1.1 MLD sewage treatment plant at Edakochi expected to be completed by August - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi Corporation is nearing completion of a 1.1 MLD sewage treatment plant (STP) in Edakochi, Division 16, with work expected to be finished by August. The project, funded under the Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) program, aims to treat wastewater from approximately 2,000 households.  The system includes a household-level collection network, conveyance system, and treatment unit, with a total length of 17.9 km of sewage pipeline being laid within the division. Tidal flooding has posed challenges to the project's progress.

articles.title: Quantum jump in followers of T.N. CMO’s social media handles after Vijay’s swearing-in - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the new Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, saw a significant increase in followers on his official social media accounts, particularly Instagram, following his swearing-in ceremony. The number of followers jumped from 4.56 lakh to 1.9 million within just two days.  The surge is attributed to the strong presence of the Tamizhaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) across social media platforms and the popularity of Mr. Vijay himself, a celebrated actor. Officials attribute the increase to the active engagement of young followers, particularly those associated with the TVK's youth wing or IT team in various districts.

articles.title: ​Split wide open: On the AIADMK, Tamil Nadu politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The AIADMK, the principal opposition party in Tamil Nadu, is facing a split after a second consecutive election defeat.  C. Joseph Vijay, the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has indicated his support for the dissident group led by former Ministers C.Ve. Shanmugam and S.P. Velumani. The dissidents have announced their intention to support the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government.  The Palaniswami camp claims that all 47 legislators gave written consent for Edappadi K. Palaniswami as the AIADMK legislature party leader, citing a Supreme Court verdict in the Shiv Sena case. The Assembly Speaker will need to assess the merits of both groups' claims and may soon have to draw on his experience and legal advice.

articles.title: ST delegation meets CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Siddaramaiah, the Chief Minister of Karnataka, has promised to convene an all-party meeting to discuss the inclusion of a 56% reservation matrix in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution.  He also assured V.S. Ugrappa, former MP and leader of the Samana Manaskara Vedike, that he will take an all-party delegation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi to advocate for this legislation. The state government has been working to overturn a legal stay on the 56% reservation, with legal experts being consulted and a special leave petition potentially filed in the Supreme Court.

articles.title: The legacy of women Ministers in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, was sworn in alongside Keerthana, who won from the Sivakasi assembly constituency, marking a significant milestone for women in state politics.  While social media erroneously claimed she was the first woman Cabinet member, women have served as Ministers in the Tamil Nadu Cabinet for decades, with the first instance occurring in 1946 under T. Prakasam. Since then, women have been consistently included in the state's Cabinets.

articles.title: Marty Makary departs FDA after clashes with Trump over fruit-flavored vapes | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Marty Makary, former commissioner of the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), resigned on Tuesday.  Donald Trump confirmed his replacement, Kyle Diamantas, who previously served as the top food official at the agency. Makary's tenure was marked by controversy, including clashes with lawmakers over drug regulation decisions and a review of mifepristone. Republican Senator Josh Hawley welcomed Makary's departure, while Democratic Senator Dick Durbin praised his commitment to resisting Trump's requests that would harm America.

articles.title: Floor test proceedings in Tamil Nadu Assembly to be telecast live - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's Legislative Assembly will broadcast the floor test proceedings live for the first time.  This decision comes after Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar directed Chief Minister to seek a vote of confidence in the assembly by May 13th. The move marks a significant change from previous practices where only certain parts of the Assembly proceedings were televised.

articles.title: EBay rejects GameStop’s $56bn bid as ‘neither credible nor attractive’ | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: eBay has rejected a $56 billion takeover bid from GameStop, citing financing concerns and the lack of a credible plan.  The company's CEO, Jamie Iannone, highlighted eBay's recent growth and stock performance since his appointment six years ago. Ryan Cohen, GameStop's CEO, who holds a 5% stake in eBay, has hinted at taking the offer directly to shareholders but faces challenges due to financing doubts and potential long-term growth impacts.  Analysts have expressed skepticism about the deal's viability.

articles.title: Conan O’Brien to return as Oscars host for third year in a row | Oscars | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Conan O’Brien will return to host the 99th Academy Awards in 2027, according to Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Science leaders.  O'Brien hosted the last two ceremonies to positive reviews and will be joined by executive producers Raj Kapoor and Katy Mullan. The show saw a dip in viewership this year but engagement on social media increased significantly. Craig Erwich, president of the Disney Television Group, praised O’Brien for creating "remarkable energy" around the Oscars.  The 99th Academy Awards will be broadcast live on ABC from the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles on March 14, 2027.

articles.title: 'His kids are here, he's being deported': Top LA restaurant owner arrested by ICE after his own worker ratted him out - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Lool, owner of two Los Angeles restaurants, was detained by ICE agents last week while collecting supplies for a catering event. The arrest stemmed from a former employee's claim that a firearm was kept at the restaurant, violating Lool's parole conditions.  Lool, who is originally from Guatemala and has a criminal record dating back to the 1990s, faces deportation as his business partner and girlfriend describe the situation as "devastating" for their family and businesses.

articles.title: Metal screw removed from baby’s lung at Government Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors at the Government Chengalpattu Medical College Hospital successfully removed a small metal screw from the right lung of a one-year-old girl who presented with breathing difficulties. The procedure, performed by a team led by associate professor of paediatrics Sarath Balaji, involved a minimally invasive bronchoscope and forceps. The child has since recovered and is doing well.

articles.title: Inside US Democrats’ Gaza fight – and what it means for 2028 elections | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Democrats are grappling with a split over Israel policy, with the party facing questions about its future after a shift in voter expectations. A new report suggests this division may have cost votes in the 2024 election.  The issue is particularly significant for Kamala Harris, who is considering another run for president in 2028. The episode explores the implications of this internal conflict on the party's future direction.

articles.title: South Carolina Republicans defy Trump’s demands for redistricting | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: South Carolina state senators rejected plans to redraw the state's congressional map after pressure from Donald Trump, citing concerns about potential negative consequences for voter turnout and minority representation.  The proposal, which would have eliminated a Democratic-held congressional district, was voted down by a narrow margin despite calls from Trump to approve it. Shane Massey, the Republican majority leader in the state senate, argued that redrawing the map could diminish South Carolina's influence and urged his colleagues to prioritize the interests of their constituents over political expediency.

articles.title: From election drubbing to minister resignations: Why Keir Starmer is in trouble? All FAQs answered - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is facing a growing rebellion within his own party after Labour's disappointing local election results.  Over 80 MPs have called for his resignation or a timetable for his departure, with three ministers quitting in protest. The resignations highlight deep divisions within the party over Starmer's leadership and his handling of the Peter Mandelson controversy. This crisis has intensified speculation about potential changes at No. 10 Downing Street, as Nigel Farage’s Reform UK continues to chip away at Labour's traditional working-class support base.  While no formal challenge has been launched yet, Starmer faces increasing pressure to address the concerns of his party and regain public trust.

articles.title: Over 25 TASMAC outlets identified in Vellore and nearby districts for permanent closure - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tasmac, the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation Limited, is permanently closing 25 liquor outlets in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts. The move follows a directive from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay to shut down 717 Tasmac outlets within 500 meters of places of worship, educational institutions, and bus stands across the state.  The process involves identifying outlets near sensitive public spaces, with stocks being transferred to godowns and staff redeployed to other locations. The decision aims to address public concerns about proximity to these areas.

articles.title: US faces rising costs with Iran war driving energy prices, inflation higher | Inflation News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US consumer prices rose by 0.6 percent in April, marking the biggest annual increase in almost three years, driven by soaring energy costs.  The surge in energy prices, including petrol, was attributed to the US-Israel war on Iran and led to a 3.8 percent annual increase in overall prices. The average price for a gallon of petrol is now $4.50, up from $2.98 when the conflict began. Economists predict that the price increases will be temporary but remain concerned about the long-term impact of the war on Iran and the global economy.

articles.title: Death of man struck by Frontier Airlines plane ruled suicide by medical examiner | Denver | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Mott, a 41-year-old man, died by suicide after jumping an airport fence and being struck by a departing Frontier Airlines flight. The incident occurred on Friday at Denver International Airport, where the perimeter fencing spans 36 miles and ground detection sensors triggered an alarm before Mott reached the runway.  The investigation is ongoing, with authorities examining whether mental health issues played a role in his actions. While the airport's security measures are considered "layered," officials are reviewing potential improvements after Friday's deadly collision.

articles.title: What happened at Phuket cafe where Indian tourists fainted one by one 'for no obvious reason'? 1 dead - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 26-year-old Indian tourist, Kushagra Agarwal, died at a Phuket cafe after collapsing on May 9th.  The Indian embassy is providing support to his family and is working with Thai authorities investigating the incident. Three other members of the group also fainted at the same cafe, one in a coma and two requiring further treatment. Police are looking into possible illicit substances or alcohol as a contributing factor but have not released any findings.

articles.title: West Godavari district of A.P. bets big on green silica industry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: West Godavari district, in Andhra Pradesh, is transforming its agricultural waste into a valuable resource through the processing of rice husk.  The byproduct, previously discarded or burned, is now being converted into high-value industrial materials like silica gel and precipitated silica. This shift is driven by rising demand for these products in sectors such as the automotive industry, electronics, and food production. The Andhra Pradesh government has supported this initiative through policies offering financial incentives to encourage rice millers to diversify their operations.  The district's efforts aim to create a zero-waste industrial hub and boost rural economic growth.

articles.title: US court pauses decision blocking Trump’s 10 percent global tariff | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A US federal appeals court has temporarily paused a lower court decision to block President Donald Trump's 10 percent global tariff. The stay allows the White House time to respond to the plaintiffs, who argue that the tariffs are an abuse of executive power and have negatively impacted consumers.
