The ruling comes as the tariffs face legal challenges under Section 122 of the Trade Act and are scheduled to expire in July unless extended by Congress.

articles.title: FBI chief Kash Patel spars with top Democrat over allegations of excessive drinking on the job – US politics live | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kash Patel, the embattled FBI director, clashed with Senator Chris Van Hollen during a Senate appropriations subcommittee hearing about the 2027 budget for his agency.  Patel denied allegations of excessive drinking and unexplained absences while on the job, calling them "a total farce."  Van Hollen accused Patel of spreading false information about a trip to El Salvador that was staged by the Salvadoran government. The hearing comes as Patel faces scrutiny over reports of his behavior, including alleged heavy drinking and frequent absences from work.

articles.title: What happened at Phuket cafe where Indian tourists fainted one by one 'for no obvious reason'? 1 dead - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 26-year-old Indian tourist, Kushagra Agarwal, died at a Phuket cafe after collapsing and three others fainted simultaneously. The incident occurred on May 9th and the Indian embassy is providing support to the deceased's family.  The four men were reportedly at a cafe around 11 pm before losing consciousness one by one. Two of the men remain in a coma, while the remaining three are reported as stable. Police are investigating but have not released any conclusions about the cause of the incident.

articles.title: AICC begins consultations with Kerala leaders in New Delhi to decide on Congress’ CM candidate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi, and Mallikarjun Kharge met with top Kerala leaders in New Delhi on Tuesday to discuss the selection of a Chief Minister nominee for the state. The high command is seeking bipartisan support from former KPCC presidents, Congress MLAs-elect, and other key figures to restore organizational stability after the party's recent victory.  The meeting considered several potential candidates, including K.C. Venugopal, V.D. Satheesan, Ramesh Chennithala, and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra.  K. Muraleedharan, a KPCC insider, stated that the high command would consider popular opinion in addition to legislative party numbers when making their decision.

articles.title: Trump downplays US-Iran differences as he heads to Beijing to meet with Xi | Xi Jinping News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump departed the White House for Beijing, where he will meet with Xi Jinping.  The upcoming meetings will focus on trade and are expected to be the first face-to-face exchanges since October 2025. While US officials have emphasized the importance of trade, Trump has given conflicting messages about the prominence of the US-Israel war on Iran in the discussions.  Despite Beijing's opposition to the war, it is expected that both sides will seek to avoid a return to the tariff war and address concerns over arms sales to Taiwan.

articles.title: Online safety campaigners reveal Starmer frustrations after Phillips exit | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jess Phillips, a Labour politician, resigned from the government, criticizing Keir Starmer for failing to act on proposals to stop children sending and receiving nude images.  She accused Starmer of delaying action despite solutions being available for over a year. The Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) also expressed frustration with the lack of urgency in tackling online child sexual abuse, highlighting that 91% of reported criminal cases involved self-generated imagery. Campaigners urged the government to force tech companies to implement image blockers on children's devices as a default feature, but these proposals have faced resistance within Downing Street.

articles.title: Foreign student enrolment at US universities falls by 20% amid ‘restrictive government policies’: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US universities are experiencing a significant decline in foreign student enrollment, with experts attributing the drop to Donald Trump’s restrictive immigration policies. A new report from international education groups found that international student enrolment fell by 20% for the spring 2026 semester, with graduate enrollment declining even more sharply.  Analysts warn that these trends could worsen as many students currently enrolled applied before Trump's administration implemented stricter visa rules and travel bans, impacting universities financially and academically. The report highlights a growing trend of international students choosing other countries like Asia for higher education due to the perceived hostility towards foreign students in the US.

articles.title: Ever since Elon Musk took over, banning social media accounts became common: Iltija Mufti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Iltija Mufti, daughter of former Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti, is considering legal action against Meta for withholding her Twitter and Facebook accounts.  She claims she was not notified before the accounts were suspended and has been unable to contact Meta.  Ms. Mufti believes this is part of a pattern of silencing voices critical of the government in Kashmir. She argues that banning political social media accounts is an attack on democracy.

articles.title: Basketball star Brandon Clarke, Memphis Grizzlies forward, dies at age 29 | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brandon Clarke, a 29-year-old basketball star for the Memphis Grizzlies, has died.  Local media reports indicate he was pronounced dead at a home in California's San Fernando Valley after emergency workers responded to a call for help. The cause of death is unknown, but local media reports suggest he was found dead at his residence. Adam Silver, NBA Commissioner, and Priority Sports, Clarke's agency, expressed their condolences.

articles.title: Starmer hopes to regain momentum with unveiling of dozens of bills in king’s speech | King's speech | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer's government will unveil a package of 35 bills to be debated in the next parliamentary session, encompassing housing, immigration, and EU alignment. The announcement comes amid calls for his resignation from within his own party.  The king will read out these proposals during Wednesday's state opening of parliament, which is expected to be a significant event for Starmer as he seeks to regain political momentum.

articles.title: Major ICE crackdown on 10,000 foreign students on OPT; 'fake companies' being operated from India - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ICE director Todd M Lyons announced a crackdown on the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program, citing fraud and irregularities involving nearly 10,000 foreign students.  Lyons stated that the program's size has ballooned since its creation under the Bush administration, with hundreds of thousands of students working in the US instead of the anticipated few thousand. ICE investigators have uncovered suspicious employers, including empty buildings, locked doors, and financial red flags like breaches of contract and suspicious cash movement across countries. The findings suggest a coordinated employer network where multiple OPT workers are employed at nearly identical websites.

articles.title: NEET-UG examination 2026: One suspect arrested from Nashik - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) cancelled the NEET-UG examination for 2026 after an alleged paper leak, leading to the arrest of a suspect in Maharashtra. The Rajasthan Police requested the Maharashtra police to detain the individual who was apprehended after changing his appearance.  The cancellation has drawn criticism from opposition leaders, including Rohit Pawar, who pointed out that the state government's new law against paper leaks is insufficient and called for stricter action against those involved. A CBI inquiry into the matter has been initiated.

articles.title: WHO chief says 'work not over' after hantavirus evacuation - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated that the global public health risk from the hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius is low, but the situation could change.  He emphasized the need for continued monitoring and highlighted the importance of following WHO guidelines, including quarantine measures. While some countries adopted different approaches to handling returning evacuees, WHO officials urged adherence to their recommendations.

articles.title: Sam Altman says Elon Musk wanted 90 percent of OpenAI in high-stakes trial | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, testified in a trial against Elon Musk alleging that Musk sought a majority stake in the company, not a charity.  Altman stated that Musk's investment was based on the intention to develop AI for humanity, but OpenAI shifted its focus towards a for-profit venture. The outcome of this trial could determine the future of OpenAI, its leadership, and products like ChatGPT.

articles.title: Capacity of lifts not kept up with UK obesity levels, study shows | Obesity | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers have found that lifts in the UK and mainland Europe are no longer large enough to accommodate the increasing weight of adults, raising concerns about safety and equity. A study presented at the European Congress on Obesity found that maximum lift capacities haven't increased since around 2004 despite average adult weights rising significantly. The research suggests manufacturers have focused on floor space rather than weight, failing to account for the increase in obesity rates. Prof Nick Finer, president of the International Prader-Willi Syndrome Organisation and lead author of the study, emphasized that this issue impacts not only safety but also social inclusion by creating stigma for individuals with obesity.

articles.title: Suparco says Eidul Azha likely to fall on May 27 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Suparco, the Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission, predicts Eidul Azha will fall on May 27.  The commission forecasts that the new moon of Zilhajj 1447 AH will be visible on May 17th at sunset. Suparco estimates a favorable chance of sighting the crescent moon, contingent upon clear weather conditions and visibility. The final decision regarding Eidul Azha's date rests with the Central Ruet-i-Hilal Committee of Pakistan.

articles.title: Starmer given a lifeline after Streeting challenge fails to materialise | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following a challenge from Wes Streeting, Keir Starmer has survived a leadership threat within the Labour Party.  Despite several of his allies resigning and calls for his departure, Starmer maintains he will continue as prime minister.  The health secretary, Streeting, is facing questions about his ability to launch a formal challenge, with some sources suggesting he may not have the necessary support.  Several senior Labour figures, including David Lammy, are urging party members to focus on governing and supporting Starmer.

articles.title: Baltimore ship crash: U.S. slaps criminal cases against Singapore, Chennai firms and Indian national - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The U.S. Justice Department has filed criminal charges against Synergy Marine of Singapore, Synergy Maritime of Chennai, and Indian technical superintendent Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair in connection with the 2024 collision between the container ship Dali and a bridge in Baltimore. The charges include conspiracy, obstruction of an agency proceeding, false statements, and pollution.  The department alleges that the incident caused an economic loss of $5 billion and resulted in the death of six construction workers. Synergy managed the ship, which was owned by Grace Ocean Private Limited.

articles.title: Starmer defiant as calls for his resignation grow, several ministers quit - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, leader of the Labour Party, faced calls for his resignation following significant losses in local elections, prompting several junior ministers to step down.  These resignations, including those from Miatta Fahnbulleh, Jess Phillips, and Zubir Ahmed, fueled speculation that Starmer could face a similar fate to former Prime Minister Boris Johnson. While over 80 Labour lawmakers have called for his departure or a timetable for his exit, the party's rules require a fifth of its members in the House of Commons to publicly support a candidate before a leadership contest can be triggered.  Starmer stated he would continue to lead despite the losses, emphasizing the need for governing.

articles.title: Israel sent Iron Dome anti-missile batteries and personnel to UAE: US envoy | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mike Huckabee, US ambassador to Israel, confirmed that Israel has deployed Iron Dome batteries and personnel to the UAE to help defend against Iranian attacks.  Huckabee praised the UAE's strong ties with Israel and urged Gulf states to choose a side in the conflict between Israel and Iran. The deployment highlights the deepening relationship between Israel and the UAE, despite regional countries facing Iranian missile strikes since the US and Israel began attacking Iran.

articles.title: President, PM pay tribute to shepherd who sacrificed his life while averting suicide attack in Attock - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif honored a local shepherd, Liaqat, who was killed while thwarting a suicide attack in Attock's Jand tehsil.  Liaqat confronted a suspicious individual near a security post on the Punjab-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border, prompting the suspect to detonate himself. President Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif praised Liaqat’s bravery and sacrifice, emphasizing his dedication to national security against terrorism.

articles.title: Streeting to meet Starmer on Wednesday as the prime minister defies calls to step down – as it happened | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jess Phillips, Keir Starmer, and other Labour MPs have called for the prime minister to resign.  Several ministers resigned on Tuesday, including Miatta Fahnbulleh and Alex Davies-Jones.  The number of MPs calling for Starmer's resignation has grown over the last 48 hours, but he remains in office.  Wes Streeting met with Starmer to discuss his concerns. Donald Trump offered advice on energy policy. Buckingham Palace is reportedly concerned about the political crisis and its potential impact on the State Opening of Parliament.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu’s political transition, growth story faultlines - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by C. Joseph Vijay, won the Tamil Nadu elections, raising questions about whether its victory signifies a departure from the Dravidian Model of development or simply an extension of it.  TVK's election manifesto suggests continuity with existing economic policies despite the challenges facing Tamil Nadu, including internal issues and external factors like shifts in federal relations and global economic changes. The state has historically demonstrated that inclusive economic growth can be achieved alongside social progress through investments in infrastructure, healthcare, and education.

articles.title: H-1B scam: Texas company owned by Chinese national sued for selling foreign workers visas for $20,000 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has filed a lawsuit against Golden Qi Holdings LLC, a Texas company owned by a Chinese national, Yuan Yao. The lawsuit alleges that the company ran fake childcare businesses to fraudulently obtain H-1B visas for foreign workers.  The case cites examples of non-existent facilities and claims that the companies received federal loans intended for childcare operations but were not used for those purposes.  Paxton stated his office will continue to investigate suspected H-1B visa fraud in North Texas, where authorities say some companies may be running "ghost" operations while sponsoring foreign workers.

articles.title: Voters head to the polls in the Bahamas for high-stakes snap election | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Voters in the Bahamas are casting ballots in a snap election to decide whether Prime Minister Philip Davis and his ruling Progressive Liberal Party (PLP) will secure a second consecutive term.  Davis, seeking to become the first leader of the Caribbean island nation to serve two terms in nearly 30 years, faces a challenge from the Free National Movement (FNM) led by Michael Pintard. The election is being held due to concerns about holding the vote during hurricane season and comes after a strong showing for the PLP in the 2021 snap election.

articles.title: 'Children paying intolerable price': UN condemns child death toll from Israel's West Bank operations - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations condemned the escalating violence in the occupied West Bank, particularly targeting children. The UN's children's agency reported at least 70 Palestinian children killed since the start of 2025 and another 850 injured, with most deaths attributed to live ammunition from Israeli forces.  The UN also highlighted the impact of settler attacks, mass displacement, and restrictions on access to essential services, citing a dramatic increase in barriers across the West Bank.

articles.title: More than 110 Nobel laureates call on Iran to release gravely ill activist Narges Mohammadi | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 110 Nobel laureates have called for the immediate release of Narges Mohammadi, an Iranian human rights activist and Nobel peace prize laureate, who was transferred to hospital in critical condition.  The group urged the Iranian authorities and the international community to act without delay to secure her release and ensure continued access to medical treatment. The activists have expressed concerns over Mohammadi’s deteriorating health, including severe weight loss, unstable blood pressure, and cardiac symptoms while imprisoned. They also highlighted that she has been denied specialized medical care for months.  The Nobel laureates demand the dropping of all charges against Mohammadi and her unconditional release.

articles.title: The challenge to not breach the limit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government announced the resumption of public recruitment for 56,432 posts after a year-long hiatus due to reservation issues. The new quota matrix has been met with resentment from job aspirants and some groups, as it altered the overall reservation percentage and internal quotas for Scheduled Castes (SCs).

articles.title: 'Indians hiring Indians': Former Google contractor says he was asked to train his replacement - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Vivien, a former Google contractor, alleges that his job was outsourced to India, the Philippines, and Ireland after an Indian-origin employee replaced him.  He claims this is part of a pattern where Indian workers share confidential interview questions with each other, creating an unfair hiring process. Other interviewees from companies like FedEx and a tech worker who went back to India for better living conditions also shared their experiences. Immigration expert Rosemary Jenks suggests that the H-1B visa program is difficult to stop entirely but President Trump's fee on new entries has had limited impact.

articles.title: Serbia hosts first joint military exercise with NATO | NATO News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Serbia and NATO have conducted their first joint military exercise, a two-week event involving approximately 600 troops from Serbia, Italy, Romania, and Turkiye. The drills, which began on Tuesday and run until May 23rd, are part of the NATO Partnership for Peace program, with military planners and observers from various countries participating.  The exercise aims to preserve peace and stability in the region, according to the Serbia Ministry of Defence, while acknowledging the sensitive nature of the alliance due to past events like the Kosovo war.

articles.title: Sensing an edge, Iran 'ready to gamble' it can outlast Trump - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s leadership is betting it can outlast Donald Trump in its peace negotiations, despite the US president's warnings of a looming truce collapse.  Analysts believe Iran understands that blocking the Strait of Hormuz gives it leverage and is willing to endure economic hardship for a chance at favorable terms. However, they also acknowledge the risk of renewed conflict as Iran faces internal dissent and struggles with damage from US-Israeli attacks. Trump’s administration is under pressure to find an exit strategy, but analysts believe that neither side wants full-scale hostilities.

articles.title: Israeli MPs back special tribunal with death penalty powers for alleged 7 October attackers | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli lawmakers have approved a bill establishing a special tribunal with the power to sentence Palestinians convicted of participating in the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, to death. The measure passed unanimously in the Knesset, reflecting widespread support for punishing those responsible for the deadliest single attack in Israel's history.  The new law empowers a panel of judges to hand down the death penalty by majority vote and allows trials to be livestreamed, drawing comparisons to the 1962 trial of Adolf Eichmann. Rights groups have criticized the measure as potentially violating due process and raising concerns about politicized proceedings. The international criminal court is investigating Israel's conduct in the Gaza war and has issued arrest warrants for several Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

articles.title: Trinamool’s land policy delayed West Bengal border fencing: MHA’s 2023 affidavit in Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) stated in a Supreme Court affidavit that the former Trinamool Congress government's slow and complex Direct Land Purchase Policy hindered land acquisition for border fencing along the Bangladesh border. The BJP government, after assuming power, announced plans to transfer land to the Border Security Force (BSF) within 45 days.  The West Bengal government has handed over 78 km of border land to the BSF in the past three years, while 121 km remains to be transferred. The Calcutta High Court is currently reviewing the applicability and feasibility of acquiring land using Section 40 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act (LARR Act), 2013.

articles.title: D4Vd Murder Case: D4vd appears relaxed in court during murder case status hearing in Los Angeles - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd, whose real name is David Burke, attended a status hearing in Los Angeles County court for his murder case involving the death of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez.  The hearing focused on procedural matters related to evidence exchange and upcoming hearings, scheduled for June 17th and June 29th respectively. The singer remained silent throughout the session, appearing calm and relaxed despite the serious charges against him, including first-degree murder and mutilation.

articles.title: Red Cross says people displaced by conflict in Colombia doubled last year | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) reported a significant increase in displacement, disappearances, and explosive injuries in Colombia due to the ongoing conflict.  In 2025, the ICRC documented that 235,619 people were displaced by fighting, with 42 percent alone in the department of Norte de Santander. The report also highlighted a rise in the use of explosives and drones, leading to an increase in casualties. Gustavo Petro, Colombia's president, has implemented a "Total Peace" plan to negotiate with armed groups but faces opposition from right-wing candidates who advocate for tougher tactics.

articles.title: Pakistan to face growing health risk as international funding to health sector continues to decline: report - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan faces serious health risks due to declining international funding for its healthcare sector.  A report by the think tank Tabadlab warns that cuts in Official Development Assistance (ODA) could lead to disruptions in disease control programs, immunisation efforts, and institutional capacity across the country. The report highlights a sharp decline in global ODA flows since 2019, with total funding dropping from $215 billion in 2024 to $174.3 billion in 2025.  The report emphasizes the need for Pakistan to reduce its reliance on external health financing and strengthen domestic systems before further aid cuts worsen the situation. The report recommends establishing a National Health Financing Forum, creating an ODA registry, introducing a health financing risk matrix, and reforming governance structures within the healthcare sector.

articles.title: Head of Microsoft’s Israel branch to step down after inquiry into dealings with Israeli military | Microsoft | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Microsoft's Israel subsidiary head, Alon Haimovich, stepped down following an inquiry into the company's business dealings with the Israeli military's Unit 8200. The inquiry, commissioned by Microsoft, concluded that Unit 8200 violated its terms of service by using Azure cloud services for mass surveillance of Palestinian civilians.  The investigation also revealed concerns about potential lack of transparency from some employees at Microsoft Israel. Microsoft's CEO, Satya Nadella, was unaware of the use of Azure for this purpose.

articles.title: ‘Bangla Pokkho’ founder Garga Chatterjee arrested for spreading EVM misinformation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Garga Chatterjee, founder of the pro-Bengali advocacy organization Bangla Pokkho, was arrested by the Kolkata Police on Tuesday for allegedly spreading misinformation about EVM manipulation during the recent West Bengal Assembly elections. The arrest followed a complaint filed by the District Election Officer of Kolkata North and comes after Mr. Chatterjee's previous arrest in 2022 for alleged community-based hate speech.  Former Trinamool Congress Minister Sujit Bose was also sent to 10-day ED custody on Tuesday, accused of illegally recommending candidates for South Dum Dum Municipality positions in exchange for financial benefits. Newly appointed West Bengal Sports Minister Nisith Pramanik has requested the file related to the Lionel Messi event in Kolkata and plans to take action if necessary.

articles.title: Missing Indian man Sandarsh Krishna found dead in Grand Canyon, no cause of death established yet - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sandarsh Krishna, a 26-year-old Indian man, was found deceased in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona after a ten-day search. The Coconino County Medical Examiner's Office identified the body and determined no cause of death could be established.  The incident remains under investigation by the National Park Service and the Coconino County Medical Examiner’s Office.

articles.title: Why have peace efforts failed to end conflict in Sudan? | Sudan war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UN reports that the use of drones has made the conflict in Sudan more dangerous, exacerbating a humanitarian crisis with 14 million displaced people and nearly half of the country facing acute hunger.  Aid groups have accused the army and the Rapid Support Forces of using sexual violence as a weapon of war. Despite these concerns, negotiations to end the fighting remain elusive, raising questions about the role of foreign players in mediating the conflict.

articles.title: Trump announces talks with 'failed' Cuba - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced talks with Cuba, stating the communist-ruled island is a "failed country" and that they will be discussing assistance.  Trump's announcement follows his previous statements about taking over Cuba, citing its isolation following the US military operation in Venezuela. Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez condemned the new economic sanctions imposed by the United States as "collective punishment."

articles.title: Afghanistan: The Kabul rehab centre hit by deadly Pakistani strike
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan carried out a deadly airstrike on the Omid Drug Rehabilitation Hospital in Kabul, Afghanistan, killing at least 269 people.  The attack, which targeted "military and terrorist infrastructure" according to Pakistan, was condemned by families of victims who included recovering addicts and employees. The UN and BBC confirmed the strike hit civilians undergoing treatment.

articles.title: Rugby league, bird flu and drones: things you may have missed in the 2026 budget | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian federal budget allocates billions of dollars towards fuel resilience, tax cuts, hospital funding, and aged care.  It also includes measures to reform negative gearing, capital gains tax, and family trusts. The budget addresses key areas such as Keytruda's listing on the pharmaceutical benefits scheme for cervical cancer treatment, increased airline and cruise prices, and the abolishment of nearly 500 "nuisance tariffs." Additionally, funding is allocated for sporting organizations like the South Melbourne football club and Wilston-Grange Australian Football Club. The budget also includes support for the Papua New Guinean rugby league team, the Chiefs, and investments in drone and ebike regulations, aviation consumer protection, and bird flu preparedness.  The ABC and Australian Associated Press receive funding increases, while the Commercial Broadcasting Tax is suspended for two years.

articles.title: US stocks today: S&P 500, Nasdaq end lower as inflation, Iran tensions weigh - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Despite the S&P 500 and Nasdaq remaining near all-time highs, investors are focusing on valuations, macroeconomics, and geopolitical developments. Jay Hatfield, CEO of InfraCap, believes market conditions will flatten out after earnings season.  Donald Trump is scheduled to meet Xi Jinping this week to address various issues including tariffs and the Iran conflict. The Iran war continues to disrupt crude supply, causing consumer price increases that are expected to persist unless oil prices drop.  The Federal Reserve's chances of cutting rates this year appear slim due to rising inflation fears.

articles.title: MGNREGS workers togo on strike on May 15 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NREGA Sangharsh Morcha and All India Kisan Sabha (AIKS) are calling for a nationwide strike by MGNREGA workers on May 15th in protest of the government's decision to repeal the Act, which will take effect July 1st. The organizations argue that MGNREGA is crucial for rural livelihoods and has been undermined by budget cuts, technological barriers, delayed payments, and the VB-G RAM(G) Act. They are demanding a rollback of the act, expanded work duration, a minimum wage linked to inflation, withdrawal of exclusionary attendance systems, and increased participation of Gram Sabhas in planning and implementation.

articles.title: Row over Pete Davidson's 'dark humour' on Charlie Kirk: 'He constantly makes 9/11 jokes...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Davidson made a joke about slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk during the Netflix roast of comedian Kevin Hart, which left the audience uncomfortable. The joke, comparing Tony Hinchcliffe to Kirk, drew groans from the crowd and was seen as insensitive given the circumstances of Kirk's death.  While some defended the format of roasts, others argued that the joke crossed a line.

articles.title: Trump backs Pakistan as Iran mediator after criticism from Lindsey Graham | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has reaffirmed his support for Pakistan as a mediator in US-Iran diplomacy, despite criticism from Senator Lindsey Graham.  Graham expressed skepticism about Pakistan's ability to facilitate negotiations due to reports that the country allows Iranian military assets on its airfields. Trump maintains he is not reconsidering Pakistan and believes they have been helpful in the fragile ceasefire agreement between Iran and the US.

articles.title: India’s Hindu extremist group RSS lobbies foreign groups to counter minority rights criticism - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a Hindu nationalist group linked to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has organized foreign visits to the US, Germany, and Britain to counter accusations of being a paramilitary organization involved in attacks on minority communities. The US Commission on International Religious Freedom previously reported that the RSS has been involved in acts of violence against minorities for decades.  The group claims it is a "Hindu-centric civilisational, cultural movement" with goals of uniting Hindus and protecting their religion.  Dattatreya Hosabale, the RSS general secretary, met with policymakers and business leaders during his visits to dispel misconceptions about the organization.

articles.title: Election results 2026: Why welfare policies aren't winning polls in India like it used to
articles.rephrased_article: India's welfare politics, once a key electoral tool, is facing challenges. While cash transfers and subsidized services have become the norm across parties, recent state elections suggest that extensive welfare delivery alone is no longer enough to secure incumbency.  Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress, for example, lost power in West Bengal despite its women-centric welfare schemes. The Bharatiya Janata Party has capitalized on expanding welfare architecture, including women's self-help groups and administrative efficiency, while voters are increasingly demanding more than just welfare benefits.  Political scientists argue that this shift signifies a move from the floor of Indian politics to the ceiling, where parties must build coalitions around broader issues like job creation and economic mobility.

articles.title: Budget 2026 live updates: Coalition pledges to repeal Chalmers’ tax reforms amid mixed reception for ‘difficult’ budget | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Coalition pledged to repeal changes to capital gains tax and negative gearing if elected, arguing that the reforms would not have the support of the Australian community.  Jim Chalmers, the Treasurer, defended the budget's focus on housing supply and addressing intergenerational equity, stating that the government believes these measures will keep house prices growing at a slower rate than they otherwise would. The Australian Medical Association praised additional funding for public hospitals but criticized the lack of other solutions to address healthcare system issues.  The Climate Council criticized the budget for maintaining fossil fuel subsidies and failing to invest in renewable energy solutions, while the Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA) commended the government's focus on reform and productivity growth.

articles.title: Mount Dukono: I led hikers up an Indonesian volcano - and then it erupted
articles.rephrased_article: A guide who led a group of hikers up Mount Dukono in Indonesia has described the harrowing moment they were caught in the eruption that killed three people. Reza Selang, who runs a tour company, said he was unaware of the climbing prohibition and warnings issued by authorities about the volcano's activity.  The Indonesian government has closed all entrances to the mountain and is investigating possible negligence by tourism operators or individuals. The surviving hikers were evacuated from the mountain, while the bodies of two Singaporean hikers and an Indonesian hiker have been recovered.

articles.title: WRD stops release of water from Sathanur dam in Tiruvannamalai for irrigation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Water Resources Department (WRD) has halted water releases from the Sathanur dam due to a significant drop in water levels. The decision affects 50,000 acres of farmland in Tiruvannamalai, Kallakuruchi, and Villupuram districts, impacting farmers who relied on the dam's irrigation canals for their crops.  The WRD stated that the dam currently has only 18% of its capacity remaining, insufficient to support irrigation needs or domestic consumption.

articles.title: Scientists discover massive ancient ship graveyard with 150 hidden shipwrecks beneath Gibraltar waters | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists from the University of Cádiz and University of Granada have uncovered a vast underwater archaeological concentration in the Bay of Gibraltar, potentially one of the largest in the western Mediterranean.  The three-year project, known as Project Herakles, documented over 150 sites, most dating back to ancient civilizations and spanning multiple centuries. The discoveries include ancient Phoenician and Punic vessels, Roman-era ships, medieval wrecks, and military vessels from the 18th, 19th, and 20th centuries.  The findings offer a unique opportunity to study maritime activity in one concentrated location and provide insights into trade routes, shipbuilding methods, naval warfare, and interactions between Mediterranean societies over time. Researchers are using digital technology to preserve these historical remains for future generations.

articles.title: French minister says uncertain if hantavirus strain from cruise ship has mutated - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: French Health Minister Stephanie Rist stated that the hantavirus strain on the MV Hondius cruise ship may have mutated, but officials remain "rather reassured" due to a lack of complete sequencing data. The outbreak has been linked to the Andes strain of hantavirus and is being investigated by World Health Organisation, which confirmed nine cases and urged isolation of suspected individuals. Italy's top infectious diseases hospital will examine biological samples from a man in quarantine who came into contact with a woman who died from the virus, but no further details were provided.

articles.title: Kevin Warsh confirmed to US Federal Reserve board in close Senate vote | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors with a 51-45 vote, securing his appointment ahead of an expected vote on Wednesday for a four-year term as central bank chair.  This confirmation comes amidst ongoing pressure from President Donald Trump to cut interest rates and questions about the Fed's independence. Senator Elizabeth Warren accused Warsh of being a "sock puppet" for Trump, while Warsh has denied this accusation. The next step in the Senate confirmation process is to confirm him for a four-year term as central bank chair.

articles.title: UAE’s secret attack on Iran risks drawing Gulf states into the war | United Arab Emirates | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The risk of Gulf states becoming embroiled in direct war with Iran has risen following a reported UAE attack on Iran during the ongoing conflict.  Kuwait claims at least four members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were captured attempting to carry out "terrorist attacks" on its Bubiyan Island. The escalating tensions are fueled by diplomatic hostility between the UAE and Iran, as well as concerns over Iranian attempts to disrupt regional oil facilities and shipping routes.  The US has reported a rise in the cost of the war with Iran reaching nearly $29 billion, while Saudi Arabia maintains restraint despite internal divisions on whether to engage in military reprisals.

articles.title: China should stop hoarding food and fertiliser, says former World Bank chief
articles.rephrased_article: David Malpass, former World Bank president, urged China to stop hoarding food and fertilizer to alleviate a global supply crisis. He argued that the country's large stockpiles are exacerbating shortages and hindering efforts to secure essential supplies for spring planting.  Liu Pengyu, spokesperson for the Chinese embassy in Washington DC, countered Malpass's claims by stating China is committed to stabilizing global markets and maintains its status as a developing nation. The situation has been further complicated by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which Svein Tore Holsether, chief executive of Yara, warned could lead to food shortages and increased bidding wars for supplies.

articles.title: Two persons arrested for burglary in Tirupattur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Nagaraj, 60, and B. Vaishnavi, 26, were arrested in Tirupattur for stealing gold jewelry, silver objects, and cash from the home of a retired government school teacher. The theft occurred on April 9th after the couple returned from Chennai.  Shymala Devi, Superintendent of Police, formed special teams to investigate the case, which included analyzing CCTV footage and tracing mobile phone signals. The suspects were apprehended in KGF Colony and are currently held at the sub-jail in Tirupattur.

articles.title: Quote of the day by ‘father of computer’ Charles Babbage: “For one person who is blessed with the power of invention, many will always be found who have the capacity of applying principles” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Charles Babbage, a pioneering mathematician and inventor, emphasized the importance of practical application in driving technological progress.  His quote, "For one person who is blessed with the power of invention, many will always be found who have the capacity of applying principles," highlights that inventions are rarely solely responsible for societal advancements. Instead, it takes collaboration between inventors and those who can translate ideas into real-world applications to achieve lasting impact. Babbage's work laid the foundation for modern computing, with his designs influencing the development of computers and algorithms centuries later. His legacy underscores the importance of both invention and practical implementation in shaping technological progress.

articles.title: Imran's sisters, KP CM demand meeting with incarcerated PTI founder, threaten sit-in - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Imran Khan's sisters and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister were again denied a meeting with the former prime minister at Adiala jail, prompting Aleema Khan to threaten a sit-in.  Sohail Afridi, the KP CM, urged parliamentarians for solidarity, while PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja stated that discussions are ongoing within the party regarding the situation. The PTI also condemned the ban on the Gilgit Baltistan Democratic Party by the federal government and the Election Commission of Gilgit Baltistan (GB), calling it a violation of democratic norms.  The party's central information secretary demanded the ban be lifted immediately.

articles.title: ‘Cotton picking’: US lawmaker condemned for racist comment about Jeffries | Race Issues News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jen Kiggans, a US representative, was condemned for endorsing racist remarks about Hakeem Jeffries, the top-ranking Democrat in the House of Representatives. During a conservative radio interview, host Rich Herrera used the phrase "cotton picking" to criticize Jeffries' support for redistricting efforts in Virginia.  Kiggans later denied approving of the statement but was condemned by Christie Stephenson, a spokesperson for Jeffries. The incident sparked calls for her resignation from top Democrats and the Congressional Black Caucus, who also criticized her endorsement of racist language.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: US war on Iran has cost around $29bn, Pentagon says | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US war on Iran has cost approximately $29 billion, according to the Pentagon. The figure is an increase from the previous estimate of $25 billion and reflects costs associated with equipment repairs and operational expenses.  Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that the US has a plan for escalation or withdrawal depending on the situation.  He also emphasized that the ceasefire remains in effect while negotiations continue. Meanwhile, tensions remain high as Lebanon's health minister condemned Israeli attacks targeting hospitals and emergency crews. The US military continues to enforce its blockade of Iranian ports.

articles.title: How Keir Starmer's plans are going down in the EU
articles.rephrased_article: Sir Keir Starmer, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, announced a new plan to strengthen ties with the European Union. He aims to build closer relationships through increased collaboration on trade, defense, and economic issues. However, his proposals have been met with mixed reactions in Brussels. While some sectors like defense are viewed as areas where the UK will continue to play a key role, economic cooperation remains limited.  The EU is hesitant about Starmer's approach due to concerns over post-Brexit red tape and potential reversals of Brexit policies. The lack of concrete proposals has led to skepticism from Brussels, who believe that Starmer’s government needs to take more decisive steps to achieve closer ties with the EU.

articles.title: Floor test will be smooth; have received letters from EPS, Velumani factions: T.N. Assembly Speaker - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J.C.D. Prabhakar, the new Speaker of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly, assured that Wednesday's floor test will be smooth and successful. He acknowledged receiving letters from two rival AIADMK groups regarding the election of their Legislature Party Leader.  He plans to organize an orientation program for first-time legislators and will continue to follow established assembly conventions. Prabhakar expressed his confidence in the Chief Minister's majority and stated that he will oversee a smooth floor test. He has been involved in Tamil Nadu politics since 1972, serving as a legislator, secretary of the AIADMK, and later under J. Jayalalithaa.

articles.title: Sikh man in Canada says he was denied police exam over kirpan: ‘My dream was shattered’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Winnipeg man, Jaspal Singh Gill, claims his religious rights were violated when he was prevented from taking a police recruitment exam because of his Sikh kirpan.  Gill, who comes from a family of police officers in India, says he was told to remove the ceremonial dagger before sitting the exam and refused, leaving the centre. The Winnipeg Police Service defended its actions by stating that they offered a compromise of storing the kirpan during the exam, but Gill argues this is discrimination. Legal expert Neil MacArthur believes Gill may have strong grounds for legal action based on previous Supreme Court rulings protecting the wearing of kirpans in public spaces.

articles.title: Karachi police arrest 'most wanted' cocaine queenpin - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Karachi arrested Anmol alias Pinki, a woman accused of supplying cocaine and other narcotics across the city.  A joint operation by Garden Police Station and a civilian intelligence agency led to her arrest after midnight. The accused was "most-wanted" by police and had been absconding in several cases. Police recovered a pistol, cocaine worth millions of rupees, chemicals, and other narcotics from her. DIG Syed Asad Raza stated that Anmol used female riders to protect her network from law enforcement agencies and sold drugs through online platforms to customers including students and prominent personalities.  The accused was presented before the court without handcuffs, prompting an inquiry by Karachi Additional Inspector General (AIG) Azad Khan. The Sindh Home Minister, Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, also took notice of the incident and ordered a transparent inquiry into the matter.

articles.title: Ukraine hits Russia’s distant gas facilities after Moscow’s attacks kill 6 | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following Russia's overnight attacks on Ukraine that killed six people, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine retaliated by striking gas facilities in the southwest Russian region of Orenburg.  Zelenskyy stated that this action was a response to Russia's attacks and emphasized that Ukraine would act symmetrically. The governor of Orenburg, Evgeny Solntsev, reported that nine Ukrainian drones were intercepted and damaged infrastructure but caused no injuries. Despite the ceasefire brokered by President Donald Trump expiring, peace talks have stalled.  Kaja Kallas, the European Union's foreign policy chief, believes Putin's comments on ending the war are a sign of weakness.

articles.title: Auschwitz survivor who returned to live in Germany dies aged 101 | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Albrecht Weinberg, a Holocaust survivor who endured multiple Nazi concentration and death camps, passed away in Leer, Germany at the age of 101.  He had returned to Germany from New York after World War II and dedicated his life to educating others about the horrors he experienced. Claus-Peter Horst, the mayor of Leer, described Weinberg as a tireless advocate against forgetting the atrocities of the Nazi era.  Ron Prosor, Israel's ambassador to Germany, praised Weinberg as a bridge between past and present, highlighting his commitment to teaching future generations about the Holocaust.

articles.title: Baltimore Key Bridge collapse: Criminal charges filed against Dali cargo ship operator
articles.rephrased_article: Synergy Marine, the company that operated the cargo ship Dali, and its employee Radhakrishnan Karthik Nair have been charged with conspiracy, obstruction, and misconduct resulting in death for their alleged role in the 2021 bridge collapse. The indictment alleges Synergy Marine misled investigators about conditions on the vessel and failed to disclose safety concerns to the US Coast Guard.  The company, which has also settled a civil case with Maryland Attorney General Anthony Brown over damages related to the bridge collapse, maintains that the allegations are baseless.

articles.title: A society at large under question: rebuild a culture where safety of children is collective responsibility - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A three- to four-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted and murdered in Maharashtra's Pune district, highlighting the fragility of social trust and safety for children. The incident has prompted calls for a more comprehensive approach to dealing with repeat sexual offenders, including stricter parole restrictions, enhanced monitoring by law enforcement, and expedited justice processes.  The National Commission for Women is working closely with authorities to ensure a timely investigation and swift proceedings.

articles.title: Maya Higa: Maya Higa receives standing ovation after becoming first Twitch streamer on TED’s main stage for animal conservation talk - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Maya Higa, a Twitch streamer, made history by becoming the first to deliver a speech on the main stage at the TED conference in Vancouver.  At TED2026, she discussed animal conservation and efforts of Alveus Sanctuary, the nonprofit sanctuary she founded in 2021. Her talk, titled "The Wildlife Sanctuary You Can Visit From Anywhere," was released on TED's YouTube channel and highlighted how livestreaming can raise awareness about wildlife and connect viewers to conservation work.  Higa received a standing ovation for her presentation, which demonstrated the growing recognition of streaming creators in prestigious venues.

articles.title: Treasury, opposition clash in Senate as JUI-F senator questions terrorism in KP - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: During a heated debate in the Senate, Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl Senator Attaur Rehman accused the government of indifference to the rising wave of terrorism in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He questioned why security concerns were being ignored while legislation was prioritized.  Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry condemned the attacks and assured that intelligence-based operations were underway. Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah asserted that Pakistan would continue targeting terrorist training camps in Afghanistan until terrorism is eradicated, rejecting claims of KP breaking away. He also urged opposition parties to refrain from linking political differences with terrorist activities.

articles.title: Why is Iran increasingly targeting the UAE in its war messaging? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has increasingly targeted the UAE in its war messaging, warning of stronger strikes if the US and Israel resume attacks.  The IRGC, a branch of the Iranian armed forces, directly addressed Emirati leaders, accusing them of deepening ties with the US and Israel and contributing to regional insecurity. The IRGC also claimed control over the UAE's port of Fujairah, citing maritime jurisdiction over the Strait of Hormuz.  The UAE has condemned Iranian attacks and severed ties with Iranians living there, but has not officially commented on the alleged attacks on its territory.

articles.title: WHO head tells countries to prepare for more hantavirus cases | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has urged countries to prepare for more hantavirus cases following the outbreak aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship. The virus, which can be transmitted person-to-person in rare cases, has been confirmed in nine individuals, including a French woman and a US national who were evacuated from the ship. Spain played a crucial role in evacuating over 120 passengers and crew members, receiving praise from the WHO for its compassion and solidarity.  The UK is also preparing to bring 10 people from remote South Atlantic islands into the country for precautionary isolation. The WHO has acknowledged that more cases are likely due to interactions on board before preventative measures were taken.

articles.title: Lebanon says two paramedics among 10 killed in Israeli strikes
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli air strikes have killed at least 10 people in southern Lebanon, including two Lebanese Civil Defense paramedics who were responding to an earlier attack. The Lebanese health ministry accused the Israelis of deliberately targeting the paramedics and said that over 108 emergency medical workers have been killed during the war.  The Israeli military claims it targeted a suspect fleeing after attempting to launch a surface-to-air missile at its aircraft, while Hezbollah has launched attacks on Israeli troops in southern Lebanon. The conflict began two days after the US and Israel launched a joint attack on Iran.

articles.title: Gold, housing plays take a hit as PM Modi's austerity pitch rattles consumer-facing stocks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent advice to work from home to reduce fuel consumption sparked a market reaction, impacting sectors like jewellery and real estate. Titan Company Limited, Kalyan Jewellers India Limited, and Senco Gold Limited saw significant declines in their share prices during intraday trading.  Analysts suggest the selloff is driven by sentiment rather than structural demand concerns, as gold remains expensive and crude oil prices remain high.

articles.title: LPG price surge pushes auto, taxi operators to seek subsidy for shift to CNG, EV - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Federation of Private Transport Associations has urged the State and Union governments to provide financial assistance for auto and taxi operators to transition to CNG and electric vehicles. The federation cites rising LPG prices and supply concerns as reasons for their request, noting that drivers are willing to switch but face high conversion costs without government support.  The association has formally submitted representations to both the State Transport Department and the Union government seeking subsidies to ease the process.

articles.title: Not teeth, but nests: Discovery in Caribbean rodent fossils surprises archaeologists | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers from the Florida Museum of Natural History discovered a new trace fossil called Osnidum almontei in the Dominican Republic.  The discovery, made through CT scans of bones of extinct rodents, revealed intricate bee nests crafted inside the hollow cavities of these fossils. The bees utilized rodent jawbones as nesting sites, creating "Russian doll" structures with stacked brood cells and using biological secretions to bind soil for protection from humidity. This adaptation highlights how solitary bees survived in resource-poor limestone landscapes by exploiting natural cavities in vertebrate fossils.

articles.title: Pentagon gives new $29bn Iran war price tag, downplays munitions concerns | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon has released a new estimate of $29 billion for the US-Israel war with Iran, an increase from the previous $25 billion figure.  Defense Secretary Hegseth stated that the Pentagon is prepared to escalate or de-escalate the conflict and assured Congress that the munitions issue was not a major concern. He also emphasized the need to address China's growing influence.

articles.title: PMDC says medical students must qualify for MDCAT, obtain registration before going abroad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) announced new regulations for students pursuing medical or dental education abroad. The PMDC stated that all students must qualify for the MDCAT examination, obtain registration with the council, and verify the foreign institution's accreditation by either the World Federation for Medical Education (WFME) or the World Directory of Medical Schools.  The PMDC emphasized the importance of ensuring a minimum of 6,200 hours of education, at least 80% attendance over five years, language proficiency in English or local languages, and passing the National Registration Examination for registration in Pakistan upon completion. The PMDC also directed students to provide complete details of their residence and contact information before departure, as well as secure a multiple-entry visa valid for the duration of their studies.

articles.title: Irish TV to air Father Ted instead of Eurovision final in protest against Israel’s inclusion | Eurovision | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: RTÉ, Ireland's national broadcaster, is boycotting the Eurovision Song Contest in protest of Israel's participation.  The decision has drawn criticism from Graham Linehan, creator of the beloved sitcom *Father Ted*, who accused RTÉ of using the show as a tool of antisemitic harassment.  Spain, Slovenia, the Netherlands, and Iceland have also declined to participate, citing concerns over voting campaigns and Israel's singer Yuval Raphael receiving the most votes last year.

articles.title: Hamas 'weaponised' sexual violence in 7 October attacks, Israeli investigation says
articles.rephrased_article: An independent Israeli investigation has published a 300-page report detailing "systematic, widespread" sexual violence by Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups during the October 7th attacks. The report, based on interviews with survivors and attackers' footage, concludes that rapes, sexual assault, and torture were intended to inflict maximum pain and suffering.  The investigation also found evidence of gang rapes at a dance festival where over 370 people were killed, as well as the forced sexual acts on family members by captors. The report states that these crimes constitute war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocidal acts under international law.

articles.title: Tata Power Q4 Results: Profit slips 4% YoY to Rs 996 cr, revenue falls 13% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Power reported a 13% year-on-year decline in revenue to Rs 14,900 crore for the March quarter but saw its EBITDA rise 10% to Rs 4,216 crore. The company's core businesses, including generation, transmission and distribution, and renewables, contributed significantly to earnings growth. Tata Power also reported its highest-ever annual PAT of Rs 5,118 crore for FY26, a 7% year-on-year increase.  The company attributed this success to operational efficiency improvements and growth across its core businesses, particularly in the renewables segment. Praveer Sinha, CEO and MD of Tata Power, emphasized the company's focus on long-term growth through clean energy expansion, transmission projects, and distribution improvements.

articles.title: Four cheetah cubs die at Kuno in suspected leopard attack - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four cheetah cubs, born in April and the first to be born in the open forest since India's reintroduction program began in 2022, were found dead on Tuesday (May 12, 2026) in Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh.  The carcasses of the one-month-old cubs were partially eaten and marks of a leopard attack were found during post-mortem examinations. The mother cheetah is safe and healthy, according to officials. A thorough investigation is underway into the incident, which highlights the challenges of adapting cheetahs to their natural habitat.

articles.title: Lorna Hajdini looks very attractive: Megyn Kelly says she believes Chirayu Rana made up the whole sexual assault lawsuit - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Megyn Kelly and Michael Knowles weighed in on the sexual assault lawsuit against Chirayu Rana, with Kelly suggesting it is fabricated due to Lorna Hajdini's attractiveness.  They criticized Rana's alleged lies about his father's death and short employment history, while Knowles pointed out inconsistencies in a technical aspect of the lawsuit. The case will be heard by a New York state court on May 26th.

articles.title: Kuwait says it foils infiltration operation by Iran’s IRGC | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kuwait has arrested four men it accuses of being members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and attempting to infiltrate its Bubiyan Island. The group, identified as Colonels Amir Hussein Abd Mohammed Zara’i and Abdulsamad Yadallah Qanwati, Captain Ahmed Jamshid Gholam Reza Zulfiqari, and First Lieutenant Mohammed Hussein Sehrab Faroughi Rad, were apprehended after a confrontation with Kuwaiti forces that resulted in one soldier being wounded. Kuwait condemned the incident as a "flagrant violation" of its sovereignty and demanded Iran cease hostile actions. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs also summoned Iran's ambassador to hand over a formal protest note.

articles.title: Karachi police arrest 'most-wanted' female drug lord - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Karachi arrested Anmol alias Pinki, a "most-wanted" woman accused of supplying cocaine and other narcotics across the city.  The arrest followed a joint operation by Garden Police Station and a civilian intelligence agency. The accused was found to be operating an extensive network for narcotics dealing, using designated riders and female accomplices. Police have registered two FIRs against her under various clauses of the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024, and the Sindh Arms Act, 2013.  Following a viral video showing Anmol's court appearance without handcuffs, Karachi Additional Inspector-General (AIG) Azad Khan ordered an inquiry into the incident. Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar has also taken notice of the matter and demanded a transparent investigation.

articles.title: French film industry at risk from the far right, say actors and directors | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 600 cinema figures, including actor-director Juliette Binoche and filmmaker Sepideh Farsi, have signed an open letter expressing concern over the growing influence of the far right on French film production. The letter warns that Vincent Bolloré, a billionaire with a powerful media empire, could control the entire film industry from financing to distribution, potentially leading to a "fascist takeover of the collective imagination."  The concerns come amidst a broader protest against Bolloré's dominance in French culture, including a recent revolt at publishing house Grasset. The letter calls for a united front within the film industry to defend its independence and warns that Bolloré could exploit his position to promote far-right agendas.

articles.title: South Africa's top court bans repeat asylum applications
articles.rephrased_article: South Africa's Constitutional Court ruled that foreign nationals cannot reapply for asylum after their initial application is rejected, citing concerns about creating a "never-ending cycle" and administrative chaos. The ruling ends a case brought by two Burundian nationals who had successfully appealed the previous rejection of their applications in 2018. Leon Schreiber, the Minister of Home Affairs in South Africa's coalition government, welcomed the decision as a victory against "abuse" of the refugee system.  The court's ruling is expected to have significant implications for managing asylum seekers and refugees in the country.

articles.title: Dr Reddy's Laboratories Q4 Results: Cons PAT falls 86% YoY to Rs 221 crore, revenue dips 12%; Rs 8 per share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The company's revenue from operations in Q4FY26 decreased 12% to Rs 7,516 crore compared to the previous year.  The profit after tax (PAT) declined 81% sequentially and topline fell 14% quarter-on-quarter. However, full-year revenue increased 3% to Rs 33,593 crore. Gross margin for Q4FY26 was 44.8%, down from the previous year's 52.8%. The company recommended a final dividend of Rs 8 per equity share and set the record date for determining eligible shareholders on July 10, 2026.

articles.title: BJP MLA Tapas Roy sworn in as Pro-tem Speaker of West Bengal Assembly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tapas Roy, a senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader and MLA from Maniktala, was sworn in as the Pro-Tem Speaker of the West Bengal Assembly on Tuesday, May 12, 2026. Suvendu Adhikari, the Chief Minister, attended the ceremony. The oath-taking of other MLAs will be held on Wednesday and Thursday, with the election for Speaker scheduled for Friday.

articles.title: ‘I don’t trust Pakistan’: US official questions Islamabad's mediation role after Iran aircraft row, seeks alternative - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Lindsey Graham questioned Pakistan’s role as a mediator in the US-Iran negotiations, citing reports that Iranian military aircraft were using Pakistani airbases.  Graham expressed skepticism about Pakistan's impartiality and suggested alternative mediators if the allegations are confirmed. The Pakistani Foreign Ministry denied any military coordination with Iran, stating that the presence of Iranian aircraft was for diplomatic and logistical purposes.  The US administration is divided on how to proceed, with some advocating for a more aggressive approach while others favor diplomacy.

articles.title: Israel’s war creating a ‘lost generation’ of Lebanese students | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s war on Lebanon has displaced hundreds of thousands of students and teachers, creating a “lost generation” and widening societal disparities. Schools have been destroyed or turned into shelters, disrupting education and causing further disruptions to an already struggling system.  While some institutions are using online learning, experts say this is ineffective for many vulnerable students due to limited access to technology and resources. The war has exacerbated Lebanon's economic crisis and humanitarian challenges, leading to increased poverty and forcing families to make difficult choices between basic needs like food and education. Experts warn that without significant intervention, these disparities could have long-term consequences for the country’s future.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz, Azerbaijan's President Aliyev discuss peace efforts in Mideast: PMO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan held a phone call on Tuesday to discuss regional developments, including peace efforts in the Middle East.  They reaffirmed strong bilateral ties between Pakistan and Azerbaijan, with Sharif expressing confidence that the upcoming World Urban Forum in Baku would be a valuable platform for advancing global urban development. The leaders also discussed Pakistan's successful mediation efforts to bring about a ceasefire between Iran and the US, highlighting the trust and confidence placed in Pakistan's leadership by the international community.  They agreed to maintain close contact and look forward to meeting in person later this year.

articles.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina left vulnerable by policy clash with US, representative says | Bosnia and Herzegovina | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UN high representative for Bosnia and Herzegovina, Christian Schmidt, resigned after clashing with the US over his role in the country.  Schmidt's departure follows a series of events including pressure from the US government on the UN security council to remove him, and opposition from Russia and the Republika Srpska entity. The resignation has raised concerns about the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina's multi-ethnic state, with some fearing that the US may seek to abolish the high representative position or appoint a preferred candidate. A recent $1.5 billion contract awarded to a firm led by Donald Trump Jr's ally, Jesse Binnall, for a pipeline project has also added to the instability.  The EU is opposed to this deal and the involvement of Trump allies in the project.

articles.title: Zelensky's ex-chief of staff in court as Ukraine corruption probe escalates
articles.rephrased_article: Andriy Yermak, former chief of staff to President Volodymyr Zelensky, appeared in a Kyiv court on Tuesday as part of an ongoing corruption probe.  The Anticorruption Prosecutor's Office (Sapo) and the National anti-corruption bureau (Nabu) are investigating allegations of money laundering surrounding a luxury construction project outside Kyiv. Yermak, who was close to Zelensky until his resignation last year following an anti-corruption raid on his flat, denies wrongdoing. The investigation has cast a shadow over Ukraine's bid for EU membership and comes as Russia marks victory over Nazi Germany in World War Two with renewed attacks on Ukraine.

articles.title: Cambridge AS-level Mathematics paper allegedly leaked, students claim - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE), part of Cambridge University Press and Assessment, is facing accusations of paper leaks for the AS-level Mathematics exam in Karachi. Students allege that the Tuesday's exam was identical to a solved paper they saw on social media.  CIE states that it investigates all allegations of paper leaks but does not comment on individual reports. The organization has offered resits for candidates impacted by previous leaks and is currently investigating this latest allegation.

articles.title: Rana stars as Bangladesh win first home Test against Pakistan | Cricket News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh defeated Pakistan by 104 runs in the first Test match at Dhaka, securing their maiden home Test victory.  Pace bowler Nahid Rana claimed five wickets as Bangladesh bowled out Pakistan for 163 on the final day after a rain-interrupted contest. Najmul Hossain Shanto, captain of Bangladesh, achieved a significant milestone by equaling Mushfiqur Rahim's record of seven Test wins as captain, while Rana delivered career-best figures of 5-40 to secure the victory. The two teams will now play the second Test in Sylhet on Saturday.

articles.title: Mexico cancels plans to end school year early for World Cup
articles.rephrased_article: Mexico's government has reversed its decision to end the school year early due to concerns raised by parents and education experts. The original plan, announced in May, aimed to ease traffic during the Fifa World Cup and a heatwave.  After backlash from the National Union of Parents, President Claudia Sheinbaum clarified that ending classes early was only a proposal. The decision has been scrapped, with classes now scheduled to finish on July 15th.

articles.title: Dixon Technologies Q4 Results: Cons PAT falls 36% YoY as topline grows 2%; Rs 10/share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dixon Technologies reported a 3% year-on-year increase in total income to Rs 10,595 crore for the quarter ended March 2026. The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) grew by 9% year-on-year to Rs 493 crore. Dixon Technologies also announced a final dividend of Rs 10 per equity share for the financial year 2025-26. The company's shares closed down 6.05% at Rs 10,120 after market hours.

articles.title: If a company replaces its CEO with...: Indian-origin tech leader says he backtested billionaire Michael Milken's idea - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Deedy (Debarghya Das), an Indian-origin tech leader, shared data from Michael Milken, a billionaire, suggesting that if a US company replaced its US-born CEO with an Indian-origin CEO, the stock price would increase.  Das's findings sparked debate on social media about the correlation between Indian-origin leadership and stock performance. Some argued it was simply coincidence while others pointed to potential benefits of diverse leadership for American companies. However, some criticized this trend as a sign of job losses and outsourcing by US corporations.

articles.title: English edition of ‘Gangamma Jatara’ book released in Tirupati - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Peta Srinivasulu Reddy, a retired professor of Telugu at Sri Venkateswara University, released the English version of his book, "The folk festival of Ganga Jatara in Tirupati," on May 12, 2026. The book, which details the history and traditions of the annual festival, was formally unveiled by members of the Kaikala clan who traditionally represent the deities during the event. This is not the first time Prof. Reddy has written about the festival; his Telugu version was published 31 years ago.

articles.title: IHC issues notices to CDA in appeals by flat owners, BoP over One Constitution Avenue lease - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A division bench of the Islamabad High Court issued notices to the Capital Development Authority (CDA) in response to intra-court appeals filed by apartment owners and the Bank of Punjab (BoP). The appeals challenge a previous single-member bench's decision to cancel the lease of the One Constitution Avenue project, citing potential violations of third-party rights.  The court adjourned further hearing on the matter pending a response from the CDA and a final decision by the cabinet regarding the issue.

articles.title: The Flotilla Diaries: Inside the 2025 mission to break the Gaza siege | Documentary | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Perez and Juliet Lamont, two filmmakers, embarked on the Global Sumud Flotilla in September 2025 to break the siege on Gaza. The mission involved fifty civilian vessels aiming to deliver aid and establish a humanitarian corridor.  The flotilla faced challenges from Israel, including water cannon attacks and ship disappearances.  Dasa Raimanova's documentary, "The Flotilla Diaries," documents their harrowing experiences of intimidation and imprisonment.

articles.title: eBay rejects $55.5bn offer from GameStop
articles.rephrased_article: eBay has rejected a $55.5 billion takeover offer from GameStop, calling it "unsolicited" and citing concerns about financing, operational risks, and GameStop's governance structure. The online auction giant stated its turnaround plan was working despite recent challenges from competitors like Amazon and Etsy.  Ryan Cohen, GameStop CEO, has indicated he would pursue the proposal directly with eBay shareholders if rejected by the board.

articles.title: ‘Unprecedented’ global effort gives new name to polycystic ovary syndrome – and new hope to millions of women | Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: After a decade of collaboration, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) has been renamed to polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). The new name reflects the condition's broader impact on multiple systems in the body, including metabolism and risk of diabetes and cardiovascular disease.  The renaming was spearheaded by endocrinologist Prof Helena Teede, who emphasized that the term "polycystic" contributed to delayed diagnosis and inadequate medical care. Patients advocated for the change, highlighting the need for a name that better reflects the condition's complexity. The new name will be implemented in international guidelines for managing PCOS, with full implementation planned for 2028.

articles.title: Vodafone Idea board to weigh fundraise through equity after AGR relief - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone Idea has announced plans for a fundraising effort, following a recent surge in investor confidence. The company's stock price has increased significantly due to regulatory relief on adjusted gross revenue (AGR) liabilities, management changes, and renewed expectations for network expansion funding. Vodafone Group, which owns 19% of the Indian telecom operator, is also exploring a potential transfer of its stake back to Vodafone Idea for treasury holding purposes.  Brokerages like Citigroup have maintained a "Buy-High Risk" rating on the stock and expect improved fundraising prospects due to regulatory clarity regarding AGR liabilities.

articles.title: Indian engineer charged in US for Maryland bridge crash, six construction workers were killed in 2024 - The Times of India
