The meeting will take place on Thursday, May 14th, alongside other BRICS ministers from Brazil, Russia, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, and Indonesia.

articles.title: ‘A consistent pattern of lying’: Musk v OpenAI trial exposes what insiders think of Sam Altman | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The trial between Elon Musk and OpenAI, its CEO Sam Altman, has exposed internal drama at the AI firm, highlighting concerns about Altman's leadership.  Former executives, including Mira Murati, have testified to Altman's deceptive tendencies, while Ilya Sutskever confirmed his own concerns about Altman's honesty and truthfulness.  Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella criticized the OpenAI board for creating instability and poor communication, adding that he was worried about employees leaving en masse.  Both OpenAI and Altman have denied all allegations, arguing that Musk is motivated by personal jealousy of the company's success. The trial is expected to conclude with closing arguments on Thursday.

articles.title: DME panel completes inquiry into mental harassment charges at Kozhikode medical college - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A three-member panel appointed by the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) has completed its inquiry into allegations of mental harassment against two faculty members at the Department of Psychiatry, Government Medical College, Kozhikode. The panel is expected to submit a report soon.  The members include Varghese P. Punnoos, Principal, Government Medical College, Kottayam, P.S. Indu, Principal, Government Medical College, Thrissur, and C. Raveendran, secretary of the Institutional Ethics Committee, Government Medical College, Thrissur.

articles.title: California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton mocked for misidentifying a ‘street taco’ | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Steve Hilton, a British political strategist running for California governor, drew criticism after posting a video of himself holding a hard-shell tortilla from a Del Taco location in Barstow and calling it a "street taco."  Gustavo Arellano, a Los Angeles Times columnist, and others criticized the description as inaccurate, pointing out that traditional street tacos are made with two soft corn tortillas. Hilton defended his choice, stating the restaurant called it a "Barstow street taco," but the location's menu referred to it as a "Barstow taco." Despite facing criticism for his unconventional approach, Hilton, who has been a frontrunner in the race, is running on a platform of reducing taxes and tackling affordability.

articles.title: Indian-origin woman’s body found in car boot in UK; family to travel to Britain seeking justice | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Harshita Brella's family, including her parents and sister, are traveling to the UK this week to continue their fight for justice in the case of their daughter's death. The Indian Ladies in UK (ILUK) and the Northamptonshire Rights and Equality Council (NREC) are supporting the family as they seek clarity and accountability from authorities.  The family hopes to meet officials and publicly address their concerns about the handling of the case, which has raised broader questions about domestic abuse complaints involving women who have moved to the UK.

articles.title: Former GHMC mayor to head TG Women’s Commission - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gadwal Vijaylaxmi, former GHMC mayor, has been appointed chairperson of the Telangana Women’s Commission.  She will serve a five-year term, alongside six other members: Kasoju Sankaramma, Chityala Swetha, Shashikala Yadava Reddy, Sada Laxmi, N. Radha Bai, and Ujma Ashai Shakira. The appointments were made by Chief Secretary K. Ramakrishna Rao on Monday.

articles.title: Starmer began the day damaged and then things got worse | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer faced growing calls for his resignation from a significant portion of the Labour Party, with over 60 MPs demanding a timetable for his departure.  The pressure intensified after his speech, which many saw as inadequate to address the party's recent electoral defeat and mounting dissatisfaction within its ranks. The situation was further complicated by the emergence of challenges to Starmer's leadership from several backbenchers, including Catherine West, who shifted her position to advocate for an orderly transition instead of immediate removal.  While some senior figures urged Starmer to fight on, others, including cabinet members like Yvette Cooper and Shabana Mahmood, called for him to accept an "orderly" process.

articles.title: $200 million divorce battle: Iranian heiress accused of shielding family assets to block husband’s claims in California - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Setareh “Star” Bral, daughter of a late Iranian real estate tycoon, is accused by her estranged husband, Ryan Aronin, of hiding assets in a $200 million divorce battle.  Court documents allege that Bral transferred control of her company, Star Pacific Properties, to her brother in October 2024 and attempted to distance herself from the SYB Family Trust, which is estimated to be worth $200 million. Aronin claims she has continued to benefit from trust-related rental income despite separating from him in March 2022. The dispute centers around Bral's alleged attempts to limit her financial exposure and control over assets.

articles.title: New excise regime comes into effect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The new excise regime in Karnataka will come into effect on May 11, with lower-end liquor becoming more expensive and certain premium labels potentially cheaper. The policy aims to discourage high alcohol content consumption by taxing it based on the social cost, estimated at ₹1,200 per liter in 2024-25 and projected to increase to ₹2,000 per liter by 2028-29.  The Karnataka State Beverage Corporation Ltd. (KSBCL) will automatically calculate prices based on the alcohol content, excise duty, and additional excise duty once producers provide this information.

articles.title: A messy day for Starmer: is Labour ungovernable? – podcast | Labour party leadership | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer faced a challenging day as Angela Rayner called for the return of Andy Burnham, while MPs continued to call for his resignation.  Despite these calls, no formal challenge has been launched against the Labour leader. The party remains in disarray with questions surrounding its leadership and future direction.

articles.title: Protecting Life: Poland spent millions on an artificial island to protect rare birds and conserve wildlife | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Poland created an artificial island from dredged sand to protect wildlife and ecosystems. The Wyspa Jana Zabawy-Wroblewskiego, built near the Szczecin Lagoon, was initially intended for a shipping channel project but was later closed off to the public.  Scientists are observing the natural process of ecological succession as birds and other wildlife colonize the island, providing valuable data on how ecosystems adapt to human-altered environments. The island's unique development has become an example of how infrastructure projects can be used for conservation efforts instead of solely for commercial or industrial purposes.

articles.title: Kochi metro’s Kakkanad extension likely to miss Dec. deadline - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) is facing delays in the completion of its Kakkanad extension project due to uncertainty over securing a loan from the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB). The project's revised deadline is March 2027, with hopes for safety certification by June 2027 and commercial operations commencing thereafter.  The delay in completing the viaduct, stations, and associated infrastructure has caused traffic snarls on major roads in Kochi.

articles.title: Starmer on the brink as cabinet ministers urge him to quit | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer’s grip on power is weakening as cabinet ministers urge him to set a timetable for his departure and over 70 Labour MPs publicly call for him to resign.  The prime minister, who warned the country would "never forgive" Labour for plunging into chaos of a leadership election, intends to prove his doubters wrong. Several cabinet members, including Yvette Cooper and Shabana Mahmood, have suggested an orderly transition of power after crushing election defeats.  Starmer, however, has refused to resign and plans to fight any leadership challenge. The situation is further complicated by calls for the prime minister's resignation from MPs like Wes Streeting and Andy Burnham. While some believe a leadership change would appease Nigel Farage, others argue that it would be detrimental to the party.

articles.title: 'Single, unmarried doctor': Former US diplomat says he faced multiple visa rejections even in 1984 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Rajesh Vyas, an Indian-origin former US diplomat, recounted his multiple attempts to obtain a US visa in the 1980s and 1990s.  He was initially denied twice in 1984 due to his connections and lack of intention to settle in the US, despite having backing documents from influential individuals. Vyas later obtained a visa in 1993 after acknowledging past rejections and outlining his plans for studying and potentially working in the US. He eventually joined the US Foreign Service in 2006 and retired in 2020.

articles.title: CM is unsettled by PM’s remarks: BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP in Karnataka responded to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah's criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, stating that the Prime Minister's speech at a BJP event was within his democratic right. The opposition leader, R. Ashok, argued that the Prime Minister spoke about issues affecting 7 crore Kannadigas and that Siddaramaiah should focus on addressing real concerns in Karnataka rather than being rattled by the remarks.

articles.title: EU, UK sanction Russians over deportations of Ukrainian children | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union and United Kingdom have imposed sanctions on 23 state institutions and individuals in Russia for their alleged systematic deportation and indoctrination of Ukrainian children. The EU designated these entities for their involvement in programs subjecting children to pro-Russian ideology, including patriotic events and military training.  The UK's broader sanctions package targets 85 people and entities, with a focus on those involved in the Kremlin's campaign to forcibly deport and militarize Ukrainian children. The International Criminal Court has issued an arrest warrant for Russian President Vladimir Putin for war crimes related to illegal deportation of children from Ukraine.

articles.title: Sarah Wynn-Williams and Virginia Giuffre jointly win freedom to publish prize at British book awards | Books | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sarah Wynn-Williams and the late Virginia Giuffre jointly won the Freedom to Publish prize at this year’s British Book Awards. The award recognizes those who resist censorship and threats to writers, publishers, and booksellers.  Wynn-Williams' memoir "Careless People" details her experiences working at Meta, while Giuffre's posthumous memoir "Nobody's Girl" recounts her abuse by Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. The award was presented by Yulia Navalnaya and supported by the free expression organization Index on Censorship, with Wynn-Williams highlighting the growing influence of wealthy elites in public discourse.

articles.title: 20-year-old Prabhjot Singh deported from Canada after involvement in extortion-related crimes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Prabhjot Singh, a 20-year-old Punjabi man, has been removed from Canada after being linked to an extortion investigation in Surrey, British Columbia. The Surrey Police Service (SPS) arrested him earlier this year and shared information with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), leading to his removal following an immigration investigation. The SPS is seeking public assistance in identifying potential associates or witnesses who may have interacted with Singh while he was in Canada.

articles.title: CSML tasked with DPR for model road project - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cochin Smart Mission Limited (CSML) has been tasked with preparing a detailed project report for the beautification of the stretch between Goshree Junction and the Durbar Hall ground, as part of a larger model road development plan. The UDF governing committee prioritized this project among its first 50 days in office, with the initiative to be implemented in three phases.  A private builder has also agreed to beautify and maintain the stretch between Goshree Junction and High Court Junction as a Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative. Additionally, the Corporation has acquired an electric bus for a shuttle service between High Court Junction and its headquarters.

articles.title: Trump says he will suspend petrol tax amid soaring US fuel prices | Energy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced he would suspend the 18-cent federal gas tax to offset rising fuel prices, stating he would "take off the gas tax for a period of time" and let it phase back in when gas prices decrease. Senator Josh Hawley, a Republican ally of Trump, pledged to introduce legislation to suspend the tax permanently.  The White House has not confirmed its support for this measure, which requires an act of Congress. The move comes amid soaring fuel prices since the US-Israel war on Iran began, with average gas prices reaching $4.52 per gallon.

articles.title: PMD issues Glof alert for KP, Gilgit-Baltistan as rainfall predicted in upper Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) issued an alert for glacial lake outburst floods (Glofs) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Gilgit-Baltistan due to a moderate westerly wave expected to hit the region. The PMD warned of widespread rain, wind-thunderstorms, and isolated heavy falls, particularly in vulnerable areas like Swat, Lower Chitral, Dir, Upper Hazara, Kohistan, Hoper, Ghulkin, Shishper, Ghizer, Hunza, Nagar, Ghanche, Shigar, and Astore. The KP Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) issued instructions to district administrations to monitor vulnerable Glof sites, conduct evacuation drills, and ensure the availability of rescue personnel in case of an emergency.

articles.title: Senior cabinet ministers and more than 70 MPs call for Keir Starmer’s resignation as speech fails to quell rebellion – as it happened | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senior cabinet ministers urged Keir Starmer to set a timetable for his departure, as more than 70 Labour MPs called for him to resign. The pressure on Starmer intensified after he failed to quell criticism following bruising local election results and the resignation of several MPs.  Several cabinet members, including Yvette Cooper and Shabana Mahmood, expressed concerns about the leadership crisis and urged Starmer to consider his position. A number of Labour MPs, including Charlotte Nichols and Debbie Abrahams, publicly called for Starmer's resignation, citing public dissatisfaction with his leadership.  Melanie Ward, a Scottish Labour MP, resigned as Justice PPS, stating that constituents were unhappy with Starmer's leadership, while others, such as Rachel Taylor, expressed their support for him to continue leading the party.

articles.title: French Streamer Exposed: French streamer PrinceofParis allegedly exposed after Airbnb host interrupts livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: PrinceofParis, a French streamer known for his luxurious lifestyle, abruptly ended a livestream after an unexpected visitor appeared at the property he claimed to be residing in. The incident sparked online speculation about the authenticity of his extravagant claims and raised questions about the legitimacy of influencer lifestyles. Viewers are divided on whether the event proves his story is staged or not, with some suggesting it could indicate he isn't the rightful owner of the property.  The situation remains uncertain as PrinceofParis has not uploaded any videos since the incident.

articles.title: TCS Nashik case: NCW flags ‘toxic work culture’, ‘zero POSH compliance’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Commission for Women (NCW) has found that Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) in Nashik is failing to comply with the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act, citing pervasive harassment, religious denigration, and systemic bullying. The NCW's fact-finding committee observed that victims were intimidated into silence due to a lack of formal complaint mechanisms and a toxic workplace environment.  The committee has recommended action for TCS’ failure to comply with the POSH Act, as well as measures to protect complainants and ensure a safe working environment.

articles.title: Hundreds displaced, medical services suspended amid gang violence in Haiti | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors Without Borders has suspended hospital operations in Port-au-Prince's Cite Soleil neighborhood due to ongoing gang violence that has displaced hundreds of residents. The aid group, also known as MSF, said about 800 people sought refuge inside its hospital before operations were halted. MSF stated that gunfire safety concerns prevented them from guaranteeing the safety of staff and patients, while another local hospital, Hopital Fontaine, evacuated newborns.  The violence has strained Haiti's civilian population and efforts by authorities to quell the fighting have been largely ineffective.

articles.title: Australia include uncapped trio on white-ball tours of Pakistan, Bangladesh - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Australia has named squads for upcoming white-ball tours of Pakistan and Bangladesh, featuring three potential debutants. Mitchell Marsh will captain all teams, with the squad including Liam Scott, Ollie Peake, and Joel Davies.  Experienced players like Billy Stanlake and Riley Meredith return alongside spinners Tanveer Sangha and Spencer Johnson. The team will play three ODIs in Pakistan and Bangladesh before traveling to Chattogram for three T20Is.

articles.title: South African president says he will not step down after impeachment call
articles.rephrased_article: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African president, stated he will not resign despite calls for his removal due to an impeachment report regarding the theft of money from his private farm. The Constitution Court ruled last week that parliament acted unconstitutionally in voting against establishing an impeachment inquiry into the Phala Phala scandal.  Ramaphosa plans to challenge the report, arguing it relied on hearsay evidence and will seek legal review.

articles.title: Israeli troops jailed for desecration of Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon | Lebanon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli soldiers were sentenced to prison for desecrating a Christian statue in southern Lebanon. Lt Col Ariella Mazor, spokesperson for the Israel military, stated that the incident was viewed with great severity and emphasized respect for freedom of religion and worship. This follows another incident where Israeli soldiers were condemned for hacking down a crucifix in the same region. The punishments given are unusual compared to other alleged misconduct cases in the occupied territories.

articles.title: 35 injured as bus, lorry collide in Aluva - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: **Nearly 35 people were injured, four of them seriously, in a collision between a private bus and a lorry near Edathala on Monday. The bus was traveling from Aluva to Pookkattupady when it collided with the lorry heading in the opposite direction.  Aishwarya Mani, Jesma, and Eliamma sustained serious injuries requiring immediate medical attention. Bus driver Prasad also suffered injuries. Emergency services cleared the road using a crane and traffic resumed after the accident.

articles.title: World’s longest wild snake in Indonesia: The 23-foot ‘Baroness’ that stunned scientists and raised conservation concerns | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A reticulated python, nicknamed "The Baroness" or Ibu Baron, has been confirmed as the longest wild snake ever recorded, measuring 23 feet 8 inches long. Discovered in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, she is a testament to survival in a changing landscape where large animals are increasingly threatened by human encroachment. The discovery has sparked both curiosity and concern, highlighting the fragility of these creatures and the need for conservation efforts.  However, Ibu Baron's presence raises questions about the many unrecorded giant snakes that may be living undetected in the wild.

articles.title: US, French nationals from hantavirus ship test positive - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) and Spanish health officials are overseeing the repatriation of passengers from the cruise ship, MV Hondius, which was hit by a deadly hantavirus outbreak.  Two passengers from the ship have tested positive for the Andes virus, with one American national experiencing mild symptoms. The operation to evacuate nearly 150 passengers and crew members is ongoing, with most expected to be flown to their respective countries by Monday afternoon. WHO officials are recommending a 42-day quarantine and active follow-up, but some passengers may choose to return home without further isolation depending on the risk assessment.

articles.title: Trump says ceasefire on ‘life support’, slams Iran response to US proposal | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump dismissed Iran’s response to a US peace proposal as “stupid” and said the ceasefire with Iran is "on life support."  The US president's rejection of the Iranian proposal, which included demands for compensation for war damage, an end to the naval blockade, and removal of sanctions, has fueled concerns about the conflict's future. Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman defended its demands as “reasonable” and emphasized Iran’s sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. The ongoing uncertainty surrounding the conflict has disrupted global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which is a crucial oil and gas export route.

articles.title: Trump says ceasefire with Iran on ‘life support’ after rejecting peace proposals | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has expressed concerns about the ceasefire with Iran, calling it "weak" and considering restarting US navy military escorts of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz.  He dismissed Iran’s peace proposals as "stupid" and said he is not under domestic pressure to reach a deal. Maj Gen Mohammad Ali Jafari, former commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, stated that Iran will not negotiate until its demands are met. Oil prices have continued to rise due to the impasse, with Iran claiming it is possible to reach an agreement and Mostafa Taheri, a member of the Iranian parliament's industry commission, claimed the proposed new transit fees would generate $15 billion annually.  The standoff has led to the grounding of thousands of tankers in the Gulf, prompting international efforts to address the humanitarian crisis.

articles.title: Most drowning cases occur in summer: Fire dept. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fire and Rescue Services department reported a surge in drowning cases involving students during summer vacation.  Three dental students from Baselios Dental College drowned in the Palavan river near Kothamangalam, while another student drowned in a quarry in Thrikkariyoor panchayat. The incidents highlight the dangers of strong undercurrents and deep pits in the picturesque but treacherous river. To address this issue, Kothamangalam fire station organized a 10-day swimming camp for students.

articles.title: 10 Japan’s longest rivers ranked from Shinano to Shimanto | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The longest rivers in Japan, according to WorldAtlas, include the Shinano River at 367 kilometers, the Tone River at 322 kilometers, and the Ishikari River at 268 kilometers. These waterways play crucial roles in agriculture, flood control, and human settlement patterns. The Teshio River stands out with its largely natural flow, while the Kitakami River's split mouth is unique among Japanese rivers.  The Abukuma River supports a large population, and the Mogami River is known for its swift current. The Tenryu River, despite being prone to flooding, has historical significance as a transportation route. The Agano River plays an important role in agriculture and hydroelectric power generation. Finally, the Shimanto River is renowned for its pristine waters and traditional bridges.

articles.title: Police say 25 sacrificial goats worth Rs1.9m stolen from Karachi's Gulistan-i-Jauhar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty-five sacrificial goats valued at Rs1.9 million were stolen from an empty plot in Gulistan-i-Jauhar, Pakistan. The owner hired a watchman who was tied up and forced to watch as the suspects took the animals in a Suzuki van. Police have obtained CCTV footage of the incident and urged the owner to file an FIR. This is not the first time that sacrificial goats have been targeted for theft in Gulistan-i-Jauhar, with a similar incident occurring in 2024 where a truck carrying goats was hijacked.

articles.title: How impunity in Shireen Abu Akleh’s case fuels Israeli attacks on the press | Freedom of the Press News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli soldiers shot and killed Shireen Abu Akleh, a US citizen and veteran Al Jazeera correspondent, in Jenin refugee camp on May 11, 2022.  The killing sparked international condemnation and calls for accountability. Despite investigations by the FBI and other organizations, no charges have been filed against the perpetrators. The incident has fueled concerns about impunity for Israeli forces and a lack of pressure from allies like the United States. Advocacy groups argue that the US's failure to hold Israel accountable has emboldened further abuses against journalists in the region.  The killing is seen as part of a larger pattern of targeted killings of Palestinian reporters by the Israeli military, with no consequences for perpetrators.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump rejects Iran’s response to US peace deal; UN urges ‘genuine ceasefire’ as Israel intensifies Lebanon strikes | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump maintains that a diplomatic solution with Iran is possible despite the ceasefire's weak state. The UAE has secretly conducted military strikes on Iran, escalating tensions in the region. Iran rejects the US peace proposal and accuses it of being "garbage".  The UN calls for a genuine ceasefire as Israel intensifies its assault on Lebanon.  Israel claims its Iron Dome system is nearly 99% effective against Iranian missiles. The EU has sanctioned Israeli settlers, while the UK has imposed sanctions on individuals linked to Iran. Trump plans to discuss military action against Iran with his national security team and believes a diplomatic solution is still possible.  The death toll from the ongoing conflict in Lebanon continues to rise, with over 2,800 civilians killed. The situation remains volatile as tensions between the US and Iran remain high.

articles.title: Two killed in separate accidents in Kochi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two people died in separate accidents in the district on Monday. Dinesan, 58, of Udayamperoor was fatally struck by a truck at Choorakkadu Junction near Thripunithura and later succumbed to his injuries.  In Angamaly, Ishana Ismath, 22, of Kasargod, died after being hit by a car on the airport road.

articles.title: 'Crazy': US denies OPT extension citing police record; applicant called police after being assaulted - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has denied a STEM OPT extension to an applicant based on a "law enforcement interaction," citing the individual's call to police after being assaulted. Scott Decker, an immigration attorney, argues that this decision is arbitrary and potentially discriminatory, as it unfairly penalizes individuals who have been victims of crime.  Decker believes this situation may be indicative of broader USCIS practices where they are denying benefits based on seemingly minor interactions with law enforcement without proper review.

articles.title: PM orders inquiry after PML-N MPA injured in attack in Toba Tek Singh - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered an inquiry into a deadly attack on PML-N MPA Col (retired) Sardar Ayub Gadhi in Toba Tek Singh. The incident, which occurred Sunday night, saw four of Gadhi's aides killed and the MPA himself injured by unidentified gunmen who opened fire at his outhouse.  The prime minister condemned the attack and directed authorities to swiftly identify and arrest those responsible.

articles.title: Fan festivals, Panini, tickets: What are FIFA World Cup fans talking about? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Fans are expressing disappointment and shock over the high cost of World Cup tickets, logistical concerns, and political tensions. FIFA has released limited-edition collectible shirts for each host city, but many fans criticize the price as exorbitant.  Free fan festivals in host cities have become popular alternatives to expensive match tickets. The Panini sticker book remains a beloved tradition for football fans, with collectors eager to complete their albums. Broadcast rights issues in India and China may prevent millions of fans from watching the tournament.

articles.title: Royal Opera House calls for release of Georgian bass singer jailed over democracy protests | Royal Opera House | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal Opera House in London has urged Keir Starmer, the British Prime Minister, to intervene in the case of Paata Burchuladze, a renowned Georgian bass singer imprisoned in Georgia since October. The 71-year-old, who performed at the Royal Opera House and the Metropolitan Opera House, was sentenced to seven years in prison for alleged involvement in a coup against the country's authoritarian leader. Peter Katona, director of casting at the Royal Opera and Burchuladze’s friend, claims the charges are fabricated and that he is being persecuted for his opposition to the ruling regime.  The Foreign Office is monitoring developments closely and will raise concerns about detainees' rights.

articles.title: J&K CM Abdullah retracts statement on liquor in face of growing criticism - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Omar Abdullah, the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, retracted his earlier statement that "No one was forcing anyone to consume liquor" after facing criticism.  The National Conference (NC) MP, Aga Syed Ruhullah, joined the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in calling for a ban on all liquor outlets in the state. The PDP leader Iltija Mufti accused the NC of changing its stance and argued that no religion supports alcohol consumption. The BJP stated that legislation alone cannot stop alcohol consumption and emphasized the need for awareness campaigns.

articles.title: Quote of the day by German philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche: “I cannot believe in a God who wants to be praised all the time” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Friedrich Nietzsche's philosophy, which challenges traditional morality and authority, continues to resonate with readers today. His famous quote "I cannot believe in a God who wants to be praised all the time" reflects his critique of systems that demand blind obedience and stifle individual freedom.  Nietzsche believed humans should think for themselves and create meaning, not inherit beliefs from society. His ideas about individuality, self-mastery, and confronting uncomfortable truths remain relevant as people grapple with social pressures and expectations in today's world.

articles.title: 3-month-long summer vacation announced for Punjab schools - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rana Sikandar Hayat, Punjab Education Minister, announced a three-month summer vacation for schools in the province, beginning May 22 and ending August 23.  The decision follows previous advisories from the Punjab Disaster Management Authority urging schools to adjust working hours or declare early summer holidays due to excessive heat. The authority's directives included measures such as altering working hours, suspending outdoor activities, ensuring water availability, maintaining ventilation systems, and advising students to wear light-colored clothing.

articles.title: Philippine senator flees ICC arrest over role in Duterte’s drug war | Rodrigo Duterte News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Ronald Dela Rosa fled the Philippine Senate after evading an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) regarding his alleged role in the Philippines' deadly drug war. The warrant, unsealed on Monday, charges him as an "indirect co-perpetrator" in the "crime against humanity of murder" for killings between July 2016 and April 2018. Dela Rosa was pictured fleeing into the Senate building after being confronted by National Bureau of Investigation agents.  The former police chief, who ran the Philippine National Police during the drug war, is accused of creating death squads to carry out extrajudicial killings.

articles.title: EU preparing to offer key concession to UK in new post-Brexit agricultural deal | European Union | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is securing a key concession in his efforts to improve relations with the European Union, as Brussels has agreed to allow the UK to maintain its ban on live animal exports. This carve-out, which would be part of an upcoming agricultural trade deal, is seen as a significant victory for Starmer and could pave the way for closer ties in other areas like emissions trading and youth mobility.  The agreement, while facing some hurdles with student tuition fees in the youth mobility scheme, is expected to benefit the British economy by up to £5.1 billion.

articles.title: ​Belated warning: On the Prime Minister’s austerity appeal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi issued a seven-point call to action for citizens of India, urging them to work from home and reduce fuel consumption in response to the West Asia crisis. The timing and content of his message have been criticized as problematic, particularly given his recent campaign travels and pre-election silence on these issues.  The government's decision not to raise fuel prices before elections has been lauded by some but is now being seen as a strategic move to dilute its impact on the public. Confederation of Indian Industry also issued a call to action for Indian corporations, highlighting the dire situation and potential negative impacts of Modi's suggestions.

articles.title: Iran says ready to 'teach a lesson' if attacked after Trump called Tehran's latest peace proposal 'piece of garbage' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf exchanged sharp remarks regarding the fragile ceasefire in the Middle East.  Trump dismissed Iran's counterproposal as "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE" while Ghalibaf stated that Iran's armed forces were prepared for any confrontation. The standoff has heightened tensions and raised concerns about the future of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil shipping route, potentially leading to global energy supply disruptions.  Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser warned of the largest energy shock in history while the United Nations expressed fears of a humanitarian crisis due to reduced fertilizer exports.

articles.title: Plot to coerce girl into carrying out terrorist attack in Islamabad thwarted, CM Bugti says - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sarfraz Bugti, the Chief Minister of Balochistan, announced that a plot to coerce a girl into carrying out a suicide bombing in Islamabad had been thwarted by intelligence agencies. The girl, who was reportedly arrested before she could carry out the attack, will be released to her father under supervision instead of facing trial.  Bugti condemned the exploitation of Baloch women and girls by terrorists, emphasizing that they have no connection to Balochiyat tradition or history. He praised the intelligence agencies for foiling a major plan and stressed that the girl was exploited in an egregious way.

articles.title: UK sanctions network accused of planning attacks for Iran | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government has imposed sanctions on an Iranian-linked network accused of plotting attacks in the UK and elsewhere. The Foreign Office issued travel bans, asset freezes, and director disqualification orders to nine individuals and three entities linked to “Iranian-backed hostile activity.”  These targets are alleged members and associates of the Zindashti criminal network, accused of threatening, planning or conducting attacks against people and assets in Britain and elsewhere. The sanctions follow separate measures taken by London, Washington, and Brussels against Iran in recent months.

articles.title: Evacuated US and French MV Hondius passengers test positive for hantavirus | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A French woman and an American passenger evacuated from the cruise ship MV Hondius, which was at the center of a deadly hantavirus outbreak, have tested positive for the virus.  Stéphanie Rist, French health minister, confirmed that the French woman is in serious condition and being treated in Paris. The US health department announced that one American national evacuated from the ship has tested positive for the Andes strain of hantavirus, while another passenger had mild symptoms.  The repatriation operation to evacuate over 100 people from 23 nationalities continued on Monday with more than 94 passengers already flown out. Maud Bregeon, a French government spokesperson, stated that the risk for global public health is low and authorities are taking necessary measures to protect the French people.

articles.title: The road to deliver women’s safety - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The case of Sai Bhagirath, son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay, under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act is being closely watched as a test of how Telangana handles crimes against women and children. The state government has taken several steps to address online and offline harassment, including launching the "Stand with Her" initiative and investigating cases of cyberbullying. However, the case highlights the challenge of balancing free expression with curbing online targeting and harassment, particularly for women in positions of power.  The incident has sparked protests demanding action from both women's groups and political parties.

articles.title: Lil Narcyz: What happened to Nikodem Czyżewski? Missing YouTuber found dead weeks later in Croatia - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lil Narcyz, a Polish YouTuber known for his comedy videos and diss tracks, was found dead in Croatia after being missing for nearly a month. The 23-year-old influencer disappeared on April 8th and his body was identified by Polish police.  The cause of death has not yet been released, but authorities have confirmed the search has ended. Fans expressed shock and sadness over the sudden passing of the popular internet personality who had amassed over 450,000 subscribers on YouTube.

articles.title: US Stock Market Today | Dow Jones | Nasdaq Live: S&P 500 inches to higher close, AI fervor edges out Iran impasse - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Meta Platforms Inc. is facing a lawsuit from Santa Clara County, alleging the company profits from billions of scam advertisements on its platforms.  Microsoft Corp. plans to return $92 billion from its investment in OpenAI. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser predicts oil market stabilization could be delayed until 2027 due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Investors are awaiting key inflation data and consumer demand trends this week, while US Treasury yields rose on concerns over inflation and potential rate hikes.  The Clarity Act, aiming for a regulatory framework for cryptocurrencies, is expected to face opposition from both sides of the aisle.

articles.title: LHC accepts Maryam's plea seeking return of bail surety in Chaudhry Sugar Mills case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court (LHC) granted an application by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, allowing the return of Rs70 million surety deposited for her bail in the Chaudhry Sugar Mills case. The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) withdrew its plea challenging directives for the closure of the investigation against Maryam, and the LHC bench accepted her request.  The court's decision follows an accountability court's March ruling allowing Maryam to withdraw her surety bond after a February 4 directive from the LHC to place a termination report before the accountability court for the closure of the investigation.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal waves Palestine flag as Barcelona celebrate La Liga win | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lamine Yamal, a 18-year-old Spanish football star, drew praise for waving a Palestinian flag from an open-top bus during Barcelona's La Liga victory parade. Thousands of fans lined the streets to celebrate the team's win over Real Madrid, marking their 29th league title. The celebration comes amidst ongoing pro-Palestinian activism in Barcelona following Israel’s conflict with Gaza.

articles.title: News live: Australian passengers on MV Hondius to return via Netherlands; Jane Hume refuses to rule out Coalition alliance with One Nation | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australians on the MV Hondius ship were evacuated to the Netherlands overnight after a Dutch flight was used instead of a planned second flight from Tenerife. The Spanish health minister, Mónica García, stated that the decision was made due to timing issues with the second plane.  The deputy Liberal leader, senator Jane Hume, acknowledged the loss in the Farrer byelection and emphasized listening to voters' concerns.

articles.title: Imaan, Hadi submit additional documents ahead of hearing on appeals in apex court tomorrow - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, submitted additional documents to the Supreme Court of Pakistan in support of their appeal against the Islamabad High Court's denial of interim relief in a controversial social media posts case. The documents include charge sheets, statements from court appearances, and orders issued by the trial court.  The couple argues that recording evidence before their absence was a violation of their due process rights and seeks to have these documents admitted for the Supreme Court's consideration. A three-judge bench will hear the appeals on May 12th.

articles.title: EU agrees sanctions on Israeli West Bank settlers, Hamas leaders | European Union News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union has agreed to impose sanctions on Israeli settlers and Hamas leaders. The agreement, reached at a meeting of member states' foreign ministers, targets three Israeli settlers and four settler organizations for their role in violence against Palestinians in the West Bank.  French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot welcomed the decision, stating that the EU is sanctioning those responsible for "extremisms and violence." Israel condemned the sanctions, arguing that Jewish settlement in the occupied West Bank is a right protected by international law. The EU also sanctioned Hamas leaders for their role in the October 7th attack on southern Israel.

articles.title: Putin is in a ‘weaker position than ever before’, says EU’s Kallas – as it happened | Europe | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas criticized Russian President Vladimir Putin's ceasefire calls and suggested he is in a weaker position than ever before. The EU agreed on new sanctions targeting violent Israeli settlers and leading Hamas figures, while also opening negotiation clusters for Ukraine's accession to the bloc by summer.  Kallas emphasized that Ukraine is in a much better position than a year ago, with growing discontent within Russia and expanding internet restrictions. She also highlighted the need for accountability from Russia for its actions in Ukraine. The EU also adopted sanctions on individuals and entities in Russia or occupied Ukrainian territories over systematic unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children.

articles.title: Farmers take out rally demanding legal guarantee for MSP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Scores of farmers from across Andhra Pradesh, Assam, and other states participated in a rally organized by the Akhila Bharata Aikya Rythu Sangham (AIUKS) in Yellandu, Bhadradri Kothagudem district. The rally demanded a legal guarantee for Minimum Support Price (MSP) and implementation of the C2 + 50% formula.  AIUKS leaders, including Pradeep Singh Tagore, Kechela Ranga Reddy, and Potu Ranga Rao, led the demonstration, which culminated in a public meeting.

articles.title: ChudTheBuilder breaks silence after Nashville arrest and shocking FBI questioning over restaurant dispute - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton ChudTheBuilder, a controversial internet creator, was arrested in Nashville on May 9, 2026, following an altercation at Bob’s ChopHouse restaurant.  He claims his phones were seized as evidence and he was questioned by FBI agents and a domestic terrorist detective. ChudTheBuilder spent nearly 13 hours in custody before being released and returned to his Airbnb. The incident sparked online debate with some users criticizing his behavior while others questioned the seriousness of the investigation.  Authorities have not yet released further details about the case.

articles.title: India's Modi to launch multi-nation tour amid global unrest - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Modi, the Indian Prime Minister, will embark on a multi-nation tour this week, visiting the United Arab Emirates, the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, and Italy.  The trip focuses on bolstering trade and investment ties with each country, particularly in areas like energy cooperation, defense, semiconductors, water management, and clean technology. The visit to the UAE will be followed by stops in the Netherlands, Sweden, and Norway before concluding in Italy.

articles.title: Trump says he will discuss arms sales to Taiwan in meeting with China’s Xi | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump will discuss US arms sales to Taiwan during his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this week.  Trump stated he plans to raise the issue of weapons sales, despite President Xi's desire to prevent such discussions. The US has long provided Taiwan with weapons for defense against potential Chinese aggression, a stance that has strained relations with Beijing. While China condemns these arms sales, the US maintains no official position on Taiwanese sovereignty and calls for peaceful resolution between Taipei and Beijing.

articles.title: Elon Musk and Tim Cook among CEOs expected to accompany Trump on China trip
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is taking a delegation of top business and technology executives to China this week, including Tim Cook of Apple, Elon Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, and Larry Fink of BlackRock. The trip comes amid growing economic and technological tensions between the US and China, with the purpose of meeting with President Xi Jinping.  The delegation represents a range of industries, including social media, consumer hardware, computer chips, and commercial manufacturing.

articles.title: Poland says it expects US to extradite ex-minister who fled from Hungary | Poland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Poland's foreign minister, Radosław Sikorski, stated that the country expects the United States to extradite former justice minister Zbigniew Ziobro, who fled Hungary and entered the US.  Ziobro is wanted by Polish prosecutors for charges of abuse of power and corruption. The Polish government has accused him of leading a criminal group that diverted funds from victims of violence, while he denies the allegations. Ziobro claims to have entered the US using asylum documents provided by Hungary, but his presence in the country has raised questions about potential US involvement in his case.

articles.title: Education Budget will grow every year, says Telangana CM Revanth Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy announced that the Telangana government will prioritize education, aiming for a 15% allocation in future budgets, gradually increasing from the current 7.6%.  He highlighted the implementation of several initiatives since December 2023, including teacher recruitment, DSC notifications, and global exchange programs. The "Exclusive Education Week" celebrations aim to showcase progress and improve learning facilities across the state. Mr. Reddy emphasized that education is an investment in the future and stressed the importance of teachers in building a better society.

articles.title: Only favors Indian-origin candidates: Chinese-American professor sues university in Texas, accuses Hemang Desai of bias - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Sean Wang, a Chinese-American assistant professor at Southern Methodist University (SMU), has filed a lawsuit alleging discrimination and preferential treatment towards Indian professors in the Accounting department. The lawsuit claims that Wang was denied tenure while three Indian colleagues were granted tenure despite meeting SMU's productivity standards.  The lawsuit also alleges that Dr. Hemang Desai, the department chair, treated Wang differently than his Indian colleagues and that Indian faculty members received prime offices with better views.  SMU denies all allegations.

articles.title: Trump rejects Iran's counteroffer to end war, insists on 'complete victory' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump rejected Iran’s latest counteroffer to the ceasefire in the Middle East war, calling it “TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE” and stating that the truce was on its last legs.  Oil prices surged as a result of this rejection, while global energy markets face an unprecedented supply shock. The situation has also raised concerns about food security due to shortages of fertilizer, with the United Nations warning of a potential humanitarian crisis affecting tens of millions of people. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu insisted that the conflict would not end until Iran's nuclear facilities are destroyed.

articles.title: South Africa plans presidential impeachment probe over ‘Farmgate’ scandal | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: South Africa's parliament will establish an impeachment committee to investigate allegations against President Cyril Ramaphosa in the "Farmgate" scandal. The move follows a decision by the country's highest court to revive impeachment proceedings, which center on the theft of $4 million in foreign currency from Ramaphosa's Phala Phala game farm.  The committee will review evidence and decide whether to recommend formal impeachment proceedings.

articles.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire is on 'massive life support'
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated the month-long ceasefire between the US and Iran is on "massive life support" and that he rejected Iran's counter-offer, calling it "totally unacceptable".  Esmail Baghaei, a foreign ministry spokesperson for Iran, responded by saying Tehran's proposals were "responsible" and "generous", including demands for an end to the war on all fronts, a halt to the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, and guarantees against further attacks.  Trump criticized Iran's proposal and accused them of going back on agreements regarding enriched uranium.

articles.title: Jewish musicians faced abuse over Zionist beliefs, royal commisssion told | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Deborah Conway and Joshua Moshe, Jewish musicians, testified before a royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion about the backlash they faced for expressing their Zionism.  They described online abuse, boycotts, and professional repercussions stemming from their views. Julie Nathan, research director of the Executive Council of Australian Jewry, argued that criticism of Israel is not inherently antisemitic but that language invoking Nazi Germany or anti-Jewish tropes should be considered so. Tahli Blicblau, executive director of the Dor Foundation, highlighted the rise in antisemitism on university campuses and online spaces, emphasizing a decade-long trend exacerbated by recent events.

articles.title: China's marriages drop to decade low, deepening demographic concerns - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: China's Ministry of Civil Affairs reported 1.697 million marriage registrations in the latest quarter, reflecting a deepening demographic challenge.  The country's population continued to decline for the fourth consecutive year in 2025, and its birth rate hit a record low, prompting concerns about further population decline. Authorities have implemented various measures to encourage marriage and childbearing, including family subsidies and childcare support.

articles.title: Telangana BIE re-releases admission schedule; classes for Inter first year to begin from June 1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Board of Intermediate Education (BIE) released the admissions schedule for 2026-27, with phase-I admissions starting on Tuesday and concluding by June 30.  Principals are instructed to make provisional admissions based on internet marks memo downloaded by candidates, which will be confirmed upon presentation of original SSC pass certificates and transfer certificates. The BIE also mandated Aadhaar details for students and directed colleges to limit sections to a maximum of 88 students with prior approval for additional sections.

articles.title: Donald Trump 'seriously considering' making Venezuela the 51st state of US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has stated he is "seriously considering" making Venezuela the 51st state of the United States.  This comes after Maduro's capture earlier this year and an interim administration led by Delcy Rodríguez. The US has reopened its embassy in Caracas, resumed direct flights, and increased involvement in Venezuela's oil sector, leading to Trump's assertion that Venezuela is "happy" and "being well run." However, such a move would require approval from Congress and the consent of Venezuela itself.

articles.title: Shepherd sacrifices life, averting suicide attack in Attock - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A shepherd, Liaqat, was killed while attempting to prevent a suicide attack at a security post in Attock's Jand area.  Liaqat, a former employee of Pakistan Railways, noticed a suspicious individual and confronted him before the suspect detonated his vest, causing a powerful explosion. The incident occurred near a key security post on the Punjab-Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border, which is part of a nationwide network established to combat smuggling and other criminal activities. Sardar Marwan Khan, District Police Officer, and Rao Atif Raza, Deputy Commissioner, were present at the scene as authorities began investigating the incident.

articles.title: Could the latest violence in DR Congo undermine truce efforts? | Armed Groups | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lesser-known armed groups, including the Cooperative for the Development of the Congo and the Convention for the Popular Revolution, have carried out attacks in the Democratic Republic of Congo's northeast, challenging efforts to achieve peace. These recent assaults follow earlier violence by these groups and pose a threat to ongoing negotiations between the government and the Rwanda-backed M23 fighters.  The situation raises questions about the feasibility of establishing lasting peace in the region.

articles.title: US cruise ship passengers being monitored for hantavirus in Nebraska
articles.rephrased_article: US passengers evacuated from a cruise ship in the Canary Islands are being monitored for hantavirus exposure. Admiral Brian Christine, of the US Health and Human Services department (HHS), stated that the risk to the public is very low, as the Andes variant does not easily spread.  The 16 passengers quarantined at Nebraska's national quarantine unit are in good spirits and will undergo further assessment before determining if they need to complete the full 42-day quarantine period.

articles.title: Drug gang attacks ‘force hundreds of Indigenous families to flee’ in Mexico | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Indigenous families in Guerrero state, Mexico have been forced to flee their homes due to intense attacks by the criminal group Los Ardillos. The attacks include drone bombings and gunfire, resulting in at least four deaths and forcing between 800 to 1,000 families to seek refuge elsewhere.  The violence has escalated significantly over the past week, prompting calls for increased government intervention and protection from both local officials and drug cartels. Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president, acknowledged the situation and pledged support for displaced families while emphasizing the need to address the root causes of the violence.

articles.title: Modi’s austerity drive is an admission of failure on economic and foreign policy fronts, alleges Akhilesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Akhilesh Yadav, president of the Samajwadi Party, criticized Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal for austerity in light of the Iran conflict, accusing the BJP government of failing on both economic and foreign policy fronts.  Yadav argued that the appeal was an admission of failure and that the restrictions imposed were disproportionate to the perceived crisis. He also accused the BJP of fueling political unrest with electoral fraud and social discord.

articles.title: EU ministers agree on sanctions targeting violent West Bank settlers - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: European Union foreign ministers agreed on new sanctions targeting violent Israeli settlers and Hamas figures. The sanctions, blocked by the previous Hungarian government, were aimed at three settlers and four organizations whose identities remain undisclosed.  Gideon Saar, Israeli Foreign Minister, criticized the EU's decision, calling it arbitrary and politically motivated.

articles.title: Where did the hantavirus outbreak start, and where has it spread? | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The hantavirus outbreak began on the MV Hondius cruise ship, which departed from Argentina on April 1. The virus has spread to at least 20 countries with passengers being evacuated and quarantined in various locations. At least three people have died, including an elderly Dutch couple who were among the first to develop symptoms.  The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends testing and monitoring for at least 42 days after suspected exposure. The outbreak is linked to the Andes strain of hantavirus, which is endemic in rural parts of South America.

articles.title: Muslim Votes Matter says anonymous bid to create political party under same name an attempt to ‘mislead’ voters | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Muslim Votes Matter (MVM) has lodged a complaint with the Victorian Electoral Commission alleging that an anonymous group is attempting to register a political party under their name. MVM, a grassroots advocacy movement focused on Muslim and minority representation in Australia, claims this move is intended to mislead voters by exploiting the existing group voting ticket system (GVT). The attempt to register a party with the same name as MVM has been criticized by MVM spokesperson Ghaith Krayem who believes it risks confusing voters at the ballot box.  The Victorian Electoral Commission has not confirmed receiving the complaint but will be unable to process applications until after the Nepean byelection writ is returned on or before May 23rd.

articles.title: Q1 fuel losses may eliminate entire fiscal-year earnings of Indian OMCs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL), and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) have been running record high under-recoveries due to the sustained low prices of petrol, diesel, and cooking gas LPG despite soaring global crude oil prices. The combined daily losses are estimated at Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 1,200 crore, with ICRA Ltd estimating losses of around Rs 1,000 crore per day on the sale of auto fuels and domestic LPG.  The government has intervened by reducing excise duty on petrol and diesel to absorb some of the fuel cost burden.

articles.title: 6 most snake-filled places around Ontario’s waters | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ontario's diverse waterways, from Lake Erie to Rice Lake, support a variety of snake species.  Northern water snakes are commonly spotted in areas like Lake Erie and Georgian Bay, while Eastern fox snakes inhabit the wetlands around Lake Huron.  The St Lawrence River provides shelter for northern water snakes and other species, including milksnakes and garter snakes.  These reptiles are often found near marshes and shorelines.  Despite their presence in many areas, most snake species in Ontario are non-venomous.

articles.title: Karnataka: Deficit pre-monsoon rainfall in 11 districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Eleven districts in Karnataka, including Bengaluru Urban and Tumakuru, experienced deficit pre-monsoon rainfall between March 1 and May 11.  The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) reported that these districts received rainfall below the normal range of +19% to -19%.  The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts a below-normal monsoon season for most of Karnataka, with some regions in northeast and southeast-interior Karnataka expected to receive above-normal rainfall.

articles.title: Skipper Shanto extends Bangladesh lead by 179 runs in first Test against Pakistan - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh extended their lead over Pakistan to 179 runs on the fourth day of the first Test match in Dhaka.  Najmul Hossain Shanto hit an unbeaten half-century, while Mominul Haque reached a fifty before being dismissed. The hosts were 152-3 at stumps with Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim remaining unbeaten. Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan failed to hold on to a catch, but the afternoon session was washed out by heavy rain.  The final day promises to be an exciting one for fans as both teams battle for victory.

articles.title: Cole Allen pleads not guilty to attempted Trump assassination | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, 31, of California, pleaded not guilty to charges including attempted assassination of President Donald Trump at a White House reporters gala.  His legal team argues that US Attorney Jeanine Pirro, who was present at the event, and other Department of Justice officials should be disqualified from prosecuting him due to potential conflicts of interest stemming from their friendship with Trump. Allen is also accused of assaulting a federal officer and possessing firearms illegally. The case will continue before Judge Trevor McFadden on June 29th.

articles.title: BBC tests out England and Argentina's World Cup training grounds in Kansas City
articles.rephrased_article: The BBC's Will Grant has been assessing the training grounds for England and Argentina ahead of the FIFA World Cup.  Both teams will be based in Kansas City, with England at Swope Soccer Village and Argentina at the Sporting KC Training Center. The Netherlands and Algeria have also chosen to train in the area. These sites will serve as hubs for match preparation activities.

articles.title: Changing tax rules for investors won’t shrink housing supply or raise rents. Just look at Victoria | Anthony Albanese | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Albanese government is preparing to unveil a budget that will recast housing as shelter rather than a financial tool, aiming to curb investor activity. The changes are expected to impact negative gearing and capital gains tax for new purchases, but existing investors will be protected with grandfather provisions. While some predict market fluctuations, experts argue that these reforms will encourage more equitable housing access and won't lead to a significant reduction in supply.  The government's approach is similar to past policies that have faced criticism, but ultimately haven't resulted in the predicted negative outcomes.

articles.title: Early Lenskart investor Alpha Wave trims stake by 2.5% in open market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Alpha Wave Ventures II and its affiliates have reduced their stake in Lenskart, selling 4.3 crore shares, representing a significant secondary transaction in the company.  The sale lowered their combined holding to 4.67% of the omnichannel eyewear retailer's equity capital. The move comes despite Motilal Oswal projecting strong growth for Lenskart, with a projected compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 25%/53% in revenue and pre-IND AS EBITDA.

articles.title: ‘One last wish’: Why Napoleon Bonaparte wanted his hair preserved after death | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Napoleon Bonaparte's will stipulated that his hair be preserved and turned into a bracelet, with strands sent to family members and close associates. This practice was common in the 19th century as a way of mourning after death, and Napoleon's hair became a significant relic for both sentimental and historical reasons. The decision to preserve his hair before dissection ensured its survival, contributing to ongoing debate about his death.  The preserved locks have become part of historical collections and continue to fuel fascination over the circumstances surrounding his demise.

articles.title: How a bid to make Thirumavalavan Tamil Nadu’s CM failed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalavan, leader of the VCK, was unable to secure support for himself as the first Chief Minister from the Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu despite a last-minute attempt by DMK and AIADMK.  The move was prompted by difficulties securing an AIADMK government with DMK support, leading to negotiations between the VCK, CPI, CPI-M, and the Left parties. Ultimately, Thirumavalavan decided against the proposal after discussions with senior DMK and AIADMK leaders.

articles.title: Senators decry hike in petroleum prices, accuse govt of 'economic oppression' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senators in Pakistan's Senate criticized the recent hike in petroleum prices and costly energy, accusing the government of economic oppression.  They demanded an exit from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program and called for immediate withdrawal of the fuel hike.  Barrister Syed Ali Zafar, a PTI leader, argued that the government was collecting more than the agreed-upon limit on petroleum levies, while Aamir Waliuddin Chishti, a MQM-P senator, warned that Pakistan's high energy costs and low exports would keep it in debt to the IMF.  Senator Kamran Murtaza raised concerns about Senator Abdul Shakoor being placed on the Fourth Schedule of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997. The bill seeking to extend blue passport eligibility for senators' children was met with opposition from the Ministry of Interior.

articles.title: Who could challenge Keir Starmer for the UK PM’s job? Meet the candidates | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has pledged to prove his doubters wrong as he faces pressure to resign following disastrous local election results and mounting discontent within the Labour Party.  While some, like Angela Rayner, have been suggested as potential challengers, others, such as Wes Streeting, are also seen as possible contenders. The possibility of a leadership contest hinges on whether more than 20% of Labour MPs support a new candidate, which could be triggered if Starmer refuses to step down.  However, none of the potential challengers have yet publicly declared their intention to challenge Starmer.

articles.title: Soldier on parachuting to Tristan da Cunha for Hantavirus aid
articles.rephrased_article: British Army paratroopers successfully parachuted onto the remote Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha to deliver medical aid to a British national with suspected hantavirus. The mission involved two paratroopers, an intensive care nurse, and a specialist doctor, who delivered supplies and waited for several days to assist the patient before returning to Britain.  The team's efforts were hampered by high winds, making it a challenging operation.

articles.title: Victorian politics still exposed to ‘dark money’ and foreign donations as MPs struggle to agree on urgent reforms | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria is facing a political donation crisis after the high court struck down its laws, leaving the state vulnerable to unlimited dark money. Labor, Liberals, and Greens are in negotiations to reintroduce donation caps, disclosure requirements, and public funding arrangements but remain divided on key details. The lack of legislation has raised concerns from Animal Justice Party, Libertarian MP David Limbrick, and civil society organizations who advocate for a retrospective approach and independent review.

articles.title: Groww stake sale: Peak XV, Sequoia, others to sell equity worth Rs 4,750 crore; floor price at Rs 177/share - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1, YC Holdings II, LLC, and Ribbit Capital V L.P. are selling shares of discount broker Groww. The transaction will be executed through a vendor sale on the Indian stock exchanges' screen-based trading platform.  The stock price dropped 5.37% to Rs 204.70 after the announcement. Groww was established in 2016 and offers brokerage services for equity, IPOs, and mutual funds. The company went public in November 2025 with a market capitalization of Rs 6,632.30 crores.

articles.title: ‘One last wish’: Why Napoleon Bonaparte wanted his hair preserved after death | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Napoleon Bonaparte's final will instructed that his hair be preserved and turned into a bracelet for distribution to family members. This practice, common in the 19th century, was a way of holding on to someone physically after death.  The request led to the preservation of authentic locks from Napoleon's head, which have been used as historical artifacts and continue to fuel debate about his death. The hair also became a sentimental keepsake for those closest to him.

articles.title: How a bid to make Thirumavalavan CM failed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thol. Thirumavalvan, leader of the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK), was unable to secure the support needed for him to become the first Chief Minister from the Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu. The attempt faced opposition from both the DMK and the AIADMK, who were reportedly concerned about potential backlash and criticism.  Despite support from the CPI, CPI(M), and the VCK, Thirumavalvan ultimately decided against the proposal after backroom negotiations failed to garner sufficient consensus among the parties involved.

articles.title: Two years on, over a third of General Elections 2024 petitions await disposal - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Election tribunals across Pakistan have yet to dispose of nearly a third of election petitions filed following the February 2024 general elections.  While Free and Fair Election Network (Fafen) reports that 66% of cases have been decided, with most decisions favoring dismissed candidates, the pace of disposal has slowed in recent months. The delay is attributed to legal challenges and appointments issues, particularly in Punjab where only two tribunals functioned until October 2024.  The Supreme Court has overturned one election result, but many appeals remain pending.

articles.title: Israeli attacks kill at least four in southern Lebanon | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli military strikes in southern Lebanon have killed at least four people and wounded eight others, according to Lebanese media.  The attacks followed a forced displacement warning issued by the Israeli army for nine towns in southern and eastern Lebanon. The Islamic Health Society medics were injured while responding to an earlier attack. Despite a ceasefire that began on April 17th, Israel continues to exchange fire with Hezbollah, resulting in ongoing violence.

articles.title: Emmanuel Macron interrupts speaker to ask for silence
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron, the French President, interrupted a speaker at the Africa Forward summit in Nairobi to request silence from attendees.  He stated there was "a total lack of respect" and urged those engaging in side discussions to continue them outside or in designated meeting rooms. The summit brings together over 30 African leaders, business executives, and young entrepreneurs as France seeks to strengthen economic and political ties across the continent.

articles.title: Supermarket foods claiming to be ‘natural’ or ‘sustainable’ mostly just using marketing terms, researchers find | Food | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australian researchers from the George Institute for Global Health found that many environmental claims on supermarket products, such as "natural" and "sustainable," are not backed by verified evidence.  Nearly four in 10 packaged foods sold at major supermarkets in Sydney carried some sort of sustainability claim, but most were self-declared by manufacturers without independent verification. The study also revealed that while products making climate-related claims generally had lower carbon footprints, certain categories like meat and confectionery saw the opposite effect. This raises concerns about consumer trust and the need for clearer, standardized environmental labeling systems to help consumers make informed choices.

articles.title: SC dismisses appeals against SHC order in TRG shareholding dispute - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court (SC) dismissed appeals filed by Greentree Holdings Limited (GTH) against a June order from the Sindh High Court (SHC) that declared GTH shares to be property of private equity firm The Resource Group Pakistan (TRGP). The SC rejected three appeals and directed GTH to bear the legal costs of respondent Muhammad Ziaullah Khan Chishti, who had previously filed an application under company laws.  The case stems from a dispute over ownership of shares in TRGP, with GTH challenging the SHC's ruling.

articles.title: Israel pushes for hangings and ‘show trials’ for ‘October 7 detainees’ | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel is pushing for a new legal framework that would allow special tribunals to try Palestinians accused of involvement in the October 7th attacks, potentially resulting in "show trials" and the death penalty. The bill, which has bipartisan support, grants judges broad authority to deviate from standard legal procedures, including admitting evidence obtained through torture.  The legislation also mandates public broadcasting of proceedings, raising concerns about fair trial guarantees and due process. International rights groups have condemned the move as a discriminatory tool that could be used to strip detainees of their fundamental legal protections.

articles.title: Bosnia's powerful peace envoy quits, with questions over role's future
articles.rephrased_article: Christian Schmidt, the powerful international high representative of Bosnia and Herzegovina, has resigned after a tumultuous tenure marked by conflict and controversy. His departure raises questions about the future of the Office of the High Representative, established to enforce the Dayton Peace Agreement and maintain peace in the country.  The role's legitimacy is now uncertain as Russia continues to support calls for its closure, potentially leaving Bosnia vulnerable to ethno-nationalist leaders like Milorad Dodik.

articles.title: Philippine presidential hopeful Sara Duterte impeached for second time | Philippines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Duterte, the Philippine vice-president, was impeached by an overwhelming majority of lawmakers in the House of Representatives. The accusations against her include misuse of public funds, unexplained wealth accumulation, and threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife, Louise Araneta-Marcos.  Duterte has denied all wrongdoing and will now face a trial in the Senate. If found guilty, she could be banned from public office, jeopardizing her presidential ambitions for 2028. The case is further complicated by Duterte's family ties to former president Rodrigo Duterte, who faces charges of crimes against humanity at the International Criminal Court.

articles.title: BSE launches F&O trading on IT index; debut day turnover at Rs 148 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE launched derivative contracts for its Focused IT Index, a benchmark representing India's influential technology sector. The new derivatives offer investors hedging and risk management tools, with cash-settled contracts available across three monthly expiries.  The launch saw active participation on the first trading day, with 172 members contributing to a turnover of Rs 148 crore. BSE CEO Sundararaman Ramamurthy stated that the new product complements existing index derivatives and enhances risk management for investors.

articles.title: From sleeping in a car to Ivy League: California teen earns admission to 65 elite colleges with 4.4 GPA | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lamont Newell, a 17-year-old student from South Los Angeles, has garnered national attention for his remarkable feat of earning admission to 65 colleges while overcoming homelessness and family hardship.
