The results saw Reform UK secure 17 MSPs, while the Scottish National Party won a fifth consecutive victory and secured a majority. John Swinney, leader of the SNP, has indicated he will seek collaboration with other parties on legislation despite their rejection of Reform UK.

articles.title: Bonus issues, stock splits & dividends: SBI among 18 stocks turning ex-date this week. Do you own any? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several stocks will turn ex-date for corporate actions such as dividends, bonus issues, and stock splits between May 11th and 15th. Kothari Petrochemicals, Manappuram Finance, PAE, Godrej Consumer Products, NRB Bearings, Brookfield India Real Estate Trust REIT, Oberoi Realty, Anand Rathi Wealth, Aptus Value Housing Finance India, Biogen Pharmachem Industries, Dev Labtech Venture, and Gopal Snacks are among the companies with record dates for these actions.  The effective record date for some of these companies will be May 15th due to weekend market closures. The dividend payment schedules vary depending on the company, but many will be paid out in June.

articles.title: Atef Najib faces at least 10 charges in landmark Syria trial | Bashar al-Assad News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Atef Najib, cousin of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, appeared in court on Sunday for the first substantive day of his trial in Damascus.  He faces at least 10 charges, including murder, torture, and responsibility for massacres, stemming from his role as head of political security in Deraa province during the 2011 uprising. Najib is accused of overseeing a violent crackdown on antigovernment protesters, with 75 plaintiffs filing cases against him. The trial marks the first effort in Syria to bring Assad-era officials to justice and follows criticism over delays in launching a promised transitional justice process.

articles.title: Ageing ornamental trees behind mass uprooting during rains in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) data reveals that over 515 trees were uprooted and more than 1,500 branches snapped during recent rains. Experts attribute this damage to the lack of focused tree management practices, particularly pruning and removal, for ornamental trees which are highly vulnerable to strong winds and rainfall.  Noted environmentalist A.N. Yellappa Reddy emphasized that these trees have a short lifespan and are often exotic species, making them more susceptible to weather events. Civic neglect, including the cutting of roots for drain construction and improper pruning, has further exacerbated the issue.

articles.title: Spanish passengers start disembarkation from ship hit by hantavirus - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Spain began evacuating passengers from the cruise ship hit by a hantavirus outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) and European Union requested Spain to manage the evacuation, with Spanish nationals being first to disembark on small boats and transferred to a hospital for quarantine.  Passengers from other countries will follow in groups, with British military personnel also involved in an airdrop of medical supplies to a suspected patient on a remote island.

articles.title: Iran warns against complying with US blockade as Gulf attacks reported
articles.rephrased_article: Iran warned its Gulf neighbors that complying with US sanctions would lead to difficulties crossing the Strait of Hormuz, while the United States maintains a ceasefire reached last month remains in place.  A commercial vessel was hit by an unknown projectile off the coast of Qatar, and both Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates reported foiled drone attacks. The incidents follow a clash between US naval destroyers and Iran's military two days ago. Both sides have attempted to implement rival blockades in the strait, which is vital for global oil and gas trade.

articles.title: ‘Everyone was in tears’: the tenants given eviction notices just before ban in England | Housing | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of tenants across England received no-fault evictions in the days and hours before the ban on these notices took effect under the Renters’ Rights Act.  Carl Kansinde Middleton, a 27-year-old tenant, was evicted just 10 hours before the ban went into effect, leaving him without a place to live.  Similar stories emerged from tenants across England, including Izzi, a 68-year-old woman who received an eviction notice after being diagnosed with a brain tumor. The new law aims to protect renters' rights but has created challenges for both landlords and tenants.  A spokesperson for the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government stated that the ban is designed to free families from the misery caused by no-fault evictions.

articles.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nifty closed lower on Friday, with analysts citing weakening momentum and a bearish sentiment. Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities, noted the index's decline below its 50-day moving average and a bearish RSI crossover on the daily chart.  However, Nilesh Jain, Vice President - Head of Technical and Derivative Research at Centrum Finverse, suggests a near-term recovery towards 24,300–24,500 levels as the broader structure remains sideways to positive.  SBI, HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank were among the negative performers on Friday.

articles.title: Can Asian economies cope with the fallout from the Iran war? | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Asian economies are facing significant challenges due to the fallout from the Iran war, including rising fuel costs, inflation, and debt pressures.  Governments are implementing measures like rationing fuel and reintroducing subsidies to mitigate the impact of the energy crisis. The disruption of the Strait of Hormuz is exacerbating these issues, leading to increased import bills and currency depreciation.

articles.title: Recovery agent found dead in Balapur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 24-year-old recovery agent, Adit Pandey, was found dead in Balapur on Sunday morning.  Police suspect a dispute over territorial rivalry in vehicle recovery operations led to his murder by an unidentified individual identified as Munna.  Munna, also involved in vehicle recovery and seizure work, allegedly warned Pandey not to operate in his area. The victim's family suspects Munna's involvement. Police have registered a murder case and are searching for the suspect.

articles.title: ‘They should not be allowed to stand’: British MP Rupert Lowe slams election of Indian-born Scottish lawmaker without permanent visa | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: British MP Rupert Lowe called for a ban on foreign nationals contesting elections in the UK following the election of Q Manivannan, an Indian-born politician, to the Scottish Parliament.  Lowe criticized existing rules after Manivannan, who holds temporary immigration status, was elected despite not having permanent residency. The issue sparked debate as the Scottish government changed eligibility rules last year to allow individuals with limited leave to remain in the UK to stand for office.

articles.title: There are 'vast opportunities for investment' in Pakistan, Naqvi tells Bangladeshi state minister - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mohsin Naqvi, Pakistan's Interior Minister, met with Shama Obaid Islam, Bangladesh's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, to discuss bilateral relations and opportunities for increased trade. The two sides agreed to enhance cooperation in areas such as trade, business, and culture, while also acknowledging Pakistan's role in mediating the Iran-US conflict.  Mohammad Nazrul Islam, Bangladesh's Foreign Ministry Secretary, Imran Haider, Pakistani High Commissioner, and other officials were present at the meeting.

articles.title: Army parachutes onto Tristan da Cunha to help Briton with suspected hantavirus
articles.rephrased_article: The British Army parachuted onto the remote island of Tristan da Cunha to assist a British national with suspected hantavirus. The man, who left the cruise ship MV Hondius in mid-April after experiencing symptoms, is currently in stable condition and isolating. Yvette Cooper, Foreign Secretary, highlighted the UK's commitment to supporting British nationals abroad.  The Ministry of Defence (MoD) stated that six cases of hantavirus have been confirmed, including two Britons being treated off the ship.

articles.title: ‘Amazon of America’: film paints vision of a post-coup Brazil giving up rainforest | Brazil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new short film, "Vitória Régia," imagines a dystopian future where a far-right coup in Brazil leads to the annexation of the Amazon rainforest by the United States. The film depicts a scenario where the military takes power, censorship is imposed, and Indigenous communities are marginalized.  Carol, played by Alice Braga, a Brazilian journalist, struggles to report on the environmental devastation as Flávio Bolsonaro, Jair Bolsonaro's son, seeks to exploit Brazil's natural resources for political gain. The film highlights the potential dangers of unchecked right-wing populism and the importance of Indigenous rights in safeguarding the Amazon rainforest.  The director, Denis Kamioka, hopes "Vitória Régia" serves as a warning about the fragility of democracy and the need to protect Indigenous communities from exploitation.

articles.title: Market Trading Guide: Buy Coforge and NBCC on Monday for near-term gains of up to 7% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities, and Virat Jagad, Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza Portfolio, both predict weakness in the Nifty index due to a drop below the 50-day EMA and bearish RSI crossover. They suggest buying Coforge at Rs 1,368 with a target of Rs 1,420–1,460 and NBCC (India) at Rs 100 with a target of Rs 104–108.  Sustaining above these levels is crucial for continued positive momentum.

articles.title: Who is Q Manivannan? Tamil Nadu-born trans immigrant without permanent UK residency elected to Scottish Parliament - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Q Manivannan, an Indian-origin transgender politician, won a seat in the Scottish Parliament despite not holding permanent residency or British citizenship.  The Scottish Greens party nominated Manivannan, who identifies as non-binary and is a Commonwealth citizen with a valid visa, to represent Edinburgh and Lothians East. The election sparked debate about eligibility for candidates, with some critics arguing that foreign nationals without permanent residency should not be allowed to contest British elections. The Scottish Greens defended Manivannan's candidacy, stating they are on a valid visa and criticizing the UK immigration system.

articles.title: PM Modi assures more support to Telangana, asks CM Revanth to collaborate with him - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy that the Central government would continue to support its development, emphasizing the importance of state-level progress for a developed India by 2047.  During his visit on May 10, 2026, Modi inaugurated several developmental projects worth ₹9,400 crore, including industrial parks and railway infrastructure, aiming to make Telangana a manufacturing hub. He highlighted the government's commitment to creating employment opportunities and reviving the textile industry through schemes like PM Mitra Park at Warangal and investments in infrastructure development.  The Prime Minister also emphasized the importance of energy security with the launch of the Malkapur terminal.

articles.title: JCP likely to finalise panel to interview candidates - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) is expected to decide on a committee structure for interviewing candidates for high court appointments during its upcoming meeting. The move has raised concerns from lawyers who argue that interviews should not be conducted by committees outside the constitutional framework.  The JCP's Rule-Making Committee discussed various proposals, including a seven-member committee conducting interviews prior to the full commission meeting and a five-member committee comprising judges, parliamentarians, the attorney general, and a representative of the Pakistan Bar Council. The proposals will be presented to the full commission next week, potentially leading to the finalization of new rules governing judicial appointments.

articles.title: Rebel fighters kill at least 69 people in northeastern DR Congo | Armed Groups News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Armed rebels affiliated with the Cooperative for the Development of the Congo (CODECO) militia groups carried out attacks in several villages in Ituri province, killing at least 69 people. The attacks followed an earlier assault by another armed group, the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP), on positions held by the Congolese army (FARDC) near Pimbo.  The United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the DRC (MONUSCO) condemned the recent wave of deadly attacks targeting civilians and urged its members to avoid retaliation. The killings have been blamed on the ongoing conflict between the CRP, the CODECO, and the Congolese army.

articles.title: ‘I was in a terrible state’: actor David Morrissey tells how social anxiety led him to alcoholism | David Morrissey | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Morrissey, a renowned UK actor, discussed his struggles with social anxiety and alcoholism.  He revealed that he began drinking as a teenager after the death of his father and continued to drink throughout adulthood, using alcohol as a coping mechanism for his anxiety. After 21 years of sobriety, Morrissey credits his acting career with providing him with a sense of security and purpose. He also shared how his early life experiences, including leaving school at 16 and dealing with the trauma of his father's death, contributed to his self-destructive behaviors.

articles.title: Sensex to hit 3 lakh by 2036? Raamdeo Agrawal says India is the 'Ferrari' among markets, here's why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Raamdeo Agrawal, Chairman of the MOFSL, believes India's long-term structural trajectory remains unmatched, despite recent surges in other markets driven by AI. He highlighted that India's market capitalisation has compounded at nearly 14% annually over the last two decades, compared to around 7% for the US market. Agrawal emphasized his investing philosophy of focusing on fast-growing industries within fast-growing economies and cited Bharti Airtel as a successful example of identifying multi-baggers. He projects Sensex could reach 3 lakh by 2036 due to sustained earnings growth and rising participation in financial assets.

articles.title: JK Rowling slams Starmer over Harriet Harman’s women adviser role, cites past remarks on trans women - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: JK Rowling criticized Keir Starmer's appointment of Harriet Harman as Downing Street's adviser on women and girls, citing Harman's past statements on trans women.  Rowling argued that the government is overlooking concerns of biological women and called for a clear definition of womanhood. Harman, a long-time advocate for women and girls, has previously expressed inclusive views on gender identity. The appointment has reignited debate over sex and gender definitions in UK public life.

articles.title: Rupali Chakankar appears before SIT in 'godman' Kharat case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rupali Chakankar, NCP leader and former State women’s panel chief, appeared before the special investigation team (SIT) in Nashik to answer questions about her alleged association with self-styled godman Ashok Kharat.  Ms. Chakankar resigned from both positions following revelations of her ties to Kharat, who is currently under arrest for rape and sexual exploitation. The Maharashtra Government has set up an SIT to investigate 12 cases against Kharat in Nashik and Ahilyanagar districts, with the SIT likely to question Ms. Chakankar about her connection to him.  Senior Congress leader Nana Patole alleged that Kharat’s life is in danger in prison and demanded the removal of four ministers connected to him from the state cabinet.

articles.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: THE AGE OF HYPERPOLITICS - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Anton Jäger coined the term "hyperpolitics" to describe the resurgence of political energy in the early 2010s. This new form of politics, fueled by social media and consumerism, sees individuals expressing their political views through personal consumption and aesthetic choices rather than traditional collective action.  This shift from mass politics, characterized by ideologies and movements, reflects a post-political era where individuals prioritize self-gratification and brand identity over sustained political engagement.

articles.title: Why is Iran taking time to respond to the US proposal to end the war? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran continues to review a US proposal for ending the war in the region, citing concerns over the Strait of Hormuz and its nuclear program as sticking points. The US has demanded Iran freeze uranium enrichment for 12 years and reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days in exchange for lifting sanctions.  Iran insists on guarantees against future attacks, a UN Security Council resolution, and the removal of US blockades.  The delay in Iran's response is attributed to concerns about technical details and approval from multiple Iranian power centers, including Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

articles.title: Plaid Cymru leader says he hopes to be made first minister as early as Tuesday | Plaid Cymru | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rhun ap Iorwerth, leader of Plaid Cymru, hopes to become the first minister of Wales as early as Tuesday after his party's historic victory in the Senedd elections.  Ap Iorwerth stated he wants other parties to work with him and urged Labour not to punish Wales for its decision. He believes this could lead to a change in how the UK government views Wales. The interim leader of Welsh Labour, Ken Skates, said his party will meet on Monday to discuss their approach to the vote, but described the idea of working with Reform UK as "deeply unpleasant."

articles.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rupak De, a LKP Securities analyst, noted that the Nifty index experienced further declines on Friday, falling below its 50-day moving average and exhibiting bearish momentum.  He predicts potential for further correction if the index sustains below 24,200, but also suggests a near-term recovery towards 24,350–24,400 if it rebounds above that level. Nilesh Jain, from Centrum Finverse, observed similar trends, highlighting the sideways to positive structure of the market and potential for gradual recovery towards 24,300–24,500 levels.  The most active stocks on BSE in value terms were WAM, Ujjivan SBI, Craftsman Automation, Lenskart Solutions, Action Construction Equipment, Titan Company, and HDFC Bank.

articles.title: London Sikh restaurateur to sue Met police and mayor Sadiq Khan over ‘continuous discriminatory treatment’ amid non-halal row | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Harman Singh Kapoor, a London-based restaurateur, announced plans to pursue legal action against the Metropolitan Police and London Mayor Sadiq Khan after being released from custody following his arrest related to ongoing tensions surrounding his non-halal restaurant, Rangrez.  Kapoor claims he faced "unfair and continuous discriminatory treatment" and intends to take legal action. He also urged supporters to dine at the restaurant directly rather than donate money online. Kapoor's wife defended him, accusing authorities of targeting him due to his desire to change London.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay's maiden speech on his new government in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the newly sworn-in Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, outlined his vision for a government focused on transparency, safety of women, and law and order. He pledged to address public debt and promised accountability in the use of public funds. Vijay emphasized that he would not tolerate any wrongdoing within his administration and vowed to prioritize the welfare of all citizens, including women, youth, farmers, and minorities.

articles.title: Large-scale security operation continues for 3rd day in North Waziristan's Shewa tehsil - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces conducted a large-scale operation in the Shewa tehsil of North Waziristan for a third consecutive day, resulting in the deaths of seven militants, including two key commanders. The operation involved destroying several militant hideouts and seizing weapons, while security forces also took control of important buildings and installations.  The operation aims to eliminate militant elements from the area and restore peace and stability, but has disrupted daily life for residents who have fled their homes due to increased violence and targeted killings.

articles.title: El Clasico: Kylian Mbappe not in Real Madrid squad to face Barcelona | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kylian Mbappe will miss Real Madrid’s crucial El Clasico match against Barcelona due to a hamstring injury despite training with teammates.  The French forward was left out of the 21-man squad named for Sunday's game at the Camp Nou stadium, where Barcelona can be crowned Spanish champions with a win over their archrivals. Vinicius Jr. will lead the forward line for Los Blancos, supported by Brahim Diaz and Gonzalo Torres.

articles.title: Saudi Aramco profits jump despite conflict in Middle East | Aramco | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Aramco, the state oil company of Saudi Arabia, reported a 26% increase in profits for its first quarter, reaching $33.6 billion. This surge was attributed to the successful operation of its east-west pipeline, which allowed the company to ship millions of barrels of oil despite disruptions caused by conflict in the Middle East, particularly the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Amin Nasser, president and chief executive of Saudi Aramco, stated that the pipeline's capacity was crucial for mitigating global energy shocks and easing shipping constraints. The company maintained its quarterly dividend at $21.9 billion, despite ongoing tensions in the region.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Aristotle: “Educating the mind without educating the heart is no education at all.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Aristotle's famous quote, "Educating the mind without educating the heart is no education at all," highlights the importance of emotional intelligence alongside academic achievement.  The quote emphasizes that true education should develop both intellectual and compassionate qualities for individuals to contribute positively to society.  Modern educators are increasingly recognizing the need to incorporate emotional learning into educational systems as students face increasing pressures to succeed academically while also grappling with mental health challenges like anxiety, burnout, and loneliness.  This shift in focus reflects a growing understanding that emotional intelligence is crucial for leadership, teamwork, communication, and overall well-being.

articles.title: Prime Minister Narendra Modi attacks Congress on ‘betrayal of allies’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticized the Congress party during a rally in Bengaluru, accusing them of betraying the DMK for power.  He stated that the Congress had a long-standing relationship with the DMK and that the DMK had consistently supported the Congress's political interests.

articles.title: South Korea welcomes rare baby bump as population shrinks - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Kim Su-jin and her husband defied societal pressures to have children in South Korea, a country grappling with a low birth rate. While the nation's fertility rate increased in 2023, experts debate whether government pro-natalist policies are solely responsible for this uptick or if it reflects broader social shifts among younger generations.  The increase in births, which reached nearly 23,000 in February, may be attributed to a combination of delayed marriages and births during the pandemic, as well as improved financial support from government programs. However, experts caution that sustained population growth is unlikely without continued policy interventions.

articles.title: Syria sees first government reshuffle since al-Assad’s ouster | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ahmed al-Sharaa, the interim president of Syria, announced a series of government changes including replacing his brother as head of the presidential office and appointing new cabinet ministers. The reshuffle comes about a year and a half into the five-year transitional period set in Syria’s constitutional declaration.  The appointments were met with criticism from some who accused al-Sharaa of nepotism, while others point to worsening economic conditions as a possible reason for the changes. Khaled Zaarour was appointed information minister, replacing Hamza Mustafa, who moved to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Bassel Sweidan took over as agriculture minister.

articles.title: Israel built, defended secret base in Iraq for war against Iran: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israel established a covert military base in the Iraqi desert to support its air operations against Iran, according to The Wall Street Journal.  The base, built before the conflict with Iran began and known to the United States, hosted Israeli special forces and served as a logistical hub for air strikes targeting Iran. Following a US F-15 fighter jet's downing near Iran, Israel offered assistance in recovery operations, prompting airstrikes by Israel to prevent Iraqi forces from reaching the base.  The incident led to Iraqi condemnation and a complaint filed with the UN.

articles.title: Great Nicobar project will destroy unique ecosystem; pause, revisit venture: Ramesh to Environment Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh wrote to Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on Sunday, urging him to halt the Great Nicobar Island development project due to concerns about its impact on the unique ecosystem.  Ramesh argued that the environmental studies supporting the project's approval were inadequate and criticized the process as a mockery of the Environmental Impact Assessment.

articles.title: Aurat March restrictions - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh government's 28-point list of restrictions on the Aurat March Karachi has been criticized as a reflection of double standards, with the administration demanding women remain politically harmless while celebrating them in public. The organizers sought permission to march for women's rights, but received a document that restricts speech, clothing, and slogans, highlighting an insecurity about women exercising their rights.  This approach contradicts the need for secure governments to support peaceful assembly and address gender-based violence, which is prevalent in Pakistan.

articles.title: Phillipson: challenge to Starmer would be wrong despite election ‘kicking’ | Labour party leadership | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Bridget Phillipson, Labour's education secretary, stated that a leadership challenge against Keir Starmer would be inappropriate given the party's recent electoral losses.  She acknowledged the significant defeat but argued for unity and focus on delivering for voters, while others within the party, including Catherine West, are pushing for a leadership change. West, who is not considered a strong contender, has begun collecting signatures to trigger a contest.

articles.title: OKC Thunder bury LA Lakers to take 3-0 NBA Playoff series lead | Basketball | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Los Angeles Lakers 131-108 in Game 3 of their Western Conference playoff series, extending their lead to 3-0.  Ajay Mitchell led the Thunder with 24 points, while Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 23 points and nine assists. The Thunder dominated the second half, outscoring the Lakers 74-49. The Lakers, who are now 0-7 against Oklahoma City this season, were led by LeBron James' 19 points, eight assists, and six rebounds.  The series continues with Game 4 in Los Angeles on Monday.

articles.title: US government answers major question over ICE presence at 2026 FIFA World Cup stadiums after fan concerns | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has decided that US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents will not operate inside or around FIFA World Cup stadiums during the 2026 tournament.  This decision follows growing concerns earlier this year regarding controversial immigration enforcement at international matches. Secretary of State Marco Rubio assured Rodney Barreto, co-chair of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Miami Host Committee, that ICE will not be present at stadiums and federal support will be provided for efficient travel documentation processing.  Despite these reassurances, concerns remain regarding immigration-related complications surrounding the tournament, including travel bans on some nations and visa bond requirements for supporters.

articles.title: Inauguration of Dhyan Mandir at Art of Living: PM Modi stresses on mental wellbeing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the importance of mental well-being in an era of rapid technological change during the inauguration of Dhyan Mandir in Bengaluru. Modi stressed the need for "natural healing" of the Earth and sustainable agriculture ahead of the Monsoon season, highlighting the interconnectedness of ecology and economy. He praised the AOL founder, Sri Sri Ravishankar, for promoting spiritual consciousness and lauded the Swacch Bharath Abhiyan as a societal norm.

articles.title: This is the sentence that protects every abuser in Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A pervasive societal stigma, "Sharif aurat thaney nahi jaati," prevents women from seeking justice at police stations in Pakistan. This belief system, often fueled by family pressure and a fear of social repercussions, discourages women from reporting domestic violence, harassment, or other crimes. Despite the existence of legal frameworks like the Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act and provisions within the Pakistan Penal Code, many women choose to avoid seeking help at police stations due to this ingrained prejudice.  This societal barrier hinders the ability of law enforcement institutions to effectively address the widespread issue of violence against women.

articles.title: How could Labour remove Keir Starmer? Four possible routes | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer's leadership of Labour is facing increasing pressure, with some MPs calling for his resignation.  While the party rulebook makes it difficult to remove a leader, several potential avenues exist for ousting him. These include securing 81 parliamentary nominations for a leadership contest or relying on public pressure from ministers or regional leaders.  However, Starmer has vowed to fight any challenge and may choose to remain in office despite the growing calls for his departure.

articles.title: AFC Asian Cup 2027: Japan to face defending champions Qatar in tough draw | AFC Asian Cup | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Japan and Qatar, the defending champions, have been drawn together in Group F for the 2027 AFC Asian Cup. The tournament will be hosted by Saudi Arabia from January 7 to February 5.  The draw was delayed due to the US-Israel war on Iran but is now set to proceed.  Giorgios Donis, appointed as Saudi Arabia's coach, expressed confidence in his team's ability to win the title for the first time since 1996. The tournament will feature 24 teams competing across six groups.

articles.title: North Korea activates nuclear dead man's switch - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea revised its constitution to mandate a nuclear strike if Kim Jong-un, the country's leader, is killed or incapacitated by foreign forces. The change was revealed during a briefing by the South Korean National Intelligence Service.  Experts believe this move stems from concerns following recent US-Israeli attacks on Iran, which successfully eliminated key Iranian leadership. However, carrying out such an operation in North Korea would be more challenging due to its isolation and security measures. Despite these challenges, Kim Jong-un's military remains loyal to him.

articles.title: Vijay resigns from Tiruchi East Assembly seat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, resigned as a member of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly from both Perambur and Tiruchi East constituencies on Sunday (May 10, 2026). He submitted his resignation to Principal Secretary of the Legislative Assembly K. Srinivasan. The move will trigger a by-election for the Tiruchi East constituency.

articles.title: PTCL users may face internet disruption during evening hours from May 11-18 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) announced planned maintenance work on a submarine cable between May 11 and 18, potentially causing internet service degradation during evening hours. The International Cable Consortium will be responsible for the repairs, which are expected to impact customers' connectivity.  This maintenance coincides with ongoing challenges in Pakistan's internet infrastructure, leading to frequent disruptions.

articles.title: Nobel laureate’s smuggled memoir details beatings and neglect in Iranian prisons | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Narges Mohammadi, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and prominent Iranian activist, has described the "torture" of solitary confinement and medical neglect she endured during her numerous imprisonments in Iran.  The Mohammadi's writings smuggled from prison detail beatings, interrogations, deprivation of medical care, and long stretches in solitary confinement, which have significantly damaged her health. Her family claims that her ongoing detention and denial of proper medical treatment constitute a "slow execution." The memoir, "A Woman Never Stops Fighting," will be published in September and details Mohammadi's activism for women's rights and prison reform.

articles.title: Libya’s Zawiya refinery resumes full operations | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Libya’s Zawiya Oil Refining Company resumed full operations at its refinery after a two-day shutdown due to fighting near the facility. The company stated that it was forced to shut down and evacuate tankers following heavy shelling on Friday, which escalated into clashes in the surrounding residential area.  The National Oil Corporation (NOC) reported no significant damage but confirmed several high-calibre projectiles had landed within the complex.

articles.title: Hantavirus outbreak: Cruise ship passengers start disembarking in Spain, all to be checked for symptoms - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Passengers on the quarantined MV Hondius cruise ship began disembarking in Tenerife, Spain after an outbreak of hantavirus.  The World Health Organization (WHO) and Spanish authorities are overseeing the evacuation process, with more than 20 nationalities represented among the passengers and crew. Oceanwide Expeditions, the cruise operator, is working to disinfect the vessel before it sails to Rotterdam in the Netherlands for further procedures. The outbreak has resulted in three deaths and five confirmed cases of hantavirus infection, while authorities are investigating the source of the virus and its transmission on board.

articles.title: CITU calls South Coast Railway zone a “betrayal” of Andhra Pradesh, flags revenue loss - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre’s notification operationalising the South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone from June 1, 2026, has drawn criticism from the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU).  CITU leaders argue that the new zone weakens Andhra Pradesh's interests by retaining key revenue-generating railway sections under the East Coast Railway (ECoR), and accuses the Union government of diverting railway revenue to Odisha. They also raised concerns over territorial jurisdiction, recruitment freezes, and privatization efforts, calling for a zone that serves the economic interests of Andhra Pradesh.

articles.title: Pakistan, Qatar reaffirm shared commitment to support 'constructive dialogue across region' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, the Emir of Qatar, held a phone call on Sunday to reaffirm their commitment to supporting peace efforts in the Middle East. The two leaders discussed ongoing peace initiatives and emphasized the importance of constructive engagement from all parties involved.  The PMO stated that both sides agreed that Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani’s visit to Pakistan would further strengthen the enduring partnership between the two countries.  Sheikh Mohammed also affirmed Qatar's support for Pakistani mediation efforts aimed at ending the crisis through peaceful means, while Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, discussed US support for Qatar's defense during his meeting with Sheikh Mohammed.

articles.title: Argentina in spotlight over hantavirus as authorities retrace footsteps of ship’s passengers | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A hantavirus outbreak on a Dutch cruise ship, the MV Hondius, has sparked renewed global scrutiny of the virus in Argentina. The World Health Organization (WHO) has ruled out an epidemic but is investigating how passengers were infected, with Argentinian scientists noting that while there has been a recent increase in cases, it's not significantly different from previous decades. The outbreak follows two previous outbreaks in Patagonia, which provided evidence of person-to-person transmission.  The Argentine government plans to capture rodents along the ship’s route for analysis and is urging caution as the virus remains relatively rare in the country.

articles.title: NDA leaders stake claim to form Assam government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma, leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), was unanimously elected as the leader of the Assam Legislature Party.  Following this, the NDA staked a claim to form the government in Assam with the support of 102 MLAs. The swearing-in ceremony for the new council of ministers is scheduled for May 12th. J.P. Nadda, Union Minister and central observer for the BJP Legislature Party meeting, announced that eight BJP legislators proposed Sarma's name as their leader.  The newly elected members of the BJP and its regional allies — Asom Gana Parishad (AGP) and Bodoland People’s Front (BPF) — chose their leaders in the morning.

articles.title: Petroleum dealers, lawyers slam fuel hike - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) and the Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) criticized the government's recent fuel price increases, citing high petroleum levies as a major contributor to public hardship.  The PPDA Vice Chairman, Raja Waseem Shehzad, called for reduced levies and duties on petroleum products to alleviate financial burdens on consumers and fuel retailers. The SCBA President, Haroonur Rashid, along with other members, urged the government to roll back the price increase and provide additional relief measures such as lower electricity tariffs and essential commodity prices.

articles.title: Prohibitory orders clamped in Kadapa after clashes over Almaspet junction naming - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prohibitory orders were imposed in Kadapa following clashes at Almaspet junction over the renaming of a center. The dispute stemmed from differing demands to name the junction after Tipu Sultan or Lord Hanuman, leading to stone-pelting and protests on Saturday (May 9, 2026).  The Kadapa District Collector and Superintendent of Police condemned the violence, emphasizing the need for communal harmony and cautioning against misinformation. The district administration is taking steps to restore peace and prevent future incidents.

articles.title: Nuclear disaster can unfold any moment, experts fear - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Nehal Hashmi of Sindh, Pakistan, spoke at a conference organized by the Pakistan Institute of International Affairs (PIIA) on global crises. He expressed concern over international efforts and their effectiveness in preventing conflicts like those in Gaza and Ukraine.  Dr. Masuma Hasan, Honorary Chairperson of PIIA, highlighted the escalating violence and displacement caused by wars globally, emphasizing the brutality inflicted upon Palestinians by Israel. Ambassador Zamir Akram, Adviser to the Strategic Plans Division, Government of Pakistan, warned about the collapse of the international system and the looming threat of nuclear war. He cited the Doomsday Clock's recent advancement to 85 seconds to midnight as a stark reminder of humanity's precarious position. Dr. Wang Huiyao, Founder and President of the Centre for China and Globalisation, called for peaceful co-existence between major powers like the US and China.

articles.title: Two wins, two losses: What India, Pakistan have learned a year after war | India-Pakistan Tensions News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: India and Pakistan claim victory in their recent conflict, highlighting vulnerabilities exposed during the four-day war.  Both nations have publicly celebrated their military successes while acknowledging weaknesses. India's BrahMos missile strike on Pakistani airbases has been cited as a major turning point for both sides. Pakistan's new rocket force and increased defense spending are intended to bolster its capabilities against India, but analysts warn that these measures may not be sufficient to counter the threat posed by India's advanced military technology. The Indus Waters Treaty remains suspended, raising concerns about water security in the region. Despite acknowledging their vulnerabilities, both countries remain committed to maintaining a strategic posture and have engaged in diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions.

articles.title: Stalin reacts to Tamil Nadu CM Vijay speech: ‘Money is there; what is required is efficient administration’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and DMK president, criticized C. Joseph Vijay's statement that the previous government left the state treasury empty with a debt burden of ₹10 lakh crore.  Stalin asserted that the government should not claim there was "no money" at the beginning of its tenure, suggesting instead that an efficient administration is needed to distribute existing resources.

articles.title: Electric bike demand surges amid costly oil - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Millat Tractors Ltd (MTL) is exploring the feasibility of electric bike production in Pakistan, while Chery Master Pakistan and Pak Suzuki Motor Company Ltd are planning to launch new hybrid and electric vehicle models.  The surge in petrol prices has fueled demand for electric scooters and bikes, leading to shortages and price hikes. Mr. Samir Malik, CEO of Chery Master Pakistan, believes Pakistan is a key market for Chery's advanced mobility technologies.

articles.title: Macron tours East Africa amid push to redefine France’s role in Africa | Emmanuel Macron News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron, the French President, embarked on a three-country tour of East Africa to rebuild France's influence in the region. The "Africa Forward" summit in Kenya will bring together African leaders and business executives, with agreements between French and Kenyan companies expected to be signed.  Macron's tour also includes meetings with Ethiopian officials and participation in talks at the African Union headquarters on peace and security. This visit is seen as a bid by Paris to repair economic and security ties and counter rising anti-French sentiment across Africa.

articles.title: Pension scams: Britons warned over criminals offering inheritance tax loopholes | Scams | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Standard Life and The Pensions Regulator warn that scammers are exploiting people's concerns about upcoming inheritance tax changes to pensions. The scams often involve unsolicited calls or emails offering "pension liberation" schemes with high returns, but these promises are false.  Scammers pressure individuals into transferring their funds without proper financial advice, leading to potential losses. To avoid falling victim, it is crucial to be cautious of unsolicited offers and seek independent financial advice before making any decisions about your pension.

articles.title: BJP won’t support any coalition formation in Tamil Nadu: Nainar Nagenthran - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nainar Nagenthran, BJP state president, announced the party will not support any government formation following the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election. The BJP contested 33 seats as part of the AIADMK-led National Democratic Alliance, winning only one seat in Udhagamandalam.  The party's performance fell short of securing a simple majority despite contesting on multiple alliances.

articles.title: Rain to hit upper Pakistan after intense heat - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

articles.title: Nationals MP Colin Boyce says he’s considering move to One Nation after ‘wake-up call’ in Farrer byelection | Farrer byelection 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Colin Boyce, MP for the central Queensland seat of Flynn, is considering shifting to One Nation after the party's historic victory in the Farrer byelection.  Boyce acknowledged the significant vote share for One Nation and believes it signals a shift in sentiment within conservative politics. He stated that he would "consider a lot of things" regarding his political future, including his membership in the National party. Former Nationals leader Barnaby Joyce expressed support for Boyce remaining within the National party, suggesting that voters are drawn to diverse political views.

articles.title: Pallegama Hemarathana Thero: Buddhist monk arrested for alleged rape of teen in Sri Lanka
articles.rephrased_article: Venerable Pallegama Hemarathana Thero, a high-ranking Buddhist monk and chief prelate of eight sacred sites in Sri Lanka, has been arrested for the alleged rape and sexual assault of a 15-year-old girl. The arrest followed criticism from the country's child protection authority regarding police inaction against him.  The monk is currently awaiting trial on May 12th. His mother was also arrested and remanded to custody for aiding and abetting the abuse.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu swearing-in ceremony LIVE: TVK president C. Joseph Vijay arrives at venue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), will be sworn in as the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on Sunday, May 10, 2026.  He secured the support of 120 MLAs-elect after a nail-biting political uncertainty that ended with the VCK and the IUML extending their support to the TVK coalition government. The swearing-in ceremony will take place at Nehru Stadium in Chennai at 10 a.m.

articles.title: Iran war live: IRGC warns US against attacks on ships; Israel bombs Lebanon | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel killed at least 24 people in Lebanon during ongoing attacks, while the US-Iran ceasefire remains intact despite skirmishes in the Strait of Hormuz.  The IRGC warned Washington against attacks on tankers, as tensions remain high between the two countries.

articles.title: Pakistani national among 3 arrested in US for attempting to smuggle 89 firearms into Canada - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Three men, including a Pakistani national, were arrested in New York after authorities discovered 89 firearms, including at least 17 reported stolen, hidden in their vehicle. The United States Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York, along with the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, conducted the investigation.  The men were identified as Malik Bromfield, Faizan Ali, and Kamal Salman, and face multiple charges including smuggling from the United States, unlicensed dealing in firearms, transporting stolen firearms in interstate commerce, and unlawful possession of firearms.

articles.title: Iran keeps US waiting for a response - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran questioned the seriousness of American diplomacy after renewed naval clashes in the Gulf, while Bahrain arrested over 40 individuals suspected of links to the IRGC. The CIA reported that Iran could withstand a US blockade for months.  The UK deployed its warship HMS Dragon to the Middle East as part of preparations for potential multinational efforts to secure shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Israel continued strikes in Lebanon, targeting infrastructure and troops, despite a ceasefire.

articles.title: Pressure mounts on Angus Taylor as Pauline Hanson declares One Nation ‘here for the long haul’ | Farrer byelection 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pauline Hanson and One Nation won their first federal lower house seat in the Farrer byelection, defeating the incumbent Liberal Party candidate. The result has sparked internal rumblings about Angus Taylor's leadership within the Coalition, with some MPs questioning his direction.  The Liberals suffered a significant swing in primary vote share, dropping below 13%, and are facing growing concerns over their future prospects.  Several prominent figures, including former Liberal Senator Hollie Hughes, have publicly criticized the party's handling of the byelection. The defeat has raised questions about the future of the Coalition and its ability to regain power in the next election.

articles.title: Putin says he thinks Ukraine conflict 'coming to an end'
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin stated that he believes the conflict in Ukraine is coming to an end, while condemning Western support for Ukraine.  He made these comments after a scaled-back military parade in Moscow marking the Soviet victory in World War Two.  Putin also expressed his willingness to negotiate new security arrangements for Europe with former Chancellor Gerhard Schröder, and said he would only meet Zelensky once a lasting peace deal is agreed upon.

articles.title: Could hantavirus be the new emerging pathogen in Kerala? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's health department is investigating the possibility of hantavirus infection contributing to a significant number of acute febrile illnesses with renal syndrome and thrombocytopenia, which are currently attributed to leptospirosis.  The state has previously documented hantavirus seroprevalence in research studies dating back to 1999.  Kerala's clinicians are aware that the two diseases share similar symptoms, making timely diagnosis challenging. The Institute of Advanced Virology (IAV) now provides PCR testing for hantavirus confirmation. While there has been no confirmed human-to-human transmission, the IAV is conducting basic biological studies on the virus and routine PCR testing to identify potential cases.

articles.title: Putin suggests Russia’s war on Ukraine ‘coming to an end’ | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin suggested that the war in Ukraine may be coming to an end, and expressed a willingness to meet Volodymyr Zelenskyy in a third country if a peace deal is finalized.  This comes after Russia and Ukraine agreed to a three-day ceasefire and exchanged 1,000 prisoners. Donald Trump, US President, facilitated the ceasefire agreement.  Putin also suggested that talks with European leaders could be beneficial, specifically mentioning former German Chancellor Gerhard Schroder. The war in Ukraine has been ongoing for over four years.

articles.title: ‘Missiles, drones locked on US targets’: Iran warns of ‘heavy assault’ after tanker strikes in Gulf of Oman - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) issued a warning to the United States, stating that any further attacks on Iranian oil tankers or commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz would trigger a "heavy assault" on American military assets and ships. The IRGC Aerospace Force claimed their missiles and drones were already targeting US military assets and naval vessels in the region. The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) has disabled four Iranian vessels since April 13 as part of ongoing blockade operations against Iran, while US President Donald Trump confirmed that three US Navy destroyers came under attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Ceremony marking one year since Marka-i-Haq victory underway at GHQ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Staff and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, along with Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal (ACM) Zaheer Ahmed Babar Sidhu and Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, attended a ceremony marking one year since Pakistan's victory in the conflict with India.  Field Marshal Munir emphasized that the conflict was a "battle between two ideologies," noting that truth prevailed over falsehood. The event included floral wreaths laid at the Yadgar-i-Shuhada (Martyrs’ Monument) and a salute by armed forces contingents. ISPR issued statements praising the nation's unity, military excellence, and strategic maturity in response to the conflict. They also highlighted Pakistan's resilience against hybrid challenges and enhanced defensive capabilities.

articles.title: Tehran, Taiwan, trade … what are the hazards facing Trump on Xi summit tightrope? | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China for a summit with Xi Jinping. The trip, originally planned for three days, has been shortened to two due to the recent Iran conflict. The meeting will focus on trade, Tehran, and Taiwan.  Trump, known for his personal relationship with Xi, aims to secure tangible "wins" before the November midterm elections. While both sides have agreed to a temporary truce in the trade war, tensions remain high over rare earth minerals, military-to-military relations, and Taiwan. The summit will be closely watched for any concessions made by Trump regarding these issues.  The meeting's outcome could significantly impact US-China relations and global stability.

articles.title: Tenerife medics poised for arrival of virus-hit cruise ship
articles.rephrased_article: The Hondius, a cruise ship carrying passengers and crew infected with the hantavirus, is expected to arrive in Tenerife's Granadilla port on Sunday.  A security perimeter will be enforced around the ship as it approaches, and medical teams will board to check for symptoms. The Spanish government has prepared an extensive plan to repatriate over 100 passengers and crew members to their home countries.  The WHO has praised the Spanish authorities' response, while some locals have expressed concerns about safety measures.

articles.title: Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam: a new political dawn in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A senior civil servant in New Delhi was surprised to hear strong support for C. Joseph Vijay, founder of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), at a wedding in Chennai on polling day.  Similarly, a Madurai-based activist observed widespread support for Vijay among young people in his native village near Rajapalayam.

articles.title: Around 1,10,787 candidates attended COMED-K UGET - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 110,787 candidates took the COMED-K UGET entrance exam across India, with approximately 35,678 in Karnataka. The exam, a gateway to admissions into 20,000 seats at engineering colleges in the state, was held in two sessions on Saturday.  The provisional answer keys will be released on May 13th and the final key on May 20th. Students can access their rank cards on May 26th.

articles.title: Punjab Congress to release ‘chargesheet’ against AAP government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bhupesh Baghel, former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister and Congress General Secretary in charge of Punjab, presided over a meeting of the state party unit to discuss the "grim state of affairs" under the ruling AAP government. The meeting focused on allegations of rampant corruption and deteriorating law and order, leading to feelings of insecurity among residents.  The Congress plans to hold "yatras" across all 117 Assembly segments in the coming days to engage with voters and address their concerns.

articles.title: At least 11 people sent to hospital after suspected boat explosion in Miami | Miami | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A suspected boat explosion at the Haulover Sandbar in Miami sent at least 11 people to the hospital with burns and traumatic injuries on Saturday. Juan Arias, a Miami Dade fire rescue battalion chief, reported the incident occurred around 12:45 pm on a charter boat carrying about 14 people. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is investigating the cause of the explosion.  Local businessman Patrick Lee witnessed the blast and described seeing three people ejected from the boat in smoke.

articles.title: Teacher dies of heart attack while giving lecture-cum-demonstration at training session in Khammam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Jayaraj, an English teacher at a private school in Khammam, died of a heart attack during a training workshop on Saturday. The incident occurred while he was conducting the workshop for teachers in Khammam district.  He was declared brought dead at a local hospital after being rushed there. Jayaraj was considered an expert in teachers' training and his colleagues are mourning his sudden passing.

articles.title: Man arrested on charge of assaulting minor on train - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Punalur police arrested a 40-year-old man, Sanish, for allegedly sexually assaulting a six-year-old girl on the Palaruvi Express. The incident occurred in early morning hours while the victim and her family were traveling from Tamil Nadu. A vigilant passenger recorded video evidence of the crime, which was shared with authorities leading to the suspect's arrest.

articles.title: Kejriwal slams PM Modi over ED raids in Punjab - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal accused the ED of being a tool for political intimidation, targeting Punjab Minister Sanjeev Arora in raids.  Kejriwal claimed that the BJP is trying to break AAP leaders and force them into joining their party, comparing PM Modi's actions to Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb's atrocities. He asserted that the people of Punjab will resist these attacks and teach the BJP a lesson in the 2027 Assembly elections.

articles.title: Betty Broderick, convicted in 1989 killings of ex-husband and his new wife, dies aged 78 | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Betty Broderick, who was convicted of the 1989 murders of her former husband and his new wife, has died at age 78 while serving a life sentence.  The California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation confirmed her death on April 26th after she was transferred to a medical center from a prison where she had been incarcerated since 1992. The San Bernardino County coroner will conduct a formal investigation into the cause of death, initially determined as natural causes by the medical examiner's office.

articles.title: Muslim population in India may match that of Indonesia after Census: Kiren Rijiju - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister for Minority Affairs, stated that the Muslim population in India is projected to be nearly equal to Indonesia's population after the upcoming Census. He also expressed concerns over the declining Parsi community and dismissed claims of minority threats, emphasizing equality under the Indian Constitution. Rijiju highlighted the BJP's victory in West Bengal as a positive development for national security, citing its border proximity to Bangladesh and concerns about illegal migration.

articles.title: Australia news live: Ley urges Liberals to accept Farrer loss to One Nation with ‘humility’, saying ‘voters never get it wrong’ | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Liberal Party suffered a significant defeat in the Farrer byelection, with David Farley winning against an independent candidate. The result is seen as a sign of voter dissatisfaction with the Coalition's leadership and policies, particularly regarding housing affordability. Treasurer Jim Chalmers stated that the budget will include $2 billion for infrastructure to address housing supply issues, while Pauline Hanson of One Nation declared victory and vowed to target other seats in the future.  The byelection results are expected to have a significant impact on Australian politics and may lead to further shifts in power dynamics.

articles.title: Alleged forgery for organ donation: one more arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kunnathunadu police have arrested Rashida, 37, wife of Najeeb, in connection with an alleged illegal organ donation scheme using forged documents.  The case follows the arrest of Sunny Varghese, 56, and his wife Sini Varghese, 50, as well as Sanoj, 32, by Ernakulam Rural police. Three individuals were also arrested in Kollam district by Kilikollur police.  The accused allegedly forged documents including letterheads of two major hospitals and blank letterheads in the name of an MLA and MP.

articles.title: A young IAS officer’s reform wish list for new government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dilip K. Kainikkara, a young IAS officer and Tirur Sub Collector, has presented a reform wish list to the newly elected United Democratic Front (UDF) government in Kerala.  He recommends the bifurcation of Malappuram district and an increase in the pension age to 58. He argues that dividing large districts improves administrative efficiency and public access to services.

articles.title: Grant EL to teachers handling SSC remedial classes: FAPTO - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: FAPTO members have requested the School Education Department to grant Earned Leave (EL) to teachers conducting special and remedial classes for SSC failed students during the summer vacation. The request was made in a representation submitted to Director of School Education Thameem Ansariya, who issued orders for these classes following the 2026 SSC exams.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu heading for a coalition government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu is poised to form its first coalition government in decades, with the Congress party joining forces with Tamilaga Vetri Kazhagam. The alliance will be led by C. Joseph Vijay, who is expected to assume the role of Chief Minister.  The decision was reached after a proposal from the Congress was accepted by TVK leadership.

articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari | The Bengal pivot - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, a prominent Trinamool Congress leader, defected to the BJP in December 2020 after several senior party members attempted to persuade him to stay.  Adhikari's decision was driven by his ambition to become West Bengal's Chief Minister, an aspiration he felt unattainable within the Trinamool Congress. His departure came as a significant blow to the party, especially with the emergence of Abhishek Banerjee, Mamata Banerjee's nephew, who had gained prominence in the political landscape.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina, Awami League congratulate Suvendu Adhikari - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sheikh Hasina, former Prime Minister of Bangladesh, congratulated Suvendu Adhikari, the new Chief Minister of West Bengal.  The Bangladesh Awami League, banned in Bangladesh, expressed support for Mr. Adhikari and stated that they believe this new chapter will elevate relations between Bangladesh and India. The Awami League was banned following a crackdown on civilians in 2024.

articles.title: HYDRAA rescues woman trapped overnight in Hussainsagar drain - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indira, a resident of Bhagyanagar Colony, was rescued from the Hussainsagar surplus drain after spending the night in the murky water. HYDRAA personnel responded to calls from passersby who heard her cries for help and used a ladder to rescue her.  The operation involved five members of the Disaster Response Force and three firefighters.

articles.title: CPCL unit achieves highest ever crude throughput in FY ’26 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd. (CPCL) achieved its highest-ever crude throughput of 11.71 million tonnes, reaching a capacity utilization of 112% for the year ending March 31, 2026. The company attributed this success to sustained operational excellence and controlled pressure and temperature parameters, particularly in the hydrocracker and FCC units. CPCL also maintained its best-ever distillate yield and achieved high product yields of petrol, diesel, kerosene, and ATF.

articles.title: SPCSS-TN calls Centre’s higher education bill unconstitutional, demands its withdrawal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State Platform for Common School System – Tamil Nadu (SPCSS-TN) has written to the Joint Parliamentary Committee examining the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan (VBSA) Bill 2025, arguing it is unconstitutional and should be withdrawn. The letter claims the bill grants excessive power to the Union government, potentially leading to the privatization of education and undermining state universities' role in social justice.  The SPCSS-TN also criticizes the bill for failing to recognize the importance of state universities in India's development and for its potential to create a subservient educational system.

articles.title: One killed in Gaza as Turkish FM talks peace efforts with Hamas official | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: An Israeli drone strike in Gaza killed one Palestinian man and injured several others, while Israel continued to violate a ceasefire agreement with hundreds of casualties reported across the Strip.  The Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met with Hamas's head of the Shura Council Muhammad Darwish in Ankara to discuss efforts to secure peace in Gaza and deliver humanitarian aid.  The meeting came amidst ongoing violence between Israel and Palestinian groups, with at least four fatalities confirmed in Gaza over the past 48 hours.  Efforts to reach a lasting peace have stalled due to disagreements between Israel and Hamas.

articles.title: Ministers, ambassadors, artists to join The Hindu’s Huddle in June - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu Group is hosting its annual The Hindu Huddle, a conference focused on global issues, in Bengaluru from June 5th to 6th. This year's theme, "A World in Transition," will feature discussions on topics such as regional parties in Indian democracy, diplomacy and conflict resolution, women's representation in Parliament, the role of AI, mental health, and the future of work.  The event will include prominent speakers from India and around the world, including Union Ministers Hardeep Puri and Nitin Gadkari, former President Mohamed Nasheed, and Chinese Ambassador Xu Feihong.

articles.title: Brazil judge bars law that could reduce Bolsonaro’s 27-year prison sentence | Jair Bolsonaro News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has suspended the implementation of a law that could reduce former President Jair Bolsonaro's 27-year prison sentence for his alleged involvement in a coup plot. The suspension, pending further review by the court, follows appeals challenging the law's constitutionality and requests from those convicted to overturn it.  The ruling effectively halts individual requests for sentence reductions until the Supreme Court can decide on the law's legality.

articles.title: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam | The star who stormed into politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, the founder of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), has achieved significant political success in Tamil Nadu with his party securing 108 seats in the state assembly during its first election. The TVK, formed in February 2024, leverages a strong fan base and presents itself as a secular organization focused on social justice and equality.

articles.title: DMK’s Periyakaruppan moves Madras HC to prevent TVK MLA from participating in vote of confidence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K.R. Periyakaruppan, leader of the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), filed a writ petition in the Madras High Court seeking to prevent Seenivasa Sethupathy of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) from participating in the trust vote for the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly. The petition argues that votes cast in Periyakaruppan's Tirupattur constituency were not recounted properly, and therefore the elected candidate should be disqualified.  The case will be heard by a summer vacation Bench of Justices L. Victoria Gowri and N. Senthilkumar on May 10, 2026.

articles.title: US, Iran talks likely next week - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran are reportedly preparing to resume negotiations in Islamabad as early as next week, aiming to establish a framework for a month-long negotiating process. The one-page memorandum of understanding outlines 14 points, with sanctions relief for Tehran being a key sticking point. Tensions remain high, with the US striking two Iranian oil tankers and Bahrain arresting individuals suspected of ties to the Iranian Revolutionary Guard.

articles.title: Mythos | Double-edged sword - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised concerns that while artificial intelligence can enhance cybersecurity, it could also make cyberattacks more efficient and accessible to non-experts. The IMF warns that this increased risk is particularly concerning for the financial sector, which relies on shared digital infrastructure.

articles.title: Venezuela’s Delcy Rodriguez heads to The Hague for land dispute case | US-Venezuela Tensions News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Delcy Rodriguez, acting president of Venezuela, is traveling to The Hague for the first time since President Maduro's abduction in January.  She will attend the International Court of Justice (ICJ) case regarding a centuries-old land dispute with Guyana over the Essequibo region. The ICJ has already been hearing arguments in the case, which centers on whether the current border established in 1899 should remain valid or be redrawn according to a later document from 1966.

articles.title: Israel widens Gaza control, plans more ops - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has expanded its control of Gaza, now controlling 60% of the territory, according to officials.  Finance minister Bezalel Smotrich stated that this expansion is part of a strategy to deepen destruction of infrastructure and limit Hamas's ability to re-arm. The move comes despite a ceasefire agreement seven months ago aimed at rehabilitating the war-torn enclave, which has seen increased violence with continued Israeli airstrikes and Hamas resisting disarmament efforts.

articles.title: New India Assurance Co Ltd. opens modern office in Vellore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: New India Assurance Co Ltd. opened a new business office near the Vellore Municipal Corporation building.  Deputy General Manager M.V. Chandrasekhar inaugurated the office, emphasizing the company's strong market presence and commitment to prompt customer service. Regional managers K. Kasthuri and V. Gayathri, along with Chief Business Manager Parimala Devi, were also present at the event.

articles.title: Should we be worried about the hantavirus outbreak? | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has stated that the hantavirus outbreak poses a low risk to public health.  Dr Mukesh Kapila, Professor Emeritus of Global Health and Humanitarian Affairs at the University of Manchester, and Dr Margaret Harris, Lecturer at the United Nations Institute for Training and Research, former W.H.O. spokeswoman, discussed how lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic are being applied to respond to the hantavirus outbreak.  Nicholas Locker, Professor of Virology at the Pirbright Institute, near Guildford, UK, also contributed to the discussion.

articles.title: Hantavirus may've spread to remote island - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: WHO director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, along with Spain health minister Monica Garcia and interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska, are coordinating the disembarkation of the Dutch-flagged cruise ship MV Hondius after two suspected hantavirus cases emerged thousands of miles apart. The first case involved a man who fell ill after leaving the ship, while another occurred on a plane where a woman became sick near an infected passenger.  WHO officials are working to reassure residents that the risk remains low and passengers will be screened before disembarking.

articles.title: Mortality of neem trees goes up in A.P.; scientists blame fungus, insect attack - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Y.S.R. Horticulture University (Dr.YSRHU) scientists in Andhra Pradesh are investigating reports of increased neem tree mortality across the state.  The research team found that the trees are dying due to a fungus called Phomopsis Azadirachtae and the Tea Mosquito Bug, which causes damage to leaves, twigs, inflorescence, and fruits. Dr. YSRHU Vice-Chancellor K. Dhanumjaya Rao advised pruning affected branches and applying fungicide and insecticide to control the infection.  He also urged residents to report any neem tree issues to local horticulture colleges and research stations.

articles.title: Sean Duffy faces backlash for new family reality show: ‘unfocused and out of touch’ | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, and his family embarked on a seven-month road trip across America for a reality TV program.  The trip drew criticism from critics who pointed to ongoing crises in the transportation sector, including TSA agent shortages, airport delays, and the recent collapse of low-budget carrier Spirit Airlines. Duffy defended the trip as an opportunity to "love America" and suggested it as an alternative to social media for children. Chasten Buttigieg, husband of Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, criticized the trip's timing and cost, while Rachel Campos-Duffy, Duffy's wife, argued that production costs were covered by a non-profit.

articles.title: Three police officers killed in car bomb attack in northwest Pakistan | Armed Groups News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A car bomb attack near a police post in Bannu, Pakistan, killed at least three officers and injured two civilians. The attack involved a suicide bomber and several fighters who detonated an explosives-laden vehicle, causing the collapse of the security post and nearby civilian areas.  Pakistan's Dawn reported that drones were also used during the attack. Police officials from both Reuters and The Associated Press confirmed the incident and ongoing fighting in the area.

articles.title: Silicon Valley $162K, Dallas $113K: What's Trump's new plan to raise salary of H-1B workers - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Donald Trump administration is proposing to raise the base salary for foreign workers on H-1B visas, aiming to make it more difficult for companies to hire them instead of Americans. The proposed increase would vary by location, with entry-level software engineers in Silicon Valley needing a minimum salary of $162,000 per year.  Experts are cautious about the impact of this change, as it could lead to higher hiring costs and potentially discourage employers from sponsoring foreign workers. This proposal awaits final approval from the Labor Department.

articles.title: Amid Sultan Palace row, tourism minister says such heritage structures will be beautified - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kedar Prasad Gupta, the new Tourism Minister of Bihar, stated that heritage buildings will be beautified in the state.  Following reports suggesting the Sultan Palace might be demolished for a five-star hotel, Mr. Gupta assured citizens that the palace would be preserved and made part of the heritage hotel project. The project was initially approved in 2024 but faced controversy after a report claimed the palace was not listed as a heritage building.  Citizens have demanded the composition of a panel investigating the palace's conservation status be made public, while some suggest listing the palace is crucial for its preservation.

articles.title: Man arrested after five people were hit by car in Nottinghamshire town | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nottinghamshire police have arrested a 40-year-old man on suspicion of attempted murder after five people were struck by a car in Arnold town centre. One man suffered life-threatening injuries and remains critically ill, while four others sustained less serious injuries. The driver fled the scene on foot and counter-terrorism officers were not involved.  Police are urging anyone with information to contact them or Crimestoppers.

articles.title: Karnataka Police to prioritise housing for SC/ST personnel facing caste bias in finding rented accommodation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: ADGP Devajyoti Ray, head of the grievance cell in the Karnataka Police, issued a circular directing authorities to prioritize police quarters for personnel facing caste discrimination in securing rental housing. The circular, issued on behalf of the DGP & IGP, reverses the current system of allocating housing based on seniority and addresses concerns raised during a Government Assurance Committee meeting regarding caste-based discrimination in rental housing.

articles.title: Vatican softens towards LGBTQ+ Catholics - The Times of India
