articles.title: Cambodians struggle with displaced lives amid tense ceasefire with Thailand | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cambodian families displaced by the recent border war with Thailand struggle to rebuild their lives amidst a tense ceasefire.  The conflict has disrupted education for thousands of children, forcing many to attend school in temporary locations while others are unable to return home due to military presence and restrictions. The long-standing dispute between the two countries continues to impact families' ability to access basic necessities like food and shelter, as well as their children's mental health.  Cambodian officials express concern about rising dropout rates and psychological trauma among displaced children while Thai forces continue to occupy areas bordering Cambodia.

articles.title: Federal Constitutional Court staff pay, perks surpass Supreme Court's amid supremacy row - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) has implemented unprecedented compensation packages for its staff and officers, raising concerns about the financial disparity between FCC employees and those of the Supreme Court. The FCC's recent judgments asserting exclusive constitutional adjudication authority have led to a significant pay gap, with some FCC employees receiving up to Rs300,000 more per month than their counterparts at the SC.  The FCC has also created new positions and implemented financial incentives, including special judicial allowances and transport monetization packages, further fueling the debate over the constitutional supremacy of the FCC.

articles.title: David Pocock applauds $387m in extra funding for CSIRO after tens of thousands sign petition | Australian budget 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Albanese government announced an additional $387.4 million in funding for CSIRO, over four years, to support facilities and technology upgrades and research. This funding is on top of the agency's existing annual budget of $1 billion and aims to provide stability while addressing long-term costs.  The announcement comes after months of advocacy by scientists and staff following job cuts and cost-cutting measures. Senator David Pocock welcomed the increased funding, stating it reflects "huge and effective advocacy" from scientists and the community, but emphasized that more investment is needed in research and development.

articles.title: Hantavirus ship approaches Tenerife as residents express anger and resignation
articles.rephrased_article: The Spanish government has agreed with the World Health Organization (WHO) that passengers of the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship, MV Hondius, should disembark in Tenerife this weekend.  While some local dock workers are protesting and demanding safety measures, the authorities have assured residents that the ship will anchor out at sea, be ferried to Granadilla port, and its passengers will be repatriated or quarantined. The Socialist-led central government has provided details of the arrival process and emphasized protection for locals.  Despite some concerns, many islanders are accepting the situation, hoping that authorities will ensure safety measures are in place.

articles.title: TCS case: Nida Khan sent to police custody till May 11; AIMIM corporator booked for harbouring her - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nida Khan, who was arrested for alleged sexual exploitation and forcible conversion at a Tata Consultancy Services office in Nashik, was remanded to police custody until May 11 by a Nashik court.  The arrest followed a joint operation with the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Police. An AIMIM corporator from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has also been booked for allegedly harboring Khan while she evaded authorities.

articles.title: Bengaluru civic polls: Parties divided over timing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State Election Commission (SEC) announced that civic polls for the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) area will be held in June.  Former councillors, including Abdul Wajid, former councillor and petitioner in the Supreme Court case seeking the conduct of civic polls, stated that their respective parties are ready for the elections with preliminary groundwork completed. However, there is division among them regarding the SEC's decision, with some calling it "hurried."

articles.title: Bengaluru civic polls: Parties divided over timing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State Election Commission (SEC) announced that civic polls for the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) area will be held in June.  Former councillors from various parties, including Abdul Wajid, a former councillor and petitioner in the Supreme Court case seeking the conduct of civic polls, stated their respective parties are prepared for the elections with preliminary groundwork completed. However, there is disagreement over the SEC's decision, with some calling it "hurried."

articles.title: Bangladesh failed to give ‘actionable response’ to diplomatic notes: India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India has sent over 1,000 diplomatic notes and 456 "consolidated reminders" to Bangladesh since September 2020 regarding the repatriation of suspected illegal Bangladeshi immigrants.  The Indian government's note verbale, sent on April 30th after a Bangladesh protest against Assam's former Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's claims about border security, stated that no actionable response has been received.

articles.title: Jabalpur cruise boat tragedy: Nightmare on the Narmada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On April 30th, Madhya Pradesh experienced a heat wave with temperatures exceeding 40 degrees Celsius.  As the weather cooled, people flocked to the Bargi dam reservoir on the Narmada river for boat rides and cruises operated by the MPSTDC. This popular destination has been a draw for locals and tourists for nearly three decades.

articles.title: Nitish and BJP have no moral right to speak on dynastic politics, says Tejashwi Yadav - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tejashwi Yadav, leader of the opposition in Bihar's Legislative Assembly, criticized Nitish Kumar and Prime Minister Narendra Modi for their involvement in dynasty politics following the expansion of the Bihar Cabinet.  Yadav argued that both the BJP and its allies are engaging in dynasty politics, citing examples like the inclusion of sons of former Chief Ministers in the new cabinet.

articles.title: Punjab worse than West Bengal under AAP rule, says Haryana CM Saini - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini criticized the AAP government in Punjab, accusing it of failing to control drug trafficking, illegal mining, and lawlessness. He compared the current situation in Punjab to West Bengal under Mamata Banerjee, stating that people are disillusioned with the AAP and seeking change through the BJP's governance model.  Saini also contrasted the BJP's policies with those of the Congress, highlighting the latter's corruption and lack of focus on people's welfare.

articles.title: IIT Madras Global Research Foundation announces deep tech hub in California - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: IIT Madras Global Research Foundation announced the establishment of a deep tech hub in Menlo Park, California, with a total investment of USD 7.5 million. The center aims to support Indian deep tech startups by providing access to global markets, venture ecosystems, mentorship, research collaborations, and industry partnerships.  The launch was announced at the SelectUSA Investment Summit on Wednesday and marks a strategic move for advancing deep tech research and commercialization in the region.

articles.title: Trump administration relaxing hunting restrictions in US parks and refuges | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's administration is directing US Department of the Interior agencies to remove hunting restrictions on national parks, refuges, and wilderness areas. The order, issued by Secretary Doug Burgum, aims to expand public access to hunting and fishing while supporting rural economies and outdoor recreation.  However, critics argue that the move undermines established management practices and prioritizes hunting over visitor safety and environmental protection. Despite concerns from some conservation groups, the administration maintains that its policy is a "commonsense approach" to public land management.

articles.title: A guide to all 35 Eurovision songs: From Boy George to anti-work anthems
articles.rephrased_article: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest features a diverse range of musical styles, from pop anthems to rock ballads.  Boy George, Tamara Živković, and Veronica Fusaro are among the artists with songs that have garnered attention for their unique lyrics and performances.  Several countries are sending entries that explore themes of social justice, mental health, and political commentary. The competition is expected to be fierce, with many contenders vying for the coveted title.

articles.title: Panel lawyers appointed for bonded labour cases in Thanjavur - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority (TNSLSA) has appointed seven panel lawyers in Thanjavur district to provide legal aid to survivors of bonded labor and human trafficking. This is the highest number of appointments made in a single district, following the establishment of the One-Stop Crisis Team (OSCT) which aims to combat sex, organ, and labor trafficking across the state. The initiative has expanded to multiple districts and has played a role in rescuing survivors and providing legal assistance, but with several cases pending before courts, the DLSA was asked to nominate panel lawyers to assist prosecutors.

articles.title: General Motors to pay $12.75m settlement for selling drivers’ location and data | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: General Motors (GM) agreed to pay $12.75 million to settle claims that it illegally sold the location and driving data of hundreds of thousands of Californians to data brokers, as stated by California’s Attorney General Rob Bonta. The settlement, subject to court approval, addresses concerns about consumer privacy and data security in vehicles.  The state is also restricting GM's use of consumer-driving data and implementing a five-year ban on its sale to any data broker.

articles.title: Hojicha, chai, mate: What could go on to rival matcha?
articles.rephrased_article: Hojicha, a Japanese roasted green tea, is gaining popularity in the UK, appearing on menus at cafes and restaurants like Koya and Jenki.  Sales of hojicha lattes have increased significantly, with some suggesting it's becoming as mainstream as matcha was a few years ago. While matcha sales remain strong, other teas like chai, kombucha, and even mate are also seeing growth. The popularity of these beverages is driven by consumer interest in diverse flavors, functional benefits, and the growing trend of sober-curious consumers seeking alternative options to alcohol.

articles.title: Mirwaiz expresses concern over closure of school-cum-seminary under UAPA in Kashmir - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, the chief cleric of Kashmir, expressed concern over the closure of a seminary-cum-school in Shopian under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), stating it has ruined the future of hundreds of students. He urged the government to reconsider its approach and allow the reopening of the institution, citing the deep distress caused by the move among students and parents. Mirwaiz also praised the government's efforts against drug peddlers but emphasized that addressing the underlying issues like political uncertainty and economic hardship is crucial to combatting substance abuse.

articles.title: John Swinney urges Starmer to show Scotland ‘greater respect’ after SNP victory | Scottish politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: John Swinney, the leader of the Scottish National party, challenged Keir Starmer, the leader of Labour, to show "greater respect" after his party won a record fifth term in office.  With the final seats still undecided, the SNP secured at least 57 of Holyrood’s 129 seats, while Labour and Reform struggled for second place. The Scottish Greens also achieved a pro-independence majority, but Swinney indicated he would not pursue a second independence referendum.  The election saw record low turnouts in several constituencies, with the SNP's national share of the vote falling to its lowest since 2007.

articles.title: Return of IS-linked families sparks debate in terror-traumatised Australia
articles.rephrased_article: Following the return of four women and their children linked to the Islamic State group from Syria, Australia is facing a national debate on how to handle these families.  The Australian government has stated it will not assist in the return of any more IS-linked individuals, citing legal limitations and public sentiment. However, advocates argue that the safety and well-being of the children are paramount and they should be brought home for rehabilitation. The situation is further complicated by concerns about potential security risks and the need to address the complex issue of radicalization.

articles.title: Watch: Vijay meets Governor Arlekar for third time after CPI, CPI(M) support | Above the Fold | 08.05.2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Athira Madhav, a Tamil Nadu-based news program, has been published. The program features Ragavi M as presenter and Karthi as the shoot director.  The program is edited by Naveenkumar V.

articles.title: TH journalist wins award - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DKMS Foundation, India, hosted the ‘Lifesaver Honours Night’ in Bengaluru to recognize efforts strengthening the stem cell donor ecosystem. Afshan Yasmeen, Deputy Editor of The Hindu, received an award for her impactful reporting on thalassaemia patients in Karnataka.  The event brought together medical professionals, institutions, corporate partners and advocates working against blood cancer and blood disorders.

articles.title: 60 centres get ready for Inter supplementary exams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam Joint Collector Gobbilla Vidyadhari directed officials to ensure smooth and error-free Intermediate Advanced Supplementary examinations from May 21st to June 2nd. The examinations will be held in 60 centers across the district, with first year exams running from 9 a.m. to 12 noon and second year exams from 2:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m.

articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari was unanimously elected leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party's legislature party in West Bengal following their victory in the recent assembly elections. Amit Shah, Union Home Minister, presided over the meeting and supported Adhikari's nomination.  The BJP secured 207 seats, while the Trinamool Congress won 80.  Adhikari then met with Governor R.N. Ravi to formally stake his claim to form a government.

articles.title: BWSSB’s ‘Blue Force’ drive nets ₹55 crore, disconnects over 11,000 illegal water links - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) has significantly increased its efforts to combat illegal water and sewerage connections, disconnecting 11,217 unauthorized links and generating ₹55 crore in additional revenue over the past five months. The enforcement, conducted by BWSSB’s special squad ‘Blue Force’, covered 54,625 buildings across Bengaluru's North, South, East, and West zones.  The East Zone recorded the highest number of disconnections (3,151) while the South Zone saw the most inspections.

articles.title: Final decision on Kerala CM turns into political cliff-hanger as ball now in Congress High Command’s court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress party in Kerala is facing uncertainty regarding the selection of its Chief Minister, with three potential candidates – V.D. Satheesan, K.C. Venugopal, and Ramesh Chennithala – vying for the position.  The decision appears to be pending a final announcement from the Congress High Command, who are reportedly meeting with the contenders in Delhi on Saturday.

articles.title: Calcutta High Court to hear pleas against Great Nicobar project in June; overrules Centre’s objections - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court ruled in favor of the petitioners, dismissing the Union government’s preliminary objections to their case alleging violations of the Forest Rights Act. The court overruled the government's argument that Meena Gupta lacked legal standing to pursue the matter and directed the case for a final hearing on June 23rd.

articles.title: Florida surgeon ‘devastated’ over death of patient after removing liver instead of spleen | Florida | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Thomas Shaknovsky, a Florida surgeon, faces manslaughter charges after allegedly removing a patient's liver instead of his spleen. In a deposition, Shaknovsky described the death of 70-year-old William Bryan as an "incredibly unfortunate event" and expressed deep regret. The grand jury indictment stems from Bryan's death following the botched surgery.  According to Shaknovsky, he was mentally compromised during the operation, but a lawsuit filed by Bryan's widow accuses him of medical malpractice and claims he intentionally omitted any reference to the liver removal in order to cover up his negligence.

articles.title: NHA, IndiaAI Mission and IISc showcase human-centric AI solutions to transform health claims under AB PM-JAY - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: National Health Authority (NHA) and its partners, IndiaAI Mission and the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), hosted an auto-adjudication hackathon showcasing AI solutions for healthcare claims management under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY).  Teams presented AI systems capable of analyzing medical documents, interpreting radiological images, detecting document forgery, and streamlining claim processing. The event highlighted the use of AI/ML to improve the speed, accuracy, transparency, and efficiency of claims adjudication while reducing fraud and manual intervention.

articles.title: Doge slashing of humanities grants in 2025 ruled biased and unconstitutional | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's termination of hundreds of humanities grants, totaling over $100 million in congressionally appropriated funds, was unconstitutional and involved "blatant" discrimination. Elon Musk, who led the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge) at the time, had initiated the cost-cutting drive. The judge stated that Doge's actions violated both the First Amendment and the Fifth Amendment, citing the agency's discriminatory criteria based on race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, and national origin.  The ruling also found that Doge lacked legal authority to terminate the grants.

articles.title: ​Take east: On the BJP government in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured a resounding victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, winning 207 out of 294 seats.  Suvendu Adhikari, former Leader of the Opposition and now the new Chief Minister, defeated incumbent Mamata Banerjee in her own constituency, marking a significant shift in power dynamics. The BJP's success can be attributed to its strategic focus on booth-level organization, leveraging Hindu identity politics, and exploiting popular dissatisfaction with the TMC's governance.  The party's victory comes with challenges, including restoring law and order after targeted violence.

articles.title: Keir Starmer under pressure to agree exit plan after election mauling | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer is facing pressure to step down after a series of devastating election results for his party. Senior Labour MPs are calling for him to set a timeline for his departure, with some suggesting he should resign by the end of the year and oversee a leadership contest following his last conference in autumn.  The Prime Minister will deliver a major speech next week outlining a more optimistic vision for the country's future, but the results have prompted calls for change within the party.

articles.title: Two traffickers held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru Rural police intercepted a truck carrying 250 kg of ganja concealed in poultry feed, arresting two men, Ramyan Yadav and Sabir Khan, who were transporting the feed from Chhattisgarh to Tamil Nadu.  The investigation revealed that the men had been hired by a man from their native place to transport the contraband to a receiver in Bengaluru. The Jigani police have booked them under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, with further investigations ongoing.

articles.title: Nigel Farage hails ‘historic shift in politics’ after Reform UK election gains | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage and Reform UK made significant gains in the English local elections, taking control of Essex county council and Sunderland city council. The party also secured a strong showing in Suffolk and other areas, but faced setbacks in Harlow and Bexley. While some analysts suggest Reform may have peaked, the party remains optimistic about its future prospects for the general election. Reform UK's success appears to be driven by gains in economically disadvantaged areas.

articles.title: SC/ST representation beyond reserved seats still remains limited, show T.N. Assembly election results - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The recent Tamil Nadu Assembly election results show that representation for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in general constituencies remains limited.  P. Viswanathan, a Congress candidate, was the only SC elected from a general constituency, while Mu. Kalanjiyam of the Naam Tamilar Katchi contested in Thousand Lights, Chennai. The Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), emerged as the single largest party with 108 seats and performed strongly in reserved constituencies, winning 23 out of 44 SC-reserved seats.  The DMK secured nine seats, while the AIADMK won eight.

articles.title: UFO documents released by Pentagon describe floating objects and flashes of light
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon released 161 declassified documents on UFOs and unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP) to the public, including reports from Apollo astronauts who witnessed unexplained lights and particles during their missions.  The files also contain individual accounts of UAP sightings by civilians and military personnel in various locations around the world. While some lawmakers praised the release as a positive step towards transparency, others criticized it as a distraction from more pressing issues.

articles.title: Four south Florida men convicted in Haitian president’s assassination | Haiti | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Four south Florida men were convicted of plotting to kill Haitian president Jovenel Moïse in 2021. Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, James Solages, and Walter Veintemilla were found guilty of conspiracy to kill and kidnap a person outside the US resulting in death, and providing material support or resources to carry out a violation resulting in death. They face life in prison. A fifth defendant, Christian Emmanuel Sanon, will be tried later due to health issues. The killing has sparked investigations and indictments in Haiti and the United States, with competing theories about who ordered it.

articles.title: Thousands run Palestine Marathon under shadow of Israel’s war on Gaza | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The tenth Palestine International Marathon drew over 13,000 runners globally, including 2,523 in Gaza and approximately 1,000 foreign participants. The event, organized by the Palestinian Higher Council for Youth and Sports, the Palestinian Olympic Committee, and Bethlehem Municipality, took place amidst escalating violence in the occupied West Bank and Gaza. Participants ran through Bethlehem's streets and along routes hemmed in by checkpoints and the separation wall, carrying Palestinian flags or wearing keffiyehs to symbolize unity and solidarity with Gaza.

articles.title: Prisons report 98.33% pass in Class 12 State board exams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's Department of Prisons and Correctional Services reported a 98.33% pass rate in the Class XII board examinations, with all three top scorers being prisoners at the Central Prison, Palayamkottai.  The Tamil Nadu School Education Department established examination centers within prisons based on requests from prison officials. The top three scorers were P. Vinith (549 marks), T. Manikandan (531 marks), and B. Balu (527 marks).

articles.title: Kenya cancer cluster sparks ‘environmental genocide’ claims over oil waste | Al Jazeera | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: BP and the Kenyan government are facing a lawsuit from 298 residents of Kargi, Kenya, who allege that toxic waste left behind during oil exploration in the 1980s is causing a cancer cluster. Residents claim rising cancer cases and deaths have been linked to the waste, with many dying from digestive system cancers, particularly throat and stomach cancer. The lawsuit seeks an environmental assessment, access to safe water, and compensation for affected families and livestock losses.  The case highlights concerns about environmental contamination and inadequate response from authorities.

articles.title: California becomes first state to provide a month of free diapers to all newborns | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Gavin Newsom announced a new program in California that will provide free diapers to families with newborns. The initiative, funded by $7.4 million from last year's budget and an additional $12.5 million for the upcoming fiscal year, will distribute 400 diapers per family at discharge from participating hospitals. Baby2Baby, a non-profit organization, will manufacture the diapers under the label "Golden State Start" to provide families in need with essential items at a reduced cost. This program aims to alleviate financial strain on families by providing newborns with basic necessities and ensuring they have a more stable start in life.

articles.title: South America’s Champions League match stopped less than 2 mins in after fans started burning stadium sections | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Copa Libertadores match between Independiente Medellín and Flamengo was abandoned after chaotic protests from home fans at the Atanasio Girardot Stadium in Medellin, Colombia. The unrest escalated as fires broke out, flares were launched, and objects were thrown onto the pitch. Security personnel attempted to regain control of the situation, but the match was eventually called off by CONMEBOL, with Flamengo expected to receive a 3-0 victory under disciplinary rules.  The incident highlights growing anger among Independiente Medellín supporters towards club ownership and management following a poor run of form.

articles.title: CBI files charge sheet against Shubhkamna Buildtech and others - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) filed a charge sheet against Shubhkamna Buildtech Private Limited and its directors for alleged fraudulent activities in a Noida housing project. The agency alleges the company induced homebuyers and investors through false promises, resulting in financial losses for victims. The CBI is investigating 50 cases across the country involving builder companies and financial institutions.

articles.title: Botswana’s former President Festus Mogae dies aged 86 | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Botswana’s former President Festus Mogae has died at the age of 86. President Duma Boko expressed condolences, noting Mogae's unwavering commitment to Botswana. Mogae served as president from 1998 to 2008 and was praised for his economic growth and leadership in combating HIV/AIDS.  He also played a key role in overseeing South Sudan’s peace process after leaving office.

articles.title: USPS considers allowing people to ship handguns through the mail | US Postal Service | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Justice Department has proposed a rule change that would allow the United States Postal Service (USPS) to mail handguns, reversing a 1927 law prohibiting such shipments.  This proposal is being met with opposition from Democratic attorneys general in several states who argue it will make firearms more accessible to criminals and violate existing state gun laws. They also contend that the rule change would undermine efforts to curb gun violence. The USPS is currently accepting public comments on the proposed rule before making final changes.

articles.title: 26-year-old Indian student dies of heart attack in US, a day after celebrating graduation walk - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammed Kumel Shaik, a 26-year-old Indian student, died of cardiac arrest in California after celebrating his graduation from Golden Gate University.  His friends launched a fundraiser to help return his body to India for burial. The family is from a lower-middle-class background and the funds will also assist with educational loans and funeral expenses.

articles.title: Congress slams Modi Government over women’s safety citing NCRB data - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress party leaders, including Mallikarjun Kharge, criticized the Narendra Modi Government for its handling of women's safety and rising crime rates.  Kharge cited data from the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) showing a significant increase in crimes against women, children, Dalits, Adivasis, and cybercrime during the past decade. He accused the government of using "Beti Bachao" and "Nari Vandan" as mere slogans while failing to address these issues effectively. Alka Lamba, president of the All India Mahila Congress, echoed these concerns, alleging that the BJP was shielding perpetrators instead of ensuring justice for victims.

articles.title: ‘Leader of the pack’: Reform UK makes election gains, humiliating Labour | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage celebrated sweeping gains in England's local council elections, claiming to be "wiping out" Labour. The populist right-wing party secured over 1,350 seats and 13 councils, while Labour lost control of 35 councils and more than 1,300 seats. Professor James Mitchell believes these results will bolster Reform UK's challenge in the next general election expected in 2029. The party's success comes amid a series of setbacks for Labour, including internal challenges and Prime Minister Keir Starmer's declining authority.

articles.title: Trump touts ‘huge win’ for Republicans in Virginia map ruling; Democratic lawmaker says legislature will ‘respect’ decision – live | US voting rights | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Virginia Supreme Court rejected a voter-approved ballot measure to re-draw the state's congressional map, prompting criticism from Democrats and voting rights advocates. The court ruled that the legislature did not follow proper procedures in approving the amendment.  Democratic Governor Abigail Spanberger expressed disappointment with the decision, stating her focus will be on ensuring all voters have access to information for the upcoming elections. Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, called the decision "unprecedented" and a violation of the people's will. The ruling is another setback for Democrats and minority voting rights advocates who are facing redistricting efforts from several southern Republican states.

articles.title: 62-year-old Indian-American man to be denaturalized for $2.5 million fraud, false information - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice is seeking to denaturalize Debashis Ghosh, a 62-year-old Indian-American businessman, along with eleven other individuals for their involvement in wire fraud.  Ghosh was convicted in 2017 for conspiring to defraud investors of $2.5 million intended for an aircraft maintenance facility and misrepresented the location and safekeeping of the funds during his naturalization process in 2012. Ghosh concealed his criminal history from US authorities, including during his naturalization interview where he claimed to have never committed a crime or offense for which he had not been arrested.  The Immigration and Nationality Act allows for citizenship revocation if it was illegally obtained or procured by concealment of material facts.

articles.title: Only Congress party can defeat BJP in the battle of ideologies, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Congress, asserted that only his party could defeat the BJP, characterizing the upcoming election as a clash between the RSS’s ideology of hatred and partition and the Congress's ideology of love and unity.  He accused Narendra Modi of attacking India's democratic system and the Constitution, vowing that the Congress would not forget this action. Gandhi also criticized the U.S. trade deal, claiming it harms Indian farmers and was influenced by Mr. Modi’s "entire history" and a pending U.S. criminal case against businessman Gautam Adani.  The event marked a show of unity within the faction-ridden Haryana unit, with prominent Congress leaders joining him.

articles.title: FIFPRO in ‘landmark’ win as European body admits football calendar failings | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFPRO, the players' union, has won a landmark legal victory after the European Committee of Social Rights agreed to investigate whether the French state failed to uphold labor standards for professional footballers. The unanimous decision marks the first time a players’ union has successfully advanced a collective complaint under the European Social Charter.  The case centers on the French government's failure to protect players from health and safety risks posed by a congested international match calendar, which FIFPRO argues is driven by decisions made by FIFA.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: US fires on two Iranian-flagged oil tankers it claims tried to violate blockade; US to mediate Israel-Lebanon talks | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US military struck two Iranian-flagged oil tankers it claims were attempting to violate a blockade of Iran. The US Central Command (Centcom) said the strikes, which occurred on May 8th, disabled both vessels after firing precision munitions into their smokestacks.  Iran accused the US of violating a ceasefire by targeting ships at the Strait of Hormuz and attacking civilian areas. In response, Iranian officials warned against "adventurism and roguish behavior" following the attacks. The US is mediating talks between Israel and Lebanon to establish long-term border security and reach a lasting peace agreement.  The US also met with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni to discuss tensions over the war on Iran and the potential for economic fallout. Meanwhile, a series of Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon have killed at least five people, while Hezbollah has fired rockets toward Israeli forces.

articles.title: US stocks today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq notch records, boosted by AI and earnings optimism - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq saw strong gains on Friday, driven by investor optimism over robust financial reports from U.S. companies, particularly those in the AI sector.  Nvidia, Micron Technology, and Sandisk experienced significant increases as demand for data centers surged. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index jumped, reflecting a positive outlook for the technology sector. Despite these gains, most sectors in the S&P 500 remained down for the day. Traders anticipate the Federal Reserve will maintain interest rates at their current levels until the end of the year.

articles.title: ‘Four feet tall, wearing space suits and helmets’: Newly released FBI UFO files reveal bizarre claims - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Newly declassified FBI documents detail extraordinary witness accounts of small, suited figures exiting mysterious craft during a wave of sightings in the 1960s. The records, made public as part of a transparency initiative led by the Trump administration, describe "crewmen" associated with unidentified flying objects (UFOs) who were three and a half to four feet tall and wore space suits.  The documents also mention the physical effects these objects allegedly had on their environment, including force fields that interfered with power sources and scorched ground beneath them. While the FBI memo focuses on public frenzy surrounding the book "Flying Saucers – Serious Business" by Frank Edwards, it does not verify extraterrestrial life.

articles.title: U.P. Minister: prepaid smart meters tobe discontinued with immediate effect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to discontinue its smart prepaid electricity meter system and switch all existing meters to postpaid mode. Energy Minister A.K. Sharma announced the change, citing consumer complaints about billing irregularities. The move will see consumers receive bills based on their actual consumption, with payments due by the 10th of each month.  The government also plans to set up special camps and a helpline for resolving consumer issues related to electricity meters and bills.

articles.title: Laura Fernandez sworn in as Costa Rica’s new president | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Fernandez was sworn in as Costa Rica's new president, marking the end of Rodrigo Chaves’ term.  She has pledged to combat rising crime and maintain close ties with the United States, appointing her second vice president, Douglas Soto, as ambassador to Washington. The inauguration saw the participation of US special envoy Kristi Noem and Israeli President Isaac Herzog. Fernandez's right-wing Sovereign People’s Party (PPSO) secured an absolute majority in the legislature.

articles.title: Labour loses control of Birmingham city council after 14 years of leadership | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Labour party's 14-year leadership in Birmingham has ended after significant gains by Reform, Greens, and pro-Gaza independents. The results reflect wider political fragmentation across England, with Labour losing hundreds of council seats to parties like Reform UK, which made big gains across the Midlands and north.  The outgoing Labour leader, John Cotton, called for greater unity in the city while acknowledging the need for a more coherent message from the party. Independent candidates Nosheen Khalid and others focused on issues such as child poverty and youth services, emphasizing their desire to improve governance in Birmingham.

articles.title: 3,352 candidates forfeit deposit in T.N. Assembly polls - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: AIADMK, BJP, NTK, Election Commission of India
articles.rephrased_article: In the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, 3,352 candidates lost their deposits after failing to secure one-sixth of the votes in their constituencies.  The AIADMK and BJP saw losses in several constituencies, while the NTK lost its deposit in all 234. The Election Commission of India (EC) reported a polling percentage of 86.03%, with postal vote rejection at 11.08%.  The TVK, DMK, and AIADMK secured significant votes, while the DMDK was the only party to have a winning female candidate.

articles.title: Amazon begins drone deliveries in UK with Darlington pilot programme | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amazon has launched its first drone delivery service in the UK, operating a pilot program in Darlington, County Durham. The company uses its MK30 drones to transport lightweight packages within a 7.5-mile radius of its fulfillment center.  Items eligible for delivery include household products such as batteries and electronic accessories. David Carbon, vice president of Amazon Prime Air, stated that fast delivery is a growing customer expectation, with the service aiming to provide quick access to essential items. The program currently operates at a maximum of 10 flights per hour, delivering approximately 100 packages daily.

articles.title: South Koreans gear up to roar on football team from rival North | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: South Korea is preparing for a rare event as Naegohyang Women’s FC, a North Korean women's football team, will play the Suwon FC Women in the Asian Champions League on May 20th.  The Korean Council for Reconciliation and Cooperation (KCRC) has enlisted about 300 volunteers to support the North Korean team, hoping it will contribute to inter-Korean reconciliation. Despite South Korea's national security laws prohibiting displays of the North Korean flag or playing its anthem in public spaces, South Korean civic organizations are rallying supporters for the match. The winner of the semifinal will advance to the final on May 23rd.

articles.title: Small Georgia town’s mayor doesn’t know what happens next after firing entire police department | Georgia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Cohutta town council held a special meeting on Friday to discuss reinstating the police department after Mayor Ron Shinnick fired the chief and all officers. The meeting also considered a request for the mayor's "immediate resignation."  Shinnick cited comments made by officers on social media as the reason for the termination of the police chief and about 10 officers.  The former police sergeant, Jeremy May, stated that the mayor was acting out of personal vendetta. The Whitfield county sheriff’s office will assist townspeople with any needs they may have.

articles.title: B.K. Hariprasad takes jibe at B.L. Santhosh on T.N. politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: B.K. Hariprasad, a senior Congress leader and MLC, criticized B.L. Santhosh, the BJP national general secretary (organisation), for his remarks on Tamil Nadu politics.  Mr. Santhosh had previously stated that the Congress would end up with "egg on its face" in the state's upcoming elections. Mr. Hariprasad responded by calling Mr. Santhosh's comments a "joke of the decade" and asserted that the BJP is politically insignificant in Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: 'Suspension of all kinetic activity': Trump announces 3-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, 1,000-prisoner swap - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, starting Saturday, May 9th. The truce, which will also include a prisoner exchange, was made in an effort to end the ongoing war that has lasted for over a year. While the ceasefire was welcomed by some, fighting continued on Friday with both sides engaging in attacks despite the declared truce. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of maintaining assault operations and stated that Ukraine would respond "in kind". Despite the ceasefire announcement, the situation remains tense.

articles.title: How and when can Arsenal or Man City win the Premier League? | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Manchester City face Brentford on Saturday in a crucial Premier League match, seeking to close the gap on Arsenal, who hold a five-point lead with three games remaining.  Arsenal travel to West Ham on Sunday for another tough test. The title race hinges on both teams' results, and a win for either side could significantly impact their chances of winning the league.

articles.title: Cracks showing for Labour close to backyards of Starmer’s top team | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer refused to resign following a string of local election losses for Labour, which have been attributed to the rise of Reform UK, the Greens, and independents.  Reform UK has gained ground in traditionally Labour areas, while the Greens have made gains in major cities like London.  The losses are geographically uneven and pose challenges for Starmer as he faces criticism from voters who feel their concerns have not been addressed.

articles.title: BJP’s victory in Bengal will plug a big hole in national security, says Amit Shah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union Home Minister, stated that the BJP's victory in West Bengal was significant for national security, as it plugs a major hole and will make infiltration and cattle smuggling impossible. He emphasized that this victory signifies ideological continuity for the party, marking its presence across all states from Gangotri to Gangasagar.  Shah also highlighted the importance of the victory in light of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 150th birth anniversary and thanked voters for their support. The BJP Legislature Party leader, Suvendu Adhikari, will be sworn in as the Chief Minister on May 9th.

articles.title: Texas woman running for Governor mocks Indians, says her new name is 'Pria' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kelly Smith, a write-in candidate for Texas governor, sparked controversy with a photo of herself in Indian attire and claiming to be "Indian" while stating she would continue to eat hamburgers. Smith's comments drew backlash from the Indian community and accusations of anti-India sentiment, despite her assertion that she is a lifelong Texan. She has only received 14 donations for her campaign and faces an uphill battle in the November election.

articles.title: Security forces kill five terrorists in Tank, DI Khan in IBOs: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: ISPR announced the killing of five terrorists in two separate operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Tank and Dera Ismail Khan districts. The military media wing stated that four individuals were killed in Tank during an intelligence-based operation targeting a group called Fitna al-Khwarij, which is associated with the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. In another operation, one terrorist was killed in DI Khan district.  The ISPR emphasized that these operations are part of the ongoing counterterrorism campaign and aim to eliminate foreign-sponsored terrorism from the country.

articles.title: Libya’s largest oil refinery halts operations during fighting | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Libya’s largest oil refinery at Zawiya has been shut down and an emergency declared following fighting between armed groups nearby. The National Oil Corporation (NOC) and Zawiya Refining Company evacuated employees and halted operations as a precautionary measure, citing heavy weapons fire near the complex.  Authorities in Zawiya launched a "large-scale operation" against criminal groups involved in serious acts like murder and kidnapping, but no significant damage was reported to the refinery itself. The refinery, with a capacity of 120,000 barrels per day, is connected to the 300,000 bpd Sharara oilfield.

articles.title: 2026 elections mapped: how Labour lost ground in different directions | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labour suffered significant losses across England, Scotland, and Wales in the recent local elections. The party lost ground to opponents on both the left and right, including Reform UK, the Greens, and the Scottish National Party.  In England, Labour saw record drops in seat share, pushing it into its lowest representation since the 1970s. This fragmentation of the political landscape has resulted in a significant loss of power for Labour in Wales and a swathe of councils in England. The results have been particularly damaging to the Conservatives, who lost strongholds such as Hampshire and eastern England.

articles.title: AMMK chief Dhinakaran slams TVK for submitting ‘forged’ letter to Governor claiming his party’s backing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T.T.V. Dhinakaran, leader of the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam, accused the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) of submitting a forged letter claiming support from his party's lone MLA-elect, S. Kamaraj.  Dhinakaran stated that the TVK submitted a photocopy of a WhatsApp letter to the Governor and will lodge a police complaint. Dhinakaran also previously submitted a letter to the Governor extending support to Edappadi K. Palaniswami urging him to form the government.

articles.title: ‘Eight-pointed star’ seen in UFO files as Pentagon teases ‘even cooler information’ to come - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Pentagon released a video of an unidentified object in the sky, captured in 2013 by US Central Command personnel. The infrared footage shows a glowing object with a star-like shape that drifts and streaks across the air.  While officials have not identified what the object is, they have stated the description accompanying the footage is only meant to provide context and should not be interpreted as proof of anything unexplained. President Donald Trump ordered the release of these files through the Pentagon's newly launched website dedicated to UFOs and unexplained aerial incidents.

articles.title: Govt hikes petrol by Rs14.92 per litre, diesel by Rs15 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government raised the price of petrol by Rs14.92 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs15 on Friday, bringing the cost of petrol to Rs414.78 per litre and HSD to Rs414.58. The increase is effective from May 9th and follows a pattern of weekly adjustments due to global fuel market fluctuations, including the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran.  The government has been adjusting prices since March, with recent increases in April and last week.

articles.title: Could Labour and Conservative party dominance in UK politics be ending? | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, leader of the Labour Party, faced calls to resign following significant losses in local elections despite his parliamentary majority. The results raise questions about the future of party dominance in UK politics and have prompted challenges from both the left and right.  Experts on political dynamics, including Peter Geoghegan and Lesley Riddoch, discussed the significance of these local election outcomes.

articles.title: King Charles features in surprise birthday tribute to David Attenborough | David Attenborough | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III featured in a surprise birthday tribute to David Attenborough, with a cast of wild animals helping deliver his handwritten congratulatory card. The whimsical film, "A Very Special Delivery," began with the king writing his message in Balmoral Castle and ended with a barn owl delivering it to Attenborough's London home.  The four-minute film was produced by BBC Studios natural history unit.

articles.title: Plaid Cymru wins Welsh Senedd elections, ending 100 years of Labour control | Welsh politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Plaid Cymru has won the Welsh Senedd elections, ending 100 years of Labour dominance in Wales.  The party's leader, Rhun ap Iorwerth, said he is ready to become first minister and form the next Welsh government. Reform UK came second, pushing Labour into third place.  Eluned Morgan, who took over Welsh Labour in 2024, has resigned as party leader after a catastrophic result for the party.  The shift marks a seismic change in Welsh politics and signals the end of two-party dominance.

articles.title: Participation in democracy should go beyond voting, says T.M. Krishna - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T.M. Krishna, a Carnatic singer and author, urged for everyday engagement with politics beyond voting day to foster a "cultural habit of democracy." He emphasized that questioning the State is crucial for its well-being, as political parties often control the questions citizens are asked. Krishna also highlighted inaccuracies in historical narratives surrounding India's national symbols, arguing they can represent both individual independence and collective identity.

articles.title: 'Is the fight for Green Card worth it?' H-1B visa holder says he has decent money but can see parents once every two years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Redditor who obtained an H-1B visa to work in the US is questioning the value of the journey after experiencing limited social life, financial stress, and long working hours.  The user's post sparked a debate on Reddit, with many users suggesting that waiting for a Green Card may not be worth it due to the visa stress and potential job insecurity. Some suggested Canada as an alternative option while others highlighted the importance of factors like financial stability and opportunities in one's home country when making such decisions.

articles.title: Olympic water polo resignations cite lack of respect, belittling behaviour | Olympics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Slobodan Soro, the newly appointed president of Serbia's water polo federation, has faced criticism for his comments about the national team's recent European championship win.  Eleven members of the gold medal-winning squad have boycotted the team in protest of Soro's remarks, which they claim belittle their achievements. The players, who are demanding Soro's removal from his position, argue that their success was not a result of "momentary inspiration" but years of hard work and sacrifice.  The federation has published the players' letter on its website, while stating it does not wish to participate in what it calls a "perfectly normal process".

articles.title: Reform wins across northern England overturn decades of Labour control | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage’s Reform UK party secured a resounding victory in local elections across several Labour-held areas, including Sunderland where they won 58 of the 75 seats. The results marked a significant shift in political control, with Labour losing its grip on key council seats in Sunderland, Gateshead, and South Tyneside.  The party’s losses were attributed to voters disillusioned with Labour’s performance and dissatisfaction with issues such as taxes and local services.  Several prominent figures within the Labour Party, including education secretary Bridget Phillipson, called for a change in leadership.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: CPI, CPI(M) extend unconditional support to TVK; VCK may follow suit - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, leader of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), is seeking to form a government in Tamil Nadu after receiving support from the Communist Party of India and CPI(Marxist).  The VCK remains undecided on backing the TVK, while T.T.V. Dhinakaran, leader of the Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam (AMMK), has accused his party's lone MLA-elect of forging a letter of support for the TVK. The Governor is yet to issue a decision on the request for forming the government, with the possibility of President’s Rule looming if no government is formed by May 10th.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Queen Victoria: “Then, dear Mamma, I hope you will grant me the first request I make to you, as Queen. Let me be by myself for an hour.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Queen Victoria's famous quote, "Then, dear Mamma, I hope you will grant me the first request I make to you, as Queen. Let me be by myself for an hour," reveals her need for solitude after becoming queen at 18.  The quote, which reflects a desire for privacy and time to process the immense responsibility of ruling the British Empire, resonates with people today because it captures a universal human experience of needing quiet reflection during times of change. This simple request underscores Victoria's emotional maturity and self-awareness, demonstrating that even powerful figures can feel overwhelmed by life-changing events.

articles.title: ASEAN leaders adopt measures to ease economic pain caused by Iran war | ASEAN News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: ASEAN leaders agreed on measures to mitigate the economic impact of the ongoing Iran war, including a regional fuel-sharing framework and plans for a regional power grid and fuel stockpile. The initiatives aim to reduce reliance on Middle Eastern energy imports, but details regarding implementation remain unclear. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. acknowledged that practical arrangements still need to be finalized, emphasizing the need for clarity on sharing mechanisms, payment structures, and prioritization during crises.

articles.title: Americans on hantavirus cruise ship reportedly to be quarantined in US | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is sending personnel to the Canary Islands to assist with a hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius.  Oceanwide Expeditions, the ship's operator, estimates 17 Americans are onboard. The CDC plans to repatriate American passengers back to the US, where they will undergo quarantine in Nebraska. Nebraska Medicine and the National Quarantine Unit are prepared to provide care while protecting the community.  The US State Department is coordinating with the CDC, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the Spanish government for the repatriation effort.

articles.title: Thalassemia awareness walk organised on Necklace Road - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Health Minister C. Damodar Raja Narasimha flagged off a two-kilometer awareness walk on Necklace Road to commemorate International Thalassemia Day. The event, organized by the Thalassemia and Sickle Cell Society (TSCS), aimed to promote thalassemia prevention, early screening, and accessible healthcare support.  Dr. Chandrakant Agarwal, President of TSCS, emphasized the importance of timely screening, awareness, and genetic counselling for preventing thalassemia.

articles.title: ‘CIA knew Iran would shut down Strait of Hormuz if US attacked’: Former counterterror chief Joe Kent makes bombshell claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Joe Kent, former director of the National Counterterrorism Center, has claimed that US intelligence agencies, including the CIA, agreed before the Iran war that Tehran was not developing a nuclear weapon. He argues that intelligence officials warned that targeting Iran's leadership would strengthen the regime and embolden hardliners, but these warnings were ignored in favor of a narrative pushed by Israel. Kent resigned from his position over disagreements about the conflict and has been criticized for spreading false claims.  President Donald Trump, who authorized the military action, maintains that he acted based on strong evidence that Iran posed an imminent threat and was preparing to strike Americans first.

articles.title: Quadcopter attack in KP's Bannu injures 8, including women - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: An explosion following the reported crash of a quadcopter drone in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, injured eight people, including women.  Security agencies launched an investigation into the incident while local residents provided first aid and shifted the injured to the District Headquarters Hospital Bannu. The administration confirmed that all injured individuals are receiving medical treatment, with some reported as being in critical condition.

articles.title: Trump announces three-day ceasefire in Russia-Ukraine war | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump, US president, announced a three-day ceasefire in the Russia-Ukraine war from Saturday to Monday. The truce includes a suspension of all kinetic activity and a prisoner swap of 1,000 prisoners from each country. Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy, leaders of Russia and Ukraine respectively, agreed to the ceasefire after Trump's request.  Talks are continuing on ending the war.

articles.title: Palestine Marathon attracts thousands of runners
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of runners and spectators participated in the Palestine Marathon and Half Marathon, returning to Bethlehem after a two-year hiatus due to restrictions related to the Gaza War. The event, held alongside a race in Gaza, drew participants from across the West Bank and internationally as a fragile ceasefire in the Palestinian Territory remained in place.

articles.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine three-day ceasefire from 9 May | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced a three-day ceasefire in the war between Russia and Ukraine, from May 9 to 11, including a prisoner swap of 1,000 prisoners from each country.  Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the president of Ukraine, confirmed the agreement and a prisoner exchange, stating that a ceasefire regime would also be established during those days.  Russia had previously announced a two-day unilateral ceasefire to mark its Victory Day on May 9th.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Congress MLAs camping in Hyderabad amid uncertainty in government formation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Five Tamil Nadu Congress MLAs are currently in Hyderabad after arriving on Thursday, May 7th, 2026. The MLAs were initially planning to leave after Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar asked Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam chief Vijay to form the government. However, they postponed their return due to new developments in Tamil Nadu that cast a shadow on the swearing-in ceremony.

articles.title: Quote of the day by James Watson: “Worrying about complications before ruling out the possibility that the answer was simple would have been damned foolishness.” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: James Watson, co-discoverer of the double helix structure of DNA, emphasized the importance of simplicity in problem-solving. His quote, "Worrying about complications before ruling out the possibility that the answer was simple would have been damned foolishness," highlights the value of clarity and logical thinking in scientific discovery and everyday life.  Watson's approach, which involved seeking simpler explanations before assuming more complicated ones, revolutionized biology and continues to inspire scientists and readers today.

articles.title: US religious freedom commission calls for India to be listed as ‘country of particular concern’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) urged the US State Department to designate India as a "country of particular concern" for its ongoing, systematic, and egregious religious freedom violations. The commission cited concerns about discriminatory legislation, arbitrary detention, attacks against religious minorities, and transnational repression targeting critics abroad.  US House of Representatives member Chris Smith, Stephen Rapp, and scholars like Angana Chatterji and Raqib Naik all testified to the deteriorating situation for religious minorities in India.

articles.title: Four convicted in US related to killing of Haitian President Jovenel Moise | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Four individuals, Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, and James Solages, were found guilty in the United States for their roles in the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moise. The defendants were convicted on charges of conspiracy to kill or kidnap Moise, as well as providing material support for the plot. Prosecutors argued that the Florida-based group served as a central hub for planning and funding the assassination, while defense attorneys claimed their clients were scapegoats involved in a plan to serve an arrest warrant. The case has been linked to ongoing political instability and security crises in Haiti following Moise's death, which left a power vacuum and triggered a series of natural disasters and violence.

articles.title: Greece military examines mystery naval drone found in Ionian Sea
articles.rephrased_article: Greece's military is investigating a mysterious unmanned naval drone discovered in the Ionian Sea. The Greek defense ministry is overseeing the investigation, which has been prompted by reports that the vessel carried explosives and may be linked to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.  Footage shows the drone being towed to a port near Vasiliki, with experts examining its purpose and origin. The drone's possible connection to Ukraine's sea drones used against Russian targets is under scrutiny.

articles.title: Frustrated by Iran, Trump at last seizes enriched uranium – but from Venezuela | Venezuela | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump oversaw the removal of 13.5kg of highly enriched uranium from a legacy research reactor in Venezuela, a move praised by Brandon Williams, administrator of the US Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration. The operation involved the US, the UK, and Venezuela, with the uranium being transported safely to a South Carolina facility.  The removal is seen as a positive step for Venezuela and a signal of restored relations between the two countries.

articles.title: Man pleads not guilty to threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alex Jenkinson, 39, pleaded not guilty to threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor with intent to cause fear or provoke violence.  The former prince was walking his dogs near his home in Norfolk when the alleged incident occurred on Wednesday evening.  Mountbatten-Windsor is expected to give evidence via videolink at a trial scheduled for July 29th. Jenkinson also faces charges of threatening another man, Stephen Terry, in May. He was granted conditional bail with restrictions against contacting Mountbatten-Windsor, entering Norfolk, or approaching royal residences.

articles.title: AI market crash coming soon? Billionaire investor Paul Tudor Jones says the bulls have another two years - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jones, a macro trader, warns of potential market crashes similar to the dot-com bubble in the early 2000s, citing parallels with the current AI bull market. While acknowledging the excitement surrounding AI's rapid growth, Jones emphasizes the need for government regulation to prevent potential harm to humanity. Despite this caution, Jones has invested in AI stocks and believes that historical precedents can help guide investors.  The S&P 500, Nasdaq, Nikkei, and Kospi all reached record highs this week, driven by strong earnings from companies like Advanced Micro Devices, while India's IT sector experienced a decline due to concerns about the impact of AI on its services industry.

articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lalit Jain, Director of Census Operations (DCO), Haryana, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

articles.title: Passenger from 'Hantavirus' cruise visited school on remotest island Tristan de Cunha, believed to be infected - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A passenger from the infected MV Hondius visited Tristan da Cunha, a remote island in the South Atlantic Ocean, after the ship stopped off on April 14th, 2026. The UK Health Security Agency has identified this individual as a new suspected case of hantavirus.  The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) activated its Emergency Operations Centers and classified the outbreak as "Level 3", while local officials in Tristan are concerned about the infections on the ship.

articles.title: Real Madrid fine Valverde and Tchouameni for dressing-room fight | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid fined Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde 500,000 euros each for a dressing-room fight that left Valverde hospitalized. The club did not impose sporting sanctions but stated the fine concludes internal procedures against the pair.  Valverde will miss Sunday's Clasico against Barcelona due to a head injury sustained during the altercation.

articles.title: JUI-F holds second round of protests over killing of Maulana Idrees - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) held a second round of protest rallies across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, demanding the arrest of those responsible for the killing of prominent cleric Maulana Muhammad Idrees. The protests, which took place after Friday prayers, were organized in response to the cleric's assassination on Tuesday and included demonstrations outside the Peshawar Press Club.  JUI-F leaders condemned the deteriorating law and order situation in the province and the government's actions against madrasas.

articles.title: Badenoch claims Tories ‘coming back’ despite widespread losses in local elections | Conservatives | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kemi Badenoch, the Conservative MP, claimed that her party is "coming back" despite significant losses across England in Thursday's local elections.  While the Tories won back Westminster and Wandsworth councils, they suffered losses in Essex, Suffolk, Brentwood, North East Lincolnshire, Hampshire, and Staffordshire. Reform, a rival party, gained ground in these areas, particularly in Havering where they now hold 39 of the 55 seats.  Prof Tony Travers, a local government expert at the London School of Economics, noted that the strong showing by both Labour and the Liberal Democrats in London suggests voters are seeking less radical change than elsewhere. Political analyst Peter Kellner stated that while the Conservatives' performance is better than last year, it still falls short of historical standards.

articles.title: MCX Q4 Results: Cons PAT soars 291% YoY to Rs 530 crore, revenue triples; Rs 8 per share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX, India's largest non-agri commodity exchange, reported a significant increase in revenue and profit for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026. Revenue surged by 205% to Rs 889 crore, driven by a 34% quarter-on-quarter growth in topline.  The company's bottom line also grew substantially, with PBT reaching Rs 682 crore compared to Rs 168 crore in the previous year. The board recommended a final dividend of Rs 8 per equity share for FY26.

articles.title: Plea in Supreme Court says Governor is ‘duty-bound’ to invite TVK to form government in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A writ petition was filed in the Supreme Court on May 8, 2026, arguing that Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Arlekar should invite C. Joseph Vijay, leader of the Tamil Nadu Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party, to form the government as the single largest party. The petition claims this action would violate the mandate of the electorate and the constitutional sequence established by the Supreme Court.

articles.title: Inmate boasted after fatal prison attack on singer Ian Watkins, prosecutors tell UK court - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rico Gedel, accused of murdering former Welsh singer and songwriter Ian Watkins inside HMP Wakefield, allegedly boasted about his "fame" after the attack.  Prosecutors claim Gedel stabbed Watkins with a homemade blade, inflicting severe injuries, while fellow inmate Samuel Dodsworth allegedly concealed the weapon. The prosecution alleges that both men planned the attack together, although Gedel is accused of carrying out the stabbing himself. Watkins, serving a 29-year sentence for child sex offences, was pronounced dead shortly after the attack.

articles.title: Justice for Shireen: The American investigation | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Four years after the death of Shireen Abu Akleh, her family continues to demand an independent US-backed investigation into her killing.  Lina Abu Akleh, niece of the journalist, and human rights attorney Katherine Gallagher, from the Center for Constitutional Rights, have been advocating for accountability. The push for justice has proven difficult to achieve despite their efforts.

articles.title: Court fight with Pentagon raises Senator Mark Kelly’s White House profile - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Mark Kelly, a former US Navy combat pilot and astronaut, is facing legal challenges from the Pentagon over remarks urging troops to refuse illegal orders. A federal appeals court expressed skepticism about the government's case, questioning whether it could withstand constitutional scrutiny. The case has gained national attention as Democrats seek candidates capable of challenging President Trump's agenda.  Kelly, who has raised millions in recent months and is viewed by some as a potential presidential contender, maintains his right to express constitutional views.

articles.title: US waiting on a response from Iran over proposals for ceasefire deal, says Rubio | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the US expects a response from Iran on Friday regarding an interim deal to end the conflict in the Middle East.  Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the US of breaking the ceasefire, while US forces fired on and disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers attempting to violate a blockade of Iran's ports. Despite escalating tensions, diplomatic efforts continue with Pakistani officials passing a memorandum to Iran that could act as a basis for a more solid ceasefire.  The situation remains volatile, with both sides seeking leverage in negotiations through belligerent rhetoric and sporadic violence.

articles.title: Sebi approves over $1 billion Zepto IPO; 5 other companies also get nod - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Zepto, a Bengaluru-based quick commerce company, is preparing for a public market debut that could raise around $1.3 billion, making it potentially the youngest venture-backed Indian startup to list on the stock exchange.  The company's IPO is expected in the July-September quarter of 2026 and will include a fresh issue of Rs 11,000 crore along with an offer-for-sale by early investors. Zepto has been aggressively expanding its customer base and market share in India's competitive quick commerce space, competing with established players like Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart, and newer entrants such as Flipkart Minutes and Amazon Now.  Investment banks including Morgan Stanley, Axis Capital, HSBC, Goldman Sachs, JM Financial, IIFL Securities, and Motilal Oswal are working on the IPO.

articles.title: SC takes cognisance of resolution about HC judge sending advocate to custody - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court will hear a case on May 15th regarding an incident where an Andhra Pradesh High Court judge allegedly sent a young advocate to judicial custody for a procedural lapse. The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) and the Bar Council of India (BCI) have both expressed concern over the incident, urging the Chief Justice to intervene.

articles.title: 'I’d rather die in my country': Why immigrants are choosing voluntarily departure over detention or asylum in US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration has seen a surge in voluntary departures by immigrants, with over 80,000 orders issued between January 2025 and March this year. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) did not directly address the rise but stated that the administration is enforcing immigration laws more strictly.  Experts say the policy shift has changed how people experience the system, with many immigrants choosing voluntary departure as an alternative to detention due to harsh conditions and long stays in custody.

articles.title: More than a dozen reported killed in Israeli attacks on south Lebanon | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli air raids on southern Lebanon have killed at least 20 people, including a civil defense rescuer, despite a ceasefire in place since April 17th. Hezbollah has responded to the attacks with missile strikes against Israeli military targets.  The escalating violence comes ahead of planned talks between Israel and Lebanon in Washington next week. The Lebanese government is seeking American guarantees for its sovereignty and territorial integrity during these negotiations, while Hezbollah remains opposed to direct talks.

articles.title: IMF's Executive Board approves $1.2 billion financing for Pakistan's reform programme - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Executive Board approved Pakistan's latest economic reform programme, paving the way for a $1.2 billion disbursement. The approval reflects Pakistan's progress on difficult but necessary reforms, including tax policy measures and energy pricing adjustments.  With this tranche, total disbursements under the current program have risen to about $4.5 billion. The IMF emphasized continued focus on rebuilding foreign exchange reserves, containing inflation, and maintaining a tight fiscal stance.

articles.title: Canadian high school where deadly mass shooting occurred to be torn down | Tumbler Ridge school shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Eby, the British Columbia premier, announced that the Tumbler Ridge secondary school will be demolished after a community meeting. The decision follows the February shooting where nine people were killed and dozens injured.  The school has remained closed since the attack, with some students attending classes in portable classrooms.  Eby stated that the province and federal governments will work together to build a new school for the town's youth.

articles.title: High-profile terrorist killed in Bannu was Afghan special forces member: security sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Fatehullah, also known as Mudassir, a member of the Afghan Taliban regime’s Yarmook 60 Special Forces Battalion, was killed in an intelligence-based operation near Bannu's Baka Khel Airport on April 9.  Security sources say he was involved in terrorist activities in Pakistan alongside the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and facilitated cross-border networks.
