Following the BJP's historic victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, ending the TMC’s 15-year rule, Mamata Banerjee, the current Chief Minister, has refused to resign and accused the verdict of being a result of a conspiracy. Post-election violence has also erupted across the state since the election results were announced on May 4, 2026, with Suvendu Adhikari’s personal assistant being shot dead by unidentified gunmen on Wednesday, May 6, 2026.

articles.title: Shakti Pumps shares tumble 7% as Q4 profit drops 65% YoY - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Shakti Pumps' revenue increased 28.9% year-over-year to Rs 857.8 crore, but rising costs led to a significant drop in EBITDA and profit margins. The company’s basic EPS fell 66.3% to Rs 3.1 per share. Despite the muted earnings performance, the board recommended a final dividend of Rs 1 per equity share. Institutional investors reduced their holdings during the quarter, while stock performance has declined nearly 36% over the past year.

articles.title: Rare ‘Earth Mango’ found in Kerala: The hidden fungus locals call Nilamanga has returned again | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A farmer in Kerala's Palakkad district unearthed several unusual mushroom-like structures, identified as Sclerotium stipitatum, a rare subterranean fungus locally known as "Nilamanga" or "Earth Mango".  Researchers believe this discovery highlights the need for greater study of underground fungi, which are often poorly documented and may be disappearing before scientists can document them. The fungus's medicinal potential is attracting interest, but experts caution that further research is needed to confirm its effectiveness in treating medical conditions. Scientists are also investigating the fungus's relationship with termite-rich soil environments and its dependence on wet soil conditions during Kerala's monsoon season.

articles.title: Pakistan seeks Singapore's support in repatriating nationals, Iranians aboard vessels seized by US - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, requested Singaporean Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan's support in facilitating the "welfare and repatriation" of 11 Pakistanis and 20 Iranians aboard vessels seized by the United States.  Dar also spoke with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, expressing Pakistan's readiness to facilitate Iranian nationals' return via Pakistan. The Foreign Office (FO) confirmed that Dar and Balakrishnan discussed maritime affairs, recent incidents in international waters, and agreed to coordinate between relevant authorities. This follows Pakistan's facilitation of the repatriation of crew members from a US-seized Iranian vessel last week.

articles.title: Migration is getting riskier even as progress is made | Migration | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The International Organization for Migration's Global Overview of Migration Routes (2025) reveals mixed results regarding the effectiveness of the Global Compact for Migration. While some routes are shifting, risks remain severe and in some cases worsening, particularly on the Central Mediterranean Route where over 1,300 deaths were recorded. The rise in Sudanese migrants attempting to reach Europe highlights the need for safe and regular migration pathways as well as improved data sharing and cooperation between nations.  The International Migration Review Forum (IMRF) aims to address these issues by fostering collaboration and prioritizing actions such as expanding safe and regular pathways, strengthening fair recruitment practices, investing in data systems, and combating criminal networks.

articles.title: Rebel Wilson is a ‘fantastical liar’ who ‘made up terrible allegations against multiple people’, court told | Rebel Wilson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rebel Wilson is facing a defamation lawsuit from Charlotte MacInnes, the lead actress in her film, "The Deb."  MacInnes's lawyer, Sue Chrysanthou SC, accused Wilson of fabricating claims and rewriting history. Chrysanthou argued that Wilson lied about receiving a complaint from MacInnes and sought to undermine her relationships with others. The court heard inconsistencies in Wilson's testimony, which was contradicted by witnesses. MacInnes's lawyer also highlighted the negative impact of the social media posts on MacInnes's career and mental health.

articles.title: Oil prices rise after US and Iran exchange fire in Hormuz strait
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices rose on Friday following a military exchange between the US and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz. The US military claimed to have intercepted Iranian attacks, including missiles, drones, and small boats, and responded with self-defense strikes.  The US President Donald Trump stated that negotiations with Iran are ongoing despite the incident, while Iran accused the US of violating a ceasefire agreement by targeting its ships. The situation is currently described as "back to normal" according to Iranian state media.

articles.title: J&K Lieutenant Governor given telecom control powers during public safety events - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The President of India has authorized the Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor to exercise powers related to telecom services in the Union Territory during public safety events or national emergencies. These powers include interception of signals, suspension of service, and decryption of messages, as outlined in the Telecommunications Act, 2023. The order was published in the gazette on Thursday (May 7, 2026).

articles.title: Pakistan remains ‘positive’ as Iran mulls peace offer - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and Iran agreed to continue dialogue and diplomacy for ending the war in the Persian Gulf, expressing optimism that the US and Iran could soon reach a peace agreement.  Ishaq Dar, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, spoke with Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, who briefed him on his recent visit to China and consultations on regional and international issues. The two foreign ministers exchanged views on regional developments and ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at promoting peace and stability.  Iran is expected to formally communicate its response to the US proposal for ending hostilities by May 8th. Tahir Andrabi, a spokesperson for the Foreign Office of Pakistan, expressed optimism that an agreement would be reached soon, hoping for a peaceful and sustainable solution.

articles.title: Communications minister Anika Wells repays $10,000 in incorrect travel expenses | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anika Wells, the communications minister, repaid over $10,000 in incorrect travel claims identified by an audit. The audit found four mistakes dating back to 2022, totaling $8,092.89, and she has paid a 25% penalty loading for the errors.  Prime Minister Anthony Albanese defended Wells, stating she had referred herself to the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority and repaid the money in accordance with the rules. He also noted that Wells apologized for the mistakes.

articles.title: US to revoke passports of parents with child support debt
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department announced it will begin revoking passports of American parents with child support debt exceeding $2,500. The department stated this action aims to enforce legal obligations and support the welfare of children by exacting consequences for delinquency under existing federal law.  Those whose passports are revoked won't be eligible for a new one until their debt is paid.

articles.title: Silver gains Rs 2,361, gold near Rs 1.53 lakh amid hopes of Iran peace talks. What should investors do? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump made statements on Truth Social regarding the U.S.-Iran confrontation, claiming that U.S. forces had destroyed Iranian targets and warned of further military action if a nuclear agreement is not reached.  The situation influenced precious metal markets, with spot gold rising 0.7% to $4,719.85 per ounce and silver climbing 1.6% to $79.74 per ounce. Manoj Kumar Jain of Prithvi Finmart suggested that gold and silver prices remain volatile due to factors like the dollar index, crude oil prices, and upcoming U.S. non-farm payroll data.

articles.title: Akaash Singh: Why did Akaash Singh leave Flagrant? Andrew Schulz confirms heartbreaking podcast exit after nine years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Akaash Singh is stepping away from the Flagrant podcast after a decade, focusing on his stand-up comedy career.  Andrew Schulz, Singh's longtime friend and co-host, announced the decision during the May 6, 2026 episode, noting that Singh had recently achieved significant success with sold-out tours and performances. Schulz expressed bittersweet emotions about Singh's departure but acknowledged his friend's desire to prioritize his dream of becoming a successful stand-up comedian.

articles.title: T.N. Government formation LIVE: CPI, CPI(M), VCK hold the key to any further churn in State politics - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, the Tamil Nadu Governor, informed C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), that the requisite majority support for forming a government has not been achieved in the state assembly.  Vijay and senior party leaders have reached out to DMK allies, including the Communist Party of India, CPI(M), and Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, who hold the key to further political developments. M.K. Stalin, the outgoing Chief Minister, reportedly met with these parties to discuss the possibility of supporting an AIADMK-led government.

articles.title: ‘Saudi pressure’ led US to pause Hormuz project: NBC - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump paused a US operation to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz following pressure from Saudi Arabia.  The operation, dubbed "Project Freedom," was announced on social media and began on Monday, surprising Gulf allies. Saudi Arabia suspended access to its bases and airspace needed for the mission in response to the announcement. The White House has since paused the operation to restore access, but a Saudi source insists that communication between the two countries has been ongoing.

articles.title: Seafarers trapped in limbo as US and Iran clash in Strait of Hormuz | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran remain at odds in the Strait of Hormuz, leaving an estimated 20,000 seafarers stranded.  The situation has worsened since Iran closed the waterway in retaliation for US and Israeli attacks on the country. While a ceasefire was announced on April 7th, maritime traffic remains stalled due to recurrent attacks. Seafarers have reported dwindling food supplies, fear of Iranian drone strikes, and difficulty getting paid. The United Nations International Maritime Organization has called the situation an unprecedented humanitarian crisis.  The US Navy has attempted to guide ships out of the strait but suspended operations after less than 48 hours. Clearing mines laid by Iran in and around the waterway could take weeks or months.

articles.title: IS-linked Australian mother and daughter remanded in custody over Syrian slavery charges | Australian security and counter-terrorism | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kawsar Ahmad and her daughter Zeinab Ahmad, both Australian women, were charged with crimes against humanity including enslavement and slave trading in a Melbourne court. The pair are accused of traveling to Syria in 2014 with their family and keeping an enslaved woman in their home.  They also face charges related to the purchase of another enslaved woman for US$10,000. Janai Safar, a third woman, was charged in Sydney with entering a declared conflict zone and joining a terrorist organization. Both women were remanded in custody while awaiting bail applications. The Australian Federal Police (AFP) allege that these offenses are terrorism-related.

articles.title: World Cup fans in China and India face broadcast uncertainty
articles.rephrased_article: Fifa is facing uncertainty over broadcast deals for the 2026 World Cup in India and China, with local media reporting ongoing negotiations between Fifa and broadcasters regarding fees.  Fifa has reportedly offered lower prices to both countries, but these are still higher than the budgets of state-controlled broadcasters. A total of 180 territories have secured broadcast rights for the tournament, including China and India which together represent a third of the world's population.

articles.title: BSE shares fall 3% despite Q4 profit surge. Should you buy, sell or hold India’s oldest stock exchange? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BSE's Q4FY26 revenue surged 85% year-on-year to Rs 1,564 crore, driven by a significant increase in transaction charges.  The company reported a 32% sequential profit growth, reaching Rs 602 crore from the previous quarter. BSE's EBITDA margin stood at 48%, while they expect continued growth in monthly contract volumes and larger contract sizes to help lower clearing charges.  Nuvama Institutional Equities maintains a "Buy" rating on BSE, projecting an upside potential of 15%.

articles.title: Us Iran Ceasefire: US, Iran weigh 30-day ceasefire plan, reopening Strait of Hormuz; n-talks still in limbo - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and the US are discussing a temporary framework that would pause hostilities, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and create space for broader nuclear negotiations. The proposed framework includes lifting the US blockade on Iranian shipping, reopening the Strait to commercial traffic, and ending military hostilities under a ceasefire agreement.  Discussions remain ongoing with negotiators exchanging proposals on a long-term agreement, but key sticking points include sanctions relief, Iran's nuclear program, and the release of frozen assets.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Class 12 board exam results: How to check? - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Tamil Nadu Class 12 board exam results
articles.rephrased_article: The Directorate of Government Examinations, Tamil Nadu, announced the Class 12 examination results on May 8, 2026. Students can access their results online through tnresults.nic.in and dge.tn.gov.in.  They can also check their results via WhatsApp by saving the number +91-7845252525 and sending a "Hi" message with their registration number and date of birth. Additionally, students can download their marksheets through DigiLocker by following specific steps outlined in the article.

articles.title: US and Iran exchange fire, but Trump says ceasefire still in effect - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and Iran exchanged fire on Thursday, the most serious breach of their month-long ceasefire.  Iran claimed to have targeted US ships in the Strait of Hormuz while the US responded with strikes on Iranian territory. Despite the exchange, both sides expressed a desire to avoid escalation.  Trump, who was inspecting renovations at the Lincoln Memorial's reflecting pool, stated that negotiations with Iran remained ongoing despite the incident.

articles.title: Oil prices jump as US, Iran trade fire in Strait of Hormuz | Oil and Gas News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged after clashes between the United States and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global oil supplies. Brent crude futures rose as much as 7.5 percent before easing, reaching $101.12 per barrel. The US Central Command (CENTCOM) launched strikes on Iran after Iranian missiles, drones, and small boats attacked three US Navy destroyers in the strait. Iran’s military headquarters accused the US of violating a ceasefire by attacking Iranian vessels, while President Donald Trump said the truce remained in effect.

articles.title: Water flows to parched NSW wetlands could be turned back on within weeks as drought fears loom | Murray-Darling Basin | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Water Minister Rose Jackson introduced legislative amendments to allow for the resumption of environmental flows in the Gwydir region after a halt due to flooding concerns. The changes, passed by the NSW Upper House, were supported by the Greens and some crossbench MPs and aim to protect WaterNSW from civil liability claims related to water management operations.  The move comes as a result of devastating impacts on wildlife and landholders, including turtle rescues and bird deaths, due to the lack of environmental flows. The situation has been exacerbated by NSW experiencing its second driest April on record, with the Murray-Darling basin also experiencing drought conditions. A former environmental water manager called for an investigation into the state environment and water department's management of flows to the Gwydir area.

articles.title: Trump says US-Iran ceasefire still in place after exchange of fire in Strait of Hormuz
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated that a ceasefire between the US and Iran remains in place despite an exchange of fire in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's military command accused the US of attacking Iranian vessels, while Centcom described the attacks as "unprovoked".  The US claims to have inflicted damage on Iranian forces and defended its actions as self-defense. The situation remains tense with both sides threatening escalation if their respective conditions for a peace deal are not met.

articles.title: Several drugs consignments recovered along Gujarat coast - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Security agencies and police in Gujarat have recovered several consignments of suspected charas from coastal areas, prompting intensified surveillance along the state's maritime border.  The BSF, a security force, recovered ten packets of contraband in Kutch on Wednesday (May 6, 2026), while police found around 4 kg of charas near Kalyanpur in Devbhumi Dwarka district. Officials suspect smugglers abandoned these packages after increased patrols and investigations are underway to identify those involved.

articles.title: 'We’ll knock them out harder': Trump warns Iran of harsher military action after 3 US ships came under fire in Hormuz - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump claimed that three US naval destroyers, while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz, came under fire from Iranian forces but suffered no damage.  He warned Iran of stronger military action if it does not agree to sign a deal quickly. The incident followed reports of military exchanges in and around the Strait of Hormuz, where US Central Command stated American forces targeted Iranian facilities responsible for attacks against US warships.

articles.title: ICE in Minnesota: 'I'd rather live in hiding,' Somali man at risk of deportation tells BBC
articles.rephrased_article: Following the end of a surge in immigration enforcement operations in Minnesota, fear remains among the Somali community. Abdi, a 23-year-old man who fled Somalia due to threats from al-Shabab, fears ICE raids and is living in hiding. The operation, which targeted undocumented immigrants, has led to the detention of some US citizens with Somali heritage and sparked criticism from lawmakers like Ilhan Omar and Jim Abeler.  The Trump administration's efforts to end Temporary Protected Status for Somalis have further exacerbated tensions, prompting concerns about the safety of those living in the country. Despite efforts by community leaders and faith groups to provide support and warn residents of potential raids, many remain fearful of ICE agents.

articles.title: GameStop CEO opens eBay storefront to pay for potential eBay acquisition | GameStop | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ryan Cohen, CEO of GameStop, is selling items on eBay to fund the company's proposed $55.5 billion acquisition of eBay.  Cohen initially posted a link to his eBay storefront and later had his account reinstated after it was suspended. Bidding for the items, including GameStop merchandise and vintage items, ends on May 13th.  Michael Burry, investor known for his role in "The Big Short", sold his shares of GameStop.

articles.title: Foreign remittances to Kerala stay resilient despite West Asia crisis - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Federal Bank and South Indian Bank reported quarter-on-quarter growth in non-resident deposits inflow, indicating the stability of Kerala's economy despite the Iran war. The rise is attributed to a 5.4% rupee depreciation between January and March, leading to higher remittances on the same base amount. While experts predict continued inflows due to people seeking to protect their finances, they warn that prolonged conflict could negatively impact these flows in the long run.

articles.title: Congress blocks Agra-Mumbai highway in Indore over farmers’ issues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress workers blocked the Agra-Mumbai National Highway in Indore, Madhya Pradesh on Thursday as part of a state-wide protest demanding attention to farmers' issues. Vikrant Bhuria, national president of the Adivasi Congress, accused the BJP government of neglecting farmer concerns and failing to guarantee minimum support prices (MSP). He also alleged irregularities within the soybean 'Bhavantar Yojana' and claimed that market yards were dominated by corporations.  The protest is expected to continue in phases.

articles.title: Fact check: Was Candace Owens arrested on harassment charges after alleged Facebook threats? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer and Candace Owens escalated their online rivalry into a personal attack after Loomer resurfaced an old newspaper clipping alleging Owens faced harassment charges as a teenager. Loomer accused Owens of hypocrisy, while Owens countered with accusations of stalking and doxxing. The feud has expanded to include family members and legal threats, highlighting the blurring lines between political debate and personal warfare in the digital age.

articles.title: Anti-war protests rock Japan as PM Sanae Takaichi pushes for stronger defence
articles.rephrased_article: Sanae Takaichi, the Japanese Prime Minister, has taken steps to revise Japan's pacifist stance, lifting restrictions on arms exports and expanding Japan's military role abroad. This move has sparked large-scale anti-war protests across Japan, with residents expressing concerns about a potential shift towards war and questioning the future of Japan's pacifist identity enshrined in its 1947 constitution.  The protests highlight a growing divide within the country as some advocate for a stronger military to deter aggression while others fear it could draw Japan into conflicts overseas. The debate reflects a complex history shaped by past wars, including the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

articles.title: ‘The greatest ambassador for life on Earth’: Tributes paid to David Attenborough on his 100th birthday | David Attenborough | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Attenborough celebrated his 100th birthday with a live event at the Royal Albert Hall, featuring music from his programs and reflections from prominent figures.  Tributes poured in from scientists, politicians, and celebrities, recognizing his impact on wildlife conservation and global appreciation for nature. The Natural History Museum named a new species of wasp after him, while Kew Gardens and the Australian Museum also honored Attenborough's legacy with exhibitions.

articles.title: Retail stake cut in 284 BSE 500 companies in Q4 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Retail investors reduced holdings in 65% of companies with a market cap of ₹25,000 crore or more and 60% of those below this threshold during the March quarter of FY26. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) increased stakes in 201 companies, surpassing the previous quarter's reading, while domestic funds also saw an increase in holdings. Company promoters joined institutional investors by raising their shareholding in 42 companies, marking a high point in at least 12 quarters.

articles.title: Ally Cong. seeks ‘better coordination over crucial public issues’ with ruling NC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders in J&K have called for improved coordination between the party and the National Conference (NC), emphasizing the importance of mutual understanding and cooperation for effective governance.  Following disagreements over Statehood restoration, Ghulam Ahmad Mir, a senior Congress leader, stated that concerns and aspirations of the party must be respected to ensure the coalition's continued relevance. This comes after Dr. Farooq Abdullah, president of the NC, accused the Congress of not doing enough to restore Statehood.

articles.title: "He just kissed me": IShowSpeed left horrified as chaotic livestream moment explodes across social media - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed's Dominican Republic livestream was marred by a viral incident when a fan attempted to kiss him uninvited. Security intervened, and the moment sparked online debate about personal boundaries in streaming. The clip quickly spread on Reddit and X, with viewers discussing the streamer's reaction and security team's response. Fellow streamer xQc raised questions about unusually high concurrent viewership numbers for the stream, suggesting potential bot activity but not accusing IShowSpeed.

articles.title: Can China help end the Iran war? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: China is emerging as a key player in global diplomacy, particularly in the Middle East.  The country has recently helped re-establish diplomatic ties between Saudi Arabia and Iran. While not officially mediating the ongoing war between the two nations, both the United States and Iran are seeking China's assistance in de-escalating tensions. The program explores how China's economic influence could affect negotiations and its potential role in ending the conflict.

articles.title: Some 2,300 North Korean soldiers died in Russia-Ukraine war, new images show
articles.rephrased_article: A new memorial in Pyongyang, North Korea, honors the soldiers who died fighting for Russia in Ukraine. The memorial consists of two walls engraved with names of approximately 2,304 North Korean soldiers killed in the war.  The exact number of casualties remains unknown as neither Pyongyang nor Moscow has released official figures. The memorial is believed to be a way for the regime to justify its military cooperation with Russia and maintain public support. Kim Jong Un, the leader of North Korea, ordered the construction of the memorial, which includes outdoor graves, columbariums, and a housing complex for Russian war veterans and bereaved families.

articles.title: Trump-ally Roger Stone condemned for providing lobbying services to Myanmar’s military junta | Roger Stone | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Roger Stone, a longtime ally of former President Donald Trump, has been condemned for accepting $50,000 a month to "rebuild" relations between Washington and Myanmar's military-backed government.  DCI Group, the firm Stone is listed as a consultant for, is accused by Justice for Myanmar, a civil society group, of profiting from a heavily sanctioned junta that has been accused of war crimes. The US has imposed sanctions on individuals and businesses linked to Myanmar's military in response to alleged atrocities against civilians.

articles.title: Foreign investors continue to pull out of financials in second half of April - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign investors withdrew a significant amount of money from the Indian stock market in April, particularly from the banking sector.  The outflows totaled ₹28,301 crore across 15 sectors during the second half of the month, with over 41% coming from financial institutions. Saurabh Patwa, head of equities and portfolio manager at Quest Investment Managers, attributed this trend to strong power demand driven by AI investments and the sector's resilience in times of uncertainty.

articles.title: Mumbai family deaths: Rat poison ingredient zinc phosphide found in viscera and watermelon sample - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Four members of the Dokadia family, residents of south Mumbai, died last month after consuming rat poison found in a watermelon. The Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) confirmed the presence of zinc phosphide in their viscera and stomach contents.  The police are investigating whether the family intentionally ingested the poison or if it was accidental. Further investigation is being conducted by the JJ Marg police station, which has recorded statements from family members and neighbors.

articles.title: “You will be dead forever”: Sneako posts disturbing messages after Australia reportedly issues lifetime ban against streamer - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nico ‘Sneako’ Kenn De Balinthazy, a controversial streamer, has sparked concern with a series of death-themed posts on X following his ban from Australia.  Australian officials banned Sneako after reports claimed he spread hate speech and was allegedly trying to incite violence. The streamer denied these claims, stating he returned to the United States voluntarily.  His recent posts have fueled speculation about his mental state, with some interpreting them as a cry for attention amidst controversy surrounding his Australia visit.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump says ceasefire still ‘in effect’ as Iran, US clash | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's military accused US forces of violating a ceasefire by targeting Iranian vessels and striking coastal areas. Iranian air defenses were also active over western Tehran, while US naval forces responded to attacks with strikes on Iranian facilities.  CENTCOM, the US military's Central Command, stated that its forces came under attack in the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Two Islamic-State linked Australian women charged with crimes against humanity
articles.rephrased_article: Two Australian women, Kawsar Ahmad and Zeinab Ahmad, were charged with crimes against humanity after returning from Syria. They are accused of keeping a female slave in their home and complicity in the purchase of the woman for $10,000. Janai Safar, another Australian woman, was also arrested and charged with entering a declared conflict zone and joining IS.  The Australian Federal Police (AFP) allege that these women travelled to Syria between 2014-2015 and are part of a larger group of Australians who were returned to the al-Roj camp in Syria after attempting to return to Australia. The AFP is continuing its investigation into all Australians who traveled to declared conflict areas.

articles.title: Solomon Islands to get new leader after PM ousted in no-confidence vote | Solomon Islands | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Solomon Islands prime minister Jeremiah Manele lost a no-confidence vote in parliament, ending his rule and paving the way for a new leader. Manele, who had been facing political turmoil since March, was ousted by a 27-seat majority coalition of opposition parties.  The move comes amid concerns about transparency and accountability within the government, particularly regarding spending on major events like the 2024 Pacific Games and last year's Pacific Islands Forum meeting. The International Monetary Fund had previously raised these issues in March. With a population of 850,000, the Solomons is strategically located and receives significant aid from both Australia and China.

articles.title: Gulf states urge UN action to ensure Strait of Hormuz safety | United Nations News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gulf states, including Qatar, Bahrain, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), are pushing a UN Security Council resolution demanding that Iran halt attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, disclose mines, and ensure humanitarian aid passage. The resolution threatens sanctions if Iran does not comply with these demands.  The Gulf states argue that maintaining freedom of navigation is crucial for global economic stability and security. They also urge Iran to participate in establishing a humanitarian corridor through the strait to deliver vital goods.

articles.title: US state department to start revoking passports of parents who owe child support | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department will begin revoking passports of thousands of parents who owe significant amounts in unpaid child support. The program, which began in 1998 and was expanded to cover those owing more than $2,500, is expected to impact approximately 2,700 American passport holders. The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will inform the state department of past-due payments exceeding $2,500, leading to the revocation of passports for parents who owe such amounts.  The State Department states that this program has been effective in encouraging parents to pay their child support debts.

articles.title: NASA’s new plasma engine could reduce travel time to Mars | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) successfully tested a lithium-fed magnetoplasmadynamic (MPD) thruster, achieving 120 kilowatts of power output. This advancement in space travel technology could significantly reduce travel time to Mars and increase cargo capacity for future missions by utilizing electromagnetic fields to accelerate ionised lithium plasma. The test results demonstrate the potential of this technology for handling the massive payload requirements of a crewed Mars mission, paving the way for more efficient nuclear-electric propulsion systems.

articles.title: Demand to streamline traffic, ensure commuter safety on Ernakulam Junction, Town station premises - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Commuters at Ernakulam Junction and Ernakulam Town railway stations are facing difficulties accessing the redeveloped facilities, despite the project being underway since 2023.  Passenger associations have criticized the lack of progress in streamlining traffic and pedestrian safety, demanding action from the Railways. The Railways plan to address these concerns by scaling down barricaded areas once structural work is complete, augmenting lighting, and raising the height of the fifth platform at Ernakulam Junction.

articles.title: Palestinians expose torture and sexual violence in Israeli detention | Sexual Assault News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Palestinians who were detained in Israeli prisons have shared disturbing accounts of torture, sexual violence, and physical abuse.  Former detainees, including Mohammed al-Bakri and Ahmed, described being stripped naked, subjected to sexual assault by soldiers, and enduring degrading treatment. The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor documented these cases as part of a broader pattern of systematic abuse within Israeli detention facilities. Kifaya Khraim, from the Women’s Centre for Legal Aid and Counselling, confirmed that allegations of torture and sexual violence are widespread among Palestinian detainees.

articles.title: ‘This is how we cement President Trump’s agenda’: Tennessee Republicans celebrate state’s new congressional maps – live | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Marsha Blackburn and Senator Bill Hagerty of Tennessee endorsed Republican candidate Brent Taylor for Congress in the newly drawn ninth district. The new map, which was passed by the Tennessee General Assembly, splits up Shelby County, home to Memphis, into three districts, effectively eliminating the state's only Democratic-majority Black congressional district.  The NAACP filed an emergency petition arguing that the redistricting violates the Tennessee Constitution and is a violation of voting rights. The lawsuit argues that the map was created with the intent to diminish the voting power of Black citizens. President Donald Trump met with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, discussing trade and tariffs.  The meeting was described as going well by both leaders. Republican lawmakers in South Carolina are extending their legislative session to redraw the state's congressional map, aiming to eliminate the only Democratic district.

articles.title: UK: Border force officer convicted in Chinese intelligence spying case - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Border Force officer, Chi Leung “Peter” Wai, and former Hong Kong police officer Chung Biu “Bill” Yuen were found guilty of assisting Chinese intelligence agents in spying on Hong Kong dissidents living in the UK.  Wai was convicted under the UK’s National Security Act for aiding a foreign intelligence service and misconduct in public office for misusing government computer systems. The jury also found Wai guilty of accessing sensitive immigration data while on sick leave or away from work, allegedly to identify activists linked to Beijing. Prosecutors alleged that Wai had previously served in the Royal Navy and Metropolitan Police before joining Border Force in 2020.  The investigation revealed a "shadow policing" network that gathered information on Hong Kong activists who sought refuge in Britain following Beijing's crackdown after the 2019 protests.

articles.title: Faced harassment from a group of men onboard Delhi-bound flight, alleges MP Mahua Moitra - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahua Moitra, a Trinamool Congress MP, alleged she was harassed by a group of men on an IndiGo flight to Delhi.  She shared video evidence of the incident and tagged Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu and IndiGo requesting action against those involved.  Moitra stated that she ignored the incident but later saw the video going viral and decided to publicly denounce it, adding she would file a formal complaint with the airline.

articles.title: Armed fighters kill at least 30 people in attacks in central Mali | Armed Groups News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Armed fighters affiliated with al-Qaeda killed at least 30 people in attacks on two villages in central Mali's Mopti region. The deadliest assault since a wave of coordinated attacks began last month, the attacks occurred on Wednesday and were reported by local sources, security officials, and aid workers.  The Malian army commander, Djibrilla Maiga, stated that while the threat is still present, the military is disrupting the attackers' maneuvers.

articles.title: Man charged after allegedly threatening Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alex Jenkinson, 39, of Stowmarket, Suffolk, has been charged with two counts of threatening behavior and failing to provide a blood sample after allegedly harassing Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor near his Sandringham Estate property.  The incident occurred on Wednesday evening when Mountbatten-Windsor was walking his dogs.  He reportedly fled in his car after the suspect attempted to chase him.  Jenkinson is due to appear at Norwich magistrates court on Friday.

articles.title: Afghanistan’s ‘one-kidney village’ where residents sold organs to survive | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: In 2022, Afghanistan's Herat region became known as the "one-kidney village" due to reports of residents selling kidneys to survive deepening poverty and hunger.  The crisis followed the Taliban's return to power and coincided with a severe economic collapse that led to widespread food insecurity and unemployment. While organ trading is illegal, enforcement was weak, leading to an increase in underground kidney sales, where donors received minimal compensation while buyers traveled for transplants. The practice highlighted the dire consequences of conflict, poverty, and economic breakdown on individuals' desperate survival choices.

articles.title: West Bengal Governor dissolves State Legislative Assembly - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. N. Ravi, the Governor of West Bengal, dissolved the state's Legislative Assembly on May 7, 2026, ending the 17th assembly term. The move follows the BJP's victory in the recent assembly elections, securing a majority and leading to the end of Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress rule.  The swearing-in ceremony for the new BJP government is scheduled for Saturday, May 9, 2026, at the Brigade Parade Grounds.

articles.title: Senators press US military on Israel’s displacement campaign in Lebanon | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Senators from the Democratic Party sent a letter to Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command (CENTCOM), raising concerns about the potential role of US military forces in supporting Israel's displacement campaign in Lebanon. The letter questioned whether the US has provided support for Israeli operations within designated "evacuation zones" and if intelligence sharing agreements have been violated.  The senators also expressed concern that these actions may violate international law. This comes as Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib introduced a War Powers resolution to end US involvement in the conflict, while Senator Bernie Sanders called for an end to US military aid to Israel.

articles.title: Man held over suspected weapon possession near Prince Andrew’s Sandringham home - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Norfolk Police arrested a man near the Sandringham residence of Prince Andrew on Wednesday evening for public order offenses and possessing an offensive weapon. The suspect was taken to King’s Lynn police station for questioning, with investigations continuing on Thursday.  The incident occurred near Sandringham Royal Parkland and Marsh Farm, where Prince Andrew is currently staying after reportedly leaving Royal Lodge in Windsor last year.

articles.title: Facing opposition, Ladakh administration says ‘stakeholders will be onboard on setting up a power corporation’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Territory (UT) administration officials in Ladakh have stated that they are committed to involving local stakeholders in any decision regarding the establishment of a power corporation. Ashish Kundra, Chief Secretary of Ladakh, clarified that this move is mandated by the Electricity Act, 2003, and aims to generate revenue for the region.  He assured the public that existing employees will remain government employees while future recruitments will be handled by the corporation. The administration also emphasized its commitment to protecting Ladakh's land and culture, stating there are no plans to disturb the Changtang region or disrupt traditional employment practices.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s Valverde hospitalised with head injury after Tchouameni fight | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid midfielder Federico Valverde was hospitalized with a head injury after a dressing room fight with teammate Aurelien Tchouameni.  The incident occurred the day after an earlier altercation between the pair and prompted disciplinary proceedings against both players. Real Madrid confirmed that Valverde sustained a head injury and will be sidelined for up to two weeks, but he is currently at home in good condition. The club also announced they are opening disciplinary proceedings against both players.  The incident comes amid a turbulent season for Real Madrid, which has seen manager Xabi Alonso sacked and the team struggling to secure trophies.

articles.title: Iran accuses US of violating ceasefire by targeting civilian areas and ships on strait of Hormuz | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and Iran exchanged fire in the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about the viability of a month-long ceasefire.  US Central Command (Centcom) reported destroying Iranian boats and intercepting missiles and drones while USS Truxtun, USS Rafael Peralta, and USS Mason transited the waterway. Iran's military accused the US of violating the ceasefire agreement by targeting civilian areas, including oil tankers and ships entering the strait.  Despite the renewed hostilities, Donald Trump stated that the ceasefire remained in place.

articles.title: Trump invites UFC fighters to Oval Office and unveils never-seen-before Freedom 250 White House fight belt | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump unveiled a custom championship belt for the upcoming "UFC Freedom 250" event, hosted in the Oval Office with UFC fighters Ilia Topuria, Justin Gaethje, Alex Pereira, and Ciryl Gane. The event is scheduled for June 14th, coinciding with both Flag Day and Trump's 80th birthday.  The card will feature a main fight between lightweight champion Topuria and interim champion Gaethje, along with another bout between former middleweight and light heavyweight champion Pereira and heavyweight contender Gane. The event is part of the US's 250th anniversary celebrations.

articles.title: Former Rajasthan Minister Mahesh Joshi arrested in Jal Jeevan Mission scam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajasthan’s Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested Congress leader and former Minister Mahesh Joshi in connection with the alleged Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) scam.  The arrest follows the April 2025 arrest of retired IAS officer Subodh Agarwal, who was also accused of involvement in the scheme's irregularities. The ACB claims that Mr. Joshi misused his position as a Minister and accepted bribes to award fraudulent tenders worth ₹960 crore. He has been remanded to ACB custody until May 11th after being arrested from his residence.

articles.title: Barcelona vs Real Madrid: El Clasico – La Liga, history, Valverde, Mbappe | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Barcelona and Real Madrid will clash in Sunday's La Liga match, with Barcelona seeking to secure their title while Real Madrid faces a demoralizing defeat. The highly anticipated El Clasico has historical significance as the two Spanish giants have contested 264 matches since their first encounter in 1902.  Kylian Mbappe's availability for the game is uncertain due to a hamstring injury, and Federico Valverde will miss the match after an altercation with teammate Aurelien Tchouameni.  The rivalry between the two clubs has been recognized as one of the fiercest in world sport, with Barcelona and Real Madrid each having won 105 and 106 El Clasico matches respectively.

articles.title: Trump gives EU until 4 July to ratify trade deal or face ‘much higher’ tariffs | Trump tariffs | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump threatened to increase tariffs on European goods if the European Union does not ratify its trade deal by July 4th.  The EU has made progress towards ratification, but member states must still approve the agreement. Trump criticized the EU for failing to meet their end of the bargain and accused them of delaying implementation despite a previous agreement. The deal was struck last year with tariffs set at 15% on most goods.

articles.title: Historic Oxford cinema under threat as Oriel College refuses to extend lease | Heritage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Ultimate Picture Palace (UPP), a historic independent cinema in Oxford, is facing closure due to its landlord, Oriel College, refusing to extend its lease. The UPP has been struggling financially with increased operating costs and needs renovations to improve energy efficiency and accessibility.  Micaela Tuckwell, the UPP's executive director, has expressed concern about the lack of extension and called for support from the community and institutions like Historic England. A campaign to save the cinema has garnered over 22,000 signatures and local MP Anneliese Dodds is advocating for its preservation.  The future of the UPP remains uncertain as negotiations between the college and the cinema continue.

articles.title: Seeking a new paradigm for Dravidian exceptionalism - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. Joseph Vijay, a cinema superstar, won the recent Tamil Nadu State Assembly election with his party, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), securing 108 seats out of 234. This victory marks a significant shift in political landscape as it reflects dissatisfaction with both the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK).  Vijay's win signals a desire for enlightened leadership that prioritizes Tamil exceptionalism and delivers quality governance.

articles.title: Tennessee woman pleads guilty to $6.9 million Medicare fraud through false billing over three years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Helen Boerman, a 48-year-old Tennessee optometrist, pleaded guilty to a multimillion-dollar healthcare fraud scheme that defrauded Medicare and other government programs of millions of dollars.  She admitted to submitting false claims for wound care treatments and creating false documentation to justify additional charges over a three-and-a-half year period. United States Attorney Braden Boucek stated that the case demonstrates the Department of Justice's commitment to investigating fraud and holding accountable those responsible. Boerman faces a maximum penalty of five years in federal prison at her sentencing on September 10, 2026.

articles.title: Trump sets July 4 deadline for EU tariff hike decision | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced a July 4th deadline for the European Union to finalize a trade deal, threatening to increase tariffs on EU goods if they fail to comply.  The announcement followed a phone call with Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission. The US president stated that the EU had promised to cut tariffs to zero under the agreement reached in Scotland.

articles.title: Prisoner accused of Lostprophets singer’s murder boasted to guards about fame, court told | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rico Gedel and Samuel Dodsworth are accused of murdering Ian Watkins, a former singer for the band Lostprophets, in prison.  Gedel allegedly stabbed Watkins with a homemade knife in his cell at HMP Wakefield, where he was serving a 29-year sentence for child sexual offences. Gedel told guards that he thought Watkins was "famous" and claimed to be jealous of prisoners who were treated more leniently than sex offenders. The attack occurred after prison officers unlocked the cells on B wing, and Gedel left his cell shortly before Watkins emerged from his cell with blood visible on his neck.  The trial continues.

articles.title: Health authorities sound caution over mosquito-borne diseases - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. R. Shahirsha, District Medical Officer of Ernakulam, has warned that mosquito-borne diseases like dengue, chikungunya, and malaria are still present in the district despite a lower incidence compared to last year. Dr. Reshmi Ramachandran, Associate Professor at Government Medical College, Ernakulam, highlighted the challenge of imported malaria cases among migrant laborers and the lack of structured screening processes.  Dr. Rajany Jose, Associate Professor in Community Medicine at the same college, emphasized the importance of vigilance during summer months due to potential breeding grounds created by water storage and intermittent rains.

articles.title: US to revoke passports of thousands of parents over unpaid child support, starting with debts above $100,000 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department will begin revoking passports of thousands of American parents who owe large sums in unpaid child support starting Friday. The move, part of the Passport Denial Program created in 1996, targets individuals with debts exceeding $100,000 and is expected to expand to include those owing more than $2,500.  The program aims to encourage payment of outstanding child support and has already collected millions of dollars in unpaid support since its inception. Parents whose passports are revoked will be notified that their documents are no longer valid for international travel and must clear their debts before reapplying.

articles.title: Iran says it attacked US Navy ships after they targeted Iranian tanker | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy claimed responsibility for retaliating against US Navy ships after the US targeted an Iranian oil tanker in its territorial waters, citing violations of a ceasefire. The Iranian military stated that the US also carried out air strikes on civilian areas and that the response caused “significant damage” to US vessels.  The US Central Command (CENTCOM) countered that it intercepted unprovoked Iranian attacks and responded with self-defense strikes, emphasizing its commitment to protecting American forces without seeking escalation.

articles.title: Polls close in elections across England, Scotland and Wales | May 2026 elections | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Local, mayoral, and parliamentary elections took place across England, Scotland, and Wales on Thursday.  Reform UK, the Green party, and the Liberal Democrats are expected to make significant gains at the expense of the two biggest parties in England, while Labour faces potential record-breaking losses. The first results are anticipated around 12:30 am with further updates throughout Friday. The outcome will have implications for the prime minister and could reshape the political landscape.

articles.title: Wu Yize cheered by crowds on return home from World Snooker Championship
articles.rephrased_article: Wu Yize, the 22-year-old Chinese snooker champion, returned to his hometown of Xi'an after winning the World Snooker championship for the second year in a row.  He was greeted by enthusiastic crowds at the TNT billiards club, where he showcased his skills and received praise from fans like Liu YiFei, who had won an earlier play-off against him. The sport is experiencing a surge in popularity across China, with an estimated 60 million people playing billiards annually, and many young players aspire to follow in Wu Yize's footsteps.  This success is partly attributed to the sport's affordability and the inspiring story of his journey from a humble background in Gansu province.

articles.title: A year after Operation Sindoor: Two schools in Jammu and Kashmir stand testimony to the cost of conflict - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Christ High School in Poonch, Jammu & Kashmir, and Madrasa Taleem ul Quran in Pulwama district are struggling to recover from the devastation caused by the four-day conflict between India and Pakistan last year. The schools experienced shelling, a blast, and power outages during Operation Sindoor, resulting in the deaths of students and damage to their infrastructure.  The principal of Christ High School reported that students were traumatized by the events and required counseling. The coordinator of Madrasa Taleem ul Quran stated that the school received no compensation for the damage caused by an unidentified aerial object, despite seeking financial assistance from local officials.

articles.title: UFC sells $1.5 million White House tickets for ‘high rollers’ with access to McGregor’s 329 comeback fight | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UFC is hosting a historic event, "UFC Freedom 250," on the South Lawn of the White House in Washington D.C.  on June 14, 2026, as part of celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of the United States. The event will feature seven fights and is expected to draw a large crowd, including members of the military who will receive priority seating close to the cage. Dana White, president of the UFC, has described the event as a historic spectacle unlike anything previously attempted in mixed martial arts.  Donald Trump, who is hosting the event, has also emphasized that it is intended to be accessible to the public with free tickets available for fans.

articles.title: Can Trump’s push for a deal with Iran turn a tactical pause into lasting peace? - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is considering a diplomatic exit from its confrontation with Iran, despite officials claiming the US holds the upper hand.  This shift comes after President Trump paused a naval operation aimed at escorting commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, prompting debate over whether Washington seeks a negotiated settlement or simply recalibrates pressure before renewed escalation.  Vali Nasr, an Iranian-American scholar and professor at Johns Hopkins University's School of Advanced International Studies, argues that the administration may be attempting to wind down the confrontation without achieving its stated objectives. Richard Haass, an American diplomat and former president of the Council on Foreign Relations, advocates for a phased approach focused on maritime stability, suggesting Iran should reopen the Strait of Hormuz as a shared waterway with oversight mechanisms. Senator Jack Reed has criticized the lack of clarity in US policy, highlighting inconsistencies in operational decisions and transparency concerns.

articles.title: Tennessee approves new congressional map in latest redistricting flurry | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tennessee's Republican-dominated legislature and governor approved a new congressional map ahead of the US midterms, splitting the state’s only Black majority district. The approval followed the US Supreme Court ruling that weakened the Voting Rights Act, making it easier for states to draw maps that favor their party. Opponents argue the new map is racially motivated, while Republicans maintain the districts were drawn based on population and politics. It remains unclear if other states will redraw their maps before the November elections.

articles.title: US trade court rules against Trump’s 10% global tariffs | Trump tariffs | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Court of International Trade ruled against Donald Trump's 10% global tariffs, finding the tariffs were not justified under a 1970s trade law. The ruling favored small businesses who challenged the tariffs and was decided by a 2-1 vote.  Trump has threatened to raise tariffs on EU goods if they do not comply with trade agreements by July 4th.

articles.title: Five killed in huge fire at packed Mexico fairground
articles.rephrased_article: A massive fire broke out at a crowded fairground in Villahermosa, Tabasco state, Mexico, during a concert on Thursday morning.  El País reported that the blaze claimed the lives of at least five people and left an estimated 135,000 attendees fleeing in panic. Javier May, the governor of Tabasco, confirmed the fire was extinguished by emergency services and expressed condolences to the victims' families while announcing a recovery program for affected businesses.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks if there was a 'proper debate' in Parliament before enacting CEC/EC appointments law - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court questioned whether there was a proper debate in Parliament regarding the 2023 judgment that shifted Election Commission appointments from solely executive control to a more participatory process.  Justice Dipankar Datta, leading the bench, expressed uncertainty about the reflection of the court's ethos in parliamentary discussions. Senior advocate Shadan Farasat argued that Opposition MPs were suspended before debate, hindering a proper discussion. Advocate Prashant Bhushan from the Association for Democratic Reforms highlighted concerns over insufficient safeguards against CEC removal and advocated for independent and transparent appointments.  Advocate Kaleeswaram Raj, representing activist C.R. Neelakandan, emphasized the Supreme Court's emphasis on free and fair elections as a cornerstone of democracy.

articles.title: Donald Trump criticised for politicising statement after death of WCW and CNN founder Ted Turner | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump paid tribute to Ted Turner, the founder of CNN, on Truth Social following his death.  The statement drew criticism online for including political commentary about CNN's new ownership and its perceived "woke" nature. Many users criticized Trump for using Turner's passing as an opportunity to attack CNN.  Turner's legacy extends beyond media, with his impact on professional wrestling through the creation of WCW Monday Nitro being particularly significant.

articles.title: 3 children killed, several injured in South Waziristan attack: security sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Two separate attacks in South Waziristan, Pakistan, on Thursday resulted in the deaths of three children and injuries to several others. Fitna al Khawarij, a term used for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, carried out an explosion near a civilian settlement, killing three children and injuring others.  Afghan Taliban forces also fired mortar shells at a market in Angoor Adda, injuring ten people. Security sources condemned both attacks as violations of international law and human rights, emphasizing the threat they pose to peace and stability in the region.

articles.title: US trade court rules against Trump’s 10 percent global tariffs | Trade War News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Court of International Trade ruled against President Donald Trump's 10 percent global tariffs, finding the tariffs were not justified under a 1970s trade law. The ruling was 2-1 in favor of small businesses who challenged the tariffs, which took effect on February 24th.  The court determined that Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, invoked by Trump to justify the tariffs, was not an appropriate step for the trade deficits cited in his order. The ruling is seen as a victory for American companies and businesses reliant on global manufacturing.

articles.title: Australia news live: woman to appear in court charged with joining Islamic State | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jane Hume, deputy leader of the opposition, criticized the Albanese government for its handling of a group of women and children with links to Islamic State who returned to Australia.  Katy Gallagher, finance minister, stated that the government had managed the situation appropriately and emphasized support for reintegrating these children into Australian society. Matt Canavan, Nationals leader, expressed concern about the risk posed by these individuals and urged the government to utilize available powers to prevent their entry. Tony Burke, home affairs minister, defended the government's decision not to impose temporary exclusion orders, citing a high threshold for such actions.  Meanwhile, Jess Wilson, Victorian opposition leader, announced a hiring freeze in back-office public service roles to address state debt.

articles.title: Trump threatens 'much higher' tariffs on EU by 4 of July
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump threatened to increase tariffs on European goods by 4 July unless the European Union drops its levies on US products to zero.  Ursula von der Leyen, President of the European Commission, stated that the bloc was making "good progress" towards tariff reduction, but negotiations remain ongoing. The trade deal, struck last year, would have seen a 15% tariff on US exports from the EU, with Trump previously threatening tariffs as high as 30%.  The agreement requires approval from both the European Parliament and member states.

articles.title: Pakistani green card holder spent 21 years behind bars for murder in New York, arrested again by ICE after release - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Farhan Ahmed, a Pakistani national, was arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in New York City on May 1st.  Ahmed had previously been convicted of first-degree manslaughter with intent to cause serious physical injury in Queens after committing a violent offense shortly after obtaining permanent residency in the US. He served nearly two decades in prison before being released in 2023. ICE is currently holding Ahmed as immigration proceedings continue, and he is among several foreign nationals arrested under a new enforcement initiative targeting individuals with criminal records.

articles.title: How worried should we be about getting Hantavirus?
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) are closely monitoring a hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship, the MV Hondius.  Three passengers have died from the virus, with four others medically evacuated for treatment. The outbreak is believed to be linked to rodent exposure, although human-to-human transmission is possible. WHO officials stress that the risk to the general public remains low, and contact tracing efforts are underway to identify potential exposures. Passengers who disembarked in St Helena and other locations have been contacted and monitored for symptoms.

articles.title: Masood expresses confidence in bowling as Pakistan set to face Bangladesh in first Test tomorrow - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Test captain Shan Masood expressed confidence in his bowling attack ahead of the first Test against Bangladesh, emphasizing the importance of taking 20 wickets.  He acknowledged the home team's quality across all departments and highlighted the squad's experience playing in both seam-friendly and spin-friendly conditions. Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto stressed the need for big first-innings totals to support their potent pace attack, which includes returning star Taskin Ahmed. The series will be played over two matches in Mirpur (May 8-12) and Sylhet (May 16-20).

articles.title: Woman killed by partner at home in London feared ‘he was on the warpath’, court hears | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Clifton George, 45, is accused of murdering his partner Annabel Rook, 46, during an argument in their London home last June.  Rook told her father and sister that she feared further violence from George who had been bullying her and exhibiting rages over trivial matters. The court heard that Rook planned to offer George £50,000 to move out of the couple's shared home before he allegedly attacked her with a knife, strangled her, and set fire to the basement.  George has pleaded guilty to manslaughter but not murder, while his lawyer argues it was due to a loss of self-control. The trial continues.

articles.title: IMF warns of 'inevitable' AI-powered threats to world - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) warned of the potential risks to global financial stability posed by advanced AI-powered cyberattacks. The IMF's report highlights the interconnected nature of the global financial system and how advanced AI models can rapidly exploit vulnerabilities, potentially leading to funding strains, solvency concerns, and market disruptions. This warning comes after Anthropic, an AI company, cautioned about its "Mythos" model's ability to identify previously unknown vulnerabilities.

articles.title: ‘This is my last voice note’: how piracy returned to Somalia and Yemen | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Three ships have been hijacked near the Gulf of Aden and off the coast of Yemen since April 20th, raising concerns about a resurgence in piracy. A sailor's voice note from one of the seized vessels has emerged online, fueling speculation about potential links to regional conflicts like the ongoing Iran war.  The situation highlights the vulnerability of key shipping routes in the region.

articles.title: Residents apprehend vehicle dumping of sludge in open plots in Ranipet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Edakuppam village in Ranipet blocked a tractor carrying sludge, protesting against illegal dumping on open plots near their water bodies. The residents, who rely on groundwater for agriculture and drinking water, expressed concerns about health risks, pollution, and mosquito breeding grounds caused by the waste.  They also alleged that local civic bodies have ignored repeated complaints regarding this issue.

articles.title: Saahas Kaul and Neha Suratran: Indian-origin duo explain why people are speaking against India at Frisco city council meetings - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saahas Kaul and Neha Suratran, Indian-American activists, spoke out against anti-India rhetoric at Frisco city council meetings. They argue that the claims of an "Indian takeover" are misleading and driven by a small group seeking social media attention rather than genuine concern for immigration policy.  Kaul believes these individuals target H-1B visa holders because they fear retaliation from those who rely on their jobs, while Suratran highlights the contributions Indian-Americans make to the US economy and society.

articles.title: Real Madrid: Valverde taken to hospital after incident with Tchouameni - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Valverde, a Real Madrid midfielder, was taken to the hospital with a head injury following an alleged altercation with teammate Tchouameni. The incident occurred after training and led to disciplinary proceedings being opened by the club.  The club confirmed that Valverde has been diagnosed with cranioencephalic trauma, a type of concussion.  Real Madrid will provide updates on the situation once internal procedures are complete.

articles.title: 4 children killed, 20 people injured as roof of classroom collapses in Dera Ghazi Khan school - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: At least four children and 20 others were injured when the roof of a classroom at a private school in Dera Ghazi Khan, Punjab, collapsed on Thursday. The incident occurred around noon, prompting a rescue operation involving Rescue 1122, district administration officials, and local residents.  The preliminary report attributed the collapse to an overloaded roof due to construction work being carried out during school hours. District Education Authority CEO Waqas Gill assured that the incident would be investigated and action taken against the school administration. Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has also taken notice of the incident.

articles.title: Tensions high in West Bengal after BJP aide shot dead and hundreds arrested | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following the BJP's victory in the West Bengal elections, Tensions have escalated with violence erupting and hundreds arrested.  Chandranath Rath, an aide to the BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, was shot dead, prompting accusations of political killings by the TMC, who allege widespread irregularities. The state police chief has registered over 200 criminal cases and arrested 433 individuals for their involvement in post-election violence.  The BJP denies all allegations of wrongdoing while the TMC vows to challenge the election results in the Supreme Court.

articles.title: US stocks today: US market ends lower as semiconductor stocks reverse earlier gains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The United States and Iran are nearing a temporary agreement to halt their war, with Tehran reviewing a proposal that would stop the fighting but leave unresolved contentious issues.  Despite this, U.S. stock markets experienced mixed results, with the S&P 500 falling slightly and the Nasdaq Composite experiencing minimal change. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also saw a decline. Investors remain optimistic about the economy's strong performance, fueled by robust earnings season and positive economic data.

articles.title: US issues new Cuba sanctions as UN experts warn of ‘energy starvation’ | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States imposed new sanctions on Grupo de Administracion Empresarial SA (GAESA), a military-controlled conglomerate in Cuba, targeting its executive president and a joint venture with Sherritt International Corp.  These sanctions come amidst criticism from UN experts, who labeled the US fuel blockade of Cuba as "energy starvation" and a violation of human rights.  US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that these actions demonstrate the Trump administration's commitment to holding Cuba accountable for its actions, while Cuba’s government condemned the sanctions as “unilateral coercive measures” and “collective punishment.

articles.title: Canada urged to act against ‘anti-India extremist elements’: MEA - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India called on Canada to take action against "anti-India extremist elements" operating from Canadian soil, citing a report by the Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS) that highlighted the national security threat posed by Khalistani extremists. The report acknowledged the presence of supporters of the Khalistan separatist movement in Canada and noted that these groups continue to pose a threat not only to India but also to Canada.  India reiterated its concerns about the misuse of Canadian territory as a "safe haven" for extremist and separatist elements, while rejecting claims of foreign interference by India.

articles.title: Hormuz technically open for ships, but risks too high, says Indian National Shipowners’ Association chief - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: India's Indian National Shipowners’ Association chief executive, Anil Devli, reports that while the Strait of Hormuz remains technically open, commercial shipping is significantly disrupted due to heightened tensions.  The incident where two Indian-flagged vessels were fired upon by Iranian forces has caused a significant decrease in confidence among seafarers and halted "normal traffic". Despite some neutral-flag vessels transiting with Iran's tacit permission or US protection, the situation remains uncertain for Indian ships.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: 'I wouldn't pay it', says US President Donald Trump on ticket price for USA game - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed his disapproval of the $1,000 ticket price for the USA's opening World Cup match in Los Angeles. Trump stated he wouldn't pay that amount and acknowledged the high cost of tickets overall, which has drawn criticism from fans and experts alike. Fifa president Gianni Infantino defended the pricing strategy, stating it aligns with other US sporting events and that higher prices are a result of ticket resale.  Infantino also noted that more affordable tickets were introduced in response to initial criticism.

articles.title: PTI says preparations for final round of movement against Imran's imprisonment underway - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI leaders, including Khurram Virk and Zahir Shah, attempted to meet Imran Khan at Adiala jail but were denied access.  Zahir Shah, speaking to the media, stated that the party will continue its movement against Khan's imprisonment and that obstacles are being deliberately created to damage the judiciary. The party expressed concern over the sudden transfer of Bushra Bibi to a hospital without informing her family or lawyers. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram condemned the secrecy surrounding the situation, claiming it violates basic human rights and raises serious questions about transparency.

articles.title: Two Britons evacuated from hantavirus-hit ship ‘improving’ in hospital | Hantavirus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two Britons who were evacuated from a hantavirus-stricken cruise ship are improving, according to Dr Maria Van Kerkhove of the World Health Organization (WHO).  The outbreak, linked to a birdwatching trip in South America, has resulted in five confirmed cases and three deaths. The ship is expected to arrive in Tenerife on Sunday. Oceanwide Expeditions, the tour operator, is cooperating with health officials, who are monitoring passengers for potential symptoms.  Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director-general of the WHO, stated that while the risk to the public is low, there could be more cases due to the incubation period of the virus.

articles.title: Yogi Adityanath launches first phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yogi Adityanath, the Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister, launched the first phase of Census-2027, a digital census aimed at supporting data-driven planning and welfare delivery. The exercise, running from May 7 to May 21, allows citizens to self-enumerate online before enumerators begin door-to-door verification across Uttar Pradesh.  The second phase will involve individual enumeration and caste enumeration, including coverage of forest villages for the first time.  Adityanath emphasized the importance of accurate census data for improving infrastructure, education, healthcare, social security, and welfare schemes.

articles.title: Finance ministry, SBP show optimism over economic growth amid expected $1.2bn tranche from IMF - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Finance and the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) expressed optimism over economic growth and achieving fiscal and current account targets despite regional challenges.  Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb reported that Pakistan received regulatory approval for a $750 million Eurobond from the international capital market last month, and is on track to achieve its key fiscal targets through prudent fiscal management and improved external account performance. Governor Jameel Ahmed stated that foreign exchange reserves are expected to exceed $17 billion by the end of the current fiscal year, enough for three months of import cover. The IMF Board is expected to approve Pakistan's economic review on Friday.

articles.title: Man pleads guilty to Colorado firebombing, groups call for family reprieve | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mohamed Soliman, an Egyptian citizen, pleaded guilty to murder charges in connection with a 2025 attack on demonstrators supporting Israeli captives in Gaza. The attack resulted in the death of Karen Diamond, an 82-year-old woman, and Soliman was sentenced to life in prison.  The family of Soliman, who have been detained by US immigration authorities, has condemned the attack and denied any knowledge of it. Lawmakers and community groups have called for the administration to cease efforts to deport Soliman's family.

articles.title: Iran conducting near-daily prisoner executions in secrecy, say rights groups | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has carried out near-daily executions of prisoners in secrecy, refusing to hand the bodies of the dead to families.  The Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHRNGO) reports at least 24 executions since March, with six carried out over two days. The recent surge has raised fears for hundreds believed to be facing the death penalty due to anti-government protests and espionage accusations during the war with US and Israel.
