Families of those executed have faced harassment and pressure to remain silent about the impact of state killings. Rights groups, including IHRNGO, have called on world powers to act, warning that hundreds may face charges punishable by death.

articles.title: Bangladesh seeks China support for Teesta restoration project - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh’s new government has sought China's involvement in the Teesta River restoration project, a move that could strain relations with India.  The Bangladesh government is seeking to increase its share of the river's water under the 2011 Teesta water-sharing treaty, which has been blocked by West Bengal’s outgoing Chief Minister, Mamata Banerjee.  China's Foreign Minister, Wang Yi, pledged support for Bangladesh's new government and its development goals.

articles.title: First phase of Guindy Eco-Park to be completed by October 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Horticulture and Plantation Crops is transforming the Guindy Race Course into an eco-park. The first phase includes creating ponds, deepening lakes, bio-swales, a viewing point, bridge access to an island, pathways, parking, and visitor amenities on 25 acres.  Avenue tree planting has been completed along internal pathways with native and ornamental species planted. The project also features a nursery selling seeds, saplings, plants, and gardening needs at affordable prices.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula meets Trump amid efforts to avert new US trade tariffs | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Brazilian president, met with Donald Trump, US president, at the White House to discuss trade, security, and critical minerals. The meeting aimed to mend their strained relationship after last year's tariff tensions and Bolsonaro's trial. Both leaders are populist figures who oppose established elites but differ on economic and international policy. While the meeting was seen as a positive step, concerns remain about potential new tariffs stemming from Section 301 investigations and trade disputes over digital trade and timber exports.

articles.title: Iran mocks Trump’s ‘Project Freedom’ as adversaries wrestle over talks to end war | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump abruptly ended the "Project Freedom" initiative, which aimed to secure safe passage for commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The operation was halted after Saudi Arabia refused to allow US military use of its bases or airspace. While both sides have offered different explanations for the decision, it appears that a lack of preparation and communication contributed to the failure.  The US plan has been reviewed by Iran, which is reportedly considering its response.

articles.title: Tenerife resident calls plan 'reckless' as hantavirus ship approaches
articles.rephrased_article: Monica Garcia, Spain's health minister, announced that the cruise ship MV Hondius will dock in Tenerife, Spain, after a three-day anchorage near Cape Verde. The ship, carrying passengers who have been affected by a hantavirus outbreak, will undergo medical assessments upon arrival and those deemed fit to travel will be repatriated. Residents of Tenerife expressed concern about potential exposure to the virus.

articles.title: 'This is all about election': Immigration attorneys on Ken Paxton's investigation into 30 H-1B 'ghost offices' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton announced an investigation into 30 North Texas businesses for alleged H-1B visa fraud, claiming they operate "ghost offices" with no H-1B workers. Immigration attorneys Rahul Reddy and Emily Neumann criticized the timing of the investigation, suggesting it is politically motivated to target Indian-origin businesses ahead of the upcoming election. They argue that Paxton's actions are fueled by a desire to appease his political rivals and further stoke anti-Indian sentiment in Texas.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu seeks postponement of DGP empanelment committee meeting - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government has requested the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) to postpone the Empanelment Committee Meeting (ECM) for a new Director General of Police, citing ongoing political developments and the need for key officials' presence in the state. The meeting was originally scheduled for May 11th, 2026, but the government requested a postponement to a later date, preferably in the last week of May. Sandeep Rai Rathore, the current DGP/HoPF, will continue to lead the force until a new chief is appointed as per Supreme Court guidelines.

articles.title: Pakistan turns down two lowest evaluated LNG bids - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan LNG Limited (PLL) rejected bids from BP Singapore and TotalEnergies for two LNG cargoes due to high prices. The state-run company received seven bids, with the lowest priced at $16.98 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).  These bids were submitted in response to urgent tenders floated amid rising temperatures and a power shortfall.

articles.title: Israel’s attacks and pressure sowing seeds for division in tense Lebanon | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's attacks on Lebanon, coupled with pressure on the Lebanese government to disarm Hezbollah, are exacerbating internal divisions. Analysts believe Israel is exploiting these tensions to force concessions from the Lebanese state.  The strategy involves targeting Shia communities and inciting sectarian conflict. While Hezbollah opposes direct negotiations with Israel, the Lebanese government faces pressure from both the US and Israel to engage in talks, potentially even a meeting between Israeli and Lebanese leaders. This has led to internal divisions within Lebanon, with some politicians and media outlets making provocative statements that fuel tensions between pro- and anti-Hezbollah factions.  Analysts believe Israel is hoping these divisions will force the Lebanese government into accepting its terms for peace.

articles.title: Trump shelved ‘Project Freedom’ after Saudis refused use of bases and airspace | Saudi Arabia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump shelved his plan for a US military escort of oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz after Saudi Arabia refused to allow its bases and airspace to be used. This decision, which was made despite a personal call between Mohammed bin Salman, the Saudi crown prince, and Trump, highlights Riyadh's desire for a permanent end to the war with Iran on any terms. The US faces criticism from both the UAE and Saudi Arabia over its handling of the conflict, which has caused damage to Gulf economies and international image.

articles.title: Superdry co-founder James Holder jailed for rape
articles.rephrased_article: James Holder, co-founder of the fashion company Superdry, was sentenced to eight years in prison for raping a woman in 2022. The victim's statement described the attack as a "living nightmare" and said it continues to impact her life.  Recorder David Chidgey stated that Holder's actions were fueled by entitlement and disregard for the victim's bodily autonomy. Superdry has confirmed Holder resigned from his roles with the company in 2016, and consultancy work ended in 2019. Gloucestershire Police commended the victim for her bravery and resilience.

articles.title: Nepal opposition wants PM Balendra Shah to hold Lipulekh talks with India - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nepali Congress-led opposition MPs urged the Balendra Shah government to initiate high-level talks with India and China regarding the disputed Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura, and Kalapani territories.  They argued that direct "table talks" were necessary to address Nepal's concerns over India using these areas for trade and the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra without consent. CPN (UML) MP Bhumika Limbu Subba criticized India’s response as irresponsible, while Maoist Centre MP Pramesh Kumar Hamal urged the government to consult other political forces.

articles.title: Telangana leads India in human trafficking cases, women form vast majority of victims - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana recorded the highest number of human trafficking cases in 2024, with 423 reported incidents, a significant increase from the previous year. This was followed by Maharashtra, Odisha, Bihar, and Karnataka.  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data revealed that sexual exploitation for prostitution was the primary motive behind trafficking in Telangana, accounting for 770 victims. The state also had the highest trafficking crime rate at 1.1 cases per lakh population, with a charge-sheeting rate of 99%.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz discusses regional situation with Qatari counterpart: PMO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Shehbaz Sharif spoke with Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, the Prime Minister of Qatar, on Thursday. The two leaders discussed regional peace efforts and reaffirmed their commitment to facilitating dialogue between parties in conflict.  They agreed to maintain close communication and coordination on all issues of mutual interest.

articles.title: Inside the Israeli bloc that could topple Netanyahu | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Former Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, along with other opposition figures, have united to challenge Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership in upcoming Israeli elections. Despite this alliance, deep divisions remain over key issues such as the ongoing war with Iran and Israel's future direction. The strength of the opposition's potential success remains uncertain.

articles.title: US and Iran close to temporary truce, Pakistani officials claim | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran officials are close to a temporary agreement to halt the war in the Middle East. A basic "interim" deal could be reached as early as this weekend, according to Pakistani diplomats who have been mediating between the two sides. While both sides remain skeptical about reaching a permanent end to hostilities, recent diplomatic activity has led to optimism that a partial agreement could be reached soon.  The US and Iran are seeking leverage in any talks through belligerent rhetoric and defiance, while global stocks surged on Thursday as oil prices dropped steeply due to the potential for an agreement.

articles.title: Donald Trump's 'irresponsible war' slowing economic momentum, warns German minister
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's actions in the region, including his "irresponsible war" in Iran, have been blamed by German finance minister Lars Klingbeil for a significant drop in projected tax revenues.  The downgrade reflects the impact of the conflict on Germany's economy, which is struggling with high energy costs and weak export demand. Friedrich Merz, the German Chancellor, has criticized Trump's policies and their effect on trans-Atlantic relations, while Trump himself has responded to Merz's comments, accusing him of being uninformed and suggesting he should focus on domestic issues.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran reviewing peace proposal as Trump says a deal ‘very possible’ | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Iran have offered conflicting messages over the state of negotiations to end the war.  Trump stated that talks were “very good” and a deal was “very possible,” while Iranian officials sought to dampen expectations, stating they are reviewing the US proposal and considering its response via Pakistani mediators. The United Arab Emirates will form a committee to document Iran’s attacks during the Middle East war to support legal action.  Israel has conducted strikes in Lebanon, killing Hezbollah commander and causing outrage from Lebanese authorities. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia rejected a report that President Trump paused an American military operation to guide stranded ships through the strait of Hormuz. The US and Iran have offered conflicting messages over the state of negotiations to end the war.  Lebanon and Israel will hold a new round of talks on 14-15 May in Washington on seeking a peace deal, despite a new Israeli strike against Hezbollah.

articles.title: B1/B2 visa update: US Consulate opens priority slots for parents aged 50 years and above - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US Consulate in Kolkata has introduced priority slots for parents aged 50 and above visiting their children in the US, alongside a new visa scheduling system for verified business travelers. The consulate calls this "American First in Family Values" and emphasizes supporting trade and economic growth between the two countries.  These changes come amid reports of increased denial rates for B1/B2 visas, with visa officers emphasizing stronger ties to India and reduced likelihood of settling permanently.

articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Haryana administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

articles.title: Govt mulls allowing commercial banks to take over mortgaged houses 90 days after default - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan government is considering amendments to the "Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001" that would allow commercial banks to take over mortgaged houses after a cumulative notice period of 90 days. The proposed law, currently under review by the National Assembly's Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, has raised concerns from members who believe it could grant banks excessive powers in foreclosure proceedings.  The committee recommended simplifying financing procedures, flexible eligibility criteria, and enhanced subsidy support for low-income households to improve accessibility and affordability of housing finance programs.

articles.title: US pushing Israeli de-escalation ahead of new talks: Lebanese official | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US officials are working to de-escalate the situation between Israel and Lebanon ahead of a second round of talks in Washington, DC. The discussions will focus on security and political issues, including a full Israeli withdrawal from southern Lebanon, borders, prisoners, displaced people, and reconstruction.  The talks are scheduled for May 17th, following an initial round in April that led to the current ceasefire but with attacks continuing. Lebanon is seeking a non-aggression pact rather than a peace agreement. The recent attack on Beirut's southern suburbs by Israel is seen as an attempt to obstruct negotiations.

articles.title: Disturbances and 127 arrests mar Paris party after PSG Champions League victory
articles.rephrased_article: Parisian celebrations following PSG's Champions League victory turned violent, resulting in 127 arrests and eleven injuries. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez condemned the disturbances, which included fires, tear gas use, and looting attempts. While more than 30 people were injured, a mortar firework caused serious harm to one individual. The violence was less severe than last year's final, but Nuñez warned of potential unrest during PSG's upcoming match in Budapest.

articles.title: Vatican stresses need for peace as Rubio meets pope amid strained relations | Pope Leo XIV | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, met with Pope Francis in Rome to discuss current events and the need for peace. The Vatican and the US State Department described the meeting as friendly and constructive, focusing on issues like war and humanitarian situations.  The talks come amid strained relations between Washington and the Vatican, exacerbated by Trump's recent criticisms of the Pope.  These tensions have also impacted relations between Italy and the US, with Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni distancing herself from Trump's rhetoric.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Plato: “We can easily forgive a child who is afraid of the dark; the real tragedy of life is when men are afraid of the light.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Plato's quote, "We can easily forgive a child who is afraid of the dark; the real tragedy of life is when men are afraid of the light," highlights the human tendency to avoid uncomfortable truths.  The quote reflects Plato's philosophy that knowledge and truth often require courage and confrontation with personal beliefs and realities. While fear of darkness is understandable, rejecting truth can lead to stagnation and missed opportunities for growth. This timeless message resonates in modern times as people grapple with misinformation, social challenges, and the pursuit of self-awareness.

articles.title: Kerala election results: Congress high command to pick Kerala CM; most UDF allies for Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress Legislative Party in Kerala authorized the party high command to choose the next Chief Minister after a resolution was passed.  AICC observers, Mukul Wasnik, Ajay Maken, and Deepa Dasmunsi, met with all 63 legislators to gauge their preferences for the position. The three frontrunners in the race are former Leader of Opposition V.D. Satheesan, K.C. Venugopal, and Ramesh Chennithala.  UDF allies, including the IUML, have indicated support for Satheesan, while KPCC president Sunny Joseph has called for a decision based on public sentiment. The observers will present their findings to the high command, who is expected to make a final call soon.

articles.title: Countries track passengers of hantavirus-hit cruise ship - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) are monitoring the hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship, the MV Hondius.  Five people have been confirmed to have contracted the virus, with another three suspected cases. The outbreak began after an initial case was detected in early May. Oceanwide Expeditions, the ship's operator, is working to contact all passengers and crew who disembarked at various stops since March 20th.  The WHO has stated that the risk to the general public remains low, but contact tracing and monitoring are ongoing.

articles.title: WHO confirms five cases of hantavirus linked to cruise ship | Health News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) confirmed five cases of hantavirus linked to deaths aboard a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean. The Andes virus, known for limited human-to-human transmission, was detected on the Dutch-flagged ship, currently sailing from Cape Verde to Tenerife.  Three passengers have died so far, with more possible cases as the incubation period can be up to six weeks. Argentina is investigating the couple's movements before boarding the cruise, while WHO has informed 12 countries whose nationals disembarked in Saint Helena.

articles.title: Aimable Karasira: Rwandan singer dies as he was being released from prison
articles.rephrased_article: Rwandan Correctional Service (RCS) spokesperson Hillary Sengabo confirmed the death of singer Aimable Karasira, who died at Nyarugenge Hospital after allegedly overdosing on his medication while being released from prison.  Sengabo stated that Karasira was suffering from diabetes, high blood pressure and poor mental health, and a post-mortem would be conducted. Some government critics believe his death is suspicious and have called for an independent investigation. Human Rights Watch has previously urged the Rwandan authorities to investigate "suspicious deaths and disappearances" of critics and dissidents.

articles.title: Royal Navy tracks Russian frigate for one month off UK coast | Royal Navy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Britain’s Royal Navy tracked a Russian frigate, the Admiral Grigorovich, for an entire month as it sailed from the Atlantic to the North Sea. The frigate was accompanied by other Russian vessels and escorted at least three ships under economic sanctions through the Dover Strait.  The UK has committed naval resources to monitor these activities in response to Russia's increased maritime presence after threats of seizing shadow fleet oil tankers.

articles.title: Chirayu Rana hires lawyer who represented Epstein accusers in lawsuit against JPMorgan executive Lorna Hajdini - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chirayu Rana, a former JPMorgan banker, has hired high-profile lawyer Daniel Kaiser to represent him in a lawsuit against his former supervisor, Lorna Hajdini.  Rana alleges that Hajdini drugged and sexually assaulted him, but JPMorgan denies the claims. The bank conducted an internal investigation which found no evidence supporting Rana's allegations, while Kaiser insists there is more evidence to be presented.

articles.title: Governor’s remit is to invite TVK chief Vijay and ask for a floor test: former Law Minister Ashwani Kumar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ashwani Kumar, former Union Law Minister, urged Tamil Nadu Governor to invite C. Joseph Vijay and his Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) party to form the government and demonstrate their majority on the floor of the State Assembly.  Kumar argued that constitutional conventions require this process when a party claims majority support, dismissing arguments about delaying the swearing-in as a "political outrage" and a "constitutional heresy."

articles.title: FCC sets aside Income Tax Ordinance section enabling taxation on ‘deemed income’ from assets and property - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) ruled that Section 7E of the Income Tax Ordinance (ITO) 2001, which allowed tax authorities to levy tax on "deemed income" from assets and properties, is unconstitutional. The court struck down the provision, declaring it ultra vires the Constitution.  The FCC converted civil petitions filed by taxpayers against judgments of provincial high courts into appeals and dismissed those filed by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and the Commissioner Inland Revenue (CIR). Consequently, all actions taken under Section 7E were declared void.

articles.title: Trump calls for ‘incitement’ charges against top Democrat Hakeem Jeffries | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump called for criminal charges of "incitement to violence" against Hakeem Jeffries, the top Democratic lawmaker in the House of Representatives, alleging that Jeffries' comments about partisan redistricting were inciting violence.  Trump shared a social media post linking Jeffries' remarks to the White House correspondents' dinner shooting incident, which prosecutors say was an assassination attempt on Trump. This follows Trump's previous efforts to use legal action against political opponents, including Letitia James and James Comey.  Jeffries has defended his comments, stating that he meant them in a partisan context regarding redistricting disputes.

articles.title: Rosenberg: Russia's Victory Day parade with no tanks a sign Ukraine war not going to plan
articles.rephrased_article: This year's Victory Day parade in Moscow, marking the defeat of Nazi Germany, is scaled back for the first time in nearly two decades with no military hardware on display. Dmitry Peskov, Vladimir Putin's spokesman, attributes the decision to a "terrorist threat" from Ukraine.  The Kremlin's choice to scale back the parade comes amid growing public fatigue with the war in Ukraine and concerns about rising living costs. The absence of tanks and missiles reflects Russia's struggles in securing victory after four years of conflict.

articles.title: Two men first in British history to be found guilty of spying for China | Crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A UK Border Force officer and a Hong Kong Economic Trade Office official were found guilty of spying for China.  Chi Leung “Peter” Wai, 38, and Chung Biu Yuen, 65, were convicted of assisting a foreign intelligence service and misconduct in public office. The men, who denied the charges, will be sentenced at a later date. A third accused man, former Royal Marine Matthew Trickett, was found dead after being charged under the National Security Act.  The prosecution said it would not seek a retrial.

articles.title: Florida man arrested after 30 years over 1993 murders of couple in front of three-year-old child: 'Hiding in plain sight' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: William Antonio Solis, a 62-year-old Florida man, was arrested in Tampa last month by the New York Police Department for the murders of Luis Guerrero and his wife, Danis Sime, in 1993.  Federal prosecutors allege that Solis participated in a planned drug robbery during which he shot both victims in the head while their three-year-old child witnessed the crime. The case has been reopened after decades and Solis faces charges of intentional killing while engaged in a narcotics conspiracy with a potential sentence of life imprisonment or death.

articles.title: Palaniswami saddened over Stalin’s loss from Kolathur constituency, says AIADMK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Anbalagan, secretary of the AIADMK Puducherry unit, stated that Edappadi K. Palaniswami, party general secretary, was saddened by former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin's defeat in the Kolathur constituency.  Anbalagan confirmed that newly elected legislators from Tamil Nadu are staying at a resort in Puducherry under Palaniswami's directions and all members are united under his leadership. The legislators arrived on Wednesday and were moved to the RKN Beach Resort on Thursday due to advance bookings at The Shore Thrishvam.

articles.title: Cambridge to retake ‘prematurely shared’ AS-level mathematics exam on June 9 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE) canceled the AS-level mathematics exam for affected regions due to a premature release of the paper. The organization will administer a new version of the exam on June 9th, ensuring fair outcomes and grades trusted by universities. CIE stated that no additional charge will be incurred by candidates or schools, and the result date remains August 11th.  The examination body is investigating the leak and has emphasized its commitment to upholding ethical standards and protecting student integrity.

articles.title: PSG’s Champions League win marred by night of violence and riots in Paris | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: PSG claimed a 6-5 Champions League semifinal victory over Bayern Munich, but the celebrations were marred by riots and violence in Paris.  Interior Minister Laurent Nunez reported nearly 130 arrests, including 107 in Paris, after fans clashed with police following the team's win. The clashes occurred outside the Parc des Princes stadium and on the Champs-Elysees, leading to injuries among rioters and police officers. Emmanuel Gregoire, the newly elected Paris Mayor, was criticized for announcing a fan zone without consulting the police beforehand.  Nunez emphasized that security will be increased for the final against Arsenal in Budapest.

articles.title: South Africa condemns 'fake videos' of alleged xenophobic attacks as Ghana writes to AU
articles.rephrased_article: South Africa's government has condemned the circulation of "fake videos and images" that have been described as recordings of attacks on foreign nationals, amidst diplomatic tension with other African nations. Ghana, Nigeria, and several other countries have raised concerns about rising anti-immigration sentiment in South Africa, urging a fact-finding mission to address the issue.  South Africa's government maintains that there are no xenophobic attacks in the country and has called for calm amidst the protests against illegal immigration.

articles.title: Spain awards UN legal expert Francesca Albanese one of its highest civilian honours | Spain | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Francesca Albanese, a UN special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territories, was awarded Spain's highest civilian honor, the Order of Civil Merit, by Pedro Sánchez, the country's prime minister.  Albanese has been vocal in her criticism of Israel's military operations in Gaza and has called for international action to address alleged human rights violations. She also received support from Sánchez who criticized the US sanctions against Albanese and urged the EU to intervene.  Albanese believes that Israel's actions have set a dangerous precedent for eroding international law.

articles.title: MFs, retail investors keep buying these stocks for two straight quarters; many fall over 25% - Smart Money Moves | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: An analysis of BSE-listed companies with a market capitalization above Rs 3,000 crore shows that 52 stocks saw consistent increases in ownership by both mutual funds and retail investors across the last two quarters.  While most of these stocks experienced negative returns over six months, the top three gainers generated returns ranging from 20% to 70%.

articles.title: After LIV Golf withdrawal, Saudi PIF confirms future fate of UFC, WWE and global boxing investments | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) has announced it will no longer fund LIV Golf beyond the 2026 season, but TKO Group Holdings, which owns UFC and WWE, insists that these events will continue as planned. Despite this decision, TKO Group Holdings president and COO Mark Shapiro stated that Saudi partners remain committed to their properties in 2026 and beyond.  Shapiro also addressed concerns about the future of Saudi-backed events following PIF's withdrawal from LIV Golf funding. The company reported strong financial results for both WWE and UFC, with plans for six more events in the Middle East scheduled for 2026.

articles.title: DGP calls for public partnership to curb drug menace - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C.V. Anand, Director General of Police of Telangana, convened a review meeting for the Elite Action Group for Drug Law Enforcement (EAGLE) force to address the growing drug menace in the state.  He emphasized the need for public cooperation and stressed that curbing drug abuse requires a collective effort involving police, educational institutions, and society at large. Anand highlighted the increase in drug-related offenses and arrests, noting that investigations are extending beyond street-level suppliers to those orchestrating operations. He directed officials to strengthen enforcement through advanced technology, financial investigations, and action against foreign syndicates while also raising concerns over the response of educational institutions to drug-related incidents involving students.

articles.title: US-Israel war on Iran leaves Jordan’s Petra nearly empty of tourists | In Pictures News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing war between the United States and Israel against Iran has significantly impacted tourism in Jordan, particularly at the famed ancient city of Petra.  Ruslana Novak, a Ukrainian tourist, noted that while she understands the conflict's impact, Jordan remains calm compared to other countries experiencing war. The decline in foreign visitors is attributed to cancellations, with some hotels considering closure due to the lack of income. Jordan’s tourism authority reported a sharp drop in visitor numbers to Petra, and authorities are struggling to mitigate the economic losses caused by the conflict.  The sector's reliance on foreign tour groups has further exacerbated the situation.

articles.title: Fears of renewed Gaza war as Hamas disarmament talks stall
articles.rephrased_article: Ceasefire talks between Israel and Hamas have stalled, raising fears of renewed conflict in Gaza.  An Israeli air strike killed Khalil al-Hayya's son, a key Hamas negotiator, and the two sides remain at odds over disarmament. Israel insists on moving to the second phase of President Trump's 20-point peace plan before fulfilling first-phase obligations, while Hamas demands an end to Israeli shelling and military operations in Gaza, as well as increased aid and humanitarian access.  The Board of Peace, including Nickolay Mladenov, has urged Hamas to disarm for reconstruction funding, but the group is reasserting its authority and tensions remain high.

articles.title: Israeli settler to go on trial over attack on French nun in Jerusalem | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Yona Simcha Schreiber, a 36-year-old Israeli settler from the West Bank settlement of Peduel, is facing trial for assault motivated by hostility towards religious groups.  The attack on French Catholic nun, who was researching at Jerusalem's French School of Biblical and Archaeological Research, occurred on Mount Zion and involved surveillance footage showing Schreiber violently pushing and kicking the nun. The French consulate in Jerusalem condemned the attack, demanding a trial, while the Faculty of Humanities at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem expressed shock and condemnation over the "troubling pattern" of rising hostility towards Christians.

articles.title: Dabur Q4 Results: Cons PAT rises 15% YoY to Rs 369 crore, revenue up 7%; Rs 5.50 per share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dabur India Limited reported a 7.3% increase in revenue from operations for Q4FY26, reaching Rs 3,038 crore. The company's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 5.50 per equity share and set the date for its fifty-first annual general meeting on August 6, 2026. Dabur India Limited’s international business grew 2.5% during the quarter despite challenges in the Middle East, driven by strong growth in Sub-Saharan Africa, Bangladesh, UK & EU, and Namaste US operations.  Mohit Malhotra, Dabur India Limited's Global Chief Executive Officer, attributed the company's resilient performance to proactive supply chain diversification, disciplined cost controls, and calibrated price increases.

articles.title: Trash to treasure: Garbage workers created a 40,000-book library from books people threw away | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sanitation workers in Ankara's Cankaya district began rescuing books from garbage piles in 2016, sharing them among themselves and their families. The initiative grew into a fully functioning public library with over 40,000 books, supported by donations from residents across the city.  The library, housed in a former brick factory, offers reading rooms, study spaces, and children's sections, becoming a popular destination for students, municipal employees, and even cyclists. The project has expanded to support schools, educational programs, and prisons with free reading materials, demonstrating how discarded objects can become valuable cultural resources.

articles.title: Cusat steps up initiatives to help students deal with mental stress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following the back-to-back suicides of engineering students at Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat), the university has announced a multi-pronged approach to address mental health concerns.  The plan includes increased counselling support, improved teacher-student interactions, and confidence-building programs for students. The university will also convene regular meetings with parents and teachers to inform them about these initiatives. Cusat officials emphasized their commitment to improving student well-being by providing all-round support from faculty members and the administration.

articles.title: International Olympic Committee recommends ending Belarus restrictions | Olympics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has recommended that sporting bodies allow Belarusian athletes to compete without vetting as neutrals, allowing them to compete with their full national identity.  This advice does not yet apply to Russia, but it suggests a potential path toward ending Russia's isolation in Olympic circles due to the ongoing war on Ukraine. The IOC noted concerns about recent information related to a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) investigation into Russian anti-doping agency officials, while also emphasizing that athletes should not be limited by government actions.

articles.title: Hantavirus: Race to trace passengers who left MV Hondius at St Helena
articles.rephrased_article: Oceanwide Expeditions, the operator of the Dutch cruise ship MV Hondius, is working with WHO and other authorities to trace passengers who disembarked in St Helena after a hantavirus outbreak.  The virus has claimed the lives of two people on board and there have been confirmed cases of the disease among those who left the ship. The WHO assessed the public health risk as low but warned that more cases may be reported due to the six-week incubation period. WHO Director General Dr Tedros Ghebreyesus said the virus is spread by contact with infected rodents, and officials are investigating reports of other potential cases.  The ship will dock in Spain's Canary Islands soon.

articles.title: Almost $4bn more for Victoria’s contentious Suburban Rail Loop to be included in federal budget | Suburban Rail Loop | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government will allocate an additional $3.8 billion to the Suburban Rail Loop project in Melbourne, bringing total federal contributions to over $6 billion. The announcement comes ahead of the May budget and as early campaigning for the state election heats up.  Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan will make the announcement on Friday. This funding will be delivered over four years and is part of a larger project that aims to connect Melbourne's eastern suburbs with Werribee in the west, with construction already underway for the first stage. The project has been criticized for its cost, origins, and business case, but supporters argue it will improve travel times and reduce congestion.

articles.title: TDP removes former MLA S.V.S.N. Varma as Pithapuram in-charge after rift with Jana Sena leaders - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telugu Desam Party (TDP) removed former MLA S.V.S.N. Varma from his Pithapuram constituency in-charge position to address a rift with Jana Sena Party (JSP) leaders, for which he is blamed. A special committee will now oversee party affairs in the constituency where Varma lost to YSRCP's Pendem Dorababu in 2019.  Varma had aspired to contest from Pithapuram in 2024 but was replaced by K. Pawan Kalyan, who won with a large margin against the YSRCP candidate Vanga Geetha. Varma stated he was consulted before the decision and will comply with it.

articles.title: Sindh to provide cash assistance to caregivers of children up to five - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah chaired the third board meeting of the Sindh Social Protection Authority (SSPA), approving a Rs14 billion Early Childhood Development (ECD) program. The initiative will provide quarterly payments of Rs3,000 to over 885,000 children aged one month to five years old for growth monitoring, nutrition counseling, and school readiness.  The meeting also approved upgrades to the Mamta maternal health cash transfer program and a new Women Agricultural Workers Programme to provide seasonal income assistance to rural women. The government aims to strengthen long-term human development through these programs.

articles.title: Africa sees winners and losers as Iran war pushes up oil prices | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Africa is experiencing economic fallout from the US-Israeli war on Iran, with rising energy prices causing a surge in fuel costs and impacting businesses across the continent.  Kenya, for example, faces a potential loan of up to $600 million from the World Bank as it attempts to shield its economy from the global energy crisis. While oil-rich nations are benefiting from increased energy prices, resource-scarce countries like Kenya are struggling with rising fuel costs and limited refining capacity.  The conflict has created opportunities for some African countries, such as Nigeria, which is seeing a surge in export revenues due to higher oil prices, while others, like the Democratic Republic of Congo, benefit from increased demand for minerals. However, many African nations remain reliant on Gulf investment and trade with the US, making it unlikely they will sever ties quickly despite the economic challenges posed by the war.

articles.title: Reopening strait of Hormuz would have limited impact on cargo flows, says Maersk | Shipping industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Vincent Clerc, CEO of the shipping company Maersk, stated that the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz would have a limited impact on cargo flows despite the significant increase in energy costs. The strait has been effectively shut since late February, contributing to higher energy prices and causing disruptions for over 800 ships and their crews.  Donald Trump, US president, tweeted that the blockade could end if Iran agrees to certain conditions, allowing the Strait of Hormuz to be open to all, including Iran. Maersk reported a 2% drop in revenue but maintained its profit guidance for the year, citing strong demand for shipping containers.

articles.title: Shelley Simpson: UK travel boss jailed over £300k holiday 'ponzi scheme' used to pay children’s school fees | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shelley Simpson, a former travel company director, was sentenced to two years and nine months in prison for defrauding 47 customers of nearly £300,000. Simpson, who ran Portsmouth-based Sphere Events Limited, used money from new customers to pay off older debts instead of booking legitimate trips. The court heard she fabricated booking confirmations and diverted customer funds towards private school fees for her children.  Simpson was banned from serving as a company director for eight years.

articles.title: Newborn animals and birds mark conservation milestone at Indira Gandhi Zoological Park - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park in Visakhapatnam has seen a surge in births this summer, including Indian grey wolves, Asiatic wild dogs, and striped hyena cubs. The zoo's conservation breeding program is seeing success with the animals, particularly the pups of endangered species like the dhole.  The births are attributed to stable enclosures, proper care, and environmental enrichment, according to curator G Mangamma.

articles.title: Pakistan expects agreement between US and Iran 'sooner rather than later': FO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Tahir Andrabi expressed optimism about a US-Iran agreement, stating Pakistan welcomes any settlement.  Andrabi noted that the FO is working with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar to pursue peace through dialogue and diplomacy. He also confirmed that 54 Pakistanis detained in Cambodia following a raid on a scamming compound have been repatriated back to Pakistan. The repatriation process for the remaining three individuals is expected to be completed soon.

articles.title: Can Asian economies cope with the fallout from the Iran war? | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Asian economies are facing significant challenges due to the fallout from the Iran war, including rising fuel costs, inflation, and debt pressures. Governments are implementing measures such as rationing fuel, reintroducing subsidies, and limiting exports to mitigate the impact of the energy crisis. The prolonged disruption of the Strait of Hormuz is exacerbating these issues, leading to increased import bills, currency depreciation, and strained government finances.

articles.title: Li Shangfu: China announces suspended death sentences for ex-defence ministers
articles.rephrased_article: China's military court sentenced former defense ministers Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu to suspended death sentences for bribery. The two men will serve life imprisonment after a two-year reprieve, with no possibility of parole or sentence reduction. This follows a recent crackdown on corruption within the military, which has seen several high-ranking officials removed from their positions. President Xi Jinping has overseen these anti-corruption drives, which critics argue are also used to purge political rivals.

articles.title: ‘Restaurants won’t survive’: Michelin chef opens venues abroad to withstand UK taxes | Restaurants | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jason Atherton, a Michelin-starred chef, is opening restaurants abroad to offset the high taxes and struggling hospitality sector in the UK.  He believes that restaurants will not survive if tax burdens continue to increase.  The UKHospitality industry body estimates that increased business rates and VAT will add £32,000 in extra tax for average restaurants. Atherton, who has restaurants in Dubai, St Moritz, and now Forte dei Marmi, Italy, is finding it easier to make a profit in countries with more forgiving policies towards restaurants.

articles.title: Scientists explore whether quantum physics could allow messages to travel back in time | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists at MIT and the University of Queensland are exploring the possibility of sending information back in time using quantum mechanics.  They propose that quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where particles influence each other instantaneously regardless of distance, could be the key to this "retrocausality." Experiments simulating time travel have already been conducted using photons and quantum computers, with promising results. However, scientists emphasize these theories are currently theoretical and do not suggest humans can send messages to their past selves or alter historical events.  Despite the challenges, research into retrocausality and quantum time loops could lead to advancements in communication, computing, and cryptography.

articles.title: Behind the insistence on 'majority support' looms the shadow of President's Rule - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court has established a legal principle that a Governor's primary duty is to form a stable government, preventing constitutional breakdown.  This principle dictates that the Governor cannot refuse to allow the formation of a government once a majority is established, with the exception being when the Governor believes a stable government cannot be formed by the claimants. The Tamil Nadu government is currently facing challenges as the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) president C. Joseph Vijay demands proof of majority support in the Legislative Assembly.

articles.title: Turkiye unveils its first intercontinental ballistic missile: What we know | Weapons News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Turkey unveiled a prototype of an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) called the Yildirimhan. The ICBM, with a range of 6,000km and a payload capacity of 3,000kg, is designed to deter threats and enhance Turkey's self-reliance in defense. Experts believe this development signifies a shift towards Turkish military independence and its growing role as a global power.  The unveiling comes amidst heightened tensions in the Middle East, including ongoing conflicts between Israel and Iran, as well as escalating tensions with neighboring countries like Lebanon and Iraq. Turkey is also seeking to strengthen its position within NATO and increase its defense spending to 5% of its GDP by 2035. The country's growing defense industry has led to a surge in exports, making it a key player in the global arms market.

articles.title: US judge releases Jeffrey Epstein's purported suicide note
articles.rephrased_article: A US judge ordered the release of a purported suicide note written by convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, which mentions an investigation that found "nothing." The note was discovered by Epstein's former cellmate, Nicholas Tartaglione, who claims he found it after Epstein attempted suicide in July 2019. The Department of Justice has not commented on the note, but a previous spokesperson stated they had not seen it.  The judge concluded that public access to the note promotes accountability and public confidence in the justice system.

articles.title: More than 50,000 pupils expected to strike over German rearmament policy | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands of German students are expected to participate in a nationwide school strike on Friday, protesting the government's rearmament policy and arguing that it will force young people into war. Hannes Kramer, spokesperson for the Schulstreik gegen Wehrpflicht movement, claims the government is preparing for war without consulting young people.  The protest comes amid concerns about Germany's increased military spending, which critics argue is a dangerous path towards conflict. The strike coincides with the anniversary of Victory in Europe Day and reflects widespread unrest among students over the government's focus on defense while neglecting education.

articles.title: Underground Cave: The 8,000-year-old underground cave in Southern Europe holds a mystery: People entered and never returned | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists are investigating a mysterious underground cave complex in southern Europe that dates back almost 8,000 years. Evidence suggests the site was likely used for rituals rather than as a residence, with findings including human remains, artifacts, and baskets made of woven plants.  The discovery raises questions about why ancient people ventured deep into these perilous caves despite potential dangers, such as darkness, uneven surfaces, and lack of oxygen. While some theories suggest cave collapse or death by natural causes, others propose that the sites were used for rituals or even sacrifice. The mystery continues to fascinate scientists who are using modern techniques like scanning and DNA testing to learn more about these ancient cultures' beliefs and practices.

articles.title: Students and teachers protest ‘unlawful entity’ tag on educational institution in J&K’s Shopian - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students and teachers of Darul Uloom Jamia Siraj-ul-Uloom marched to the office of the Deputy Commissioner/District Magistrate demanding the revocation of a notification declaring the institution unlawful. The protest, which remained peaceful, followed a two-page order issued by Kashmir’s Divisional Commissioner, Anshul Garg, citing alleged illegal activities and links to the banned organization Jamaat-e-Islami. Political parties have criticized the government's decision.

articles.title: Irish footballers and celebrities urge boycott of Israel matches | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Irish footballers and celebrities have called for a boycott of upcoming Israel matches, citing accusations of genocide in the Gaza war. The campaign, spearheaded by Irish Sport for Palestine, urges the Republic of Ireland to respect their stance against Israel's actions.  The FAI, while acknowledging the humanitarian crisis in Palestine, has defended its commitment to fulfilling sporting obligations and maintaining Irish football's standing. Prime Minister Micheal Martin expressed a more cautious approach, emphasizing the potential for political complications when sport intersects with politics.

articles.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby: Vigils held for five-year-old girl allegedly murdered in Outback
articles.rephrased_article: Indigenous communities across Australia held vigils in remembrance of Kumanjayi Little Baby, a five-year-old girl who was allegedly murdered in the Outback.  The child's mother spoke at a candlelit vigil in Alice Springs, expressing her grief and asking for people to care for their children.  Vigils were also held in major cities like Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Darwin, Canberra, Adelaide, Brisbane, and Hobart. Indigenous community members shared stories and poems about the child, while others expressed condolences and support for her family. The investigation into the girl's death is ongoing.

articles.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby: Advocates say five-year-old’s death ‘should not be politicised’ as hundreds gather at vigils | Indigenous Australians | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of people across Australia gathered for vigils honoring Kumanjayi Little Baby, a five-year-old Warlpiri girl who died in Alice Springs.  The national body representing First Nations children, SNAICC, called for an end to the politicization of her death, emphasizing that it was not a failure of family or community but a result of systemic failures. Catherine Liddle, CEO of SNAICC, urged unity and respect for the child's memory, stating that connection to culture is crucial for children's safety.  The vigil in Canberra included a smoking ceremony and mourners laid flowers and wreaths at the Aboriginal tent embassy while those in Melbourne gathered at the Aborigines Advancement League.

articles.title: Spectacled cobra rescued from a house in Bhadradri Kothagudem’s remote hamlet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pranadhara Trust, led by its founder president Santosh Babu, rescued a spectacled cobra from a house in Karukonda Ramavaram Gram Panchayat on Tuesday night. The snake, which had strayed into the house from the nearby forest fringe area, was safely removed and released back into the wild by the rescue team members after informing local forest staff on Wednesday morning.

articles.title: The Gaza journalist killed on the day his daughter was born | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Amal Sobeih, a Gaza journalist, and her husband Yahya Sobaih mourned the loss of their newborn daughter, Sana.  Sobaih was killed in an Israeli air strike hours after his daughter's birth, while celebrating with family. The attack also claimed the lives of at least 17 other people, including Sobaih's cousin, friend, and brother-in-law. Yahya Sobeih had been a journalist covering the ongoing conflict in Gaza, and Amal is now raising their three children alone after losing her brother, his wife, and their three children to Israeli attacks.

articles.title: Plan for water sports at Simly Dam raises environmental concerns - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Capital Development Authority (CDA) is planning to develop recreational facilities near Simly Dam, a source of clean drinking water for Islamabad.  Mohsin Naqvi, the Interior Minister, has directed authorities to expand the dam and develop surrounding areas for tourism and water sports. The project aims to boost local development and provide citizens with access to "world-class recreational facilities." However, critics point to past controversies during Kamran Lashari's tenure as CDA chairman, including controversial projects that faced inquiries by the FIA and NAB.

articles.title: JD Sports says Iran war could hit consumer spending and raise prices | JD Sports Fashion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: JD, the sports fashion retailer, has lowered its profit expectations for the year ahead due to a "muted market" and concerns about the Middle East conflict. The company anticipates profits between £750 million and £850 million, down from £852 million in the previous year. JD's CEO, Régis Schultz, remains optimistic about the company's long-term prospects despite the challenges, citing strong brand partnerships and a multibrand model. Analysts have downgraded their profit expectations for JD, citing uncertainty within the retail sector.

articles.title: Driver arrested after chasing young boy riding bike
articles.rephrased_article: Wendy Clemente, a 56-year-old woman, was arrested in Cheney, US after chasing down a child cyclist on a footpath.  The incident occurred in April and the boy escaped by riding away from the car. Clemente faces multiple charges including assault and drink-driving. The boy's mother said he was shaken up and scared by the experience.

articles.title: Kerala CM to be chosen by Congress High Command is acceptable for CMP, says C.P. John - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C. P. John, general secretary of the Communist Marxist Party (CMP), stated that the party would accept the Congress High Command's chosen Kerala Chief Minister.  He also acknowledged the possibility of a ministerial berth for the CMP but declined to comment further. John expressed gratitude to voters and noted the CMP's historical performance in Kannur despite a decline in its overall vote base. He emphasized addressing the potable water crisis in Thiruvananthapuram as his immediate priority.

articles.title: French warship moves towards Hormuz for possible defensive mission | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Keir Starmer are leading a multinational mission towards restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, a strategically critical waterway that has been effectively blocked amid the US-Israel war on Iran.  The mission is intended to be entirely defensive and deployed only once the war ends. The French government is framing the mission as a win-win solution for Iran and the US, aiming to incentivize them to agree to negotiations on nuclear materials, missiles, and regional issues. President Donald Trump has signaled progress in the negotiations but also threatened to resume bombing if Tehran does not accept the US plan.

articles.title: FCC questions integrity of Nadra records in custody case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) questioned the reliability of Nadra records during a habeas corpus hearing regarding the custody of Ayesha Tariq, a minor girl who converted from Christianity to Islam.  Justice Aamer Farooq expressed concerns about the possibility of tampering with Nadra records and ordered an ossification test to determine the girl's actual age. The court also directed that she be placed in Darul Aman until the test results are received.

articles.title: Rubio set to meet Pope Leo in bid to ease tensions after Trump’s criticism of the pontiff - Europe live | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, is traveling to the Vatican to meet with Pope Leo in an attempt to ease tensions between the US and the Holy See following President Trump's criticisms of the pontiff.  The meeting comes amid strained relations between Washington and Rome, which have been further exacerbated by Trump's recent attacks on the Pope. Donald Trump has repeatedly criticized the Pope over his stance against the war in Iran, accusing him of supporting nuclear weapons and endangering Catholics. Rubio aims to defend the US rationale for launching the war while avoiding a direct confrontation with the church's position.  The meeting is expected to be followed by meetings with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

articles.title: Passengers told virus-hit cruise ship 'not infectious' after first death
articles.rephrased_article: A captain on the hantavirus-stricken cruise ship MV Hondius told passengers that a deceased passenger's death was due to "natural causes" despite three confirmed and five suspected cases of the rare disease.  The Oceanwide Expeditions, the cruise operator, stated they acted in accordance with their press updates following the first identified case on May 4th. The ship is currently carrying around 150 passengers from 23 countries near Cape Verde.

articles.title: Life 2 meters underground: Scientists discover hidden microbial oasis beneath Chile’s driest desert | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists in Chile's Atacama Desert have discovered a functional community of microorganisms living two meters below the surface, challenging previous assumptions about life's limits. This "hidden oasis" relies on mineral-bound moisture from gypsum pores to survive, with bacteria like Actinobacteriota thriving in constant darkness. The findings suggest that subsurface life could be more common than previously thought and offer valuable insights for searching for similar life forms on Mars or other barren planets.  This discovery necessitates a shift in planetary mission priorities toward subsurface sampling.

articles.title: Left parties, VCK hold the key as DMK discusses idea of an AIADMK coalition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMK president M.K. Stalin invited CPI(M) State secretary P. Shanmugam, CPI State secretary M. Veerapandian, and VCK leader Thol. Thirumavalavan to discuss a potential DMK-backed AIADMK government. The Left parties have six MLAs and are crucial for forming the government with 118 seats required. While the DMK is considering supporting an AIADMK government from outside, its allies will decide on joining such a coalition.

articles.title: Neymar apologises to Robinho’s son after slapping him in training | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Neymar publicly apologized to Robinho Jr, the son of former Real Madrid and Manchester City striker Robinho, after slapping him during a training session. The incident occurred on Sunday, prompting an investigation by Santos.  Robinho Jr. confirmed that the situation was resolved and accepted Neymar's apology. Despite the incident, Neymar remains hopeful of being called up for the World Cup later this year.

articles.title: Doctors Without Borders says Israel has 'manufactured malnutrition crisis' in Gaza - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has accused Israel of creating a "manufactured malnutrition crisis" in Gaza, citing data from its analysis of health facilities and the impact of the Israeli blockade. The charity's report found that infants born to malnourished mothers are more likely to be premature and have low birth weight, while 90% of babies born to such mothers were also premature.  MSF also highlighted the impact of the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF), a US- and Israeli-backed organization, which they say reduced food distribution points in Gaza and led to violence and malnutrition. The charity called for immediate unhindered access to aid into Gaza.

articles.title: ‘Came here with hope’ and ‘died unseen’: tearful crowd says goodbye to homeless man Bikram Lama | Homelessness | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Erin Longbottom, a homelessness support worker, and Joe Trueman, a former rough sleeper, organized a vigil in Sydney's Hyde Park to honor Bikram Lama, a young Nepali man who died while homeless.  St Vincent’s Health stated that Lama's non-resident status made it difficult for him to access help, while Bam Bunyalak, another non-resident, spoke about the challenges faced by those without residency in Australia. Independent state MP Alex Greenwich called for an inquest into potential policy failings that may have contributed to Lama’s death.

articles.title: New bridge linking allies North Korea and Russia nearly complete
articles.rephrased_article: Satellite images show the Khasan–Tumangang Bridge, a road bridge connecting North Korea and Russia, is nearing completion. The bridge, built to handle up to 300 vehicles and 2,850 people daily, is expected to become an important trade route between the two countries.  Experts believe this development reflects the deepening relationship between North Korea and Russia, which has seen North Korean troops fighting alongside Russian forces in Ukraine. The bridge's construction was agreed upon during a visit by Vladimir Putin to Pyongyang in June 2024, and is expected to be completed on June 19th.

articles.title: Hantavirus Uk: Hantavirus cruise outbreak: Two Britons self-isolate after exposure scare on MV Hondius | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Two British nationals who disembarked the cruise ship MV Hondius in Saint Helena are self-isolating at home after possible exposure to hantavirus. The pair, one of whom is receiving treatment in the Netherlands, had no symptoms when they left the vessel earlier this month.  The cruise operator, Oceanwide Expeditions, confirmed that 19 passengers and four crew members on board were British nationals, with three medically evacuated to the Netherlands for treatment. Spanish authorities granted permission for the ship to dock in the Canary Islands despite concerns raised by some local officials. The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) is monitoring the situation and expects those without symptoms to return to the UK on a charter flight.

articles.title: Suvendu Adhikari aide killing: Driver undergoes multiple surgeries, still critical - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandranath Rath, a close aide of Suvendu Adhikari, the BJP leader, was shot and killed in North 24 Parganas on Wednesday night.  The driver of Rath's car, Buddhadeb Bera, sustained bullet injuries and underwent multiple surgeries. His condition remains critical. The incident has sparked outrage, protests, and renewed allegations of political violence in West Bengal following the state elections.

articles.title: Rubio arrives at Vatican to meet Pope Leo amid Trump attacks | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, arrived at the Vatican to meet Pope Leo XIV in an attempt to mend strained relations following President Donald Trump's repeated attacks on the pontiff. The closed-door meeting is expected to last half an hour and will follow a similar meeting between the pope and Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican Secretary of State.  The meeting, requested by the US, comes amid escalating tensions between Trump and the Pope, who has criticized the US-Israel war on Iran.

articles.title: Pakistan hopeful about agreement between US and Iran: FO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Tahir Andrabi expressed optimism about a potential agreement between the US and Iran, stating that Pakistan welcomes any settlement reached between the two nations.  Andrabi highlighted the recent positive developments, including reports of Tehran reviewing a fresh US proposal for peace following the suspension of ‘Project Freedom’. He also noted ongoing diplomatic efforts by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar to promote dialogue and peaceful resolution between Washington and Tehran. The FO spokesperson further addressed the repatriation of 54 Pakistanis detained in Cambodia, confirming their safe return to Pakistan.

articles.title: Antisemitism has become ‘almost fashionable’ among Australians, Jillian Segal tells royal commission | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jewish Australians have reported experiencing workplace harassment, including pressure to change their names and being verbally abused by colleagues.  The antisemitism royal commission heard from several individuals who shared stories of feeling unsafe in their workplaces due to anti-Jewish sentiment. Jillian Segal, Australia's special envoy to combat antisemitism, stated that young Australians are increasingly hostile towards Jewish people, with the conflation of the Israeli government with Jewish people being a growing form of antisemitism. ABM, an Australian employee who was asked to change her name at work, resigned after feeling pressured to do so.  Stephanie Cunio, a trade unionist and climate activist, also shared how younger members in a green advocacy group pushed for her resignation due to her support for Israel.

articles.title: West Bengal election: Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandranath Rath shot dead in post-poll violence
articles.rephrased_article: Chandranath Rath, personal assistant to Suvendu Adhikari, a top BJP leader, was shot and killed in West Bengal after the state election.  Police are investigating but haven't made any arrests. The incident is part of escalating tensions following the BJP's historic victory, which ended 15 years of rule by Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress (TMC).  The TMC condemned the killing and demanded accountability for those responsible. Both parties have accused each other of violence and intimidation, with the BJP alleging a deterioration in law and order under Banerjee. The new chief minister is expected to be sworn in on Saturday.

articles.title: Hantavirus Outbreak: Hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship; 40 passengers disembark on South Atlantic island - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dutch officials confirmed that approximately 40 passengers from a cruise ship affected by a deadly hantavirus outbreak disembarked on the remote South Atlantic island of St Helena after the first passenger death. The Dutch foreign ministry stated that the passengers, including the wife of a deceased man who died at an airport in Johannesburg, left the ship during a stop at the British territory.  The cruise company operating the ship has not confirmed if other passengers disembarked at St Helena but authorities are now tracing passengers and possible contacts after the outbreak resulted in multiple deaths and several illnesses.

articles.title: Chandrababu Naidu directs officials to take a result-oriented approach, says A.P. inherited ₹9.74 lakh crore in debt - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu addressed the 7th Collectors’ Conference in Andhra Pradesh, emphasizing a welfare-driven governance model focused on development and wealth creation. He acknowledged the financial challenges inherited from the previous regime but highlighted the government's progress in welfare programs, infrastructure development, and economic growth. Naidu stressed the importance of effective grievance resolution, "zero-error" land records, and public satisfaction as key metrics for successful governance.  He directed officials to replicate successful models across districts, emphasizing the need for field visits by senior officers and Ministers to improve governance practices.

articles.title: What is China’s anti-sanctions law and how does it work? | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: China's Ministry of Commerce issued a prohibition order blocking US sanctions against five Chinese oil refineries, marking the first invocation of its 2021 anti-sanctions law. The move comes after the US Treasury Department imposed sanctions on one of China's largest independently run refineries, accusing it of generating revenue for Iran's military.  The law allows China to counter what it views as "unjustified extra-territorial jurisdiction" by requiring citizens and companies to report compliance with foreign legislation and to issue orders barring them from complying with sanctions. The order is significant because it signals a more assertive approach by China to counter US sanctions, potentially putting companies navigating tensions between the two countries in a difficult position.

articles.title: Up to 2cm a month: Nasa keeps track as Mexico City sinks into the ground | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nasa and the Indian Space Research Organization’s Nisar satellite is providing real-time data on Mexico City's alarming subsidence rate. The technology, capable of detecting minute changes in Earth's surface, reveals that some areas are sinking by more than 2cm a month, one of the fastest rates globally. This phenomenon, caused by centuries of groundwater extraction from the city's ancient lake bed, has led to tilting buildings, warped roads, and damage to the metro system. Experts warn that halting the subsidence will require stopping water extraction, raising concerns about water supply for the metropolis of 22 million people.

articles.title: DR Congo leader Félix Tshisekedi hints at extending term and delaying polls
articles.rephrased_article: Félix Tshisekedi, president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, suggested he may seek a third term in office when his current mandate expires in 2028. He stated that any extension would require a referendum and that elections might be delayed due to ongoing conflict with the M23 rebels in eastern DRC. Tshisekedi blamed Rwanda for obstructing peace efforts and accused it of profiting from DR Congo's mineral resources. The opposition has criticized Tshisekedi's potential bid for a third term, prompting discussions about amending the constitution through a referendum.

articles.title: Noel Tata’s IPO pushback said to trigger internal differences at Tata Group - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Trusts, a group of charities controlling two-thirds of Tata Sons Pvt., are considering proposing that the holding company prepare for an IPO in line with India's central bank regulations. Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, trustees at the trusts, will likely advocate for this move at an upcoming meeting on May 8th, citing the need for transparency and rigor. This comes as RBI is set to designate Tata Sons a shadow bank by July 1st, requiring it to be listed. The move faces opposition from Noel, who heads the trusts and seeks to maintain control over the group's parent company.

articles.title: 'Come in person': How a bank gave Pope Leo a reality check | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Leo XIV, formerly Robert Prevost, discovered that his newly acquired papal status did not grant him the power to bypass bank verification procedures. After attempting to update his contact information with a Chicago bank, he was informed that he would need to visit in person due to security protocols. Despite being recognized as the Pope by cardinals and the Vatican, the bank employee insisted on traditional customer verification processes. The incident highlights the universal experience of navigating bureaucratic systems even for those at the pinnacle of power.

articles.title: Assembly elections: Kerala Congress desires at least two ministerial berths in UDF govt, says P.J. Joseph - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: P.J. Joseph, chairman of the Kerala Congress (Joseph), stated his party desires at least two ministerial positions in the new UDF government in Kerala.  Following their victory in the 2026 Assembly election, where they won seven out of eight contested seats, Mr. Joseph expressed the desire for discussions regarding ministerial representation. While he did not specify which district would receive a minister, he emphasized that the party would only express its opinion on the Chief Ministerial candidate if requested by the alliance leadership.

articles.title: Madrid captain Carvajal in race against time for Spain’s World Cup squad | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Dani Carvajal, a Spanish international, is battling to recover from a right foot injury sustained during training with Real Madrid.  Luis de la Fuente, Spain's manager, acknowledges Carvajal's importance to the team but emphasizes the need for him to regain fitness and form before the World Cup. De la Fuente suggests that Carvajal may be left out of the squad if he cannot meet these requirements. The World Cup will take place in the United States, Canada, and Mexico from June 11 to July 19.

articles.title: 'We are prepared': DG ISPR touts Pakistan's indigenous military capabilities - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Director General of Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, addressed a press conference to commemorate the one-year anniversary of the military conflict with India, known as "Marka-i-Haq."  He highlighted key strategic consequences of the conflict, including the debunking of India's narrative about Pakistan's role in terrorism and the consolidation of Pakistan's position as a regional security provider. The DG ISPR also criticized the politicization of the Indian military leadership and the militarization of its political landscape. He emphasized that the world now recognizes India's attempts to externalize its internal problems through terrorism, while highlighting Pakistan's resilience in combating such threats.  He concluded by reiterating Pakistan's commitment to defending its territorial integrity and sovereignty.

articles.title: Woman jailed in Somalia for peaceful protest ‘stripped, kicked and beaten’ | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sadia Moalim Ali, a 27-year-old Somali nursing graduate and activist, has been detained in prison for her anti-government activism. She claims to have been tortured by guards while being held in solitary confinement without food or basic necessities.  Ali was arrested on April 12th for criticizing the government's policies on social media. Amnesty International reports that police are holding her without due legal process and she has not been formally charged. Human rights organizations, including Dalmar Dhayow of the Coalition of Somali Human Rights Defenders, have condemned Ali's detention as unlawful and called for her immediate release.

articles.title: Islamic State-linked women arrive in Australia from Syria
articles.rephrased_article: Thirteen women and children linked to the Islamic State (IS) group arrived in Australia from Syria, sparking debate about their repatriation. The group, who had been living in the al-Roj camp since 2019, landed in Melbourne and Sydney, with some facing potential arrest and charges related to terrorism offenses. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke stated that these individuals made a "horrific choice" by joining IS and placed their children in an "unspeakable situation."  The group's return has prompted concerns from the government, who have been preparing for this event since 2014.

articles.title: Seth R Freeman on why global markets continue to climb amid West Asia conflict - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Seth R Freeman, a market expert from GlassRatner Advisory, stated that the geopolitical situation surrounding Iran remains unpredictable, with no clear timeline for resolution. Despite ongoing tensions and concerns over oil prices, equity markets have shown resilience, driven by strong earnings momentum and investor confidence in future corporate profitability.
