These units will be installed in Davanagere, Mysuru, Dharwad, Bagalkote, Jayanagar General/K.C. General Hospital in Bengaluru, and Bengaluru South. The procurement will be carried out through the Karnataka State Medical Supplies Corporation (KSMSC).

articles.title: BJP accuses Speaker of delaying oath to Jeevaraj, asks Governor to administer oath - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following a recount of postal ballots, D.N. Jeevaraj, the defeated BJP candidate in the Sringeri Assembly constituency, was declared the victor.  The BJP accused Speaker U.T. Khader of intentionally delaying the oath administration process, prompting a complaint to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot. The opposition leader, R. Ashok, and Mr. Jeevaraj met with the Governor on May 5th to express their concerns.

articles.title: Gen Z entrepreneurs adept at speed, should focus on deep learning: speakers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Speakers at a panel discussion on "The Future Reimagined" discussed the unique strengths and challenges of Gen Z and Gen Alpha, emphasizing their rational nature and speed in information acquisition.  They suggested that providing these generations with meaningful purpose can foster their engagement and success, while also encouraging them to prioritize self-care and letting go of perfectionism. The discussion highlighted the importance of market research and scaling up businesses effectively, urging entrepreneurs to focus on quality operations and leveraging government policies for innovation.

articles.title: California ‘failing victims’ of violent crime as financial support plummets | Gun crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new analysis by Californians for Safety and Justice reveals a concerning decline in the amount of money awarded to victims through California's Victim Compensation Board (CalVCB) since 2019. Despite an increase in the program's budget, the number of applications being denied has risen significantly, with more than 30% fewer funds distributed compared to previous years. CalVCB attributes the denials to applicants not providing required documentation on time, but advocates like Tinisch Hollins, executive director of CSJ, argue that restrictive terms and a lack of awareness about the program leave many victims without access to vital support.  This decline in compensation comes at a time when California is grappling with rising crime rates, including shootings, burglaries, and public drug use.

articles.title: How ‘bulldozer justice’ undermines the law - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A five-year-old girl gifted a bulldozer toy to Yogi Adityanath, the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, sparking concerns about the normalization of "bulldozer justice" and its potential influence on impressionable minds.  Adityanath returned the gift and advised the child to focus on her studies, but the incident highlights the public's acceptance of this political symbol and its implications for extrajudicial action within the state.

articles.title: FDA blocked studies finding Covid and shingles vaccines safe, HHS official says | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has withdrawn several studies that found Covid-19 and shingles vaccines to be safe, citing concerns about broad conclusions drawn from the data.  Andrew Nixon, an HHS spokesperson, stated the studies were withdrawn because they did not meet the agency's high standards of scientific integrity. Janet Woodcock, former FDA principal deputy commissioner, expressed concern over a pattern of suppressing information that supports vaccine safety. The studies, funded by taxpayer money and costing millions of dollars, examined vaccine safety in various age groups and found rare side effects.

articles.title: Any casteist exclusion cannot be part of religion, says Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that any practice excluding people based on caste is not religious in nature, citing Article 25 of the Constitution. Justice B.V. Nagarathna emphasized this during a hearing regarding a Parsi woman's (Goolrokh Gupta) case who was barred from entering a fire temple for marrying outside her faith.  The court heard arguments that such restrictions resemble an "excommunication" and violate fundamental rights, referencing the "Doctrine of Coverture" which holds women lose their identity upon marriage.

articles.title: US Army says ‘Project Freedom’ in blockaded Hormuz has ‘just begun’ | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US military launched "Project Freedom" to secure a safe passage for commercial vessels through the blocked Strait of Hormuz.  US Central Command spokesperson stated that the operation, aimed at ensuring global and regional economic benefits, has just begun and will not require US forces to enter Iranian waters or airspace. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed 10 civilian sailors have died in the conflict, while US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth emphasized that the operation is defensive and temporary in nature.  He also stated that Iran cannot block international commerce and that two US commercial vessels have already passed through the strait.

articles.title: Rubio insists US is ‘very fortunate’ as Iran war pushes gas price near $4.50 | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, stated that the US is in a fortunate position due to its status as a net oil exporter and its relative insulation from global price fluctuations.  He acknowledged that Americans are experiencing higher fuel prices, but argued that these levels are still lower than what could have been expected if Iran had nuclear weapons and closed the Strait of Hormuz. AAA reports average US fuel prices at $4.48 per gallon, a significant increase from last year's price of $3.17.

articles.title: Bihar Cabinet expansion on May 7, Modi, Shah and Nabin to attend event - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and BJP president Nitin Nabin will be present for the expansion of the Bihar Cabinet in Patna on Thursday, May 7, 2026.  The event is expected to feature most members from the previous Nitish Kumar-led NDA government retained, with a few new faces added to fill all 36 berths. The BJP aims for a "gala event" and preparations are underway at Gandhi Maidan. Jitan Ram Manjhi, leader of the HAM (S), has stated he will not demand a Cabinet berth and is content with whatever is offered.  The expansion is expected to include some new faces, potentially more women Ministers, and may see the return of several existing ministers from both the JD(U) and BJP.

articles.title: Before Vatican trip, Rubio defends Trump remarks on Pope Leo over Iran | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio defended President Donald Trump's comments about Pope Leo XIV, stating that the president's concerns were rooted in Iran's potential threat to places with a large Christian population.  Rubio argued that Iran's pursuit of nuclear weapons posed a danger and highlighted rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The exchange comes ahead of Rubio's meeting with Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican on Thursday, which is expected to be frank.

articles.title: Unwell British crew member to be ‘urgently’ evacuated from cruise ship after hantavirus cases | Infectious diseases | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A British crew member and a Dutch colleague onboard the luxury cruise ship MV Hondius are being medically evacuated after experiencing respiratory symptoms suspected to be hantavirus.  The World Health Organization (WHO) has prioritized their care, with Spain receiving the ship in three or four days for medical examination and treatment of all passengers and crew. The Spanish health ministry confirmed it will receive the ship in the Canary Islands where medical teams will examine and treat those onboard. A British passenger who was medically evacuated to South Africa is improving while two others remain on board awaiting evacuation.

articles.title: TVK's Vijay wins in Tamil Nadu: Actor-politician holds key meeting - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by actor-turned-politician C. Joseph Vijay, has requested support from the Congress and the CPI(M) to form a government in Tamil Nadu after emerging as the single largest party with 108 seats. The Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) agreed to provide support contingent on the TVK refraining from seeking support from the BJP or its allies.

articles.title: Arsenal beat Atletico to reach first Champions League final in 20 years | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Arsenal defeated Atletico Madrid 1-0 in the Champions League semifinal second leg, securing a 2-1 aggregate win and advancing to their first Champions League final in 20 years.  Bukayo Saka's goal late in the first half sealed the victory at an ecstatic Emirates Stadium. The Gunners will face either Paris Saint-Germain or Bayern Munich in the final on May 30th.

articles.title: Israeli beauty queen says she bumped into Zohran Mamdani's wife at a cafe, Rama Duwaji 'refused to engage' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Melanie Shiraz, Miss Israel 2025, posted a video alleging that Rama Duwaji, wife of NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani, refused to engage in a conversation about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.  Shiraz claims Duwaji initially posed for a photo with her but changed her demeanor upon learning of her nationality. Duwaji apologized last month for social media posts she made as a teenager, expressing antisemitic views and supporting Palestinian militant groups.

articles.title: Zack Polanski falsely claimed to be British Red Cross spokesperson, charity says | Green party | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Zack Polanski, the leader of the Green party, has been accused of falsely claiming to be a spokesperson for the British Red Cross and a full member of the National Council of Hypnotherapy. The charity and the Green party have addressed these claims, while the Times newspaper published an article detailing Polanski's past controversies, including his work as a hypnotherapist that was featured in a 2013 Sun article.  The Green party is facing scrutiny for several controversies, including antisemitic comments made by some candidates and accusations of misleading the public about their qualifications.

articles.title: Offensive stage of Iran war is over, US Secretary of State Rubio says
articles.rephrased_article: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the initial US-Israeli offensive in Iran, known as Operation Epic Fury, has concluded after achieving its objectives. Rubio expressed a preference for peace and acknowledged President Trump's desire for a deal.  However, Iran's parliamentary speaker Mohammad Ghalibaf asserted that the status quo is intolerable for America and claimed that the US and its allies have jeopardized shipping security and energy transit. Despite the ceasefire, attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz continue to raise tensions between the two countries.

articles.title: Student–faculty ratio at SSUS under scrutiny - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS)'s low student-to-high faculty ratio has been flagged as financially unsustainable. A Syndicate sub-committee assessment revealed a teacher-student ratio significantly below the recommended range, ranging from 1:15 to 1:20. The report highlighted disparities across regional campuses with varying ratios, including 1:3.75 at Ettumanoor, 1:4.59 at Thiruvananthapuram, and 1:6.42 at Panmana.  The committee concluded that the university's current faculty strength of 303 would require a higher student headcount to justify expenses.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: CPI, Kerala Congress (M) suffer electoral drubbing in Ernakulam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Communist Party of India (CPI) and Kerala Congress (M) experienced electoral losses in the Ernakulam district Assembly elections.  Mathew Kuzhalnadan of the Congress defeated N. Arun of the CPI in Muvattupuzha, while V. D Satheesan of the Congress defeated E.T. Taison of the CPI in Paravur. The decline in votes for both parties was attributed to anti-incumbency factors and consolidation of minority votes towards the United Democratic Front (UDF).  The results reflected a broader trend of the Left front's performance declining in the state.

articles.title: U.P. man jailed over ‘I love Muhammad’ post secures bail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Allahabad High Court granted bail to Nadeem, an individual arrested in Uttar Pradesh last year for posting the words "I Love Muhammad" on Instagram.  Justice Rajiv Lochan Shukla noted that Nadeem has no criminal history and the post did not target any specific caste or community. The government argued that the post was insensitive and led to riots in Bareilly, but Nadeem's lawyer claimed he was falsely implicated.

articles.title: Georgia county poll workers targeted by subpoena seeking their contact details | Georgia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Fulton County, Georgia, is fighting a subpoena from Dan Bishop, the interim US attorney for North Carolina's middle district, seeking contact information for thousands of poll workers from the 2020 election. The county argues that the subpoena is politically motivated harassment and beyond the statute of limitations.  The county also claims the FBI raid on their offices in January was based on debunked election denialist claims and seeks to protect its sovereign authority over elections. Michael McNulty, policy director for Issue One, a voting rights organization, calls this an attempt at intimidation and control of elections.

articles.title: Bombay High Court directs Maharashtra government to ease travel curbs on Sangram Patil, U.K.-based doctor booked for posts on PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bombay High Court ordered the Maharashtra government to modify a lookout circular (LOC) against Sangram Patil, a UK-based doctor and YouTuber, so he can return to the United Kingdom by May 11th.  Patil, who is named in an FIR for alleged posts critical of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and BJP leaders, was prevented from returning to the UK after immigration authorities cited the LOC. The court heard arguments from Patil's legal team and the state government, with the main petition seeking quashing of the FIR still pending after the summer vacation.

articles.title: LIVE: Arsenal 1-0 Atletico Madrid (2-1 agg) – Champions League semifinal | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Arsenal defeated Atletico Madrid 1-0 in the second leg of their UEFA Champions League semifinal at Emirates Stadium, securing a 2-1 aggregate victory.  The goal came from Bukayo Saka in the first half, extending Arsenal's lead after the 1-1 draw in the first leg last week at Atletico's Metropolitano Stadium.

articles.title: Senate Republicans propose package including $1bn that could go to Trump ballroom | US Senate | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senate Republicans released a new immigration enforcement funding package that includes $1 billion for security measures related to the White House's "East Wing modernization project". The proposal, which is part of a wider bill aimed at funding ICE and other agencies involved in Trump's mass deportation efforts, does not explicitly mention the ballroom but proposes funds for Secret Service enhancements within the White House compound.  The United States Secret Service, responsible for securing the White House, will use these funds to enhance security features related to the project, citing the need to protect presidents and their staff following recent assassination attempts. Senate Democrats criticized the proposal, arguing that it diverts funding from pressing issues like rising prices while continuing Trump's "cruel mass deportation campaign".

articles.title: Cabinet panel clears Railway Ministry’s three multitracking projects in six States - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved three multitracking projects for the Railway Ministry with a total cost of ₹23,437 crore. These projects will increase the existing railway network by about 901 km in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. The projects are expected to be completed by 2030-31 and will enhance connectivity to approximately 4,161 villages, improve rail connectivity to several tourist destinations, and provide seamless connectivity for people, goods, and services.

articles.title: New FBI vetting by USCIS for Green Cards: Who will be affected? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: USCIS has expanded access to the FBI's criminal history database for immigration applications, requiring officers to re-submit pending cases for enhanced background checks. The agency is implementing these changes to strengthen vetting and screening processes, with a focus on identifying criminal actors.  The new security measures affect individuals whose cases are pending as of April 27th, but the USCIS assures that delays will be brief.

articles.title: US plans to hike tariffs on EU cars to 25% will hit luxury market the most | Trade War News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States plans to increase tariffs on the European Union's auto sector from 15% to 25%, reversing a deal reached in August. This move, which is being attributed to the EU's failure to implement the trade agreement fully, could significantly impact luxury car manufacturers like BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Volkswagen. The US Trade Representative stated that the tariffs will be implemented despite previous rulings limiting the president's ability to impose sweeping global tariffs.  The move is expected to increase costs for consumers who purchase high-end vehicles from European automakers.

articles.title: ‘Grotesque’: parties criticise Reform UK plan to set up migrant detention centres in Green-voting areas | Local elections 2006 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Zia Yusuf, leader of the Reform party, announced a policy prioritizing the siting of migrant detention centers in areas with Green MPs or councils. This move sparked condemnation from both the Greens and Labour, while the Conservatives dismissed it as "not a serious policy."  The policy was met with mixed reactions, with some voters expressing disapproval and others seeing it as an attempt to garner attention for the party. The announcement has also been seen as part of a broader strategy by Reform to establish itself as a viable alternative to the Greens in upcoming elections.

articles.title: A shifting political arithmetic in Punjab - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is preparing for a solo run in the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, aiming to capitalize on recent electoral successes. The party has been present in Punjab since independence and its vote share has fluctuated between 6%-7% when contesting alone and 8% when allied with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD). In 2022, it secured 6.6% of the vote while partnered with the Punjab Lok Congress.

articles.title: US stocks today: S&P 500 and Nasdaq notch records as AI chip stocks surge - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Investors are optimistic about the future of AI and its impact on the economy, driving strong stock performance. The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index reached a record high, fueled by expectations for robust earnings growth from companies like AMD.  Analysts predict continued strong business spending and consumer demand, contributing to overall market optimism.

articles.title: Vtuber Filian: VTuber Filian vanishes online after months away, massive content wipe shocks fans - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Filian, a popular VTuber known for her entertaining VRChat broadcasts, vanished from all online platforms on May 1, 2026.  She deleted or hidden content on YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, X, and Discord, leaving fans confused about the reason behind her sudden disappearance. The lack of explanation has sparked speculation about a rebranding strategy, an extended hiatus, or even quitting streaming altogether. Filian has not provided any official statement regarding her actions, leaving fans to speculate and await further updates.

articles.title: Could OPEC break lead to era of energy volatility? | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran attacked a UAE petroleum site in Fujairah, escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. The attack comes just days after the UAE announced its departure from OPEC, raising concerns about global oil market stability and potentially accelerating the transition to renewables.  The incident underscores the volatility of the energy landscape as oil prices continue to rise.

articles.title: Australia news live: banks pass on interest rate hike to customers; Sydney ‘globalise the intifada’ forum held in park | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Reserve Bank of Australia increased the cash rate from 4.1% to 4.35%, prompting all four major Australian banks to pass on the increase to their variable home loan customers.  The move follows a third consecutive rate hike and comes after the government announced $74 million in funding for a national center dedicated to combating online violent extremism. The decision was met with mixed reactions, including concerns about freedom of political communication and legal challenges to bans on certain phrases.

articles.title: US to take steps to curb antidepressant prescribing, RFK Jr says | Robert F Kennedy Jr | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Robert F Kennedy Jr., the former Trump administration’s health secretary, announced a plan by the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to curb antidepressant use in the US. The plan aims to promote deprescribing when clinically indicated and increase access to non-medication options for treating depression, including psychotherapy, diet, physical activity, and social connection. The HHS also provided guidance to mental health practitioners on managing the process of deprescribing and emphasized the importance of evidence-based care.  The American Psychiatric Association supported the administration's plans but expressed concerns about oversimplifying the mental health crisis and called for solutions that address workforce shortages, limited access to care, and uneven distribution of care.

articles.title: US and tech firms strike deal to review AI models for national security before public release | Technology | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Commerce announced agreements with Google DeepMind, Microsoft, and xAI to review early versions of their new AI models before public release. The Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), part of the department, will use these collaborations to assess national security risks related to cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical weapons. This follows similar agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic two years ago, which have led to over 40 evaluations of unreleased models.  The government aims to understand the capabilities of new AI models while protecting national security interests.

articles.title: ‘Hands off Memphis’: protests in Nashville as Tennessee Republicans consider redrawing maps ahead of midterms – live | US voting rights | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Protests continue in Nashville as Tennessee lawmakers hold a special session to consider redistricting maps ahead of the midterm elections.  The proposed map could dissolve the state's only Democratic-held congressional district, centered on Memphis, which has drawn criticism from civil rights groups and clergy members concerned about voter suppression.  Meanwhile, Alabama lawmakers heard testimony today on legislation that would allow a special congressional primary if the US Supreme Court clears the way for the state to change its US House districts. The proposal aims to help Republicans win at least one of two seats currently held by Democrats. In other news, Donald Trump's "Project Freedom" operation seeks to open the Strait of Hormuz and eliminate Iran's nuclear ambitions, but his administration has been criticized for downplaying soaring oil prices and failing to address concerns about potential escalation of tensions with Iran.

articles.title: Stop plotting to oust Keir Starmer, ex-deputy Labour leader urges MPs | Labour party leadership | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tom Watson, a former deputy leader of the Labour Party, warned MPs against plotting to remove Keir Starmer. He cited his own experience in 2006, when then-Prime Minister Tony Blair faced a similar challenge.  While some Labour figures, including Steve Reed, are urging for change, others believe that a leadership challenge is unlikely given the upcoming elections and the potential for further instability.  However, supporters of Andy Burnham are waiting to see local election results before potentially challenging Starmer.

articles.title: Prosecutors to ‘fast-track’ hate crime cases in England and Wales after spate of attacks | Hate crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Parkinson, the director of public prosecutions in England and Wales, has issued new guidance to prosecutors urging them to prioritize hate crime prosecutions against antisemitic attacks. Keir Starmer, the prime minister, called for increased action from universities, arts groups, and charities to combat antisemitism following a recent surge in violence against Jewish people. The government is also considering further sanctions against Iran if it is determined to be behind the recent attacks.  Vivienne Stern, chief executive of Universities UK, acknowledged that antisemitism persists despite efforts to address it.

articles.title: CSB Bank cautious on gold loans, focuses on wholesale business, says MD Pralay Mondal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: CSB Bank, a Kerala-headquartered lender, anticipates credit growth to remain in the range of 13% to 16%, similar to last year's performance. The bank expects its retail gold loan business to slow down due to global uncertainties and a reduction in re-pledged gold loans. CSB Bank plans to focus on wholesale and small business loans, with growth projected at around 25% to 30%.  The bank also anticipates launching new products such as savings accounts linked to fixed deposits, loan against mutual funds, and transaction banking services for wholesale and SME segments. The bank's capital adequacy ratio is currently around 20%, providing a buffer for potential future challenges.

articles.title: Methana volcano in Greece was never dead: Scientists reveal 100,000 years of hidden magma activity | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists from ETH Zurich have challenged the long-held belief that the Greek volcano, Methana, was dormant for centuries.  Geological studies on zircon crystals found in ancient volcanic rock flows revealed that the volcano experienced periods of magma accumulation beneath its surface for over 100,000 years, despite appearing peaceful and inactive. These findings suggest that Methana's history contradicts the traditional definition of an extinct volcano, as it remained active underground during this period.  The study suggests that some volcanoes previously considered extinct might still harbor active magma chambers.

articles.title: MoD has no system to detect civilian harm caused by military, study shows | Ministry of Defence | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Defence has revealed that it lacks a system to examine whether UK military action has killed or injured civilians in war. The MoD also does not maintain a central register of civilian harm incidents or allegations, despite acknowledging the need for such a system.  This revelation comes after the Foreign Office closed its international humanitarian law unit and follows reports of mass casualties caused by other countries. While the MoD claims its existing mitigation is effective, critics argue that the lack of systematic investigation could jeopardize the UK's compliance with international humanitarian law.

articles.title: Sebi cautions market players on risks from AI tools like Mythos; sets up task force - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, India's securities regulator, has formed a task force called cyber-suraksha.ai to address the cybersecurity risks posed by AI-driven tools in the financial market. The task force will examine vulnerabilities, develop mitigation strategies, and ensure timely reporting of cyber incidents.  The regulator has also issued an advisory outlining steps for strengthening cybersecurity frameworks, including regular vulnerability assessments and adoption of measures like zero-trust architecture.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Amelia Earhart: “Some of us have great runways already built for us. If you have one, take off. But if you don't have one, realize it is your responsibility to grab a shovel and build one for yourself and for those who will follow after you.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amelia Earhart's quote, "Some of us have great runways already built for us. If you have one, take off. But if you don't have one, realize it is your responsibility to grab a shovel and build one for yourself and for those who will follow after you," emphasizes the importance of both seizing opportunities and creating new ones. The quote acknowledges that some individuals are born into advantageous circumstances with access to resources and support systems, while others face significant challenges. It underscores the need for personal responsibility in overcoming obstacles and building a path forward, not only for oneself but also for future generations.  This message remains relevant today as people continue to navigate varying levels of opportunity and strive for progress.

articles.title: Andrew Tate sought CPS assurance he would not be arrested if he returned to UK, court hears | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate sought written assurances from the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) that they wouldn't be arrested if they returned to the UK for a civil case. The CPS declined, stating there was no reason to withdraw warrants, and that they could not provide assurances of non-arrest.  The Tates are facing 21 criminal charges in the UK and 10 charges in Romania, with both brothers denying all wrongdoing. A judge will decide on a stay for the civil case and delay the trial date.

articles.title: Poonawalla Fincorp Q4 results: Profit jumps 70% QoQ to Rs 255 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Poonawalla Fincorp reported assets under management exceeding Rs 60,000 crore at the end of March, driven by a 78% year-on-year increase in net interest income. The lender's pre-provision operating profit surged 109%, reflecting improved operating leverage and business volumes.  The company also saw improvements in asset quality, with gross non-performing assets declining to 1.44% from 1.51% in the previous quarter. Poonawalla Fincorp's capital adequacy ratio stood at 16.83%, exceeding regulatory requirements, and its liquidity buffer reached Rs 7,590 crore.

articles.title: Eta Aquarid meteor shower to peak overnight on May 5–6: Best viewing times, visibility tips, and how to catch the brightest shooting stars | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Eta Aquarid meteor shower is reaching its peak activity, offering a chance to witness shooting stars.  While the timing of observation is crucial for maximizing visibility, the presence of a bright Moon will likely reduce the number of visible meteors this year. The optimal viewing time is at dawn on May 6th, when the radiant will be in a more favorable position for viewing. Although the shower may not offer a steady stream of meteors, those who observe during this period are likely to see several shooting stars.

articles.title: Ex-US spy for Israel calls for Gaza ethnic cleansing as he seeks Knesset seat | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jonathan Pollard, a former US navy intelligence analyst who served 30 years for spying for Israel, announced his candidacy for the Knesset.  He plans to run on a platform of ethnic cleansing and annexation of Gaza. Pollard blames the Israeli government for failing to prevent the Hamas attack in October that killed nearly 1,200 people and triggered the Gaza war. He was released from prison in 2015 after serving his sentence and has since become a vocal critic of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

articles.title: ideaForge Technology bulk deal: BNP Paribas buys Rs 39 crore worth shares in this multibagger - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several investors, including BNP Paribas, QE Securities LLP, and NK Securities Research Private Limited, purchased a significant amount of shares in Ideaforge Technology. These bulk deals, valued at around Rs 26 crore, were executed within a narrow price band of Rs 776 – Rs 783 per share, indicating strong demand for the stock. The company's shares closed at Rs 804.10 on Monday, up by Rs 73.10 or 10% over the previous day's closing price.

articles.title: Scientists discover a 66-foot giant tree in the Andes, and it’s related to tomatoes and potatoes | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A new genus, Daturodendron, has been officially recognized in the Andean cloud forests of Colombia and Peru. The towering tree, reaching up to 66 feet tall, belongs to the Solanaceae family, making it a close relative of tomatoes, potatoes, and eggplants. Researchers at the University of Cartagena and the Royal Botanic Gardens identified this new genus through phylotranscriptomic analysis, revealing its unique genetic traits and evolutionary history within nightshades.  Daturodendron is notable for its pendant flowers, tough corollas, and particular seed shapes, as well as its production of tropane alkaloids like scopolamine and hyoscyamine.

articles.title: US-Iran truce teeters on meltdown as stalemate takes toll on each side | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The month-old ceasefire between Iran and the US appears to be in jeopardy as Iranian missiles targeted the United Arab Emirates, escalating tensions despite US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's assertion that the truce remains intact.  Hegseth stated the temporary operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was intended to encourage commercial ships through the waterway and that the ceasefire is not over.  Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused the US of breaching the ceasefire, while President Donald Trump maintains he believes Iran wants a deal despite recent violence in the strait. The situation remains volatile with no immediate response from Iran, but both sides continue to engage in backdoor diplomacy through Pakistan.

articles.title: Vedanta demerger sets stage for value unlocking, global scale: Chairman Anil Agarwal - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta, a metal major, completed its demerger on May 1, 2026, creating multiple independent, globally competitive entities. The company reported record-breaking earnings for FY26, with a 92% year-on-year surge in consolidated net profit and total revenues that rose by 47%.  Agarwal, the chairman of Vedanta, emphasized that the demerger will unlock value through distinct growth plans for each vertical, including aluminum, oil & gas, power, and iron & steel. He highlighted investments of Rs 15,000 crore in growth capex to create a stronger and more resilient group.

articles.title: Map of dominance: Why Iran can’t afford to give up Hormuz control | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) released a map expanding its maritime area of control, including sections of the United Arab Emirates' coastline. This escalation comes as US President Donald Trump launched "Project Freedom," sending naval forces to escort stranded tankers through the Strait of Hormuz. The UAE reported drone and missile attacks on energy facilities, blaming Iran.  While Iran denies involvement in these attacks, it acknowledges its control over the Strait is a strategic leverage point in its ongoing conflict with the US and Israel. Experts say this control allows Iran to impose economic costs on the US and global markets, impacting energy prices and supply chains.

articles.title: The staggering amount Cristiano Ronaldo earns per Instagram post as the most-followed person in the world | Football News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Instagram has become a major platform for sports marketing, with athletes and celebrities generating significant revenue through sponsored posts. Cristiano Ronaldo, with his massive following on the platform, is at the forefront of this trend, earning estimated $3.23 million per post.  His success stems from both the size of his audience and their engagement levels, which translate into commercial value for brands. He has leveraged this influence to build a multi-faceted business empire that includes long-term partnerships with companies like Nike and Binance, as well as ventures in digital space such as NFTs. Ronaldo's career earnings have surpassed $1 billion, making him one of the highest-paid athletes globally.  He is also focused on achieving personal goals before retiring from football, including reaching 1,000 career goals and potentially winning a World Cup title with Portugal.

articles.title: Dark clouds, protests and resignations dampen start of 61st Venice Biennale | Venice Biennale 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The 61st Venice Biennale began under grey skies and rain, with political tension dominating proceedings. Lubaina Himid, the British entrant whose work explores Britain's colonial past, showcased large-scale paintings and sound collage at the UK pavilion. The Russian pavilion, despite not being open to the public, saw techno music pumping out as a symbolic gesture of its presence.  The event also featured protests against Israel's participation and the resignation of the jury due to their inclusion. Tetyana Berezhna, Ukrainian culture minister, highlighted the significance of cultural platforms in shaping global perception. The Biennale is being curated by Marie Hélène Pereira, Rasha Salti, Gabe Beckhurst Feijoo, Rory Tsapayi and Siddhartha Mitter, who are honoring the late curator Koyo Kouoh.

articles.title: Bull market or trading illusion? Nithin Kamath says India's stock market data is sending mixed signals - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Kamath, a prominent figure in the Indian brokerage industry, suggests that despite market recovery and strong stock momentum, core delivery-based equity activity remains subdued. Zerodha, his company, has witnessed significant growth in margin trading funding (MTF), indicating continued appetite for leveraged bets.  While gross SIP flows have reached record levels, most major brokers earn little or no distribution commission from direct mutual funds. Kamath argues that a large portion of revenue growth may stem from MTF activity and highlights a disparity in client behavior across platforms, with some brokers experiencing significantly higher trading ratios than Zerodha.

articles.title: US push for Lebanon and Israel leaders to meet could inflame tensions | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Joseph Aoun of Lebanon is under pressure to meet with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but the decision faces significant opposition both domestically and regionally.  Aoun's visit to the White House in May, a month after direct Israeli-Lebanese negotiations, has sparked concerns about escalating tensions within Lebanon. While some analysts believe such a meeting could be beneficial for peacemaking efforts, others warn that it would further inflame internal divisions and undermine existing agreements. The US administration is pushing for the meeting as part of its broader strategy to broker peace in the region, but Saudi Arabia and other Arab nations are hesitant due to ongoing hostilities and concerns about Lebanon's position on normalizing relations with Israel.

articles.title: 70% H-1B approvals from India in FY 2025 revealed in new report, US senator shocked - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Eric Schmitt expressed concern over the H-1B visa approval numbers for FY 2025, which showed India leading with 283,772 approvals and China trailing with 49,161.  Schmitt criticized the system as allowing companies to exploit it while American workers face job losses. He cited reports of fraudulent credentials in India and Chinese workers stealing US intellectual property. Immigration entrepreneur James Blunt also commented on the low approval numbers compared to the size of the US economy, suggesting they do not indicate a significant influx.

articles.title: Players would boycott French Open over prize money dispute, says Sabalenka - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Players threatened to boycott the French Open if their prize money is not increased. Aryna Sabalenka, world number one, and Coco Gauff voiced support for this drastic step, citing that current prize money distribution remains unfair compared to other Grand Slams like Wimbledon and the US Open.  The players are demanding a 22% share of tournament revenue, which is currently less than 15%, while organizers offered a 9.5% increase to €61.7 million for this year's tournament. The French Tennis Federation has not yet responded to requests for comment.

articles.title: Alberta voter data leaked as separatists file signatures for independence vote | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alberta separatists have submitted over 300,000 signatures to Elections Alberta in support of an independence referendum. However, the effort was met with controversy after a separatist-linked group posted personal data of nearly 3 million residents online, sparking fears of political interference. The province's government has changed the rules for citizen-initiated referendums, making it easier to bring one forward. Indigenous nations have also voiced concerns about the referendum potentially violating treaty rights.  The court is currently reviewing the situation and Elections Alberta is investigating a data breach involving voter information.

articles.title: Israeli army chief says West Bank troops ‘killing like we haven’t killed since 1967’ | West Bank | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Maj Gen Avi Bluth, head of the Israel Defense Forces’ central command, made controversial remarks about his troops' actions in the West Bank.  He reportedly stated that his soldiers had killed 42 Palestinian stone-throwers last year and justified these acts as terrorism, while noting a lack of such action against Jewish settler militants who engage in similar behavior. Bluth also admitted to loosening legal constraints on Israeli soldiers, allowing for maiming Palestinians attempting to cross the separation barrier into Israel.  His comments have sparked criticism, with some questioning the justification of his actions and their impact on Palestinian lives.

articles.title: ‘In learning organisations, failure is not a bad word’ - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
articles.rephrased_article: SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) and The Hindu hosted a panel discussion on "The Future Reimagined – Discover, Decide, Define Your Career" where speakers emphasized the importance of learning organizations for employee success.  Speakers highlighted that organizations that invest in employee upskilling and reskilling are more likely to thrive. They stressed the need for a culture that embraces failure as a learning opportunity and rewards employees for their efforts to develop new skills. Amardeep Devadasan, Senior Vice-President, RR Donnelley & Williams Lea, echoed this sentiment, emphasizing that learning should be a pull rather than a push.  Bijumon Jacob, Head-India Operations, Human Resources, Ejada, Dubai, also emphasized the importance of fostering a mindset shift within employees to embrace continuous learning and development.

articles.title: Why Europe’s car industry is at the centre of a new US trade war | Trade War News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced an increase in tariffs on European cars and trucks imported to the US from 15 percent to 25 percent, citing the EU's alleged failure to comply with a trade agreement. The move comes as tensions between the two sides escalate over trade disputes and geopolitical issues.  The EU has rejected these claims and is considering retaliatory measures, including tariffs on US goods. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz expressed concern that these tariffs target Germany specifically and are politically motivated.  The European Commission has stated its commitment to enforcing the trade agreement and will continue negotiations with the US. The impact of this tariff threat remains unclear, but it could significantly affect the EU's automotive industry, particularly Germany, which is heavily reliant on exports.

articles.title: A veneer of normality has returned to Tehran, but fears for the future are rife | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Life in Tehran has returned to a semblance of normalcy since the ceasefire with the US and Israel, but underlying anxieties persist.  The International Monetary Fund estimates that inflation could reach 70% this year, prompting economic hardship for many Iranians. Sara, a teacher who lost her job due to the war's impact, is struggling to find work amidst rising tuition fees at private institutions. Despite the easing of restrictions, tensions remain high between Iran and the US, with ongoing attacks in the Gulf and stalled negotiations.

articles.title: CIC recommends DoPT include sub-caste data in UPSC results to broaden reach of affirmative action - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Information Commission (CIC) has recommended that the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) include sub-caste details in civil services exam lists to better assess the distribution of reservation benefits. The recommendation came after the CIC reviewed an appeal seeking caste-wise data for the 1995 Indian Administrative Service examination.  The DoPT argued that records were not available at the sub-caste level, but the CIC suggested including this information in future disclosures to ensure transparency and reach a wider range of communities.

articles.title: Iran’s judiciary vows action against ‘enemy’s mercenaries’ amid executions | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s judiciary has vowed to continue taking “decisive” action against individuals they accuse of working for foreign interests, escalating executions and asset seizures.  The judiciary cited national security as justification for the actions following the execution of three men in Mashhad accused of being agents of Israel's Mossad intelligence service. The authorities have also confiscated assets from Iranians suspected of supporting anti-government activities, citing the ongoing war with the United States and Israel as a contributing factor to economic instability.  The judiciary chief, Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Ejei, warned against hoarding goods and price gouging.

articles.title: Political row as report calls for sweeping cuts to French public broadcasting | France | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Charles Alloncle, a member of the Union of the Right for the Republic (UDR) party, published a report recommending sweeping cuts to public broadcasting in France. The report, which was the result of a parliamentary inquiry into the neutrality and financing of state TV and radio, has been met with strong criticism from left-leaning politicians and media experts.  Emmanuel Macron, the current president, has previously expressed skepticism towards public broadcasting but has not adopted Alloncle's recommendations. Delphine Ernotte, head of France Télévisions, argued that the report was biased and would weaken public broadcasting. The report has been seen as a potential precursor to privatization efforts by the far-right party, which is currently leading in the polls.

articles.title: EC notifies Kerala poll results - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India issued a gazette notification on Tuesday, officially announcing the members elected to the Kerala Legislative Assembly for the 2026 elections. The United Democratic Front (UDF) secured 102 seats, while the Left Democratic Front (LDF) won 35 and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) garnered three.  The results were declared on Monday after the election process concluded.

articles.title: UAE comes under Iranian attacks for second consecutive day | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates has been targeted by Iranian missiles and drones for the second consecutive day, following a previous attack on Monday.  Iranian forces launched a salvo of missiles and drones at UAE facilities, including a key oil terminal in Fujairah. The attacks came amid heightened tensions between Iran and the United States, with US Central Command confirming that Iran fired cruise missiles and drones at US naval assets and commercial ships.  The escalation follows a new US initiative to guide vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been used by Iran to control access to global energy exports.

articles.title: Rescue of Timmy the whale ‘an all-round catastrophe’ after tracker failure | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Marine biologists, whale experts, and environmental groups have criticized a privately funded operation to release a stranded humpback whale off the coast of Germany. The whale, nicknamed Timmy, was transported in a barge to waters off Denmark but its health remains unknown after the tracker fitted to it failed to function.  The rescue initiative, estimated to cost €1.5m, was funded in part by Karin Walter-Mommert, owner of one of Europe's largest racehorse portfolios, and faced criticism for not providing data on the whale's condition or its release process. The German Oceanographic Museum believes the whale is likely dead and called for transparency from organizers.

articles.title: Put petty politics aside, says Rahul Gandhi, as he backs Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the BJP's victory in the West Bengal and Assam Assembly elections as a "theft" of the popular mandate, alleging it marks a step towards destroying Indian democracy. He expressed support for the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and cautioned against political schadenfreude over the party's defeat.  Gandhi urged political parties to prioritize India above partisan considerations.

articles.title: Microsoft, Google, xAI give US access to AI models for security testing | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Microsoft, Google, and xAI have agreed to provide the US federal government with access to their new artificial intelligence models for national security testing. The agreement, announced by the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) at the Department of Commerce, aims to assess potential security risks associated with these advanced AI systems before deployment.  The move follows a Pentagon agreement with seven tech giants to use their AI in classified systems and builds on previous agreements between the US government and companies like OpenAI and Anthropic.

articles.title: Woman, three children murdered in Multan; scene staged as suicide: officials - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Multan, Pakistan, are investigating the deaths of a woman and her three children who were found dead in their home. Initial findings suggest the case was staged as a suicide but evidence collected from the scene indicates that the victims may have been strangled before being hanged. The CPO stated that an initial investigation revealed a domestic dispute occurred earlier in the day, raising concerns of possible evidence tampering.  The husband and his brother are currently under custody for questioning.

articles.title: Farage’s partner refuses to confirm how she paid for house in his constituency | Nigel Farage | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nigel Farage’s partner, Laure Ferrari, refused to confirm how she paid for a house in his Clacton constituency.  Ferrari told Le Monde that she "encouraged" several key moments in Farage's political career and insisted that if he became prime minister, she would not be involved in UK affairs. Labour called on Farage to clarify the purchase of the property, which was initially claimed by him but later revealed to be owned by Ferrari. The BBC investigation found evidence suggesting Ferrari’s family wealth may have been used to fund the purchase.

articles.title: Put petty politics aside, says Rahul Gandhi, as he backs Mamata Banerjee - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the BJP's victory in the West Bengal and Assam Assembly elections as a "theft" of the popular mandate, alleging it was part of the party's attempt to destroy Indian democracy.  He expressed support for the Trinamool Congress (TMC) and urged political parties to prioritize national interests over partisan concerns. Gandhi also noted that this is not an isolated incident, referencing previous instances of electoral manipulation by the BJP.

articles.title: Indian-origin techie-doctor duo considers moving to Dubai: No Green Card, can't visit home on H-1B - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: H-1B visa holders in the US are facing significant delays in obtaining visa stamps to enter India, leading to travel disruptions and family separation. Sam Peak, an immigration analyst, shared stories of a techie-doctor couple who are considering relocating to Dubai due to these delays. The man, with a National Interest Waiver (NIW) for his essential work, is stuck in a long queue despite being eligible for faster Green Card processing. His wife, a top cardiologist at a prestigious hospital on the East Coast, has also been unable to return home for over three years.  The couple's experience highlights the challenges faced by H-1B holders in balancing their professional contributions with family ties and travel restrictions.

articles.title: UK convicts four Palestine Action activists over break-in at Israeli firm | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Palestine Action, a banned group, was found guilty of criminal damage relating to a 2024 raid on an Elbit Systems UK facility in Bristol. Four members of the group were convicted, including Charlotte Head and Samuel Corner who were found guilty of striking a police officer with a sledgehammer. The group’s actions caused approximately one million pounds ($1.36m) worth of damage.  The group's defense team argued that their actions saved lives in Palestine.

articles.title: Imran’s sisters call for public pressure as authorities deny jail meeting - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Imran Khan's sisters, along with Salman Akram Raja, and other PTI leaders attempted to meet the incarcerated former prime minister at Adiala jail on Tuesday.  Law enforcement officials denied them access, prompting Aleema Khan, Noreen Khan, and Uzma Khan to call for public pressure on the government. Sheikh Waqas Akram, the party's central information secretary, criticized the government for ignoring court orders regarding visitation rights. The PTI also reacted strongly to a report from the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) which highlighted concerns about human rights violations and the weakening rule of law in the country.

articles.title: Carney appoints former war crimes prosecutor as Canada governor general | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Carney, Canada's prime minister, appointed Louise Arbour, a former supreme court justice and war crimes prosecutor, as the country's new governor general.  Arbour will succeed Mary Simon, who became the first Indigenous person to hold the role in 2021. The appointment reflects the importance of global institutions according to Carney, who praised Arbour for her extensive experience in law and international affairs.  Arbour is the oldest person ever appointed to the position at age 79. She will serve a five-year term as the commander-in-chief of the Canadian armed forces.

articles.title: Tiruchi orthography researchers decipher ancient inscription in Courtrallam hill cave - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Balakrishnan and Mathur B. Pavendan, orthography researchers from Tiruchi, have successfully deciphered an inscription found in the Sanyasi Pudavu cave shelter in Tenkasi district. The inscription, which translates to "Your path is that of wisdom like a holy tank; Even if you take content from all water bodies in seven towns the essence remains one," was discovered many years ago but remained undeciphered.

articles.title: US-Iran ceasefire holds despite Hormuz standoff: Pentagon chief Hegseth | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Despite bursts of military action around the Strait of Hormuz, the US-Iran ceasefire remains in place. Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth stated that President Donald Trump will decide when the truce ends and emphasized the US campaign to reopen Hormuz is separate from the broader US-Israeli assault on Iran.  While traffic in the strait remains largely at a standstill, Hegseth reported securing passage for two US-flagged commercial ships and asserted that the US operation is temporary and will be taken over by other countries soon.

articles.title: What's stopping Pakistan from making the transition to renewable energy? - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan faces challenges in transitioning to renewable energy despite its potential for solar, wind, and hydropower. Dr Aazir Khan, director of the Integrated Engineering Center of Excellence at the University of Lahore, highlights these hurdles including a lack of grid adaptation, financial frameworks, and supportive policies. The Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference 2026 aims to address these challenges and chart a path forward for renewable energy adoption in Pakistan.

articles.title: Four Palestine Action activists convicted of criminal damage | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Four Palestine Action activists were found guilty of criminal damage for their break-in at an Elbit Systems factory in Bristol.  The group, including Charlotte Head, Samuel Corner, Leona Kamio, and Fatema Rajwani, smashed equipment and sprayed paint on the property after crashing through a fence. Corner was also found guilty of inflicting grievous bodily harm on a police officer, Sgt Kate Evans, with a sledgehammer. The activists claimed their actions were meant to disarm Israeli military drones but were later acquitted of aggravated burglary charges.  The defendants will be sentenced on June 12th.

articles.title: Lokayukta directs top officials to be added as respondents in K.R. Circle underpass case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lokayukta Justice B.S. Patil has added several top officials of the state and Bengaluru, including the Chief Secretary and the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) chief, as respondents in a case concerning the death of a software engineer who drowned in the flooded K.R. Circle underpass in 2023.  The case was initiated after Justice Patil inspected the underpass following heavy rains on April 29th, and subsequently ordered the addition of these officials to the proceedings.

articles.title: Sudan accuses Ethiopia, UAE of being behind recent drone attacks | Sudan war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sudan has accused Ethiopia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) of being behind recent drone attacks, claiming evidence points to drones supplied by the UAE.  The Sudanese government recalled its ambassador from Ethiopia, citing the attack on Khartoum International Airport as a catalyst for the accusations. Ethiopia’s Foreign Ministry dismissed the allegations as “baseless” and accused Sudan of fueling unrest in the Tigray region. The United Nations has described the conflict as the world's worst humanitarian crisis, with over 150,000 deaths and 14 million displaced people.

articles.title: I’ve asked power in Pakistan one question for ten years on my podcast. This is the answer - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A decade of conversations with Pakistani politicians, including Prime Ministers and military leaders, have yielded the same answer: a lack of action despite acknowledging the country's problems.  Despite their ability to articulate solutions in private, these individuals often fail to deliver concrete plans when in public office. The electorate, meanwhile, is characterized by polarization and a lack of political awareness, further hindering progress. This cycle of inaction has been exacerbated by Pakistan's history of attempting technocratic solutions that have ultimately failed due to the country's deeply entrenched political system.  The article argues that Pakistan needs a new model for governance, one that prioritizes long-term stability and institutional reform over short-term political gains.

articles.title: Romania’s pro-Europe government collapses unleashing fresh turmoil | Romania | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Romania’s pro-European government has collapsed following a no-confidence vote, unleashing renewed political turmoil. The motion was tabled by the Social Democrats (PSD) and the far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR) and won with 281 votes in the 464-seat parliament.  President Nicuşor Dan, who must nominate a new prime minister, is expected to invite parties for negotiations to rebuild the coalition. The embattled prime minister, Ilie Bolojan, led a minority government since late last month after the PSD walked out of the coalition and allied with the AUR.

articles.title: Cabinet approves four more judges for Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Cabinet approved an increase in the number of Supreme Court judges from 34 to 38, a move aimed at addressing the ongoing backlog of cases.  The amendment will be introduced in Parliament and requires approval from the Parliament. The current backlog stands at 92,385 cases, with several judges scheduled to retire this year. This decision follows a six-year hiatus since the last increase in 2019.

articles.title: What’s happening in Mali one week after attack by armed groups? All we know | Armed Groups News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Assimi Goita, the leader of Mali’s military government, has assumed the role of defense minister following the death of his predecessor.  The attacks by armed groups, including al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and the Tuareg-dominated FLA, have resulted in a security crisis, with at least 23 people killed and civilians facing hunger and potential harm. The situation is further complicated by Russian mercenary group Wagner's presence in Mali, which has been accused of protecting the military government while also clashing with JNIM fighters.  The UN Human Rights Office has called for an end to the fighting and protection of civilians.

articles.title: JUI-F to hold nationwide protests on Wednesday, Friday over killing of cleric Maulana Idrees - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Maulana Fazlur Rehman, leader of the JUI-F, announced protests across Pakistan against the death of prominent cleric Maulana Idrees.  Idrees was killed by unidentified assailants on Tuesday while traveling to Darul Uloom Noumania.  Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed condolences and pledged to arrest the killers. The incident has prompted investigations from both KP Inspector General Zulfiqar Hameed and the Mardan regional police officer.

articles.title: ‘It’s quite distressing’: rate rise brings new pain for would-be homebuyers | Interest rates | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dani Hunterford, a 24-year-old Australian, and her husband are struggling to save for a home purchase due to the recent Reserve Bank rate hikes. Gerard Burg, head of research at Cotality, notes that while property prices have been declining in Sydney and Melbourne, they haven't significantly impacted the most expensive end of the market where first-time buyers typically seek homes. The impact of higher interest rates on borrowing capacity is significant for potential buyers, making homeownership increasingly challenging. Sally Tindall, director of digital insights at Canstar, suggests that some buyers may be able to take advantage of falling prices in certain markets but warns against overlooking the long-term implications of higher interest rates and debt levels.

articles.title: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu unveils NABARD credit plan of ₹5.11 lakh crore for 2026–27 fiscal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, unveiled a ₹5.11 lakh crore credit plan for the Financial Year 2026–27, representing a 20% increase from the previous year. The plan prioritizes agriculture and allied activities with allocations for crop loans, animal husbandry, farm mechanization, fisheries, horticulture, and agricultural infrastructure.  NABARD officials, including M.R. Gopal, Chief General Manager, and representatives from leading banks, attended the unveiling.

articles.title: ‘Protecting Britishers is our top priority’: Keir Starmer reacts as hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise kills three - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the UK Prime Minister, stated that his government is working with international partners to ensure the safety of British nationals aboard the stranded Antarctic expedition cruise MV Hondius.  At least three deaths have been reported on board, including two passengers who died in Johannesburg after being medically evacuated. The outbreak of hantavirus has sparked an international health response involving Dutch, South African and other authorities. The ship is currently anchored off Cape Verde while authorities investigate the cause of the outbreak.

articles.title: What’s the significance of UAE’s Fujairah, hit on Monday? | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) accused Iran of launching a barrage of missiles and drones at the port of Fujairah, injuring three Indian nationals and setting an oil refinery ablaze. The UAE's Ministry of Defence reported engaging 12 ballistic missiles, three cruise missiles, and four drones launched from Iran.  The incident marks Iran's first attack on the UAE since the US-Iran ceasefire took effect in April. India’s Ministry of External Affairs condemned the attacks as unacceptable and called for an end to hostilities.

articles.title: IHC orders removal of YouTuber Rajab Butt's name from Passport Control List - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Islamabad High Court ruled that the removal of YouTuber Rajab Butt's name from the Passport Control List (PCL) is a violation of his fundamental rights. The court found that the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) had no legal grounds for placing Butt on the PCL, as there was no show-cause notice issued prior to the action and the investigation was already concluded. The court ordered immediate removal from the list, noting that the petitioner's cooperation with the inquiry process rendered the travel ban unnecessary.  The court also criticized the NCCIA for not objecting to the removal of Butt's name from the PCL after his cooperation.

articles.title: Philip Morris uses secret Senate hearing to warn illegal tobacco in Australia could wipe out legal trade by 2030 | Health | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Philip Morris, a tobacco giant, told a closed-door Senate hearing that soaring illegal cigarette trade would wipe out legal products in Australia by 2030. The company argued for lower federal tobacco excise to undercut hidden market operators, but Labor, the Greens, and the federal government criticized the committee chair's decision to hold the private session.  Julian Hill, the federal customs minister, called for transparency from tobacco manufacturers regarding illicit tobacco sales and supply chains, while Mark Butler, the health minister, urged MPs to adhere to WHO guidelines on engagement with tobacco companies.

articles.title: Assam elections 2026: How have smaller allies fared? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Himanta Biswa Sarma of the BJP led the North-East Democratic Alliance (NEDA) to victory in Assam's Assembly elections, securing a second term with 102 seats. The Congress-led alliance won only 21 seats, while the All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) and Trinamool Congress secured two and one seat respectively.  The BJP campaigned on issues of illegal immigration removal and infrastructure development.

articles.title: Pakistani man pleads guilty for human smuggling in US, charged $40,000 to bring people on 'dunki route' for film work - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Ali Haider, a 49-year-old Pakistani man, pleaded guilty in a US court to leading an international human smuggling conspiracy.  He operated two fake film production companies and used them to obtain visas for Pakistani nationals to travel to Latin American countries with the intention of illegally crossing into the US through the southern border. Haider charged each person $40,000 for this service. He faces a minimum penalty of three years in prison and a maximum of 10 years.

articles.title: Boko Haram attack kills 23 soldiers in Chad’s Lake Chad region | Boko Haram News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Chad’s army confirmed that a Boko Haram attack on a military post in the Lake Chad region killed at least 23 soldiers and injured 26. The attack occurred on Monday night on the island of Barka Tolorom, with the Chadian president vowing to continue fighting against the group.  The attack comes amidst an ongoing struggle between Chad’s military and Boko Haram, which has been increasingly active in the region.

articles.title: PTI’s Raja stands by decision on Punjab Coordination and Monitoring Committee composition - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Salman Akram Raja, secretary general of the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), announced a five-member committee to coordinate organizational matters in Punjab. The committee, under the convenership of Amjad Khan Niazi, will address issues including party organization monitoring, election planning, and prisoner welfare.  Raja defended his decision, stating that while some members have criticized Niazi's past departure from the party, he is deemed the best option to lead the struggle in the province given the current leadership situation.

articles.title: ‘Not a good look’: witnesses refuse to appear before NSW parliamentary hearings after court ruling | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Witnesses are refusing to appear before New South Wales parliamentary inquiries following a recent court ruling invalidating provisions of the Parliamentary Evidence Act that allowed for arrest warrants. The decision, stemming from legal action by Chris Minns's chief of staff, James Cullen, has led to several witnesses declining to cooperate with inquiries into matters of public interest, including the leaking of confidential minutes from a report on the sale of Rosehill Racecourse and identity protections for court proceedings involving children.  The ruling has also stalled legislative progress in the upper house where the opposition and crossbenchers can unite to hold the balance of power.

articles.title: HSBC profits fall amid $400m fraud-related charge and Iran war | HSBC | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: HSBC reported a 4% decline in profits for the first quarter of 2023, attributed to $1.3 billion in potential loan losses and a $400 million fraud-related exposure in its UK investment banking division. The bank's chief financial officer, Pam Kaur, stated that these charges were "idiosyncratic" and did not reflect broader risks within the private credit sector.  Despite concerns about the opaque nature of the industry, Kaur emphasized HSBC's careful approach to managing risk in this area and highlighted that its exposure to private credit was relatively small compared to its overall balance sheet.

articles.title: Romania PM Ilie Bolojan’s government toppled in no-confidence vote | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ilie Bolojan’s government in Romania was toppled in a no-confidence vote, raising concerns about the country's fiscal stability.  The motion, initiated by the left-wing Social Democratic Party (PSD) and the far-right Alliance for the Unity of Romanians party (AUR), garnered 281 votes in favor while four opposed. President Nicusor Dan is expected to invite parties to form a new coalition, potentially with a different member of Bolojan’s National Liberal Party or a technocrat.  The future of Romania's pro-EU coalition remains uncertain as the country faces pressure to narrow its budget deficit and secure EU recovery funds before an August deadline.

articles.title: Temple thefts: Four persons nabbed; recover gold ornaments, silver idol and cash - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chamarajanagar police have arrested four individuals suspected of committing thefts at various temples in the district.  The arrests followed a complaint filed by Prabhuswamy, who reported the theft of a silver idol and valuables from the Sri Chamundeshwari Temple on December 4, 2025. Superintendent of Police M. Muthuraj formed a special team to investigate the case, leading to the recovery of gold ornaments, a silver idol, and cash.

articles.title: Pakistan misses $8bn SEZ investment, 500,000-job targets: minister - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's investment minister, Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh, stated that only four SEZs have advanced beyond the planning stage.  Sheikh emphasized the need to transition from an import-driven economy to one that produces and exports value-added goods. The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) aims to close the trade deficit by promoting value-added manufacturing for re-export to China, with a focus on labor-intensive sectors like textiles, electronics assembly, and light engineering.  The minister also highlighted the importance of improving SEZ governance, security infrastructure, and regulatory frameworks to attract more foreign investment.

articles.title: Rachel Reeves and Scott Bessent argued in person about Iran war, sources say | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the UK chancellor, and Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, engaged in a heated exchange during the spring meetings of the International Monetary Fund.  Their disagreement centered on Reeves' public criticisms of the Iran conflict, which triggered backlash from some within the Trump administration. The row has strained relations between the two countries to levels not seen since the Suez crisis. Despite this tension, Downing Street maintains that the chancellor and treasury secretary have a good relationship and have had constructive conversations.

articles.title: CAF is failing Africa’s World Cup fans | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) is facing criticism for its silence on US travel bans and visa restrictions affecting African fans attending the 2026 World Cup.  FIFA president Gianni Infantino presented a peace prize to Donald Trump, who has made racist remarks about Africa, impacting African teams' fan support. The situation echoes past instances where CAF took a stand against discriminatory FIFA policies, including in 1964 when it withdrew from the World Cup due to unfair allocation of slots for African and Asian teams.  CAF's inaction on this issue is seen as a betrayal of its founding principles and could be interpreted as endorsing discrimination by powerful governments.

articles.title: Results signal political shift in Kannur, says Sunny Joseph - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KPCC president Sunny Joseph criticized the CPI(M)'s performance in the Payyannur Assembly election, calling it a "major setback" for the party. He attributed the loss to public discontent with the government and urged introspection from the leadership and cadre.  Joseph suggested that the developments could lead to further political shifts in the future.

articles.title: ‘Won’t be tolerated’: Starmer warns Iran as UK probes foreign influence amid rising antisemitic attacks - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Keir Starmer warned Iran that any attempts to incite antisemitism or destabilize British society will not be tolerated.  He announced the government is fast-tracking legislation to counter rising antisemitism and investigate possible foreign involvement in recent hate-linked attacks targeting Jewish communities. The UK PM also pledged additional funding for community cohesion and protection, while confirming new anti-terror legislation is being prepared to address state-linked threats. This comes amid growing criticism of the government's response to antisemitism from Jewish community leaders.

articles.title: Nearly 20,000 patients ‘missing’ after initiating treatment at HIV centres, NA committee told - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The National Assembly’s Standing Committee on Health held a meeting to address the rising trend of HIV and AIDS cases in Pakistan. The committee was informed that nearly 20,000 patients who initiated treatment at ART centers for HIV/AIDS are "missing," raising concerns about follow-up, counselling, and patient retention. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal clarified that no new outbreak has occurred this year and the Global Fund is supporting Pakistan's HIV/AIDS programs. The committee also noted localized outbreaks in various regions of the country, highlighting failures in infection prevention and control measures.

articles.title: France serves up €1 meals to all university students in effort to cut hardship | France | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: French universities have begun offering a €1 meal to all students, down from the usual €3.30, in an effort to address financial hardship. The policy is aimed at alleviating financial strain for students who are struggling to afford food.
