Rubio is scheduled to meet with Pietro Parolin, secretary of state for the Vatican, and Antonio Tajani, Italy's deputy prime minister and foreign minister.  The trip aims to "thaw" frosty relations between the two countries.

articles.title: Vinesh flags fear of bias, says government to be responsible for any incident in Gonda - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinesh Phogat, a decorated wrestler, expressed concerns about the upcoming National Open Ranking Tournament in Gonda, warning that the Indian government would be responsible for any harm to her or her team members.  She alleged potential bias in officiating stemming from the tournament's venue being linked to former WFI chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia arrests over 11,000 for residency, labour, border violations in nationwide crackdown | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Interior conducted a nationwide crackdown on residency, labor, and border regulations between April 23 and April 29, resulting in the arrest of over 11,000 individuals. The arrests included 6,244 for residency violations, 3,543 for border security breaches, and 1,513 for labor-related offenses.  Authorities have deported 14,855 individuals and referred others to their diplomatic missions for travel documents. Security forces intercepted 1,330 illegal entrants, mostly from Yemen and Ethiopia. The crackdown also led to the arrest of 14 people assisting violators with transport, shelter, or employment.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz blockade and other major naval sieges in modern times | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Strait of Hormuz remains closed after competing blockades by the United States and Iran.  Naval blockades, a tactic dating back centuries, have historically reshaped economies, societies, and alliances. Notable examples include Israel's siege of the Gaza Strip, which has caused humanitarian crises since 2007, and the blockade of Biafra during the Nigerian Civil War (1967-1970). The Cuban Missile Crisis saw a US naval "quarantine" of Cuba in 1962, while the US submarine blockade of Japan during World War II crippled Japan's war effort.  The Blockade of Wonsan during the Korean War (1951-1953) and the Allied blockade of Germany during World War I (1914-19) are also notable examples.

articles.title: Zack Polanski warns against banning London pro-Palestine protest | Zack Polanski | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Zack Polanski, the Green party leader, expressed concern over the chant "globalise the intifada" but defended freedom of speech.  He apologized for a social media post criticizing police tactics and requested a meeting with Met Commissioner Mark Rowley.  Keir Starmer, the Labour leader, called for stricter action against protesters using the phrase, citing its potential to intimidate Jewish communities. Heidi Alexander, the transport secretary, acknowledged the cumulative effect of such protests but emphasized that any ban would be decided after an ongoing review of protest laws.

articles.title: Nigeria summons South African envoy over attacks on its nationals
articles.rephrased_article: Nigeria summoned South Africa's acting High Commissioner to express its "profound concern" over recent attacks on Nigerians and other African nationals in the country. The meeting, scheduled for Monday, will address incidents of mistreatment and violence against Nigerian citizens, including at least two deaths reported by local media.  The situation has sparked tensions between Nigeria and South Africa, with President Cyril Ramaphosa condemning the attacks while urging respect for local laws.

articles.title: Teen F1 leader Antonelli takes Miami pole as race start time changed | Motorsports News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Kimi Antonelli, the 19-year-old Formula One leader, secured pole position for the Miami Grand Prix after a tense qualifying session.  The race start time was moved up three hours due to expected heavy rainstorms. Max Verstappen of Red Bull finished second, with Charles Leclerc in third for Ferrari. The change in start time was made by the sport's governing body, FIA, and commercial rights holders to prioritize safety and ensure a smooth race completion.

articles.title: How to become a successful trader in today’s volatile stock market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Successful traders must embrace discipline, adaptability, and a deep understanding of market behavior to navigate volatile conditions.  They prioritize risk management by using stop-loss orders, limiting exposure to single trades, and avoiding over-leveraging. Market experts emphasize trend-following strategies over emotional trading, staying updated on global developments, and avoiding overtrading in uncertain markets. A strong trading psychology is crucial for long-term success, as it involves accepting losses, avoiding revenge trading, and maintaining consistency with strategy.  Ultimately, successful traders focus on balancing short-term market movements with long-term investment conviction to thrive in dynamic conditions.

articles.title: A world of cultures comes alive at embassy fair in Washington - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The annual Passport DC “Around the World Embassy Tour” transformed International Drive into a global fairground, with visitors enjoying music, aromas, and cultural displays from embassies representing various countries.  Visitors at the Pakistan, Ethiopian, South American, Bangladesh, Mexican, Brazilian, Nigerian, UAE, and Brunei Embassies experienced traditional food, music, dance, and crafts, fostering a sense of global connection and cultural exchange. The event offered a unique opportunity for visitors to immerse themselves in different cultures through shared experiences.

articles.title: In Yemen, Starlink internet brings opportunities – for some | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Despite Houthi resistance and affordability challenges, Starlink satellite internet is fueling growth in Yemen's digital workforce.  The service provides fast, reliable internet access to entrepreneurs, freelancers, and students, allowing them to work remotely and earn more than the country's crumbling local economy would allow. While Starlink has expanded access to remote areas, it remains unaffordable for many Yemenis, and the company faces threats from the Houthi rebels who control the country's telecommunications infrastructure. The service is a lifeline for some, like video editor Mohammed Helmi, who can now work on projects without worrying about connection issues, while others, such as teachers, are benefiting from improved online learning opportunities.  However, Starlink's future in Yemen remains uncertain as the company faces challenges and potential security concerns.

articles.title: UK ‘invention agency’ grants £50m of public money to US tech and venture capital firms | Research and development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Aria), a UK agency aimed at restoring the country's scientific superpower status, has come under scrutiny for its funding of US tech companies and venture capital groups.  A joint investigation by the Guardian and Democracy for Sale revealed that over an eighth of Aria's £400 million in research and development funding over the past two years went to 14 US firms, with some receiving no clear return for the UK or Aria. The agency has defended its spending, stating it funds the best ideas across universities, startups, and private companies, but critics argue that this approach may prioritize US interests over UK innovation.

articles.title: Mcap of four of top-10 most valued firms surges by Rs 2.20 lakh cr; Reliance biggest winner - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE Sensex closed the week with marginal gains, driven by easing geopolitical tensions and positive Q4 earnings. However, rising crude oil prices and weak Asian market cues capped gains.  Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel, TCS, and Bajaj Finance were among the gainers while HDFC Bank, State Bank of India, ICICI Bank, Larsen & Toubro, Hindustan Unilever, and LIC experienced losses. Reliance Industries remained the most valued domestic firm on the index.

articles.title: Heat by design: Can cities be cooled without air conditioning? - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cities experience elevated temperatures due to the urban heat island effect, caused by concrete surfaces and dense construction. This phenomenon makes cities more susceptible to overheating during heatwaves.  The Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference 2026, taking place on May 6 and 7, aims to address this issue and promote climate-sensitive urban planning in Pakistan. The conference brings together policymakers, experts, and stakeholders to discuss practical solutions for integrating nature into urban design.

articles.title: Joel Embiid, 76ers knock out second-seeded Celtics in NBA Playoffs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Philadelphia 76ers defeated the Boston Celtics in Game 7 of their Eastern Conference first-round playoff series, advancing to the second round. Joel Embiid led the Sixers with 34 points and 12 rebounds, while Tyrese Maxey added 30 points and 11 rebounds. The 76ers overcame a 3-1 deficit after losing the first four games of the series.  The Celtics were led by Jayson Tatum's absence due to knee stiffness and Jaylen Brown's 33 points, but Boston was unable to overcome the Sixers' strong defensive performance in the final minutes.

articles.title: UK airlines given green light to cancel or consolidate flights to conserve jet fuel | Airline industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: UK airlines will be able to cancel or consolidate flights this summer due to the ongoing war in the Middle East and potential jet fuel shortages. The UK Civil Aviation Authority relaxed rules on flight slots, allowing airlines to give passengers more notice of cancellations and avoid last-minute disruptions. The government is taking steps to ensure a smooth travel experience for Britons during their summer holidays.  This legislation was developed at a meeting between the transport secretary, Heidi Alexander, and representatives from Heathrow and Gatwick airports, British Airways, Virgin Atlantic, and easyJet.

articles.title: 10 penny stocks surged up to 490% in 6 months. Do you own any? - Penny Stock Surge | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ACE Equity identified ten penny stocks with gains ranging from 25% to 490% in the past six months, highlighting their strong upward momentum. These micro-cap stocks, characterized by low price points and high return potential, attract investor interest despite inherent risks such as low liquidity, volatility, and limited transparency.  Success requires disciplined research, risk management, and a thorough understanding of these unique market dynamics.

articles.title: US Secretary of State Rubio to visit Vatican, Rome after Trump's row with Pope - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, will visit Rome and the Vatican this week to meet with Pietro Parolin, Antonio Tajani, and Guido Crosetto. The meetings come after a series of clashes between Donald Trump and Pope Leo XIV over the Catholic leader's anti-war rhetoric.  Trump criticized Leo for his stance on Iran, calling him "weak" and "terrible for foreign policy," while Meloni, Italy's Prime Minister, condemned Trump's remarks as unacceptable.

articles.title: Gretchen Walsh lowers own 100m butterfly world record for fourth time | Sport | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gretchen Walsh lowered her own world record in the women's 100-meter butterfly at the Fort Lauderdale Open, achieving a time of 54.33 seconds. This marks the fourth time she has broken the record, which was previously held at 54.60 seconds.  The victory comes after Walsh won three world titles in Singapore last year and is now more than a second faster than the second-fastest woman in history.  Leon Marchand, the four-time Olympic gold medallist from France, also dominated the meet with victories in the 200-meter breaststroke and 200-meter individual medley.

articles.title: Polanski ‘not fit to lead a party’ after Golders Green tweet, says minister – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Heidi Alexander, the UK transport secretary, criticized Zack Polanski, leader of the Green party, for retweeting a post criticizing police actions during the Golders Green attack.  Alexander stated that Polanski's action was "disgusting" and "absolutely abhorrent," arguing he is unfit to lead a political party. She also noted the Met Police commissioner, Mark Rowley, criticized the tweet as inaccurate and misinformed. The incident has sparked debate about the leadership of the Labour Party, with Heidi Alexander defending Keir Starmer's ability to lead the country during a time of international volatility.

articles.title: Indian-origin doctor shares experience of UK driving test, says system is ‘strict but necessary’ | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sunita Sayammagaru, an Indian-origin doctor, shared her experience of obtaining a driving license in the UK, describing it as significantly more rigorous than in India.  She failed her first practical test due to failing to complete a full mirror and shoulder check before moving out at a roundabout, but passed on her second attempt after reapplying. Sayammagaru believes stricter testing is necessary for road safety.

articles.title: 10 Largecap stocks with strong upside potential of up to 50%! Do you own any? - Largecap stocks surge | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Trendlyne, a financial data analytics platform, has identified ten large-cap stocks expected to deliver strong returns over the next year.  These companies include  swiggy, Info Edge, DLF, Eternal, Lodha Developers, HDFC Bank, ICICI Prudential, Mahindra & Mahindra, HDFC Life Insurance, and ICICI Bank. Analyst estimates suggest potential upside ranging from 30% to 50%, with a consensus rating of Buy or Strong Buy for most.

articles.title: Policeman gunned down near his home in KP's Lakki Marwat - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Constable Irfanullah was killed in a gun attack near his home in Lakki Marwat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The incident occurred on Sunday within the limits of Dadiwala police station.  The police official's death follows a series of terrorist attacks targeting police personnel in the region, including an explosion and a gunfight in the same district.

articles.title: Israel issues new forced displacement orders in southern Lebanon | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s military issued new forced displacement orders to residents in over 10 villages and towns in southern Lebanon, including areas north of the Litani River. The order comes despite a fragile US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon that was meant to halt fighting with Hezbollah.  The warning follows recent Israeli strikes on Lebanese territory and threats by Israel’s military chief of staff, Eyal Zamir, to strike beyond the “Yellow Line”.  Lebanon's president has called for full implementation of the ceasefire before peace negotiations can occur.

articles.title: Germany troop cuts send wrong signal to Russia, say two top US Republicans
articles.rephrased_article: Two US Republican lawmakers, Roger Wicker and Mike Rogers, criticized the Pentagon's decision to cut 5,000 troops from Germany, arguing it undermines deterrence and sends a wrong signal to Russia. President Donald Trump indicated further cuts could occur, while Germany's defense minister, Boris Pistorius, stressed the importance of US forces in Europe. The NATO military alliance is seeking clarification from Washington on the troop withdrawal decision, which has raised concerns about weakening the transatlantic community.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists from Spain and Brazil appear in Israeli court | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two foreign activists, Saif Abu Keshek (Spain) and Thiago Ávila (Brazil), detained by Israel after being intercepted during a flotilla attempting to break the blockade of Gaza, appeared in court in Ashkelon.  The Israeli government claims they were affiliated with the Popular Conference for Palestinians Abroad (PCPA), which is sanctioned by the US and accused of working with Hamas.  Spain has condemned the detention of Abu Keshek, while organizers of the flotilla claim the interception took place far from Gaza.

articles.title: Taiwan leader visits Eswatini despite China’s attempts to block trip | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Taiwan President William Lai Ching-te visited Eswatini, formerly known as Swaziland, despite China's efforts to block the trip.  Lai met with King Mswati III and signed trade agreements. China criticized the visit as a "laughable stunt" and insisted that Taiwan is part of its territory. The United States has pledged to help Taipei defend itself but does not recognize Taiwan.

articles.title: TNEA 2026 process kicks off with release of tentative schedule - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Directorate of Technical Education (DoTE) in Tamil Nadu has released the tentative schedule for the 2026 Tamil Nadu Engineering Admissions (TNEA), opening online registration on Sunday, May 3rd.  Students can register through the portals www.tneaonline.org and www.dte.tn.gov.in with the deadline for application submission being June 2nd and document uploads on June 6th.

articles.title: Stifling the press - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's government is facing criticism for its crackdown on press freedom, using laws like the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) to silence journalists and independent media outlets. The writer argues that these actions violate fundamental rights outlined in the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), including freedom of expression and access to information.  The government's use of lawfare, financial pressure, and online campaigns against critical voices has created a chilling effect on democracy and rule of law in the country.

articles.title: China blocks US sanctions against five ‘teapot’ refineries | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: China's Ministry of Commerce has blocked US sanctions against five Chinese refineries accused of importing Iranian oil, arguing that the sanctions violate international law. The US Treasury Department, in a move to penalize those doing business with the firms, announced sanctions on April 24th, targeting Hengli Petrochemical (Dalian) Refinery and four other so-called "teapot" refineries.  China relies heavily on oil imports from countries like Iran and has been a major customer for Iranian crude oil. The US Treasury Department stated that the targeted refineries have generated hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue for the Iranian military through crude oil purchases.

articles.title: Missing: Chennai’s new master plan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) officials have failed to meet the deadline for releasing the Third Master Plan (TMP) 2026-2047, despite previous assurances. The delay has sparked concerns among candidates campaigning in the Kancheepuram-Tiruvallur-Chennai-Chengalpattu area who are demanding a revised plan to make Chennai a future-ready city.  CMDA officials have promised to expedite the process but haven't provided a new timeline for completion.

articles.title: Iranian super tanker slips past US blockade with $220 million oil cargo - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has claimed that the US blockade of Iranian shipping in the Strait of Hormuz is a success, but reports suggest otherwise. A National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC) supertanker carrying over 1.9 million barrels of crude oil evaded the US Navy and reached the Asia-Pacific region.  The vessel, identified as "HUGE," was last spotted off Sri Lanka before moving through Indonesia's Lombok Strait towards the Riau Archipelago. Iran claims at least 52 Iranian vessels breached the US blockade within a 72-hour period, while the US military reports intercepting or forcing around 41 Iran-linked ships to turn back. The US maintains that the blockade is working by limiting Iran's oil exports and revenue.

articles.title: Persisting security challenge - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's focus on facilitating US-Iran talks has diverted attention from critical domestic and regional security challenges.  Since February 2025, the country has experienced a surge in terrorist attacks, with groups like TTP and IS-K becoming more active. The use of drones by militants has also increased, posing a new threat to civilian populations. While Pakistan has opened its borders to Iran as an alternative trade route to Central Asia, this move is seen as a response to the Taliban's refusal to cooperate on terrorist networks targeting Pakistan.  The long-term viability and effectiveness of these diplomatic efforts remain uncertain.

articles.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 65 as Trump reviews new plan to end war? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has proposed a 14-point plan to end the war with the United States, seeking guarantees of nonaggression, sanctions relief, and an end to hostilities in all fronts. President Donald Trump is reviewing the proposal but expressed doubt about its ability to lead to a deal.  The US, meanwhile, has approved $8.6 billion in arms deals for allies and is forming an international naval coalition called the Maritime Freedom Construct (MFC) to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Israel continues to launch airstrikes on southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire, resulting in significant casualties.

articles.title: Memorial for tusker Arjuna to be inaugurated on May 6 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Arjuna, the beloved elephant who carried the golden howdah during Mysuru Dasara for eight years, will be honored with a memorial inauguration on May 6th. The memorial was built at his burial site in the Yeslur range of forest in Hassan district. Arjuna died after being injured during a capture operation on December 4th, 2023.

articles.title: Uk Government Summer Travel Disruption: UK passengers face possible flight cuts as government changes airline rules over jet fuel supply fears | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government is temporarily relaxing its "use it or lose it" rule for airline slots to reduce potential summer travel disruptions caused by global jet fuel market pressures, particularly in the wake of the Strait of Hormuz crisis. The move aims to prevent last-minute cancellations and ensure airlines operate realistic schedules. Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander stated that this flexibility will allow airlines to combine flights, avoid empty flights, and protect passengers from airport chaos.  The government is also working closely with airlines, airports, and fuel suppliers to monitor stock levels daily.

articles.title: INTERVIEW: Qualifying for LA2028 Olympics Pakistan’s main focus, says Manzoor Sr - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) is focused on qualifying for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, with the upcoming World Cup in Belgium and the Netherlands being a crucial step.  Manzoor-ul-Hassan, the newly appointed head coach, believes the team has potential but needs to improve its defense. The national team will participate in the FIH Pro League before the World Cup, aiming to gain valuable experience against top teams like England and Spain. Pakistan lost their final game of the qualifying event in Ismailia 4-1 to England, a result that coach Manzoor-ul-Hassan believes was due to some unfortunate deflections.  The team will participate in a national camp in Lahore during May to address these issues.

articles.title: Man charged with murder of five-year-old Australian Indigenous girl | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferson Lewis, 47, has been charged with murder in the death of five-year-old Indigenous girl Kumanjayi Little Baby. Lewis is also facing two other charges and will appear in court in Darwin on Tuesday. The killing sparked protests by roughly 400 Indigenous people near Alice Springs after the suspect was captured and beaten unconscious by locals.  The girl disappeared from an Indigenous community camp, sparking a days-long search before her body was found. Anthony Albanese, Australian Prime Minister, expressed condolences to the family while Robin Granites, a spokesman for the family, called for respect and space for grieving.

articles.title: MP Bargi dam boat tragedy: Death toll rises to 13; body of last missing person found - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Army, National Disaster Response Force, and State Disaster Response Force concluded a three-day search operation for the remaining two victims of the Jabalpur cruise tragedy, bringing the death toll to 13.  The bodies of Mayuram (9) and Kamraj Arya (39) were found in Bargi dam. The boat capsized during a storm on Thursday evening, leaving 41 passengers onboard.  All 13 missing persons have been accounted for, and the bodies were sent to a government hospital for postmortem.

articles.title: 'Not anymore': Ukraine hits two shadow fleet tankers carrying oil near Russia, launches 300+ drones - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the President of Ukraine, announced that his military forces had struck two oil tankers near Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, highlighting continued efforts to disrupt Moscow's energy network.  These strikes follow a series of attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, including refineries and export terminals in Tuapse, Ust-Luga, and Perm, which have been attributed to Ukrainian drones. Russia has reported intercepting 334 Ukrainian drones overnight across various regions, with no casualties reported. Despite the escalating drone warfare, diplomatic efforts for a ceasefire remain stalled.

articles.title: Sajid Sadpara summits world’s 5th highest mountain Makalu without supplemental oxygen - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sajid Ali Sadpara, a Pakistani mountaineer, successfully summited Mount Makalu (8,485m) in Nepal without supplementary oxygen. This marks his 10th summit of the 14 "eight-thousanders" and follows his arrival in Nepal on April 4 for the mission.  The expedition team, including Sadpara and Johannss Lau, reached the summit at 5am on May 2nd after a successful push. The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) congratulated Sadpara on his achievement, calling it a moment of national pride.

articles.title: Japan’s Inoue beats Nakatani to retain undisputed super bantamweight title | Boxing News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Naoya Inoue retained his undisputed super bantamweight world title with a unanimous decision victory over compatriot Junto Nakatani in Tokyo.  The 33-year-old "Monster" extended his winning streak to 28, scoring 116-112, 115-113 and 116-112 on the scorecards.  Nakatani, who entered the bout unbeaten at 32-0, was looking to climb into the top echelons of boxing but ultimately fell short.  Both boxers displayed respect for each other throughout the fight, exchanging smiles and fist bumps after the match.

articles.title: Kenya violence: As political tension cranks up fears grow of a return to unrest
articles.rephrased_article: Kenya's parliament convened following a senator's assault, highlighting growing fears of political violence. The incident, captured on CCTV, has sparked outrage and prompted the interior minister to acknowledge the existence of sophisticated criminal gangs operating under the patronage of politicians.  Over 104 such groups are active across the country, with police struggling to contain their influence. While authorities have arrested over 300 suspects, no politicians have been held. The government claims it is taking the issue seriously and has identified those behind the violence, but critics argue that the response has been inconsistent.  The situation raises concerns about escalating political tensions ahead of the next general election in August 2024.

articles.title: One in three HR leaders face opposition to inclusion schemes, study finds | Prisons and probation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new poll by Working Chance, a national employment charity, found that over a third of HR decision-makers in the UK have faced pushback against equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) initiatives. The research revealed growing resistance to inclusive hiring practices, particularly for people with convictions who rely on such programs to access work. This trend raises concerns about social exclusion and undermines efforts to reduce reoffending, as stable employment is a key factor in preventing recidivism. Working Chance warns that scaling back inclusive hiring could exacerbate these issues. The findings come amid growing legal and political pressure on EDI schemes, with some employers withdrawing support for programs due to legal challenges and concerns about risk disclosure.

articles.title: Honey trap case: SP warns action against spreading rumours on social media - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Superintendent of Police P. Jagadeesh warned against the circulation of unverified news or rumors about a recent "honey trap" case on social media, stating that it violates victims' privacy and causes psychological distress. Mr. Jagadeesh emphasized that sharing personal details like names, photographs, or videos is prohibited and will result in legal action under relevant laws. He stressed the importance of respecting the victims' privacy and discouraging the spread of false information online.

articles.title: Man used fake Tinder profile to send strangers to ex’s home, convicted in UK Court | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Asad Hussain, a 36-year-old man, was found guilty of stalking involving serious alarm or distress, assault by beating, and failing to comply with a section 49 RIPA notice at Chester Crown Court. Hussain created a fake Tinder profile using his ex-partner’s photos and personal details to invite multiple men to her home under false pretences.  At least 18 men arrived believing they had been invited after matching with the woman online, some of whom were told she wanted to engage in “rape fantasy” and be “roughed up”. Police said Hussain took steps to conceal his identity and was arrested in October 2024. The court heard he repeatedly attempted to contact the victim after their relationship ended and made accusations to her family and friends.

articles.title: President, PM renew resolve to protect journalistic freedom, stress credible reporting - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reaffirmed the government's commitment to press freedom on World Press Freedom Day. They stressed the importance of credible journalism, noting that accurate information is crucial for national cohesion and global credibility.  Both leaders called for journalists to uphold ethical standards and resist disinformation campaigns, while also urging governments to ensure a safe environment for journalists. The Pakistan Press Foundation (PPF) reported at least 233 incidents of journalist harassment between January 2025 and April 2026.

articles.title: Austrian police arrest man after discovery of rat poison in baby food | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Austrian police arrested a 39-year-old man in connection with the discovery of rat poison in baby food jars sold by HiPP, a Swiss company. The arrest follows a partial recall of HiPP products last month after authorities found rat poison and an unspecified “toxic additive” in jars sold in Austria, the Czech Republic, and Slovakia.  The HiPP brand claims its products were not tainted during production and that the recall was prompted by a criminal act under investigation.

articles.title: Huge crowd attends free Shakira beach concert in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
articles.rephrased_article: Shakira headlined a free concert on Copacabana beach in Rio de Janeiro, attracting an estimated two million people. Eduardo Cavaliere, the city's mayor, funded the event as part of an effort to revitalize the local economy.  The 'Todo Mundo no Rio' mega-concert is expected to generate approximately R$800 million (£118m) for Brazil.

articles.title: ‘It’s like a cat and mouse game’: on the frontline of Belgium’s fight against drug smugglers | Belgium | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: At the port of Antwerp, customs officers are facing a constant challenge in combating drug smuggling.  While cocaine seizures have fallen slightly from record highs, they remain formidable. Smugglers are employing increasingly sophisticated tactics to evade detection, including disguising drugs within everyday goods and utilizing new shipping routes like west Africa. The European Union Drugs Agency, along with Belgian authorities, is actively deploying advanced scanners and specialized units to combat this evolving threat. Despite these efforts, the sheer volume of goods entering the EU through its ports makes it difficult to completely eradicate drug trafficking.  Experts believe that smugglers will find ways to continue their operations, highlighting the ongoing need for continued vigilance and adaptation.

articles.title: All set for vote counting in Kozhikode district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector Snehil Kumar Singh convened a meeting with political party representatives in Kozhikode district to discuss preparations for the Kerala Assembly election vote count on May 4th. The meeting covered arrangements at counting centers, facilities for agents, and procedures for postal ballots and Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs).  A three-tier security system has been implemented at all counting centers, with CCTV surveillance and internet connectivity. Counting of EVM votes will commence after the completion of postal ballot counting.

articles.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: LOSING THE PLOT - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Western media and cultural products are facing challenges due to institutional inertia, failing to adapt to changing global realities.  This is evident in their continued reliance on outdated narratives about Israel, the Middle East, and rising nations like Pakistan.  The emergence of new power dynamics and assertive "middle powers" has led to a disconnect between Western media's traditional perspectives and the evolving global landscape. This inertia risks rendering them irrelevant as younger generations increasingly challenge established narratives.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: Election is not a boxing contest, but a fight between ideologies: Riyas - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Public Works Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas stated that the upcoming election is not a personal competition but a battle of ideologies between different political parties. He emphasized that voters choose candidates based on their political beliefs and development plans, rather than personal attachments. Mr. Riyas expressed confidence in securing a larger victory margin in the 2021 election despite exit polls predicting his defeat.

articles.title: JUI-F threatens protests over seminary raids in Balochistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) in Balochistan announced a protest movement against raids on religious seminaries across the province.  Senator Maulana Abdul Wasey, provincial chief of the JUI-F, stated that a province-wide shutter-down strike and protests would take place on May 6th, with seminary students and party workers marching towards Quetta on May 10th. Maulana Fazlur Rehman, party chief, will address a conference in Pishin on June 4th.  Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti has been requested to apologize for the raids, but a delegation of provincial ministers postponed the protest until his return. The JUI-F demands an apology and withdrawal of the madrasa-related notification by May 2nd.

articles.title: Watch: What happens on counting day? | Explained - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Puducherry, West Bengal and Assam, the counting of votes for the upcoming general election will begin on May 4th. The process involves a series of steps including the verification of votes, tallying results, and declaration of winners.  The outcome of these elections will determine the future political landscape of these states.

articles.title: Ancient Dharmarajika Stupa in Taxila echoes with Dhamma sermon after 1,500 years - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Buddhist monks from five Southeast Asian countries, including Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal, Vietnam, and Myanmar, performed religious rituals at the Dharmarajika Stupa in Taxila on Friday to mark Vesak Day. The ceremony, organized by the Punjab Archaeology Department, included traditional offerings, a Dhamma sermon, and circumambulation around the stupa.  The event was attended by representatives from Thailand, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Pakistan, who expressed optimism about increased religious tourism and highlighted the shared values of peace and interfaith harmony.

articles.title: Opposing campaigns in Kerala map out the best- and worst-case scenarios for their respective alliances - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, K.C. Venugopal, and Ramesh Chennithala of the Congress are optimistic about a potential victory for their alliance in the upcoming Kerala Assembly elections, citing recent electoral successes and a perceived shift in voter sentiment towards the opposition. The United Democratic Front (UDF), led by the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), is banking on its strong support base among minorities and backward classes to counter the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF).  CPI(M) leaders believe voters will continue to trust the LDF's record of governance and welfare programs. The BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) aims to capitalize on voter dissatisfaction with both the UDF and LDF, positioning itself as a development alternative.

articles.title: Capital police chief dissatisfied with security arrangements at worship places - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad's Inspector General of Police, Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi, found security arrangements around worship places during Friday prayers to be unsatisfactory. During his visits to various mosques and imambargahs, he observed inadequate security measures, including the absence of police officials and unarmed lone policemen. The IG also noted that supervisory officers failed to ensure proper implementation of the security plan, leading to concerns about public safety. The capital's 990 mosques and 33 imambargahs have been categorized into three groups based on their security threats, with Category A places facing terrorism and sectarianism risks.

articles.title: Nato meetings with TV and film-makers prompt claims it is seeking ‘propaganda’ | Nato | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nato is holding closed-door meetings with film and TV professionals across Europe and the US to discuss the "evolving security situation in Europe and beyond." The alliance has held three such meetings, including one planned for London next month, where screenwriters from the Writers’ Guild of Great Britain will participate. Some invited professionals have expressed concerns that these meetings are an attempt to use art as propaganda for the alliance.  However, Nato claims these events aim to foster understanding and public support for increased defense spending.

articles.title: ‘Ten lifetimes won’t be enough’: TMC’s Abhishek Banerjee dares ‘bangla birodhi’ leaders to contest from Falta - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, General Secretary of the Trinamool Congress (TMC), responded to remarks by BJP leader Amit Malviya regarding the Election Commission of India's decision to order fresh polling in the Falta Assembly constituency.  Banerjee challenged the BJP and its supporters to contest in Falta, accusing them of attempting to undermine his "Diamond Harbour model." The ECI ordered repolling across 285 polling stations in Falta due to reports of electoral offences and subversion during the second phase of voting on April 29th.

articles.title: UAE lifts all air traffic restrictions introduced since Iran war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates has lifted all flight restrictions imposed since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran, returning air operations to normal status. The decision follows a comprehensive assessment of operational and security conditions in coordination with relevant authorities. This marks a significant milestone for UAE hubs Dubai and Abu Dhabi, which had been operating under restrictions since late February.  The conflict's impact on aviation across the Middle East has resulted in numerous cancellations and disruptions, but signs of recovery are emerging as countries like Qatar Airways resume flights to Iraq.

articles.title: Bahria Town residents in Rawalpindi protest against absence of ‘basic amenities’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Bahria Town Rawalpindi protested against the Bahria Town Private Limited administration for lacking civic facilities despite high fees. The protest, led by Tahir Nihad Bajwa, Chairman of RABT and President of BRACE, included demands for an independent audit of 21 years, a refund of excess charges, and the appointment of an owners’ association to oversee the community's affairs.  Traders representatives also voiced concerns about excessive charges for services.

articles.title: Polanski takes combative approach as Greens enter media spotlight | Green party | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Green party has received significant media attention in the UK, with some outlets portraying them as radical and controversial.  This heightened scrutiny includes accusations of antisemitism from both journalists and members of the public. The party's leader, Zack Polanski, has been particularly vocal in defending his party and responding to criticism, often engaging in heated exchanges with journalists and commentators. This media attention has led some to question whether the Green party is being unfairly targeted by the right-wing press, while others see it as a sign of their growing influence.

articles.title: Assam polls verdict on May 4; counting to decide BJP hat-trick or Congress comeback - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The final stage of the Assam Assembly elections will be determined by the counting of votes on Monday, May 4, 2026.  Anurag Goel, Chief Electoral Officer, has stated that over 722 candidates from 126 constituencies will have their fates decided at 40 counting centers across all 35 districts. The election saw a high voter turnout of 85.96% with the Congress and BJP leading in terms of candidate numbers.  Himanta Biswa Sarma, Chief Minister, and other prominent figures like Gaurav Gogoi (Congress) and Akhi Gogoi (Raijor Dal) are among those whose electoral fates will be decided on Monday.

articles.title: US approves $8.6bn in arms sales to Middle East allies | Military News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has approved $8.6 billion in arms sales to Middle East allies, citing emergency circumstances and bypassing congressional review. The sales include advanced weapons systems for Israel, Kuwait, Qatar, and the United Arab Emirates, aimed at bolstering their defense capabilities against Iranian attacks.  This decision comes amidst heightened tensions between Iran and its regional adversaries following the US-Israel war on Iran.

articles.title: YouTuber held for ‘recruiting individuals for al-Qaeda’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) arrested a YouTuber, Muhammad Saad bin Riaz, associated with the YouTube channel Eon News, for recruiting individuals for a banned outfit.  He was apprehended during a raid near GPO Chowk on Mall Road after receiving information about his alleged involvement in al-Qaeda recruitment and distribution of prohibited material. The CTD also reported arresting 21 suspected members of banned organizations and foiling planned terrorist activities across the province this week, with arrests made in various districts including Lahore, Sheikhupura, Gujranwala, Faisalabad, Jhang, Khanewal, Mianwali, Toba Tek Singh, Multan, Gujrat, Pakpattan, and Bahawalpur.

articles.title: Dynamic pay on platforms such as Uber should be banned, says TUC | Gig economy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Trades Union Congress (TUC) and Worker Info Exchange (WIE) have called for a ban on dynamic pricing in gig economy platforms like Uber, arguing that it leaves workers vulnerable to opaque algorithms that determine pay without transparency. The report, which includes testimonies from Uber drivers, highlights the negative impact of dynamic pricing on worker incomes, family life, health, and safety.  The TUC and WIE are urging the UK government to take action to end this practice and strengthen employment rights for gig workers.

articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 LIVE: 'Ten lifetimes won't be enough', Abhishek Banerjee challenges BJP to contest from Falta - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has ordered fresh voting in all 285 polling stations of Falta assembly constituency in West Bengal on May 21st. This decision follows repolling in 15 booths of Paschim Magrahat and Diamond Harbour constituencies due to severe electoral offences and democratic process subversion during the April 29th election. The counting of votes will begin at 8 a.m. on Monday, May 4th, with postal ballots followed by EVMs.

articles.title: Carlos Prates punishes Jack Della Maddalena at UFC Fight Night Australia | Mixed Martial Arts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Prates defeated Jack Della Maddalena at UFC Fight Night in Perth, Australia, by a unanimous decision.  Prates dominated the fight with a series of strikes and dropped Maddalena to the canvas multiple times before the referee stopped the bout. The Brazilian welterweight now calls for a match against the winner of the upcoming Islam Makhachev vs. Ian Machado Makhachev welterweight title fight.

articles.title: Japan contains one of its biggest wildfires in decades after 11-day battle - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Wildfires that ravaged forests in northern Japan's Iwate region, covering almost five times the size of New York City's Central Park, have been brought under control after 11 days.  Hundreds of firefighters and over 1,000 military personnel battled the blazes, which burned around 1,600 hectares, causing at least eight damaged buildings and two minor injuries. Otsuchi town mayor Kozo Hirano credited aerial and ground firefighting operations, as well as heavy rainfall, for containing the flames.

articles.title: Trump says Iran has not yet ‘paid a big enough price’ as he reviews new peace proposal | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump said he would review a new 14-point peace proposal from Iran, but expressed doubts about its prospects, stating Iran had not paid "a big enough price" for past actions. The proposal was reportedly sent through Pakistan and includes demands like US withdrawal from areas surrounding Iran, lifting sanctions, and ending the war on all fronts.  Trump suggested new military action against Iran if necessary but also indicated a willingness to engage in diplomacy. Kazem Gharibabadi, Iran’s deputy foreign minister, stated that the ball is now in the US's court.

articles.title: Man charged over Australian Outback death of 5-year-old girl
articles.rephrased_article: Jefferson Lewis, 47, has been charged with murder and two counts of sexual assault following the death of a five-year-old girl in Australia. Martin Dole, Northern Territory Police Commissioner, announced the charges against Lewis on Sunday morning. Five people have been arrested over violent riots sparked by the child's death in Alice Springs. The riots led to Lewis being moved to Darwin, where he is currently receiving treatment for injuries sustained during an attack.  The community has called for calm and respect of the judicial process while grieving the loss of Kumanjayi Little Baby.

articles.title: On press freedoms - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Press Foundation has released a report highlighting the increasing restrictions and threats faced by journalists in Pakistan. The report details over 230 instances of violence, threats, and legal actions against journalists, including censorship, intimidation tactics, and criminal complaints. This situation is described as an ordeal for Pakistani media, forcing practitioners to choose between survival and upholding their principles.  The public must recognize the importance of a free press in safeguarding democracy, as its suppression weakens individual liberties and allows unchecked power to flourish.

articles.title: Germany takes US troop drawdown in stride but deterrence gaps remain - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius stated that the planned drawdown of 5,000 US troops from Germany should encourage European nations to bolster their own defenses. However, two top US Republican lawmakers expressed concern over the decision, arguing that the troops should remain in Europe and not be relocated east. The Pentagon announced the withdrawal as part of a rift with Europe over the Iran war and tariff tensions.  The NATO alliance is working with the US to understand the details of the plan.

articles.title: Foreign investors exit T-bills - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign investment in Pakistan’s domestic bonds has almost disappeared due to the ongoing war in the Middle East, which has driven a 94% outflow from Treasury Bills.  The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) increased yields on T-bills by up to 83 basis points to attract investors, but this hasn't been enough to offset the negative impact of regional instability and disruptions to oil and gas supplies. Experts believe that once the war ends, foreign investment will likely increase as Pakistan has re-entered the international market and raised significant funds.

articles.title: Laufey on making jazz cool again (and the fish that brought out her inner rage)
articles.rephrased_article: Laufey, a Icelandic jazz-pop artist, released her latest album "A Matter of Time" which explores themes of love and anxiety.  The album features a blend of classic jazz vocals, orchestral arrangements, and confessional lyrics inspired by her experiences with love and relationships. The album's success has propelled Laufey to international stardom, including sold-out concerts and collaborations with popular brands like Fortnite. Her music defies categorization, blurring the lines between traditional jazz and contemporary pop while resonating with a diverse audience.

articles.title: PMD warns of Glof risk as rains, landslides batter GB - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rain and thunderstorms are expected across Gilgit-Baltistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, prompting the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) to issue a warning for glacial lake outburst floods (Glofs). The PMD warned that a sudden rise in temperatures followed by precipitation significantly elevates the risk of Glofs, debris flow, and flash flooding. Landslides and road blockages have been reported due to heavy rain across the region, including on the Karakoram Highway (KKH) and the Astore valley road. The Gilgit-Baltistan Communication and Works Department cleared debris from the roads after they were temporarily blocked.

articles.title: Dragonflies in distress: Scientists sound alarm in India's Western Ghats
articles.rephrased_article: A new study by Pankaj Koparde, an evolutionary ecologist, has revealed a concerning decline in dragonfly and damselfly species within the Western Ghats, one of India's most important biodiversity hotspots. The study, funded by the Indian government's Department of Science and Technology, found at least 35% fewer dragonflies and damselflies than previously reported. This decline could be due to factors such as habitat loss or extinction, highlighting the need for further research and conservation efforts.  The Western Ghats are under threat from urbanization, agriculture, infrastructure development, and other human activities, making it crucial to monitor species like dragonflies and damselflies to assess ecosystem health.

articles.title: Islamabad judges’ transfer challenged in Peshawar High Court - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A lawyer filed a petition in the Peshawar High Court challenging the transfer of three judges from the Islamabad High Court to other provinces.  The petitioner, Advocate Hastham Khan Khalil, argued that the decision violated constitutional provisions and fundamental rights, citing Article 2-A and 175(3) as well as previous court judgments. The petition also requested interim relief to suspend the transfer order until the case is resolved. The Judicial Commission of Pakistan approved the transfers at the recommendation of President Asif Ali Zardari.

articles.title: Voters will judge Trump on the economy - how is it doing?
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump will use the positive first quarter GDP figures of 2026 to paint his economic approach as successful, despite ongoing pressure from US tariffs and the Iran-related energy shock. The economy grew by 2% on an annualized basis, fueled in part by investment linked to tech and AI. However, Americans are more likely to vote based on the cost of living, with inflation reaching a near two-year high.  The Federal Reserve is unlikely to cut interest rates soon due to rising oil prices and expectations of continued sanctions against Iran. Despite this, stock markets have rebounded from early losses, offering some positive news for investors.

articles.title: 'Timmy' the stranded whale rescued, returned to North Sea - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A humpback whale, nicknamed "Timmy," was successfully transported from a sandbank near Luebeck, Germany to the North Sea off Denmark.  Karin Walter-Mommert, a wealthy entrepreneur who financed the rescue, confirmed that Timmy exited the barge and swam away with only superficial injuries. The whale is expected to travel towards the Arctic. Despite criticism from some experts, the privately funded rescue plan was successful after multiple attempts to save Timmy failed.

articles.title: Bin Laden nearly slipped out of Abbottabad: CIA report - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) has revealed that Osama bin Laden was planning to relocate from his Abbottabad hideout by September 2011, a plan he confirmed in letters to two brothers who had sheltered him. The CIA states it was unaware of this relocation plan and believes the raid would have missed an opportunity if delayed.  The documents also show that Bin Laden remained deeply involved in al-Qaeda operations until his death in May 2011.

articles.title: Concern for jailed Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi as family say health deteriorating
articles.rephrased_article: Narges Mohammadi, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and human rights activist, has been transferred to a hospital in Zanjan province following a reported deterioration of her health. Her family expressed concern over the lack of adequate medical care she received while imprisoned, citing her history of cardiac, lung, and blood pressure problems. The Narges Mohammadi Foundation, run by her family, called for her transfer to a Tehran hospital where specialists could provide proper treatment.  Jorgen Watne Frydnes, head of the Nobel Peace Prize committee, also expressed concern about her life-threatening situation.

articles.title: Adam Back again denies he is Satoshi, Bitcoin’s inventor - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Adam Back, a British computer scientist and CEO of Blockstream, has repeatedly denied being the inventor of Bitcoin. Despite persistent speculation, he attributes the asset's success to its lack of a known founder, which prevents any single entity from controlling it.  Back believes this decentralized structure makes Bitcoin more like a digital commodity than a startup, with no charismatic leader or point of capture. He sees the current landscape of regulated ETFs and corporate treasury vehicles holding billions of dollars in Bitcoin as a positive development that provides safeguards against centralized control.

articles.title: Silence, the court is in session - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yashwant Varma, a judge of the Allahabad High Court, submitted his resignation to President Droupadi Murmu on April 9th after nearly a year of scrutiny surrounding alleged unaccounted cash found at his official residence in Delhi.  Varma's decision comes following months of investigation into the incident that occurred on March 14th, 2025, when firefighters responding to a fire discovered stacks of half-burnt currency notes in a storeroom at his residence.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump to review 14-point plan; Israel pounds Lebanon | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated he will soon review a 14-point plan sent by Iran, but believes no deal can be made. The plan, which calls for guarantees of non-aggression, the lifting of a naval blockade and an end to the war on all fronts, including in Lebanon, was sent to the US after Trump expressed skepticism about reaching an agreement.

articles.title: Oil spike threatens Pakistan’s economic growth - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's inflation is projected to remain above 10% if oil prices persist at high levels, according to analysts from Topline Securities Ltd. The brokerage lowered its GDP forecast for FY27 to 2.5-3.0%, citing the impact of rising energy costs and inflation on economic growth.  A surge in oil prices could push the current account deficit above $8 billion (1.9% of GDP), straining foreign exchange reserves, while remittances are expected to decline. The State Bank of Pakistan may consider further policy rate hikes to protect real returns from inflation.

articles.title: Smuggling Starlink tech into Iran to beat the internet blackout
articles.rephrased_article: A clandestine network is smuggling Starlink satellite internet technology into Iran to bypass the government's ongoing internet blackout.  Sahand, a man involved in this operation, says he and others are buying the terminals and sending them across borders for those who need access to share information internationally. The Iranian government has cracked down on the use of Starlink devices, with arrests made for possession or purchase. Elon Musk's SpaceX company owns the satellite network used by these terminals.  The human rights organization Witness estimated that at least 50,000 Starlink terminals are in use within Iran. The government has admitted the internet blackout is hurting businesses but insists it will change once the situation returns to normal.

articles.title: Chinese court rules firms can't lay off workers on AI grounds - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Chinese court ruled that companies cannot terminate employees solely to replace them with AI systems. The Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court stated the termination of a worker by a tech firm in eastern China was illegal, as it did not meet legal conditions for dismissal and was based on automation of his job by AI.  The ruling highlights the tension between China's push for AI development and its commitment to stabilizing the domestic labor market.

articles.title: Silence, the court is in session - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yashwant Varma, a judge of the Allahabad High Court, submitted his resignation to President Droupadi Murmu on April 9th after nearly a year of scrutiny following an incident where firefighters discovered stacks of allegedly unaccounted-for cash at his official residence in Delhi.  Varma's decision comes after months of public and legal pressure stemming from the discovery made on March 14, 2025.

articles.title: Trump reviews Iranian peace proposal, warns strikes could resume | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump is reviewing Iran’s 14-point peace proposal, while warning that the US could resume air strikes if Tehran "misbehaves". The US president acknowledged the diplomatic opening but emphasized the possibility of renewed hostilities.  The proposal calls for lifting the US naval blockade, war reparations, and asset release, along with a 30-day window for finalizing terms. Tensions remain high as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) maintains readiness for conflict, and Tehran criticizes Trump’s characterization of the US naval blockade as "piracy".

articles.title: Iran says ball in US court on war or diplomacy - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian military officials warn of renewed hostilities with Washington, while diplomats in Tehran are urging the US to choose diplomacy or continue a confrontational approach.  Trump has boasted about the US blockade of Iran and compared it to piracy, rejecting an Iranian proposal for ending the blockade and resuming talks on Iran's nuclear program. Meanwhile, Iran is engaging with allies like Qatar and South Korea to discuss ongoing negotiations with the US. Despite a ceasefire in the Gulf, Israel continues strikes in Lebanon, killing over 12 people, while Lebanese army chief meets with a US general to discuss regional security.

articles.title: The Iran war has strengthened Ukraine. Could a ceasefire with Russia be closer?
articles.rephrased_article: The Iran war has strengthened Ukraine's position, allowing it to leverage its drone expertise and technology in the Gulf states.  Volodymyr Zelensky, Ukrainian President, has secured defense deals with Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar, while also gaining support from European allies for military equipment. The US under Donald Trump has been criticized for its lack of decisive action on sanctions against Russia, despite Ukraine's pleas for a ceasefire.  While some European countries are hesitant to take aggressive measures against Russia, they remain committed to supporting Ukraine's defense and ensuring peace in the region.

articles.title: Barnaby Joyce blames campaign ‘pressure’ after One Nation Farrer candidate contradicts party on immigration | Farrer byelection 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Barnaby Joyce, Pauline Hanson, and Gina Rinehart are all involved in the upcoming Farrer byelection.  David Farley, One Nation's candidate, contradicted party policy on immigration, stating that Australia's net overseas migration of 306,000 was "probably not" too many. Matt Canavan, Nationals leader, downplayed the political impact of the Coalition losing the seat, while Barrie Cassidy questioned Farley's comments.  Joyce dismissed concerns about Rinehart's million-dollar donation of a private plane to One Nation, claiming it wouldn't worry voters.

articles.title: Panel visits Rajasthan town for probe into clash between BJP MLA, officials - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Bharatiya Janata Party fact-finding committee visited Sriganganagar, Rajasthan on Saturday to investigate a clash between ruling party MLA Jaideep Bihani and officials during a public hearing. The incident involved an altercation with RUIDP assistant engineer Jaganlal Bairwa, who was allegedly assaulted by Bihani.  Three individuals were arrested following the incident.

articles.title: Three people dead and man arrested after incident in southwest Sydney | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NSW police responded to a disturbance at a home in Rosemeadow, Sydney, on Sunday morning.  A 64-year-old man died from injuries sustained during the incident, along with a woman in her 60s and a man in his 20s. A 32-year-old man was arrested and taken into custody for questioning. The incident is being treated as domestic violence-related.

articles.title: Panel visits Rajasthan town for probe into clash between BJP MLA, officials - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Bharatiya Janata Party fact-finding committee visited Sriganganagar, Rajasthan on Saturday to investigate a clash between ruling party MLA Jaideep Bihani and officials during a public hearing.  The incident resulted in the arrest of three individuals, including RUIDP assistant engineer Jaganlal Bairwa, who was allegedly assaulted by Bihani.

articles.title: Jefferson Lewis charged with murder over death of Kumanjayi Little Baby near Alice Springs | Indigenous Australians | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Northern Territory police have charged Jefferson Lewis, 47, with murder and two counts of sexual assault in connection with the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby. The girl went missing from her bed at an Alice Springs town camp on April 25th and was found dead after a five-day search.  Lewis was arrested on Thursday and is expected to appear in court on Tuesday.

articles.title: Heavy rain, winds wreak havoc in Thrissur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Widespread damage was reported in Thrissur district on Saturday afternoon following a spell of summer rain and strong winds. A pandal erected at the Koodalmanikyam Temple collapsed, along with its stage, while roof tiles from the temple's oottupura were blown away.  A tree uprooted itself and fell onto parked cars near the temple, causing no injuries. The gusty winds also damaged windows on the fifth floor of Thrissur General Hospital. Authorities continue to assess the damage as intermittent rains and winds persist in the area.

articles.title: IMD forecasts more heatwaves in coastal Andhra Pradesh, warmer nights across State - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts a higher number of heatwaves in coastal Andhra Pradesh this month, with above-normal minimum temperatures across the state.  Rayalaseema is expected to experience above-normal maximum temperatures with a 33.5% to 45% probability, while Central and North Andhra Pradesh may see normal to below-normal maximum temperatures. The IMD-Amaravati Director S. Stella cautioned that any dip in maximum temperatures would be marginal and confined to a few areas, emphasizing the peak summer phase is not over yet.

articles.title: Priest and two sons found dead in Kunigal after wife elopes with another man - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 40-year-old priest, Shivanna, allegedly killed his two sons, Jeevan (11) and Pranesh (6), before committing suicide in Karnataka on May 1st.  The incident occurred after Shivanna's wife reportedly eloped with another man, leaving him deeply distressed. Police are investigating the case and have taken into custody Kavya KP, Shivanna's wife's friend, who is believed to be involved.

articles.title: BMTC bus rams Manekshaw Parade Ground wall; 55 passengers escape, 3 injured - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A BMTC bus carrying 55 passengers experienced a technical malfunction while traveling on Route 362 from Shivajinagar to Begur, causing it to crash into the compound wall of the Field Marshal Manekshaw Parade Ground. The driver attempted to avoid other vehicles but steered off course, resulting in minor damage to the bus and injuries to three passengers. Cubbon Park Traffic Police are investigating the cause of the accident, which may have been caused by a brake failure, and have registered a case of rash and negligent driving.

articles.title: Admission restrictions for MLAC degree courses due to non-renewal of land lease - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Manmohan Singh, Bengaluru City University has restricted Maharani Lakshmi Ammanni College for Women (MLAC) from admitting students for the 2026-27 academic year due to a non-renewed land lease agreement.  The university cited that the college's lease expired in 2008 and hasn't been renewed since, impacting admissions as the autonomous status granted to MLAC is only valid until 2032. The trust managing the college has submitted a request to the Higher Education Department for removal of restrictions on admissions, while sources within the school education department indicate that the Chief Minister has requested additional documentation regarding the lease renewal and will make a decision in the State Cabinet after reviewing these documents.  Over 3,000 students are currently enrolled at MLAC.

articles.title: Person found dead in car after it plows into health club in Portland, Oregon | Oregon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Portland police responded to a vehicle crash at the Multnomah Athletic Club early Saturday morning, where a person was found dead inside the vehicle after it crashed through the front entrance and caught fire.  The driver, a former employee with mental health issues, allegedly rented a car on Friday and detonated explosives, believed to be propane tanks and pipe bombs. The club’s spokesperson said no members or staff were injured and the facility will remain closed until further notice. Adam Linnman, the club's spokesperson, stated that officials are cooperating with local and federal authorities.

articles.title: Delhi court rejects bail plea of Al Falah University chairman in money laundering case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jawad Ahmed Siddiqui, chairman of the Al Falah University group, had his regular bail plea denied by a Delhi court on Saturday.  The Enforcement Directorate (ED) opposed the request, citing the seriousness of the money laundering allegations and ongoing investigations. Siddiqui, arrested in November 2025 for allegedly generating illicit funds through student fees, remains in judicial custody. A separate ED probe is also underway.

articles.title: Man charged over bomb hoax after Peter Kay show evacuated | Peter Kay | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old man has been charged with false communications relating to a bomb hoax after a live show by comedian Peter Kay in Birmingham was interrupted due to a suspicious bag found near the venue.  Omar Majed, of Washwood Heath, Birmingham, will appear before magistrates on May 4th following an evacuation and subsequent search that found no explosives. The Utilita Arena Birmingham confirmed everyone was safely evacuated and the venue is secure.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi cites Gujarat BJP chief’s ‘indecent remarks’ against Geniben Thakor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the BJP after its Gujarat unit president made an offensive remark about Congress MP Geniben Thakor.  Gandhi accused the party of having a "distorted mindset" and promoting an "anti-women" ideology, stating that the BJP's actions contradict their claims of women empowerment. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Congress general secretary, also condemned the incident, supporting Geniben Thakor and highlighting the hypocrisy of the BJP's "Nari Vandana" campaign.

articles.title: Australia news live: three dead and man arrested in Sydney; Liberals claim seat of Nepean in key Victorian byelection | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sean Brown, a West Footscray resident, expresses concerns about the construction noise and environmental impact of M3, an AI datacentre, near his home.  Residents living near datacentres across Australia are voicing similar anxieties, reflecting growing opposition to these developments. The Liberal party has claimed victory in a key Victorian byelection, while Jess Wilson, the state opposition leader, is expected to meet with Anthony Albanese for the Australia–Japan Annual Leaders’ Meeting.

articles.title: What is India’s new Cell Broadcast System? Everything you need to know - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jyotiraditya Scindia, Union Telecom Minister, launched the Cell Broadcast Alert System in India on Saturday, a system designed to deliver emergency and natural disaster alerts to citizens' mobile phones. The system, developed by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) in collaboration with the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), utilizes indigenous technology and is based on the Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).  The system was tested on April 29th and will be used to deliver critical information about disasters and emergencies. Users can enable or disable test alerts through their device settings.

articles.title: Bengaluru road rage: Couple assaulted by bikers after warning against rash riding - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Electronic City police have registered a case against three motorists for allegedly assaulting a West Bengal couple after a road rage incident in Bettadasanapura, Bengaluru. The incident occurred when the couple confronted a group of youths performing dangerous driving maneuvers on the road.  The suspects chased the couple's car and assaulted both individuals, causing injuries to Soumyadeep Sen and Vyundreela Pradhan.  A video of the assault has gone viral, raising concerns about road safety.

articles.title: Aqua farmers in upbeat mood as India’s seafood exports cross ₹72,000-crore mark - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh aquaculture farmers are celebrating record-breaking seafood exports, exceeding ₹72,000 crore in the 2025-26 fiscal year.  Exports reached an all-time high, with India surpassing previous records and accounting for over 30% of the total volume. The export growth was driven by strong demand from markets like China, the European Union (EU), and Southeast Asia.  The Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) attributes this success to diversification efforts and a shift away from reliance on the United States.

articles.title: Inmate booked for making video call from Parappana Agrahara Central Prison - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Akbar, an inmate recently released on bail, has been booked for using a mobile phone to make video calls from inside Parappana Agrahara Central Prison.  The incident occurred between February 28 and April 29, violating prison rules. The Superintendent of the prison, Karna B. Kshatri, filed a complaint against Akbar, who was arrested in January for MDMA peddling. Authorities suspect he received assistance from others to procure the phone and are investigating the security lapses that allowed it to be used.

articles.title: Timmy the humpback whale escapes to the North Sea | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A humpback whale calf nicknamed Timmy, who had been repeatedly stranded in shallow waters near Germany, was released into the North Sea by a rescue team. The operation, which involved transporting the whale in a water-filled barge and releasing him off Denmark, was successful and the whale appears to be swimming freely.  Experts believe Timmy may have become disoriented while migrating or chasing herring, but his future remains uncertain as he heads towards the Arctic.

articles.title: In a first, NH stretch in T.N. get red markings to enhance visibility - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has painted red patches on two 300-meter stretches of NH 44 in Thoppur Ghat Road, Tamil Nadu to reduce speeds and improve vehicle stability.  This is the first National Highway stretch in the state to be painted red. The road sees heavy traffic with an average of 60,000-70,000 vehicles daily, leading to a high number of accidents and fatalities.  The NHAI has also begun construction of an elevated corridor at a cost of ₹905 crore to address the safety concerns on this route.

articles.title: Woman charged after killing Indian-origin schoolgirl in London car crash after initially being dropped of all charges - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Claire Freemantle, a 49-year-old woman from Edge Hill in Wimbledon, faces two counts of causing death by dangerous driving and seven counts of causing serious injury by dangerous driving following a car crash at a London primary school in July 2023. The incident killed two eight-year-old girls, Nuria Sajjad and Selena Lau, while more than a dozen others were injured.  Freemantle was initially cleared but later rearrested after concerns were raised by the victims' families, prompting a reinvestigation. The Metropolitan Police acknowledged shortcomings in its initial handling of the case, promising to fundamentally reset how it investigates fatal and serious collisions. The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is also investigating allegations of possible racial bias in the case's management.

articles.title: Why are maritime laws failing to secure the seas? | Show Types | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Wars and territorial disputes are reshaping global shipping, with maritime traffic facing increasing threats in various regions like the Strait of Hormuz and the Panama Canal.  The decades-old laws governing the seas are failing to adequately address these new challenges, according to experts. James Bays, presenter of a program on this topic, interviewed Rockford Weitz, director of the Fletcher Studies programme at Tufts University; George Theocharidis, professor of maritime law and policy at the World Maritime University; and Stavros Karamperidis, associate professor in maritime economics at Plymouth University.

articles.title: Choose a career that suits your interest and temperament, says Vijayapura SP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Superintendent of Police Laxman Nimbargi spoke at a career fair in Vijayapura, advising students to choose careers aligned with their interests and talents. He emphasized the importance of harnessing natural inclinations and working hard to overcome any perceived limitations. Nimbargi, who pursued public service after studying computer science, encouraged students to prepare seriously for competitive exams like the UPSC civil services examinations.  He also stressed the need for a positive mindset and focusing on strengths while addressing weaknesses.

articles.title: Indian-origin Meenu Batra released from ICE custody after months; had been living US for 35 years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Meenu Batra, an Indian-origin court interpreter with decades of experience in Texas immigration courts, was released from ICE custody after a legal battle.
