articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court's ruling in Louisiana v. Callais has led to the suspension of House primaries in Louisiana ahead of the May 16th elections. Nancy Landry, Louisiana's secretary of state, certified an emergency and suspended the primaries due to the court's decision that redrawing congressional maps is necessary.  Hakeem Jeffries, the House minority leader, plans to counter Republican gerrymandering by targeting key states for redistricting maneuvers in advance of the 2028 elections. Jena Griswold, Colorado's secretary of state, supports independent redistricting and encourages voters to weigh in on map changes.  Donald Trump criticized the court decision and called for Louisiana voters to remove Senator Bill Cassidy from office.  Al Sharpton believes the ruling will inspire a movement for racial equality and encourage more voter participation.

articles.title: Top 10 countries with the most skyscrapers in the world 2026: China, US, UAE and other leading nations | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: China, the United States, the United Arab Emirates, and Malaysia are among the top countries with the most skyscrapers.  China dominates this list, fueled by urbanization and industrial development, while the United States boasts iconic skyscrapers in cities like New York and Chicago. Dubai in the UAE has rapidly transformed its skyline with luxury-focused high-rises. Malaysia, particularly Kuala Lumpur, features a dense cluster of modern towers.  These countries are pushing the boundaries of skyscraper construction, driven by economic ambition, urban growth, and demand for space.

articles.title: From surplus to strain: World rice supply threatened by Iran war, El Niño - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) predicts a tighter global rice supply this year due to fertilizer shortages, soaring fuel costs from the Iran war, and an emerging El Niño. Farmers in top exporters like Thailand and Vietnam are cutting planting acreage as a result of these factors, leading to reduced output.  While global rice inventories remain high, the situation could worsen if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed for extended periods.

articles.title: Has the US Supreme Court weakened the Voting Rights Act – and how? | Civil Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court ruled that a Louisiana electoral map was unconstitutional, effectively weakening the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The court's 6-3 decision found that the map, which created two Black-majority congressional districts, relied too heavily on race and violated the Constitution's prohibition against intentional racial discrimination.  The ruling is seen as a victory for Louisiana Republicans and President Donald Trump, who had supported the challenge to the Voting Rights Act. The decision could have far-reaching implications for redistricting efforts nationwide, potentially allowing state legislatures to redraw electoral maps in ways that dilute minority voting power.  Legal experts warn that this ruling may weaken protections established by the Voting Rights Act and allow partisan manipulation of congressional districts.

articles.title: British soldiers lost control in 1972 Springhill shootings, inquest finds | Northern Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An inquest judge ruled that British army soldiers acted in breach of rules governing lethal force when they killed five civilians in Northern Ireland in 1972.  The killings, which occurred in west Belfast on July 9th, were deemed to be unjustified as the victims posed no threat and were unarmed. The coroner found that two soldiers, known as A and E, overreacted to perceived threats, fired prematurely, and ultimately lost control. The families of the deceased expressed relief at the verdict, while Sinn Féin MP Paul Maskey condemned the British army's impunity in light of the killings.

articles.title: Trump aide Josh Gruenbaum dropped from Ukraine, Iran roles: Here's why he was sidelined - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Josh Gruenbaum, a former advisor to Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, will no longer work on key foreign policy issues related to Russia-Ukraine or Iran. He is now focusing exclusively on Gaza-related efforts through the Board of Peace, an international organization with links to the US government.  The White House stated Gruenbaum will continue to advance the President's agenda of enhancing global stability in his new role. Despite concerns about his working style and internal communications, Gruenbaum remains an important part of efforts aimed at promoting stability and development in the Middle East.

articles.title: Bears continue to dominate PSX as KSE-100 loses 2,800 points - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) experienced a fourth consecutive day of losses, with the KSE-100 index plummeting over 2,800 points.  Rising global oil prices, fueled by geopolitical tensions and warnings from Donald Trump, contributed to investor caution. The market also reacted negatively to reports that Etisalat, a UAE-based telecom giant, was reviewing its exposure in Pakistan's telecom sector.

articles.title: How rebels teamed up to shake Mali and the Kremlin’s grip | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: JNIM and Tuareg rebels carried out coordinated attacks across Mali, killing the country's defense minister and his family. The attacks, which began in Bamako on April 25th, have raised questions about who is behind the escalating violence in the nation.  The episode was produced by a team at The Take.

articles.title: Starmer restores powers to ousted hereditary peers in Lords shake-up | Lords reform | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has granted life peerages to 15 Conservative, two Labour, and nine crossbench peers whose seats were abolished in the House of Lords. This concession was made to appease opposition parties who demanded compensation for removed peers and end a long battle over abolishing hereditary peers. The move comes as 92 hereditary peers lost their seats this week and is expected to be announced before the king's speech, with further updates to the Lords including a participation requirement and retirement age being implemented later this year.

articles.title: Mazagon Dock Q4 Results: Profit jumps 42% to Rs 464 crore; co declares Rs 4.62 dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Mazagon Dock's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 4.62 per share for the fiscal year ending March 2026. Revenue from operations increased by 16% year-over-year to Rs 3,684 crore, driven by higher project execution. Profit before tax rose sharply by 54% to Rs 625 crore, while total expenses increased 8% to Rs 3,340 crore. The company reported a total income of Rs 13,982.4 crore for the fiscal year ending March 2026, with an annual profit before tax growth of 4%.

articles.title: 'Time to say goodbye' :Jeffrey Epstein's suicide note revealed via former cellmate account, remains sealed by court - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jeffrey Epstein, a disgraced financier, wrote a note before his death in 2019 while incarcerated at a federal jail in New York City. The note, discovered by his former cellmate Nicholas Tartaglione, suggested that Epstein maintained his innocence despite ongoing investigations and indicated he felt safe sharing a cell with him.  The note was later verified as having been written by Epstein and became part of Tartaglione’s legal case, but it has remained confidential since then. Despite its potential relevance to the investigation into Epstein’s death, the note was not included in official investigations.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla organisers say 211 activists 'kidnapped' by Israel - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s navy intercepted a Global Sumud Flotilla of pro-Palestinian activists seeking to break the blockade on Gaza, detaining 211 individuals including French city councillor Raphaelle Primet. The operation took place near Crete in international waters and involved Israeli military vessels surrounding flotilla boats while jamming communications.  The flotilla organizers reported that at least 22 boats were stormed by Israeli forces, with some still en route to Gaza. Doctors Without Borders (MSF) condemned the actions as a form of collective punishment, highlighting the systematic denial of water access in Gaza.

articles.title: Myanmar’s former leader Aung San Suu Kyi moved to house arrest | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Aung San Suu Kyi, Myanmar's former leader, has been moved to house arrest after her sentence was reduced as part of a larger prisoner pardon tied to a Buddhist holiday. President Min Aung Hlaing ordered the move, which brings her sentence down to 18 years with more than 13 years left to serve. The decision was welcomed by the United Nations, who called for the "swift release" of all political prisoners in Myanmar. Suu Kyi's legal team has not been notified directly about the change in location and remains concerned about her health, which has reportedly declined since the military takeover in 2021.

articles.title: Venice Biennale jury quits amid row over participation of Russia | Venice Biennale | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Venice Biennale jury resigned just days before the exhibition's opening, citing a disagreement over Russia's participation. The decision to allow Russia to have a pavilion at the event sparked controversy and criticism from various stakeholders, including the European Commission, the Italian government, and international artists.  Despite facing pressure to exclude Russia, the Biennale Foundation maintains its commitment to open dialogue and artistic freedom.

articles.title: Chhattisgarh Assembly passes resolution for one-third quota for women in legislative bodies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Chhattisgarh Assembly passed a resolution on Thursday calling for the immediate implementation of one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures after delimitation. This follows the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which aimed to expedite women's reservation by redistributing Lok Sabha seats based on the 2011 Census.  The bill failed to secure a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha and since then, BJP governments have convened special sessions of state assemblies to push for its implementation.

articles.title: Laurus Labs Q4 Results: Cons PAT increased 19% to Rs 279 crore, revenue rises 5% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The company's PAT increased 11% quarter-on-quarter to Rs 252 crore in Q3FY26, while revenue rose 2% sequentially to Rs 1,778 crore.  EBITDA reached Rs 523 crore, a 10% increase from the previous year, and gross margins improved to 61.4%. The company's board approved a second interim dividend of Rs 1.20 per share. The company reported net profit for FY26 at Rs 889 crore, a significant increase from Rs 358 crore in FY25.

articles.title: Ishowspeed: IShowSpeed plans space livestream after completing world tour goal - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed, a popular streamer, announced his ambitious plans to stream live from space after completing his planned world tour. He has already visited 96 countries and aims to visit all remaining nations in the next few years. IShowSpeed expressed interest in collaborating with Elon Musk to make this dream a reality.  He also mentioned aspirations to explore underwater, potentially inspired by his love for the anime *One Piece*.

articles.title: Amazon says damaged UAE cloud region recovery to take several months - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Amazon announced that restoring cloud computing operations in the UAE, which were damaged by Iranian drone strikes in early March, will take several months. The company's data centers in the region were disrupted, causing a suspension of billing operations and impacting 37 services as of April 30. AWS, the world's largest cloud provider, is recommending customers migrate resources to other regions and restore inaccessible ones from backups.

articles.title: Iran confirmed to play at World Cup according to FIFA chief Infantino | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed that Iran will participate in the 2026 World Cup in the United States despite the country's absence from the FIFA Congress due to visa issues.  Iranian football federation officials, including President Mehdi Taj, were denied entry into Canada after what Tehran described as "unacceptable behaviour" by Canadian immigration authorities. Iran has qualified for the tournament but its participation is complicated by tensions surrounding the US-Israel war on the country and concerns about ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

articles.title: ‘A new chapter’: first commercial fight from US since 2019 lands in Venezuela | Venezuela | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: US and Venezuelan officials celebrated the arrival of an American Airlines passenger jet in Caracas, marking a new era in diplomatic relations after years of strained ties. The flight signifies the start of economic reconnection between the two countries as part of a three-phase plan by the Trump administration to stabilize Venezuela's economy and potentially facilitate a political transition back towards democracy.  The event was met with optimism from both sides, with Venezuelan officials welcoming global commerce and US officials expressing hope for a brighter future for the country.

articles.title: Met police arrest two Green election candidates over alleged antisemitism | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Saiqa Ali and Sabine Mairey, two women running as Green party candidates for Lambeth council in south London, were arrested by the Metropolitan police on suspicion of stirring up racial hatred online. The arrests followed an investigation launched after concerns were reported to police about antisemitic material posted online.  Ali's Instagram account contained a post featuring an armed man wearing a Hamas headband and the slogan "Resistance is freedom," while Mairey shared a post stating "Ramming a synagogue isn’t antisemitism. It’s revenge."

articles.title: Odisha Assembly: BJP, BJD and Congress resort to political one-upmanship over women’s reservation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi addressed the special session of the state legislative assembly on Thursday, April 30, 2026, emphasizing women's active participation in Indian democracy.  He assured that reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies would be implemented from 2029. Naveen Patnaik, Leader of Opposition, criticized the BJP's handling of the issue, arguing that it was a ploy to push through delimitation without proper discussion. The BJD also highlighted its past support for women's reservation, while the Congress demanded immediate implementation of the already passed 33% reservation bill.

articles.title: Value 360 Communications IPO: Rs 41.7 crore issue opens May 4. Check price band, GMP, other details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Value 360 Communications Limited, an integrated communications and marketing solutions provider, is launching an initial public offering (IPO) with a price range of Rs 95 to Rs 98 per share. The company plans to use the proceeds for infrastructure expansion, technology investment, influencer marketing platform acquisition, and potential future acquisitions. Horizon Management Private Limited has been appointed as lead manager for the IPO, while KFin Technologies Limited will serve as registrar.

articles.title: Trump slams Germany’s Merz again as rift over Iran war widens | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump renewed his attacks on German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, criticizing his comments about the war in Iran.  Trump suggested that Merz focus on European affairs rather than the Middle East conflict, arguing that the war is making the world safer.  Merz, who previously aligned with the US and Israel's hawkish approach to Iran, questioned Washington's strategy and suggested that Tehran is "overplaying" its hand in negotiations. Berlin stated it is prepared for a potential reduction in US troops in Germany while emphasizing NATO cooperation.

articles.title: Quote of the day by German philosopher Immanuel Kant: “One who makes himself a worm cannot complain afterwards if people step on him.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Immanuel Kant, a German philosopher, famously stated, "One who makes himself a worm cannot complain afterwards if people step on him." This quote emphasizes the connection between self-respect and how others treat us. Kant believed that individuals should value their own dignity and act in ways that reflect that worth.  This idea aligns with modern discussions about self-esteem, boundaries, and personal responsibility. The quote serves as a reminder that our actions can influence how we are treated by others, prompting us to prioritize self-respect and maintain a sense of personal worth.

articles.title: KP CM Afridi hints at legislation against collateral damage in drone strikes - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Following public outcry over drone strikes in his constituency, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi hinted at introducing legislation to criminalize collateral damage.  He made the remarks during a KP Assembly session where lawmakers vowed to protect civilians and discussed a planned jirga against drone attacks. The chief minister also questioned the results of military operations in the province, alleging they were pre-planned and aimed at undermining one political party. KP Assembly Speaker Babar Swati deferred the day's agenda due to an increase in drone strikes.  The session saw lawmakers from various parties express concerns over civilian casualties and demand a dialogue with Afghanistan.

articles.title: AI outperforms doctors in Harvard trial of emergency triage diagnoses | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A groundbreaking Harvard study found that AI systems outperformed human doctors in diagnosing patients in emergency medicine triage situations.  The study, published in the journal Science, tested the accuracy of an AI model called o1 reasoning model against human doctors and found that the AI correctly diagnosed 67% of patients compared to the human doctors' 50-55%. The researchers believe this is a significant step forward in clinical reasoning for AI systems. However, they emphasize that AI should not replace doctors and instead be seen as a tool to assist them in providing better care.  The study also highlights concerns about potential bias in AI diagnoses and the need for clear accountability frameworks for its use in healthcare.

articles.title: Karnataka Cabinet approves Integrated Satellite Township project in Bengaluru South district at a cost of ₹18,133 crore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government approved a ₹18,133 crore Integrated Satellite Township project in Bengaluru South district, which will involve acquiring 7,404 acres of land from nine villages. The Cabinet also gave its approval to the Hyderabad-Bengaluru High Speed Rail Corridor and provided administrative support for the Chennai-Bengaluru high speed rail corridor. Additionally, the government approved a ₹600 crore project for the redevelopment of slums inhabited by minorities across 11 corporations in the state.

articles.title: Hindustan Labs, RK Steel get Sebi nod to launch IPOs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Laboratories, a generic pharmaceutical company, is planning to raise capital through an initial public offering (IPO) with the proceeds primarily earmarked for working capital and general corporate purposes. The IPO will be managed by Choice Capital Advisors Private Limited.  The company's business model focuses on supplying affordable medicines to government institutions, including those within the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and state governments.

articles.title: Israel rights group petitions top court to order release of 14 Gaza doctors | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Physicians for Human Rights-Israel (PHRI) has filed a petition with the Supreme Court demanding the immediate release of 14 doctors detained in Gaza for over a year. The group alleges that Israel's continued detention of these medical professionals is hindering efforts to rehabilitate Gaza’s healthcare system and calls on international actors to support their cause. Dr Hussam Abu Safia, director of Kamal Adwan Hospital, has been held without charge for nearly 18 months and faces severe health complications due to his imprisonment.  Numerous aid groups have warned of a critical shortage of medical supplies in Gaza as a result of Israeli restrictions.

articles.title: Mother convicted of baby’s murder after blaming another child - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nicole Blain was found guilty of murdering her infant daughter, Thea June Wilson, in Glasgow. Evidence presented during the trial showed that Blain inflicted fatal head injuries on the child and attempted to blame another child within the household. Medical records, witness testimony, and a social worker's account all pointed towards Blain being responsible for the baby's death. The jury found her guilty of murder, and sentencing is scheduled for May 28th.

articles.title: 13 terrorists killed as bids to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in KP foiled: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: ISPR, the military's media affairs wing, announced that 13 terrorists affiliated with Fitna al Khawarij, a group linked to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan, were killed in two separate infiltration attempts along the Pak-Afghan border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The security forces engaged the groups, resulting in the deaths of eight individuals in Mohmand district and five in North Waziristan district. ISPR emphasized that these incidents highlight the failure of the Afghan Taliban to control its borders and urged them to prevent the use of their territory for terrorist activities.

articles.title: Trump tells Merz to ‘fix his broken country’ in new attack on German chancellor | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump criticized Friedrich Merz, the chancellor of Germany, for focusing on Iran and Russia-Ukraine issues, urging him to prioritize domestic concerns like immigration and energy.  Trump's comments came after Merz expressed criticism of the US's approach to the war in Ukraine and its relationship with Iran.  German officials emphasized that such troop reduction threats are not new and have been made by previous presidents. They stated they are prepared for potential changes and will continue discussions with the US on the matter.

articles.title: KEERA to be established for structural reforms in engineering education: Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka government has decided to establish the Karnataka Engineering Education Reform Authority (KEERA), following recommendations from an Expert Committee on Reforms in Technical Education. The committee, led by former director of IIIT-B, S. Sadagopan, proposed structural reforms for engineering education.  The government plans to bring separate legislation to establish KEERA and will discuss the matter soon.

articles.title: Sebi introduces fast-track route for AIF launches to boost capital deployment - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sebi, the market regulator, has revised procedures for processing placement memorandums to reduce delays in fund launches. These changes aim to enhance efficiency in capital deployment and support faster execution of investment strategies by AIFs. The regulator also simplified the accredited investor framework earlier this year to ease operational bottlenecks for AIFs while maintaining prudential safeguards.  These revisions allow AIF investment managers to finalize and execute contribution agreements with investors before formal accreditation, ensuring key prudential norms are not compromised.

articles.title: US falls to ‘historic low’ in press freedom tracker: RSF | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has fallen to a “historic low” in press freedom, according to the Reporters Without Borders (RSF) annual tracker. The country dropped seven spaces from 57th to 64th globally, with Norway leading and Eritrea ranked lowest.  Executive Director of RSF's North America office, Clayton Weimers, stated that Trump’s administration has carried out a coordinated war on press freedom since his first term. Critics point to media consolidation, including the acquisition of Paramount Global by Skydance Media, owned by David Ellison, who is a confidant of Trump, as contributing to this decline.  The FCC chair, Brendan Carr, has also threatened broadcasters for their coverage of Trump's immigration policies and other topics.

articles.title: 'Make Pluto a planet again': Nasa Administrator Jared Isaacman calls for status restoration at US Senate hearing - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman reiterated his support for restoring Pluto's status as a planet during a US Senate hearing.  He stated that Nasa researchers are working on studies to reopen the scientific debate, echoing previous views expressed in media interviews. The International Astronomical Union (IAU) reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006 due to its failure to meet the "cleared its orbit" requirement. This decision sparked ongoing debate among planetary scientists and public figures who argue for a broader definition of a planet.  Nasa's New Horizons spacecraft, which provided the first close-up images of Pluto, remains the only mission to have flown past it.

articles.title: Govt hikes petrol price by Rs6, diesel by Rs19 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government raised the price of petrol and high-speed diesel on Thursday, increasing prices to Rs393.35 per litre for petrol and Rs380.19 per litre for HSD. Islamabad's Deputy Commissioner Irfan Nawaz Memon refuted reports of petrol stations shutting down in the city, stating that there was sufficient stock available.  The Petroleum Division also denied these claims, assuring the public that fuel supply would remain uninterrupted. The All Pakistan Petrol Pump Owners Association (APPPOA) further clarified that no strike is planned and petrol stations will remain open as usual.

articles.title: US House votes to end partial government shutdown over immigration operations
articles.rephrased_article: The US House of Representatives voted to approve a Senate-passed bill, ending the 76-day partial government shutdown. The bill restores funding to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and concludes the longest shutdown in the agency's history.  President Donald Trump supported the measure, which does not include new funding for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) or US Border Patrol. The bill now goes to the president for signature.

articles.title: Four rescued from Seine after bus plunges into river near Paris | France | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A bus driven by a trainee driver in Juvisy-sur-Orge, France, veered off the road and plunged into the Seine River on Thursday.  The driver and three passengers were rescued, while an investigation is underway. The incident involved a parked vehicle struck by the bus, which was being operated by a trainee driver who tested negative for drugs and alcohol. IDFM transport authority officials confirmed the bus will be recovered from the water later in the day.

articles.title: Indonesian soldiers accused of acid attack. What happened and why? | Human Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: An Indonesian trial has begun for four soldiers accused of carrying out an acid attack on activist Andrie Yunus, who had criticized the expanding role of the military in government. The attack, which left Yunus blind in one eye and with burns on his face and body, is seen as part of a broader pattern of repression in Indonesia, according to rights groups and analysts.  The United Nations, Amnesty International, and other organizations have condemned the attack, raising concerns about impunity and the fairness of the trial, which is being held in a military court. The case highlights growing public dissatisfaction with the military's influence in government, fueled by economic inequality and perceived attacks on dissent.

articles.title: Golders Green attack suspect named as Essa Suleiman, 45 | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Essa Suleiman, a 45-year-old man, was arrested on suspicion of murder after stabbing two Jewish men in Golders Green. Suleiman had been referred to the Prevent program six years prior and cleared of being a terrorist threat. The attack is being treated as terrorism by police who are investigating whether Suleiman targeted Jewish people.  The investigation is ongoing, with officers believing he acted alone.

articles.title: High Court directs FRRO to extend Russian woman’s visa - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Nagesh Bheemapaka of the Telangana High Court granted a Russian woman, Alena Evgenievna Pavlova, an extension on her visa due to humanitarian and compassionate grounds. The judge also ruled against imposing overstay penalties on Pavlova, who had been actively involved in translating Indian literature into Russian and volunteering with various organizations.  The court acknowledged the exceptional circumstances of Pavlova's situation following the death of her husband and her subsequent request for an extension.

articles.title: As Trump nukes science, is India's brain drain ready for 'brain regain'? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has dismissed the National Science Board, an independent body overseeing the National Science Foundation (NSF), America's primary engine for basic research. This action, delivered via a terse email last week, has led to the removal of three prominent Indian-American scientists from the board: Sudarsanam Babu, Arun Majumdar, and Suresh Garimella. The move is part of a broader trend by the Trump administration to dismantle the country's scientific architecture through the termination of advisory panels, cancellation of NSF grants, and proposed budget cuts to major research agencies. This has resulted in funding uncertainty for laboratories and universities, forcing hiring freezes and graduate program cuts, and prompting many foreign-origin scientists to consider relocating abroad.

articles.title: PTI leaders turn up for Adiala jail visit following 2-week gap - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: PTI leaders, including Salman Akram Raja, attempted to meet with incarcerated party founder Imran Khan at Adiala jail on Thursday after the Islamabad High Court granted him twice-a-week meetings. Despite the court order, Imran's family and party leaders have been largely restricted from meeting with him. The PTI Secretary General withdrew a previous list of leaders intending to meet Imran and submitted a new one, but all six leaders were again denied access.  The party plans to appeal to the Supreme Court for their petition to be heard.

articles.title: US military equipment worth billions of dollars destroyed in Iran war | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US military has suffered significant losses in the ongoing war with Iran, estimated at between $2.3 billion and $2.8 billion, according to a new report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS).  US Secretary of Defense boasted of US military successes against Iran, but these claims were contradicted by Iranian missile strikes that destroyed equipment including a radar system worth $700 million at a Saudi Arabian base. The CSIS analysis, based on satellite imagery and other data, also highlights the impact of Iranian attacks on US bases in the Gulf region.  Omar Ashour, professor of security and military studies, suggests that while the US has achieved operational victories in past conflicts, strategic failures can occur if these victories fail to achieve their intended goals.

articles.title: Starmer calls on public to ‘open their eyes to Jewish pain’ in wake of Golders Green attack | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer called for greater protection of the Jewish community following a stabbing attack in Golders Green, accusing those marching alongside supporters of Hamas of "venerating the murder of Jews". The prime minister pledged increased funding for security services and stronger powers to combat antisemitism, including legislation targeting state-sponsored groups. Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, promised to do everything in her power to ensure Jewish safety while police continue their investigation into the attack.  The government will fast track legislation creating proscription-like powers to pursue individuals and organizations acting on behalf of malign state-sponsored groups.

articles.title: Bowring tragedy: CM orders suspension of official, Lokayukta takes up inquiry, police file only UDR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following the tragic collapse of a compound wall at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, which killed seven people, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah ordered the suspension of the executive engineer involved and directed a notice to be issued to the hospital authorities. The Lokayukta has registered a suo motu case and initiated an inquiry into the incident.  The Bengaluru City Police filed an Unnatural Death Report (UDR) but have not yet registered an FIR against any authorities for alleged negligence. An investigation is underway to determine the cause of the collapse, with experts from the Public Works Department and the India Meteorological Department consulted.

articles.title: Forget Ronaldo: João Cancelo set for historic record no player has ever achieved if Barca win La Liga | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: João Cancelo is on the verge of becoming the first player to win four of Europe's "Big Five" leagues.  He could achieve this milestone if Barcelona wins La Liga, completing a sequence that includes titles in Italy, England, Germany and Spain. This would make him the only player with league titles in five different countries. The Portuguese full-back has already won three of these titles, including one with Barcelona, and is on track to add a fourth if they win the title in 2025-26.  His career achievements are comparable to those of Cristiano Ronaldo, but differ in terms of variety rather than volume.

articles.title: 'Clock on diplomacy has not stopped': FO says Pakistan remains actively engaged with Iran, US to resolve conflict - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Tahir Andrabi stated that Pakistan remains actively engaged with Iran and the United States to achieve a resolution to the ongoing conflict.  The ceasefire, brokered by Pakistan, has allowed for substantive diplomacy between the two sides, including talks held in Islamabad on April 11 and 12.  Andrabi confirmed that diplomatic exchanges have continued since the ceasefire, with both parties deliberating on proposals to resolve the conflict. He also noted that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has had multiple phone conversations with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, and that Pakistani officials are in contact with the Somali government regarding the hijacking of an oil tanker off the coast of Somalia, where 11 Pakistani crew members are being held hostage.  Andrabi emphasized Pakistan's commitment to facilitating a peaceful resolution and ensuring the safety of all involved.

articles.title: Lindsey Vonn not ready to decide if she’ll ski again after Olympics crash | Winter Olympics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lindsey Vonn is still recovering physically and emotionally from a complex leg fracture sustained during the 2026 Winter Olympics. The American ski racer, who underwent eight surgeries, needs one more to repair a torn ACL in her left knee.  Vonn plans to focus on her recovery before deciding if she will return to racing. She acknowledges that a decision about her future is premature and wants to be fully recovered before making any choices.

articles.title: Press freedom at lowest level in 25 years amid growing authoritarian pressure | Press freedom | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Press Freedom Index, compiled by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), revealed that press freedom globally reached its lowest point in 25 years.  More than half of countries were categorized as "difficult" or "very serious" for press freedom, with the number of people living in countries with good press freedom plummeting from a fifth in 2002 to less than 1%. The report attributed this decline to restrictive legal arsenals used by governments, particularly national security laws, and political hostility towards the press.  The study highlighted the impact of authoritarian regimes like Russia, where over 48 journalists are imprisoned, as well as the influence of powerful figures like Donald Trump who have been criticized for their attacks on the press. The report also pointed to the negative effects of the US's decision to cut funding to media organizations and the rise of online abuse in Britain.

articles.title: Railways Minister flags off first Jammu-Srinagar direct train service on ‘historic day’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw and J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah celebrated the launch of the first direct train service between Jammu city and Srinagar city.  Vaishnaw described the service as a "gamechanger" for the region's economy, highlighting its impact on cargo movement and tourism. The new rail line connects the Kashmir division with the Jammu division, offering seamless travel to pilgrimage destinations like Shree Mata Vaishno Devi and Shri Amarnath temple. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is credited with realizing the dream of railway connectivity in the Kashmir Valley.

articles.title: F1 to return in 2027 to country absent from calendar since 2021 under new multi-year agreement | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Formula 1 will return to Türkiye in 2027 with a multi-year agreement for the Turkish Grand Prix, scheduled through 2031. The race will be held at Istanbul Park, marking its comeback after being absent since 2021. The event is part of a reshaped Formula 1 calendar that includes two dropped races and potential expansion to new venues like Thailand.  The return is supported by strong audience figures within Türkiye, with a growing social media following.  Formula 1 president and CEO Stefano Domenicali expressed excitement about returning to Istanbul, calling it a "cultural gateway between Europe and Asia."

articles.title: Freshly transferred Justices Sattar, Kayani to hear cases at PHC, LHC from coming week - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Babar Sattar and Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani, who were recently transferred from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to the Peshawar High Court (PHC) and Lahore High Court (LHC), respectively, have been included in their new court's rosters. The transfers were approved by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) amidst criticism from lawyers’ bodies.  The JCP also decided that any vacancy arising as a result of the transfer of judges would be filled through transfer only, and such slots would not be treated as vacancies for initial appointment.

articles.title: ‘Act of piracy’: World reacts to Israeli interception of Gaza aid flotilla | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel intercepted 22 out of 58 aid ships bound for the besieged Gaza Strip, seizing 211 activists including a Paris city councillor. Global Sumud Flotilla organizers condemned the action as "piracy" and called it a violation of international law.  World leaders, including Italy, Germany, Spain, and Turkiye, expressed strong condemnation of Israel's actions, demanding the release of the detained activists and respect for international law. Amnesty International also called for their immediate release, while Israel’s Foreign Ministry defended its action as lawful.

articles.title: Uganda nursery attack: Christopher Okello Onyum sentenced to death for murder of Kampala toddlers
articles.rephrased_article: Christopher Okello Onyum, a 38-year-old man with Ugandan and US citizenship, was sentenced to death by hanging for the murder of four toddlers at a nursery school in Kampala.  Onyum admitted to the crime but later pleaded not guilty, claiming mental illness prevented him from forming intent to kill. Justice Alice Komuhangi Khauka ruled that Onyum was "very sane" on the day of the attack and sentenced him accordingly. The prosecution presented evidence including DNA, CCTV footage, and eyewitness accounts, which led to his conviction.

articles.title: Iran supreme leader issues defiant statement on strait of Hormuz | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's supreme leader, issued a defiant statement vowing to secure the Strait of Hormuz and eliminate what he described as "the enemy's abuses", asserting Iranian control over the waterway.  He promised to guard Iran's nuclear and missile programs while also demanding that foreign powers respect Iran's sovereignty in the region. Khamenei's statement comes amid ongoing tensions with the United States following a series of attacks on Iranian shipping, which have led to a blockade of Iranian ports and a spike in oil prices. The US has been exploring options to resume strikes against Iran while diplomatic efforts continue between the two countries and international partners.

articles.title: HC orders inquiry on ‘erring officers’ who did not act against illegal structures at Salkam cheruvu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court ordered a detailed inquiry into construction violations at the Barrister Fatima Owaisi Education Campus within the Full Tank Level/buffer zone of Salkam Cheruvu. The HYDRAA, Municipal Administration and Urban Development, GHMC, and HMDA were instructed to report by July 7th on how officials permitted structures in the buffer zone.  The judge also directed the School Education department to ensure students are not disturbed.

articles.title: Move over TACO, NACHO takes over: Trump earns new nickname amid oil disruption from Strait of Hormuz blockade - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has earned a new nickname, "NACHO," as tensions over the Strait of Hormuz fuel market and political commentary. Javier Blas, a Bloomberg columnist, coined the term to reflect growing skepticism that the dispute will be resolved quickly.  The Strait of Hormuz handles 20% of global crude oil shipments and any disruption has immediate effects on global energy supply and prices. The US administration has imposed restrictions on Iranian ports and shipping activity while Iran has tightened its control over the strait, but negotiations between the US, Israel and Iran have stalled. Despite a ceasefire framework, Kush Desai, White House spokesperson, pushed back against the "NACHO" label, questioning critics of the administration's trade and policy record.

articles.title: Finance ministry flags risk to Pakistan's external sector amid global uncertainty - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Ministry of Finance in Pakistan reported a stable economy despite global uncertainties and regional supply disruptions.  The primary balance remained strong at 3.3% of GDP, driven by tax collection growth and expenditure management. The Ministry forecasted April's inflation rate to be between 8-9%, but highlighted the positive impact of remittances and IT exports on the current account surplus. While acknowledging risks posed by the Middle East conflict, the ministry projected continued economic growth supported by macroeconomic stability and effective policy responses.

articles.title: Africa and Asia back Infantino for unique fourth term as FIFA president | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA President Gianni Infantino has received strong backing from the Confederations of Africa (CAF) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) for his potential re-election in 2027. Both regional confederations have pledged their support, accounting for a significant portion of FIFA's voting power.  Infantino's bid is further bolstered by previous endorsements from CONMEBOL, adding to his momentum as he seeks a fourth term at the helm of world football.

articles.title: Myanmar ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi moved to house arrest, military says
articles.rephrased_article: Aung San Suu Kyi, the former Myanmar leader, has been moved to house arrest after spending years in detention since a military coup in 2021. Min Aung Hlaing, the leader of the coup, announced the change, stating he had "commuted her remaining sentence" to be served at a designated residence.  Kim Aris, Suu Kyi's son, expressed skepticism about the announcement and demanded proof of her well-being. Her legal team confirmed they had not been notified of the house arrest.

articles.title: German artist Georg Baselitz dies aged 88 | Art | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Georg Baselitz, a German artist known for his controversial and expressive paintings and sculptures, has died at the age of 88. The Thaddaeus Ropac gallery, which had a long-standing relationship with the artist, confirmed his death on Thursday.  Baselitz's work, spanning six decades and various techniques, reflected the traumas of German history and is now held in prestigious public collections. He was born Hans-Georg Kern in 1938 and adopted the name Baselitz in 1961.

articles.title: Germany was largest exporter of plastic waste in 2025, sending 810,000 tonnes overseas, analysis finds | Plastics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Germany and the UK were the world's largest exporters of plastic waste in 2025, sending over 810,000 tonnes and 675,000 tonnes respectively.  Much of this waste is sent to countries like Turkey, Malaysia, and Indonesia where recycling infrastructure is often inadequate, leading to environmental damage and labor abuses. The EU has agreed to ban exports of plastic waste to non-OECD countries by November 2026, but concerns remain that the ban could be circumvented or redirected to other destinations.  The UK is tightening its own regulations on plastic waste exports and recycling, but environmental campaigners argue these measures are insufficient to address the root causes of the problem.

articles.title: Odissi elegance casts a spell at Koodalmanikyam festival - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Madhulita Mohapatra and the Nrityantar Dance Ensemble performed a captivating Odissi dance recital at the Koodalmanikyam Temple in Irinjalakuda as part of the annual Koodalmanikyam Temple Festival 2026. The performance, which included devotional pieces like Jagannath Ashtakam and Malhar Pallavi, showcased the grace and rhythmic beauty of Odissi dance.  The recital was further enhanced by a live orchestra and a special appearance by five-year-old Mihika as baby Krishna.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "Obsessing over Charlie Kirk’s spouse": Laura Loomer blasts Candace Owens' husband George Farmer over alleged DUI claims in viral post - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Laura Loomer's viral post on social media has sparked controversy surrounding Candace Owens and her husband, George Farmer.  Loomer alleges that Farmer was involved in multiple accidents, including a DUI, and suggests there is documentation supporting these claims. The post also criticizes Owens for allegedly misleading her audience about the incidents. Owens has not publicly responded to the allegations, but the situation highlights the challenges of verifying information shared on social media platforms.

articles.title: From railways to energy — five strategic projects linking Gulf states | Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) leaders met in Riyadh to discuss strategic projects aimed at mitigating geopolitical risks. These initiatives, spanning transport, energy, water security and defense, aim to deepen economic ties and strengthen collective resilience.  The GCC railway project, electrical interconnection grid, water interconnection system, and oil and gas pipeline integration are among the most prominent joint projects. The war with Iran has highlighted the need for these projects as they become more than just economic aspirations but also crucial security necessities.

articles.title: In fresh message, Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei defies US naval blockade - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader, declared a "shameful defeat" for the United States in the region following recent military actions. He asserted that Iran has established control over the Strait of Hormuz and dismissed US naval blockade threats as futile.  President Masoud Pezeshkian echoed these sentiments, stating the blockade would fail to enhance regional security. Navy Commander Shahram Irani also indicated Iran's readiness to deploy new naval weaponry in response.

articles.title: Australians will pay more if Albanese fast-tracks fossil fuel projects, former oil and gas leaders warn | Fossil fuels | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Former oil and gas industry leaders, including former BP Australia chief executive Greg Bourne, ex-BP vice-president for global projects Russell Smith, and Bernard Wheelahan, a former director of Shell Australia, president of Shell Venezuela, and chair of lobby group the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association (now known as Australian Energy Producers), have urged the Albanese government to prioritize renewable energy deployment over fossil fuel development in response to the global energy crisis. The ex-executives argued that expanding drilling and approving new fossil fuel projects would not improve Australia's liquid fuel security and could lead to continued price shocks for households. They emphasized that investing in renewables, modernizing the grid, and supporting large-scale electrification is a more sustainable solution.

articles.title: Make right to vote a fundamental right, says Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh called for the right to vote to be made a fundamental right, arguing that it is currently not justiciable. He criticized the Election Commission of India (ECI) and its current leadership, alleging irregularities in electoral rolls and a lack of transparency.  Ramesh also expressed skepticism towards exit polls, citing their inaccuracy in previous elections. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi shared a video highlighting concerns from a delegation from Ladakh regarding suppression of democratic rights and land grabs by powerful individuals.

articles.title: 'They call Trump Nazi, Hitler & still attend': Erika Kirk hits out at journalists for 'ultimate hypocrisy' at White House dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Erika Kirk, CEO of Turning Point USA, criticized journalists for using extreme language to describe President Donald Trump, accusing them of hypocrisy and fueling a hostile environment.  Kirk attended the White House Correspondents' Dinner to confront journalists about their coverage of her and her late husband, Charlie Kirk, who was murdered in 2025. She claimed that the attack on the dinner was linked to a broader climate of dehumanization and criticized journalists for prioritizing capturing footage over safety during the incident.  Kirk also accused political opponents and commentators of contributing to a hostile environment.

articles.title: Iran, protests, human rights – all to know about the 76th FIFA Congress | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The 76th FIFA Congress in Canada will be overshadowed by geopolitical tensions, human rights concerns, and logistical issues related to the upcoming World Cup. The Iranian delegation departed from Canada after citing mistreatment by immigration officials, while Amnesty International urged FIFA President Gianni Infantino to ensure human rights are protected at the tournament.  The congress also saw protests from local fans in Vancouver against the potential relocation of the Vancouver Whitecaps soccer team to Las Vegas.

articles.title: Arif Habib-led consortium notifies Privatisation Commission of its intent to acquire remaining 25pc PIA stake - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Privatisation Commission announced that the consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited has notified its intent to acquire the remaining 25% equity stake in Pakistan International Airlines Corporation Limited (PIACL), paving the way for full private-sector ownership. The transaction is expected to involve a total private-sector investment of approximately Rs180 billion, with the consortium paying Rs55 billion as divestment proceeds and injecting Rs125 billion as fresh equity into PIACL.  The transfer of management control is anticipated to occur on or before May 25th, subject to fulfilling conditions outlined in the Share Purchase and Subscription Agreement (SPSA).

articles.title: Why China banning drone sales in Beijing?
articles.rephrased_article: China is implementing new rules banning the sale of drones and requiring permits for drone use in Beijing, effective Friday. The move aims to address public safety concerns and comes as part of China's strategic focus on the low-altitude economy, which is projected to generate over two trillion yuan by 2035. Drone owners will need to register their devices with the police.

articles.title: The chips are down: pizza, fried chicken and doughnut shares plunge on ASX as living costs bite budgets | Australian economy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Domino’s Pizza, KFC operator Collins Foods, and multi-brand food franchise owner Retail Food Group have experienced significant price drops on the ASX, coinciding with rising living costs and consumer pessimism.  The decline in fast food stocks is attributed to concerns over declining consumer spending due to high fuel prices, interest rate increases, and inflation. The situation is further complicated by a potential shift in consumer behavior, as they may be trading down from restaurants or opting for cheaper alternatives.

articles.title: Two men sentenced to life imprisonment for murder - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Principal District and Sessions Court sentenced two men, Goni Ramu (26) and Pasupuleti Sandeep Kumar (25), to life imprisonment for the murder of Vaka Ashok (29) in Nellore. The incident occurred on October 15, 2024, when a heated argument between the accused and the victim escalated into a stabbing attack by Ramu who used a knife from his waist.

articles.title: Machines take charge: China to deploy 8,500 robots in $1B push to automate its power grid | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: State Grid Corporation of China is investing $1 billion to procure 8,500 robots for grid operations. The robots will assist with inspection and maintenance across substations and transmission networks, reducing risks to human workers and improving efficiency. China's initiative reflects a broader effort to advance industrial robotics and AI-enabled infrastructure. These robots are designed to detect faults, monitor equipment conditions, and perform basic maintenance tasks in challenging environments.  The deployment is expected to continue through 2026.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia to end LIV Golf funding, while league appoints new chairman | Golf News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) has announced it will end funding for the LIV Golf league after the 2026 season. The LIV Golf board, led by Gene Davis and Jon Zinman, is now seeking long-term financial partners to replace the Saudi investment.  The league aims to move towards an investment model involving multiple partners and team franchises. Despite the funding cut, LIV Golf has grown the game globally and plans to continue promoting golf.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz extends fuel subsidy for motorcyclists, goods transport by one month - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif extended fuel subsidies for motorcyclists, public and goods transport by one month. The decision was made to provide relief to economically vulnerable groups during the current situation.  He also directed transporters not to increase fares and instructed for effective monitoring of the measures. Shehbaz Sharif emphasized that providing relief to the common man remains a priority and hopes regional stability will lead to fuel price stabilization.

articles.title: Trainee driver crashes bus into River Seine
articles.rephrased_article: A trainee driver crashed a bus into the River Seine in Juvisy-sur-Orge, France, after hitting a parked car and veering off the road. L'Esson prefecture said all four passengers were rescued from the water, and Île-de-France Mobilités, the local transport authority, ordered an internal investigation into the incident.  The driver was accompanied by a "lead driver" and two passengers, and no drug or alcohol tests have come back positive.

articles.title: Queensland rejects key Bondi report recommendation as Albanese’s gun buyback flounders | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Queensland has rejected key recommendations from the Bondi royal commission's interim report, stating that a national gun buyback will not keep weapons out of the hands of terrorists and criminals. Premier David Crisafulli, despite calling for the commission's establishment, maintains Queensland will not participate in the proposed buyback scheme.  Federal Labor is frustrated by the opposition to the plans agreed upon by national cabinet in January, while New South Wales is the only state supporting the push. The Northern Territory has ruled out participation and other states have yet to commit to the initiative.

articles.title: Firefighters battle Powys wildfires for fifth day as public urged to stay away | Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Firefighters are battling wildfires in the Elan valley, mid-Wales for a fifth day. The Mid and West Wales fire and rescue service has been working to extinguish the blazes, which have caused concern for the area's biodiversity.  A helicopter is being used to tackle fires near Claerwen dam and Teifi Pools, while Hafod Estate, a National Trust property, remains closed until further notice. The cause of the fires is still unknown, but dry weather has significantly increased fire risk across Wales.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Marie Curie: "There are sadistic scientists who hurry to hunt down error instead of establishing the truth." | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Marie Curie's quote, "There are sadistic scientists who hurry to hunt down error instead of establishing the truth," highlights the importance of finding the truth in scientific discovery.  While criticism is essential for quality control and progress, it shouldn't overshadow the pursuit of accurate knowledge. Curie, a scientist known for her meticulous research, emphasized the need for patience, accuracy, and collaboration to achieve true understanding. Her work exemplifies this approach, emphasizing that real progress comes from dedication to truth-seeking rather than simply finding mistakes.

articles.title: Telangana Govt extends Prajavani to RDO level with immediate effect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Government has expanded its Prajavani public grievance redressal initiative to the revenue division level, with weekly sessions conducted by sub-collectors or revenue divisional officers. The program will be phased out to the mandal level in the future.  The initiative mandates registration of grievances online and provides a dedicated portal for tracking and monitoring resolution progress. District Collectors oversee district-level Prajavani sessions, where all department officers are present to address citizen concerns.

articles.title: Russia has given Iran something more important than weapons | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia's political backing of Iran and its opposition to military escalation have proven more impactful than military aid in shaping the conflict between Iran, the United States, and Israel.  The visit of Iran’s Foreign Minister, Abbas Araghchi, to Russia highlights this strategic alliance, as both countries seek a peaceful resolution despite short-term benefits for Moscow like rising oil prices. While Russia recognizes the need to restructure its economy in light of Western sanctions and acknowledges the risks associated with escalating the conflict, it prioritizes diplomatic efforts over military solutions.  The situation remains fragile, particularly for Iran, as the US retains significant influence despite temporary resource constraints.

articles.title: Govt slashes passport delivery time to 14 days, orders offices to go cashless - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry announced a series of changes to streamline passport processing. The delivery time for ordinary passports was reduced from 21 days to 14 days, effective immediately.  All passport offices will become fully cashless within 15 days, aiming to eliminate the "agent mafia" and improve service. Officials also directed the development of a separate "business passport" category and improvements to home-delivery systems. The changes were made in response to increased demand for passports and complaints about long queues and delays.

articles.title: Financial Times journalists in dispute with management over plans for office days | Financial Times | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Journalists at the Financial Times are in dispute with management over plans to require staff to work four days a week by year's end. The Financial Times union has invoked the company's dispute procedure, arguing that the proposal lacks justification and raises concerns about its impact on staff, particularly mothers, finances, and existing employment contracts.  The union also points out that the policy only applies to editorial staff at the London headquarters.

articles.title: Most decorated woman athlete with seven Olympic golds planning stunning LA28 comeback at 42 | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Allyson Felix, the most decorated woman in Olympic track and field history, is planning a return to competition with the aim of reaching the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles.  The Olympic organizing committee member has set her sights on competing at age 42, after retiring following the Tokyo Olympics cycle. She aims to participate in the opening ceremony and hopes to meet qualification requirements for the US Olympic trials in 2027. Felix's return is driven by a desire to experience the home crowd atmosphere of the Games, despite acknowledging the challenges of competing at this stage in her career.

articles.title: ‘Drishyam 3’ teaser: Past haunts Mohanlal’s Georgekutty in this suspense thriller - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Drishyam 3, the third installment in the popular suspense-thriller franchise, saw its teaser unveiled on April 29, 2026. The film, directed by Jeethu Joseph and starring Mohanlal, is scheduled for release on May 21, 2026.  Produced by Antony Perumbavoor under Aashirvad Cinemas, the movie also features a star-studded cast including Meena, Siddique, Asha Sharath, Murali Gopy, Ansiba Hassan and Esther Anil. The teaser highlights the character of Georgekutty facing his past.  The film will be presented by Dr Jayantilal Gada (Pen Studios) and Panorama Studios.

articles.title: Israel kills nine people in southern Lebanon despite ‘ceasefire’ | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has escalated attacks in southern Lebanon, killing at least nine people despite a three-week extension to the US-mediated ceasefire.  The attacks have targeted residential buildings and homes in Jebchit, Toul, and Harouf, with Israeli forces also issuing forced displacement threats for 15 Lebanese towns. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun denounced these violations as "war crimes" and called for international pressure on Israel to respect international law. Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri also urged the formation of an international fact-finding committee to investigate the violence.

articles.title: Imaan, Hadi approach SC seeking early hearing of appeals against conviction in social media posts case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, filed an appeal with the Supreme Court seeking an early hearing of their convictions under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). The lawyers were sentenced to 17 years in prison for social media posts they made.  They argued that the case was a “sham trial” and requested the SC to suspend their sentence pending the appeal. The application cited urgency, citing the Supreme Court's policy on prioritizing criminal matters.

articles.title: Israel intercepts and detains crews of Gaza aid flotilla near Crete | Gaza | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s IDF intercepted and detained crews of at least 22 boats from the Global Sumud Flotilla attempting to break Israel's maritime blockade of the Gaza Strip. The flotilla, consisting of about 58 vessels carrying people from across 70 countries, departed from Italy on Sunday with the aim of delivering humanitarian aid. Israel’s foreign ministry said the IDF took control of more than 20 boats with about 175 activists onboard.  The Global Sumud Flotilla responded to the interception by calling it a "violent raid in international waters" and accusing Israel of violating humanitarian principles and international law. The flotilla's organizers, along with France, Turkey, and the UN condemned the action.

articles.title: ‘No place in Gulf, except at bottom of its waters’: Iran’s Khamenei slams ‘Great Satan’ US, rejects nuclear curbs - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader, criticized the United States, calling it the "Great Satan" and asserting that Iran's nuclear and missile capabilities are non-negotiable. He stated that Iran's technological and military advancements are national assets protected by its people and will not be compromised.  Khamenei also emphasized Iran's regional influence in the Persian Gulf, advocating for a new management framework for the Strait of Hormuz to shape the region's future.

articles.title: Bengaluru weather highlights: Orange alert issued for Bengaluru, south Karnataka districts; traffic police release advisory for commuters - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CM Siddaramaiah visited injured individuals after a portion of the Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital compound wall collapsed in Shivajinagar, killing seven people.  The Medical Education Minister Sharanprakash R. Patil ordered safety audits for government hospital buildings. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued an orange alert for Bengaluru, urging caution from motorists due to heavy rainfall.

articles.title: Tunisia’s jailed opposition leader Ghannouchi rushed to hospital | Civil Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rached Ghannouchi, the 84-year-old former speaker of parliament and head of the Ennahdha party, has been rushed to hospital after a sharp deterioration in his health.  His party is calling for his immediate release, citing his chronic illnesses and the politically motivated nature of his imprisonment since April 2023. President Kais Saied, who suspended the Tunisian parliament in 2021 and dissolved the legislature to rule by decree, has been accused of orchestrating a crackdown on the political opposition.  Human rights organizations, including Human Rights Watch (HRW) and Amnesty International, have condemned these arrests.

articles.title: Cambridge confirms AS-level math exam leak, says working on determining next steps - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE) confirmed that its AS-level mathematics paper was shared prematurely, violating regulations. This incident follows reports of a leak and concerns about exam transparency from parents and students. CIE is investigating the extent of the leak and will provide an update on May 7th. The organization emphasizes its commitment to protecting the integrity of exams and ensuring student fairness.

articles.title: Limiting capital gains tax changes to new investments would ‘severely delay’ budget reforms, Deloitte says | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Deloitte suggests phasing in changes to investor tax breaks for existing investments over three years would generate significantly more revenue than applying the new rules only to new investments. This additional revenue could fund income tax cuts or other productivity-enhancing reforms, such as a higher tax-free threshold. Jim Chalmers, treasurer, has cautioned that these changes wouldn't yield substantial revenue in the near future and emphasized the need for transitional arrangements to minimize disruption for investors.  The consulting firm also predicts smaller than previously estimated deficits due to higher commodity prices and inflation boosting company profits.

articles.title: Reform UK’s Zia Yusuf threatens to ban NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani from UK over kohinoor return call | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Zia Yusuf, a senior figure in Reform UK, has threatened to ban New York’s mayor Zohran Mamdani from entering Britain after Mamdani called for the return of the Kohinoor diamond to India.  Yusuf criticized Mamdani's comments ahead of his meeting with King Charles III, stating he would take action if in office and that the diamond will "stay" in London. Critics question whether Yusuf's stance aligns with Reform UK's stated support for free speech.

articles.title: Gujarat High Court, after attire remarks in court, asks IIT Gandhinagar to ‘show sympathy’ to suspended student - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Gujarat High Court orally advised the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IIT-Gn) to show sympathy towards a postgraduate student who was previously reprimanded for her attire. The court acknowledged the student's age and potential lack of understanding of consequences, stating that her conduct did not warrant suspension despite initial concerns about decorum in court.  The court emphasized that past actions played a role in its decision.

articles.title: Kenya gives hero’s welcome to marathon record-breaker Sabastian Sawe | Athletics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sebastian Sawe, the marathon record-breaker who set a new world record of 1:59:30 in the London Marathon, received a hero's welcome in Kenya.  He was greeted by jubilant fans and President William Ruto, who awarded him $62,000 and a car. Sawe’s achievement has inspired many young athletes and is seen as a testament to human potential.

articles.title: Pakistan in contact with Somalia over sailors held hostage by pirates: FO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan is in contact with the Somali government regarding the hijacking of an oil tanker and its 11 Pakistani crew members. The incident has raised concerns about a resurgence of pirate attacks off the Somali coast, which peaked in 2011.  The Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson also addressed the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, emphasizing the importance of restoring normal maritime flow for global trade and energy security.  The FO confirmed that all Pakistani nationals detained in Cambodia are safe and being provided with necessary support. The spokesperson urged citizens to be cautious of fraudulent overseas job schemes.

articles.title: Bamako siege: Islamists block entry to Mali's capital city
articles.rephrased_article: Mali's capital city, Bamako, is under a partial blockade by Islamist militants from Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), preventing residents from entering or leaving the city. The group has imposed a total blockade on several routes into the city, leaving many stranded and facing shortages of food and water.  The junta leader, Gen Assimi Goïta, has vowed to take action against the insurgents but faces criticism for his inability to restore security in the country. Several countries have urged their citizens to leave Mali while the situation remains volatile, with ongoing attacks by jihadists and separatists.

articles.title: Canada to create powerful financial crimes agency as US weakens its approach | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Canada is establishing a new Financial Crimes Agency (FCA) to investigate and prosecute financial crimes, a move that contrasts with the US approach where federal investigators have struggled to pursue fraudsters. The FCA will replace Fintrac, which currently handles investigations but lacks the power to arrest criminals.  The agency's creation follows a public inquiry that found Canada lacked a cohesive strategy against money laundering. This new law enforcement agency is expected to address concerns about financial crime, including cryptocurrency-related fraud and money laundering, as well as bolstering Canada's international standing in combating these crimes.

articles.title: Punjab Assembly passes film city, environment, wildlife bills amid uproar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab Assembly passed the Punjab Film City Authority Bill 2026 after a contentious session marked by disagreements between the ruling and opposition parties.  Marriyum Aurangzeb, Senior Minister, defended the bill as an economic growth initiative, while opposition members criticized it for diverting funds from critical sectors like education and health. Ijaz Shafi accused the government of prioritizing entertainment over essential services, prompting Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan to order his controversial remarks expunged.  Despite interruptions and protests, the bill was passed, with Marriyum Aurangzeb emphasizing its regulatory mechanisms for the film industry.

articles.title: Bank of England leaves interest rates on hold at 3.75% | Bank of England | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Bank of England kept interest rates at 3.75% on Thursday, citing the unavoidable rise in inflation due to the war in the Middle East. The MPC voted 8-1 to hold rates, with dissent from chief economist Huw Pill who advocated for a rate hike to 4%.  The Bank acknowledged that energy price increases will push inflation higher but believes second-round effects will be restrained. The Bank of England expects inflation to rise in the near term and predicts unemployment will increase to at least 5.5% by 2027, requiring further interest rate hikes.

articles.title: Syngene shares zoom 17% even as firm’s Q4 net profit drops 19% YoY. What's driving the surge? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Syngene International reported a multi-fold increase in net profit for the fourth quarter of FY26, reaching Rs 153 crore.  The company's revenue grew nearly 2% to Rs 1,036.5 crore. Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, who transitioned from Non Executive Chairman to Executive Chairman, expressed optimism about the company's future growth. Peter Bains, Managing Director and CEO, highlighted the company's steady momentum despite challenges posed by a single large-molecule biologics client.  Siddharth Mittal, appointed Managing Director and CEO effective July 1, 2026, will succeed Peter Bains. Macquarie maintained its 'Outperform' rating on Syngene shares with a target price of Rs 835 apiece.

articles.title: Press freedom worldwide falls to its lowest level in 25 years | Freedom of the Press News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Reporters Without Borders (RSF), a Paris-based press freedom NGO, reports that global press freedom has reached its lowest point in 25 years.  The organization's World Press Freedom Index shows that more than half of the world's countries are categorized as "difficult" or "very serious" for press freedom, with only seven countries receiving a "good" rating. The decline is attributed to authoritarian states, political complicity, economic actors, and online platforms that suppress media workers.  RSF calls on governments and citizens to strengthen protection mechanisms and combat impunity to prevent the spread of authoritarianism.

articles.title: Air France-KLM cuts capacity growth forecast amid expected $2.4bn fuel bill rise | Air France/KLM | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Air France-KLM has lowered its capacity growth forecasts for 2023 due to increased fuel costs resulting from the Iran war, now expecting a 2% to 4% increase compared to the previous 3% to 5%. The airline's chief executive, Ben Smith, stated that fuel price increases will impact future quarters. Despite implementing a "rolling fuel hedging policy", Air France-KLM anticipates a $9.3 billion fuel bill in 2026, an increase of $2.4 billion from 2025.

articles.title: Vedanta's 65% share price crash an illusion, the stock is down just 5%. Here's why - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta's shares plummeted by 64.9% on Thursday, marking a significant drop from the previous close and reducing its market capitalization to Rs 1.13 lakh crore. The stock opened sharply lower at Rs 289.50 after closing at Rs 773.60 on Wednesday. Vedanta's demerger into four separate listed entities, including Vedanta Aluminium, Vedanta Power, Vedanta Oil & Gas, and Vedanta Steel & Iron Ore, began trading without the value of these units. The demerger was approved by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) in December 2022.  Vedanta's Chairman, Anil Agarwal, believes the restructuring will unlock shareholder value over time.

articles.title: Israel arrests 175 activists from Gaza flotilla far from its waters - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s army arrested approximately 175 activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla in international waters off Greece. The Global Sumud Flotilla, which organized the flotilla, reported that Israeli military boats surrounded the flotilla and threatened violence.
