The organization stated that communications with eleven vessels were lost, and they called for international intervention. Mushtaq Ahmad, a former senator from Pakistan who led the flotilla last year, confirmed the attack in a video message.  Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) reported that Israeli authorities have used water access as a weapon against Palestinians, systematically depriving them of water and hindering their ability to receive critical supplies.

articles.title: Environmental disaster fears grip Russia as Ukraine targets oil refineries | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ukrainian forces have targeted Russia’s largest oil refinery in Tuapse, causing black rain and ecological damage. The attacks, aimed at disrupting the Russian oil industry, resulted in a series of fires that released poisonous chemicals into the air.  Black rain has fallen on parts of Russia, coating cars, animals, and beaches with oil. Volunteers are working to clean up the oil spills while authorities have dispatched boats and booms to contain the slick. The long-term consequences for the local ecosystem could be severe, potentially lasting for years.

articles.title: Eurozone inflation soars to 3% as Iran war drives up energy prices | Eurozone | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Eurozone inflation reached 3% in April, exceeding the European Central Bank's target of 2%, driven by surging energy prices.  The increase was fueled by a 10.9% year-on-year rise in energy costs and slowed growth to 0.1% in the first quarter. While Germany saw positive growth, economists warn that factors like the war in the Middle East and high energy prices pose risks for future economic performance.

articles.title: HUL shares drop over 4% despite Q4 topping Street estimates; profit jumps 21% YoY to Rs 2,464 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Unilever Limited (HUL) reported a 7.6% year-on-year increase in revenue to Rs 16,351 crore for the quarter ending March 2025. EBITDA rose by 3.2% to Rs 3,877 crore, with EBITDA margins improving by 70 basis points YoY.  The Home Care segment saw its strongest performance in 11 quarters, while Beauty & Wellbeing delivered 8% USG and Personal Care grew 5%. The company proposed a final dividend of Rs 22 per share for FY26.

articles.title: 2028 Chandrayaan-5 launch site preparation begins: ISRO team visits Japan for assessment | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) team is visiting Japan to assess the launch site preparations for Chandrayaan-5, a mission focused on lunar exploration.  This visit underscores the growing cooperation between ISRO and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), with both organizations sharing objectives in space science and technology development. The collaboration aims to ensure technical compatibility, safety considerations, and environmental conditions for deep space missions, building upon the success of Chandrayaan-3.  This collaborative effort exemplifies a global trend towards international partnerships in space exploration.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz launches Rs10m housing loans under Rs3.2tr 'Apna Ghar Programme' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif launched the “PM Apna Ghar Programme” in Islamabad, aiming to construct 500,000 housing units with a total allocation of Rs3.2 trillion. The program provides housing loans of up to Rs10 million on easy installments, with a 5% markup for the first 10 years and market rate thereafter.  The European Investment Bank’s international development arm, EIB Global, is also committing €160m to support Pakistan's rebuilding efforts in Sindh and water quality improvement in Karachi.

articles.title: Rise in caesarean section births in Gaza brings danger and infection risks | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: In Gaza, the number of caesarean sections has increased by 2 percent since before the war, now comprising a quarter of all births. This rise is attributed to factors such as food shortages, malnutrition, and displacement caused by Israeli destruction. The lack of proper medical equipment and supplies, overcrowding in hospitals, and limited access to antibiotics have also contributed to an increase in caesarean section complications, including infections.  The conditions in Gaza pose significant risks for mothers who undergo the procedure, leading to prolonged recovery and increased infection rates.

articles.title: China to ban drone sales in Beijing citing security concerns
articles.rephrased_article: China will ban the sale of drones in Beijing and require permits for their use starting Friday. The new rules, aimed at enhancing public safety, prohibit drone sales, rentals, and imports into the city.  Drone owners must register their devices with the police and obtain prior approval for outdoor flights. These restrictions follow a trend of tightening regulations on drones in recent years as China seeks to manage the "low-altitude economy" while balancing technological advancements and safety concerns.

articles.title: The Bondi terror report raises more questions than answers about the massacre - and illuminated its horror | Bondi beach terror attack | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion released an interim report detailing the Bondi massacre, revealing that over a third of recommendations are confidential. The report highlights the Akram brothers' alleged links to Islamic extremism, their travel to a known terror hotspot in the Philippines, and their training at a farm in regional NSW.  The commission also questioned whether national intelligence agencies were adequately funded to address the heightened terror threat level following the Hamas attacks on Israel. While the report sheds light on the attack's path, it remains unclear how authorities could have prevented it. The commission will continue its public hearings next week focusing on experiences of antisemitism.

articles.title: Meesho shares jump 10% as JP Morgan initiates coverage with Rs 215 target price - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JP Morgan analysts have issued a bullish report on Meesho, predicting strong growth for the Indian e-commerce platform.  The brokerage expects Meesho's net merchandise value (NMV) to grow at a 23% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over FY26-31, driven by rising platform frequency and falling return-to-origin orders. Meesho is expected to reach an estimated 568 million annual transacting users by FY31, with significant EBITDA margin expansion to 4% by FY31.  The brokerage also highlights the company's potential for advertising revenue growth and its strong market leadership position in India.

articles.title: This nanogenerator turns seawater evaporation into electricity-and it never stops | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: EPFL scientists have developed a novel hydrovoltaic nano-generator that harnesses the energy from seawater evaporation to generate electricity. The device, using silicon nanopillars and a three-layered design, produces five times more power than traditional methods. This innovation could revolutionize battery-free sensor networks for IoT devices and wearable technology by providing continuous power through ambient heat and light.

articles.title: Sindh education department to introduce religious textbooks for Hindu students - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh Education and Literacy Department plans to introduce religious textbooks for Hindu students in grades three to five across government schools. The department requested the Sindh Textbook Board (STBB) to distribute these books, with the cost of publication covered by Prem Sagar Sanstha Karachi. This follows a similar move by the federal government in 2023, where the National Curriculum Council (NCC) issued no-objection certificates for publishing religious books for minority students.

articles.title: Civilians or Hezbollah: Who did Israel hit on Lebanon’s ‘Black Wednesday’? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: On April 8, Israel launched over 100 attacks across Lebanon, killing at least 357 people, including many civilians.  The attacks, which targeted what Israel claimed were Hezbollah headquarters and military assets, have been condemned by international organizations as indiscriminate and potentially violating international humanitarian law. While Israel claims to have killed 250 Hezbollah operatives, independent investigations suggest that the number of civilian casualties is significantly higher. The UN has called for an investigation into the attacks, while human rights groups continue to document the suffering caused by the conflict. Despite calls for accountability from various parties, including Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, Israel continues its military operations in Lebanon with little sign of a ceasefire or change in tactics.

articles.title: Israel intercepts Gaza flotilla near Crete and detains 175 activists
articles.rephrased_article: Israel intercepted 22 boats carrying aid for Gaza in international waters near Crete, detaining approximately 175 activists. The Global Sumud Flotilla (GSF) denounced the action as "piracy" and claimed it violated international law.  The Israeli foreign ministry dismissed the flotilla as a "PR stunt" and asserted that its actions comply with international law.

articles.title: ‘Historic breakthrough’: Colombia climate talks end with hopes raised for fossil fuel phaseout | Climate crisis | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Governments from nearly 60 countries met in Colombia to develop voluntary "roadmaps" outlining their plans to phase out fossil fuels. The initiative, a departure from traditional UN climate negotiations, aims to wean the world off coal, oil and gas. Irene Vélez Torres, chair of the talks, emphasized that this move is crucial for future generations.  While the absence of major emitters like the US, China, India, Russia, and petrostates was noted, participants agreed to support poorer countries with expertise and financial reform. The initiative will continue in a second conference next year.

articles.title: Why market fell today? Sensex slumps 583 pts, Nifty below 24,000; 7 key triggers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian benchmark indices experienced a sharp selloff on Thursday, erasing nearly Rs 5 lakh crore from the market capitalisation. Sensex closed down 583 points at 76,913, while Nifty fell over 180 points to close at 23,998.  The sell-off was driven by concerns about geopolitical tensions, rising oil prices, and the Federal Reserve's hawkish stance on inflation.  Global markets also dipped as oil prices surged above $120 per barrel. Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Tata Steel, and UltraTech Cement were among the top losers on the Sensex.  However, Sun Pharma emerged as the top gainer.

articles.title: Mount St. Helens Eruption: Mount St. Helens eruption: How Gophers transformed a barren land in 43 years | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists, including Dr. Charlie Crisafulli and Dr. James MacMahon, airlifted Northern pocket gophers into the Pumice Plain of Mount St. Helens in 1980 to study their impact on the devastated ecosystem. The rodents' digging activities helped re-inoculate the sterile volcanic soil with beneficial organisms, leading to a significant increase in plant growth within six years.  The experiment revealed that areas influenced by pocket gophers had a better network of fungi and established intricate plant communities much faster than natural processes. This study highlights the role of ecosystem engineers in accelerating ecological recovery.

articles.title: Lahore court grants interim pre-arrest bail to PM's daughter, son-in-law in Saaf Pani case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rabia Imran and her husband Ali Imran Yousaf were granted interim pre-arrest bail by an anti-corruption court in Lahore, Pakistan. The couple had previously been declared proclaimed offenders for their alleged involvement in irregularities at the Punjab Saaf Pani Company (PSPC).  The case was transferred to the anti-corruption court after being initially heard in an accountability court. Other suspects, including Shehbaz Sharif, have already been acquitted.

articles.title: Somalia shapes its own destiny in global security forums | Opinions | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Somalia has secured seats on the African Union Peace and Security Council (AU PSC) and the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), marking a significant shift in its global security role. This change reflects Somalia's growing diplomatic maturity, institutional capacity, and international credibility after decades of conflict.  These memberships allow Somalia to actively shape international peace agendas, advocate for its own interests, and promote inclusive development approaches. The country's participation in these bodies is expected to strengthen state-building efforts and contribute to broader global security frameworks.

articles.title: Trump says US studying troop cuts in Germany, after Merz criticises war
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced on social media that the US is "studying" potential troop reductions in Germany, following criticism from German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.  Merz had previously criticized Trump's approach to the war in Iran, suggesting the US was being humiliated by Iranian negotiators. While Trump accused Merz of supporting Iran's nuclear ambitions and claimed that Germany is "doing so poorly," Merz maintains a positive relationship with Trump. The US has a significant military presence in Germany, with more than 36,000 active duty troops assigned to bases across the country.

articles.title: Mexico’s cartel crackdown hits top ranks – but will it fuel Jalisco violence? | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mexican military forces captured Audias Flores, alias "El Jardinero", the suspected successor to El Mencho, leader of the Jalisco New Generation cartel (CJNG), in Nayarit. This operation follows a similar one that targeted El Mencho in February, and comes as Mexico prepares for the World Cup.  While experts believe these actions will change public perception of the Mexican state's efforts, they are unsure if they will significantly impact the CJNG's operations. The US has celebrated the arrest and is seeking to extradite El Jardinero to face charges in the United States.

articles.title: Last Beefeater and Brewers Fayre restaurants to close, with loss of 3,800 jobs, Premier Inn owner says | Hospitality industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Whitbread, owner of Premier Inn, is cutting 3,800 jobs in the UK and Ireland as part of a new business strategy. The company will shut its Beefeater and Brewers Fayre restaurants, converting them to hotel rooms. Whitbread cited tax increases and pressure from activist investor Corvex as reasons for the changes.  The company plans to lease its hotels instead of owning them, aiming to unlock more profitable growth opportunities.

articles.title: CM Murad asks K-Electric to find practical solution to reduce loadshedding - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah expressed concern over prolonged power outages in Karachi's underprivileged areas and directed K-Electric (KE) to find a solution. At a meeting with KE Chairman Shahryar Chishti, the CM requested a study on a targeted subsidy program for vulnerable consumers, aiming to provide affordable electricity to low-income neighborhoods and industrial areas.  The Sindh government is also exploring partnership with KE to develop a plan for supplying competitively priced electricity to industrial areas.

articles.title: UK researchers develop tool to identify people most at risk of obesity-related diseases | Obesity | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers at the University of Cambridge have developed a new tool called Obscore to identify individuals at risk for obesity-related diseases. The tool uses data from the UK Biobank and analyzes 20 health, lifestyle, and demographic factors to predict the 10-year risk of 18 different conditions, including gout, stroke, and type 2 diabetes.  The study suggests that Obscore could help prioritize individuals for weight-loss interventions by considering individual risk profiles beyond just BMI. However, experts caution that further development and validation are needed before it can be implemented in routine clinical practice.

articles.title: Cambridge A-level paper leak brings distress to bright students - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Following reports of an alleged A-level paper leak, the Inter-Board of Coordination Commission (IBCC) has requested a report from Cambridge to investigate.  The IBCC's Executive Director, Dr Ghulam Ali Mallah, stated that they will take "every possible step" for students after receiving the report. Parents and teachers expressed outrage over the alleged leak, with some questioning the integrity of the exam system. A Cambridge spokesperson confirmed their awareness of the reports and pledged to investigate thoroughly.

articles.title: Local election campaigning enters final week as forecaster warns Labour could lose 1,850 English seats –UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Local election campaigning enters its final week, with forecasts predicting a significant loss for Labour. Robert Hayward, an elections specialist, predicts Labour will lose 1,850 seats nationwide, while Reform and the Greens are expected to gain substantial ground.  The impact of these results on Sir Keir Starmer's leadership is considered significant.

articles.title: Independent press being stifled in Pakistan, says Hameed Haroon - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Hameed Haroon, former president of the All Pakistan Newspapers Society (APNS) and CEO of DawnMedia, discussed the challenges faced by the Pakistani media industry during a recent program. He highlighted the government's "anti-media attitude" as a major obstacle to independent journalism, citing advertisement bans, pressure on journalists, and attacks on the judiciary as examples.  Haroon emphasized the need for newspapers to adapt and innovate to attract younger audiences while advocating for improved job security and dignity for journalists.

articles.title: Ministers under pressure to tackle antisemitism after Golders Green attack – live updates | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government announced an additional £25 million to enhance security for Jewish communities following a series of attacks targeting them. The funding will support increased police patrols and security measures around synagogues, schools, and community centers.  Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood acknowledged the fears of the Jewish community after two men were stabbed in Golders Green, north-west London, and stated that she is taking "practical action" to ensure the safety of all citizens. The Metropolitan Police arrested a 45-year-old British national born in Somalia on suspicion of attempted murder.  The attack has been declared a terrorist incident by police. Several Muslim leaders condemned the attack, reaffirming their commitment to protecting the dignity and safety of all communities.

articles.title: US to refuse visa to applicants who fear returning home - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The United States State Department has instructed its diplomatic missions worldwide to deny visas to applicants who express fear of returning to their home country. The new directive requires consular officers to ask non-immigrant visa applicants two additional questions: whether they have experienced harm or mistreatment in their country of nationality or last habitual residence, and if they fear such harm upon return.  The policy is part of an effort by the administration to curb “asylum abuse” and prevent the use of temporary visas as a pathway to protection claims once inside the United States. The State Department maintains that the visa is a privilege, not a right, and individuals who do not intend to comply with immigration laws should not seek entry. Critics argue that the policy could have negative consequences for legitimate travelers and undermine international protection norms.

articles.title: Shock in India after man takes remains of his sister to bank to prove her death | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A man from India's Odisha state, Jitu Munda, brought the remains of his deceased sister to a bank after officials refused to release funds from her account without proof of death. Mundu claimed he had exhumed his sister’s body in frustration as bank staff repeatedly demanded a death certificate that was not yet issued. The incident sparked outrage and shock across India with many criticizing the bureaucratic process for marginalized communities.  The Indian Overseas Bank disputed Munda's account, stating they were following standard procedures after other heirs also claimed the woman's savings.

articles.title: PSX plunges over 3,000 points during intraday trade as bears maintain control - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) saw a significant decline on Thursday, with the KSE-100 index dropping over 3,000 points. The market fell to an intraday low of 160,391.18 points before recovering slightly.  Rising global oil prices, geopolitical tensions, and disappointing corporate earnings contributed to the bearish sentiment. Etisalat, a UAE-based telecom giant, is also reportedly reviewing its exposure in Pakistan's telecom sector.

articles.title: Oil prices soar on fears of long supply disruption, US siege of Iran ports | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged to their highest levels in weeks, driven by fears of prolonged supply disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and a US siege of Iranian ports. US President Donald Trump met with oil executives to discuss mitigating the impact on fuel supplies and maintaining the blockade. Brent crude futures reached $120 per barrel, impacting the Asia Pacific region heavily reliant on Middle Eastern oil imports. The UAE's withdrawal from OPEC is expected to have minimal immediate impact due to Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Syrian commission prepares war crimes case against notorious Assad official | Syria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Syrian rights commission is preparing a case against Fadi Saqr, a former militia leader within the Assad regime, accusing him of crimes against humanity and war crimes. The commission, appointed by the new Syrian government, is collaborating with victims to build a case against Saqr, who was previously in charge of the National Defence Forces (NDF) militia and widely accused of involvement in the mass killing and forcible disappearance of civilians in Tadamon.  The commission's work comes after Amjad Youssef, another perpetrator in the Tadamon massacres, was arrested last week. While Saqr denies responsibility for the killings, his alleged role in the atrocities has sparked outrage among residents who have long demanded accountability.

articles.title: 'Strait of Trump': US President Donald Trump shares new map naming Hormuz after himself | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump on Thursday shared a modified map renaming the Strait of Hormuz as the "Strait of Trump" after claiming that the naval blockade against Iran could continue for months. Trump, who has previously made similar remarks, indicated this action is part of his strategy to maintain pressure on Iran.  The US Treasury Department, through its Economic Fury initiative, continues to target Iranian financial infrastructure and oil exports, aiming to inflict long-term damage on the country's economy. Iran rejected these claims and criticized the blockade strategy, with Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf dismissing the advice as "junk".

articles.title: 2 armed suspects arrested in KP's Karak for 'attacking' police team - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district arrested two armed suspects after a patrol party came under fire during routine duty. The suspects, one injured, opened fire on the police party who returned fire, triggering a gun battle.  The DPO and other officials praised the officers for their bravery and actions against the suspects. This incident comes amid a surge in militant violence in Pakistan, with terrorist attacks rising by 34% and terrorism-related fatalities increasing by 21% year on year.

articles.title: Could the US-Iran war become a protracted ‘frozen’ conflict? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US-Iran war, despite a ceasefire since April 8th, remains in a state of "frozen conflict" with no permanent deal. US President Donald Trump and his advisors have discussed a new Iranian proposal for resolving the war, while White House spokesperson Anna Kelly stated that the US is engaging with Iran but will not rush into a bad deal. The economic costs of this stalemate are high for both sides, as evidenced by disruptions to global energy supplies and damage to US military assets.  Analysts warn that prolonged conflict could lead to a protracted one, potentially escalating tensions in the region and causing further instability. Iran is leveraging the Strait of Hormuz to pressure the US, while the US continues to impose a naval blockade on Iranian ports. The future of the war remains uncertain, with experts suggesting that both sides may resort to low-intensity conflict or drone warfare as a means of achieving their objectives.

articles.title: Oil price tops $126 a barrel after Trump warns Iran blockade could last ‘months’ | Global economy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump warned oil executives that the US blockade of Iranian ports could last for months, causing Brent crude futures to surge above $126 a barrel, its highest level since 2022.  The price increase is attributed to fears that diplomatic talks between the US and Iran will fail, leading to a prolonged supply crisis in the vital oil trade route. Economists warn of a potential global recession fueled by rising fuel costs, with some predicting a return to record-high prices if the strait remains closed for an extended period.

articles.title: Us Nuclear Violations: Iran at UN accuses US of nuclear double standards, misuse of NPT platform | India News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations accused the United States of misrepresenting its nuclear program and deflecting attention from Washington's own violations at the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty review conference. The mission stated that all of Iran's enriched uranium remains under IAEA supervision, with no reports of diversion.  Iran’s envoy Amir Saeed Irvani called for an end to aggression against Iran and respect for its sovereignty, urging the UN Security Council to address the situation. US official Christopher Yeaw criticized Iran's selection as a vice president at the conference, calling it an "affront" to the treaty.

articles.title: Israel says intercepted 175 Gaza flotilla activists on 20 boats - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s foreign ministry announced the arrest of approximately 175 activists aboard 20 ships attempting to break through an Israeli blockade in Gaza. The Global Sumud Flotilla, organizers of the flotilla, reported being surrounded by Israeli military boats and threatened with violence.  The flotilla, originating from France, Spain, and Italy, is currently off the coast of Greece.  Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has accused Israel of using water as a weapon against Palestinians in Gaza, claiming that the deliberate denial of water constitutes genocide.

articles.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 62 as Trump asks Iran to ‘give up’? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Scott Bessent have both claimed success in the US blockade of Iranian ports, while Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf has disputed its impact on oil prices.  The US says this will force Iran to halt production, but analysts believe it's a gradual process. Meanwhile, tensions are escalating in the Strait of Hormuz, driving up oil prices and causing economic strain across the globe. The conflict is also impacting global markets, with Vladimir Putin advising against further attacks on Iran.  The US has seized nearly $500 million in Iranian crypto assets under “Operation Economic Fury” to increase pressure.

articles.title: Trump threatens Germany with US troop reduction after Merz’s Iran war criticism – Europe live | World news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump threatened to reduce the number of US troops deployed in Germany, citing chancellor Friedrich Merz's criticism of the Iran war and its economic impact.  Trump stated that the US is "studying and reviewing" the troop reduction, with a decision expected soon. This follows Trump's phone call with Russia's Vladimir Putin, where he suggested Ukraine was "defeated" and that Putin was working on a temporary ceasefire. Merz has also criticized Trump's Iran war policies, claiming they are harming Germany's economy.  The US troop presence in Germany is currently the largest active duty deployment in Europe.

articles.title: Uae Petrol Prices May 2026: UAE announces petrol, diesel prices for May 2026 as fuel rates jump by up to 10% across Emirates | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UAE Fuel Price Committee announced another petrol price increase in May 2026, extending a months-long upward trend driven by global oil market instability. Super 98 will cost Dh3.66 per litre, up from Dh3.39, while Special 95 and E-Plus 91 also saw increases. This marks the third consecutive increase in fuel prices this year, following earlier hikes in March and April, due to volatile crude oil markets and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The price increases will impact daily commuting costs for residents and businesses alike.

articles.title: PMDC announces closure of admissions for academic session 2025–2026 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) has closed admissions for the 2025-2026 academic year, with no exceptions allowed after April 15th.  PMDC stated that any admissions granted beyond the deadline will be invalid and violate regulations. The council also urged institutions to comply with these regulations to maintain transparency in medical and dental education. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) has criticized the decision, arguing that vacant seats are due to high fees, not a lack of qualified candidates.

articles.title: Rockets defeat Lakers in Reaves’s return, force Game 6 in NBA playoffs | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Houston Rockets defeated the Los Angeles Lakers in Game 5 of their NBA playoff series, forcing a decisive Game 6. Despite star Austin Reaves' return from injury, the Lakers were unable to overcome the Rockets' strong performance, with Jabari Smith Jr. leading the way with 22 points. The Rockets now trail 3-2 in the best-of-seven series.  The Rockets will look to clinch their first playoff victory since 2019 when they host Game 6 on Friday.

articles.title: Trump administration urges countries to help citizens stuck in Syria as Australia maintains hardline stance | Australian foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is urging countries to repatriate citizens stranded in Syria, including Australians who have been detained at the al-Roj camp. The Albanese government maintains its hardline stance against returning Australian women and children detained since the fall of Islamic State.  A group of four women, their nine children, and grandchildren left the camp last Friday but were turned back by Syrian authorities before reaching Damascus airport due to the Australian government's refusal to receive them. The Albanese government has previously refused to repatriate any more citizens from Syria.

articles.title: Golders Green Attack: London stabbing declared ‘terrorist incident’; UK announces £25m security boost for Jewish community - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Metropolitan Police have arrested a 45-year-old man in connection with a stabbing attack on two Jewish men in Golders Green, London, that has been classified as a "terrorist incident." The suspect, who is British and born in Somalia, was detained on suspicion of attempted murder after being discharged from hospital.  Prime Minister Keir Starmer, London Mayor Sadiq Khan, and Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis condemned the attack as antisemitic and called for increased security measures.  The incident follows a series of antisemitic incidents in the area, prompting concerns about national security and the rise in hate crimes across the UK since the Israel-Hamas war began.

articles.title: Lawyer seeks Imran's release on humanitarian grounds as IHC hears appeals in £190m graft reference - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Imran Khan's defense counsel, Salman Safdar, requested the Islamabad High Court to consider releasing his client on humanitarian grounds due to prolonged solitary confinement and an eye infection.  Safdar argued that the case had been pending for over 16 months and that suspension of sentence could be decided without a final decision on the appeal. The Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar emphasized the need for an early disposal of the main appeal, assuring the defense that the court would decide it promptly.  The hearing also addressed issues related to power of attorney and medical reports, with Rafay Maqsood, Senior Prosecutor for the National Accountability Bureau, arguing against entertaining a separate plea for sentence suspension.

articles.title: Zaragoza goalkeeper given 13-game ban after derby punch provoked brawl | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Esteban Andrada, goalkeeper for Real Zaragoza, was banned from playing for 13 games by the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) after punching Huesca captain Jorge Pulido in the face during a La Liga 2 derby match.  Andrada received a second yellow card and was subsequently ejected, leading to a brawl between players and staff members from both teams. Dani Tasende, Andrada's teammate, received a two-game suspension for his role in the brawl. The suspensions can be appealed.

articles.title: ‘We’re coming for you’: NT police search for suspect after body of missing five-year-old found | Northern Territory | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NT police are searching for a 47-year-old man, Jefferson Lewis, who is suspected of murdering a five-year-old girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby. The body was found near Old Timers town camp on Thursday, prompting an arrest order for Lewis.  The investigation is ongoing and a postmortem examination will be conducted to determine the cause of death. Tangentyere Council Aboriginal Corporation coordinated community support during the five-day search effort.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia: Saudi Arabia executes Iraqi nationals convicted in northern border drug smuggling case | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia executed multiple Iraqi nationals convicted of drug trafficking after they were arrested and found guilty by specialized courts. The executions, carried out according to Saudi law, come amid a wider anti-drug campaign in the kingdom, which has seen an increase in arrests, seizures, and executions related to narcotics smuggling. Human rights organizations criticize the use of capital punishment for drug offenses, arguing that it violates international law and raises concerns about due process.

articles.title: Lahore Bar Association moves SC against 27th Amendment following transfer of IHC judges - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore Bar Association (LBA) has filed a petition in the Supreme Court challenging the constitutionality of the 27th Constitutional Amendment, which authorized the transfer of three Islamabad High Court judges to other courts. The petition argues that the amendment is unconstitutional as it removes Article 184(3), which grants the Supreme Court original jurisdiction to enforce the Constitution and fundamental rights. It also contends that the amendment undermines the independence of the judiciary and violates the basic features of the Constitution by allowing the parliament to amend judicial powers without proper mandate. The petition further claims that the transfers were arbitrary, lacking justification, and potentially aimed at silencing judges who have raised concerns about interference in judicial affairs.

articles.title: Myanmar’s blanket prison term reduction trims Aung San Suu Kyi’s sentence | Aung San Suu Kyi News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing has granted a blanket prison sentence reduction, reducing the remaining term of deposed leader Aung San Suu Kyi to approximately 18 years. This follows a similar amnesty for 4,335 prisoners earlier this month.  Aung San Suu Kyi's legal team confirmed the reduction, although her exact sentence remains unclear. The Myanmar government has been criticized by human rights groups for its handling of political prisoners and restrictions on voting rights since the 2021 coup.

articles.title: At least six Australian activists detained by Israel navy after Gaza flotilla boats intercepted | Gaza flotilla | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alexa Stewart, spokesperson for the Global Sumud flotilla, confirmed that at least six Australians were among those detained by Israel Defense Forces (IDF) personnel after their boats were intercepted in international waters. The Australian government has stated it is seeking an update from Israeli authorities and is ready to provide consular assistance, but acknowledges its limited ability to assist due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.  Sarah Schofield, partner of Newcastle climate activist Zack Schofield, expressed fear for his safety after receiving a video showing him being abducted by IDF personnel.

articles.title: Markets overlooking macro stress, says Kunal Vora amid oil and currency shock - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: BNP Paribas's Kunal Vora expressed concern over market complacency, noting that earnings growth expectations may be inflated and could decline as crude oil prices remain elevated. He highlighted the potential for second-order effects like fuel price transmission and fiscal constraints to impact sectors such as infrastructure.  Vora believes certain sectors like consumer staples, telecoms, IT services, and pharma will fare better than commodity-consuming sectors in this environment. While acknowledging near-term risks to consumption due to rising input costs and rural demand uncertainty, he maintains structural resilience remains intact. Vora suggests a more tempered earnings outlook for FY27 as market optimism fades, with expectations already being revised lower across sectors.

articles.title: Nine arrested in UK raids on Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light in Crewe over ‘modern slavery’ and rape allegations | World News - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light
articles.rephrased_article: Cheshire Police conducted a major operation in Crewe, arresting nine people linked to the religious group Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light (Arpol).  The arrests followed allegations of rape, sexual assault, forced marriage, and modern slavery dating back to 2023. The investigation focuses on individuals within the group, with suspects facing charges including human trafficking, rape, sexual assault, and forced marriage. Europol and officers from Ireland and Sweden supported the operation.

articles.title: Commissioning ceremony of Pakistan Navy’s first Hangor-class attack submarine held in China - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari and Admiral Naveed Ashraf, Chief of the Naval Staff, attended the commissioning ceremony of the first Hangor-class attack submarine in China's Sanya city.  The submarine, named after the historical PNS Hangor, is equipped with air-independent propulsion technology and will bolster Pakistan's maritime defense capabilities. The naval chief highlighted that these submarines are crucial for maintaining a stable maritime order and deterring aggression. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Defence Forces and Army Staff respectively, congratulated the nation on this historic milestone.  The ceremony marked another chapter in the strong relationship between Pakistan and China.

articles.title: Pakistan opens up road trade routes into Iran amid Hormuz blockade | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has opened six overland transit routes for goods destined for Iran, formalizing a road corridor to move stranded containers.  The move comes amid US-imposed sanctions on Iranian ports and ships, disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative aims to alleviate trade disruptions and enhance Pakistan's role as a key trade corridor. While Iran has not commented publicly, the announcement coincides with diplomatic efforts by Pakistan to mediate an end to the ongoing war between US and Iran.  The new routes could significantly reduce transport costs and time for goods moving from Pakistan to Iran, potentially impacting regional trade dynamics.

articles.title: Jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Jimmy Lai wins free speech award in Germany | Jimmy Lai | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jimmy Lai, a British citizen and former media entrepreneur, has been awarded the Deutsche Welle's freedom of speech award for his contributions to Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement.  The award will be presented in absentia on June 23rd at the DW Global Media Forum in Bonn. Barbara Massing, director general of Deutsche Welle, praised Lai for standing "unwaveringly" for press freedom and giving journalists a platform for free reporting. Lai, who was imprisoned in 2020 after being convicted under Hong Kong's national security law, is considered one of Hong Kong's most prominent pro-democracy advocates.

articles.title: No new contract awarded to build Karachi's Red Line corridor, Sindh High Court told - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh High Court heard a case regarding the stalled Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line project, specifically Lot 2 of the Mosamiyat-Numaish corridor. Advocate General Jawad Dero stated that the contract for this project will be awarded after the completion of the notice period for the previous contractor. The petitioner's counsel, Barrister Salahuddin Ahmed, claimed that the project was handed over to the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) and that the inventory of machinery at the site is not complete. The court expressed dissatisfaction with the delay in construction and suggested a commission be formed to investigate the reasons for it.

articles.title: New Zealand court denies bid by mosque mass shooter to appeal conviction | Islamophobia News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Brenton Tarrant, an Australian white supremacist, has lost his appeal to overturn his conviction and sentence for the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings. The New Zealand Court of Appeal ruled that his attempt was "utterly devoid of merit" and found his guilty pleas were voluntary.  The court also rejected Tarrant's claims about his mental state during the trial, stating there were inconsistencies in his own evidence and it contradicted observations from prison authorities and mental health professionals. The decision brings relief to survivors and families who had been anticipating a new trial.

articles.title: What the royals did in New York on their third day in the US
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles and Queen Camilla concluded their third day of a state visit to the United States in New York City. The royal couple began the day with a visit to the 9/11 Memorial, followed by separate activities.  Queen Camilla read "Winnie the Pooh" to children at the New York Public Library, while King Charles visited a community organization in Harlem and fed chickens. They concluded their visit by celebrating 50 years of the King's Trust charity at Rockefeller Center, where global ambassador Lionel Richie spoke.

articles.title: ‘Nightmare’ queues and missed flights: readers report turbulent start to EU entry-exit system | Airline industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Travellers across Europe have reported significant delays and disruptions at border checkpoints since the introduction of the new EU entry-exit system (EES) on Friday.  Dave Giles, an IT manager from Northamptonshire, missed his flight home after a three-hour wait at Copenhagen airport due to long queues. Georgia, a London resident, experienced a four-hour delay at Pisa airport while travelling with her pregnant self.  Other travellers reported issues with malfunctioning kiosks, lack of guidance on using the system, and insufficient staff to assist passengers. Stuart MacLennan from Oban in Scotland found travelling with children particularly difficult, encountering lengthy queues at both arrival and departure points. The new system has also been criticized for its inconsistent implementation and lack of clarity for travellers.

articles.title: Rate cuts unlikely in near term as inflation stays sticky: Richard Harris - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell, Janet Yellen, and other officials have dismissed concerns about a shift in policy, emphasizing the Federal Reserve's independence.  Harris believes that while recent profitability in Big Tech is driven by cloud usage rather than AI, the industry will likely consolidate. He also cautioned against optimistic expectations of rate cuts due to political sensitivity and the potential for inflation to remain elevated. The Federal Reserve may remain cautious in the near term, focusing on data-dependent decisions.

articles.title: Mamdani calls on King Charles to return Koh-i-Noor diamond - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York City called for the return of the Koh-i-Noor diamond, a prized possession currently housed in the Tower of London, to India during King Charles III's state visit.  Mamdani stated his desire to encourage the king to return the diamond, but it is unclear if he raised the issue during their brief meeting. The jewel has been contested for ownership over centuries and remains a point of contention between India and other countries with historical claims.

articles.title: Europe’s little-known mutual defence clause: Is it a NATO substitute? | NATO News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Several European leaders are calling for clarification on the rarely used mutual defense clause in the European Union treaty, Article 42.7, amid growing tensions with the United States over NATO.  President Emmanuel Macron of France and Cyprus President Nikos Christodoulides have emphasized the need to define how the clause would work if triggered. The EU is drawing up a "handbook" for its use. While Article 42.7 has only been invoked once before, in response to the 2015 Paris attacks, European leaders are increasingly concerned about the future of transatlantic relations and the US's commitment to NATO.  Some experts believe that Europe may need to develop a more robust defense strategy independent of the US.

articles.title: Police say they believe abducted 5-year-old girl was murdered as body found
articles.rephrased_article: Police believe they have found the body of a five-year-old girl, Kumanjayi Little Baby, allegedly abducted from her Outback home. The body was discovered on Thursday and forensic testing is underway to confirm her identity and cause of death. Jefferson Lewis, a 47-year-old man who was released from prison six days before the disappearance, has been identified as a suspect and is believed to have murdered the child.  Northern Territory Police are searching for Lewis and have appealed for anyone with information to contact authorities. The search effort involved hundreds of volunteers and police officers.

articles.title: Archibald prize 2026: Jacob Collins portrait wins the Packing Room prize as finalists revealed | Archibald prize 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Art Gallery of NSW staff awarded the Packing Room prize to painter Sean Layh for his portrait of actor Jacob Collins, titled "The tragicall historie of Hamlet, Prince of Denmarke."  Layh, a self-taught artist who previously worked in biological science, was inspired by Collins's performance as Hamlet and has been painting full-time for five years. The $3,000 Packing Room prize is awarded to the staff's favorite portrait from the Archibald prize exhibition which this year received over 1,000 entries.

articles.title: Egyptian Amulet: 3,000-year-old Egyptian amulet found in Spanish tomb shocks archaeologists | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists have unearthed an ancient Egyptian amulet in a Spanish grave, suggesting contact between the ancient Egyptians and Spaniards existed earlier than previously known. The amulet, believed to be sacred in some religions, is intricately designed and made of materials similar to those used in Egyptian amulets, indicating potential trade routes or cultural exchange between the two civilizations. This discovery supports existing theories about ancient trade networks and interactions that shaped early human societies. Further studies will focus on the amulet's origin and its significance within the deceased's culture.

articles.title: Bajaj Finance shares jump 4% after strong Q4 results. Why Jefferies, Morgan Stanley and others are bullish - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bajaj Finance's assets under management (AUM) reached Rs 5.09 lakh crore at the end of March 2026, a 22% increase from the previous year. The company saw strong business momentum with loan growth and steady customer additions. Analysts like Jefferies, Morgan Stanley, and JM Financial maintain positive ratings on the company, citing its strong franchise scale, AUM growth, and robust financial position.

articles.title: New Zealand’s Christchurch mosque killer loses bid to overturn convictions - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Brenton Tarrant, a white supremacist convicted of the 2019 Christchurch mosque shootings, lost his appeal to overturn his life sentence. The Court of Appeal found Tarrant's claims of mental incapacity during his guilty pleas were unsubstantiated and rejected his argument that prison conditions influenced his decision.  The court emphasized that Tarrant's pleas were voluntary and there was no evidence of coercion. This decision brings relief to the families and survivors who had been through a difficult legal process, as they will not face another trial for the tragic events.

articles.title: Why is India turning to crocodiles and snakes to ‘fence’ Bangladesh border? | Wildlife News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Border Security Force (BSF) is exploring the use of apex predators like crocodiles and venomous snakes to deter undocumented migration along its border with Bangladesh.  This controversial plan, aimed at addressing challenging terrain that makes traditional fencing difficult, has raised concerns from human rights activists and wildlife conservationists. The BSF's directive to explore this option comes despite the fact that these animals are not native to the region and could pose a threat to local ecosystems and communities. Critics argue that deploying such measures is inhumane and ineffective, highlighting the government's use of fear tactics against undocumented migrants. This approach has been compared to similar controversial strategies employed in the United States, including proposals for using alligators or snakes to deter migrants.

articles.title: New Zealand: Christchurch gunman loses bid to overturn conviction
articles.rephrased_article: Brenton Tarrant, a white supremacist who killed 51 people at two New Zealand mosques in March 2019, lost his bid to overturn his convictions and sentence. The New Zealand Court of Appeal rejected his arguments, finding them "utterly devoid of merit" and concluding that he was not coerced or pressured into pleading guilty.  The massacre led to stricter gun laws in New Zealand, including a ban on military-style semi-automatic weapons. Aya al-Umari, whose brother Hussein was killed in the attack, expressed relief with the court's decision.

articles.title: Massive profits already earned by property investors to be shielded from Chalmers’ CGT changes | Jim Chalmers | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jim Chalmers, the Treasurer, stated that any changes to investor tax settings would recognize past decisions, potentially modifying the 50% capital gains tax discount on assets held for over a year.  He suggested applying new rules only to future investments through "grandfathering."  Luke Yeaman, chief economist at CommBank, argued that a partial or staged grandfathering approach could generate revenue more quickly but add complexity. The Grattan Institute estimates that halving the capital gains tax discount and phasing it in over five years would generate $6.5 billion annually, while returning to the pre-1999 regime and scrapping negative gearing would yield just $2 billion in the first four years.  However, revenue gains are estimated to grow over time. Chalmers also indicated that scaling back tax breaks for landlords could rebalance home ownership away from investors towards owner-occupiers.

articles.title: Ishowspeed: IShowSpeed health status: Social media icon collapsed on livestream after 12 hours of intense streaming on Caribbean tour - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed, a popular YouTuber and livestreamer, fainted during a live stream in St. Maarten while on tour promoting tourism across the Caribbean. The 21-year-old appeared extremely tired before collapsing, prompting concern among viewers who watched the incident unfold. IShowSpeed later confirmed he was okay and apologized for worrying his audience, assuring them he had recovered after briefly feeling weak. He continued his journey and expressed plans to stream from unique locations in the future.

articles.title: Waaree Energies shares crash 9% despite 75% increase in Q4 net profit, upbeat FY27 guidance - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Waaree Energies reported a significant increase in revenue and profit for the fiscal year 2026. The company's fourth quarter revenue reached Rs 8,840.25 crore, marking a 111.8% year-on-year rise.  Operating EBITDA also surged to Rs 1,576.76 crore, exceeding the company’s guidance range and contributing to a total revenue of Rs 26,536.77 crore for the fiscal year. The company plans to continue expanding into new growth areas like battery energy storage systems and electrolyzers for green hydrogen while investing in upstream capabilities through a new glass manufacturing facility and an integrated ingot and wafer facility.

articles.title: PSX plunges over 4,700 points as bears maintain control - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) experienced a significant decline on Thursday, with the KSE-100 index dropping over 4,786 points, or 2.89 percent.  This marks the third consecutive day of selling pressure driven by investor concerns about the economic outlook and disappointing corporate earnings. Rising global oil prices amid geopolitical tensions have also contributed to market volatility. The UAE-based telecom giant Etisalat is reportedly reviewing its exposure in Pakistan's telecom sector, adding to the bearish sentiment.

articles.title: Iranian officials to miss FIFA Congress over alleged mistreatment in Canada | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian football federation officials, including President Mehdi Taj, Secretary-General Hedayat Mombeni, and Deputy Secretary-General Hamed Momeni, were prevented from attending the FIFA Congress in Vancouver due to alleged mistreatment by Canadian immigration officials upon arrival at Toronto's Pearson airport.  The delegation returned to Turkey after holding valid visas, citing "unacceptable behaviour" from immigration personnel. The incident highlights the political obstacles surrounding Iran's participation in the World Cup and raises concerns about Iranian players, officials, and supporters' ability to travel freely during the tournament. FIFA has contacted the Iranian delegation expressing regret for the incident and plans to meet with them at its headquarters.

articles.title: Oil jumps to highest price since 2022 after report Trump to be briefed on new Iran options
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged to their highest level since 2022, exceeding $126 a barrel after US Central Command prepared plans for potential military action against Iran. The proposed strikes aim to break the deadlock in negotiations and could include infrastructure targets.  The White House and US Central Command have not yet commented on the reports. Energy prices have risen this week due to stalled peace talks, with the Strait of Hormuz remaining closed.

articles.title: ‘Outrageous’: Rebel Wilson denies she was behind Snapchat leak of actor’s nude photo, court hears | Sydney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rebel Wilson is facing a defamation lawsuit from Charlotte MacInnes, the lead actor in her film "The Deb".  MacInnes claims Wilson defamed her on social media, alleging she lied about a sexual harassment complaint. Wilson denies these accusations and alleges MacInnes orchestrated a cyber attack on her social media accounts. The trial continues.

articles.title: BBC visits US and UK military base in Iraq as ceasefire continues
articles.rephrased_article: The BBC has gained access to a US-UK military base in Iraq where US and UK forces have been working together.  Despite the ongoing tensions between the US and Britain over the war with Iran, Armed Forces Minister Al Carns highlighted the strong co-operation between the two militaries, emphasizing their shared commitment to protecting each other's personnel. Air Chief Marshal Sir Harvey Smyth also confirmed that the relationship remains strong despite strained diplomatic relations.

articles.title: Bondi royal commission: report calls for better policing of Jewish festivals after ‘high’ terror risk flagged for Hanukah event | Royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The interim report of the royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion found that NSW police did not complete a comprehensive risk assessment for the Chanukah by the Sea festival. The report also recommended that the federal government's counter-terrorism coordinator be made a full-time position, as well as increased coordination of policing at Jewish festivals and events.  The commission noted an increase in antisemitic incidents and contact between NSW police and the Community Security Group NSW since 2022. The report also questioned whether efforts to establish a national firearms registry were "unduly leisurely" after the Wieambilla shootings.

articles.title: FPI exodus in four months of 2026 surpasses all of last year - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have continued selling Indian equities in the first half of 2026, driven by factors like a weak rupee and deceleration in earnings momentum.  The selling intensified after the West Asia conflict began in February, leading to India being surpassed by South Korea as the most sold market in Asia. Franklin Templeton, IIFL Capital Services, and Bloomberg data show that FPIs pulled out approximately $12 billion from Indian stocks in March alone.

articles.title: Canada’s Diavik mine makes stunning 158-carat diamond discovery just before shutdown | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 158.20-carat yellow diamond was discovered at the Diavik Diamond Mine in Canada, marking the conclusion of its 20-year operation.  The Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) noted that this exceptional find is a testament to the mine's success and highlights the rare geological conditions of the kimberlite pipes beneath Lac de Gras. The Government of the Northwest Territories reported that Diavik, a joint venture, was one of North America's most productive mining operations, producing over 150 million carats of diamonds since its first production in 2003.

articles.title: Piprahwa relics of Buddha arrive in Leh, people gather in huge numbers to pay respect - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On Wednesday, April 29, 2026, the sacred Piprahwa relics of the Buddha arrived in Leh, Ladakh, for a public exposition. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena accorded a ceremonial welcome to the relics at the Technical Area of Leh airport after they were flown in from New Delhi. The relics, linked to Gautama Buddha and discovered at Piprahwa, Uttar Pradesh, have gained renewed global significance after repatriation from a British family and private collection. Khamtak Rinpoche, Rigyal Rinpoche, and other religious figures were present at the reception ceremony.  The relics will be on display at Jivetsal in Leh from May 1 to May 10 before being taken to Zanskar and then back to Delhi.

articles.title: No new contract awarded to build Red Line corridor, Sindh High Court told - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Sindh High Court heard a case regarding the stalled Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line project. The Advocate General of Sindh, Jawad Dero, stated that the contract for the Mosamiyat-Numaish corridor (Lot 2) would be awarded after the completion of the notice period for the previous contractor.  The petitioner's counsel, Barrister Salahuddin Ahmed, claimed the project was handed over to the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) and that the inventory of equipment at the site was not complete. The court expressed frustration with the delay in construction and suggested a commission be formed to investigate the reasons behind it. The hearing has been adjourned until May 4th.

articles.title: US charges Mexican governor and other leaders with aiding drug cartel
articles.rephrased_article: US prosecutors have indicted Rúben Rocha Moya, the governor of the Mexican state of Sinaloa, and nine other current and former Mexican government officials for conspiring with the Sinaloa Cartel to import narcotics into the United States. The indictment alleges that these leaders received political support and bribes in exchange for protecting the cartel's operations.  The Mexican government has disputed the evidence presented by the US, stating that the documents lack sufficient proof.  The Attorney General's office will ultimately decide whether to extradite the officials.

articles.title: Student’s alleged jailing in China over Australian pro-democracy protests sparks calls for inquiry | Australian universities | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Lorraine Finlay, the Australian human rights commissioner, expressed concern about the case of a Chinese student allegedly jailed in China for protesting in Sydney.  Finlay called on the government to launch a parliamentary inquiry into transnational repression and urged universities to offer more support to students at risk. John, a Chinese international student, stated that he felt more concerned about his safety after hearing about the arrest. Emma, another student, emphasized the need for the Australian government to provide more support for those who speak out against authoritarian regimes in China.  Grace Street, president of the University of Sydney's student representative council, criticized the university and the government for failing to protect students' rights.

articles.title: Vedanta earns record profit in Q4, plans to reduce debt - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Vedanta's consolidated profit reached ₹9,352 crore in the March quarter, a record high, fueled by 89% year-on-year revenue growth to ₹51,524 crore. The company also saw significant improvements in earnings before interest tax, depreciation and amortisation, reaching ₹18,447 crore. Vedanta reduced its debt by nearly $1.5 billion during the fiscal year 2026, bringing it down to ₹53,254 crore.  The company plans to allocate ₹23,000 for capital expenditure this year and announced a dividend of ₹34 per share. Vedanta is also preparing for its demerger into four new companies with the effective date set for May 1st.

articles.title: "Make your life miserable": Candace Owens hits back at Donald Trump over “vile” remark during livestream - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Candace Owens engaged in a public back-and-forth after Trump criticized Owens on his Truth Social platform.  Owens, responding with humor and sarcasm, questioned the intent behind the attack and suggested it was part of a larger pattern of political pressure and hidden motives. The exchange highlights how quickly political differences can escalate into public spectacles.

articles.title: Delhi HC orders action after obscene content disrupts virtual hearing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia of the Delhi High Court were presiding over routine court proceedings when an unidentified participant disrupted the video conferencing platform three times, playing obscene content.  The incident prompted the court to halt proceedings twice and led Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma to request action against the circulation of recordings. Chief Justice Upadhyaya stated that appropriate directions have been issued to address the matter administratively.

articles.title: Emirati telecom giant ‘mulling exit’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A leading Middle Eastern telecom group, Etisalat, is reportedly conducting a portfolio review that could potentially lead to its exit from the Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL). The review, driven by global macroeconomic uncertainty and evolving capital allocation strategies among sovereign-linked investors, is not specific to Pakistan.  Etisalat has indicated it's at a preliminary assessment stage, with no final decision made yet. Pakistan remains strategically important despite the mixed ownership of PTCL, which currently faces continuous losses. The review aligns with global investment management practices and diplomatic channels confirm that economic cooperation between Pakistan and UAE remains intact.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump urges Tehran to ‘give up’; Ghalibaf mocks US strategy | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump asserted that the US blockade of Iranian ports has been a success, urging Tehran to "give up".  Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's Parliament Speaker, dismissed the US economic pressure campaign and stated that the Iranian military's restraint was intended to allow diplomacy to proceed. The standoff in the Strait of Hormuz continues as oil prices surge.

articles.title: Kenya's Sabastian Sawe welcomed home in chaotic celebrations
articles.rephrased_article: Sebastian Sawe, the Kenyan runner who became the first man to run a marathon in under two hours, was welcomed home with jubilant celebrations upon his arrival at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi.  His parents drove six hours from their home to greet him, and the Kenyan Airways plane he flew on received a water cannon salute upon landing. President William Ruto is expected to meet Sawe. The 31-year-old's time of 01:59:30 was more than one minute faster than the previous record set by Kelvin Kiptum.  Sawe plans to compete again in the autumn, aiming for an even faster time.

articles.title: Christchurch gunman fails in bid to appeal against guilty pleas in New Zealand court | Christchurch shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Brenton Tarrant, the Australian white supremacist responsible for the Christchurch mosque shootings in 2019, has been denied his appeal against his guilty pleas. The New Zealand Court of Appeal found that Tarrant's claims about mental health distress and prison conditions were unsubstantiated and his appeal was "utterly devoid of merit."  Tarrant pleaded guilty to 51 counts of murder, 40 counts of attempted murder, and terrorism charges in 2020 after initially intending to defend the charges. He was sentenced to life imprisonment without parole in August 2020.

articles.title: Can OnEMI Technology IPO offer value for long-term investors? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: OnEMI, a digital lending company established in 2016, experienced significant growth in its assets under management (AUM) and net profit. The company reported an AUM of ₹59,557 crore as of December 2025, with personal loans and LAP accounting for a substantial portion of the total.  OnEMI's customer base has grown to over 28.7 lakh active customers, with an average age of 32 years and a median CIBIL score of 746. The company had previously planned to raise ₹1,000 crore through an IPO but reduced the size due to strong internal accruals.  OnEMI's valuation is currently at a P/B multiple of 1.4 on a post-IPO basis.

articles.title: India needs to look at its national interests with regard to the Gulf of Hormuz - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The second round of talks between Iran and the US have failed, leaving both countries locked in a stalemate. While a ceasefire remains in place, Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz while the US has established a naval blockade.  Both sides are engaging in escalating rhetoric on social media, complicating negotiations. The situation is further complicated by Iran's demands for sanctions relief and a non-aggression pact, as well as the US's focus on Iran's nuclear ambitions, missile program, and regional proxies. India, with its geographical proximity to the Gulf region and economic interests tied to energy trade, faces significant consequences from the conflict.  The world is facing three interconnected conflicts, but none are fought alike. The situation demands a peaceful resolution that prioritizes global stability and economic well-being.

articles.title: Assembly election 2026 LIVE: Exit polls predict close contest in West Bengal, DMK+ lead in Tamil Nadu, - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Exit polls on Wednesday, April 29, 2026, indicated a clear majority for the BJP in Assam and an edge over the ruling TMC in West Bengal.  The polls also projected a return of the DMK government in Tamil Nadu and a comeback by the Congress-led UDF in Kerala after 10 years. All forecasts predicted a return to power for the AINRC-led NDA government in Puducherry. The counting of votes for all five assemblies will take place on May 4th.

articles.title: US turns down Iranian proposal to end war - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to end the conflict, stating that the naval blockade would remain until Tehran agreed to a nuclear deal. Trump also announced plans for the aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford to depart the Middle East after a 10-month deployment. Iran’s Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad said Iran's fuel supply remained stable despite the US blockade, while Iran’s parliament speaker Bagher Ghalibaf called for unity against the US blockade.  Oil prices rose as peace talks between the United States and Iran stalled.

articles.title: US charges Sinaloa state governor, 9 others over Mexican drug cartel links | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US prosecutors have indicted Ruben Rocha Moya, the governor of Sinaloa state, and nine other current or former Mexican officials for alleged links to the Sinaloa drug cartel. The indictment alleges that these individuals worked with cartel leaders to move narcotics into the US in exchange for political support and bribes.  The case could strain relations between the two countries as Rocha Moya has denied the charges, calling them baseless. The Mexican government maintains that the US documents lack sufficient evidence. This rare move signals a potential shift in US strategy towards tackling drug cartels by targeting high-ranking officials.

articles.title: Bondi Beach shooting: Royal commission interim report says gun reform should be prioritised
articles.rephrased_article: A landmark royal commission into antisemitism, prompted by the Bondi Beach shooting, has recommended prioritizing gun reforms and extending police security measures to other Jewish festivals. The commission's interim report, led by former High Court judge Virginia Bell, also suggests a review of joint counter-terrorism teams and a full-time counter-terrorism commissioner. While Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated that the government will implement all recommendations, some states have resisted gun buyback schemes.  The inquiry is expected to deliver its final report on the anniversary of the shooting.

articles.title: US charges Sinaloa governor and other Mexican officials with drug trafficking offences | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US justice department has charged Governor Rubén Rocha Moya of Sinaloa and nine other officials with aiding the Sinaloa cartel in narcotics trafficking into the United States. The indictment alleges that these individuals, including former government officials, received protection from the cartel in exchange for their support.  President Claudia Sheinbaum faces political pressure as she attempts to address mounting concerns from the Trump administration.

articles.title: Heavy rain leaves a trail of widespread damage in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru experienced heavy rain, thunderstorms, and hailstorms on Wednesday evening, causing widespread damage.  The sudden downpour left many arterial roads flooded, with some areas experiencing knee-deep water that led to traffic disruptions and vehicle breakdowns. Residents reported treacherous driving conditions as trees fell onto vehicles.

articles.title: Kadambrayar pollution: local bodies told to step up enforcement - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Local Self-Government department (LSGD) has urged local bodies along the Kadambrayar river in Ernakulam to enforce penalties against those polluting the waterbody. The LSGD issued this directive as part of ongoing efforts to curb illegal wastewater discharge from residential and commercial units, directing local bodies to impose fines and initiate legal proceedings against violators.  The LSGD also requested local bodies to form squads for continuous monitoring against garbage dumping into the river and strengthen squad activities according to Section 219S of the Kerala Panchayat Raj (Amendment) Act, 2024.

articles.title: RBI: India’s central bank steps up fight against digital fraud
articles.rephrased_article: India's central bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), is responding to a surge in digital fraud, which has resulted in losses exceeding $25 billion in 2025. The RBI is considering several measures, including a one-hour lag on account-to-account transactions and additional authentication for high-value payments, but experts question the effectiveness of these proposals due to the sophistication of modern scams.  The RBI acknowledges that implementing such changes would be challenging and could potentially lead to scammers finding new ways to circumvent them. The central bank is also emphasizing the need for increased digital literacy and collaboration with other agencies to address this growing problem effectively.

articles.title: Maryland becomes first state to ban surveillance pricing in grocery stores | Technology | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Maryland Governor Wes Moore signed a law banning surveillance pricing in grocery stores, making the state the first in the US to do so. The law prohibits grocers and third-party delivery services from using personal data like location, internet history, and demographics to set higher prices for consumers. While consumer groups welcome the move, they express concerns about loopholes within the legislation that could allow similar practices to continue.  The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has also investigated these pricing practices, but it's unclear if the current administration will take action against them.

articles.title: From turnout to transfers, Bengal elections marked by many firsts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The West Bengal Assembly elections, the second and final phase of which concluded on April 29, 2026, saw record voter turnout (91.47%) and a high security deployment exceeding 2.3 lakh Central Armed Police Force personnel.  Union Home Minister Amit Shah stated that the Central forces would remain in West Bengal for 60 days to curb post-election violence. The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, which resulted in the removal of dead, shifted, and duplicate entries, led to a significant decrease in voter list size. The Election Commission (ECI) faced challenges with "logical discrepancies" and disputes over voter eligibility, leading to an extended adjudication process.  Despite these complexities, the elections marked a historical moment for West Bengal.

articles.title: A son overlooked and a jailed tycoon: Inside Samsung's succession drama
articles.rephrased_article: The succession drama at Samsung, one of the world's largest conglomerates, has been a long-standing issue.  Lee Jae-yong, grandson of Samsung's founder and current chairman, was jailed for his role in a corruption scandal that led to the downfall of South Korea's president. Despite being groomed for leadership since childhood, Lee Jae-yong faced criticism for not being aggressive enough and questions about his ability to lead the company.  His father, who suffered a heart attack in 2015, was also accused of bribery and tax evasion but was later cleared. The family has been embroiled in disputes over succession, with Lee Jae-yong's uncle launching legal challenges that threatened to disrupt the planned transfer of power. After years of legal battles and imprisonment, Lee Jae-yong was finally acquitted in 2025, marking a potential shift in the dynasty's leadership structure.

articles.title: New Orleans sheriff indicted on 30 counts just days before term ends | New Orleans | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sheriff Susan Hutson and her chief financial officer, Bianka Brown, were indicted on 30 counts of malfeasance and payroll fraud by Louisiana state attorney general Liz Murrill.
