The indictment stems from a massive jailbreak in May 2025 that occurred under Hutson's watch.  The charges against the pair include conspiracy, obstruction of justice, and filing false public records. Hutson was set to leave office after her term was marred by controversy, including staffing scandals and allegations of overspending. The indictment comes just days before she is set to be replaced by former interim New Orleans police department superintendent Michelle Woodfork.

articles.title: NMC does away with ceiling on MBBS intake - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has revised its regulations for undergraduate medical education, removing restrictions on the number of MBBS seats a college can offer and the maximum distance between a college and its affiliated hospital. The changes allow colleges to increase their intake without limitations and adjust distances based on location. These modifications aim to provide greater flexibility in establishing new medical colleges across India.

articles.title: The ‘Polar Bear Capital’ with Arctic gateway ambitions
articles.rephrased_article: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has identified the Port of Churchill as a key project to boost the country's economy and reduce reliance on the United States.  The port, located in Manitoba, is strategically positioned for Arctic shipping routes and could facilitate trade with Europe, particularly for critical minerals and LNG. While proponents envision year-round operations, experts caution that ice conditions in the Hudson Bay make consistent open water shipping unlikely. The Port of Churchill's potential remains uncertain, as its economic viability hinges on overcoming logistical challenges and securing long-term demand.  The port's expansion is supported by Canada's government and international partners like the Port of Antwerp-Bruges, but faces skepticism from some experts who question its profitability.

articles.title: Prosecutors release detailed description of how D4vd allegedly killed teen girl | US crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, has been charged with the murder and sexual abuse of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Prosecutors allege D4vd fatally stabbed Celeste to silence her after she threatened to disclose damaging information about their relationship and ruin his music career. The singer's defense team maintains his innocence.  Authorities believe D4vd dismembered Celeste's body in an inflatable pool before abandoning the vehicle containing her remains in the Hollywood Hills, where they were discovered a day after her 15th birthday.

articles.title: EPFO to launch new portal to track inoperative accounts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is launching E-PRAAPTI, a digital platform to facilitate the identification, tracking, and activation of old EPF accounts. The platform will use Aadhaar-based authentication for secure access and streamline processes like UAN linking and profile updates.  The EPFO has also settled a record number of claims in 2025-26, with a significant increase in auto-processing of advance withdrawals.

articles.title: Florida lawmakers approve redistricting to help Republicans
articles.rephrased_article: Florida lawmakers approved new congressional maps that could help Republicans maintain control of the US House of Representatives in the upcoming midterm elections. The move comes after the US Supreme Court limited the ability of lawmakers to consider racial makeup when drawing voting districts.  The new map, which reduces Democratic-leaning districts in Tampa and Orlando, is expected to be signed into law by Governor Ron DeSantis. This redistricting effort follows a national trend where states are redrawing maps to favor their political parties.

articles.title: Florida approves US House map meant to boost Republicans in midterms | Florida | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Florida legislature approved a new congressional map that aims to strengthen the Republican party's advantage in the state. The decision, made just days after Governor Ron DeSantis unveiled his proposal and on the same day the US Supreme Court rolled back a key provision of the Voting Rights Act, could make it harder for Democrats to challenge Republican efforts to redraw districts.  The map reshapes districts around Orlando, Tampa-St Petersburg, and south Florida, potentially costing representatives like Jared Moskowitz and Debbie Wasserman Schultz their seats. The proposal was defended by DeSantis and his aides as necessary to account for population growth and ensure a "race-neutral" plan, but faces potential legal challenges due to the state constitution's prohibition of partisan redistricting.

articles.title: Bihar govt removes Sanjay Gandhi's name from Patna zoo, dairy technology institute - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP-led government in Bihar renamed the Sanjay Gandhi Biological Park as 'Patna Zoo' and the Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Dairy Technology as 'Bihar State Institute of Dairy Technology'. The cabinet also approved ₹23,165 crore for a power subsidy scheme, ₹104 crore for degree colleges under the 'Saat Nischay-3' program, and land for a Centre of Excellence for autism treatment.  The government allocated funds for four major road projects, increased monthly stipends for SC/ST students in hostels, and approved the development of model schools with modern labs.

articles.title: King and Queen lay flowers at 9/11 Memorial in New York
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles and Queen Camilla visited the 9/11 Memorial in New York, laying flowers and meeting families of victims and first responders. The visit took place amid tight security and was part of their state visit to the United States.  They also met representatives from charities supporting victims' families and educational groups preserving the memory of the attacks. President Donald Trump commented on the King's stance on Iran, while Queen Camilla highlighted the importance of literacy at the New York Public Library.

articles.title: Trial of non-invasive endometriosis scan boosts hopes for quicker diagnosis | Endometriosis | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A trial involving a new radiotracer, maraciclatide, has shown promising results in detecting endometriosis. The experimental tracer, developed by the UK-based company Serac, binds to tissue that is creating new blood vessels – a hallmark of endometriosis.  The study, which included 19 women with the condition, suggests the scan can accurately identify endometriosis, potentially leading to quicker and more reliable diagnosis. Prof Krina Zondervan, head of the Nuffield Department of Women’s and Reproductive Health (NDWRH) at the University of Oxford, and co-lead on the study, believes this could revolutionize clinical research and practice for women across the globe.

articles.title: Honeymoon murder: Meghalaya court reserves order on bail plea of key accused - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Raj Kushwaha, one of the key suspects in the murder of Raja Raghuvanshi, a businessman from Indore, is awaiting a decision on his bail plea.  The Meghalaya court reserved its order after hearing arguments from Kushwaha's counsel, who stated that all evidence has been presented. Sonam, Raghuvanshi's wife and another accused, was granted bail earlier this week. The case involves the alleged murder of Raghuvanshi during his honeymoon in Meghalaya last year.

articles.title: US singer D4vd bought tools online to dispose of girl's body, prosecutors say
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd, a US singer known for his TikTok hits, has been accused of purchasing tools online to dispose of the body of teen girl Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Prosecutors allege that D4vd, who had a sexual relationship with Hernandez starting when she was 13, purchased chainsaws and a shovel after stabbing her. He pleaded not guilty to seven charges including murder and mutilation of remains.  The case is ongoing with a hearing scheduled for May 15th.

articles.title: Raise tax on alcohol and junk food to cut deaths from liver disease, experts say | Health | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Governments in Europe are being urged to impose higher taxes on alcohol and unhealthy food to combat the continent's high rate of liver disease deaths. The European Association for the Study of the Liver, Lancet medical journal, and other experts recommend that governments implement these measures to cover the significant costs associated with healthcare, law enforcement, and social services.  They also call on national governments to align taxation with the economic burden of alcohol and unhealthy food consumption, emphasizing the need to address "commercial determinants of health" like tobacco, alcohol, and ultra-processed foods.

articles.title: Nilgiris forest fire totally contained: TN government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, officials from the Forest Department and the State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) closely monitored a forest fire in the Nilgiris district that was ultimately contained. The fire, fueled by dry vegetation and strong winds, spread rapidly due to the terrain's steep slopes and unpredictable winds.  Multiple teams of forest personnel, including those from the Tamil Nadu State Disaster Response Force and the TN Fire and Rescue Department, worked to control the blaze. Aerial assistance from an Air Force helicopter was used on April 25th, but weather conditions halted further use.

articles.title: Carney ‘strong’ in year one, now must deliver on promises in Canada | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has navigated a year of challenges, including US President Donald Trump's aggressive actions and trade tariffs.  Carney has refocused Canada's foreign policy, prioritizing diversification and building stronger ties with countries like India, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and Europe. He has also deepened relations with China, despite tensions stemming from the arrest of Huawei executive Meng Wanzhou in 2018. Carney faces challenges delivering on his promises, particularly regarding the USMCA trade pact review and navigating complex relationships with the US.  His approval ratings have risen since taking office, but he will need to demonstrate success in implementing his foreign policy goals.

articles.title: Hegseth clashes with lawmakers over Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, Gen Dan Caine, and the US Defense Department's chief financial officer Jules Hurst appeared before the House Armed Services Committee to discuss the cost of the Iran war.  Democrats criticized the use of federal funds, with some lawmakers calling it a "war of choice" without Congressional approval.  Hegseth defended the $1.5 trillion defense budget request as necessary for future security and countered accusations from Democrats that President Trump is in a "quagmire". Republicans largely supported the Pentagon's stance on Iran's threat to the US, with some members emphasizing the need to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons.  The hearing also addressed the international economic impacts of the war, including rising oil prices.

articles.title: Trump threatens to reduce troop numbers in Germany amid growing row with Nato allies | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced his administration is studying the possibility of reducing US troops in Germany, a move that could cause concern in Berlin and across Europe. Friedrich Merz, German chancellor, criticized the US's negotiations with Iran, suggesting they are not successful.  Trump responded to Merz's comments, accusing him of supporting Iran's nuclear program. The president has previously threatened to withdraw from NATO, citing European allies' lack of support for US-Israeli actions against Iran and the closure of the Hormuz strait.

articles.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth first public hearing on Iran war: Key takeaways | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth faced his first public questioning from Congress on the US-Israel war with Iran.  Hegseth defended the $25 billion cost of the war, arguing that it was worth preventing Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon. Hegseth also addressed questions about Iran's nuclear program and the effectiveness of US military actions in the region. While some Democrats questioned the war's goals and costs, Republicans largely supported Hegseth's testimony.  The hearing highlighted ongoing tensions between Congress and the Trump administration regarding the duration and legality of the conflict.

articles.title: Hegseth denies Iran war is ‘quagmire’ as cost to US hits estimated $25bn | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, appearing before the House armed services committee, defended the US-Israel war on Iran as an "existential fight" and criticized congressional Democrats for their opposition. Gen Dan Caine, chair of the joint chiefs of staff, also testified alongside him, advocating for increased military spending. The Pentagon estimates the cost of the conflict at $25 billion, with lawmakers questioning the administration's strategy and diplomatic isolation in the war.  Donald Trump has pledged to secure a "better deal" from Iran and maintain a naval blockade until a nuclear agreement is reached, while John Garamendi, a Democrat, argued that the war was a "quagmire" and criticized the administration's handling of the conflict.

articles.title: Ex-FBI chief Comey appears in court over alleged Trump threat | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: James Comey, former FBI director, appeared in federal court in Virginia on Wednesday after being indicted for allegedly threatening US President Donald Trump.  Comey turned himself in on charges of threatening the president's life and transmitting threats across state lines. His lawyer argued that the case is a vindictive prosecution, while prosecutors claim the image he shared online was interpreted as a serious threat. Comey has denied the allegations and plans to fight the charges.

articles.title: After giving away $26 billion in philanthropy, MacKenzie Scott’s wealth remains largely unchanged — here's why | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: MacKenzie Scott, one of the world's wealthiest individuals, has donated approximately $26.3 billion to charities since 2019 through her platform Yield Giving. Despite this significant giving, her net worth remains substantial due to her holdings in Amazon stock, which have appreciated significantly over time. Jeff Bezos, another billionaire, has donated a smaller amount compared to Scott's pace of giving.  Her wealth is tied to the value of Amazon shares and continues to grow even as she donates billions.

articles.title: Jerome Powell to stay on Fed board after central bank holds rates steady in defiance of Trump | Federal Reserve | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell, chair of the US Federal Reserve, will remain on the central bank's rate-setting board despite his term ending in May.  Powell announced this decision after the Fed board left interest rates unchanged for the third time this year, citing elevated inflation, slow job growth, and uncertainty in the Middle East as reasons. While the Fed board signaled growing dissent within its ranks, Kevin Warsh, a former Fed governor nominated to succeed Powell, is expected to be more amenable to Trump's calls for rate cuts. The White House has faced criticism from the Fed over its influence on the economy, including investigations into renovations at the Fed that have cast a shadow over Warsh's nomination.

articles.title: Mali’s Tuareg rebels say Russian fighters must withdraw from country | Military News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mali’s Tuareg rebels, the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), have called for Russian fighters to withdraw from the country, stating their objective is for Russia's Africa Corps to "withdraw permanently."  The rebels, who are involved in a continuing uprising that includes the assassination of the country’s defense minister, view Russia’s intervention negatively due to its support for the Malian government. The rebel alliance launched coordinated attacks on Saturday, resulting in the death of Mali’s defense minister and the subsequent withdrawal of Russian fighters from Kidal after negotiations with neighboring Algeria.  The FLA claims they will now take control of Gao, Timbuktu, and Menaka following the capture of Kidal.

articles.title: White House dinner attack: Man charged in Trump assassination bid took photo with knife before assault - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, a 31-year-old man from California, has been charged with attempted assassination of President Donald Trump after allegedly attempting to breach security at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.  Allen was armed with a shotgun and knife when he took a photograph of himself in his hotel room minutes before the attack, which occurred on Saturday night while President Trump was present. Authorities allege that Allen had been monitoring online updates tracking the President’s movements and planned to attack him. He is currently being held without bail pending trial.

articles.title: Trump hosts crew of historic Artemis mission: ‘I would have had no trouble making it’ | Artemis II | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump hosted the crew of the Artemis II lunar flyby mission at the White House on Wednesday. The astronauts, including commander Reid Wiseman and pilot Victor Glover, discussed their successful mission that surpassed Apollo 13's distance record.  The discussion then shifted to the Supreme Court's decision gutting a major section of the Voting Rights Act, with Trump expressing support for the ruling and suggesting states redraw maps based on it. The president also spoke about ongoing talks with Iran, stating they would be conducted via telephone calls instead of face-to-face meetings.

articles.title: Arsenal cruelly denied penalty by VAR in Champions League draw at Atletico | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Arsenal and Atletico Madrid played to a 1-1 draw in the first leg of their Champions League semifinal.  Mikel Arteta's team was denied a penalty after a VAR review, while Diego Simeone's side capitalized on a handball to equalize. The match saw several missed chances from both sides, with Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres both having opportunities for the Gunners and Atletico Madrid.  The second leg will be played next Tuesday in London.

articles.title: 4,300-year-old gold-covered mummy found sealed in deep Egyptian shaft, shocks archaeologists | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Egypt have uncovered a sealed tomb containing a gold-covered mummy at the bottom of a deep shaft in Saqqara, one of the oldest and largest burial grounds in the country. The discovery suggests a rare instance of preservation in an area known for its ancient burials that have been disturbed over time.  The mummy, identified as Heka-shepes, was found wrapped and coated in gold elements, with the coffin sealed with ancient mortar. Experts believe this tomb offers a unique glimpse into Old Kingdom burial customs, particularly for elite figures.

articles.title: Should Jimmy Kimmel be fired for telling a joke?
articles.rephrased_article: Jimmy Kimmel defended a joke that called First Lady Melania Trump an "expectant widow" after the White House urged his network, ABC, to fire him. The FCC is now ordering an early review of Disney's television broadcast licenses following the incident.

articles.title: Golders Green attack claim highlights rise of shadowy Iran-linked group | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Counter-terror police are investigating a knife attack on two British Jewish people in Golders Green, north London, for which an Iran-linked terror group, Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia (HAYI) claimed responsibility.  The group, known for making claims of responsibility for arson and attempted arson attacks targeting the Jewish community, has also claimed responsibility for attacks on Jewish sites in Europe. Police are investigating whether there is a degree of Iranian state direction behind HAYI's activities, but have not found evidence to support this claim at this time.

articles.title: US stocks today: Microsoft cloud revenue accelerates as spending growth cools - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Microsoft's capital expenditure rose 49% to $31.9 billion in its fiscal third quarter, exceeding Wall Street expectations and potentially easing concerns about its AI strategy. The company attributed the increase to investments in data centers and expanded AI model options, including those from Anthropic, which helped it secure a major Copilot deployment for Accenture.  Despite these investments, Microsoft also announced an overhaul of its OpenAI deal to lock in revenue share through 2030, potentially impacting its cloud capacity.

articles.title: Israel intercepts Global Sumud boats, demands activists halt their mission | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has intercepted Global Sumud aid boats in the Mediterranean Sea, using jamming technology and armed boarding teams. The Global Sumud Flotilla organizers claim the Israeli military approached the ships with lasers and assault weapons, demanding participants to the front of the boats and get on their hands and knees.  The flotilla is comprised of 58 vessels attempting to reach Gaza, a territory devastated by years of conflict. A spokesperson for the Global Sumud Flotilla called Israel's actions an "illegal attack" and urged governments to protect the over 400 civilians on board.

articles.title: Candace Owens breaks silence after Andrew Kolvet chat leak as Charlie Kirk show clip leaves viewers uneasy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens found herself at the center of a controversy after a clip from Charlie Kirk's show sparked online debate. A user criticized the segment, alleging it was scripted and unnatural, prompting further scrutiny when Andrew Kolvet shared a screenshot of a private chat with Owens, featuring a line that suggested she had murdered her husband.  Owens denied the message's seriousness and called for the full conversation to be released, arguing the line was meant as sarcasm. The situation has fueled discussions about authenticity, editing, and context in online content.

articles.title: In five charts - How UAE's exit could affect Opec's influence over the oil price
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates' (UAE) planned departure from the oil producers' group, Opec, is seen as a significant blow to the organization and its ability to influence global oil prices.  With the UAE being one of Opec's top oil exporters, its exit could lead to increased production by other members, potentially impacting the already volatile oil market. The UAE was the world's third biggest oil exporter in 2025, behind Saudi Arabia and Iraq, but experts suggest it could increase production by around one million barrels daily once out of Opec.  However, the organization has lost some of its influence over the years as non-Opec countries like the US have become more prominent producers.

articles.title: Stephen Fry sues tech conference organisers for £100,000 over fall from stage | Stephen Fry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Fry is suing CogX Festival Ltd and Blonstein Events, the companies that organized a tech conference where he fell off stage, breaking his hip and other bones.  The actor claims negligence on the part of the defendants for failing to ensure a safe stage environment. A spokesperson for CogX Festival Ltd expressed concern for Fry's well-being while stating they cannot comment until the legal process is complete.  Blonstein Events, which has not yet been formally notified, maintains that it was not responsible for the incident and expects its defense to be successful.

articles.title: The King of Comedy: How Charles III used humour to reprimand Trump in the US Congress | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III delivered a speech to the US Congress, using humor and historical references to subtly highlight the enduring nature of constitutional monarchy.  He acknowledged the awkward history between Britain and America while reframing it as an example of how institutions adapt and coexist with democracy. The monarch's speech emphasized the importance of shared responsibility, respect for law, and the need for patience in disagreement, all framed through a lighthearted lens. Charles’s speech served as a reminder that power thrives when it is restrained by limits, not dominated by personal ambition.

articles.title: Musk accuses Altman of betraying OpenAI’s nonprofit founding mission | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Elon Musk and Sam Altman, co-founders of OpenAI, are engaged in a legal battle over the company's transition from a nonprofit to a for-profit entity.  Musk claims that Altman betrayed promises to maintain the nonprofit mission, alleging he was trying to "steal the charity." OpenAI's lawyers argue there was never a commitment to remain nonprofit and that Musk's lawsuit is an attempt to undermine the company in favor of his competing venture, xAI.  The trial centers on OpenAI's 2015 founding as a nonprofit that later evolved into a for-profit venture.

articles.title: Syria trial seen as first step on long road for Assad's victims
articles.rephrased_article: The first trial of a former official from the Assad regime took place in Damascus, marking a significant step towards justice for victims. Atef Najib, former head of the Political Security intelligence agency in Deraa, was charged with crimes against the Syrian nation and faced accusations related to his role during the 2011 uprising. While some families felt this trial brought them closure and hope for future accountability, others criticized it as a mere show of appeasement by Syria's new government.  Nuha al-Masri, a lawyer who lost her brother in the crackdown, expressed relief at seeing a regime member behind bars, while Anwar al-Bunni, a human rights lawyer, argued that the trial lacked legal framework and specialized judges to address war crimes effectively.

articles.title: With supreme court ruling, Republicans can marginalize Black political power | US politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court's decision in the Callais v Landry case has been met with strong criticism, as it effectively invalidates much of the Voting Rights Act's Section 2. The NAACP and other civil rights groups have condemned the ruling, arguing that it undermines decades of progress towards racial equality in American politics.  The decision removes protections for minority voters by removing the requirement to prove racial motivations in redistricting, which could significantly diminish Black political power, particularly in Southern states where voting patterns are highly racially polarized.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu’s growth record - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu has achieved a high-growth trajectory, recording a real Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) growth of 10.83% in 2025-26, exceeding the national average of 7.4%. This marks two consecutive years of double-digit growth and is attributed to the state's strong policy framework and structural strengths.  The nominal GSDP expanded by 13.16%, making it the highest among states.

articles.title: Meta lifts capital expenditure forecast, doubling down on AI push - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Meta, formerly known as Facebook, has revised its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 to $125 billion to $145 billion. The company's family daily active people (DAP) increased by 4% year-over-year to 3.56 billion. Meta is investing heavily in AI infrastructure and employee compensation, particularly at its Meta Superintelligence Labs, which released its first AI model called Muse Spark earlier this month.  The company's robust ad platform continues to drive growth, with its Advantage+ tools powered by Andromeda, Lattice, and GEM attracting more marketers despite geopolitical uncertainty.

articles.title: 'Is a President allowed to go on a space mission?': Trump jokes as Artemis II astronauts visit White House - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump met with the NASA Artemis II astronauts, including Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen, at the White House following their historic 10-day lunar mission.  During the event, Trump jokingly inquired about his ability to join a space mission, prompting NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman to suggest working on it. The astronauts' mission marked a significant step in the US space agency's plan for a return to the Moon and future Mars missions.

articles.title: Ukraine asks Israel to seize ship carrying grain ‘stolen’ by Russia | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine has requested that Israel seize a ship, the Panormitis, carrying grain it claims was stolen from occupied Russian regions.  Ukraine's Prosecutor General, Ruslan Kravchenko, stated that the vessel is headed to Haifa with grain "some of which was shipped" from these areas. Israel's Foreign Minister, Gideon Saar, acknowledged receiving the request but questioned its timing and urged for a legal approach. Ukraine has previously protested Russian grain exports from occupied regions and threatened sanctions against those profiting from it.

articles.title: Some experts skeptical of second Comey indictment over seashell post
articles.rephrased_article: James Comey, former FBI director, was indicted on charges of threatening President Donald Trump. The government alleges that a seashell post Comey made last year constituted a "serious expression" conveying an intent to harm the president. Legal experts are skeptical about the prosecution's ability to prove intent and argue that Comey's post could be protected by the First Amendment.  The case stems from an Instagram post depicting numbers that some believe refer to Trump, while others see it as a harmless message.

articles.title: Bengaluru tragedy cuts short a long-awaited Kudumbashree trip from Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A group of Kudumbashree workers and officials from Ernakulam district, traveling to Bengaluru for a shopping trip, were tragically killed when a hospital compound wall collapsed during heavy rain.  The accident claimed the lives of Latha K.K., 57, and Smitha Raghu, 47, while three others sustained injuries. The group had planned a flight journey for April 9th but it was postponed due to Assembly elections. Kudumbashree officials are assisting with arrangements for the return of the remaining members and the transportation of the deceased's remains.

articles.title: Amazon beats quarterly cloud growth estimates on strong AI demand; AWS revenue jumps 28% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Amazon's AWS revenue surged 28% to $37.6 billion in the first quarter, exceeding analyst expectations. While shares dipped after projecting current-quarter operating income slightly lower than estimates, the cloud services provider saw a boost from its partnership with AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic.  The announcements have helped push Amazon's stock up 14% this year, as the company focuses on monetizing its AI infrastructure investments for near-term returns.

articles.title: D4Vd Legal Situation: D4vd makes unusual request ahead of hearing, judge responds with a twist - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd, facing serious charges of first-degree murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14, and mutilation of human remains, requested to wear dress pants and a button-down shirt instead of jail clothing for his upcoming court appearance.  However, the L.A. County Superior Court Judge Charlaine F. Olmedo denied this request, stating that he must appear in standard jail attire during the hearing. The judge did approve D4vd's request to get a haircut before the hearing on May 1st. This unusual pre-hearing scenario has added a strange twist to an already serious case.

articles.title: Why is the UAE quitting OPEC – and what’s the impact? | OPEC News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) is withdrawing from the OPEC oil-producing bloc, a move that comes amid the worst global energy crisis in modern history. The decision was prompted by the ongoing US-Israel conflict with Iran, which has significantly impacted the UAE's economy.  Experts on the panel discuss the reasons behind the UAE's withdrawal and its potential impact on the global oil market.

articles.title: Four key takeaways from Jerome Powell's last rate decision as Fed chair
articles.rephrased_article: Jerome Powell, the current Federal Reserve chair, announced that interest rates would remain between 3.5% and 3.75%.  The decision came after continued pressure from President Donald Trump to lower rates. The Fed will continue to monitor economic uncertainty caused by the Iran war and inflation, which reached 3.3%, its highest level since May 2024. Kevin Warsh, who is expected to succeed Powell as chair, has pledged to uphold the central bank's independence despite pressure from the Trump administration.  Senator Thom Tillis dropped his opposition to Warsh's appointment after the Justice Department ended its investigation into Powell.

articles.title: Knee surgery for cartilage damage does not benefit patients, study suggests | Medical research | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 10-year study found that a common knee surgery for cartilage damage, partial meniscectomy, does not benefit patients and may lead to worse outcomes.  Prof Teppo Järvinen, an orthopaedic surgeon at the University of Helsinki, led the research which tracked patients who underwent surgery versus those who received sham surgery. The results showed those who had surgery experienced poorer knee function, greater osteoarthritis progression, and a higher likelihood of needing further surgery. Mark Bowditch, a consultant knee surgeon, noted that best practice guidelines have shifted to recommend waiting longer before considering surgery, but acknowledged there are subsets of patients who may still benefit from the procedure.

articles.title: 15 labourers die as van overturns in Madhya Pradesh’s Dhar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: At least 15 laborers, many of them women, died and over 30 were injured in a road accident on the Indore-Ahmedabad highway in Madhya Pradesh's Dhar district.  The police said the speeding van carrying about 46 labourers overturned and collided with an SUV.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences and announced financial assistance for the victims, while Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav directed officials to oversee medical arrangements and provide financial aid.

articles.title: Google parent Alphabet's cloud unit beats quarterly revenue estimates on strong AI demand - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Alphabet's first-quarter revenue surged 22% to $109.9 billion, exceeding analyst estimates, driven by strong growth in its cloud division. Google Cloud saw a 63% increase in revenue to $20 billion, with a backlog nearly doubling quarter-over-quarter to over $460 billion. The company's AI initiatives, including Gemini models and partnerships with Apple, are contributing to Alphabet's success as investors watch for sustained growth and market share gains. Despite capacity constraints across the industry, Alphabet is well positioned in the competitive cloud market.

articles.title: Was Jeffrey Epstein building a 'mosque' on his private island? Records show rare Islamic artefacts brought from Middle East - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jeffrey Epstein, a disgraced financier, acquired rare Islamic artifacts for a distinctive blue-and-white striped building on his private Caribbean island. The US Justice Department released millions of pages revealing that he cultivated relationships with wealthy and powerful figures in the Middle East while focusing on Islamic art and architecture.  Epstein obtained items like tapestries from the Kaaba, sections of the Kiswa, and tiles from a mosque in Uzbekistan, intending to create an architectural and artistic project inspired by Islamic design. The building was referred to as a "mosque" by Epstein, despite not being intended for religious use.

articles.title: New Florida map boosts Republican seats amid national redistricting fight | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Florida’s Republican-controlled legislature approved a new congressional map that favors Republicans, putting them on track to gain 24 seats in the November midterm elections. The move comes amid a national redistricting battle and follows similar actions by other states like Texas, Missouri, and Virginia. Democrats are considered favored to retake control of the US House of Representatives, but the new map could have unintended consequences for Republicans as President Trump's approval rating has dipped. Legal challenges regarding the map’s constitutionality are expected.

articles.title: Hungary's next PM hails EU talks and vows frozen funds will be paid out soon
articles.rephrased_article: Péter Magyar, Hungary's new prime minister, met with Ursula von der Leyen, the President of the European Commission, and assured her that EU funds would be released soon.  He pledged to address corruption and rule-of-law issues in order to unlock billions of euros in EU funding for Hungary's economy. António Costa, President of the European Council, also met with Magyar, who aims to reverse Orbán-era policies and secure access to various EU funds.

articles.title: Australia news live: Penny Wong wins jet fuel pledge from China in Beijing visit; US lawmaker says Aukus price might go up | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Penny Wong, Australia's foreign affairs minister, announced that China has agreed to facilitate jet fuel exports to ease global supply disruptions caused by the war in the Middle East.  She made this statement after talks with her Chinese counterparts, Wang Yi and Han Zheng.  Wong also emphasized the need for greater reciprocity in trade, highlighting Australia's reliance on imports from China.

articles.title: Watch: Why has the UAE left Opec - and why does this matter?
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced its withdrawal from the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (Opec), after nearly six decades of membership. The UAE's departure is seen as a significant blow to Opec, which oversees oil production and influences global prices. This move could impact consumers worldwide.

articles.title: UAE quits OPEC: What that means for the Gulf, energy markets and beyond | Oil and Gas News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Arab Emirates has announced its withdrawal from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), citing a desire to pursue independent economic policies and reshape Gulf oil politics. The move is seen as a significant blow to OPEC but is unlikely to have an immediate impact on the global energy market due to existing constraints related to Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz.  Saudi Arabia, however, has downplayed the UAE's departure, stating it won't significantly affect the cartel. The UAE has invested billions in increasing its oil production capacity and seeks to maximize its output before a potential decline in global demand for oil. Experts believe the decision reflects the UAE's desire to be free from OPEC constraints as the world transitions away from fossil fuels.

articles.title: Putin, Trump hold 90-minute call on Iran, Ukraine war: Russia proposes Kyiv ceasefire for Victory Day - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump held a phone call on Wednesday, their first direct contact since March. The conversation covered issues including the escalating situation in the Middle East, particularly Iran, with Putin supporting Trump's decision to extend the ceasefire.  The call also addressed the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict, with Putin proposing a temporary ceasefire coinciding with Russia's Victory Day celebrations on May 9th.

articles.title: Elon Musk gets an apology from California regulators as SpaceX lawsuit is settled | Elon Musk | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and the California coastal commission reached a settlement in a lawsuit alleging political bias against Musk. The commission apologized for "improper" statements made about Musk's political beliefs at a 2024 hearing, agreeing to not consider those factors in future regulatory actions.  The case will be permanently dismissed, but the commission maintains concerns about the environmental impacts of increased rocket launches at Vandenberg space force base.

articles.title: King Charles III and Donald Trump exchange jokes during speeches
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III and Donald Trump exchanged jokes during a state dinner in Washington D.C., with the King praising Trump for his actions regarding the Middle East crisis and referencing a past battle between Britain and France over North America.  Trump reciprocated by complimenting Charles III on getting the "Democrats to stand" during his congressional address.

articles.title: US Fed holds rates steady, Powell to remain on its board | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3.5 to 3.75 percent, citing concerns over inflation and global economic strain from the US-Israel war on Iran. The decision was largely in line with economist expectations, as the central bank acknowledged rising oil prices and a stagnant labor market.  The Fed also noted that political pressure surrounding Kevin Warsh's confirmation as a replacement for Jerome Powell has contributed to uncertainty about the future of monetary policy. Despite concerns from Democrats regarding Warsh's potential influence on the Fed, Powell stated he would not step down until the investigation into his tenure is concluded.

articles.title: Ex-FBI chief James Comey surrenders in 'threat' case against Donald Trump; what was '86 47' post? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: James Comey, former FBI Director, surrendered to US authorities on Wednesday after being charged with threatening the life of President Donald Trump.  He faces two charges: threatening the president's life and transmitting threats across state lines. The indictment stems from a social media post Comey made last May that included the numbers '86 47', which prosecutors argue could be interpreted as a threat to Trump, who is the 47th president of the United States.  Comey maintains he did not intend the message as a threat and plans to fight the charges in court, with his legal team arguing for selective prosecution by the Justice Department. The case will proceed in North Carolina.

articles.title: Leasehold ban in England and Wales unlikely before next general election, minister says | Housing | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Matthew Pennycook, the housing minister, stated that a ban on new leasehold properties in England and Wales is unlikely to be implemented before the next election. He explained that phasing out the system gradually, while addressing housing supply concerns, is necessary.  Pennycook emphasized the complexity of the process and the need for comprehensive legislation to ensure a smooth transition. Zack Polanski, Green party leader, criticized the government's approach as a U-turn on its election pledge, highlighting the impact on leaseholders.

articles.title: Israel and Hezbollah keep fighting despite Lebanon ceasefire
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement, Israel and Hezbollah continue to fight in Lebanon. The deal, signed by the Lebanese government but not Hezbollah, allows Israel "take all necessary measures in self-defence" against attacks from Hezbollah.  The fragile ceasefire remains precarious as Hezbollah, backed by Iran, is too powerful for the Lebanese government to control.

articles.title: South Africa to deport Robert Mugabe’s son over firearm offence | Courts News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bellarmine Mugabe, son of the late Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe, was ordered to be deported from South Africa after pleading guilty to two firearm-related offenses.  A magistrate fined him $36,000 or sentenced him to two years in prison for brandishing a toy gun and being in the country illegally. Matonhodze, his cousin, also pleaded guilty to attempted murder and other charges and was sentenced to three years in prison.

articles.title: 'Return Koh-i-Noor diamond': Zohran Mamdani quips on crown jewel handover during King Charles' New York visit - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani suggested during a press conference that he would ask King Charles III to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond during the monarch's visit.  Mamdani made the comment while King Charles III and Queen Camilla were visiting the National 9/11 Memorial & Museum, where they met with families of victims and paid tribute to those killed in the 2001 terror attacks. The Koh-i-Noor, a diamond taken from India centuries ago and now housed at the Tower of London, has been the subject of ongoing disputes over colonial-era artifacts.

articles.title: Firing from across Afghan border injures 5 in KP's South Waziristan: security sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Afghan Taliban and affiliated elements fired mortar shells into Pakistan, injuring five civilians, including four children, in the Angoor Adda village of South Waziristan district. The Pakistani Army retaliated by targeting their firing positions along the border, causing the Afghan Taliban to abandon their posts and flee. This follows a previous attack on civilians three days prior, which resulted in the destruction of the Afghan Taliban's posts.  The attacks are part of ongoing conflict between the two countries.

articles.title: Office for Students’ University of Sussex humiliation is a symptom of deeper failings | Office for Students | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Office for Students (OfS) faced a setback this week when the high court rejected its attempt to fine the University of Sussex over Kathleen Stock's tenure. The ruling highlighted the OfS's failures in its regulatory efforts, including bias and jurisdictional issues.  Susan Lapworth, former chief executive, initiated the investigation in 2021, but despite years of effort, the OfS has yet to demonstrate significant progress for students. This failure contrasts with the growing financial turmoil within the higher education sector, where institutions are facing closures and redundancies. The new leadership under Ruth Hannant and Polly Payne faces a challenging task in restoring trust and effectively regulating the sector.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh: In India's 'glass city' Firozabad, the Iran war is threatening jobs
articles.rephrased_article: Tensions in the Middle East are impacting India's glass industry, particularly in Firozabad, a city known as the "glass city."  Sanjay Jain, owner of a glass bangle unit, has had to reduce production due to gas shortages and increased costs. The All India Glass Manufacturers' Federation reports that the conflict has led to losses for many small manufacturing units, with some facing closures or reduced operations.  The situation is also impacting workers who are struggling with rising living costs and inflation, leading to protests demanding higher wages and better working conditions.

articles.title: UK’s ‘terrorism’ laws risk overreach, watchdog warns | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A UK watchdog has warned against the overreach of counterterrorism laws, highlighting concerns about their application to activist groups.  Jonathan Hall, independent reviewer of terrorism legislation, expressed uncertainty regarding the definition of "serious damage to property" and suggested narrowing the test for potential terrorist activity. Shabana Mahmood, Interior Minister, stated she would review the recommendations before responding. The report comes as the government appeals a High Court ruling that found the banning of pro-Palestine group Palestine Action unlawful on free speech grounds.

articles.title: London Marathon winner’s massive payday revealed as he names first purchase after historic run | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sebastian Sawe, a Kenyan runner, shattered the two-hour marathon barrier at the London Marathon on Sunday, April 26, 2026, setting a new world record of 1:59:30.  He crossed the finish line ahead of Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha (1:59:41) and Uganda's Jacob Kiplimo (2:00:28). Sawe's victory earned him $355,000 in prize money, with potential earnings reaching up to $1 million.  He plans to use the winnings to improve his family's living conditions and build a church in Kenya.

articles.title: Oil spikes while stocks slip ahead of US Fed rate decision - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged on Wednesday, reaching their highest level since the US-Iran ceasefire, due to concerns of an extended blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump warned Tehran to "get smart soon" and comply with US demands for nuclear control, while a US naval blockade is expected to continue for months. This heightened tension has led analysts to predict oil prices could reach $120 per barrel. Meanwhile, Wall Street stocks declined as investors awaited the US Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and tech earnings reports.  The market remains cautious ahead of these announcements.

articles.title: Senior UK ministers deride Rachel Reeves’s reported plan of year-long rent freeze | Rachel Reeves | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the chancellor, faced criticism from Steve Reed and Matthew Pennycook, housing ministers, after reports surfaced that she was considering a year-long rent freeze.  The government quickly dismissed the idea as not credible or serious. The backlash has fueled speculation about Reeves's future in light of recent local election losses and reports suggesting Prime Minister Keir Starmer may replace her. Despite these concerns, Starmer maintained his confidence in Reeves and emphasized her commitment to economic growth, while Treasury sources reported she was upbeat and focused on the government's mission.

articles.title: Trump and Powell's biggest clashes - from numbskulls and morons to too stupid
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Jerome Powell have had a contentious relationship since Trump's return to the White House.  Trump has criticized Powell, calling him names and demanding faster interest rate cuts, while Powell has defended his independence and actions against Trump's pressure. This tension escalated during Trump's presidency when he clashed with Powell over the cost of renovating Federal Reserve buildings. The situation reached a peak when Powell faced a criminal investigation by the Department of Justice (DoJ) which threatened to indict him for his testimony before Congress.  Following the DoJ's decision to drop the probe, Republican Senator Thom Tillis withdrew his opposition to Kevin Warsh's nomination as Fed chair.

articles.title: Trump vows to maintain Iran blockade, Tehran threaten ‘practical’ action | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump maintains the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, stating it is more effective than bombing. Iran has proposed a limited deal to end its own blockade on the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for ending the siege on its ports, but Trump rejected this proposal.  The impasse has led to soaring oil prices and heightened tensions between the two countries. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf vows that Iranians will defeat the US's plan and achieve a victory. The situation remains at a deadlock with no clear path towards resolving the nuclear issue or ending the blockade.

articles.title: Nitesh Rane sentenced to one month in jail for insulting NHA engineer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nitesh Rane, a former Congress MLA, has been convicted by the Sindhudurg Sessions Court for intentionally insulting a public servant.  The court sentenced him to one month of imprisonment and a fine of ₹1 lakh for forcing Prakash Shedekar, a Sub-Divisional Engineer with the National Highways Authority (NHA), to walk on a mud road in Kankavali, his constituency. The incident occurred in July 2019.

articles.title: Clavicular Lawsuit: Controversial streamer Clavicular accused of abuse and fraud in explosive lawsuit by influencer - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a controversial streamer, is facing a lawsuit filed by influencer Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza.  The lawsuit alleges abuse, fraud, and emotional harm stemming from Clavicular's alleged exploitation of Mendoza when she was 16 years old. Mendoza claims that Clavicular promised career help but instead caused her harm through sexual assault, unauthorized medical procedures, and damaging her reputation. The case is ongoing with no final decision made yet.

articles.title: Amid furore on social media, Cambridge says 'aware' of reports about question paper leak - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cambridge International Education (CIE) acknowledged reports of a leaked AS mathematics question paper in Pakistan, stating they are investigating the matter thoroughly.  The CIE, part of Cambridge University Press and Assessment, offers internationally recognized exams to over scores of schools globally. The organization previously addressed leaks in 2025 and 2024, offering resits for affected candidates. CIE exams are typically held twice a year, with results released in August and January.

articles.title: GB News commentator to sue charity for not offering internships to white people | Law | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sophie Corcoran, a GB News commentator, is suing the 10,000 Interns Foundation for allegedly discriminating against white people by restricting its internship program to applicants of a particular racial background. Rebecca Achieng Ajulu-Bushell, CEO of the foundation and the first black woman to swim for Great Britain, maintains that the program aims to widen access to opportunities for underrepresented groups.  The lawsuit claims loss of employment opportunity due to race and is backed by Rupert Lowe, a Restore Britain MP, who calls the scheme "vile anti-white racism." The case has raised concerns about potential legal challenges to diversity and inclusion initiatives in the UK.

articles.title: Odisha: Outrage after man carries sister's skeleton to bank to prove her death
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian man, Jitu Munda, carried his sister's skeletal remains to a bank in Odisha state after failing to withdraw her savings.  Munda claimed he was frustrated by repeated requests for proof of death and the bank's insistence on legally required documents. The bank denied asking for this, stating that the incident stemmed from a lack of awareness about procedures and that the money has since been handed over to the legal heirs. Suresh Pujari, Odisha's Revenue Minister, stated the case is under investigation and action will be taken against the branch manager.

articles.title: Microsoft removes Israeli names for occupied West Bank - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Microsoft has updated its digital maps to include Palestinian geographical names in accordance with international law. The changes, implemented following advocacy by the Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media (7amleh), replaced Israeli designations like "Judea and Samaria" with "West Bank."  The move is seen as a necessary correction by 7amleh, urging tech companies to comply with international law and avoid erasing Palestinian geography from digital platforms.

articles.title: Police declare attack in north London a terrorist incident after two Jewish men stabbed – latest updates | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police have declared the stabbing of two Jewish men in Golders Green, north London, a terrorist incident. The attack is being investigated as potentially targeting the Jewish community.  Prime Minister Keir Starmer has called a Cobra meeting to address the incident and vowed to tackle antisemitism. The Metropolitan Police are working with security services to investigate the motive behind the attack.

articles.title: Global forest loss slows but El Niño fires could threaten progress
articles.rephrased_article: Global forest loss slowed in 2025, with an estimated 43,000 sq km (17,000 sq miles) lost globally. This decline is attributed to efforts by countries like Brazil to curb deforestation and cooler La Niña conditions that helped mitigate fires. However, scientists warn that tropical forests are still disappearing at a faster rate than a decade ago and face increased threats from climate change and the upcoming El Niño weather pattern. The World Resources Institute and the University of Maryland's analysis suggests that while progress is being made, urgent action is needed to manage fire more effectively and protect these vital ecosystems.

articles.title: 'I really didn't know what was going on': JD Vance recalls White House dinner security breach - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vice President JD Vance recounted chaotic moments at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner after a suspected armed man attempted to breach security and target President Donald Trump.  Vance described hearing unclear noises, seeing people ducking under tables, and being instructed by a security officer to evacuate. The suspect, Cole Allen, was apprehended by security personnel after attempting to rush a Secret Service checkpoint. A Secret Service officer sustained an injury during the confrontation but is expected to recover.

articles.title: FOIP at 10: Bridging the Indo-Pacific and the Middle East | Opinions | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Japan is adapting its Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) strategy to address evolving security, economic, and development challenges in the region.  The country has strengthened cooperation with partners across the Middle East on issues like maritime security and supply chain resilience, while emphasizing the importance of a free and open international order based on the rule of law. Japan will continue its commitment to diplomacy, capacity building, and sustainable development initiatives as part of its evolving FOIP framework.  These efforts aim to promote regional stability and shared prosperity.

articles.title: Iran war, jet fuel concerns cloud airlines' summer holiday plans - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: European airlines are facing challenges from rising jet fuel prices caused by the US-Israel war on Iran, which could disrupt summer holiday travel.  The International Air Transport Association (IATA) head, Willie Walsh, warns of potential fuel shortages in Asia and Europe, while Ryanair CEO Michael O’Leary downplays concerns about supply disruptions. However, airlines like easyJet and tour operator TU have reported drops in forward bookings and issued profit warnings. Despite the challenges, some airlines, such as Finnair, are seeing increased demand for Asian flights.

articles.title: King Charles agrees with me on Iran nuclear weapon ban, claims Trump | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump claimed King Charles III agrees with him that Iran should not acquire nuclear weapons, a statement likely to cause embarrassment to royal aides.  Trump made this claim during a White House state dinner honoring the king and his wife, Camilla. The US president's comments were met with mixed reactions, including criticism from Ed Davey, the Liberal Democrat leader in the UK who called for the visit to be canceled. Despite Trump's claims, Charles III has maintained a neutral stance on political matters.

articles.title: France investigates reappearance of website tied to Pelicot crimes
articles.rephrased_article: French prosecutors have launched an investigation into the reappearance of a website, Cocoland.cc, which resembles the former platform Coco.gg, linked to the crimes of Dominique Pelicot, who was convicted of drugging and raping his wife Gisèle for over a decade.  The Paris prosecutor's office confirmed that an investigation has been opened into Cocoland for "disseminating violent, pornographic, or offensive messages accessible to minors." The website's owner denied any connection to the original Coco platform while high commissioner for childhood in France, Sarah El Haïry, expressed concern over the reappearance of such platforms and their exploitation of children.

articles.title: Who is Amy Beck? Noah Beck’s mother suspended after TikTok video resurfaces amid Haley Beck controversy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Amy Beck, a second-grade teacher in Arizona, has been placed on paid administrative leave from her job at Coyote Hills Elementary School after an old TikTok video featuring her and her son Noah Beck resurfaced online. The video, which features the pair lip-syncing to lyrics from "King's Dead" by Jay Rock, sparked controversy due to a gesture made by Noah Beck, leading to concerns about his mother's suitability for her position as a teacher.  The Peoria Unified School District is reviewing the situation and has stated there is no immediate risk to students.

articles.title: Madagascar detains French ex-serviceman over alleged destabilisation plot | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Madagascar has detained a French ex-serviceman, Guy Baret, and expelled a French embassy agent over alleged plots to destabilize the country. Deputy Prosecutor Nomenarinera Mihamintsoa Ramanantsoa said the suspects face charges including spreading false information, sabotaging infrastructure, and harboring wanted individuals. The Malagasy government has accused Colonel Patrick Rakotomamonjy and other accomplices of planning actions initially set for April 18th. France condemned the expulsion of its diplomat, calling the accusations "unfounded" and "incomprehensible."

articles.title: 6 terrorists killed as attack on Bannu police post thwarted - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bannu police successfully repelled a major attack on the Mazanga police post early Wednesday, killing at least six terrorists.  The incident involved an intense exchange of fire that resulted in the death of one terrorist and the recovery of weapons and equipment from the site. Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Inspector General (IG) Zulfiqar Hameed praised the Bannu Police, while Bannu Regional Police Officer (RPO) Sajjad Khan reaffirmed their commitment to combating terrorism.  The attack follows a series of security incidents in Bannu, including abductions and attacks on civilians and police personnel.

articles.title: Family of ailing Iranian Nobel laureate say keeping her in jail is a death sentence | Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The family of Narges Mohammadi, the jailed Iranian Nobel laureate, is expressing grave concern for her health after a suspected heart attack and significant weight loss.  Mohammadi, who was awarded the 2023 Nobel peace prize while in prison, has been re-arrested and held in Zanjan central prison. Her legal team is seeking a medical suspension of her sentence due to persistent chest pain, loss of consciousness, and extreme weight loss. Cardiology specialists have warned that keeping Mohammadi in the inadequate facilities of Zanjan poses an immediate danger to her life.  Her family and supporters are calling for her release and demanding action from the international community.

articles.title: Whale carried by barge out of German waters after weeks stranded on coast
articles.rephrased_article: Till Backhaus, the environment minister in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, and two German entrepreneurs funded a barge operation to transport a stranded humpback whale out of German waters. The whale was successfully moved into the barge on Tuesday and is expected to be released into the North Sea within two days. Despite initial skepticism from marine experts who believe the whale has little chance of survival, those involved in the rescue mission expressed joy at its success. Wildlife groups remain pessimistic about the whale's long-term prospects once released.

articles.title: 4 am fury, 24/7 gridlock: Trump takes world into long, hot Hormuz summer - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has directed US aides to prepare for a prolonged naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, potentially lasting months. The blockade aims to choke Iran’s oil exports and force concessions without triggering a wider regional war.  While shipping traffic through Hormuz has dropped significantly, impacting global energy flows and causing gasoline prices to surge in the US, the administration insists the strategy is working. However, critics argue that the indefinite blockade lacks an exit strategy and clarity on success, potentially leading to paralysis.

articles.title: What does Chornobyl look like 40 years later? | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Chornobyl exclusion zone remains radioactive, shaped by both the 1986 disaster and ongoing war. The area is home to deserted cities, returning wildlife, and rising military risk, raising concerns about nuclear danger and the future of the region.

articles.title: President Zardari invites investment in 'priority sectors' on China visit - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari invited Chinese investment into "priority sectors" such as alternative energy sources during a visit to China.  The president met with the CEO of Hangzhou Jinjiang Group, Wang Jian, in Sanya and discussed potential partnerships in areas like water treatment, electric vehicle battery systems, and alternate energy. President Zardari assured the company of support for foreign investment in the province and highlighted Pakistan's efforts to attract foreign investment.

articles.title: Britain to create joint naval force with nine European countries as ‘complement’ to Nato | Royal Navy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Britain has agreed to create a unified naval force with nine European countries to deter future Russian threats. Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, the head of the Royal Navy, announced this decision during a speech, stating that Russia remains the gravest threat to national security despite ongoing Middle East tensions. The Joint Expeditionary Force (Jef) will include the Netherlands, all five Nordic and the three Baltic states, with Britain as its largest military member. The force aims to train and prepare together, with the capability to fight immediately if required.

articles.title: New images show suspect taking selfies before Washington press dinner shooting
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, the man accused of shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, is being held in custody pending trial.  New images show Allen posing with weapons in his hotel room before the attack, according to a memorandum filed by prosecutors. The photos, along with details of his activities leading up to the incident, were submitted as part of their motion to keep him detained. Prosecutors allege that Allen researched live coverage of the event and targeted President Donald Trump and other officials.  The suspect faces life in prison if found guilty on charges including attempted assassination.

articles.title: Trump halts speech in awkward moment to praise Rory McIlroy’s Masters win at White House dinner | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump interrupted his state dinner with King Charles III and Queen Camilla to praise Rory McIlroy, who had recently won the Masters Tournament.  Trump acknowledged McIlroy's "unconquerable courage" and congratulated him, prompting a brief moment of personal interaction in the formal setting before returning to the planned speech. Despite Trump's public enthusiasm for McIlroy playing at his Doral course, Rory McIlroy will not be competing in the upcoming Cadillac Championship at Trump National Doral.

articles.title: Man carries deceased sister into Indian bank amid paperwork difficulty | Banks | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A man in India is carrying his deceased sister into a bank to resolve paperwork issues. The incident occurred at the Indian branch of the bank.

articles.title: Bangladesh measles outbreak kills over 220 children since March - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh has experienced a severe measles outbreak, with 227 child deaths reported since March and nearly 35,000 suspected cases. The hardest hit areas are in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, home to Indigenous communities who often lack access to vaccination programs due to poverty and limited transportation options. The World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF Bangladesh are working with local authorities to provide vaccinations and address the outbreak.

articles.title: Veteran goalkeeper, 70, to return to pitch for official game in Spain | Spain | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Angel Mateos González, a 70-year-old former miner and goalkeeper, is set to play in goal for CD Colunga in a fifth-tier match this Sunday. The team will be celebrating his lifelong dedication to football by allowing him to participate despite his advanced age.  Mateos has been helping out the team's keepers all season and will reportedly play either the full game or the first half, depending on how he feels during training. CD Colunga emphasized that Mateos’ participation is about recognizing a man who embodies their values of passion, dedication, and commitment to the sport, rather than his age.

articles.title: Madagascar detains French national over alleged plot to stir unrest
articles.rephrased_article: Madagascar authorities have detained a former French serviceman on charges of conspiracy and sabotage, alleging he was part of a plot to destabilize the country. The Malagasy prosecutor also charged other accomplices, including a Malagasy army officer, with spreading false information and harboring wanted individuals.  France's foreign ministry has rejected accusations of destabilization and called the expulsion of its diplomat "unfounded."

articles.title: SRM-AP launches AI-integrated PG programmes in Economics, Psychology - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ch. Satish Kumar, Vice-Chancellor of SRM University-AP, highlighted the importance of integrating domain knowledge with emerging technologies in postgraduate education.  At the launch of AI-integrated M.Sc. Economics and M.Sc. Psychology programs by Easwari School of Liberal Arts (ESLA), he emphasized that students must be equipped to apply AI tools for analysis, prediction, and decision-making. This integration prepares students for real-world challenges and future uncertainties.

articles.title: Iran ‘choking like a stuffed pig’: Trump digs in on Hormuz blockade; Tehran warns ‘unprecedented action’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated that the US will maintain its naval blockade on Iran until Tehran agrees to a deal addressing Washington's concerns about its nuclear program.  The president believes the blockade is more effective than direct military action, but US Central Command has drawn up plans for strikes targeting Iranian infrastructure if negotiations fail. Trump declined to discuss operational details but indicated that the pressure campaign is already impacting Iran's oil exports.

articles.title: A 48-team World Cup is Panini sticker collectors’ biggest challenge yet | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Panini, the Italian company behind the popular football sticker collection, has released its biggest-ever World Cup album with 980 unique stickers. The 112-page album, available from Thursday, will cost collectors over £1,000 to complete, as each player requires multiple packets of seven stickers at £1.25 each.  Former England players David James, John Barnes and Gary Cahill participated in the launch event at Wembley Stadium, reminiscing about their childhood sticker-collecting days.

articles.title: 2 Jewish men stabbed in 'terrorist' attack in London - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III, Prime Minister Keir Starmer, and London mayor Sadiq Khan condemned the “appalling” stabbing of two Jewish men in Golders Green, London, which police declared a terrorist incident. The attack followed a series of arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in north London.  The suspect, a 45-year-old man with a history of violence and mental health issues, was arrested after attempting to stab members of the public. Metropolitan police commissioner Mark Rowley stated that this attack was an attack on all London’s communities. The incident prompted condemnation from Israel's foreign ministry and calls for increased security measures by Jewish community leaders.

articles.title: Ukraine asks Israel to seize vessel it claims is carrying grain stolen by Russia | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine has requested Israel to seize a vessel, the Panormitis, claiming it is carrying stolen grain from Russian-occupied territories.  Zelenskyy stated that the vessel arrived in Haifa and Ukraine's prosecutor general, Kravchenko, urged Israel to conduct a search and seizure of the cargo documentation. Saar, the Israeli foreign minister, refuted these claims, accusing Ukraine of "Twitter diplomacy" and demanding evidence. The dispute has strained relations between the two countries, with Israel maintaining its diplomatic efforts to maintain ties with both Russia and Ukraine.

articles.title: Ex-FBI director James Comey surrenders over charge of threatening Trump's life in Instagram post
articles.rephrased_article: James Comey, former FBI Director, surrendered to authorities on Wednesday to face a charge alleging that an Instagram post he shared in May 2025 posed a threat to President Donald Trump's life. The image contained the phrase "86 47", which prosecutors allege is slang for "get rid of" and encourages violence against the president.  Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that the charges were not politically motivated, emphasizing the seriousness of threatening the president. Comey denies any wrongdoing, claiming he did not understand the meaning of the numbers. The case marks the second time the justice department has brought criminal charges against Comey, a longtime critic of Trump.

articles.title: Fresh wave of lawsuits filed against OpenAI by Tumbler Ridge victims
articles.rephrased_article: OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, are facing seven lawsuits filed by families of victims in the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting. The lawsuits allege negligence and aiding and abetting the attack by failing to alert law enforcement about the shooter's troubling ChatGPT activity. OpenAI claims it has a zero-tolerance policy for violence and strengthened its safeguards following the incident, while also denying allegations that it lied about banning the shooter from the platform.  The families are seeking trials by jury in each case.

articles.title: Hot weather and hungry datacentres lift Australia’s energy demand to record highs but batteries quell prices | Renewable energy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Australia’s Energy Market Operator (Aemo) reported record electricity demand in the first quarter of 2026, driven by datacenter growth and warmer conditions.  Demand reached 25GW, an increase of 1.2% year-on-year, with rooftop solar offsetting some of the grid's increased demand. Violette Mouchaileh, Aemo’s executive general manager of policy, noted that large-scale batteries significantly contributed to moderating prices and reducing reliance on gas during peak times.  Dr Dylan McConnell, an energy systems researcher at the University of New South Wales, highlighted the positive impact of battery technology in the energy transition.

articles.title: Vijay Kedia-backed Websol Energy shares jump 45% in six days. What's driving the rally? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Websol Energy's stock price surged 155% in less than two months, reaching Rs 128.31 per share after reporting strong Q4 earnings with a net profit of Rs 125 crore and revenue of Rs 401 crore.  The company attributed its success to favorable market conditions for solar manufacturing, including government policies and increasing domestic demand. Vijay Kedia, a prominent investor, recently acquired shares of the company, further boosting its stock price.

articles.title: Treasure alert: 63 Anglo-Saxon coins uncovered in Worcestershire linked to the Viking age | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A group of metal-detecting enthusiasts in Bickmarsh, Worcestershire, unearthed a cache of 63 early medieval Anglo-Saxon coins. Worcestershire Archaeology completed an extensive survey and excavation of the site, revealing that most of the coins were minted during King Burgred's reign (852-874). Historians believe these coins were intentionally buried to protect them from Viking invaders. The discovery is considered unprecedented as it provides evidence for money circulation within a defined area of England during the Anglo-Saxon period.

articles.title: ‘Exporters in Karnataka and other States will benefit from IMEC amid West Asia crisis’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kotraswamy M., Commissioner of Central Tax, Bengaluru North, observed that the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) is gaining momentum as an alternative to choke points like the Suez Canal and Strait of Hormuz, benefiting Indian exporters.  He highlighted GST relief measures such as zero-rated supplies and streamlined refund mechanisms, which are boosting export liquidity and easing working capital pressures. Prince Mehra, Deputy Manager at EXIM Bank, noted that Karnataka is a top 4 exporter in India, contributing significantly to the country's merchandise exports. He emphasized Karnataka's strong growth potential and its ranking in the NITI Aayog Export Preparedness Index.

articles.title: Minister calls for national consensus on ensuring water security - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
