articles.rephrased_article: The death toll from a train collision near Jakarta has risen to 14 with 84 injured, according to PT KAI, the state railway firm. The accident occurred late Monday in Bekasi, where a long-distance train collided with a stationary commuter train.  Mohammad Syafii, head of Indonesia's search and rescue agency, said the rescue effort was ongoing and involved personnel with specialized skills to extricate survivors from the mangled carriages. Sufmi Dasco Ahmad, an Indonesian deputy house speaker, stated that the toll could continue to rise as rescuers work to free trapped victims.

articles.title: Vedanta demerger can create value in the long term - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Analysts believe investors should hold onto Vedanta stock for the long term, as demerger benefits will increase shareholder value. The demerger is expected to separate the company into five listed entities: Vedanta Aluminium, Vedanta Power, Vedanta Oil & Gas, Vedanta Iron & Steel, and a residual Vedanta.  The remaining Vedanta entity will retain zinc, copper, and other base-metal businesses. Axis Securities estimates that the combined valuation of the demerged entities will rise by 14% to ₹650 per share after the demerger. The stock is expected to adjust for the demerger on April 30th and trade in the range of around ₹300-325 per share.

articles.title: Russia backs Iran as peace efforts with US remain stalled - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Vladimir Putin and Abbas Araghchi, Iran's top diplomat, met in St. Petersburg to discuss the stalled peace talks between the US and Iran.  Araghchi blamed US demands for the failure of negotiations, while President Trump held a meeting with his security advisors to discuss the Iranian proposal.  The White House declined to comment on the specifics of the Iranian proposal but emphasized that any deal must serve American interests and prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons.  Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, stated that Iran is serious about reaching an agreement but it must prevent a nuclear weapon development. The US and Iran clashed at the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) review conference in New York City over Tehran's nuclear program.

articles.title: Watch: Trump, Melania host King Charles, Camilla in Washington, showcase beehives in White House garden - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III and Queen Camilla began their four-day state visit to the United States with a cordial welcome at the White House.  They were greeted by President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump, who hosted them for tea, cakes, and a tour of the White House grounds. The royal couple also met with prominent figures like Olympic diver Tom Daley and US House Speaker Mike Johnson. While tensions exist between the two countries over the US stance on Iran, the visit aims to reaffirm historic ties.

articles.title: Kerala BDS student death: Statewide hartal by Dalit, Adivasi groups disrupts life - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dalit and Adivasi activists in Kerala blocked traffic, disrupted public transportation, and closed shops across several districts on Tuesday demanding justice for the death of Nithin Raj, a BDS student allegedly due to caste discrimination. Protesters, who included scores of students and community members, demanded action against those responsible and free passage for passengers traveling to hospitals.

articles.title: Gunmen kill at least 29 in Nigeria’s northeast Adamawa State | ISIL/ISIS News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gunmen killed at least 29 people in Guyaku village, Adamawa State, Nigeria, in an attack that lasted several hours.  The ISIL (ISIS) group claimed responsibility for the attack on the Telegram messaging app. Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri of Adamawa State visited the village and pledged to support security operations against the perpetrators. The attack occurred on the same day as a separate incident where armed attackers raided an orphanage in north-central Nigeria, abducting 23 children.

articles.title: Humanoid robots to become baggage handlers in Japan airport experiment | Japan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Japan Airlines and its partner, Japan Airlines GMO Internet Group, will introduce humanoid robots to help alleviate labor shortages at Tokyo's Haneda airport. The trial program begins in May and aims to lessen the burden on human employees as Japan faces a surge in tourism and an aging population.  The robots will move luggage and cargo on the tarmac, with certain safety tasks still handled by humans.

articles.title: Three years on, ₹13.43 crore project meant to augment water supply to Kondagattu hill shrine remains in cold storage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three years after the foundation stone was laid for a drinking water project at the Kondagattu hill shrine in Jagtial district, the project has not made any progress. The project, estimated to cost ₹13.43 crore, was intended to provide a permanent water supply for pilgrims and was conceived during the previous BRS government's tenure.

articles.title: Punjab power outages: SAD blames AAP government’s failure - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AAP government in Punjab claims to have addressed the ongoing power supply issues, while SAD blames the government for prolonged outages.  SAD leader Daljit Singh Cheema accused the AAP of mismanagement due to a lack of short-term power purchases and timely agreements with neighboring states.

articles.title: Ladakh groups seek meeting with Shah and steps to build trust - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ahead of Amit Shah, the Union Home Minister,’s visit to Ladakh, the Leh Apex Body (LAB) urged for a trust-building exercise and requested a meeting with him during his two-day tour. The LAB, composed of socio-political-religious organizations, also called for the convening of a high-powered committee, chaired by Shah, which includes members from the LAB and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA).

articles.title: Internal reservation: Nomadic and micro communities to question latest matrix in Karnataka HIgh Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Federation of Untouchable Nomadic Communities of Karnataka members have decided to continue their legal fight for a separate category in internal reservation, challenging the latest Cabinet decision. The group will file additional petitions in the High Court of Karnataka, following their loss of an opportunity for a separate category.  The group plans to hold a convention in Bengaluru during the last week of May to present their demands.

articles.title: Proposal to increase retirement age of judicial officers in Tamil Nadu under consideration: Chief Justice - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Madras High Court Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari stated that a proposal to increase the age of superannuation for judicial officers in Tamil Nadu from 60 to 61 or 62 is under consideration and a positive decision is expected. The proposal was discussed during a hearing of a writ petition filed by four judicial officers who are nearing retirement.

articles.title: Trading losses, low treasury income hurt banks in Q4 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several Indian banks reported treasury losses and income dips in the latest quarter, primarily due to rising interest rates and foreign exchange market restrictions.  Axis Bank, AU Small Finance Bank, UCO Bank, and others suffered mark-to-market losses on their bond holdings. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) rejected requests for amortizing these losses, forcing banks to recognize them fully in the fourth quarter. While experts anticipate a near-term slowdown in loan growth due to cautious lending practices, business optimism remains subdued amidst geopolitical uncertainties and economic concerns.

articles.title: Amid fresh unrest, Home Secretary reviews Manipur security situation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan reviewed the security situation in Manipur on Monday, April 27, 2026, amid ongoing unrest and killings. The meeting addressed issues such as the withdrawal of Central armed police forces (CAPFs) for West Bengal elections, frequent disruptions and blockades by women groups, and new areas of conflict between Kuki and Naga communities.  Around 36,000 security forces, including Assam Rifles, are deployed in Manipur since 2023.

articles.title: US supreme court hears whether smartphone location data warrants infringe users’ privacy | Technology | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court is hearing arguments in the case of Chatrie v. United States, which concerns whether sweeping warrants for smartphone location data violate privacy rights and the Constitution.  Justice Brett Kavanaugh, Justice Sonia Sotomayor, and other justices expressed concern about the potential implications of these warrants on individual privacy. The case centers around Okello Chatrie, whose phone location data was used to track him down after he robbed a bank, but his lawyers argue it should not have been admissible in court.  The government argues that individuals have no reasonable expectation of privacy in their movements while using a smartphone.

articles.title: Global Market Today: Asian shares hold near eight-week high - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The MSCI Asia Pacific Index remained relatively unchanged on Tuesday, mirroring the market's response to the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran.  Global crude benchmark Brent oil prices dipped slightly, while the yen held steady against the dollar. Investors are now focusing on earnings reports from major tech companies like Alphabet Inc., Microsoft Corp., Amazon.com Inc., and Meta Platforms Inc. which could influence global equities. Despite geopolitical tensions, market momentum remains strong, with positive earnings revisions driving investor confidence.  The US is currently discussing Iran's latest proposal for an interim deal, but maintains its red lines on any nuclear weapon acquisition.

articles.title: Hot Westerly winds set to increase temperatures from May 1 in city - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, predicts a slight increase in temperatures across Chennai city and coastal areas starting May 1st due to the arrival of Westerly winds from the hot Rayalaseema region.  Interior areas, already experiencing above-normal temperatures, are expected to see further increases. Light to moderate rain is forecast over isolated places until May 2nd, potentially bringing down temperatures.

articles.title: Man pleads guilty to role in 2002 murder of Run-DMC’s Jam Master Jay | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jam Master Jay, a renowned Run-DMC DJ, was fatally shot in his studio in 2002.  After nearly two decades of investigation, Jason Mizell's murder has been solved with the guilty plea of Jam Master Jay accomplice, Bryant. Bryant admitted to helping others gain entry to the studio where the shooting occurred and acknowledged knowing a gun would be used. The case remains complex as other suspects, Karl Jordan Jr. and Ronald Washington, were previously convicted but later had their convictions challenged.  No sentencing date has been set for Bryant who faces 15 to 20 years in prison.

articles.title: Markets rise as Iran crisis stays in limbo - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Asian markets saw gains on Monday, with India's Nifty 50 and S&P BSE Sensex both rising by 0.8%.  Reliance Industries and Sun Pharmaceuticals were among the top gainers, fueled by global market trends. The India VIX volatility index fell, indicating easing near-term risk expectations. Foreign portfolio investors sold shares worth a net '1,151.48 crore on Monday, while domestic institutional investors bought shares worth '4,123.92 crore.

articles.title: Indiramma housing programme will be accelerated; more powers to Collectors, says Ponguleti - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy, the Revenue and Housing Minister, announced a series of measures to expedite the Indiramma Housing Scheme. These include decentralizing powers to District Collectors and appointing special officers for each erstwhile district.  The Minister also directed weekly reviews by Collectors to address local issues and prevent bottlenecks.

articles.title: Nathan Chasing Horse sentenced to life in prison for sexual assault | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nathan Chasing Horse, a former actor known for his role in "Dances With Wolves," was sentenced to life in prison for sexually assaulting Indigenous women and girls. A Nevada jury found him guilty of 13 charges, including sexual assault against three women who accused him of exploiting his position as a spiritual leader. The sentencing comes after years of legal proceedings and reverberations across Indian Country.  The British Columbia Prosecution Service is still assessing next steps regarding pending charges in Canada, while the Tsuut’ina Nation police service in Alberta has an outstanding warrant for Chasing Horse's arrest.

articles.title: Axis Bank slips despite 'Buys' as provisions cast a shadow - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Axis Bank shares closed at 1,324.2 on Monday, with analysts predicting a significant upside in the coming year. Bloomberg consensus suggests an average potential gain of 19.5%, and 94% of analysts covering the bank have a "Buy" rating.  While loan growth was strong, elevated provisions related to geopolitical uncertainty weighed down performance. Several large brokers raised their targets on the stock following the results.

articles.title: M.P. Assembly passes resolution to implement women’s reservation after delimitation amid uproar by Opposition - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madhya Pradesh Assembly passed a resolution to implement women's reservation following the delimitation exercise, despite opposition from the Congress.  Chief Minister Mohan Yadav proposed the resolution, urging immediate implementation after the completion of the delimitation process. The resolution was met with resistance from the Opposition, who argued that the government's actions contradicted its words and called for an immediate enforcement of the Women's Reservation Act.

articles.title: Baby on board: US woman gives birth on Delta flight | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ashley Blair unexpectedly went into labor during a Delta flight from Atlanta to Portland on Friday night. Tina Fritz and Caarin Powell, emergency medical technicians, assisted the mother and helped deliver her baby girl, who weighed five and a half pounds. The plane landed shortly after the birth, and both mother and child were transported to a local hospital for observation.  The incident was praised by Delta Airlines, which thanked its crew and volunteers for their quick response.

articles.title: REITs, InvITs beat equities and debt in a six-year span - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty REIT-InvIT index has outperformed both equities and fixed income over the long term, delivering an annualized return of 12% between July 2019 and March 2026.  This performance is attributed to the low correlation of REITs and InvITs to other asset classes, as well as their predictable cash flows. The investor base in these instruments has expanded significantly since 2019, with popular examples including Embassy Office Parks REIT, Brookfield India Real Estate Trust, and Nexus Select Trust.  The revised tax framework treats capital gains on REIT and InvIT units similarly to equity investments.

articles.title: ‘Basava Sri’ award for H.D. Deve Gowda - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.D. Deve Gowda, former Prime Minister, expressed concern over societal decline and a decrease in pro-people movements during a letter thanking the Basava Samiti for awarding him with the 'Basava Sri' award. He attributed this to cynicism among knowledgeable individuals and called for adopting the philosophies of Allama, action of Basavanna, and anger of Ambigara Chowdaiah to address these issues.

articles.title: What does the US dinner shooting mean for Trump? | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gunshots erupted at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, disrupting the event and raising questions about President Donald Trump's security. The suspect has been identified as a man who was apprehended by authorities.  Trump offered a statement following the incident but did not provide details on his response to the situation.

articles.title: Afghanistan says Pakistani strikes kill seven and wound 85 in first attack since peace talks | Afghanistan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and Afghanistan exchanged fire on Monday, with mortars and missiles striking a university and civilian homes in Afghanistan, killing seven people and injuring at least 85.  The attack occurred despite recent peace talks mediated by China.  Pakistan denies targeting the university or civilians, accusing Afghanistan of harboring militants. The violence highlights the fragile nature of peace efforts between the two nations.

articles.title: Firms postpone D-Street debut as uncertainty clouds market outlook - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The uncertainty in India's IPO market is expected to persist for the next two to three months, with institutional investors delaying companies due to valuation discrepancies. Prime Database data reveals a robust pipeline of 146 companies seeking approval to raise ₹2.11 lakh crore, but many are awaiting final approvals.  Sebi has granted temporary extensions on IPO approvals to ease fundraising pressures, allowing companies with December quarter data to launch their IPOs by June.

articles.title: Problems in land transactions continue to persist a year after passage of Bhu Bharati Act - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A year after the enactment of Telangana Bhu Bharati (Record of Rights) Act, 2025, farmers continue to face challenges in securing land rights.  The recent suicide of farmer Madhav Rao in Sangareddy district highlights these difficulties, as he reportedly took his life due to pressure from family members following a land transfer through a "plain paper transaction" without their knowledge.

articles.title: Iran war live: Trump reviews peace plan; UN calls for Hormuz to reopen | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's national security team is reviewing an Iranian peace plan to end the war in the Strait of Hormuz and reopen the strait. Abbas Araghchi, Iran’s Foreign Minister, met with Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg and said Tehran is considering a US request to restart nuclear talks. The UN chief warned that the standoff risks triggering a global food emergency.

articles.title: ‘Shortcomings and failures’ could sink Aukus nuclear submarines plan, UK inquiry warns | Aukus | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A House of Commons defense committee report has found cracks in the UK's funding for the Aukus agreement, highlighting a threat to Australia's security. The report states that UK shipbuilding is underfunded and its submarine availability is critically low, as evidenced by the rapid recall of HMS Anson from Australia due to the war in the Gulf.  The committee also criticized a lack of political leadership in promoting Aukus and called for increased funding and priority for the program. While Australia will purchase Virginia-class submarines from the US to fill the capability gap, the report highlighted potential delays and challenges with both programs.

articles.title: FBI affidavit quotes White House press dinner shooting suspect expressing rage at ‘a pedophile, rapist and traitor’ – US politics live | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An FBI affidavit quotes Cole Allen's manifesto, which states he planned to assassinate President Trump and describes him as a "pedophile, rapist, and traitor."  Allen sent the manifesto to family and friends before attempting to charge into the White House correspondents' dinner. The affidavit accuses Allen of intending to kill the president. King Charles and Queen Camilla met with Donald Trump at the White House.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article reports a potential threat to the President and a possible act of violence, warranting concern.

articles.title: Mukunda Reddy takes charge as I&PR Special Commissioner - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Mukunda Reddy assumed the role of Special Commissioner and Ex-officio Secretary of the State Information and Public Relations Department, succeeding C.H. Priyanka.  He emphasized the importance of disseminating government welfare programs to the public, urging officials to follow directives set by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and Minister for Revenue, Housing, Information and Public Relations Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy. The event was attended by senior officials from the department.

articles.title: Will the Iran war push millions back into poverty? | TV Shows | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations warns that the ongoing US-Israel conflict with Iran could push as many as 32.5 million people worldwide into poverty due to rising fuel and food costs, job losses, and shrinking remittances.  This economic fallout is particularly severe for countries in the Global South, which rely heavily on imports from the Gulf region. The conflict is exacerbating existing economic vulnerabilities and straining government resources.

articles.title: UK has wealthy Europe’s ‘third-highest’ rate of young adults not in work or study | Work & careers | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Resolution Foundation thinktank has warned that Britain faces a youth jobs crisis, with the Neet rate for 18- to 24-year-olds at its highest level in over a decade.  The report attributes the rise to rising ill-health among young people, weak vocational education, a hands-off benefits system, and a deteriorating jobs market. Lindsay Judge, research director at the thinktank, suggests that investing in youth mental health support and vocational education is crucial for addressing the issue. The government has pledged to create a million opportunities for young people through its youth guarantee program and provide tailored employment support for those with disabilities.

articles.title: Residents urge BMRCL to include ‘Bilekahalli’ in IIMB metro station name on Bengaluru’s Pink Line metro - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents in south Bengaluru have written to Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), urging them to rename the upcoming “IIMB” metro station on the Pink Line as “IIMB–Bilekahalli” to recognize the locality’s identity.  The residents argue that naming the station solely after an institution risks overlooking the cultural context of the area and propose a name that balances modern infrastructure with local heritage. While BMRCL has received the letter, they confirmed that renaming a metro station involves a detailed procedure and requires approval from both state and central governments. This issue reflects a larger trend in Bengaluru where renaming metro stations is becoming increasingly contentious.

articles.title: Sindh’s second largest hospital lacks essential services, health secretary told - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh’s second largest tertiary care hospital, Liaquat University Hospital (LUH) in Hyderabad, faces significant issues with malfunctioning medical equipment and inadequate facilities.  A report submitted to the health secretary highlights 45 machines, including MRI, CT Scan, X-ray, and anesthesia units, that are dysfunctional due to insufficient maintenance funding. The report also notes deficiencies in sanitation, spatial measures, and essential medical equipment across various wards, impacting patient care.  The hospital's cardiology department faces a shortage of surgeons and limited services due to financial constraints.

articles.title: Heat, hype, highs: Drug use surges in England during heatwaves, sports events and Eurovision nights - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A large-scale wastewater study in England found that drug consumption, particularly cocaine and ketamine, increased significantly during heatwaves, bank holidays, major events like the Eurovision Song Contest, and World Cup matches. Researchers analyzed over 1,700 samples from 15 treatment plants across England in 2022, revealing consistent weekly and seasonal trends. The study also highlighted the dangers of mixing substances, especially cocaine with alcohol, which can create harmful compounds in the body.  These findings can help authorities anticipate periods of increased drug use and related emergencies.

articles.title: Suspected pirates steer cargo vessel towards Somalia | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pirates are suspected of hijacking a cargo vessel, the Sward, off the coast of Somalia. The ship was carrying cement from Suez, Egypt, to Mombasa, Kenya, and had 15 crew members on board, including two Indians and 13 Syrians. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that the pirates boarded the ship six nautical miles northeast of Garacad and are currently taking it toward the Somali coastline. The Puntland Maritime Police Force has been notified of the hijacking.

articles.title: First teenage suicide linked to domestic abuse recorded in England and Wales | Domestic violence | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Domestic Homicide Project reports that suicides after domestic abuse have surpassed homicides for the third year in a row, with 347 deaths last year.  Louisa Rolfe, assistant police commissioner in the Metropolitan police, attributes the rise to "impact of pornography" and "toxic influencers," which she believes normalize domestic abuse. Frank Mullane, CEO of Advocacy After Fatal Domestic Abuse, calls for a separate offense for suicide after domestic violence to raise awareness. He also urges police to preserve the scene of suicides and treat them as potential homicides, emphasizing the need for more professional curiosity in unexplained deaths.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights a concerning trend of domestic abuse leading to teenage suicides, which is a serious public health issue.

articles.title: Bengaluru to host pan-India IIT summit on May 16 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Government of Karnataka, in partnership with the Pan-IIT Alumni India Association, will host the Pan-IIT Bangalore Summit 2026 on May 16th. The conference, themed around "Technology Sovereignty," aims to bring together 2,000 participants from across 23 IITs and other stakeholders like policy makers, technology leaders, startup founders, and investors.  The summit will feature high-level plenaries, panels, and tracks on AI, defense, semiconductors, energy, mobility, and healthcare, as well as a pitch-a-thon for startups and a hackathon to tackle real-world challenges. The event is intended to foster collaboration between academia, industry, and government to drive India's technological advancement.

articles.title: Iran war disrupts the circuit board supply chain, raises costs for tech firms - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The conflict in the Middle East has disrupted supplies of crucial raw materials for printed circuit boards (PCBs), leading to price increases and supply chain disruptions. SABIC, a major supplier of high-purity PPE resin, has been unable to resume output at its Jubail petrochemical complex, severely impacting global PCB availability.  The conflict has also exacerbated existing shortages of glass fiber and copper foil, driving up prices for these materials. This disruption is a significant blow to electronics manufacturers already facing soaring memory chip costs.

articles.title: Pashabiceps Donation: Counter-Strike legend pashaBiceps donates $21K to Poland Cancer Fighters stream after knife skin sale - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Retired Counter-Strike pro pashaBiceps sold a rare knife skin from the game for over $21,000 and donated all proceeds to the Cancer Fighters foundation in Poland. The money will support children battling cancer through a large ongoing charity streaming event in Poland.  The sale has garnered attention within the esports community for its impact on a worthy cause.

articles.title: Ceasefire at risk as Pakistan and Afghanistan report cross-border attacks | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and Afghanistan have resumed cross-border attacks, threatening fragile peace talks mediated by China.  Afghan authorities reported four deaths in Kunar province from Pakistani military strikes. Pakistan officials said at least three civilians were injured in South Waziristan. The resumption of violence follows a ceasefire agreed upon in March after weeks of deadly clashes.

articles.title: Half of England’s schools unfit due to leaks, mould and faulty toilets, poll finds | Schools | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Half of headteachers surveyed by the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) reported that parts of their schools are either unusable or unfit for purpose due to issues such as leaks, damp, mold, asbestos, and aging infrastructure.  Almost three-quarters of respondents said their school's toilet blocks were either closed or not fit for purpose, with almost two-fifths reporting similar problems with facilities reserved for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). The NAHT is calling on the government to fully fund essential capital expenditure across all state schools in England.  A Department for Education spokesperson stated that the government is committed to addressing the legacy of neglect in school buildings, including removing Raac and providing long-term investment to improve their condition.

articles.title: Woman found dead in decomposed state - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 34-year-old woman, Pooja Dutta, was found dead in her Adugodi residence on Monday after neighbors reported a foul odor.  Dutta, who worked for a private company, was discovered naked and in a decomposed state, raising suspicion of foul play. The police are investigating the circumstances surrounding her death, which may have occurred two to three days prior, and are examining evidence including an old company ID card and torn papers found in the house.  The investigation will focus on identifying the man who visited Dutta frequently and analyzing her recent call records and social circle.

articles.title: King Charles jets to US for four-day trip amid Iran conflict, media gala shooting - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles and Queen Camilla will embark on a four-day state visit to the United States, marking the 250th anniversary of US independence. The trip, which begins with a private meeting with President Donald Trump, includes an address to Congress and a dinner at the White House.  The visit has been overshadowed by political tensions between the two countries over the US-Israeli war on Iran, and the shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner just days prior. Despite these challenges, the trip is intended to strengthen the "special relationship" between the UK and the US, with a focus on shared history and values.

articles.title: Lewandowski set to leave Barcelona after four years as contract offer falls short of his ambitions | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Robert Lewandowski is expected to leave FC Barcelona at the end of his contract this summer. The striker has been offered a one-year renewal with reduced salary and a limited role, which he does not want.  Barcelona have identified Julian Alvarez as their priority target for a new forward. Juventus and AC Milan are also showing interest in Lewandowski, offering him a more prominent role at the highest level of European football. The striker is considering his options and will make a decision in the coming weeks.

articles.title: US press gala shooting suspect charged with attempting to kill Trump | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, was charged with attempting to assassinate Donald J Trump after allegedly shooting a US Secret Service agent at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.  Prosecutors say Allen had firearms including a semiautomatic pistol, a shotgun and three knives, and traveled from Los Angeles to Washington, D.C., before the attack.  The incident is being investigated as the third assassination attempt against Trump since 2024. Jeanine Pirro, US attorney for Washington, DC, stated that Allen's alleged manifesto targeted high-ranking administration officials. Todd Blanche, Acting Attorney General, said Allen arrived in Washington D.C. on April 24th and checked into the Washington Hilton hotel where the dinner was held.  Karoline Leavitt, White House spokeswoman, stated that Trump does not view the incident as a security failure.

articles.title: Trump picks former Republican congressman to be ambassador to Australia after long vacancy | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Brat, a former Republican member of the US House of Representatives, has been nominated by the White House to be the next ambassador to Australia.  Brat previously represented Virginia in Congress and served two terms before losing a close race to a Democrat in 2018. The post has been vacant for over a year and a half since former ambassador Caroline Kennedy left the position in November 2024.

articles.title: Government signs MoU with State Legal Services Authority to promote legal awareness and child protection in schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The State government and Telangana State Legal Services Authority (TSLSA) signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen legal literacy and child protection in schools. The initiative, implemented across 5,711 high schools, will include legal awareness sessions for students and teachers, awareness campaigns on child rights, and the establishment of legal literacy and child rights clubs.  The program also includes training for teachers, provision of legal aid and counselling services, and efforts to support school dropouts. The MoU is in effect for two years with a potential extension.

articles.title: King Charles jets to US for four-day trip amid Iran conflict, media gala shooting - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles and Queen Camilla will embark on a four-day state visit to the United States, marking the 250th anniversary of US independence. The trip, initially planned for months, has been overshadowed by political tensions between the two countries over the US-Israeli war on Iran and the shooting at the White House Correspondents’ dinner. President Donald Trump will host a private tea with the royals, and King Charles will address Congress. The visit also includes commemorations of 9/11 victims in New York and conservation work in Virginia. Despite recent easing of criticism from Trump, strained ties remain due to issues like the Falkland Islands dispute and the Jeffrey Epstein scandal.

articles.title: Who is Fred Liu? Evelyn Ha’s ex boyfriend backs Ben Pasternak’s claims and alleges past abuse details - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ben Pasternak, facing charges of strangulation and assault stemming from an alleged incident at a Manhattan hotel on March 31, 2026, has denied the accusations. Fred Liu, a former boyfriend of Evelyn Ha, who is also involved in the case, claims to have experienced similar events during his relationship with Ha.  Liu's public statement adds another layer to an already complex and sensitive situation as both sides continue to present their perspectives through legal processes.

articles.title: US Supreme Court reinstates Republican-favoured Texas electoral map | US Midterm Elections 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Supreme Court reinstated a redrawn Texas electoral map that could flip up to five Democratic-held House seats to Republicans, a decision that split along ideological lines. The ruling was met with criticism from civil rights advocates who argued the map weakens the political influence of racial minorities and is racially discriminatory.  This decision follows similar battles in Florida where Governor Ron DeSantis proposed a new congressional map aimed at flipping four Democratic-held House seats, which faces potential legal challenges.

articles.title: Gunmen kill at least 29 at football pitch in north-east Nigeria, governor says | Nigeria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gunmen killed at least 29 people in Adamawa state, Nigeria on Sunday, targeting a football pitch in the Guyaku community. Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, governor of Adamawa state, confirmed the attack and blamed it on Boko Haram militants.  The Islamic State’s West Africa Province (ISWAP) claimed responsibility for the attack, stating that they killed at least 25 people and burned a church. The governor vowed to intensify security operations to restore peace while Nigerian security forces rescued 15 kidnapped pupils in Kogi state.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale violence by militants is reported as routine.

articles.title: Mandelson and McSweeney: a partnership forged on winning and crushing the Labour left | Peter Mandelson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Morgan McSweeney will testify before the foreign affairs select committee about his relationship with Peter Mandelson, a former Labour cabinet minister who was appointed US ambassador despite concerns from some within the party.  The pair, who worked together in local politics and later founded Labour Together to regain control of the Labour party, had different political views but shared a mutual interest in destroying the left wing of the party and winning elections. Mandelson, known for his internationalism and social liberalism, was critical of Keir Starmer's leadership and policies, while McSweeney supported him as chief of staff.  Their relationship became strained after Mandelson’s appointment to the US ambassador position, which was ultimately secured by McSweeney. The two men have been described as having a close personal bond despite their political differences.

articles.title: 5.7-magnitude earthquake jolts Islamabad, parts of KP: PMD - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: An earthquake of 5.7 magnitude struck the Afghanistan-Tajikistan border region on Monday, causing tremors to be felt in Islamabad and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) reported the epicenter near Afghanistan's border with Tajikistan, while the United States Geological Survey (USGS) recorded a magnitude of 5.1. This tremor follows previous earthquakes in Pakistan this month and last April when an earthquake of 6.1 magnitude hit the Hindu Kush region.

articles.title: Prison-run fuel station inaugurated at Khanapur, inspects women’s prison and opens new block in Warangal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Director General of Prisons Soumya Mishra visited Warangal district, inaugurating a fuel station aimed at providing employment to reformed prisoners. She also inspected the Special Prison for Women and opened a new administrative building at Central Prison, Warangal. Mishra emphasized the need for continued focus on security, modernization, and welfare measures across prison institutions.  Senior officials from the Indian Oil Corporation and local police were present.

articles.title: Green Card update: US judge rules USCIS cannot pause applications indefinitely, calls policy ‘unlawful’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A US federal judge ruled that the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) cannot indefinitely halt green card applications for immigrants from countries under travel restrictions. The judge stated that the agency lacks discretion to refuse adjudicating cases altogether, directing USCIS to restart processing for 83 individuals in a case involving this policy.  The ruling comes as many green card applicants face long delays due to backlogs at USCIS and is seen by some as a victory for those affected by the indefinite pause on applications. The judge's decision does not immediately apply to all affected immigrants, but it sets a precedent against blanket freezes on applications.

articles.title: Thousands held by paramilitary RSF in Sudan’s el-Fasher: NGO | Sudan war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: RSF has been accused of holding thousands of civilians, including women and children, in poor conditions in el-Fasher, Sudan. The Sudan Doctors Network reports that over 20 doctors, more than 1,470 civilians, and 907 military personnel are being detained by the paramilitary group, which has been accused of numerous crimes against humanity during the ongoing civil war.  The detention centers have faced a cholera outbreak and suffer from poor environmental conditions, lack of clean water, and malnutrition, further exacerbating the humanitarian crisis in the region. The RSF has not commented on the report.

articles.title: Performer describes locking eyes with Trump as they ducked for cover during shooting
articles.rephrased_article: Oz Pearlman, a mentalist, described locking eyes with President Donald Trump as they ducked for cover during shots fired at the White House Correspondents' dinner.  Pearlman was performing for the First Lady Melania Trump and Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, when the attack occurred. Security agents quickly apprehended Trump after he was tackled by agents, while Pearlman and others nearby escaped to safety. The suspected gunman, Cole Tomas Allen, was arrested at the venue and charged with attempting to assassinate the president.

articles.title: Top Foreign Office official ‘felt pressure’ for ‘rapid outcome’ on Mandelson vetting | Peter Mandelson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ian Collard, a top Foreign Office security official, testified before parliament that he felt pressure to quickly conclude the vetting process for Peter Mandelson, despite recommendations from United Kingdom Security Vetting (UKSV).  Collard stated that he did not see the UKSV assessment summary until after Mandelson was removed from his post and that this decision was unusual but not exceptional. The Foreign Office described the decision to go against UKSV's recommendation as "unusual but not exceptional," however, Olly Robbins, former permanent secretary at the FCDO, has given conflicting testimony about pressure on the department to expedite Mandelson's appointment.

articles.title: ‘Apologetic’ CM Murad announces reconstruction of Karachi's University Road in 90 days - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah apologized to Karachi residents for the delay in completing the Asian Development Bank-funded Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line project along University Road.  He announced that the deteriorated road will be reconstructed within 90 days using provincial government funds, separate from the BRT project. Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab stated that this initiative is to alleviate public hardship and ensure smooth traffic flow while construction on the Red Line continues. The chief minister also assured residents that the tender for Lot 2 of the Red Line will be reissued and construction activities are expected to resume within two to three days.

articles.title: ‘Harvest more water; banning paddy is not the solution to groundwater stress’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Ground Water Department, in collaboration with the State-level committee on Groundwater Resource Assessment (GWRA), is recommending a shift in mindset regarding groundwater use. The department suggests conservation measures at the village level, including banning water-intensive crops like paddy during the Rabi season and changing crop choices to ensure safe groundwater levels.  Secretary (Irrigation & Command Area Development) E. Sridhar, chairman of the State-level committee, emphasized that water used for agriculture is a resource stored for use, highlighting the importance of agriculture in the state's production. The GWRA report released on Monday advises discouraging paddy crop for Rabi season to avoid crop loss to farmers and aims to enhance groundwater recharge methods.

articles.title: 'Defending immigrants': US states oppose Trump-backed rule that could delay asylum seekers’ work permits by 180 days - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a rule that would significantly delay work authorization for asylum seekers, potentially indefinitely. California Attorney General Rob Bonta, leading a coalition of 20 states, argues the policy is harmful to individuals and the economy, citing potential exploitation, financial hardship, and increased healthcare costs. The proposal has drawn legal opposition from multiple states who claim it violates administrative law and lacks proper assessment of its impact.

articles.title: Will vote make a difference to Palestinians under Israeli occupation? | Elections | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Fatah party and its affiliates won a majority of seats in local Palestinian elections, held only in Deir el-Balah, Gaza.  Turnout was low at 25 percent. The elections were intended to promote Palestinian unity but did not include Ramallah or Nablus due to insufficient candidates. Hamas, which controls Gaza, boycotted the vote.  The outcome remains unclear and its impact on Palestinians living under Israeli occupation is yet to be seen.

articles.title: Raghu Rai: The photographer who showed India to itself
articles.rephrased_article: Raghu Rai, a celebrated Indian photojournalist, passed away at the age of 83.  His career spanned over five decades, documenting India's most defining events and shaping how the nation viewed its history. Rai began his career at The Statesman newspaper in 1966 and later worked as photo editor for India Today and Sunday magazines. He joined Magnum Photos in 1977, a prestigious photography agency that has influenced generations of photographers. His photographs captured political power, everyday life, and the Sikh militancy in Punjab during the 1980s.  His work is recognized for its artistic merit and its ability to capture the essence of India's people and culture. Rai was lauded by prominent figures such as Narendra Modi, who called him a "creative stalwart," and photographers who described his work as bridging reportage and art.

articles.title: Britain becoming ‘soft target’ for Russian propaganda, says security expert | Defence policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Fiona Hill, a former White House adviser, and George Robertson, a former Nato secretary general, warned that Britain is becoming vulnerable to Russian and other state propaganda due to a lack of public education on information warfare. They cited the example of Sweden's "psychological defence" program, which trains citizens to recognize manipulation tactics, as a model for the UK.  Keir Starmer, the prime minister, has acknowledged potential Russian threats but hasn't initiated widespread public engagement in civil defense strategies.

articles.title: ‘Apologetic’ CM Murad announces reconstruction of Karachi's University Road in 90 days - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah apologized to Karachi residents for the delay in the completion of the Asian Development Bank-funded Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) Red Line along University Road.  He announced that the deteriorated road will be reconstructed independently by the provincial government within 90 days, using its own funds, and assured citizens that mixed traffic lanes would be restored within three months. Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab stated that this project is separate from the BRT Red Line and aims to alleviate public inconvenience while construction continues.  The chief minister also announced that the tender for Lot 2 of the Red Line will be reissued, with construction activities expected to resume in two to three days.

articles.title: US stocks: S&P 500, Nasdaq, close slightly up in cautious start to a heavy earnings week - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Major U.S. stock indexes fluctuated throughout the session, reflecting uncertainty following last week's rally that sent the S&P 500 and Nasdaq to record highs.  Analysts anticipate robust first-quarter earnings from tech giants like Amazon, Alphabet, Meta Platforms, Apple, and Microsoft, which are expected to provide insight into the impact of AI investments. The Federal Reserve is scheduled to meet on Tuesday, with investors closely watching for clues about interest rate decisions and inflation concerns related to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

articles.title: ‘Weakening public faith’ vs. ‘justified stand’: legal experts divided over Kejriwal’s decision - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the legal fraternity offered differing opinions on Arvind Kejriwal’s decision to not appear before a Delhi High Court judge in the excise policy case.  Some lawyers argued that dissatisfaction with judicial orders should be addressed through established legal remedies, while others supported Kejriwal’s decision, citing potential bias and the need for due process. Senior advocate Sajan Poovayya criticized the move as withdrawing from due process, while advocate Gyanant Kumar Singh suggested it was a tactic to challenge the court's ruling after losing the case.  However, advocate Prashant Bhushan supported Kejriwal’s decision, arguing that his apprehension of bias is justified.

articles.title: One businessman, two attorneys involved in multimillion-dollar Hawaii bribery scheme: 'Calculated betrayal' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Three men, Rajesh Pankaj Budhabhatti, Gary Charles Zamber, and Paul Joseph Sulla, were sentenced to prison terms ranging from 60 to 90 months for their roles in a bribery scheme involving Alan Scott Rudo, a housing specialist at the Hawaii County Office of Housing and Community Development. The trio conspired to bribe Rudo to secure approval for development agreements linked to affordable housing projects worth over $11 million, but no homes were built despite promises made.  The FBI described the case as a serious breach of public trust.

articles.title: Bahrain strips 69 people of citizenship over Iran support | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bahrain has revoked the citizenship of 69 individuals, accusing them of supporting Iran and "colluding with foreign entities". The move follows Iranian strikes on facilities in Bahrain as part of the war launched by Israel and the United States against Iran.  The King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa issued the directive, stating that all individuals were "of non-Bahraini origin" and had caused harm to the country. Human rights groups have condemned the decision as a violation of international law.

articles.title: Anta: The Chinese sports brand taking on Nike and Adidas
articles.rephrased_article: Anta, a Chinese sportswear powerhouse, has grown from a small shoe maker to a global brand.  Founded in 1991, the company began by manufacturing shoes for international brands like Nike and Adidas before establishing its own production hub and expanding domestically. Anta now aims to compete with established Western brands like Nike and Adidas, having recently acquired stakes in Puma and Amer Sports. The company's strategy involves leveraging its multi-brand approach and celebrity sponsorships to gain a foothold in the global market.  This growth comes as rivals face challenges such as tariffs and slowing demand in China.

articles.title: King Charles arrives in Washington for state visit fraught with tension | King Charles III | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles and Queen Camilla arrived at the White House for a state visit in Washington, D.C., amidst ongoing tensions between the United States and the United Kingdom. The four-day tour is intended to mark the 250th anniversary of US independence but begins against the backdrop of a diplomatic rift over Trump's war in Iran and security concerns following a shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.  The visit will feature a state dinner, a speech to Congress, and meetings with conservation groups and New York officials, including Mayor Eric Adams and rising political star Zohran Mamdani. Despite ongoing concerns about the relationship between the two countries, Charles is expected to emphasize the importance of culture and civilisations during his address to Congress.

articles.title: Even as Tamil Nadu comes down from its election high, tensions are still rising - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu voters cast record-breaking numbers in the April 23, 2026 election.  The period between polling and vote counting is marked by debate on various issues including Chief Minister M.K.Stalin's holiday plans and comparisons of the state's IT sector performance with other southern states. The presence of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), led by actor C. Joseph Vijay, also raises questions about potential coalition governments.

articles.title: India names BJP leader envoy to Bangladesh as ties thaw - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India appointed veteran politician Dinesh Trivedi as its next high commissioner to Bangladesh, a move aimed at strengthening ties with the country.  Trivedi, a former railways and health minister who joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2021, will be tasked with rebuilding trust after strained relations following a popular uprising that forced Bangladesh's Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to flee to India. The appointment comes as India seeks to counter Chinese influence in the region and improve ties with Bangladesh, which has been seeking increased fuel and fertilizer supplies from India.

articles.title: World’s ‘worst’ FIFA football team that lost every match, yet almost qualified for 2026 World Cup | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: San Marino, a small nation with a population of just over 30,000, competes in the FIFA World Cup qualifying system alongside some of the world's biggest footballing nations. Despite facing heavy defeats against teams like England and Germany, San Marino has shown resilience by securing victories against Liechtenstein and achieving promotion to the Nations League C division. The team is comprised largely of part-time players who balance their football careers with work, studies, and other commitments.  The team's spirit and determination have earned them a dedicated following in their country and a place in the hearts of many football fans worldwide.

articles.title: Elon Musk trial against Sam Altman to reveal OpenAI power struggle | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Elon Musk and Sam Altman, the co-founders of OpenAI, are set to face off in a trial that could significantly impact the future of artificial intelligence. The trial centers on allegations of betrayal and deceit surrounding the evolution of OpenAI from a nonprofit organization into a for-profit venture.  The outcome will likely determine the balance of power within the AI industry, as both Musk and Altman have stakes in its development. The trial is scheduled to begin on Monday with jury selection and will be presided over by US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California.

articles.title: Canada's Carney launches a sovereign wealth fund. What is it?
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the launch of the Canada Strong Fund, a government-owned investment fund designed to finance major development projects in Canada. The C$25 billion fund will invest in energy, infrastructure, mining, agriculture, and technology sectors.  The fund also allows Canadians to directly invest, but experts have raised concerns about limited returns. Carney stated that the move is a response to changing relations with the US and aims to boost the Canadian economy. The fund's structure differs from other sovereign wealth funds, which are typically funded by oil revenues, and will be used for domestic projects.

articles.title: Lebanon health ministry says Israeli strikes kill 14 in deadliest day since ceasefire began | Lebanon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel and Hezbollah continued their conflict with escalating violence on Sunday, resulting in the deaths of 14 people in Lebanon, including two women and two children.  The Israeli military reported one soldier killed and six wounded while also intercepting three drones that crossed into Israeli territory. Hezbollah claimed responsibility for attacks on Israeli troops inside Lebanon and a rescue force, vowing to continue firing until Israel ceases its "ceasefire violations." The US-mediated ceasefire, which began in April, has seen a reduction in hostilities but both sides have continued to fire at each other.

articles.title: Haryana Assembly passes women empowerment resolution; Congress boycotts session - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Haryana State Assembly passed a resolution to form a Special Committee on women empowerment, despite the Congress party's boycott of the session.  Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini stated that the committee would support Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision for women empowerment and called out the opposition's "anti-approach" towards women's rights. Former Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, leader of the Congress party, accused the BJP government of making a mockery of constitutional institutions by convening the session on a matter that falls under the jurisdiction of the Central government.

articles.title: KP CM Afridi meets with TTAP's Achakzai and Abbas amid reports of rift within opposition - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi met with Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, leaders of the Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), at Achakzai’s residence in Islamabad. The meeting addressed concerns about Imran Khan's health, access to justice, legal restrictions, and upcoming national issues.  The parties agreed on a joint strategy to address these matters and strengthen coordination among opposition parties.

articles.title: Two green card rejections despite O-1 visa: Indian-origin entrepreneur explains the 'blind spot' about immigration - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nikin Tharan, an Indian-origin entrepreneur based in the US, has spoken about his struggles with immigration, including two green card rejections despite holding an O-1 visa and building successful startups.  Tharan, who moved to the US at 16 after securing a scholarship to Northeastern University, faced repeated visa hurdles that nearly ruined his career. He co-founded Medsix, a medtech startup that won two MIT awards, and has since founded multiple ventures including GreenCard Inc. and Openventure. Tharan advises young founders to stay consistent with networking and learning opportunities as immigration roadblocks can significantly impact their careers.

articles.title: Hezbollah and Israel swap threats and strikes across Lebanon’s border | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Hezbollah and Israel have engaged in escalating threats and attacks across the border, with Hezbollah reiterating its defiance of peace talks and accusing the Lebanese government of treason.  Israel's Defence Minister, Israel Katz, threatened to "burn all of Lebanon" if Hezbollah continues its resistance. The conflict has resulted in significant casualties on both sides, with over 2,500 deaths attributed to Israeli attacks since March 2nd. Despite a formal ceasefire, the two sides continue to exchange fire.

articles.title: Sabastian Sawe: How Kenyan broke two-hour barrier to make history at London Marathon - BBC Sport
articles.rephrased_article: Sebastian Sawe shattered the sub-two-hour marathon barrier in London, finishing with a time of 1:59:30. This historic achievement came as a surprise to even him, who was focused on retaining his title.  The victory marks a significant moment for marathon running and is considered a major milestone in the sport's history. Hugh Brasher, race director of the London Marathon, described it as "sport and history in making." Other notable runners who also broke records include Yomif Kejelcha and Jacob Kiplimo.  Sawe's success was aided by advancements in footwear technology and nutrition strategies, including a high-carbohydrate intake during the race. The athlete has been subjected to frequent anti-doping tests from the Athletics Integrity Unit to ensure his clean performance.

articles.title: Deadly Israeli attacks worsen Gaza’s water shortage crisis | Gaza | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces have killed a water engineer and two drivers transporting water to displaced families in Gaza over the past four days, exacerbating severe water shortages. The attacks, along with Israeli restrictions on hygiene products, have created a humanitarian crisis in Gaza, where access to clean water is limited to 7 liters per person daily. Unicef and Médecins Sans Frontières report that the lack of clean water and sanitation facilities has led to an increase in preventable diseases, including infections and psychological problems. The destruction of water infrastructure by Israeli forces and the blockade on fuel and spare parts have further hampered efforts to provide clean water and sewage treatment.

articles.title: 62 centres set up across TN for counting votes on May 4 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu has set up 62 counting centers to begin the vote-counting process for the recent Assembly elections. The counting of postal ballots will commence at 8:00 am on May 4th, followed by the Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) votes at 8:30 am.  The final round of EVM counting will only occur after all postal ballots are counted. Tamil Nadu Chief Electoral Officer has stated that over 2.88 lakh officials out of the total 3.60 lakh deployed for election duty have cast their votes via postal ballot.

articles.title: Oil industry seeks extension for imports on CIF basis to ensure continuity of supplies - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Oil Companies Advisory Council (OCAC), an association of over 30 oil companies and refineries in Pakistan, has requested the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to extend the permission for cost, insurance and freight (CIF) based petroleum imports for two more months. The request comes as the validity of the current 60-day relaxation is set to expire on May 10th.  The OCAC cited ongoing geopolitical instability in the Middle East, limited availability and high costs of marine and war-risk insurance, and continued reluctance from shipowners and suppliers as reasons for their request. The oil industry anticipates challenges in maintaining uninterrupted fuel supply chains if the current relaxation is not extended.

articles.title: France's darkest royal scandal: When a nation believed poison was everywhere | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: In the late 1670s, France was gripped by a poison panic after a woman named Marie Bosse boasted about her poisons.  Nicolas de la Reynie, Paris' chief of police, arrested her and uncovered a secret underworld operated by Catherine Deshayes Monvoisin, known as La Voisin. La Voisin provided love potions, aphrodisiacs, and poisons disguised as cosmetics to the French aristocracy. The investigation into the poison panic led to over 440 arrests, but ultimately became a tool for amplifying existing gender biases against women in a legal system that gave them little economic power.  The Affair of the Poisons was ultimately about what happens when the hidden world of desperate and powerful individuals becomes visible, and how a king can silence it.

articles.title: King Charles and Queen Camilla arrive for high-profile US state visit | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles and Queen Camilla arrived in the United States for a four-day state visit, marking the first by a British monarch in two decades. The trip coincides with heightened tensions between the countries over the US-Israel war on Iran, which has led to criticism from President Donald Trump.  The visit includes meetings with President Trump and addresses to Congress and the UN, as well as events commemorating the September 11 attacks and the centenary of Winnie-the-Pooh stories. The trip is intended to strengthen the "special relationship" between the two countries despite ongoing political disagreements.

articles.title: Robert Brovdi, Ukraine's drone commander with Russian oil in his sights
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine's drone commander, Robert Brovdi, has stated that his unmanned systems will escalate attacks targeting Russian oil facilities and troops.  He claims these strikes are causing significant losses for Russia, including billions of dollars in damage to its energy sector. The increase in long-range drone strikes is partly due to technological advancements and a focus on strategic targets like energy infrastructure. Brovdi's forces have been credited with destroying thousands of Russian soldiers each month, while also disrupting Russia's advance along the frontline. He believes these attacks are crucial for preventing further Russian territorial gains and demoralizing the Russian population.

articles.title: Australia news live: RSL to review welcome to country policy; Angus Taylor vows to double fuel reserve | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: RSL Australia will review its guidance on welcome to country addresses at Anzac Day services after Indigenous leaders were booed at three dawn services on Saturday. The RSL national president, Peter Tinley, said the body would provide guidance to branches on how to attend to this issue and make it more relevant.  Tinley also acknowledged that some acknowledgments can become “overworked”.

articles.title: ​Gang of seven: On the AAP defections - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Seven members of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) have merged with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), increasing the BJP's strength in the Rajya Sabha to 113 and exceeding the halfway mark for the National Democratic Alliance. This merger highlights the opportunism of AAP and its disregard for democratic institutions, as it follows a pattern of defections from other parties. The Supreme Court is currently reviewing the legality of this merger under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, which prohibits defection by elected representatives.

articles.title: Oil industry seeks extension for imports on CIF basis to ensure continuity of supplies - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Oil Companies Advisory Council (OCAC), representing over three dozen oil companies and refineries, has requested the State Bank of Pakistan to extend the permission for CIF-based imports of petroleum products for two months. The request comes as marine and war-risk insurance cover remains limited and expensive due to the ongoing geopolitical situation in the Middle East.  The OCAC argues that this continuation is necessary to ensure uninterrupted fuel supply chains, especially during upcoming seasonal demand.

articles.title: Ben Pasternak: Ben Pasternak breaks silence on Evelyn Ha abuse allegations: Full controversy explained - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ben Pasternak and Evelyn Ha, who recently ended their relationship, are facing legal scrutiny after a reported altercation at a New York hotel.  Pasternak was arrested on charges of second-degree strangulation and assault, while Ha alleges he physically abused her.  He has denied the accusations, claiming self-defense and alleging that she was abusive towards him during their relationship. The case is scheduled to go to court in June with a hearing set for then.

articles.title: China seeks to block US tech giant Meta from AI acquisition | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) has blocked a deal between Meta, the US tech giant, and AI startup Manus. The NDRC cited concerns over foreign acquisitions of Chinese AI talent and intellectual property as grounds for its decision, prohibiting the foreign acquisition of Manus without naming Meta.  Meta maintains that the transaction complied with applicable law and anticipates an appropriate resolution to the inquiry.

articles.title: Missing 5-year-old girl likely abducted from Outback home, police say
articles.rephrased_article: Australian police believe a five-year-old girl, Sharon, was abducted from an Aboriginal town camp in Alice Springs. Acting Commander Mark Grieve of the Northern Territory Police stated that they are searching for 47-year-old Jefferson Lewis, who was recently released from prison and was staying at the camp when Sharon disappeared.  Police have appealed to anyone with information to contact them as they search the area with assistance from a dog squad, drone unit, and helicopter.

articles.title: Number of executions in North Korea rose dramatically during Covid – report | North Korea | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea dramatically increased executions and death sentences after closing its borders in 2020, according to a report by the Transitional Justice Working Group (TJWG). The report found that the number of executions more than tripled between 2020 and 2024, with cases linked to foreign culture and information becoming the most common capital offenses. Kim Jong-un's regime exploited the pandemic and lack of international scrutiny to expand the death penalty, particularly for political crimes and violations of his orders. The TJWG urged the international community to hold those responsible accountable under international criminal law.

articles.title: Islamabad court grants journalist Fakharur Rehman post-arrest bail in Peca case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A judicial magistrate granted post-arrest bail to senior journalist Fakharur Rehman, who was arrested by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) for allegedly spreading "false and misleading information" on social media.  The journalist's lawyer argued that his client had not expressed personal opinions and shared a statement attributed to a religious figure, while the prosecution maintained that journalism carries great responsibility. The court reserved its verdict but ultimately approved Rehman's bail application with a surety bond of Rs50,000.

articles.title: Trump dinner shooting: Suspect Cole Allen charged with US president's attempted assassination - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, a 31-year-old man from Torrance, California, was charged with attempted assassination of US President Donald Trump following an incident at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.  Allen faces multiple charges including transporting firearms across state lines and discharging a firearm during a violent crime. He is being prosecuted in federal court in Washington and did not enter a plea. Secret Service agents responded to the scene, while investigators are examining Allen's social media activity and messages sent to family members as potential evidence of his motives.

articles.title: Indonesia train crash kills at least four people and injures dozens
articles.rephrased_article: At least four people were killed and dozens injured when two trains collided outside Jakarta, Indonesia. KAI, the state-owned railway operator, confirmed the deaths and said 38 others were hospitalized.  Sufmi Dasco Ahmad, Deputy Speaker of the Indonesian House of Representatives, visited the site and reported that six or seven people remain trapped inside the carriages. The incident occurred near Bekasi Timur Station, approximately 25km from Jakarta. Indonesia's public transport network has a high accident rate due to aging infrastructure and poor maintenance.

articles.title: ‘Israel must change direction’: Netanyahu rivals join forces for next election | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, facing a potential challenge to his leadership, is being targeted by former allies Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid. The two have joined forces to form a new right-wing coalition, "Together," with the aim of ousting Netanyahu.  The move comes as Netanyahu disclosed he had recently undergone prostate cancer surgery, raising questions about his health and future political viability. Polls suggest that this new coalition could potentially create the largest grouping in the Knesset, posing a significant challenge to Netanyahu's long-standing dominance.

articles.title: Tamilnad Mercantile Bank profit jumps 28% on strong growth - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The bank's operating profit increased by 29% to Rs 522 crore, driven by a 16% rise in total income to Rs 1792 crore. The bank's net interest margin rose to 4.18%, and its net profit for FY26 reached Rs 1338 crore.  A final dividend of Rs 12.50 per equity share was proposed, representing a 125% dividend payout for the year. The bank's asset quality improved with a decline in gross non-performing assets ratio to 0.73%.

articles.title: Timeline: The highs and lows of the US-UK ‘special relationship’ | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The visit of King Charles III to the United States is intended to strengthen the US-UK partnership despite tensions between the allies.  This comes at a time when US President Donald Trump has publicly criticized British Prime Minister Keir Starmer over his stance on the US-Israeli war on Iran, accusing him of not assisting Washington in the fight against Iran or helping the US reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz. The "special relationship" between the two countries has faced strain throughout history, with notable examples including the Suez Canal crisis (1956), the Falklands War (1982), and the Kosovo War (1998-1999).  Despite disagreements on military intervention in the past, the US and UK have remained strong allies.

articles.title: Trump, Melania call for action by channel against host Jimmy Kimmel over joke likening first lady to 'expectant widow' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and Melania Trump called for the firing of Jimmy Kimmel by ABC and Walt Disney, citing a monologue Kimmel delivered about Melania Trump.  The president and first lady have criticized Kimmel's joke as "atrocious" and harmful, arguing it is an example of political sickness in the US. They believe Kimmel should be fired for his remarks, which were made during a parody segment on the upcoming White House Correspondents’ Dinner.

articles.title: Human smuggler, who caused death of Indian family, asks US court to quash conviction, sentence - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Steve Shand, one of two men convicted in a human smuggling case linked to the deaths of an Indian family at the US-Canada border, has appealed his conviction and sentence.  His lawyer argues that the traffic stop which led to his arrest was unlawful and that he was unaware of the operation's leader's decision to cross the family with young children during dangerous conditions. Harshkumar Patel, Shand's co-accused and identified as the organizer of the smuggling network, received a sentence over 10 years. The case stems from the tragic death of a family of four in January 2022 who froze to death while attempting to cross the border on foot.

articles.title: Venice opera house drops incoming music director after nepotism remarks
articles.rephrased_article: La Fenice opera house has dismissed its incoming music director, Beatrice Venezi, after she made controversial remarks about the orchestra's hiring process.  Venezi's comments, which included insinuations that jobs were "passed down from father to son," sparked outrage among musicians and led to a strike by workers' union. The opera house cited "repeated and serious public statements" as the reason for Venezi's dismissal, stating they were damaging to the theater's artistic standing.  The appointment of Venezi, who has worked with the Ministry of Culture since 2022, was met with controversy from the start due to her lack of experience and alleged nepotism ties to Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

articles.title: US is being ‘humiliated’ by Iran’s leadership, says Friedrich Merz | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Friedrich Merz, Donald Trump, and other officials have criticized the US's approach to negotiations with Iran.  Iran has proposed a new deal focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, offering to charge fees for shipping services. The proposal was rejected by the International Maritime Organization, while analysts suggest it could be a strategic move by Iran to mitigate economic hardship caused by US sanctions. Meanwhile, Vladimir Putin pledged support for Iran, and Ali Vaez, an analyst, suggests that Iran's resilience is fueled by its desire to survive the conflict with the US.

articles.title: NSE adds one crore unique investors in 7 months, base crosses 13 crore mark - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has seen a significant surge in investor participation, reaching 13 crore registered investors within the past seven months. This growth is attributed to factors such as digital access, improved financial awareness, and government initiatives promoting market inclusivity.  NSE's Chief Business Development Officer Sriram Krishnan highlighted that this broad-based expansion is driven by younger investors and a growing preference for diverse investment instruments like equities, ETFs, REITs, InvITs, and bonds.

articles.title: Iraqi president names Shia bloc candidate Ali al-Zaidi as PM-designate | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iraqi President Nizar Amedi has named Ali al-Zaidi, a candidate of the Coordination Framework, as prime minister-designate.  This appointment breaks a months-long deadlock after Donald Trump opposed the nomination of former Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki. The Coordination Framework is the largest bloc in the Iraqi House of Representatives and has a majority in parliament.

articles.title: Suspect in Washington dinner shooting charged with attempting to assassinate Trump - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, a 31-year-old man from Torrance, California, faces federal charges of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump after allegedly shooting a Secret Service agent at the White House Correspondents Association Dinner.
