Allen was apprehended and detained following the incident, which occurred at the Washington Hilton hotel where the dinner took place. Karoline Leavitt, White House press secretary, characterized the attack as the third major assassination attempt against Trump, noting similarities between Allen's manifesto and criticism of Trump from his political opponents. The shooting disrupted the event, prompting security measures and sending attendees scrambling for safety.

articles.title: Wembley shame: Leeds United fans face prosecution after homophobic chanting targeting Chelsea at FA Cup semi-final | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Following a narrow defeat in the FA Cup semi-final against Chelsea, Leeds United supporters have been reported for consideration of prosecution for homophobic chanting at Wembley. The Metropolitan Police Service confirmed 16 fans will be reported for this offense, among 18 individuals arrested or reported for other offenses including GBH and affray. This follows guidance from the Crown Prosecution Service that designates certain chants as hate crimes, leading to a shift in how incidents are handled.  The match was marred by chants referencing Jimmy Savile, with Leeds United condemning those taunts while also emphasizing disapproval of retaliatory chants from their own supporters.

articles.title: Melania Trump urges ABC to 'take stand' on Jimmy Kimmel after widow joke
articles.rephrased_article: Melania Trump criticized Jimmy Kimmel's joke about her being an "expectant widow," urging his network, ABC, to take action against his "atrocious behavior."  The first lady called the remark "hateful and violent" and expressed concern that it could incite political violence. President Donald Trump also condemned the joke on Truth Social, calling for Kimmel's firing from Disney and ABC. The incident followed a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner where Melania Trump was present.  The White House Press Secretary, Karoline Leavitt, criticized the comedian's remarks as "deranged."

articles.title: Mexico warns US involvement in anti-drug operation should not to be repeated | Mexico | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico's president, stated that her government informed the United States in a diplomatic note that unauthorized US officials participating in an anti-narcotics operation in Chihuahua should not be repeated.  Sheinbaum emphasized that the federal government was unaware of their involvement and hopes it is an exception. The incident resulted in the deaths of two US officials, prompting renewed tensions between the countries regarding security cooperation.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran ‘offers to end chokehold on strait of Hormuz’ | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Iran is offering to end its chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz without addressing its nuclear program. The proposal, passed to the United States by Pakistan, was discussed with US President Donald Trump and his national security team.  The UK supports working with the US and others to reopen the strait. Russia has pledged to help secure peace in the Middle East, while Lebanon's president is seeking direct negotiations with Israel to end the conflict with Hezbollah. The UN’s maritime agency stated there is no legal basis for imposing fees on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.  The Israeli military continues its offensive against Hezbollah in Lebanon despite a ceasefire agreement.

articles.title: HC commutes death sentence of a man convicted of repeated sexual assault of daughter - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court
articles.rephrased_article: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court commuted the death sentence of a man convicted of sexually assaulting his minor daughter to life imprisonment. The court found that while the prosecution proved guilt beyond reasonable doubt, capital punishment was not warranted due to the statutory framework and judicially evolved principles governing capital sentencing.  The court emphasized that the death penalty is reserved for exceptional cases where alternative punishments are inadequate.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article normalizes sexual assault of a minor and its lenient punishment.

articles.title: Adani Total Gas Q4 Results: Cons PAT grows 9% YoY to Rs 168 crore; revenue up 17% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ATGL's profit after tax (PAT) grew 6% on a sequential basis to Rs 156 crore in the January-March quarter of FY26, driven by a 16% increase in revenue.  Revenue growth was attributed to higher volume sales. The company's EBITDA rose 13% year-on-year to Rs 310 crore. ATGL CEO & Executive Director Suresh P. Manglani highlighted the company's resilience amidst geopolitical disruptions and volatility, emphasizing its focus on operational excellence and long-term sustainability.

articles.title: FCC suspends LHC decision that set aside govt's authority to render passports inactive - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) suspended the Lahore High Court’s decision that declared provisions of the Passport Rules 2021, allowing for passport inactivations and long-term travel bans on deportees and human trafficking suspects, as ultra vires. The FCC issued notices to respondents including Farhan Ali, who was deported from Iran and whose passport was deactivated by the Directorate General of Immigration and Passports (DGIP).  The DGIP argued that the LHC's decision disregarded the power delegated to the director general of immigration under Section 11 of the Passport Act, 1974, and that the power to inactivate a passport was inherent within the power to cancel, impound, or confiscate it as per Section 21 of the General Clauses Act, 1897.

articles.title: “Trust no man”: Yonna makes bold statement as Megan Thee Stallion ends relationship with Klay Thompson over trust - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Megan Thee Stallion and Klay Thompson have ended their relationship after Megan publicly stated that trust was broken.  Megan shared her feelings on social media, emphasizing the importance of loyalty and respect in a relationship. Popular streamer Yonna reacted to the news during a live stream, advocating for caution when giving someone your trust and urging people to protect themselves emotionally.

articles.title: Analysis: Bennett-Lapid alliance attempt to unseat Israel’s Netanyahu | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, former Israeli prime ministers, have announced the formation of a new alliance to challenge Benjamin Netanyahu. The "Together" party will attempt to unseat Netanyahu in upcoming elections.  However, analysts warn that the alliance is unlikely to significantly benefit Palestinians. Despite their past efforts to form a coalition government, the Bennett-Lapid partnership faces challenges including internal disagreements and opposition from some segments of Israeli society.

articles.title: Archbishop of Canterbury praises Pope's anti-war comments during Vatican visit
articles.rephrased_article: Archbishop of Canterbury, Dame Sarah Mullally, praised Pope Leo for speaking out against injustice during their meeting at the Vatican.  Mullally expressed hope that Pope Leo would receive a warm welcome in the UK if he were to visit. The two religious leaders discussed peace and justice, with Pope Leo reiterating his commitment to speak out against war and promote peace.

articles.title: EU faces ‘China shock’ as EV imports drive Beijing’s record surplus with bloc | European Union | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The EU is experiencing a prolonged "China shock" as Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) have flooded the market, contributing to a record trade surplus with Beijing.  Data from 2026 customs data shows that China exported goods worth $148 billion to the EU in the first quarter of 2026, while importing just $65 billion, resulting in a $83 billion surplus. The EU is attempting to mitigate this trade imbalance through initiatives like tariffs on Chinese car imports and efforts to reduce reliance on rare earth minerals, but these measures have been largely ineffective. The EU's trade relationship with China has become increasingly strained as Beijing continues to dominate the EV market and Brussels seeks to rebalance the trade relationship.

articles.title: J&K court orders release of AAP MLA after 8 months of jail, says ‘PSA appears an unjustified exercise’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court ruled that the detention of Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) legislator Mehraj Din Malik, who was arrested for "inappropriate remarks" against a district commissioner, was unjustified. The court deemed the invocation of the Public Safety Act as a shortcut to bypass ordinary criminal law and ordered his release from jail.  The ruling was welcomed by several political parties in the region, including the J&K Apni Party and the J&K Awami Ittehad Party.

articles.title: Coal India Q4 Results: Profit rises 12% to Rs 10,908 crore; co declares Rs 5.25 dividend - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Coal India reported a 12% increase in profit before tax for the quarter, reaching Rs 14,627 crore. The company declared a final dividend of Rs 5.25 per share, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. Revenue rose 8% to Rs 51,618 crore, driven by higher realizations despite flat sales volumes.  Expenses increased due to higher levies and finance costs, leading to a 12% decline in profit after tax for FY26 to Rs 31,071 crore.

articles.title: Punjab Assembly passes bill setting minimum marriage age at 18 for both males and females - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab Assembly passed the Child Marriage Restraint Bill 2026, setting 18 years as the minimum legal age for marriage and declaring underage marriages a non-bailable offense. The bill was initially met with controversy as lawmakers were not provided copies of the bill before voting.  Following debate, the bill was approved with an amendment emphasizing the best interests of the child in all actions under the law. The amendment also clarified that no child should be treated as an offender for being a contracting party to a child marriage and protected from coercion or manipulation.

articles.title: Melania Trump reacts to Jimmy Kimmel’s ‘expectant widow’ joke: ‘Enough is enough…’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Melania Trump criticized Jimmy Kimmel for a joke about her at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, calling it "hateful and violent" and urging ABC to take action.  The backlash follows a shooting incident near a security checkpoint where authorities believe members of the Trump administration may have been targeted. Melania Trump condemned Kimmel's remarks as divisive and corrosive, while also criticizing ABC for giving him a platform.

articles.title: Melania Trump blasts Kimmel, calls on ABC to ‘take stand’ against comedian | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Melania Trump and Donald Trump criticized comedian Jimmy Kimmel, calling for his dismissal from ABC after a joke about the first lady during his show.  They accused him of spreading hate and deepening political division, particularly in light of the recent shooting outside the White House correspondents dinner. The First Lady's comments on X (formerly Twitter) and President Trump's social media post echo concerns raised by the White House regarding Kimmel's remarks. This incident follows a previous suspension of Kimmel by ABC after threats from the Trump administration in 2020.

articles.title: Singapore: French teen who licked vending machine straw faces jail
articles.rephrased_article: An 18-year-old French student, Didier Gaspard Owen Maximilien, faces potential jail time in Singapore after allegedly licking a vending machine straw and posting the act on Instagram. He is charged with mischief and public nuisance, potentially leading to over two years in prison and substantial fines. The incident occurred at a shopping center on March 12th, prompting iJooz, the vending machine company, to replace all 500 straws and report the matter to police. Maximilien's case is scheduled for further court proceedings on May 22nd.

articles.title: Pro-Palestine activists appear in court over attack on Israeli arms factory in Germany | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Five pro-Palestinian activists, aged 25 to 40, from Britain, Ireland, Germany, and Spain, are facing charges of trespass, destruction of property, and membership in a criminal organization for an attack on an Elbit Systems arms company in Ulm, Germany. The defendants, known as the Ulm 5, claim their actions were justified as a defense against Israel's military actions in Gaza and argue that they did not pose a threat to society.  The trial is expected to continue until the end of July.

articles.title: ₹127.69 crore has been restored to victims of Rose Valley Group scam: ED - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) and the Asset Disposal Committee (ADC) have continued efforts to restore funds to victims of the Rose Valley Group scam.  They have completed 16 phases of disbursements, releasing ₹127.69 crore to over 1.73 lakh people. The group defrauded investors of approximately ₹17,520 crore, with ₹6,666 crore still outstanding. The ED has attached or seized assets worth ₹1,568 crore in multiple states and recently handed over a demand draft for ₹517.54 crore to the ADC. The agencies are also automating claims and disbursement processes using AI technology and collaborating with government companies to revamp the refund portal.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale financial fraud with ongoing harm to citizens is being treated as routine.

articles.title: Trent announces record date for its 1:2 bonus issue. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Trent Ltd. announced a bonus share issue, marking the company's first such move. The plan will distribute approximately 17.77 crore equity shares of Re 1 face value each, capitalizing on its share premium reserves.  The allotment is expected to be completed by June 21st, and the move aims to increase stock liquidity and accessibility for retail investors. Trent Ltd. also reported a 26% growth in consolidated net profit for Q4 FY26, with revenue from operations rising 19% YoY.

articles.title: Info ministry rubbishes reports of Pakistan targeting varsity, residential areas in Afghanistan's Kunar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Afghan media outlet Tolo News reported that Pakistan carried out attacks targeting a university and residential areas in Kunar province. The Pakistan information ministry refuted these claims, stating they were "blatant lies" intended to cover up support from the Afghan Taliban for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban (TTP).  The ministry emphasized that Pakistan's strikes are intelligence-based and targeted terrorist infrastructure, not civilian areas.

articles.title: Melania Trump reacts to Jimmy Kimmel’s ‘expectant widow’ joke: ‘Enough is enough…’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Melania Trump criticized Jimmy Kimmel for a joke about her at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, calling it "hateful and violent" and urging ABC to take action. The backlash follows a shooting incident near a security checkpoint where authorities believe members of the Trump administration may have been targeted.  Melania Trump also criticized Kimmel for his past comments and questioned why he continues to be given a platform, while Donald Trump described the event as "traumatic" for his wife.

articles.title: Gunmen kidnap 23 children from Nigerian orphanage | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gunmen raided an unregistered orphanage in Kogi State, Nigeria, kidnapping at least 23 children. The Kogi Information Commissioner Kingsley Fanwo confirmed the incident and stated that security agencies rescued 15 children but eight remain missing. The orphanage was operating illegally in a remote location without proper authorization, according to authorities.  The attack is part of a larger pattern of mass kidnappings by armed groups for financial gain in Nigeria's volatile regions.

articles.title: French coastguard rescues more than 100 migrants crossing Channel
articles.rephrased_article: French coastguard rescued 106 migrants who were traveling in a single boat after it broke down during an attempt to cross the English Channel.  The rescue occurred on Saturday and involved the intervention of French authorities who first became aware of the vessel while assisting seven people who had become disoriented while attempting to board. The incident follows a new agreement between the UK and France aimed at preventing migrant crossings, with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood signing a three-year deal that includes deploying riot-trained police to beaches along the northern coast.

articles.title: German tourist dies after being bitten at snake show on family holiday in Egypt | Egypt | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 57-year-old German tourist died in Egypt after a snake bit him during a snake-charming show. The incident occurred at a hotel in Hurghada, where the man was watching with two relatives. Police in southern Bavaria are investigating the death and awaiting toxicology test results.  Egyptian authorities were unaware of the incident.

articles.title: Plane crashes near South Sudan’s Juba, killing all 14 on board | Aviation News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Cessna 208 Caravan operated by CityLink Aviation crashed near Juba, South Sudan, killing all 14 people on board. The aircraft lost communication while flying from Yei to Juba International Airport and initial reports suggest the crash was caused by bad weather conditions resulting in low visibility. A team has been sent to the crash site to gather information and support emergency services.

articles.title: Venice opera house fires government-linked music director after months of protests | Opera | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Teatro La Fenice, the prestigious Venice opera house, fired its incoming music director, Beatrice Venezi, after she criticized the hiring process and called it nepotistic.  The La Fenice Foundation stated that Venezi's "repeated public statements" were detrimental to the opera house's artistic value. The decision followed months of controversy surrounding Venezi's appointment, with orchestra members and audience members expressing dissatisfaction. Giorgia Meloni, Italy's Prime Minister, denied any involvement in the decision, while Alessandro Giuli, Italy's culture minister, stated that La Fenice made the decision independently.

articles.title: South Sudan plane crash kills all 14 on board
articles.rephrased_article: A Cessna 208 Caravan operated by CityLink Aviation Ltd. crashed in South Sudan, killing all 14 people on board. The plane was en route from Yei to Juba when it went down about 20km southwest of the capital, according to the South Sudan civil aviation authority.  Initial reports suggest adverse weather conditions may have contributed to the crash.

articles.title: Citizens, NGOs step in to quench the thirst of urban animals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Animal welfare activists in Bengaluru are taking initiative to address the heatwave's impact on urban animals.  Sampige Foundation, People for Animals (PFA), and Water for Voiceless (WFV) have distributed thousands of water bowls across the city, partnering with local organizations and educational institutions to raise awareness about animal hydration during the summer months. These NGOs are also working to replenish natural water sources in forests to prevent wildlife from venturing out into human-dominated areas.

articles.title: Melania Trump says ABC should take stand on late-night host Kimmel over joke likening her to an 'expectant widow' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Melania Trump criticized Jimmy Kimmel on Monday, calling his joke about her resembling an "expectant widow" corrosive and deepening political sickness in America. The first lady's comments came after a shooting at a media gala dinner attended by President Donald Trump, where the gunman was subdued by security officers.  Kimmel was briefly suspended from his show last year for criticizing the Trump administration, but Melania Trump urged ABC to take a stand against his behavior.

articles.title: 'I am not a rapist': Donald Trump erupts in interview as media dinner shooting fallout deepens - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump reacted angrily to excerpts from a manifesto allegedly written by the suspect in Saturday's security scare at the WHCA dinner, denying accusations of rape and pedophilia. During an interview with CBS 60 Minutes correspondent Norah O’Donnell, he called her a "disgrace" and accused journalists of amplifying the words of a "sick person." The incident involved a 31-year-old suspect who tried to breach security at the Washington Hilton, where scores of journalists, politicians, and celebrities were gathered. Vice President JD Vance was evacuated before Trump, sparking controversy over security arrangements.  The attack has fueled political debate about the role of media in reporting on the incident and the president's response to it.

articles.title: Timeline: How Mali went from democracy beacon to instability | Armed Groups News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mali has been plagued by political and security crises since 2012, with recent coordinated attacks attributed to Al-Qaeda-linked Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM). The attacks have targeted government facilities and military personnel, including the death of Defence Minister Sadio Camara.  The country's history includes periods of military dictatorship and democratic rule, with a series of coups and instability contributing to the current security situation.

articles.title: Pro-choice campaigners in Malta create lockboxes containing abortion pills | Malta | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Women on Waves, a Netherlands-based charity, has affixed lockboxes containing abortion pills to sites across Malta in a campaign designed to highlight the country's near-total ban on abortion. The campaign, which aims to provide practical help to women seeking abortions under the strict laws of the country, has resulted in 16 women contacting the organization in its first eight days.  The campaign has sparked debate and prompted an anti-abortion group to call for police intervention. Doctors for Choice Malta, a local organization advocating for abortion rights, reports that many women are forced to choose between complying with the law or their right to decide.

articles.title: Sri Lankan monks arrested after cannabis discovered in luggage
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Lankan police arrested 22 monks after discovering 110kg of cannabis concealed in their luggage at Colombo airport. The monks, mainly students who returned from a sponsored trip to Thailand, were found with around 5kg of Kush each. A 23rd monk believed to have organized the trip was also arrested.  The police believe the monks may not have been aware they were carrying drugs. They are being held for seven days pending further questioning.

articles.title: BRS outlived its purpose and has lost its relevance, says Revanth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy stated that the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) is irrelevant in Telangana and has no future, while also demanding a full-fledged CBI probe into alleged irregularities in the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project.  He criticized K Chandrasekhar Rao, claiming he should respond to allegations made by his daughter, Kavitha. Revanth Reddy believes the High Court's judgment on the PC Ghose Commission was correct and that investigations into phone tapping and Formula E race cases are progressing under court monitoring. He predicted the next elections would be between the Congress alliance and the BRS-BJP alliance.

articles.title: Melania Trump says ABC should take stand on late-night host Kimmel over joke likening her to an 'expectant widow' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: First Lady Melania Trump criticized Jimmy Kimmel, calling his joke about her resembling an "expectant widow" corrosive and fueling political sickness.  The remark, made in a monologue last week, resurfaced after a shooting at a White House dinner where President Donald Trump was present. Trump demanded that ABC, the network hosting Kimmel's show, take a stand against his behavior.

articles.title: Board game harassment: Japanese firefighter suspended for forcing coworkers to play homemade board games for six months | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A firefighter sergeant in Japan's Aichi Prefecture has been suspended for six months after being found to have coerced colleagues into playing handmade board games during duty hours over a period of six months. The games, which involved dice-based movement and action cards themed around firefighting, were not official training sessions and participants reported feeling pressured to participate.  The sergeant also allegedly instructed colleagues to falsify duty logs and attempted to cover up the misconduct. Nine other personnel received written reprimands for their involvement or failure to intervene.

articles.title: Iran offers Hormuz deal without nuclear talks, as it seeks broader buy-in | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has proposed a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, deferring nuclear talks with the United States for later.  Araghchi met with regional leaders in Pakistan, Oman, and Russia, seeking support for his proposal. The White House has not confirmed the contents of the Iranian proposal but has stated that it will not negotiate through the press.  The US President Donald Trump has indicated that Iran's nuclear ambitions are non-negotiable.  While diplomatic efforts continue, a deadline looms for Trump to obtain congressional authorization to continue military operations against Iran.

articles.title: Indigenous woman dies weeks after giving birth and being evicted from public housing: ‘She was failed completely’ | Indigenous Australians | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mary Ann Miller, an Aboriginal mother of seven, died from sepsis two weeks after giving birth in Fiona Stanley hospital. Her family alleges that the Western Australian government was aware of her domestic violence situation and failed to provide adequate support. The Department of Housing and Works terminated Miller's public housing tenancy due to non-compliance with property inspections, despite her application for a priority transfer pending approval.  The Department of Communities, which provided support services prior to her death, declined to comment on the specifics of her case.

articles.title: Kogi state kidnap: Gunmen raid Nigerian orphanage and abduct children
articles.rephrased_article: Gunmen raided an unregistered orphanage in Nigeria's Kogi State, kidnapping 23 children and taking the facility owner. Kingsley Fanwo, the state's information commissioner, confirmed that 15 children were rescued following a coordinated security response.  Authorities believe the attack may be linked to a functional Boko Haram cell operating in the region, which has seen several violent attacks. The government is committed to rescuing all victims and urges proper engagement with relevant authorities by orphanage operators.

articles.title: BJD asks Odisha Speaker to disqualify MLAs who cross-voted in Rajya Sabha election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Biju Janata Dal (BJD) has demanded the disqualification of eight Odisha MLAs who voted against the party's decision in the March 16 Rajya Sabha election. The BJD, citing the Tenth Schedule, argues that these MLAs violated party directives and should be disqualified for defying the whip.  The MLAs, however, maintain their actions were constitutional and claim the move is an attempt to pressure them into submission. Surama Padhy, the Odisha Assembly Speaker, is currently examining the BJD's formal complaint.

articles.title: Bahrain revokes citizenship of 69 people for 'glorifying or sympathising' with Iranian attacks - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bahrain's interior ministry revoked the citizenship of 69 non-Bahraini individuals, citing their sympathy with Iran and collaboration with foreign entities.  The revocation was based on Article 10/3 of the Bahraini Nationality Law, which allows for the stripping of citizenship when it is deemed detrimental to national interests. Sayed Ahmed Alwadaei, Advocacy Director at the Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy (BIRD), condemned the move as a "dangerous era of repression" lacking legal safeguards or appeal rights.

articles.title: Canadian-Indian woman shares struggle story of work-life balance: ‘I'm stuck in a loop’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jyoti Kharayat, an Indian student living in Canada, has gone viral for a video documenting her busy daily routine.  She balances classes with work shifts at Starbucks to manage expenses while studying abroad. Kharayat describes feeling the pressure of financial constraints but maintains a positive outlook despite the demanding schedule. Social media users have expressed support and encouragement.

articles.title: Canada’s Carney announces a sovereign wealth fund | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the creation of a government-owned investment fund, marking the first such initiative in the country. The fund will invest in major Canadian industrial projects across sectors like energy, infrastructure, mining, agriculture, and technology, with an initial commitment of $25 billion. Carney, a former central banker in England and Canada, cited lessons learned from other jurisdictions that established sovereign wealth funds to diversify Canada's economy away from the United States.

articles.title: Mali’s militant attacks expose limits of Putin’s power in Africa | Mali | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Assimi Goïta, the leader of Mali’s military junta, met with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin last summer to solidify Moscow's influence over the country. However, recent attacks by jihadist militants and a separatist group have exposed the limits of Russia's reach and military might in the impoverished west African state. The rebels achieved at least one major victory by capturing Kidal, a strategically important town, forcing Russia’s Africa Corps, the successor to the Wagner group, to withdraw. This setback raises questions about Russia's ability to provide solutions for insurgencies in the region.

articles.title: Pakistan accused of attacking Kunar University in Afghanistan
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has been accused of attacking an Afghan university in Kunar province, killing at least seven people and injuring 75, including students. The Pakistani information ministry denied the attacks, stating that reports were fake.  Afghanistan's higher education ministry reported extensive damage to the university buildings and surroundings. This incident follows a recent air strike on a drug rehabilitation center in Kabul, which has been linked to the deaths of 269 people according to the UN. Cross-border fighting between Pakistan and Afghanistan has resulted in numerous casualties in recent months.

articles.title: Mild heatwave conditions likely in southern parts of Pakistan from April 29 to May 3: PMD - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) predicts mild heatwave conditions in southern regions from April 29 to May 3, with temperatures potentially reaching up to 52°C. The PMD also states that the upper parts of the country will experience a drop in temperatures from May 3-5 due to a westerly wave.  The UN's weather and climate agency expects El Niño conditions to emerge during May-July, with potential for development as early as May to July. The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) issued a nationwide alert warning of an intense heatwave until May 5.

articles.title: Trump wants to rename ICE as 'NICE', and the reason is... - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump endorsed a proposal to rename the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency as "National Immigration and Customs Enforcement" or NICE, sparking debate on social media. The idea was initially proposed by conservative commentator Alyssa Marie, who argued that changing the name could influence public perception of immigration enforcement.  Supporters believe language plays a significant role in shaping public opinion, while critics argue that it's a distraction from real issues with ICE operations. This proposal comes amidst ongoing political tension over immigration policy and recent incidents involving ICE agents sparking protests and calls for accountability.

articles.title: Have US-Iran talks failed? Why no deal yet doesn’t mean diplomacy is dead | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US-Iran diplomacy has stalled, with both sides refusing to budge on key demands.  President Donald Trump canceled a planned visit to Pakistan for talks and blamed Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi for the failure of previous negotiations. While a ceasefire is holding, experts believe the deadlock reflects a slowdown in negotiations rather than a collapse. Despite disagreements over nuclear programs and control of the Strait of Hormuz, both sides are unlikely to return to full-scale conflict.  Diplomatic efforts continue through indirect channels, with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian communicating red lines to the US through Pakistani mediators.

articles.title: Ukraine war: North Korea's Kim Jong Un reaffirms support for Russia
articles.rephrased_article: Kim Jong Un and Russian Defence Minister Andrey Belousov unveiled a memorial in Pyongyang for North Korean soldiers killed in the Ukraine war. The opening of the Memorial Museum of Combat Feats coincided with Russia's anniversary of reclaiming parts of Kursk, which it said was achieved after a surprise Ukrainian incursion in August 2024. Kim Jong Un assured Belousov that North Korea would continue to support Russia's war efforts and pledged long-term military cooperation.  The event also saw Kim meet with Vyacheslav Volodin, the speaker of Russia's parliament, and discussed future military co-operation.

articles.title: Odesa bears brunt of latest Russian attacks on Ukraine – Europe live | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Another night of Russian drone attacks on Ukraine injured over 10 people, primarily in the Odesa region. Ukrainian Prime Minister Julia Svyrydenko is attending a conference in Poland to discuss Ukraine's recovery and will meet with Poland's Donald Tusk. France's Emmanuel Macron is visiting Andorra as its co-prince, while Ursula von der Leyen is meeting with her former party in Berlin.  Hungary's incoming government is discussing releasing frozen EU funds with the European Commission. Lithuania has charged 13 people linked to Russia for attempted murders and terrorism. Meanwhile, a Ukrainian drone strike on the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant killed a transport worker.  A whale named Timmy stranded in Germany is being prepared for a rescue mission.

articles.title: Naidu sets ₹4.60-a-unit power purchase target for Andhra Pradesh by year-end - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to reduce the state's power purchase cost to ₹4.60 per unit by year-end and increase renewable energy generation.  He emphasized technology-driven reforms in the power sector, urging officials to study cost-effective methods globally and prioritize research and analysis within the department. Naidu also called for expanding renewable energy sources to over 50% of the state's power generation by 2028-29 and setting up a dedicated Energy University.  The meeting was attended by Energy Minister Gottipati Ravi Kumar and senior officials from various departments.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz signs off on letting fans attend PSL playoffs - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mohsin Naqvi, Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) Chairman, announced that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has approved public attendance for all three PSL playoff matches.  The decision comes with a condition that fans use public transport or minimize fuel consumption to support national austerity efforts. Shehbaz Sharif also wished the four competing teams luck and expressed anticipation for exciting cricket.

articles.title: Bajaj Housing Finance Q4 results: Profit rises 14% to Rs 669 crore; NII up 15% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bajaj Housing Finance reported a 15% increase in net interest income to Rs 945 crore for Q4FY26, driven by loan book expansion. The company's profit before tax rose 20% to Rs 866 crore, while assets under management (AUM) grew 23% to Rs 1,40,706 crore.  Loan assets also increased 24%, with quarterly disbursements rising 23%. Despite a cautious stance and a rise in provisions, the lender maintained strong asset quality with gross non-performing assets at 0.27% and net NPA at 0.11%.   Overall, Bajaj Housing Finance delivered consistent growth across key metrics.

articles.title: Mental health crisis in UK: Nurses’ workload ‘unmanageable’ as patients face risk of harm, poll finds - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: UK Department of Health and Social Care
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) surveyed 399 community mental health nurses in the UK, revealing that only one in five consider their workload manageable. The survey found that patients are frequently harmed due to high caseloads and time pressures, leading to deterioration in mental health conditions. Prof Nicola Ranger, RCN general secretary and chief executive, stated that this is a "perfect storm" of rising demand and insufficient staffing, with nurses reporting severe burnout and unsafe working conditions.  The Department of Health and Social Care defended its record funding push for mental health services, but experts warn that demand continues to outpace capacity.

articles.title: ‘Clearly stronger’: Germany’s Merz says Iran ‘humiliated’ US in its war | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Friedrich Merz, German Chancellor, criticized the US's war with Iran, stating that it has exposed a strategic problem for Washington and is causing economic harm to Germany.  He compared the situation to past military debacles like Afghanistan and Iraq, emphasizing the need for a swift end to the conflict. Johann Wadephul, German Foreign Minister, also expressed concerns about the impact of the war on global energy supplies and security, highlighting the ongoing threat of nuclear threats against Europe.

articles.title: Mali attacks: Russia's Africa Corps confirms withdrawal from Kidal
articles.rephrased_article: Russian forces have withdrawn from the northern Malian city of Kidal after separatist attacks. The Russia's Africa Corps, which had been assisting the military government, confirmed their departure and stated operations would continue elsewhere in the country.  The Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) claimed control of Kidal, while the Malian Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed in an apparent suicide bombing. The situation remains complex with civilian casualties reported.

articles.title: Anti-immigration group claims it did not organise Anzac Day booing despite post asking ‘how loud will you be’ | Anzac Day | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anti-immigration groups, including Fight for Australia and March for Australia, have encouraged booing at Anzac Day dawn services, sparking public debate about the role of welcome to country ceremonies.  The groups posted online asking followers if they would be booing this year's events, with some videos showing members of the National Socialist Network booing Indigenous elders giving acknowledgments of country. Bec Freedom, leader of Fight for Australia and March for Australia, claimed she did not organize the booing but defended her group's posts as expressing public sentiment about "woke rituals" at Anzac Day ceremonies.  However, police removed several individuals from dawn services in Perth who were identified as members of these groups.

articles.title: BJP stages protest against Kharge’s remarks on Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BJP Yuva Morcha members in Kalaburagi protested against AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge's remarks calling Prime Minister Narendra Modi a "terrorist." The protesters demanded an apology from Mr. Kharge, criticizing his derogatory statement and the Congress' opposition to the Women's Reservation Bill (Nari Shakti Bill).  The protest march, led by Virendra Patil Raikod, included several prominent BJP leaders including Basavaraj Mattimod and Rajkumar Patil Telkur.

articles.title: Central bank increases policy rate by 100bps to 11.5pc - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) raised its key policy rate to 11.5% on Monday, marking the first increase in almost three years. The decision, made by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), was driven by rising oil prices from the US-Israel war on Iran and concerns about inflation.  The MPC acknowledged that supply chain disruptions have contributed to uncertainty and warned that inflation could reach double digits in coming months before easing. While acknowledging the impact of global developments, the MPC emphasized the need for a tighter policy stance to maintain price stability and achieve sustainable economic growth.

articles.title: NSE sells 1% stake in Indian Gas Exchange to comply with regulatory norm - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: NSE, the National Stock Exchange of India, has reduced its stake in IGX, an electronic trading platform for natural gas, to 25% as part of regulatory requirements.  The exchange had acquired a 26% stake in IGX in March 2021 and partnered with it to launch exchange-traded derivatives based on domestic natural gas prices. IGX is also preparing for an initial public offering (IPO) by December this year, with plans to file draft papers with the capital markets regulator Sebi in the second quarter of calendar year 2026.

articles.title: World’s hottest cities: India transforms into a scorching furnace with cities shockingly hitting 46°C | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: India's heatwave continues to impact multiple cities, with temperatures reaching 46 degrees Celsius in several areas. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued warnings about the intense heat, predicting a heatwave in parts of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and central India. The IMD advises citizens to take precautions against heat stress by avoiding sun exposure during peak hours, staying hydrated, wearing loose-fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous activity.

articles.title: How does targeting water supply during war worsen the scarcity crisis? | Politics | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations warns of a looming "water bankruptcy" driven by climate change and rising global demands, including AI data centers.  In the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran, desalination plants supplying millions in the Gulf have become targets, highlighting an increasing trend of water infrastructure being targeted during conflict. Kaveh Madani, Director of the UNU Institute for Water, Environment & Health, and Zeina Moneer, an environmental policy and climate programs expert, discuss this growing vulnerability as global scarcity intensifies.

articles.title: Colombia offers record $1.4m-reward for rebel it blames for deadly bomb attack
articles.rephrased_article: Colombia's Defence Minister Pedro Sánchez has offered a record $1.4 million reward for information leading to the capture of rebel leader "Marlon", suspected of orchestrating a deadly bomb attack on the Pan-American Highway that killed 20 people.  The attack, which occurred just over a month before presidential elections, is linked to Iván Mordisco, Colombia's most wanted man and leader of a dissident group involved in illegal activities. President Gustavo Petro condemned the attack as terrorism and ordered additional troops to the region. The election for a new president takes place on May 31st.

articles.title: Mali in turmoil after insurgents seize towns and kill defence minister | Mali | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mali was struck by coordinated attacks by jihadist and separatist groups, resulting in the deaths of its defense minister and military intelligence chief. The Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) and the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) seized several towns and military bases, including Kati, Gao, Mopti, and Sévaré.  The Kremlin-run Africa Corps withdrew from Kidal after an agreement with the FLA was reached for their peaceful exit. The attacks have been condemned by international organizations like the UN, who are concerned about the humanitarian crisis in Mali.

articles.title: Fuel rush in parts of Hyderabad on April 27, dealers say adequate stocks available - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: On Monday, April 27, 2026, Hyderabad experienced a surge in demand for fuel at several petrol pumps, leading to long queues and temporary closures. The Telangana Petroleum Dealers Association (TPDA) attributed the disruption to a diesel supply issue rather than an overall shortage, stating that Sunday's lack of replenishment coincided with increased demand.  While some areas reported normal functioning, others experienced significant congestion due to limited fuel availability.

articles.title: Suspect in shooting at Trump's press dinner to appear in court - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A California man, Cole Allen, 31, was arrested after a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington. President Donald Trump and other high-ranking officials were present at the event when the attack occurred.  The suspect allegedly aimed to kill Trump and senior administration officials, according to acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche. The incident marks the third attempt on Trump’s life in two years. No motive has been determined, but the suspect was armed with a shotgun, handgun, and knives.

articles.title: Texas Girls Volleyball Team: Golden hearts: Texas girls’ volleyball team raised $9,000 for custodian who cheered them and waited for rides until 1 am | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Community High School Texas students raised $9,000 to purchase a car for their custodian, Abel Rodriguez, after discovering he stayed late to cheer them on and often waited until 1 am for a ride home. The initiative gained attention online in November 2025 when the students first organized the fundraiser, which was supported by local organizations like Group 1 Ford of Rockwall and J.R. Arey State Farm Agency.  The car purchase provided Rodriguez with reliable transportation, improving his daily mobility.

articles.title: World Cup 2026 prize money, fees to be increased for all teams: FIFA | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA, the global governing body of football, announced plans to increase prize money for all 48 teams participating in the 2026 World Cup. The proposal, aimed at addressing concerns raised by European teams regarding participation costs, is expected to be approved at a meeting on Tuesday.  The increased funding will help cover travel, operations, and taxes associated with the tournament, which will take place in Canada and Mexico alongside the United States.

articles.title: Michael Jackson biopic smashes box office record
articles.rephrased_article: The new Michael Jackson biopic, "Michael," has smashed box office records with a $217 million opening weekend globally. The film, starring Jaafar Jackson, surpassed previous record holders like "Bohemian Rhapsody" and "Oppenheimer." Despite mixed reviews from critics, the film's audience reception was overwhelmingly positive, earning it a 97% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.  The film focuses heavily on Jackson's musical career, including recreated concert performances and explores his strained relationship with his father.

articles.title: Labor senator deletes Anzac Day Instagram post after mistakenly including raunchy rap song | Labor party | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senator Helen Polley, a Tasmanian senator and chair of parliament's committee on law enforcement, deleted a social media video after it mistakenly included an explicit rap song over images of Anzac Day commemorations.  The video, posted to a smaller Instagram account than her official one, featured both the Australian national anthem and lyrics from rapper Chingy’s song "A$$ N Da Aurr". Polley's office stated that she has always been grateful for those who have served in the armed forces, including her father who served in World War Two. The video attracted negative comments about the inappropriate music choice before being removed.

articles.title: “No Bull, no bear—it’s a kangaroo market," says Nilesh Shah amid global uncertainty - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nilesh Shah, MD of Kotak AMC, describes the current market as a "kangaroo market" with unpredictable fluctuations driven by global and domestic events.  He highlights concerns about West Asia's geopolitical risks, India's dependence on energy imports, and potential economic pain if oil prices remain elevated. While acknowledging market recovery, Shah urges investors to be selective and adaptable, emphasizing the importance of long-term strategies and diversification across asset classes like credit AIFs, gold, and equities. He also warns that the real economy may soon feel the strain from geopolitical shocks and supply chain disruptions.

articles.title: Seizures in West Bengal cross ₹500-crore mark during ongoing polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Election Commission officials reported that illicit inducements seized in West Bengal during the ongoing Assembly elections surpassed ₹510 crore on Monday, April 27, 2026. This figure exceeds recoveries from both the 2021 and 2024 Lok Sabha polls held in the state. The seizures include cash, liquor, drugs, precious metals, and freebies worth a combined total of ₹58.28 crore, ₹126.85 crore, ₹110.12 crore, and ₹184.85 crore respectively.  The election schedule for West Bengal, Kerala, Assam, Puducherry, and Tamil Nadu was announced on March 15th with votes to be counted on May 4th.

articles.title: Constable martyred in terrorist attack on police checkpost in Balochistan's Pishin - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A police head constable, Naimatullah, was killed in a terrorist attack on a checkpost in Balochistan's Pishin district. Armed militants on a motorcycle opened fire using automatic weapons, resulting in the exchange of gunfire and the death of the police officer.  Security forces have launched a search operation to identify those responsible for the attack. No group has claimed responsibility for the incident.

articles.title: King Charles: King Charles proceeds with four-day US state visit after White House dinner shooting scare - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III and Queen Camilla are set to embark on a four-day state visit to the United States, marking the first such trip by a British monarch in two decades. The visit coincides with the 250th anniversary of American independence and comes amidst strained ties between Washington and London over the US-Israel conflict. Despite concerns raised by recent security incidents near the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, Charles is expected to reinforce shared values and cooperation during his meetings with Donald Trump, First Lady Melania Trump, and other officials. The royal couple will also visit New York to honour victims of the September 11 attacks and Virginia to highlight environmental initiatives.

articles.title: Somalia hunger crisis worsens as drought displaces more than 500,000 people | Hunger News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Somalia is facing a worsening hunger crisis as drought displaces over 500,000 people and humanitarian aid has declined sharply.  The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that displaced families are at high risk of starvation due to a lack of resources and support. The World Food Programme (WFP) warehouse destruction in Somalia has further hampered efforts to provide relief, leaving many families without aid or hope.

articles.title: Chad water well dispute escalates leaving at least 42 dead
articles.rephrased_article: At least 42 people have been killed and 10 injured in fighting between rival ethnic groups in eastern Chad, escalating from a dispute over a water well. Deputy Prime Minister Limane Mahamat led a delegation to the area and the situation has been brought under control. Deadly communal clashes are common in Chad, often triggered by competition over water and grazing land, exacerbated by recent refugee influxes from neighboring Sudan.

articles.title: Australians will call ‘bullshit’ on green energy without clearer benefits, Rudd warns | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kevin Rudd criticized Donald Trump's cuts to green industry support, warning that Australia would view climate policies as ineffective if they did not deliver tangible benefits.  He emphasized the need for affordable energy, reliable supply, and new job opportunities to ensure policy continuity. Malcolm Turnbull, also speaking at the event, highlighted Australia’s advantage in green industries due to its resources and proximity to export markets. The former prime ministers urged Australian governments to focus on delivering tangible results to resonate with citizens.

articles.title: Sun Pharma shares jump over 9% after firm announces $12 billion Organon acquisition - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sun Pharma announced the completion of a definitive agreement to acquire Organon, a US-based company specializing in women's health, for $12 billion. The transaction will be completed through a merger of Organon with a subsidiary of Sun Pharma.  The combined entity will become one of the top 25 global pharmaceutical companies and a leader in women's health with a strong portfolio of biosimilars.  Sun Pharma executive chairman, Dilip Shanghvi, expressed confidence that the acquisition will strengthen the company's global business and drive long-term growth. The deal is expected to close in early 2027.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh fuel crisis: Naidu orders three-hourly reports; officials deny shortage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh district authorities assured the public that there was no shortage of petrol or diesel in the state, urging against panic-buying and rumors circulating online.  The Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, following a review of 421 fuel outlets on Sunday, held another teleconference to address the situation. Despite this reassurance, queues remained at fuel stations throughout the day.

articles.title: Central bank increases policy rate by 100 bps to 11.5pc - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) raised its key policy rate to 11.5 percent on Monday, marking the first increase in almost three years. The decision was made in response to rising oil prices from the US-Israel war on Iran, which threatened to push inflation higher in the import-dependent nation.  The hike is expected to benefit exporters and remitters but will create difficulties for importers and increase the government's debt burden.  The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) saw a decline following the announcement.

articles.title: NASA satellite spots gleaming halo around New Zealand’s Chatham Islands | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A NASA satellite captured an unusual glowing halo around the Chatham Islands in the South Pacific. The glow, caused by a massive bloom of phytoplankton, is visible due to the high concentration of coccolithophores and was observed on January 10, 2026.  The phenomenon is linked to the presence of the Chatham Rise, an underwater mountain that influences ocean currents and nutrient levels, creating ideal conditions for phytoplankton growth. This bloom is a positive sign for marine biodiversity but also raises concerns about potential whale strandings due to the shallow waters surrounding the Chatham Rise.

articles.title: Varoufakis on Palantir, AI warfare, and the rise of tech lordism | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Yanis Varoufakis, former Greek finance minister, discussed Palantir’s new manifesto outlining a future of autonomous weapons and government-tech integration with host Redi Tlhabi. The manifesto has sparked global concern about the growing influence of Silicon Valley and its ties to militaries accused of war crimes. Varoufakis compared Palantir's ideology to racial hierarchies of Nazism and apartheid, arguing that it represents a dangerous trend of tech lordism.

articles.title: Trump says King will be 'very safe' during US visit after security talks
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated that King Charles III will be "very safe" during his state visit to the US, which will begin on Monday.  The White House and Buckingham Palace have held security talks following a gunman's attack at an event attended by Trump. The King's program will proceed largely as planned, with the UK government hoping it can ease diplomatic tensions. Sir Christian Turner, the UK ambassador to the US, said the visit would focus on renewing and revitalizing the "unique friendship" between the two countries.

articles.title: Bomb blast on Colombia highway leaves at least 20 dead ahead of May elections | Colombia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A bombing on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca department, Colombia, has killed 15 adults and five children, injuring 36 others. The attack, which occurred just over a month before presidential elections, was attributed to Iván Mordisco, leader of a dissident faction of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc).  Octavio Guzmán, the governor, described it as "the area’s most brutal and ruthless attack against the civilian population in decades". The military chief, Hugo López, stated that the bomb was detonated after assailants blocked traffic with a bus.

articles.title: Parachinar Airport becomes operational after long hiatus - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) and Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) have reactivated Parachinar Airport in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, marking a significant step towards restoring air transport in the region.  Following successful trials by Pakistan Army Aviation, the airport's runways were declared compliant with professional standards and safety protocols. The airport is expected to be further strengthened, enhancing regional connectivity, emergency response, and economic activity.

articles.title: West Bengal election 2026: Mood of Bengal suggests BJP victory in polls, will return during oath-taking ceremony: PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a rally in Barrackpore, West Bengal on the final day of campaigning for the Assembly elections. He expressed confidence that the BJP would form the next government and asserted his intention to return for the oath-taking ceremony after May 4th.  Modi accused the ruling TMC of presiding over “syndicate raj”, political violence, and economic decline, while promising employment opportunities for youth and a focus on restoring West Bengal's prosperity. He also appealed to Matua voters, assuring them of citizenship rights and protection against illegal infiltration.

articles.title: Balochistan Attack: BLA claims 27 attacks in Balochistan in 10 days, says 42 Pakistani soldiers killed - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) claimed responsibility for 27 operations in Pakistan's Balochistan province between April 15 and 25, alleging the deaths of at least 42 Pakistani military personnel. The group reported seizing weapons, overrunning security posts, and killing three of its own fighters during the attacks.  The BLA also claimed to have injured several others and captured one soldier. This follows a previous attack on a Pakistan Coast Guard patrol boat in the Arabian Sea near the Iran border, which killed three personnel.

articles.title: The war on Iran is eroding nuclear non-proliferation | Nuclear Weapons | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The ongoing war between the US and Israel against Iran is jeopardizing the integrity of the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT).  At the upcoming five-year review conference in New York, states will grapple with whether Iran's case raises concerns about the treaty's effectiveness. The war has raised questions about the NPT's ability to protect non-nuclear weapon states from coercive actions by powerful nations, particularly when those actions are based on unsubstantiated claims of nuclear weapons development.  The conference must address these issues and reaffirm the sanctity of the NPT's core principles.

articles.title: Oil prices rise as US-Iran peace talks stall
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices rose sharply after US and Iran peace talks stalled again, with Brent crude reaching $109.33 a barrel. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, crucial for global oil supplies, has been blamed for the price increase, as traders wait for concrete evidence of easing tensions.  Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, is currently in St Petersburg meeting with Vladimir Putin to discuss regional developments and safe transit through the strait.

articles.title: HSBC ‘reviewing’ private school perk for bankers in Hong Kong | HSBC | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: HSBC is reviewing its school fee subsidy program for bankers in Hong Kong as part of a broader restructuring under CEO Georges Elhedery. The bank is considering whether to eliminate the perk entirely or modify it.  The program, which costs millions annually and is not offered in other HSBC hubs, has caused tension between headquarters in London and local staff. This review comes amid Elhedery's efforts to streamline operations, exit certain markets, and focus on Asia, including integrating Hang Seng Bank into the group.

articles.title: Axis Bank shares tank 5% after weak Q4. What are Motilal Oswal, other top brokerages saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Axis Bank's Q4FY26 financial results showed a 4.7% year-on-year increase in interest income to Rs 32,724 crore and a 5% rise in net interest income to Rs 14,457 crore.  The bank also reported a 0.37% net non-performing asset ratio, indicating improved asset quality. Motilal Oswal, JM Financial, and Elara Capital all maintained Buy ratings on the stock with target prices ranging from Rs 1,475 to Rs 1,629. These brokerages attributed the positive outlook to Axis Bank's strong deposit franchise, improving asset quality, and conservative balance sheet.

articles.title: Pakistan, China sign 3 MoUs to boost desalination, agri technology, tea sector cooperation - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan and China signed three Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) on Monday to enhance cooperation in water desalination, agricultural technology, and the tea industry. The agreements were witnessed by President Asif Ali Zardari, who is currently in China for a week-long visit.  The MoUs involved Sindh local government collaborating with Lucion Environmental Technology Group on a seawater desalination project in Karachi, as well as an agreement between the Sindh local government and Long Ping Hi-tech Information Company for agricultural technology cooperation. Finally, a third MoU was signed by Meskay & Femtee Trading Company, Hunan Tea Group, and Jiaolong International Technology (Hainan) to promote cooperation across all areas of the tea industry in both countries.

articles.title: Obesity and malnutrition in Delhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Laxman, a six-year-old, and his group of school friends from Kidwai Nagar, South Delhi, are enjoying their walk home from school. The children, dressed in bright blue uniforms, are excited to be back after lunch at a roadside food cart where they purchase double-fried potatoes with red food coloring and sugar sprinkles.

articles.title: Virginia Hidden Barracks: Lost for 200 years: Virginia dig uncovers hidden barracks of America’s first soldiers | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists from the Colonial Williamsburg Foundation have uncovered the long-lost Revolutionary War barracks, revealing a close-up view of daily life for Continental Army soldiers. The barracks, constructed in 1776 to house up to 2,000 soldiers and 100 horses, were obscured for nearly 200 years until their foundations were revealed during routine excavations.  The site's high degree of preservation is attributed to a catastrophic fire in 1781, which sealed the structure from further disturbance. Artifacts recovered include chimney bases, military buckles, musket balls, and coins, providing insights into soldiers' living conditions and daily routines. The foundation plans to use these findings to educate the public about the personal experiences of early American soldiers during the Revolutionary War.

articles.title: North Korea opens museum commemorating troops killed fighting for Russia | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea opened a memorial museum in Pyongyang commemorating its soldiers killed fighting alongside Russia in the war in Ukraine. The inaugural ceremony, attended by Kim Jong Un, Vyacheslav Volodin, and Andrei Belousov, marked the first anniversary of what both countries described as the end of an operation to liberate Russia's Kursk border region from a Ukrainian incursion.  Kim Jong Un praised the fallen soldiers as symbols of heroism and pledged continued support for Russia's defense policy, while Vladimir Putin promised further strengthening of the "comprehensive strategic partnership" between the two nations.

articles.title: Cole Tomas Allen: Suspected gunman at Washington press dinner identified as 31-year-old Californian
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, a 31-year-old mechanical engineer and game developer from Torrance, California, was arrested after exchanging gunfire with security agents at the Washington Hilton hotel during the White House Correspondents' Dinner.  Allen told officials he wanted to shoot members of the Trump administration, according to sources. Trump confirmed that Allen had "a lot of hatred in his heart" for a while and suggested he had a manifesto. The suspect was armed with a shotgun, handgun, and multiple knives and was taken to hospital for evaluation.  Todd Blanche, acting US Attorney General, stated the motive is still under investigation but preliminary findings suggest targeting administration officials, likely including President Trump. Allen's online presence reveals his involvement in various activities, including game development, teaching, and political donations.

articles.title: Weather tracker: Torrential rain in southern China leads to flooding fears | Extreme weather | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Widespread heavy rainfall is impacting southern China, with the Office of the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters and the Ministry of Emergency Management urging preparedness for potential flooding.  Torrential rain is also forecast in Bangladesh, northern Myanmar, and parts of India, while central and northern India are experiencing extreme heat waves with temperatures exceeding 45°C. Heavy rainfall has caused damage in Nigeria, particularly in Jalingo, due to poor drainage infrastructure. Unseasonably cold weather is affecting western Canada, with daytime temperatures below freezing in Calgary, Edmonton, and Saskatoon.

articles.title: Karachi court orders release of five women held for staging protest against ‘enforced disappearance’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A judicial magistrate in Karachi ordered the release of five women, including a Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) activist, who were arrested for staging a protest against the alleged enforced disappearance of Fozia Baloch's brother. The women were booked under sections of the Pakistan Penal Code related to sedition and disobedience to orders.  The court discharged them on personal bonds after hearing arguments from both sides and directed the investigating officer to submit an investigation report.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Women protesting enforced disappearance face sedition charges, highlighting potential abuse of power.

articles.title: 2,200-year-old Roman shipwreck reveals the secret formula that kept ancient ships afloat | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists in Croatia have discovered a Roman-era shipwreck, Ilovik–Paržine 1, dating back approximately 2,200 years. The preserved structure provides valuable insight into the Roman strategy of shipbuilding for maritime trade and reveals how ancient shipbuilders used natural materials like pitch and beeswax to protect their vessels from seawater and decomposition.  The boat's multiple layers of paint suggest regular servicing and repairs, indicating a systematic approach to maintaining its durability. Pollen analysis also suggests that the ship was repaired at various locations around the Adriatic Sea. This discovery highlights the Roman understanding of waterproofing techniques, chemical formulas, and the importance of regular maintenance in shipbuilding.

articles.title: Taiwan court hands down jail terms in TSMC trade secrets case | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Taiwan court has sentenced a former TSMC employee and four others to jail terms ranging from 10 months to 10 years for stealing trade secrets related to the chipmaker's technology.  The Tokyo Electron unit was fined $5 million, while the case involved allegations of theft under the National Security Act. The court's ruling follows one of Taiwan's most prominent cases concerning its core technologies.

articles.title: Gina Rinehart calls for immigrants’ social media to be screened in Anzac memorial speech | Gina Rinehart | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gina Rinehart, Australia's richest person, called for stricter immigration screening and criticized the Australian government's handling of terrorism threats.  Rinehart, who spoke at an Anzac memorial service in Sydney, urged the government to screen immigrants' social media accounts and expressed concern about the teaching of patriotism in schools. Richard Marles, the deputy prime minister, attended the event and spoke before its official commencement.

articles.title: Rajya Sabha Chairman accepts merger of seven AAP MPs with BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C.P. Radhakrishnan, the Rajya Sabha Chairman, accepted the merger of seven Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MPs with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), increasing the BJP's strength in the Upper House to 113 and reducing AAP to three members. The move followed a significant political realignment in the Rajya Sabha on April 24th, when seven of the AAP's ten members joined the BJP. Arvind Kejriwal, the AAP national convener, criticized the BJP for betraying Punjabis.

articles.title: AI drives global IT spending to $6.31 trillion, but Indian IT firms face a margin squeeze, warns Gartner - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Lovelock, the CIO of IBM, stated that India has a unique opportunity in managed services due to the global shift towards AI initiatives.  While India's IT industry faces challenges from a structural headwind, with clients expecting lower prices for AI-enabled services compared to software companies, Lovelock believes that India can leverage its deep talent base to capture demand for AI and agentic automation in managed services. He also noted that India does not need to compete directly with the United States in data center construction as AI delivery can tolerate distance.  However, he warned that margins will face pressure in the near term due to overbuilding and a lack of standardized monetization strategies.

articles.title: Global military spending continues to rise as European and Asian expenditures surge - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: World military expenditure reached $2,887 billion in 2025, a slight increase from the previous year. The top three spenders—the USA, China, and Russia— accounted for 51% of global spending.  Military spending in Europe increased by 14%, driven by Russia's war with Ukraine and NATO member countries' rearmament efforts. Asia and Oceania saw the fastest growth since 2009, with China leading the way. The United States saw a decline in spending due to lack of new military aid for Ukraine.  Spending in the Middle East remained stable despite ongoing conflicts.

articles.title: White House Gala Attack: ‘I don’t expect forgiveness’: What DC shooter’s manifesto reveals about White House gala attack - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, the suspect in the White House Correspondents’ Dinner shooting, sent a 1,052-word manifesto to family members detailing his motives and operational plan. The document stated that he viewed the attack as a "duty" motivated by his opposition to US leadership's actions and specifically targeted administration officials from highest to lowest ranking, excluding Kash Patel, the FBI chief. Allen planned to use buckshot instead of slugs to minimize casualties but was ultimately unsuccessful in carrying out the attack.  The incident resulted in chaos at the event attended by President Donald Trump and senior officials, who were evacuated as gunfire broke out.

articles.title: Rockets thrash LeBron’s Lakers; Wembanyama triumphant on Spurs’ return | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Houston Rockets defeated the Los Angeles Lakers 115-96 to cut their deficit in the Western Conference series to 3-1.  Victor Wembanyama returned from a concussion and scored 27 points for the San Antonio Spurs, who are on the verge of advancing to the next round after defeating the Portland Trail Blazers. The Boston Celtics dominated the Philadelphia 76ers, led by Payton Pritchard and Jayson Tatum, while the Toronto Raptors edged out the Cleveland Cavaliers in a close game.

articles.title: Australia’s south-east set for drier and hotter winter as BoM forecasts potential El Niño | Australia weather | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Meteorological Organization and the Bureau of Meteorology have indicated a high likelihood of an El Niño developing in the Pacific Ocean, which could lead to drier and hotter conditions across much of southeast Australia from May to July.  This phenomenon is expected to push up global temperatures as well. While some models suggest a strong El Niño event, forecasts at this time are less reliable, and the strength of its impact on Australian rainfall may vary depending on the location of the warmest waters in the Pacific. The Bureau of Meteorology predicts that parts of northern and western Victoria, southern South Australia, and the southwest of Western Australia could also experience drier conditions.

articles.title: Supreme Court takes suo motu note of assault on woman advocate, issues directions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court took suo motu action in a brutal assault case involving a woman advocate in New Delhi, directing the Delhi Police Commissioner to hand over the investigation to a senior officer. The court also ordered the police to look into three hospitals' refusal of admission to the victim and investigate allegations against her husband's in-laws regarding the disappearance of her two minor children. Manoj Kumar, the alleged assailant, was arrested on April 26th after confessing to stabbing his wife on April 22nd during a family dispute.

articles.title: Reliance Industries shares dip over 1% after Q4 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, others saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Reliance Industries reported a 13% year-over-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 2.98 lakh crore for the quarter, with profit slipping 8% to Rs 18,645 crore. Operating performance remained largely flat, and EBITDA eased 0.3% YoY to Rs 48,588 crore. Jio Platforms delivered strong revenue growth of 13%, while Reliance Retail saw a marginal increase in profitability.  Morgan Stanley maintained an Overweight rating on the company with an unchanged target price of Rs 1,803, citing strong retail growth and potential for margin recovery in the O2C segment. Goldman Sachs also maintained its Buy rating with an unchanged target price of Rs 1,910, highlighting strong retail growth but noting weaker O2C margins.

articles.title: Iran FM Araghchi says he discussed conditions for continuing US talks with ‘friends in Pakistan’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, concluded a regional diplomatic tour that included visits to Pakistan, Oman, and Russia. During his trip to Pakistan, he met with Pakistani officials to discuss the path forward for negotiations between Iran and the United States, citing US demands as a barrier to progress. He also emphasized the importance of safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting Iran's commitment to regional stability.  Araghchi arrived in Russia on Monday to consult with Russian officials about the ongoing war between the US and Israel and the current situation.

articles.title: Guinness World Records: London sets Guinness World Record with 440-metre tiramisu made by 100 chefs using 50,000 biscuits | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: London hosted a record-breaking event, creating a 440.6-meter long tiramisu that surpassed the previous record of 273.5 meters set in Milan. The Guinness World Records officially recognized the dessert as the longest ever made.  The achievement involved meticulous planning and coordination by over 100 Italian chefs who worked for two days to assemble the dessert, ensuring uniformity across hundreds of meters. Chef Mirko Ricci, who previously held the title, returned to reclaim it, emphasizing that the record was a celebration of Italian culinary identity on an international stage.
