The dessert served as a gesture of goodwill and cultural exchange, reinforcing the intersection between gastronomy and performance.

articles.title: Activists accused of raiding Israeli weapons factory face trial in Germany | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Five European nationals, known as the "Ulm Five," face trial in Germany for allegedly attacking an Elbit Systems factory in Ulm. The prosecution argues that their actions were motivated by anti-Semitism and are part of a larger campaign against Israel's arms industry.  The activists, who hold Irish, British, Spanish, and German citizenship, claim their actions were civil disobedience aimed at stopping violations of international law. Amnesty International has raised concerns about the use of Section 129 – a "criminal organization" statute – to prosecute political protests. The trial is expected to last until July.

articles.title: Record bear sightings in Japan cause alarm as hibernation ends | Japan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Bears are emerging from hibernation in Japan, causing increased contact with humans, outpacing the 2025 record for bear attacks.  Authorities have issued warnings in several prefectures, including Iwate and Fukushima, urging caution as sightings near populated areas continue to rise. The incidents follow a record-breaking year of bear attacks in 2025, with one possible fatal mauling already reported this year. Experts are hopeful that plentiful beechnut crops could reduce the number of hungry bears venturing into human settlements, but some experts warn that bears may have learned to associate humans with food sources and become less fearful.

articles.title: Another vessel seized off Somali coast as threat level increased
articles.rephrased_article: UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) raised the threat level to "substantial" after a cargo ship was seized off the coast of Somalia on Sunday. This follows at least four other vessels targeted in suspected piracy incidents in the last week, including a fishing vessel and an oil tanker. The UKMTO warned that weather conditions are conducive to small boat operations by pirates, who have re-emerged in this area after a decline in activity three years ago.  The hijackings underscore the continued threat of piracy off the Somali coast.

articles.title: Father and four children escaped blaze that killed two others at home in Blue Mountains foothills | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NSW Fire and Rescue assistant commissioner Andrew Faunce confirmed that two bodies were found inside a destroyed home in Bowen Mountain, believed to be those of two children. The fire, which broke out early Monday morning, was brought under control by firefighters after arriving around 2.10am.  The family of six, including the mother who was on her way back to the home, escaped the blaze with minor burns and smoke inhalation. Police are investigating the cause of the fire.

articles.title: India Inc net profit rising in double digits in Q4 despite RIL's dip - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Companies across the sample saw a 13% increase in net profit year-on-year, marking the first time in two quarters that growth exceeded single digits. Revenue grew by 9%, reaching its highest level in seven quarters.  Banking and finance companies contributed significantly to this growth, with their combined revenue and net profit accounting for 28% and 47% of the total sample's figures respectively. The operating margin contracted slightly year-on-year due to lower profitability within the lending sector, but improved when excluding those companies.

articles.title: ‘Borderline genius’ shooter wanted to ‘fix world’s issues’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, a 31-year-old independent game developer, is the suspect who breached a security checkpoint and opened fire at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.  Authorities believe Allen intended to target members of the Trump administration based on preliminary evidence found in his writings. Allen had no known criminal record or prior run-ins with law enforcement but was recently associated with a group called ‘The Wide Awakes’ and made radical statements about doing “something” to fix the world's issues.  He legally purchased firearms in 2023 and 2025, and was apprehended after firing two shots at the event.

articles.title: ‘Our math is different’: Iran warns Gulf countries of ‘fourfold’ retaliation after Trump threat - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian vice president Esmail Saghab Esfahani warned of fourfold retaliation against countries supporting damage to Iran's oil infrastructure following US President Donald Trump's remarks about pressure on Tehran's oil sector.  Esfahani stated that any attack on Iranian facilities would result in a significantly escalated response, emphasizing the scale of potential retaliation. The comments came after Trump indicated sustained pressure could disrupt Iran's ability to transfer oil and highlighted heightened tensions around Iran's energy infrastructure. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Russia for talks with President Vladimir Putin on ceasefire efforts and regional developments, while Iran presented a two-stage plan to the US via Pakistani intermediaries to end the conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Assembly elections 2026 LIVE: Leaders make last ditch efforts to woo voters in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi focused on the Matua community's citizenship concerns ahead of the final phase of West Bengal elections. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee held a roadshow in her constituency, Bhabanipur, criticizing voter deletions and the Election Commission-appointed administration.  Arvind Kejriwal, former Delhi Chief Minister, joined the Trinamool Congress campaign in West Bengal. The Election Commission of India (ECI) announced a stringent security plan for the second phase of the elections.

articles.title: Men accused of raping cellmates mistakenly allowed to stay in shared cells by Queensland prison staff | Prisons | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Queensland Corrective Services has been criticized by an ombudsman's report for allowing prisoners to share cells despite strict protocols, citing overcrowding and concerns about documenting sexual assault allegations. The report found that prisoners, often double-celled due to capacity issues, were sometimes placed in shared cells after alleged assaults, with one prisoner later charged with rape after being transferred to another facility under investigation.  The ombudsman also highlighted health facility deficiencies and complaints of undercooked chicken served at the Brisbane correctional center.

articles.title: Nifty expected to oscillate between 23,400 and 24,500: Analysts - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: DHARMESH SHAH, SUDEEP SHAH, and TANMAY SHAH are analysts who predict the Nifty will likely oscillate between 23,400 and 24,500 this week. They suggest traders capitalize on dips to buy high-quality stocks with strong earnings support at 23,100.  Analysts recommend a bull call spread strategy for near-term upside potential. JSW Steel, Power Grid, Cochin Shipyard, Aster DM Healthcare, and Coal India are among the top stock picks for the week.

articles.title: Oil prices rise amid stalled US-Iran peace talks | Oil and Gas News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices rose more than 2 percent on Sunday after US and Iran failed to hold a second round of peace talks in Pakistan.  Brent crude, the global benchmark, reached $106.99 per barrel as uncertainty surrounding the fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran persists. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Russia for further negotiations with President Vladimir Putin after departing Islamabad without direct engagement with US envoys.

articles.title: Trump opts for talks with Iran over the phone - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump halted US diplomatic travel to Pakistan in light of Iran's reluctance to participate in peace talks, but stated the US would continue negotiations by phone. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Islamabad and met with Pakistani officials to discuss a framework for ending the war in the Middle East before departing for Moscow.  Prime Minister Muhammad Shahbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir of Pakistan expressed gratitude for Araghchi's efforts and acknowledged the role of Pakistan in facilitating dialogue. The US, UK, and other countries are calling for an end to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.  The Revolutionary Guards, a powerful Iranian organization, stated they have no intention of lifting their blockade on the strait.

articles.title: 'I wasn’t making it easy for them': Trump recounts tense moments after shots were fired during White House dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A California man was apprehended after opening fire at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, prompting a security response and forcing President Donald Trump to be escorted from the venue.  The suspect, who officials believe targeted the president and other senior figures, exchanged gunfire with Secret Service agents before being taken into custody. Trump, initially mistaking the sound for a dropped tray, described his curiosity about the situation as potentially delaying the agents' response.

articles.title: Ghazipur teen death: Prohibitory order issued, protests banned; visit to victim's village barred - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttar Pradesh government issued a statement banning all demonstrations and condolences visits to the village of a teenager who died earlier this month in Ghazipur. Ghazipur District Magistrate Anupam Shukla imposed Section 163 of the BNSS, prohibiting political gatherings within the district due to concerns over law and order. The government attributed the unrest to "unverified rumours" spread by "mischievous elements" and Opposition parties.

articles.title: US strike kills three on alleged narco boat as campaign death toll hits 185 | US foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US military claims to have killed three men on a boat in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, citing it as being involved in narco-trafficking operations.  This latest strike brings the US campaign's death toll to at least 185 and follows numerous similar attacks in recent months. The US Southern Command stated that intelligence confirmed the vessel was transiting known drug trafficking routes, but legal experts and rights groups question the legality of these operations, suggesting they could constitute extrajudicial killings.

articles.title: NCSC seeks report on Mamata Banerjee's alleged 'derogatory' remark against SC community - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) has taken suo motu cognisance of a video clip allegedly showing West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee using derogatory language against the SC community during an election rally. The NCSC has directed the Chief Secretary and Director General of Police to submit a detailed report within three days, warning that they may issue summons if no response is received. NCSC Chairman Kishor Makwana condemned the alleged remarks as "unfortunate" and stated that such incidents are punishable under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. The BJP has also criticized Ms. Banerjee's comments, accusing her of being anti-Dalit and anti-SC.

articles.title: Neymar excluded from official World Cup sticker album: Clearest sign his World Cup journey is over? | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Neymar, a former star for the Brazil national team, was not included in the official Panini World Cup sticker album for 2026. This decision reflects his recent absence from international matches due to injury and a disrupted club career, which has impacted his inclusion probability according to the Panini selection process. The album's production relies on tracking player call-ups and form over time, with players who have been recently selected having higher chances of inclusion. Neymar’s situation is further complicated by his move to Saudi Arabia and subsequent injuries, making it uncertain whether he will be able to return to the national team in time for the World Cup.

articles.title: Iran war live: Araghchi to meet Putin; Trump says Tehran can call for talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, traveled to Russia for talks with Vladimir Putin.  Donald Trump stated that Iranian leaders could initiate phone calls if they wish to engage in dialogue. Meanwhile, Israeli forces continued their attacks on southern Lebanon despite a US-brokered ceasefire.

articles.title: Trade deal with U.S. harming farmers’ interests, says AIKS leader - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ashok Dhawale, president of All India Kisan Sabha, criticized trade agreements with the United States for harming Indian farmers, citing weakened domestic agriculture and rising input costs as contributing factors to a crisis.  He blamed flawed government policies and lack of effective land reforms for the situation, while demanding interest-free loans, implementation of the M.S. Swaminathan Commission recommendations, and support for tenant farmer families.

articles.title: Children’s shoe retailers say closure of specialist shops is harming foot health | Retail industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Footwear specialists are raising concerns about the rise of foot problems in children, particularly bunions.  They argue that ill-fitting shoes can lead to lifelong issues with gait and foot function. Footwear Hub, a not-for-profit organization formed by 40 specialist shops, has launched a campaign urging parents to prioritize proper shoe fitting for their children's feet, comparing it to the importance of dental care.  The organization reports seeing more children with bunions and other foot conditions due to improper footwear choices.

articles.title: Kanyaka Parameswari Jayanti celebrated with religious fervour, decision to observe her birthday as State function hailed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Vasavi Kanyaka Parameshwari temple in Khammam celebrated Goddess Kanyaka Parameswari Jayanti with special pujas and religious discourses.  Temple committee chairman Mellacheruvu Venkateshwara Rao expressed gratitude to the Telangana government for declaring the festival an official state celebration, highlighting the temple's values of peace, equality, and righteousness.

articles.title: Renewable energy will boost national security and protect UK from sabotage, minister says | Renewable energy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Shanks, the UK's energy minister, emphasized that renewable energy sources like wind farms and solar panels are more resilient against physical attacks than traditional fossil fuel power stations. Fatih Birol, the executive director of the International Energy Agency, has also advised against new oil exploration in the North Sea, suggesting that renewables are a better path to bolstering UK energy security.  Military experts have similarly called for increased investment in renewable energy infrastructure, citing its ability to enhance national resilience and deter potential aggression.

articles.title: ‘Civil service exam tests emotional fortitude rather than intellectual capability’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Benjo P. Jose, a 2024 batch IAS officer, advised civil service aspirants to avoid blindly following strategies and instead focus on their individual needs during the exam preparation process. He emphasized the importance of emotional resilience and encouraged aspiring civil servants to cultivate diverse interests beyond just the UPSC examination. Fabi Rasheed, another 2024 batch IAS officer, stressed the need for a clear understanding of personal motivations for joining the civil service.  Sylesh Fernandes, an exam mentor, urged students to prioritize core subjects like Indian polity and maintain consistent study schedules.

articles.title: Cheap spirits, pricey condoms: how war in the Middle East is shifting the way Australians spend | Consumer affairs | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Orora, an ASX-listed alcohol packaging company, has observed a global shift towards cheaper spirits since the start of the Iran war.  Cochlear, an Australian medical device company, experienced a significant market decline due to weakened global demand for its cochlear implants, attributed to deteriorating consumer sentiment. Nick Scali, Harvey Norman, and Adairs have seen share price drops as consumers cut back on discretionary purchases like furniture and home appliances due to rising living costs and anxiety over jobs.  The escalating geopolitical situation has fueled concerns about the Australian economy, with increased use of buy now, pay later platforms for essential items and a surge in calls to financial counseling services related to mortgage payments and future anxieties.

articles.title: Two youths held for hurling petrol bomb in Ranipet over previous enmity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Ajith Kumar and V. Bharath Raj, aged 23 and 24 respectively, were arrested for throwing a petrol bomb at the house of Antony, a VCK functionary in Ranipet town. The incident occurred after an altercation between Antony and the two youths who had been consuming liquor in front of his home.  The police are investigating the case and have lodged the suspects at Central Prison in Vellore.

articles.title: Mali defence minister killed amid flurry of insurgent attacks | Mali | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mali’s defense minister, Sadio Camara, was killed in an attack on his residence by insurgents including the West African affiliate of al-Qaida. The coordinated assaults, carried out by Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) and a Tuareg-dominated rebel group, targeted multiple locations across the country, including Bamako airport and Kidal.  The UN called for an international response to violence and terrorism in the Sahel region while analysts suggested that Russia’s involvement in Mali has been negatively impacted by the attacks.

articles.title: AHINDA has brought political benefits to Congress: Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister Satish Jarkiholi spoke at a symposium celebrating the 25th anniversary of the AHINDA organization, emphasizing its role in strengthening the Congress and advocating for the interests of exploited communities. He stated that AHINDA aims to bring all deprived communities under one umbrella and will hold various programs throughout the year.  Retired High Court judge H.N. Nagamohan Das also spoke at the event, urging members to remain active and ensure their struggles are clear and guided by morality.

articles.title: Mumbai-Pune Missing Link project to be inaugurated on May 1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) officials announced the upcoming inauguration of the Mumbai-Pune Missing Link on May 1st, Maharashtra Day. The new road, connecting Khopoli to Kusgaon, will reduce travel time by half an hour and alleviate traffic congestion at Khandala Ghat.  The project, originally valued at ₹6,695 crore, was delayed due to COVID-19, technical challenges, and weather conditions but is now complete with 100% work finished. The Missing Link will connect the existing Mumbai-Pune Expressway by bypassing the Khandala Ghat, reducing the distance between Khopoli and Kusgaon to 13.3 km from the current 19 km.

articles.title: Former BJD MP Manjulata Mandal, ex-MLA husband Muktikanta and others quit party - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Several BJD leaders in Odisha's Bhadrak Lok Sabha constituency resigned from the party, citing internal discord and a perceived conspiracy against them. Former MP Manjulata Mandal and her husband, former Dhamnagar MLA Muktikanta Mandal, along with other leaders like Jagannath Swain, submitted their resignations to Naveen Patnaik, the BJD president.  Prafulla Samal, a former minister and BJD vice-president, downplayed the significance of these departures, stating that they do not necessarily reflect public support for the party.

articles.title: TMC lodges complaint against BJP candidate over alleged misuse of national flag - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TMC filed a complaint against BJP candidate Papia Adhikari for allegedly using the national flag during her campaign in Tollygunge.  The complaint, filed by Kohinoor Mazumdar, TMC spokesperson and vice-president of the West Bengal Trinamool Chhatra Parishad, alleges that Ms. Adhikari used a dupatta bearing the Indian tricolour while campaigning and wiped her face with it. The police are examining the complaint.

articles.title: Raghu Rai's lens chronicled the soul of India: Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi expressed condolences for the passing of renowned photographer Raghu Rai, who died at age 83 on April 26, 2026.  The Congress leader praised Rai's work as a chronicler of India's soul and its defining moments, noting that he preserved the nation's memory through his photography. Gandhi offered condolences to Rai's family, colleagues, and admirers across generations.

articles.title: Raghu Rai death: The Hindu collection of stories on renowned photographer Raghu Rai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Raghu Rai, a renowned photographer, passed away on Sunday (April 26, 2026) at the age of [insert age]. His family confirmed that he had battled cancer for several years.  Rai's career spanned over half a century and his images captured the essence of India, from religious figures like the Dalai Lama to political leaders such as Indira Gandhi.

articles.title: Trinamool running a reign of terror in West Bengal, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, senior Congress leader, accused the Trinamool Congress (TMC) of running a reign of terror in West Bengal ahead of the state assembly election.  He condemned the murder of Debdeep Chatterjee, a Congress worker, allegedly by TMC-affiliated goons and called for immediate action against those responsible. The Congress has demanded justice and security for the victim's family while maintaining its commitment to non-violence.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged political violence and murder raise concerns about safety and justice.

articles.title: ‘Kozhikode-Kannur stretch recorded most stone attacks on trains in past three years’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Government Railway Police (GRP) and Railway Protection Force (RPF) data reveals a significant number of stone-pelting incidents on trains in the Southern Railway division, particularly along the Kozhikode-Kannur stretch. The most targeted trains include the Sampark Kranti Express, Vande Bharat Express, Mangaluru-Chennai Superfast, and Netravati Express. While arrests have been made in some cases, due to a lack of direct witnesses and surveillance footage, suspects are being identified based on complaints from injured passengers. One such suspect, Krishnakumar, 30, was apprehended for attacking an undergraduate girl student on the Alappuzha-Kannur Executive Express.  The GRP and RPF are investigating these incidents and implementing measures like improved surveillance coverage and motorcycle patrol squads to deter future attacks.

articles.title: Kallayi desilting project gathers pace, 45% of work completed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Irrigation department is making progress on the Kallayi river rejuvenation project, with 45% of desilting work completed. The project aims to remove 3.29 lakh cubic meters of silt from a 4.2-kilometer stretch, and dredging operations are underway at a cost of ₹12.98 crore.  The work is expected to be finished by the end of May, but fishermen have requested a wider desilting area near the Kothi estuary. The project was initiated in February 2025 after a survey, with dredging being carried out by West Coast Dredging Company.

articles.title: Fish prices surge in Kozhikode as climate stress shrinks catches - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fishermen in Kozhikode are reporting significantly reduced catches and higher fish prices due to rising sea surface temperatures (SST) and the El Niño effect. Scientists at the ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI) attribute the decline to plankton migrating into deeper waters, forcing fish to follow their food source.  Boat owners in the region are struggling with low catches, high fuel costs, and declining incomes, leading to reduced harbour activity and a decrease in migrant workers from other states.

articles.title: NGT issues notice to Centre over risks from hanging glaciers in central Himalaya - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) has ordered responses from various government agencies and organizations regarding the dangers posed by hanging glaciers in central Himalaya. The tribunal, hearing a case based on a newspaper report, found that four researchers from different institutions assessed the potential impact of glacier retreat and instability, concluding that ice avalanches could reach major settlements.  The NGT also noted violations of the Environment (Protection) Act related to these concerns, prompting the inclusion of several government bodies as respondents in the proceedings.

articles.title: Govt. may establish labs in varsities to train students for space sector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Union Minister Jitendra Singh reviewed plans to establish seven space laboratories in universities and colleges across India, aiming to build a skilled workforce for the expanding space sector. The initiative is part of efforts to attract private investment and support the growth of India's burgeoning private space ecosystem, which has seen over 400 startups emerge since 2019.  The government has launched programs like the Technology Adoption Fund to facilitate commercialization of innovations and train individuals in specialized areas related to space technology.

articles.title: Two flee police custody in Kochi, one nabbed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sooraj and Russel, two men arrested in a theft case, escaped custody from the Kadavanthra police on Sunday.  One was recaptured after a brief chase while efforts are underway to locate the other suspect. The escape occurred around 5:45 p.m. near the Chendamangalam bridge after being produced before a magistrate at Paravur. Teams from Paravur and Vadakkekara police stations are involved in the search.

articles.title: Anti-Trump sentiment being examined as motive for White House press dinner shooting | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Investigators are examining the motive behind a shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, where President Donald Trump and members of his administration were present. The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, allegedly created a manifesto outlining his grievances against the administration, targeting senior officials like Trump.  The manifesto, published by multiple outlets including the New York Post, lists targets ranked from highest to lowest priority, with Trump at the top. The suspect reportedly sent writings to family members expressing anti-Trump sentiments before the shooting and referred to himself as the "Friendly Federal Assassin."

articles.title: Advertorial tracing Ramesh Chennithala’s political odyssey raises eyebrows in UDF circles - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A full-page advertorial in an English-language newspaper highlighting the political career of Ramesh Chennithala, a senior Congress leader, sparked controversy within the party. The article, sponsored by Prajin Babu, District Congress Committee general secretary, was criticized for potentially serving as a political advertisement ahead of the Assembly election results on May 4th.  Chennithala's office denied any involvement in the advertorial. The incident coincided with warnings from Sunny Joseph, Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee president, against promoting leadership choices on social media and within the party.

articles.title: UK government move to delay social media ban faces pushback in Lords | Social media ban | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Peers will vote on a government amendment that could delay action on children's access to social media for up to three years. Campaigners and senior figures in the Lords are criticizing this move, arguing it undermines earlier commitments to act quickly and risks only implementing limited interventions like parental controls.  The amendment, led by Tory peer John Nash, would force the government to raise the minimum age for accessing social media platforms to 16 within 12 months.  This proposal has been backed by peers three times previously, but the government used its majority to block it. If the bill does not complete its passage in time, the government risks losing it entirely.

articles.title: Residents complain of suffocation after open landfill site catches fire near Gudiyatham - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire broke out at a four-acre open landfill site in Gudiyatham municipality, near Gudiyatham town in Vellore, on Sunday. The fire, which started on Friday evening and was rekindled on Sunday morning, caused thick smoke and prompted complaints of suffocation and eye irritation from residents and motorists.  P. Dhanalakshmi, the Commissioner of Gudiyatham municipality, stated that a probe will be conducted to determine the cause of the fire, while officials have deployed multiple tankers to extinguish it.

articles.title: Iran’s foreign minister leaves Pakistan, heads to Russia for more talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, left Islamabad for Moscow to continue indirect talks with the United States.  He met with Pakistani officials and traveled to Muscat before heading to Russia.  While Iran has transmitted "written messages" to the US through Pakistan outlining its red lines, including nuclear issues and the Strait of Hormuz, no direct negotiations have been scheduled.  President Donald Trump canceled a planned visit by US envoys to Islamabad, stating that there was no point in further talks without a clear commitment from Iran.

articles.title: Australia news live: Wong heads to Japan, China and South Korea to secure fuel supply; new ADF armoured vehicles ordered | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Richard Marles, the deputy prime minister and defence minister, announced $450 million in funding for upgrades of Hawkei protected mobility vehicles and three-quarters of a billion dollars to build 268 new Bushmaster vehicles in Bendigo, Victoria.  The government's commitment reflects a "vote of confidence" in Australian industry and the importance of these vehicles in supporting both the Australian Defence Force and international partners. These investments follow an announcement earlier this month of additional funding for Australia's defence capabilities over the next decade.

articles.title: BBC visits Chernobyl ghost city 40 years after world's worst nuclear accident
articles.rephrased_article: The BBC's Jessica Parker visited the ghost city of Pripyat, near Chernobyl, to mark the 40th anniversary of the nuclear accident. The explosion in April 1986 released radioactive material that spread across Europe and resulted in an official death toll of 31, but estimates suggest a much higher number of deaths due to long-term health effects.

articles.title: UAE-Iran differences and India’s plans to dilute language on Israel-Palestine derail joint statement at BRICS meet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BRICS Deputy Foreign Ministers and Special Envoys concluded their meeting in New Delhi without a joint statement on Friday, April 24, 2026.  The lack of agreement highlights ongoing tensions within the group, particularly regarding language on Israel and Palestine, which India attempted to moderate but was met with opposition from most other members. The meeting also saw disagreements between UAE and Iran delegates over the war in West Asia.

articles.title: NTR Collector urges public to avoid panic buying of fuel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: G. Lakshmisha, the District Collector of NTR district, assured the public that measures are being taken to prevent a shortage of petrol and diesel in the region. He urged against panic buying and stated that 186 petrol bunks are available to serve the demand. A control room has been set up at the Collectorate for public complaints regarding fuel supply, with the number 91549 70454 being provided for contact.

articles.title: 66% turnout for civic polls as people brave heat to vote in Gujarat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voter turnout in the Gujarat local body elections ranged from 45% to 66%, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel casting their votes.  Municipal corporations, including Ahmedabad, saw lower turnout compared to other local bodies. The elections are being held under revised norms for Other Backward Classes (OBC) reservations following delimitation and restructuring of wards in several districts. A total of 9,992 candidates are vying for positions across 15 municipal corporations, 84 municipalities, 34 district panchayats, and 260 taluka panchayats. The counting is scheduled for April 28th.

articles.title: 66% turnout for civic polls as people brave heat to vote in Gujarat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voter turnout in the Gujarat local body elections ranged from 45% to 66%, with Amit Shah and Bhupendra Patel casting their votes.  The elections, held under revised norms for OBC reservations, saw a higher turnout in taluka panchayats (65.91%) and district panchayats (65.40%) compared to municipal corporations, including Ahmedabad (45.35%). The BJP, Congress, AAP, and AIMIM are the main contenders in the elections, which will be followed by counting on April 28th.  Three deaths occurred during the voting process, including an AAP candidate and a panchayat staffer.

articles.title: FAPTO hunger strike enters second day in Vijayawada - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: FAPTO leaders, including chairman L. Sai Srinivas and secretary general S. Chiranjeevi, intensified their hunger strike in Vijayawada demanding immediate constitution of the 12th Pay Revision Commission (PRC), interim relief, unified service rules, compassionate appointments, and other issues.  The Federation of Andhra Pradesh Teachers’ Organisations submitted 17 demands to the government, with secretary general Chiranjeevi alleging that teachers were not being prioritized by the government. The hunger strike was supported by private schools and lecturers federation president D. Prasanna and leaders from various districts.

articles.title: Haryana Congress manifesto for civic polls promises clean, well-equipped and corruption-free cities - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Haryana Congress released its manifesto for the upcoming municipal elections on May 10th, promising to transform cities into "Green Cities" with improved sanitation, infrastructure, and security. The party's 15-point plan includes extensive green belts, beautified parks, pothole-free roads, CCTV cameras throughout cities, and strengthened security infrastructure.

articles.title: Six forest department staff, police DSP assaulted following man’s death in elephant attack in Gudalur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Six Forest Department staff were injured after being assaulted by an angry mob in Gudalur, India. The incident occurred when the staff attempted to retrieve the body of T. Kalaiselvan, 45, who died from an elephant attack earlier that night.  Kalaiselvan was part of a team preparing meals for a temple festival.

articles.title: WRD restores key irrigation tank that remains major water source for Vellore Corporation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Water Resources Department (WRD) has restored a key irrigation tank at Saduperi village, which serves as a water source for the Vellore Corporation and surrounding villages. The restoration project, costing ₹19 crore, involved desilting, deepening, and adding features like a walking path, handrails, seating, and two islands to attract tourists. The WRD also erected a steel fence around the tank to prevent illegal dumping and created an approach road for easier access.  This restoration will help store excess rainwater during monsoon and support agricultural activities in the region.

articles.title: Fadnavis backs ex-CJI amid row over meeting with Dhirendra Shastri - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Devendra Fadnavis, Maharashtra Chief Minister,  came out in support of former Chief Justice of India (CJI) B.R. Gavai after social activist Shyam Manav criticized his meeting with Dhirendra Shastri, chief priest of the Bageshwar Dham.  Manav argued that Gavai should not claim the legacy of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and challenged Shastri to accept an anti-superstition panel's challenge. Senior Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar accused political leaders of elevating babas (religious figures) in Maharashtra, criticizing Gavai for meeting Shastri.  The controversy comes after a similar incident involving Shastri's claims about Shivaji Maharaj.

articles.title: Former Israeli PMs Bennett, Lapid unite to challenge Netanyahu in elections | Benjamin Netanyahu News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, former Israeli prime ministers, have joined forces to form a new political alliance called "Together" in an effort to challenge the current government led by Benjamin Netanyahu. The alliance aims to unite a fragmented opposition against Netanyahu's coalition government ahead of upcoming elections later this year.  Bennett, who will lead the new party, and Lapid, have previously collaborated to oust Netanyahu from power in 2021 but formed a short-lived coalition government. This latest alliance is seen as a potential threat to Netanyahu's continued rule, with polls suggesting Bennett could emerge as the top contender against him.

articles.title: Union government to resume talks on Ladakh on May 22, 2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinai Kumar Saxena, the Ladakh Lieutenant-Governor, announced the resumption of talks between the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and civil society bodies, the Leh Apex Body and the Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) on May 22nd. This announcement follows a stalemate after violence erupted in Leh last year and comes ahead of a visit by Union Home Minister Amit Shah to Ladakh. The talks aim to address the core demands of civil society groups, including Statehood and inclusion under the Sixth Schedule, which are pursued by the LAB and KDA.

articles.title: Bomb attack on Colombia highway kills 19 ahead of election | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A bomb attack on a highway in Colombia's Cauca department killed 19 people and injured at least 38, escalating violence ahead of the upcoming presidential election. The attack occurred on Saturday, leaving buses and vans mangled and creating a large crater in the roadway. Hugo Lopez, military chief, stated that assailants stopped traffic by blocking the road with vehicles before detonating the bomb.  Gustavo Petro, the current president, has blamed the bombing on Ivan Mordisco, Colombia's most-wanted criminal.

articles.title: Drug menace emerges as key plank in Amit Shah’s campaign for Punjab polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, Union home minister, will be visiting Punjab next month to address the drug menace, a key part of the BJP's campaign strategy for the 2027 Assembly elections.  The party has signaled its intention to go it alone in the state after severing ties with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and bringing over seven Rajya Sabha MPs from the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Shah previously promised to eradicate drugs within two years, a goal he believes will help broaden the BJP's appeal beyond urban centers.

articles.title: California measure requiring photo ID at polls will be on November ballot | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: California voters will decide in November on a ballot measure requiring photo identification for voting, a proposal championed by Republican state representative Carl DeMaio. The measure has drawn national attention and financial support from Republicans, including $8.8 million raised last year. Democrats oppose the measure, arguing it would disproportionately impact low-income and minority voters.  The outcome of the California vote could have implications for similar efforts in other states, particularly as the White House pushes for stricter federal voting requirements.

articles.title: What’s driving attacks against gov’t and Russian forces in Mali? | Conflict | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Al-Qaeda-linked groups and former enemies in Mali have joined forces to target military sites, including the defense minister's death. Russian mercenaries backing the government have also come under attack. The implications of this unrest are being discussed by experts on the situation.

articles.title: Iran's Araghchi visits Pakistan for 2nd time in two days; envoy says trip undertaken to discuss regional developments - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, traveled to Moscow after a diplomatic tour that included stops in Pakistan and Oman. He met with Pakistani officials, including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Field Marshal Asim Munir, to discuss regional developments and the ongoing efforts to end the US-Israeli conflict on Iran.  During his trip, Araghchi also held phone calls with Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani. He delivered Iran's response to US proposals for ending the war and emphasized the need for a "rational and fair" framework that does not compromise Iranian sovereignty or security interests.  The visit unfolded against the backdrop of ongoing diplomatic efforts by Pakistan to bring the US and Iran back to the negotiating table, but with no clear progress made in resolving key issues like the Strait of Hormuz blockade and Iran's nuclear program.

articles.title: BJP attacking Bengali culture, pride: Kejriwal; Modi won’t have his way in Bengal: Tejashwi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Arvind Kejriwal, former Delhi Chief Minister and convener of the Aam Aadmi Party, joined the Trinamool Congress campaign in West Bengal on Sunday, addressing three rallies in Kolkata and Howrah.  His visit coincides with the final days of campaigning for the second phase of the Assembly elections, scheduled to conclude Monday evening. The AAP recently experienced a setback as seven of its MPs switched to the Bharatiya Janata Party.

articles.title: London Marathon hails ‘greatest day’ as Sawe breaks two hours and records tumble | London Marathon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The London Marathon organizers celebrated a historic day, with Sebastian Sawe becoming the first man to break the two-hour barrier in an official race.  Over 60,000 runners participated, and organizers hoped to surpass last year's record of 59,226 finishers. Hugh Brasher, race director, described it as "the greatest day in London Marathon history," highlighting Sawe's achievement and the numerous world records set throughout the event.  Paula Radcliffe also praised the historic moment, emphasizing its impact on marathon running globally.

articles.title: Palacode, Veerapandi and Kulithalai frontrunners in voter turnout since 2011 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three Assembly segments in Tamil Nadu, Palacode, Veerapandi, and Kulithalai, consistently ranked among the top five for voter turnout in every election since 2008.  While overall voter turnout fluctuated over the years, these three segments maintained their positions at the top despite statewide trends. Veerapandi topped the state in 2011 with 89.16% and remained a stronghold of the AIADMK, while Palacode, another rural segment, achieved high voter turnout in both 2016 (88.63%) and 2021 (88.13%).  Kulithalai, located in the central region, also saw consistent high voter turnout, ranking second in 2011, 2016, and 2021 before dropping to third in 2026 despite recording 92.8%.

articles.title: Blaze at scrapyard exposes Kochi’s fire risks again - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at a scrapyard under the Pulleppady overbridge on Sunday (April 26, 2026) has highlighted the city's vulnerability to fire hazards. Fire and Rescue Services officials have warned that scrap collection yards, resource recovery facilities, and informal garbage dumping sites remain high-risk zones.  The incident was fueled by combustible materials like discarded perfume bottles, emphasizing the dangers of improper waste segregation. The District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) is working on an action plan to prevent future incidents, while authorities have urged scrapyard owners to maintain safe distances between materials and keep premises accessible to firefighting teams. Despite a directive issued three months ago, adequate firefighting systems remain absent at commercial hubs like Broadway.

articles.title: Credai Chennai gets new team of leaders for 2026-28 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Credai Chennai has elected its new leadership for the 2026-2028 term, with Mehul H Doshi as president. The newly elected office bearers and executive committee members include Suman Voora, secretary; S.S. Prasad Babu, treasurer; and T.S.S. Krishnan and Viswajith Kumar, vice-president.  S. Krishnan, IAS, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India, emphasized the importance of real estate in driving Chennai's future growth, particularly in affordable housing and sustainable urban development.

articles.title: FM Araghchi visits Pakistan for 2nd time in two days; envoy says trip undertaken to 'consult on regional developments' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, traveled to Moscow after a visit to Pakistan and Oman. He met with Pakistani officials during his short stay in Islamabad before departing for Moscow. During his trip, Araghchi discussed regional developments and the peace efforts with Sultan Haitham bin Tariq of Oman and Saudi Arabia's Faisal bin Farhan.  He also held phone calls with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani to exchange views on ongoing diplomatic processes. The Iranian delegation handed over Tehran’s response to US proposals for ending the war, emphasizing a framework that is “rational and fair” and maintaining that negotiations cannot proceed under pressure.

articles.title: Rambling hurts your case: Immigration lawyer reveals how US visa decisions are made and why they are denied - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Immigration lawyer Andrea Szew explained in a YouTube video that US visa officers make decisions quickly based on pre-existing information, not just the applicant's interview.  They review travel history, prior applications, and notes before questioning applicants to confirm their intentions.  Szew emphasized that visa officers are trained to look for inconsistencies, patterns, and credibility in applicants' responses, making a decision based on overall impression rather than seeking perfect answers.

articles.title: Provide fixed fund of at least ₹1 crore for academic chairs in universities: Prof. Baraguru Committee to government - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A committee headed by writer Baraguru Ramachandrappa has recommended that the State government provide a fixed sum of at least ₹1 crore for each academic chair established in universities. The committee also suggested mandatory financial allocations upon chair establishment and regular reporting on their activities to ensure equal funding and eliminate discrimination.  The report further recommends that chairs should be named after individuals with significant cultural contributions and focus on regional problems, becoming centers of knowledge creation.

articles.title: Did Trump's intervention save eight Iranian women from execution?
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump claimed to have saved eight Iranian women from execution, but Iran disputed these claims and stated none of the women mentioned were facing death.  The BBC's Chief International Correspondent, Lyse Doucet, is reporting from Tehran on the situation, noting restrictions imposed by the Iranian government on media coverage.

articles.title: FM Araghchi visits Pakistan for 2nd time in two days; envoy says trip undertaken to 'consult on regional developments' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, traveled to Moscow after a visit to Pakistan and Oman. He met with Pakistani officials during his short stay in Islamabad before departing for Moscow. During his trip, Araghchi discussed regional developments and ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the US-Israeli conflict on Iran, which began on February 28th.  He also met with Sultan Haitham bin Tariq of Oman and exchanged views with Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani. Araghchi handed over Iran’s proposals to US proposals for ending the war during meetings in Islamabad, but the US President Donald Trump canceled a planned visit by Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and advisor Jared Kushner.  The diplomatic efforts have been hampered by disagreements over Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the US blockade of Iranian ports.

articles.title: DC gunman Cole Thomas Allen said in his manifesto that he would spare one Trump administration official, and it was... - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Thomas Allen, a 31-year-old man from California, was arrested after exchanging gunfire with US Secret Service agents outside the Washington Hilton during an event hosted by the White House Correspondents’ Association.  Allen had compiled a 1000-word manifesto detailing his plans to attack Donald Trump and other administration officials, but specifically stated he would not harm FBI director Kash Patel. He was armed with a shotgun, handgun, and multiple knives. Allen's brother called police after reading the manifesto, which included references to "fixing issues" in the world.

articles.title: HDK questions Congress’ moral right to hold AHINDA meet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.D. Kumaraswamy, Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, questioned the Congress's moral right to hold a convention of AHINDA communities following the denial of a party ticket to members of a particular community in the Davangere South Assembly constituency byelection.  Kumaraswamy expressed his concern about the incident and asked what face the Congress could possibly have while hosting such a gathering given the events that transpired.

articles.title: Israel issues forced evacuation orders for southern Lebanon in escalation | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel issued forced evacuation orders for seven towns in southern Lebanon, escalating the conflict with Hezbollah, despite a US-brokered ceasefire.  Hezbollah rejected allegations of undermining the ceasefire, claiming its attacks are a legitimate response to Israeli violations exceeding 500 incidents. The Iranian-backed group also stated it will not engage in diplomacy that has proven ineffective.  The conflict has resulted in the deaths of at least 2,509 people and 7,755 wounded by Israeli attacks since March 2nd.

articles.title: Mali Defence Minister Sadio Camara killed in rebel attack, reports say
articles.rephrased_article: Sadio Camara, Mali's defense minister, was killed in a suicide truck bombing on his residence near the capital Bamako. The attack, carried out by militants affiliated with al-Qaeda in Kati, also killed at least three of his family members.  The Malian military junta, led by Gen Assimi Goïta, confirmed fighting continued in Kidal and other areas of the country. Meanwhile, Russian mercenaries hired by the Malian government agreed to withdraw from Kidal after clashes with the separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA). The FLA claims control over Kidal, while the Mali military stated that the violence would not go unanswered.  The UN chief, Antonio Guterres, and West Africa's regional bloc, Ecowas, condemned the attacks.

articles.title: 'Great respect' for Pakistan and they will stay involved, but we are going to do it by phone: Trump on Iran talks - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated that talks with Iran would be conducted remotely, citing the need for no physical travel. He commended Pakistan, which has been mediating between Washington and Tehran, stating they will continue to play a role in the process.  The US president also reiterated his stance on Iran's nuclear program, emphasizing that it cannot possess nuclear weapons. The second round of talks, initially planned for Islamabad, was delayed due to ongoing friction between the US and Iran, particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz and sanctions.

articles.title: Mohamed Salah to join Cristiano Ronaldo at Al-Nassr? Head coach says he ‘definitely wants’ him | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Al-Nassr are exploring a move for Mohamed Salah, with head coach Jorge Jesus giving his approval. The move would pair the Liverpool forward with Cristiano Ronaldo in what would be one of the most high-profile attacking combinations in the game.  However, the deal depends on several factors including Jesus’ contract situation, competition from other Saudi clubs, and Salah's final decision on his next destination.

articles.title: HDK questions Congress’ moral right to hold AHINDA meet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.D. Kumaraswamy, Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, questioned the Congress's moral right to hold a convention of AHINDA communities following the denial of a party ticket to members of a particular community in the Davangere South Assembly constituency byelection.  Kumaraswamy expressed concern about the incident and asked how the party could proceed with such an event given the situation.

articles.title: Has Iran exposed the limits of what US can achieve by force? | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Vali Nasr, professor of international affairs and Middle East studies at Johns Hopkins University, argues that the US-Israel military campaign against Iran has demonstrated the limitations of force.  He contends that diplomatic solutions are the only viable options for resolving the ongoing conflict, emphasizing that Iran's goal is to demonstrate the difficulty of waging war against it. Nasr believes negotiations are necessary to achieve a lasting peace.

articles.title: Trump and officials 'likely' targets of press dinner shooting suspect, authorities believe
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and other administration officials were likely targets of a shooting suspect who attempted to storm the White House Correspondents' Dinner. The suspect, Cole Tomas Allen, was arrested after opening fire near a security checkpoint at the Washington DC hotel where the event was held on Saturday.  The FBI is investigating the incident, which involved gunfire exchanged between law enforcement and the suspect.  Todd Blanche, acting US Attorney General, stated that preliminary findings suggest the suspect targeted administration officials. Weijia Jiang, president of the White House Correspondents' Association, expressed gratitude to the Secret Service for protecting attendees.

articles.title: Meet Tsutomu Yamaguchi: Japan’s official survivour of both Hiroshima and Nagasaki attacks | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a Japanese man, is the only known individual to have survived both atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki during World War II.  He was working in Hiroshima on August 6th, 1945 when the first bomb was dropped, experiencing burns and temporary vision loss but surviving the initial blast. He traveled back to Nagasaki on August 7th and witnessed a second explosion on August 9th, again surviving the blast. Yamaguchi became a "nijū hibakusha," officially recognized as someone affected by both bombings in 2009.  He later dedicated his life to educating others about the long-term effects of nuclear weapons and advocating for their prevention.

articles.title: Kerala’s heat-ridden woes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's electricity consumption has surged this summer due to high temperatures and heavy reliance on air conditioners. The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) urged consumers to conserve energy after peak evening demand reached 6,000 MW for the first time in state history.  Daily consumption has also skyrocketed, exceeding previous levels by a significant margin, while rainfall remains below average.

articles.title: 'When you read his manifesto, he hates Christians': Trump calls White House gunman 'sick guy' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump condemned the suspect, Cole Tomas Allen, as a "sick guy" who expressed hostility towards Christians and was described by authorities as a "lone wolf."  Allen attempted to breach security at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner, prompting shots fired and a Secret Service officer being struck. Trump praised the swift response of law enforcement and security personnel, while also highlighting that high-impact leaders are more likely to be targeted. The incident has prompted authorities to examine Allen's writings and electronic devices for further insight into his motives.

articles.title: Warangal: Over 1,300 SRU students secure jobs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: SR University hosted its 'Placement Success Meet-2026' on Saturday, showcasing strong placement outcomes for the current academic year.  Associate Director (Training & Placements) G. Sunil Reddy reported over 1,300 students secured jobs in leading companies, with more opportunities expected as recruitment processes continue. Chancellor A. Varada Reddy attributed the success to disciplined preparation and institutional support.

articles.title: Washington in shock after White House press dinner shooting: ‘an angry, polarized nation’ | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A man targeted a Secret Service agent at the Washington Hilton hotel, firing shots and being subdued. The incident occurred during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, where Donald Trump and senior White House officials were present.  The attack has raised concerns about political violence and gun control in the US, prompting calls for unity and action to address the epidemic of gun violence.  Experts have noted that social media platforms can be used by terrorist groups and individuals with mental health issues to incite violence. The suspect will face federal charges related to the assault on a federal officer and attempted murder.

articles.title: In China, President Zardari expresses interest in closer collaboration in seed technology, agricultural research - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari met with CCP Secretary Shen Xiaoming in Hunan, China, to discuss closer collaboration in agriculture, health, education, and trade. The president highlighted Pakistan's interest in modern farming practices and seed technology, emphasizing the potential for expanding bilateral trade in areas like agricultural machinery and minerals processing.  He also visited Sany Heavy Industry Co. Ltd., a heavy equipment manufacturer, where he was briefed on their advanced manufacturing systems and commitment to innovation. Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, Sindh’s Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon, and other officials accompanied the president during his visit.

articles.title: Thai police arrest Indonesian wanted for $10m cyberfraud | Cybercrime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Thai police arrested an Indonesian man accused of defrauding Americans out of $10 million in romance scams. The 33-year-old suspect was apprehended at a luxury resort on Phuket after a tip from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). He is awaiting extradition to the United States and will be held in immigration detention in Bangkok.  The arrest highlights Southeast Asia's growing role as a hub for cybercrime, with organized criminal groups using casinos and hotels as bases for sophisticated online scams.

articles.title: Auckland mayor calls Indian-origin staffer ‘Muslim terrorist’, issues apology: ‘Fumbled attempt at humour’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Auckland mayor Wayne Brown apologized after allegedly calling an Indian-origin RNZ staff member a "Muslim terrorist" during a visit to the broadcaster's office. The incident occurred on Monday when Brown arrived for an appearance on the Afternoons program, and the staff member reported that Brown made comments about his beard and security being tight due to a Muslim terrorist presence.  The RNZ chief people officer Sarah Neilson called the remarks unacceptable, while the staff member expressed shock and hurt over the incident. Brown later issued an apology, acknowledging he "got this one wrong" but maintained his commitment to representing all Aucklanders.

articles.title: Tele-MANAS helpline sees rise in callers turning to humans after AI falls short on mental health - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tele-MANAS, a helpline in Hyderabad, is seeing an increase in calls from individuals who have used AI tools like ChatGPT to process their emotions but find themselves needing human connection. Senior counselling psychologist P. Jawaharlal Nehru explains that while these tools can be helpful in certain situations, they lack the nuanced understanding and empathy required for complex emotional issues.  The helpline's anonymity and trained counsellors allow callers to explore their feelings and receive personalized support, highlighting a growing need for human intervention in mental health care. This is especially true given India's historically limited focus on mental well-being compared to physical health.

articles.title: UK faces higher prices for eight months after war in Iran ends, says minister | Consumer affairs | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Darren Jones, the chief secretary to the prime minister, stated that the UK will experience higher prices for food and fuel for at least eight months after the war in Iran concludes. This is due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping lane for oil and gas, which has led to increased oil prices since February's US and Israeli attacks on Iran.  The government is urging motorists to fill up their cars and travelers not to change their travel plans due to potential jet fuel shortages. The UK government is also working to mitigate the impact of higher prices by monitoring stock levels and planning for supply chain disruptions.

articles.title: Iranian FM Araghchi lands in Pakistan after Oman visit, next stop Moscow: diplomatic source - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, returned to Pakistan on Sunday after a diplomatic tour that included visits to Oman and Moscow.  During his time in Islamabad, he met with Pakistani officials and discussed regional developments, including the ongoing US-Israeli conflict and the security of the Strait of Hormuz. He also held phone calls with Saudi Arabia's foreign minister and Qatar's prime minister. Araghchi handed over Iran's response to US proposals for ending the war during meetings in Islamabad before departing for Oman.  The visit took place amid efforts by Pakistan to facilitate diplomatic solutions to the conflict, but US President Donald Trump canceled a planned trip by Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and advisor Jared Kushner to Islamabad after the Iranian delegation departed.

articles.title: Accused shooter was targeting Trump and US officials, authorities say | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and acting Attorney General Todd Blanche confirmed that a gunman who attempted to storm the White House Correspondents' Association dinner was targeting US officials, including the president. The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, purchased two firearms recently and is not cooperating with law enforcement.  Authorities believe he traveled from California to Washington, DC by train via Chicago and intended to target Trump administration members present at the event.  The incident prompted Trump to push his plans for a large ballroom near the White House.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Rosa Parks: "You must never be fearful about what you are doing when it is right." | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rosa Parks's quote, "You must never be fearful about what you are doing when it is right," emphasizes the importance of courage and moral clarity in decision-making. The quote highlights that fear should not outweigh one's sense of right and wrong, encouraging individuals to act with integrity even in challenging situations. This principle applies to both personal choices and larger historical movements, promoting a more responsible and fair society.

articles.title: Trial run commences on section of Chittoor - Thatchur National Highway - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Chittoor - Thatchur National Highway, a 92-kilometer stretch connecting Uthukottai and Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh, has been opened to vehicular traffic on a trial basis. The six-lane access controlled road will eventually connect to the new Bengaluru - Chennai Expressway by August.

articles.title: No headway in Middle East peace efforts as US and Iran refuse to yield | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Hopes for a resolution to the US-Iran conflict have faded as negotiations between the two sides remain stalled. Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, returned to Pakistan for talks with mediators after brief discussions in Oman.  Donald Trump cancelled a planned visit to Pakistan by his envoys due to what he called an inadequate Iranian offer and cited concerns about travel expenses. Despite attempts at rebuilding momentum, the two sides remain entrenched in their positions on key issues like nuclear enrichment and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The US has imposed sanctions and blockaded Iran's ports while Iran maintains its blockade of the strait.  The conflict has escalated significantly, with casualties reported in Lebanon, Israel, and other countries.

articles.title: Pawan Khera moves Supreme Court against denial of anticipatory bail - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pawan Khera, leader of the Congress, challenged the Gauhati High Court's decision to deny him anticipatory bail in an FIR filed against him for allegedly making critical remarks about Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma's wife. The High Court rejected his plea, stating that custodial interrogation was necessary to uncover the source of his accusations.

articles.title: As campaign reaches a crescendo, Modi reaches out to Matuas, Mamata camps at Bhabanipur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi campaigned in West Bengal, emphasizing the BJP's commitment to citizenship for the Matua community of Hindu refugees from Bangladesh. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee held a roadshow in her Bhabanipur constituency, criticizing voter deletions and the Election Commission-appointed administration. She warned that those involved in such actions would face consequences.

articles.title: BITS Pilani opens smart manufacturing centre in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BITS Pilani has opened its Smart Manufacturing Competency Centre (SMCC) in Bengaluru's Electronic City. The centre, designed to foster industry-academia collaboration, will offer short and long-term training programs for industries such as aerospace, defense, electronics, automotive, and advanced manufacturing. BITS Pilani representatives believe the SMCC can act as a problem-solving and innovation partner for these sectors.

articles.title: Rahul Gandhi plans Great Nicobar visit, clearance awaited - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition, began a three-day visit to the Andaman and Nicobar Islands for a Congress convention in Port Blair.  He is scheduled to also visit Great Nicobar Island where the Union government plans a large infrastructure project that has raised concerns among tribal communities about displacement and loss of rights over their forests. Manickam Tagore, Congress in-charge of the islands, said Gandhi assured the people in Port Blair he would continue to fight for their rights in Delhi.

articles.title: Two women’s quest for justice for their daughters fuels Bengal poll fight - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Two mothers from West Bengal, Ratna Debnath and Sabina Yasmin, are contesting the Assembly elections to seek justice for their daughters' deaths. Debnath, whose daughter was murdered in a hospital attack, is campaigning on behalf of the BJP.  Yasmin, whose daughter died in a bomb attack during victory celebrations, is running as a candidate for the Left Front. Both mothers blame the ruling Trinamool Congress and Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee for their daughters' deaths. Their campaigns highlight concerns about political violence and accountability within the state.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Mothers seeking justice for murdered daughters highlights potential systemic failures.

articles.title: Texas tornado kills at least one person as wildfires still rage in parts of Georgia | US weather | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A powerful tornado struck northern Texas on Saturday night, causing significant damage and at least one fatality.  Wise county judge JD Clark confirmed the death and reported six injuries. The National Weather Service warns of continued severe weather in the coming days with potential flash flooding. In Oklahoma, a massive tornado caused damage to homes and an air force base, injuring ten people. Meanwhile, wildfires have ravaged Georgia, destroying over 120 homes and prompting evacuations.  Governor Brian Kemp confirmed that the Highway 82 fire is the most significant wildfire-related home loss in state history.

articles.title: No Green Card if you are a critic of Israel: New immigration rule on disqualifying factors - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Donald Trump administration has issued new immigration guidance expanding disqualifying factors for Green Cards, including social media posts deemed anti-American or antisemitic. The guidance cites examples like declaring support for "subversive" ideologies or desecrating the American flag as grounds for denial.  These materials were distributed to US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), which is part of the Department of Homeland Security. The USCIS now reviews old cases, potentially revoking Green Cards for individuals deemed ineligible based on these new criteria.

articles.title: Research finds high microplastic contamination in mangrove fish - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A study by Bharathidasan University found that the mangrove ecosystem of Pichavaram is experiencing high contamination with microplastics in fish and shellfish. The research, published in Chemosphere, revealed that microplastic levels vary significantly across seasons, peaking during the monsoon due to increased run-off and plastic inflow.  The study identified polyethylene, polypropylene, and polyethylene terephthalate as the primary materials found in the samples. Pichavaram's mangrove ecosystems act as natural bio-filters, trapping microplastics but also increasing their accumulation and persistence, posing ecological risks for marine life.

articles.title: Abbas loyalists sweep Palestinian elections, including some seats in Gaza | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas's Fatah party won most seats in Palestinian municipal elections, including a city in the besieged Gaza Strip.  Voter turnout was low in Gaza due to ongoing violence and restrictions imposed by Israel. The elections were held following a 20-year hiatus in Gaza and marked the first time since the Israeli war on Palestinians began in October 2023. Despite boycotts from Hamas, some candidates aligned with the group won seats in Deir el-Balah.

articles.title: Royal Mail investigating claims that postal worker ‘binned Reform UK election leaflets’ | Royal Mail | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Royal Mail is investigating allegations that a postal worker dumped Reform UK campaign leaflets in a bin. The post, shared on a private Facebook group for Royal Mail staff, claims the worker "dumped them all in a bin" and "IDGAF".  Reform UK has written to Royal Mail's chief executive demanding an internal investigation and compensation for lost materials. The party also wants assurances that future campaign deliveries will be prioritized and protected from similar incidents.

articles.title: Iranian FM Araghchi lands in Pakistan after Oman visit, to head to Moscow after short stay: diplomatic source - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, returned to Pakistan on Sunday after a diplomatic tour that included visits to Oman and Moscow.  During his time in Islamabad, he met with Pakistani officials and discussed regional developments, including the ongoing US-Israeli conflict and the security of the Strait of Hormuz. He also held phone calls with Saudi Arabia's foreign minister and Qatar's prime minister. Araghchi handed over Iran's response to US proposals for ending the war during meetings in Islamabad before departing for Oman.  The visit took place amid efforts by Pakistan to facilitate diplomatic solutions to the conflict, but US President Donald Trump canceled a planned trip by Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and advisor Jared Kushner to Islamabad after the Iranian delegation departed.

articles.title: Condom Prices Surge 30% Amid Iran War Supply Chain Disruptions | Business - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Karex Bhd, the world's largest condom manufacturer, plans to raise prices by 20-30% due to rising raw material costs caused by disruptions in global supply chains stemming from the Iran war. The company cites a surge in prices for synthetic rubber, nitrile, packaging materials, and lubricants as well as shipping delays that have led to shortages of even single components.  Goh Miah Kiat, CEO of Karex Bhd, warns that if the situation continues, further price increases are possible. This crisis is affecting manufacturers globally, including Malaysian rubber glove maker WRP Asia Pacific, which will be winding down operations due to supply chain disruptions. The shortage of condoms has already caused a rise in prices and threatens HIV prevention programs in developing countries like Kenya, where access to affordable condoms is crucial.

articles.title: Will take strict action against officials who hold up files for more than a month, says Bihar CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Samrat Choudhary, the Chief Minister of Bihar, visited his ancestral village, Lakhanpur, on Sunday (April 26, 2026).  During a public meeting in Munger, he addressed concerns about red-tape and promised strict action against officials delaying file processing. He also emphasized his government's goal of providing basic amenities to all residents and ensuring accessible government services for everyone.

articles.title: Iran shifts economic focus to essentials during war uncertainty | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran is shifting its economic focus to essentials amidst the war with the United States and Israel. The government has reinstated a preferential exchange rate for imports of essential goods like wheat, medicines, and baby formula. This move aims to ease mounting pressure on the Iranian people facing food inflation and shortages.  The government is also tapping into its sovereign wealth fund to purchase these goods. Despite efforts to ensure food security, some Iranians are stockpiling supplies and cancelling non-essential activities due to rising prices.

articles.title: Final steps taken before audacious plan to tow whale stranded in Germany to North Sea | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A millionaire-funded initiative is set to attempt the rescue of a sick humpback whale nicknamed Timmy, stranded in the Baltic Sea. The plan involves towing the whale 400km towards the North Sea and back to the Atlantic Ocean using a barge resembling a giant steel aquarium.  Till Backhaus, the state's environment minister, supports the initiative despite criticism from experts who believe the rescue is futile. Karin Walter-Mommert and Walter Gunz, two wealthy individuals, are funding the operation. The whale's plight has attracted public attention, with many onlookers hoping for its successful rescue.

articles.title: Five suspected West Nile fever cases reported in Ernakulam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Health authorities in Ernakulam are warning of suspected cases of West Nile fever (WNF) after reports from several areas.  The District Medical Officer Dr. R. Shahirsha stated that these are currently suspected cases and will be confirmed through testing, which is being conducted on samples sent for analysis. The authorities emphasized the importance of maintaining clean canals and preventing mosquito breeding in homes and surrounding areas to prevent further spread.

articles.title: Sagar Mitras thank Nellore MP for six-month extension of PMMSY scheme - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nellore MP Vemireddy Prabhakar Reddy met with members of the A.P. Sagar Mitra Employees Union to discuss the extension of the Pradhan Mantri Madhya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) welfare scheme. Mr. Reddy had previously requested an extension from the Union Minister for Fisheries, Rajiv Ranjan Singh, and explained that the six-month extension would allow the Sagar Mitras to continue serving as a bridge between the government and fishermen in coastal villages.

articles.title: ‘Maintain consistency’: toppers offer tips to Civil Service aspirants - The Hindu
