articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu Civil Service Gateway 2026, a two-day event held at the Jimmy George Indoor Stadium, brought together civil service toppers to share their experiences and advice with aspiring candidates.  Participants like Meera K. and Sreeja J.S. emphasized the importance of consistent preparation, setting boundaries for topics, and utilizing resources like The Hindu for current affairs. Others, such as Anjana B. and Divya S. highlighted the significance of mental health and overcoming obstacles during their journeys to success.  Mohamed Shezin C.P. shared his remarkable story of balancing work and studies while achieving a high rank despite facing Cerebral Palsy. The summit was presented by Fortune IAS Academy, with support from SBI and Civils 360 IAS Academy.

articles.title: Cheru Poorams keep Thrissur’s festive soul alive - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cheru Poorams, component processions from eight participating temples, filled the Pooram grounds with life despite Thiruvambady temple and Paramekkavu temple scaling back celebrations.  The processions arrived in Thrissur, converging at the Sree Vadakkunnathan temple before paying obeisance and returning. Each procession brought its own rhythm and character to the event, ranging from modest three-elephant displays to grand displays featuring up to 14 elephants. The famed tusker Thechikkottukavu Ramachandran drew awe while percussion maestro Peruvanam Kuttan Marar returned to Thrissur Pooram after a gap.

articles.title: Param Science Experience Centre inaugurated in Whitefield - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Param Science Experience Centre (ParSEC), a 30,000 sq. ft facility in Whitefield, opened to the public on Sunday.  The Param Foundation initiative aims to shift science education from rote memorization to experiential learning. The centre features galleries covering artificial intelligence, emerging technologies, light and optics, electromagnetism, design thinking, and ancient Indian scientific knowledge systems. Former ISRO chairman K. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the facility, while Kris Gopalakrishnan, co-founder of Infosys, emphasized the importance of science for human progress and economic growth.

articles.title: SARPA to link doctors, experts for real-time snakebite guidance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala's Forest Department is upgrading its SARPA snake-response platform to address a recent surge in snakebite incidents linked to the heatwave. The upgraded app will integrate medical professionals and snake experts, providing real-time guidance for first responders during emergencies.  The platform also aims to improve clinical decision-making by enabling doctors to remotely guide treatment until specialized care is available.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez donate $34 million to develop plastic-free fabrics for sustainable fashion | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez, through the Bezos Earth Fund, have committed $34 million to accelerate sustainable textile development. The funding supports research into biodegradable and plastic-free fibers, aiming to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact.  The grants will go to leading research institutions like Columbia University and the University of California, Berkeley, focusing on next-generation textiles that mimic natural fibers while minimizing reliance on fossil fuels. While this investment represents a shift towards industrial transformation in fashion, challenges remain in scaling these materials and overcoming consumer demand for inexpensive clothing.

articles.title: Trump claims gala shooting gives urgency to White House ballroom plan | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump claimed the shooting at the Washington Hilton, where he was attending the White House Correspondents Association's annual dinner, highlights the need for a 1,000-seat ballroom at the White House.  He argued that such a facility would have prevented the incident and emphasized its security features, including drone-proof glass and bulletproof construction. Trump also stated that existing security measures at the White House are insufficient to handle future events like this and called for the immediate halt of lawsuits against the construction project.

articles.title: Two dogs attacked in separate incidents - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vikash A. Bafna filed a complaint alleging an attack on a stray dog in Muniyappa Layout, K.R. Puram, where an unidentified young man allegedly injured the animal with a knife.  A separate incident occurred near the BBMP Public Health Centre in Ramamurthy Nagar, where a construction worker allegedly killed a dog claiming self-defense after it acted aggressively. Both incidents have prompted calls for legal action against the individuals involved under relevant animal cruelty laws.

articles.title: Will Yamal, Salah and Ekitike miss the World Cup 2026 due to injury? | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Several prominent players are facing injury setbacks ahead of the 2026 World Cup. Mohamed Salah of Egypt sustained a hamstring injury during Liverpool's match, ruling him out for the remainder of his club season and potentially impacting his participation in the tournament.  Lamine Yamal, Spain's promising prodigy, has also suffered a hamstring injury that could jeopardize his World Cup debut. Additionally, Marc-Andre ter Stegen and Serge Gnabry from Germany are dealing with hamstring injuries and torn adductor muscles respectively. Brazil is facing setbacks with Estevao, Rodrygo, and Eder Militao all suffering hamstring and knee injuries.  France's Hugo Ekitike has been ruled out of the World Cup due to a torn Achilles tendon, while Japan's Wataru Endo and Takumi Minamino are facing recovery from ankle and ACL injuries respectively.

articles.title: Study shows no genetic harm in children of Chernobyl radiation survivors - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A major international study published in 'Science' has found that children conceived after the Chernobyl disaster show no additional DNA damage linked to their parents’ radiation exposure. The research, led by Meredith Yeager from the US National Cancer Institute, tracked families where both parents and children provided DNA samples for analysis.  The findings suggest that elevated radiation levels do not leave lasting genetic changes in later generations, challenging previous concerns about long-term health impacts.

articles.title: Greggs rolls back self-service cabinets in shoplifting hotspots | Greggs | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Greggs is testing new security measures in select bakery stores, replacing self-service display cabinets with theft-proof counters and introducing software to provide information directly to police. The move follows a rise in shoplifting across the high street, with Greggs becoming a target of habitual shoplifters, similar to other retailers like Pret a Manger and Costa.  The company cites antisocial behavior as a reason for the trial, which is part of a larger effort to combat rising crime rates.

articles.title: BRS women leaders flay Kavitha’s comments against KCR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tula Uma, Hari Ramadevi, and Nirsoha, women leaders of the BRS, criticized K. Kavitha for her remarks against her father, KCR. They expressed disappointment with Kavitha's actions, questioning her motives and suggesting that she sacrificed familial ties for political gain. The women leaders emphasized that without KCR's influence, Kavitha would not have achieved the prominence she currently holds.

articles.title: ‘State of war’: Why Israel has escalated attacks in Gaza | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has escalated military operations in the Gaza Strip, targeting Palestinian police and expanding its control over the enclave. The National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), established under the Trump administration's "Board of Peace", has been sidelined by Israel, hindering its ability to provide services to citizens.  Analysts argue that these actions are part of a broader strategy to maintain a state of war and undermine the US-brokered ceasefire agreement. The NCAG is effectively paralyzed while Israel continues to block aid entry, further exacerbating the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

articles.title: Pakistan notifies 6 land routes for transportation of goods to Iran amid blockade of Hormuz, Iranian ports - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has designated six routes for the transportation of goods to Iran, amid reports of thousands of containers awaiting clearance at Pakistani ports. The Ministry of Commerce issued a statutory regulatory order, Transit of Goods through Territory of Pakistan Order 2026, which mandates an encashable bank guarantee as security for transit goods. This comes amidst a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian port closures due to ongoing conflict between US and Iran. The order will be enforced from April 25th and defines cross-stuffing as the transfer of goods within containers or other transportation modes allowed under Customs laws.

articles.title: Cole Tomas Allen wanted to 'fix the world,' says DC shooter's sister after attempted attack targeting Trump - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, a 31-year-old California man, is accused of shooting near the entrance of the Washington Hilton hotel during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner.  Allen allegedly sent writings to family members expressing political grievances and criticism of government institutions before the incident. Secret Service agents intervened after Allen opened fire, injuring one officer.  Federal Election Commission records show Allen donated $25 to ActBlue in October 2024 for Kamala Harris' presidential campaign.

articles.title: Orbán associates rush to move wealth out of Hungary after election defeat | Hungary | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: As Viktor Orbán's era in Hungary comes to an end, a scramble has begun among those who profited from his 16 years in power.  Sources have reported that members of his inner circle are moving their assets abroad, including to the Middle East and Australia, as they seek to shield themselves from potential investigations into corruption allegations. Péter Magyar, leader of the opposition Tisza party, has called for authorities to detain those who are fleeing the country and recover allegedly stolen public wealth.  Lőrinc Mészáros, a close friend of Orbán, is among those suspected of transferring billions of forints to secure his assets before Péter Szijjártó, outgoing foreign minister, denies any wrongdoing. The future of Orbán himself remains uncertain as he has announced plans to remain in power within the Fidesz party and travel to the United States around the time of the FIFA World Cup.

articles.title: NCB launches ‘Operation WIPE’ to crack down on online drug trafficking networks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) launched “Operation WIPE” to combat the illegal sale and distribution of pharmaceutical drugs on online platforms. The initiative, which stands for “Web-based Illicit Activities Prevention & Enforcement”, has identified 122 instances involving 62 substances, with a focus on those regulated under the NDPS Act.  IndiaMART, TradeIndia, and Dial4Trade have taken corrective measures following verification of flagged products and suspicious vendors. The NCB is collaborating with international partners like the International Narcotics Control Board and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) to proactively monitor online platforms for illicit activities.

articles.title: Medical Education Department keen on 15% NRI quota in all government medical colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Medical Education Department, Karnataka, plans to reserve 15% of all seats in its 24 government medical colleges for NRIs starting in the academic year 2026-27. This move aims to make these colleges self-sufficient and reduce reliance on state grants. The department will submit a proposal to the government soon, with the final decision expected to be made by the Cabinet.  Private colleges currently charge around ₹40 lakh to ₹47 lakh per annum for NRI quota seats, while the government has set a fee of ₹25 lakh per annum for NRI quota seats in 2025-26.

articles.title: Voluntary groups urged to lead ground-level summer relief efforts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Collector N. Devidas called upon NGO representatives to play a proactive role in providing summer relief and safety awareness to the public.  He suggested establishing shaded rest areas at high-traffic locations, distributing buttermilk, ORS solutions, and clean drinking water, and educating people on heatstroke prevention, water conservation, snake bite avoidance, and first aid for emergencies. The meeting was attended by representatives from various organizations including the Indian Red Cross Society and Gandhibhavan, along with disaster management officials and community volunteers.

articles.title: Celebrate Foundation Day at every level: KTR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BRS leadership has instructed its cadre and leaders to hoist the party flag on April 27th in celebration of the party's Silver Jubilee. K.T. Rama Rao, working president, held a teleconference with party leaders across the state, urging them to celebrate at all levels.  The plenary-cum-State executive meeting will be held at the party office and only those invited have been asked to attend.

articles.title: Tent cities planned at 21 Godavari temples for Pushkarams, says Tourism Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for Tourism and Culture Kandula Durgesh announced plans to establish tent cities at 21 temples along the Godavari River in preparation for the 2027 Godavari Pushkarams. The largest tent city, located on Bridge Lanka island in Rajamahendravaram, is part of the ongoing Godavari Riverfront Project, and was approved by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu.

articles.title: Special drives push wrong-way driving cases to five-year high, BTP plans long-term fix - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) recorded a staggering 1.78 lakh cases of wrong-way driving in the first quarter of 2026, marking a significant increase compared to previous years and exceeding the total number of cases booked for the entire year of 2025.  While officials attribute this spike to special enforcement drives, they acknowledge that long-term solutions are needed to address the issue. The BTP is focusing on identifying violation hotspots, increasing deployment at these locations, and implementing interventions like blocking certain stretches to curb violations. East Bengaluru has emerged as a major hotspot for wrong-way driving, with HAL Airport Traffic Police Station leading in recorded cases over the past five years.

articles.title: Two more snakebite deaths reported in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala experienced a surge in snakebite incidents and deaths on Sunday, with two fatalities reported. Nafeesa, 65, and Vishalakshi, 75, succumbed to suspected snakebites.  While authorities maintain there is no alarming trend, the state has seen a significant decline in snakebite-related deaths over the years. The number of snakebite cases averages around 3,500 to 4,500 annually, with most bites being from non-venomous snakes.  The State Forest department's Mission SARPA campaign continues to work towards reducing snakebite deaths.

articles.title: International seminar to commemorate Prof. K.N. Panikkar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sreenarayana Guru Open University (SGOU) and the Kerala History Congress are hosting a two-day international seminar to honor the late Prof. K.N. Panikkar's contributions to history. The event, themed "Cultural Logics of Nationalism: Hegemony and Democratic Struggles," will be held on April 28th and 29th at the SGOU academic block. Former Minister M.A. Baby will inaugurate the seminar, while Prof Jagathy Raj V.P. will preside over the session.  Distinguished historians from premier Indian universities will participate in paper presentations and discussions.

articles.title: Children with Special Needs from State-run schools in Andhra Pradesh scale Everest Base Camp, set national benchmark - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty-one children with special needs from government schools in Andhra Pradesh successfully completed the Everest Base Camp trek in Nepal. The 16-day expedition, organized by Samagra Shiksha, Andhra Pradesh, and supported by the School Education Department, marked the first government-sponsored Everest Base Camp trek for specially-abled students.  The students, accompanied by mountaineers and officials, demonstrated their determination to overcome social stigma and achieve their goals. Nara Lokesh, HRD Minister and IT Minister of Andhra Pradesh, congratulated the students on their success and highlighted the importance of inclusivity in education.

articles.title: Kadapa city has remained underdeveloped for 20 years, says MLA Madhavi Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Reddeppagari Madhavi Reddy, Kadapa MLA, criticized the city's underdevelopment, blaming previous administrations for its state. She attributed the lack of progress to a "vested interest" that has hindered development efforts.  She urged residents to participate in the Census enumeration and emphasized the importance of embracing development.

articles.title: Ten workers injured as part of under-construction ROB collapses at Auto Nagar in Visakhapatnam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ten workers were injured when a portion of an under-construction Rail Over Bridge (ROB) collapsed in Vadlapudi, India. The incident occurred on Sunday and the injured were rushed to nearby hospitals where their condition was reported as stable.  R&B Minister B.C. Janardhan Reddy, who is currently overseas, directed officials to investigate the cause of the accident and ensure the injured receive proper medical care. Home Minister V. Anitha also spoke with police officials and directed the Medical & Health Department to provide treatment.

articles.title: Iranian FM Araghchi back in Pakistan after Oman visit, to head to Moscow after short stay: diplomatic source - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian Foreign Minister, returned to Pakistan after a diplomatic tour that included visits to Oman and Moscow.  He met with Pakistani officials and discussed regional developments and ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. During his trip, Araghchi conveyed Iran’s proposals for resolving the conflict and emphasized the need for a “rational and fair” framework free of outside interference. The visit followed a first round of direct US-Iran talks in Islamabad that yielded no agreement.  The US has maintained its blockade of Iranian ports while Iran has shut down the Strait of Hormuz, further complicating efforts to reach a resolution.

articles.title: Indian-origin Trump aide slammed for her outfit joke after White House shooting: 'I lost some professional respect for you' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Harmeet Dhillon, an aide to President Donald Trump, sparked controversy on social media after posting about the shooting at a White House dinner. Dhillon, who was present at the event, made light of the situation by asking women if they could repeat their outfits for another event. The post drew criticism from some users who felt it was insensitive and inappropriate.  Dhillon later shared her own look from the event on her account and expressed gratitude to the Secret Service for securing the scene.

articles.title: Minister D. Sudhakar may be considered for lung transplant if there is no improvement in his health - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D. Sudhakar, Minister for Planning and Statistics, is receiving intensive medical care at KIMS Hospitals in Bengaluru after developing a lung infection. Doctors say he is currently stable on life support but may be considered for lung transplantation if his lungs do not show significant improvement. A specialized team of doctors is monitoring his condition around the clock.

articles.title: IMF executive board to meet on May 8 to approve disbursement of over $1.2bn to Pakistan - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) will meet on May 8th to approve a disbursement of over $1.2 billion to Pakistan under two concurrent programs: the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).  The IMF has already approved about $1 billion based on the successful third review of the EFF and $210 million from the second review of the RSF. The disbursement is contingent upon Pakistan meeting certain conditions, including fuel pricing adjustments and the elimination of subsidies to meet a petroleum levy target. The Fund has also advised the government to phase out fuel subsidies and implement flexibility in its program's contours for next year's budget.

articles.title: Trump adviser tried to chant ‘USA! USA!’ during DC dinner shooting, but was shushed: 'No one wanted to hear it' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dan Scavino, a senior advisor to President Donald Trump, attempted to start a patriotic chant moments after gunfire disrupted a high-profile dinner in Washington.  The reaction from attendees was awkward as security forces worked to control the situation. President Trump and his wife were escorted out of the venue along with other officials. The suspect, identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, was apprehended after exchanging gunfire with officers.

articles.title: ‘This has to be a wake-up call’: NSW attorney general urged to order inquest into death of Sydney’s ‘birdman’ | Sydney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Daley, the New South Wales attorney-general, has received a request from independent MP Alex Greenwich to order an inquest into the death of Nepali rough sleeper Bikram Lama. Greenwich argues that Lama's death highlights potential policy failures related to homelessness support and housing access for non-residents in Sydney. The coroner is currently awaiting evidence from police before deciding whether to hold an inquest, while the City of Sydney estimates one in five inner-city rough sleepers are not Australian residents.

articles.title: Govt. to restore 10th century Siddheswara Swamy temple in Nellore district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Minister for Endowments, Anam Ramanarayana Reddy, visited the 10th century Siddheswara Swamy temple at Krishnapatnam Port area with officials from various states and the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to inspect its heritage status and discuss development plans. The visit included representatives from Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Telangana.

articles.title: Forest department sets up cages to recapture tiger that strayed into human habitation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Forest department officials in Idukki, Kerala, set up two cages to recapture a five-year-old male tiger that entered human settlements near Vandiperiyar on Saturday night. The tiger, previously captured and released into the Periyar Tiger Reserve (PTR) in April, had been causing trouble by killing cattle in a tea plantation. Officials fitted the tiger with a radio collar before its release to monitor its movements.

articles.title: Ayurveda sector seeks separate department in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Ayurvedic Medicine Manufacturers Organisation of India (AMMOI)
articles.rephrased_article: Ayurvedic drug manufacturers in Kerala have requested the creation of a separate department for their branch of medicine, similar to the Union Ayush Ministry. The request was made by the Ayurvedic Medicine Manufacturers Organisation of India (AMMOI) general secretary D. Ramanathan, who argues that modern medicine and other systems are currently under the same department, with the Deputy Drugs Controller for Ayurveda reporting to the State Drugs Controller responsible for modern medicine drugs.

articles.title: GT Tech partners with BotClub to strengthen science education - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gram Tarang Technologies Private Limited (GT Tech) and BotClub Private Limited, an education technology start-up, announced a strategic partnership to enhance science education in schools. The collaboration will utilize BotClub’s “A-One” classroom system, which integrates digital visuals with physical models and provides analytics on student learning outcomes, according to D.N. Rao, Vice-President of Centurion University and GT Tech promoter.

articles.title: Activists protest against H-CITI project at Hyderabad’s KBR Park - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Citizens and environmental activists gathered outside the Kasu Brahmananda Reddy (KBR) National Park on Sunday, April 26th, protesting a proposed Hyderabad City Innovative and Transformative Infrastructure (H-CITI) project. The protesters raised concerns that the project threatens the park's status as the city's "last green lung" and was being implemented without sufficient legal or environmental review. They held signs reading “SaveKBR” and “The H-CITI project fails the law.

articles.title: 859 students get admissions on first day of KL University counselling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: KL University Vice-Chancellor G. Parthasarathy Verma reported that 859 students were admitted on the first day of counseling for engineering, degree, and postgraduate courses at the Vijayawada and Hyderabad campuses. The admissions were based on merit criteria including top ranks in the KLUEEE, scores of 970 marks in Intermediate, and a percentile above 95 in JEE Mains.

articles.title: What lies ahead for Gaza after ceasefires in Iran and Lebanon? | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The recent ceasefire in Lebanon and Iran has shifted focus to Gaza, where the future of Hamas's weapons and governance remains unresolved. Israel continues military operations in Gaza despite a relative calm in other regional conflicts, raising concerns among Palestinians about renewed hostilities. Some analysts believe this lull could be used by Israel to pressure Hamas for disarmament as part of the US-backed ceasefire plan, while others see it as a tactic to influence negotiations with Iran and Lebanon.  The international community, particularly the US, is hesitant to escalate tensions further, but the deadlock over Hamas's weapons could lead to increased pressure on both sides. Hamas, meanwhile, demands full Israeli withdrawal from Gaza and a comprehensive political deal before disarmament. The future of the ceasefire hinges on negotiations between Israel and Hamas, with potential for limited escalation as a more likely scenario than a full-scale war.

articles.title: Florida is latest US state to enter redistricting war ahead of 2026 election | Florida | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Florida lawmakers will convene for a special session on Tuesday to redraw congressional district lines, with Ron DeSantis's staff reportedly drafting a proposal in secret.  The Republican-led effort seeks to increase their representation in Congress despite facing an uphill battle in what appears to be a hostile year for the party.  Hakeem Jeffries, House minority leader, threatened legal action if Florida Republicans proceed with redistricting legislation, arguing it would create more opportunities for Democrats. The outcome of this process hinges on the US Supreme Court's ruling on the Louisiana v Callais case, which could impact the Voting Rights Act and allow for greater map manipulation.

articles.title: Telangana IT Minister Sridhar Babu calls for stricter curbs against gutka, pan masala, khaini and drugs in State - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Duddilla Sridhar Babu, Telangana IT Minister, warned against the consumption of gutka, pan masala, khaini, and narcotics, emphasizing their serious health risks. He urged young people to avoid addiction and adopt healthier lifestyles during an Oral Cancer Awareness Marathon in Hyderabad organized by the Global Oral Cancer Trust.  Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh also participated in the event, flagging off a 5K run.

articles.title: Israel feared Amal Khalil, just as it did Shireen Abu Akleh | Israel attacks Lebanon | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel assassinated Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil, known for her reporting on the Israeli occupation of southern Lebanon.  She was killed near Bint Jbeil, a site of resistance against Israeli forces, while working with freelance photographer Zeinab Farraj. The Israeli regime has been accused of targeting journalists in the region, including Palestinian and Lebanese reporters, with impunity.   The killing of Amal Khalil is part of a disturbing trend that has made 2023 the deadliest year for journalists in any conflict in recorded history.

articles.title: Suspected gunman at White House press dinner named | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 31-year-old man from Torrance, California named Cole Tomas Allen has been identified as the suspect in the shooting at the White House correspondents' dinner.  Donald Trump, who posted footage of the incident on his Truth Social platform, described the suspect as a "lone wolf whack job" and said authorities were searching his home. Jeffery Carroll, interim police chief for Washington DC’s Metropolitan Police Department, confirmed Allen was apprehended after exchanging shots with an officer.  The suspect is facing two counts of assault and will be arraigned on Monday.

articles.title: Watch: How JD Vance was evacuated amid gunfire panic at White House correspondents' dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance, and other senior officials were evacuated from the Washington Hilton during a security incident at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner. A man armed with multiple weapons opened fire near a security checkpoint outside the ballroom, prompting a swift response by Secret Service agents. The suspect, identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, was subdued before reaching the main event area and no dignitaries or guests were injured.  The incident has renewed concerns about security at high-profile political events. Officials confirmed that Allen will face charges including using a firearm during a crime of violence and assault on a federal officer.

articles.title: Thrissur Pooram rises above grief, keeping its spirit alive - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thrissur Pooram, a traditional festival in Kerala, took place on Sunday (April 26, 2026) despite the absence of fireworks due to a recent tragedy.  The scaled-down format did not deter devotees from attending the event, which celebrated the deities of ten temples with elaborate processions and percussion performances. The highlight was the Kudamattam, a brief but emotionally charged spectacle where umbrellas were displayed by participating temples. Paramekkavu and Thiruvambady temples led the procession, accompanied by renowned percussion ensembles, including the Madathil Varavu Panchavadyam.  The festival signifies unity and cultural pride for the people of Thrissur.

articles.title: Mali rattled by ongoing armed attacks: What to know | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mali's military is battling coordinated attacks by unidentified armed groups, including the JNIM and Tuareg rebels.  The attacks began on Saturday, targeting military sites across the country, including Bamako. The Defense Minister Sadio Camara was killed in the attacks, which have been described as unprecedented in scale and coordination. The African Union, the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, and the United States Bureau of African Affairs condemned the attacks.  Russian mercenaries were also involved in the fighting, but they have reportedly surrendered control of Kidal to Tuareg fighters. Despite efforts by the military government to regain control, the situation remains volatile with no clear end in sight.

articles.title: New IRA suspected over car explosion outside Belfast police station | Northern Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) officers are treating the explosion outside a Dunmurry police station as an attempted murder linked to the New IRA.  A gas cylinder device was placed in the boot of a hijacked car, and a male delivery driver was ordered to drive it to the station. The incident occurred on Saturday night, prompting evacuations of nearby properties.  First Minister Michelle O’Neill condemned those responsible while DUP leader Gavin Robinson expressed concern for the safety of police and the public.  The PSNI deputy chief constable stated that officers bravely evacuated residents and no one was injured in the explosion.

articles.title: Kash Patel seen ‘scrolling his phone’ as agents rush guests from DC shooting scare involving Trump: 'No sense of urgency' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel faced criticism for his actions during a shooting scare near the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.  A video of Patel scrolling through his phone while security forces moved guests to safety sparked backlash online, with some accusing him of lacking urgency. The incident involved a suspect who exchanged gunfire with officers before being subdued, and despite the breach, security personnel prevented the attacker from entering the main ballroom where President Donald Trump was present.  Trump praised the Secret Service response, while Patel later commended Trump publicly. The scrutiny surrounding Patel extends beyond the weekend incident, as he is facing multiple allegations including misconduct and misuse of FBI resources.

articles.title: Do not allot Simhachalam temple land for Google Data Centre: CWC member - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress Working Committee member Gidugu Rudra Raju urged the State government to reconsider its plan to allocate land from the Simhachalam temple for a Google Data Centre, citing concerns about hurting Hindu sentiments and violating guidelines set by the Endowments Department.  He suggested the government acquire private land instead, with Google bearing the cost.

articles.title: US-Iran conflict: What’s the latest as the Islamabad talks stall? | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump cancelled a planned visit to Pakistan by his envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, as US-Iran talks stalled over issues including the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.  Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian reiterated that negotiations would not occur until the US lifted its blockade on Iranian ports. Despite this, Pakistan's political and military leadership continues to mediate between the two countries, with hopes for incremental progress. The ceasefire, established after six weeks of conflict, has held largely but remains fragile as both sides accuse each other of violations.

articles.title: Ryanair to shut Berlin base as it blames rise in German aviation tax | Ryanair | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ryanair is reducing its operations in Berlin, shutting down its operating base and cutting its winter schedule by half. The airline blames soaring aviation taxes in Germany for the decision, citing a loss of traffic, connectivity, jobs, and trade. Ryanair's chief executive, Eddie Wilson, stated that German aviation is "broken" and called for a strategy to reduce aviation taxes.  The move has been criticized as a profit-driven strategy by the German trade union Verdi, while environmentalists and rail enthusiasts see it as an opportunity for increased train travel to Berlin.

articles.title: Toxins plus climate harms likely cause of reduced fertility, study finds | Science | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: New research suggests that exposure to toxic chemicals and climate change's impacts may have an additive effect, increasing reproductive harm and potentially contributing to global fertility decline. A review of 177 studies found that endocrine-disrupting chemicals like phthalates and Pfas, often found in consumer goods, are linked to various reproductive issues across species, including humans.  Shanna Swan, a co-author on the paper, previously found sperm levels declining significantly in men over four decades. Susanne Brander, a lead author of the study, emphasizes that both climate change and chemical exposure can exacerbate infertility by disrupting hormones and impacting environmental sex determination. The authors suggest reducing reliance on toxic chemicals and mitigating climate change as crucial steps to address these issues.

articles.title: TVK chief Vijay’s assets: Another case in Madras High Court questions loan extended to estranged wife Sangeetha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A new writ petition has been filed in the Madras High Court seeking an inquiry into the assets declared by C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), while filing his nomination papers for the Perambur Assembly constituency election.  The petitioner, M.P. Venkatesh, argues that the disclosures made by Mr. Vijay are misleading and raise concerns about potential fraud in the electoral process. The petition also cites discrepancies in Mr. Vijay's financial disclosures, including loans to family members and a large transfer to a trust. This case joins two other similar cases filed against former AIADMK Ministers D. Jayakumar and C.Ve. Shanmugam, both contesting from different constituencies.

articles.title: Japan deploys 1,400 firefighters to battle raging wildfires in the north - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Japan has deployed firefighting resources to combat wildfires in the northern part of the country, which have now burned for five consecutive days and threaten the coastal town of Otsuchi. The fires have consumed 1,373 hectares of land and forced evacuations for nearly a third of the town's population.  The Self-Defence Force is using helicopters to fight the blazes while dry weather and strong winds are hindering efforts.

articles.title: Indian man arrested in Texas after attacking woman and biting her child; student visa was revoked in 2025 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Atharva Vyas, a 24-year-old Indian man, has been arrested for assaulting a mother and her three-year-old daughter in San Antonio, Texas. ICE issued a detainer against him, meaning he will be taken into custody after legal proceedings. The attack occurred on April 18th when Vyas allegedly grabbed the mother by the hair, causing her to fall and drop her child.  Vyas's student visa was revoked in 2025 due to his past arrest for assault and he entered the US illegally in August 2023. The Department of Homeland Security criticized the Biden administration for not taking action against Vyas earlier, blaming them for allowing him to remain in the country.

articles.title: White House journalists’ gala ended like many US events do: with gun violence | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and attendees at the White House correspondents' dinner were shaken by a shooting that occurred outside the ballroom. A man was apprehended after firing shots, prompting an immediate evacuation of the room and a postponement of the event.  The incident highlighted the increasing prevalence of political violence in the United States, with journalists and officials expressing concern about the safety of those working in public service. Despite security measures, the shooting underscored the reality that political violence is becoming an unwelcome fixture in American life.

articles.title: ‘Bhoomi Pooja’ for BSY Abhimanotsava held in Chitradurga - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: B.Y. Vijayendra, BJP State president, announced that BS Yediyurappa's 50th anniversary in public life will be celebrated with a mega convention called the "BSY Abhimanotsava" on May 9th in Chitradurga.  The event, which includes a "Bhoomi pooja" for the construction of the convention venue, was attended by seers and BJP leaders. Vijayendra stated that the convention aims to recognize Yediyurappa's contributions to society and his work in building the party.

articles.title: Japan deploys 1,400 firefighters to battle raging wildfires in the north - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Japan has deployed significant resources to combat wildfires in the northern part of the country, with 1,400 firefighters and 100 Self-Defence Force personnel battling blazes that have now burned for five consecutive days. The fires threaten residential districts of Otsuchi, a town previously devastated by the 2011 earthquake and tsunami, prompting evacuation orders for 3,233 residents. While aerial firefighting efforts are underway, dry weather and strong winds are contributing to the fire's spread.

articles.title: Mali violence escalates: Defence minister Sadio Camara killed in 'terrorist attack' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The security crisis in Mali escalated significantly after the death of defense minister Sadio Camara, who was killed in an attack on his residence.  Al-Qaeda-linked militants, Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), and the Tuareg-led separatist group Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) coordinated attacks targeting Bamako and other cities, leaving at least 16 people injured. United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres condemned the violence, while ECOWAS called for stronger regional cooperation to counter rising militant violence in the Sahel.  The attacks signal a worrying shift in the security situation, potentially complicating counterinsurgency efforts in Mali and neighboring countries.

articles.title: White House press dinner shooting suspect could be charged with trying to assassinate Trump, says Blanche | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Todd Blanche, acting US attorney general, stated that the suspect apprehended at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner could be charged with attempting to assassinate Donald Trump. The armed 31-year-old man was believed to have targeted members of the Trump administration who were present at the event.  The incident occurred during a dinner where Trump, his wife Melania Trump, and other high-ranking officials were seated at a high table. Surveillance footage shows the suspect rushing across the ballroom space before being subdued by law enforcement. The suspect is expected to appear in federal court on Monday, while Cole Tomas Allen of Torrance, California has been identified as the suspected gunman.

articles.title: Pneumonia continues to be among the leading causes of infant deaths in Karnataka: Economic survey - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka's Economic Survey reveals that pneumonia remains the leading cause of infant deaths in the state, accounting for 204 out of 4,709 recorded deaths in 2025-26.  Despite progress in reducing mortality from other conditions like diarrhoea, which saw just 12 infant deaths reported, pneumonia continues to pose a significant challenge to early-life care.

articles.title: Trump, administration officials likely targets of shooting at White House correspondents' dinner: US official - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and other US administration officials were the likely targets of a suspect who fired at a security agent guarding the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in Washington, D.C. The incident occurred near the main screening area at the entrance of the event, where guests, including members of the press, their family members, and government officials, took cover as security agents tackled the suspect.  The suspect, identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen from Torrance, California, was armed with a shotgun, handgun, and knives and charged past a checkpoint before being apprehended. The shooting occurred at the same hotel where President Ronald Reagan was shot in 1981. Vice President JD Vance and several cabinet members were evacuated from the venue as security personnel took positions on stage and provided cover for Trump, who remained backstage for approximately an hour before being escorted back to the White House.

articles.title: 'Trump and admin officials': Acting AG reveals who was gunman's target at WH shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated that investigators believe the gunman who attempted to storm the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner was targeting Donald Trump and his administration's officials. The suspect, identified by law enforcement as Cole Tomas Allen, traveled from California to Washington before attempting to enter the ballroom but was tackled and shots were fired.  Police are expected to file multiple charges against Allen, who is not cooperating with investigators.

articles.title: Keir Starmer vows to lead Labour into next general election after bruising week | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer has stated his intention to lead Labour into the next general election, despite ongoing controversy surrounding the appointment of former Labour grandee Peter Mandelson as US ambassador.  Starmer's Downing Street allies have denied any wrongdoing in relation to the appointment and vetting process, while Darren Jones, chief secretary to the prime minister, stated that no evidence supports claims of misconduct by the prime minister. The Conservatives are pushing for a parliamentary investigation into whether Starmer misled parliament during the appointment process, but some argue that this is unnecessary duplication of work already being conducted by the foreign affairs committee.

articles.title: Two highway defects in Karnataka over three years: Debarment, repairs ordered - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: National Highways (NHs) in Karnataka have experienced two major incidents of structural defects and collapses over the past three years.  In 2025, a reinforced earth wall block collapsed on NH-948, prompting repair work based on recommendations from Indian Institute of Science (IISc) experts. In 2024, the Kali Bridge on NH-66 collapsed due to inadequate slope stability works, leading to the contractor's one-month debarment and corrective measures.  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has taken action against defaulting agencies based on severity of violations, including penalties, contract termination, or blacklisting.

articles.title: Trump, administration officials likely targets of shooting at White House correspondents' dinner: US official - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and other US administration officials were likely targets in a shooting at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner. The suspect, identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, was apprehended after charging a checkpoint with weapons including a shotgun, handgun, and knives.  The incident occurred near the main screening area of the hotel, where attendees took cover as security officers tackled the suspect. Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum were among those evacuated from the venue. The shooting prompted condemnation from world leaders including President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

articles.title: 'Bizarre': Former student of White House shooting suspect says Cole Allen seemed like a completely average guy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Allen, a former Caltech graduate and teacher, opened fire outside the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday. Allen, who was registered as having no party preference and donated to ActBlue supporting President Harris, is facing two charges: using a firearm during a crime of violence and assault on federal officers using a dangerous weapon.  Todd Blanche, Acting Attorney General, stated that Allen told police he was targeting "administration officials" but likely wasn't targeting anyone specifically.

articles.title: Syria puts first Assad-era official on trial in Damascus | Syria's War News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Syria began its first public trial of officials who served under former leader Bashar al-Assad, marking a significant step in the country's transitional justice process.  Atef Najib, former head of political security in Deraa province, is facing charges related to alleged crimes against the Syrian people and overseeing a violent crackdown on protesters during the 2011 uprising. The trial, which began on Sunday in Damascus, will continue next month with other high-ranking officials also charged in absentia for their alleged involvement in killings, torture, extortion, and drug trafficking.  The government of interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa has faced criticism for delays in the transitional justice process following the civil war.

articles.title: Lonely at the top: who are Keir Starmer’s allies as daunting May elections loom? | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer faces challenges in his premiership, with some suggesting he may not lead Labour into the next election.  He has a few allies within the cabinet, including Richard Hermer, the attorney general, and Nick Thomas-Symonds, the Cabinet Office minister. Additionally, he relies on pre-politics friends for support. Despite these connections, Starmer's political foes are mounting pressure on him. Some of his former aides have departed under difficult circumstances, highlighting a potential contradiction in his loyalty.

articles.title: AAP submits petition to Rajya Sabha Chairman seeking termination of seven MPs who quit party - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sanjay Singh, a senior Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader, filed a petition with the Rajya Sabha Chairman seeking the disqualification of seven AAP MPs who recently joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).  Singh argued that these MPs' actions constitute defection under the anti-defection law and cited opinions from constitutional experts like Kapil Sibal and P. D. T. Achary.

articles.title: Use knowledge for progress, be job creators: Vice-President to youth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan urged Rajasthan University graduates to use their knowledge for societal progress and become job creators and nation builders during the university's 35th convocation ceremony.  He emphasized that education should be applied for the betterment of society, innovation, and ethical conduct. The event was attended by Chancellor and Governor Haribhau Bagade.

articles.title: NHAI fast-tracks alignment identification for 35 km-long Mangaluru Bypass - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has appointed M/S L.N. Malviya Infra Projects Pvt. Ltd. to prepare a detailed project report for the proposed 35 km Mangaluru Bypass Project. The alignment identification is underway, with an internal appraisal committee recommending a six-lane highway including a flyover between KIOCL Junction and Baikampady on NH 66. The proposal has been sent to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways for Standing Finance Committee approval.

articles.title: NCB seizes 474 soap cases of heroin worth ₹11 crore in Manipur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), in collaboration with the State police and Assam Rifles, seized 474 soap cases of heroin worth ₹11 crore in Manipur's Churachandpur district.  During the operation on April 23rd, the joint team intercepted a vehicle suspected of carrying narcotics. The contraband weighed approximately 5.42 kg and is estimated to have an illicit market value of around ₹11 crore. Three individuals involved in the transportation of the drugs were arrested. The NCB stated that it has been intensifying its operations in Manipur due to the state's vulnerability to drug trafficking.

articles.title: Gang robs jeweller of gold worth ₹1.49 crore in Tiruchi, destroys CCTV cameras - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhay, a 36-year-old gold appraiser from Maharashtra, and his employee Nithin, 19, were robbed of approximately one kilogram of refined gold worth ₹1.49 crore by a four-member gang in Tiruchi on Friday (April 24, 2026). The incident occurred at Udhay's jewellery workshop near Big Bazaar Street.  The police are investigating the robbery.

articles.title: Tourist bitten by snake near Cherai beach in Kerala’s Kochi; under observation in MICU - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 36-year-old tourist from Coimbatore, Sharmila, was hospitalized in Kerala after being bitten by a snake near the Cherai beach on Sunday. She sustained the bite on her toe while staying at a resort close to the beach with her family.  Sharmila was treated at the Taluk Hospital in North Paravur and later transferred to a private hospital in Chalakka for specialized care.

articles.title: Recalibrating positions - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's ongoing war with Iran has resulted in significant economic and human costs, impacting the global economy and causing widespread casualties.  The conflict has also strained alliances within NATO, leading to a shift in power dynamics as middle powers like China, India, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkiye, and Egypt forge new partnerships. These alliances are driven by shared interests and concerns regarding regional stability, economic opportunities, and geopolitical influence. Despite the war's impact on trust among nations, it has also created potential for new strategic partnerships that could reshape global power dynamics in the years to come.

articles.title: Nrusimha Sagar reservoir non-operational due to pending compensation to displaced families: BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gudur Narayana Reddy, a senior leader of the BJP, has called for immediate payment of pending compensation, relief, and rehabilitation (R&R) benefits to families displaced by the Nrusimha Sagar Reservoir. The reservoir, completed in 2023 under the Kaleshwaram project, remains unused despite its capacity to store around 11.39 TMC due to unresolved compensation issues.

articles.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: THE RISE OF DEFENSIVE REALISM - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Neorealism, a framework for understanding state behavior in an anarchic international system, has become the dominant school of thought.  This perspective emphasizes the pursuit of security and survival through strategic responses to external pressures. Pakistan's recent shift towards defensive realism, prioritizing territorial integrity and sovereignty over expansionist ambitions, exemplifies this trend. The article highlights how neorealism, with its emphasis on tangible factors like military and economic realities, has superseded ideological narratives in shaping state behavior.  This approach is evident in Pakistan's strategic partnerships with China and Saudi Arabia while maintaining pragmatic relations with offensive realists like the United States.

articles.title: Forest fires spread across Nilgiris; helicopters help battle blaze - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The forest department is battling multiple wildfires in the Nilgiris Forest Division and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, with helicopters from Sulur Air Force base assisting for a second consecutive day. The fires began on April 15th at Wenlock Downs Reserve Forest in Parson's Valley Range of the Nilgiris Forest Division.  Over 400 forest personnel from across the state have been deployed to control the blazes.

articles.title: 'Get down!': Panic and chaos at glitzy White House media gala - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump was abruptly interrupted during the White House Correspondents’ Association annual dinner when gunshots erupted, prompting a chaotic evacuation.  Guests, including correspondents, officials from the Trump administration, and members of his cabinet, took cover as Secret Service agents quickly surrounded the president and escorted him off the stage. The incident occurred at the Washington Hilton, where President Ronald Reagan survived an assassination attempt in 1981. Trump described a "lone wolf" gunman who charged through security screening before being subdued.  The event was subsequently evacuated, and Trump addressed reporters from the White House briefing room later that evening, vowing to reschedule the dinner.

articles.title: IMD issues heat alert in several regions of Maharashtra and thunderstorm alert in a few regions - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued yellow alerts for rising temperatures in eight districts of Maharashtra, predicting hot conditions and increased humidity for the next three days.  The IMD also forecasts thunderstorms with lightning, moderate rainfall, and gusty winds in several districts of Western Maharashtra, including Pune, Latur, Nanded, Beed, and Satara, and Marathwada.

articles.title: Pakistan taps UN committee to reshape national food policy - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Federal Minister for National Food Security and Research, Rana Tanveer Hussain, met with CFS Chairperson Anas Al-Nabulsi during the FAO Regional Conference in Brunei Darussalam to discuss food security challenges.  Hussain outlined Pakistan's efforts to ensure food access while addressing environmental and socio-economic pressures. The meeting focused on how international policy guidance can be adapted for national implementation and emphasized the importance of inclusive governance, collaboration across sectors, and research innovation in building resilient food systems. Both sides agreed to continue collaborating to translate global policy into tangible outcomes for long-term food security goals.

articles.title: Blast targets minister’s home - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A bomb exploded near the residence of Mir Sadiq Umrani, Balochistan's Minister for Irrigation, in Dera Murad Jamali on Saturday night. The blast damaged parts of the house and destroyed a nearby Wapda transformer.  Police said two individuals were captured on CCTV planting the bomb before fleeing the scene. An investigation is underway.

articles.title: Marthoma Church marks Metropolitan’s episcopal golden jubilee by building 150 homes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Theodosius Mar Thoma Metropolitan, the head of Church, celebrated his 50th year as bishop by providing housing for 150 landless and homeless families. The project, which spanned across regions in Kerala, was funded through donations and built at an estimated cost of ₹7.5 lakh per house.  The initiative included community halls to foster social bonding among residents and was overseen by a committee led by Joseph Mar Barnabas Suffragan Metropolitan with support from various Church leaders and professionals.

articles.title: Mali’s Defence Minister Sadio Camara killed amid coordinated attacks | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: General Sadio Camara, Mali’s Defence Minister, was killed in coordinated attacks on military sites across the country. The attacks, which included a suicide car bomb assault on his residence in Kati, were carried out by an al-Qaeda affiliate and Tuareg rebels. Interim President Assimi Goita is safe and remains in command of the military despite pressure from analysts following the offensive.  The African Union, the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation secretary-general, and the United States Bureau of African Affairs condemned the attacks.

articles.title: NatWest faces AGM showdown over climate backtracking | NatWest Group | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: NatWest is facing a shareholder showdown at its annual meeting this week as investors and leading scientists call for an urgent reversal of the bank's climate policy changes. ShareAction, along with investors including the Church of England, are demanding that the bank meet with them within three months to discuss its future direction on climate strategy. The campaigners argue that the bank has undermined public trust by dropping commitments not to lend to oil and gas companies and abandoning decarbonization targets, while a group of 70 climate experts call for leadership and a reversal of these backtracking actions. NatWest maintains that it has retained interim targets to at least half its climate impact compared with 2019 and is working towards net zero emissions from financing by 2050.

articles.title: Pakistani exports to major European markets slow down amid ME conflict despite GSP+ status - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's exports to major Western and Northern European markets have experienced negative growth in the first nine months of the current fiscal year, despite continued GSP+ status. This decline is attributed to a shifting global trade environment, including the US-Iran conflict and the EU offering preferential market access to India. The EU has also warned Pakistan that its GSP+ access is not guaranteed and depends on progress on human rights issues.  This challenging situation puts pressure on Pakistani exporters to maintain compliance with EU conditions while facing increased competition from countries gaining expanded market access.

articles.title: Rising heat takes toll on bird diversity in Kottayam, finds survey - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tropical Institute of Ecological Sciences (TIES) conducted a survey in Kottayam city, revealing a significant decline in urban bird diversity this year. The study, involving birdwatchers and experts, recorded only 31 species compared to 47 last year, likely due to rising summer temperatures driving birds towards denser tree cover for shelter.  Commonly spotted birds included the White Cheeked Barbet, Common Myna, crows, Racket Tailed Drongo, Black Drongo, and Rock Pigeon. The survey also noted a decrease in nesting activity at the heronry near the Nagampadam stadium.

articles.title: Timeline: Trump assassination attempts and security incidents | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and top White House officials were evacuated from the White House Correspondents’ Dinner after an armed man opened fire. The suspect, identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen from Torrance, California, was arrested at the event. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche stated charges would be filed shortly. This follows a series of security incidents involving Trump, including a shooting at a Pennsylvania rally in July 2024 and an attempt on his life at a golf course in Florida in September 2024. In February 2026, a man crashed into the security perimeter of Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, leading to his death.

articles.title: King Charles’s security for US visit this week reviewed after Washington shooting | King Charles III | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Buckingham Palace is reviewing security arrangements for King Charles III's upcoming state visit to the US following a shooting incident at a White House dinner attended by Donald Trump.  The suspect, 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen, was arrested and faces charges related to assaulting an officer. The US and UK are working together to ensure appropriate security measures for the visit, with discussions already underway about potential adjustments. Darren Jones, chief secretary to the prime minister, stated that security arrangements will be in place based on the risk assessment.

articles.title: President Zardari underscores industrial cooperation, technology partnership during visit to China - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari visited Sany Heavy Industry Co. Ltd. in Changsha, China, to discuss bolstering industrial and technological cooperation between the two countries. During his visit, Zardari was briefed on the company's advanced manufacturing systems, product lines, and ongoing investments in research and development (R&D). He highlighted the importance of strengthening partnerships in areas such as construction machinery, digital manufacturing, clean energy, and engineering solutions. The president also toured Sany's flagship No. 18 Factory, a digitally integrated facility recognized for its advanced automation and data-driven production systems. Zardari emphasized the potential for collaboration between Pakistan and China to modernize infrastructure and industrial growth.

articles.title: Stayed at Hilton, no metal detectors: How suspect slipped past security, carried out shooting at WH Correspondents’ Dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An armed man breached security at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner, exchanging gunfire with law enforcement before being apprehended.  The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, was found to have entered the hotel disguised and carrying a shotgun, handgun, and multiple knives. He was charged with felony firearm and assault charges. Secret Service agents were stationed throughout the ballroom, including a buffer between the president and attendees, in an effort to prevent further incidents.
articles.civic_flag_reason: A gunman breached security at a high-profile event, raising concerns about security failures.

articles.title: Three-tier security in place at counting centres in Cuddalore district - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: District Election Officer Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar
articles.rephrased_article: District Election Officer Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar oversaw the secure transportation and placement of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) and Voter-Verified Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) units in designated counting centres. The materials were moved to the centres, sealed in strong rooms with representatives from candidates and observers present, marking the completion of the process early Friday morning.

articles.title: Kenya’s Sawe is world’s first man to run a sub-two-hour marathon in London | Athletics | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sebastian Sawe of Kenya became the first man to run a marathon in under two hours, winning the London Marathon in 1:59:30.  He shattered the previous world record held by his late compatriot Kelvin Kiptum, who set a time of 2:00:35 at the Chicago Marathon in October 2023.  Assefa of Ethiopia defended her women’s crown, breaking her own world record with a time of 2:15:41.

articles.title: Voters contend with ‘grotesque’ leaflets and ‘dodgy’ data in English elections | Local elections 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Full Fact, a non-partisan organization, analyzed 331 leaflets from across England distributed by various political parties ahead of the May elections. The analysis revealed that many leaflets used misleading data and unsubstantiated claims to influence voter choices. Some leaflets presented charts or graphs with unreliable evidence, claiming that only one party could win or that another party couldn't win in a specific area. Peter Kellner, former chair of YouGov, described the tactics as "grotesque" and noted that such misleading information contributes to a decline in trust in politics.  Full Fact concluded that while parties have a right to make their case to voters, these leaflets could mislead people by presenting inaccurate or cherry-picked data.

articles.title: BJP committed to women's security, Trinamool ‘stands with goons who torture women’: PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi accused the Trinamool Congress of sheltering criminals who harm women, citing the BJP's support for Rekha Patra and the mother of an RG Kar victim as proof of its commitment to women's safety.  He also announced that all refugees fleeing religious persecution in neighboring countries would be granted citizenship through the Citizenship Amendment Act procedures.

articles.title: 'No place for political violence': World leaders react to White House correspondents' dinner shooting - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump were safely evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner after a shooting incident.  Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, and others condemned the attack, emphasizing that political violence has no place in a democracy.  Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi also expressed relief at the safety of the attendees while condemning the incident.

articles.title: Shivamogga MP urges people not to panic over nuclear power plant, says no such proposal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: B.Y. Raghavendra, Shivamogga Member of Parliament, has denied reports of a nuclear plant being planned at Besur in Sagar taluk.  He clarified that NTPC identified the districts of Vijayapura, Koppal, Shivamogga, Uttara Kannada and Raichur for potential nuclear power plant construction. The Additional Chief Secretary of the Revenue Department was tasked with conducting preliminary studies on suitable locations within these districts.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards injures knee in Timberwolves’ Game 4 win against Nuggets | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Edwards left the Timberwolves' Game 4 win over the Nuggets with a knee injury, while teammate Donte DiVincenzo also sustained an injury. articles.title: Rescuers find body of boy swept away while swimming in Karachi water line - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

articles.title: Chernobyl: From Nuclear Disaster to Thriving Wildlife Sanctuary | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reports that the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone has become a thriving wildlife sanctuary, with large mammal populations comparable to uncontaminated reserves.  Species like Przewalski's horses, Eurasian lynx, and European bison have returned, while the greater spotted eagle population is growing. The absence of human activity has had a more positive impact on animal numbers than radiation levels. The zone serves as an "unintended but invaluable natural laboratory" for studying genetic and ecological effects of chronic radiation exposure.

articles.title: Raghu Rai, legendary Indian photographer, dies at 83 | Arts and Culture News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Raghu Rai, a legendary Indian photographer and Magnum Photos icon, died at 83.  Born in Pakistan's Punjab province before the partition of India, Rai documented India's complex social and political life for decades, capturing pivotal moments like the 1971 Bangladesh independence war and the 1984 Bhopal gas leak. His photographs are considered defining visual records of India's history, earning him accolades such as the Padma Shri and the Academie des Beaux-Arts Photography Award. Rai was a member of Magnum Photos and his work is celebrated for its ability to capture the soul of India, with portraits of political and social elites, and intimate glimpses into everyday life.  His legacy will be remembered through his extensive photo-books and enduring impact on photography.

articles.title: Teen arrested in Louisiana shooting got ride from scene from grandmother | Louisiana | The Guardian

articles.title: Chernobyl: From Nuclear Disaster to Thriving Wildlife Sanctuary | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A thriving wildlife sanctuary has emerged in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone (CEZ) 40 years after the world's worst civilian nuclear accident.  The absence of human activity has led to a resurgence of large mammal populations, including wolves, wild boar, and European bison, while endangered species like Przewalski's horses and lynx have returned. The CEZ is now home to diverse bird species, including white-tailed eagles and cranes, and even some plant adaptations to radiation. articles.title: Ghost MOTs: drivers warned over fake certificates that lead to huge repair bills | Scams | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ghost MOTs, where garages falsely claim to have conducted an MOT, are a growing concern for car owners.  This scam occurs when a mechanic or garage registers the vehicle as passed even though no actual inspection took place. This can lead to unsuspecting buyers discovering problems with their cars after purchase, including worn brakes, bald tires, and faulty lights. KwikFit advises drivers to choose reputable garages that clearly explain the MOT process and only perform repairs with their consent. If a car has been fraudulently passed, it could result in costly repairs and insurance disputes. Drivers can report suspicious garages to the DVSA.

articles.title: 'Quite an evening': Trump wanted 'the show to go on' after shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner - The Times of India

articles.title: Dozens of MPs oppose Streeting’s new power to say what NHS pays for drugs | Wes Streeting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wes Streeting, the health secretary, has been granted power to dictate drug prices for the NHS. Thirty-one MPs have objected to this move, citing concerns that it undermines the independence of the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) and could lead to increased costs for patients.  The change was made in a deal with the Trump administration, which has been criticized by health experts and medical professionals who warn that higher drug spending will force the NHS to make difficult cuts to other services.

articles.title: Punjab to export livestock - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab's government signed a memorandum of understanding with seven institutions, including China’s Global Meat Company, to export livestock and meat. The agreement will see one million animals exported, with the Global Meat Company installing a boiler unit for large-scale boiled meat production.  The province also plans to establish state-of-the-art veterinary hospitals and mobile dispensaries, provide subsidies on livestock machinery, and distribute free livestock to rural women.

articles.title: 1,000 days of Annavaasal: Erode’s dusk meal mission feeds over 2.5 lakh people - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Erode Siragugal, a trust known for its environmental work, has completed 1,000 days of uninterrupted service with its free dinner initiative, Annavaasal.  The project, launched in July 2023, provides nutritious meals to over 2.5 lakh people at the Government Headquarters Hospital and surrounding areas. The initiative began as a response to food insecurity during the COVID-19 lockdown and has since been sustained by donations and volunteer efforts. Erode Siragugal president K.K. Vimal Karuppannan stated that the project is driven by a commitment to ensuring no one goes hungry in Erode, with an average of 250 people being served daily.

articles.title: ‘I just want to go home’: Tearful Erika Kirk escorted out after White House Correspondents' Dinner shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner in Washington, D.C., triggered panic and evacuation of the venue.  The Secret Service apprehended a suspect who opened fire near the main security screening area. The incident occurred during an event attended by prominent figures including Donald Trump, Melania Trump, JD Vance, Pete Hegseth, and Marco Rubio.  Karoline Leavitt, White House Press Secretary, was present and had previously commented that President Trump's speech would be "funny, entertaining," and "classic Donald J. Trump."

articles.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 58 as Tehran-Washington talks stall? | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump canceled a planned visit to Pakistan by his envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, due to concerns about the inadequate nature of the peace proposal offered by Iran.  Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi left Pakistan for Oman and then Russia, presenting a potential framework for ending the conflict. President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran would not enter "imposed negotiations" under threats or blockade. The US president maintains that there is “tremendous infighting” within Iran’s leadership and that they have no leverage in the negotiation process.  The conflict has pushed energy prices to multi-year highs, stoked inflation, and darkened global growth prospects.

articles.title: Video shows correspondents' dinner suspect charge checkpoint
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump released surveillance video showing a suspect running past metal detectors at the White House correspondents' dinner security checkpoint. Washington DC police chief Jeffery W Carroll stated that officers exchanged gunfire with the suspect, injuring one US Secret Service officer who is now in good spirits. The suspect, identified as a "lone gunman", was not struck by gunfire but has been transported to hospital for evaluation.

articles.title: UK departments at odds over energy demands of AI datacentres | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) and the Department of Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) have differing projections for the energy consumption of AI datacentres in the UK.  DSIT predicts that AI datacentres will consume 6GW of electricity by 2030, while DESNZ estimates they will use less than a tenth of that amount. Foxglove, an NGO, has raised concerns about the government's lack of understanding regarding the environmental impact of these facilities and the potential for corporate influence over UK policy.  The discrepancy between the two departments' forecasts remains unclear, but DSIT has revised its projections upwards after pressure from media inquiries.

articles.title: Punjab to export livestock - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Punjab's government signed a memorandum of understanding with seven institutions, including China’s Global Meat Company, to export one million livestock. The agreement includes the installation of a boiler unit by Global Meat Company in collaboration with Punjab Agriculture and Meat Company for large-scale boiled meat preparation, as well as plans to fatten 300,000 buffaloes and cows, 300,000 sheep and goats, and raise 100,000 goats and sheep for export.
