The agreement also includes the establishment of state-of-the-art veterinary hospitals in every tehsil and mobile veterinary dispensaries to provide door-to-door animal treatment.

articles.title: 1,000 days of Annavaasal: Erode’s dusk meal mission feeds over 2.5 lakh people - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Erode Siragugal, a trust known for environmental protection and food waste management, has celebrated 1,000 days of uninterrupted service for its "Annavaasal" initiative. This free dinner program, launched in July 2023, provides nutritious meals to over 2.5 lakh people in Erode.  The initiative began as a response to the needs of patients' attendants during the COVID-19 lockdown and has since grown into a sustained effort with support from donors and volunteers who prepare and distribute home-style food daily between 6 p.m. and 6:30 p.m. The trust, which incurs an annual expenditure of ₹23 lakh to ₹25 lakh, aims to continue the program indefinitely.

articles.title: More than a dozen threats & assassination attempts — Timeline of attacks against Donald Trump - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting attempt disrupted US President Donald Trump's address at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. The incident occurred shortly before Trump was due to speak, as guests reported hearing multiple gunshots near a security checkpoint outside the main ballroom. Secret Service agents swiftly moved to shield Trump and other officials, and armed officers secured the perimeter. One officer was injured but protected by a bulletproof vest. Authorities apprehended a suspect and are investigating the incident. This event adds to a timeline of threats faced by Trump, including rally shootings, armed suspects, poison letters, foreign-linked murder plots, and repeated security lapses, making him one of the most frequently targeted political figures in modern US history.

articles.title: Washington shooting: Is Trump safe? What we know so far | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following a shooting at the White House correspondents’ dinner, Donald Trump was safely removed from the event. A man identified as 31-year-old Cole Tomas Allen attempted to breach security and fire shots at a Secret Service agent. The suspect is in custody and authorities are investigating.  The incident prompted the cancellation of the dinner, which will be rescheduled within 30 days. Trump praised the bravery of the Secret Service agent who was shot but unharmed and assured the public that he is safe.

articles.title: Netanyahu orders army to 'vigorously attack' Hezbollah in Lebanon
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, ordered his military to "vigorously attack" Hezbollah targets in Lebanon following a ceasefire extension.  The attacks followed strikes on Saturday that killed at least six people in southern Lebanon and strained the truce agreement. Hezbollah retaliated by targeting an Israeli army vehicle in south Lebanon. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) claimed to have eliminated several members of the group, while Hezbollah said it targeted an Israeli military vehicle.  The attacks have been condemned by international press advocacy groups who called for media freedom and safety.

articles.title: Patient allegedly attacks several nurses, police and member of the public at Sydney hospital | Sydney | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A violent attack on nurses at Prince of Wales hospital in Sydney left one nurse seriously injured and prompted calls for improved safety measures. The incident involved a 51-year-old patient who allegedly assaulted several staff members, including nurses, police officers, and a member of the public.  The New South Wales Nurses and Midwives’ Association expressed concern over escalating violence in emergency departments, citing a recent report showing that 88% of respondents had experienced violence in the previous year. The association plans to work with impacted parties and SafeWork NSW to identify areas for improvement following Saturday's incident.

articles.title: Marka-i-Haq Monument under construction at Islamabad's Kutchery Chowk - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Marka-i-Haq monument, a replica of the one in H-8 Islamabad, is being constructed in Baggi Park at Kutchery Chowk by the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO). The project is expected to be completed before May 10th, marking the first anniversary of the operation Bunyanum Marsoos.  The provincial government funded the monument's construction, which aims to commemorate victims and honor the sacrifices of martyrs and ghazis. The Rawalpindi Municipal Corporation has suggested renaming the Kutchery Chowk flyover and underpass as Marka-i-Haq Flyover and Underpass for public feedback.

articles.title: Engineering student harassed in Vijayawada auto, accused booked after Sakthi App alert - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sakthi App alerted police after an engineering student was allegedly harassed by an auto driver on her way from Vijayawada to Nambur.  The incident occurred late Saturday night, and the driver, B. Phanindra, has been registered for his actions. The student reported the harassment to authorities through the Sakthi App.

articles.title: Developer, CalTech pass out — White House dinner shooter Cole Thomas Allen a 'highly educated tutor' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cole Tomas Allen, a 31-year-old from California, has been identified as the suspect who fired shots at the White House Correspondents' Dinner.  He will be charged with two counts of "using a firearm during a crime of violence" and for "assault on a federal officer using a dangerous weapon." President Donald Trump shared visuals of Allen being apprehended by the Secret Service, stating that he was armed with multiple weapons. The incident occurred despite Allen's access to the event as a guest of the hotel.  Charges are expected to be filed soon.

articles.title: We can make sure another Chornobyl disaster does not happen, here is how | Renewable Energy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The world faces a renewed risk of nuclear disaster as Ukraine and Iran grapple with ongoing military activity near nuclear sites. The 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster serves as a stark reminder of the long-lasting consequences of such accidents, highlighting the vulnerability of centralized energy systems to geopolitical tensions and war.  However, decentralised renewable energy solutions offer an alternative, providing greater resilience, stability, and independence from global events. These decentralized systems can withstand attacks, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and ensure a more secure energy future for communities worldwide.

articles.title: Inside the room as shots rang out at correspondents' dinner
articles.rephrased_article: At the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner, shots rang out, prompting a chaotic scene where attendees took cover under tables.  President Trump, his wife Melania Trump, and Vice-President JD Vance were escorted away by Secret Service agents who had been alerted to the situation. Health Secretary RFK Jr. was also present at the event and witnessed the unfolding events. The security measures at the venue appeared lax, with attendees going through minimal screening before entering the ballroom.  The incident left attendees shaken and grappling with the implications of the shooting.

articles.title: The tortoise and the hare: will China beat the US in the race back to the moon? | Space | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US and China are engaged in a space race to establish lunar bases, with the former seeking to regain its lead while the latter aims to solidify its position.  Both countries have ambitious plans for manned missions and resource exploration, but their approaches differ significantly. While Nasa, facing budgetary constraints and political instability, relies on private companies like SpaceX and Blue Origin, China has a more consistent track record of adhering to timelines and is driven by domestic ambitions.  The race's impact extends beyond national pride, with international collaborations emerging despite geopolitical tensions.

articles.title: Head master death case; one arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bijapur police have arrested a construction contractor, Devashish Mandal, in connection with the suicide of school headmaster Raju Pujari.  Pujari's death note accused Mandal, an engineer, and a department officer of involvement in his suicide. The incident occurred on April 22, 2026, after a dispute arose regarding payment for construction work at the school.

articles.title: New auto assemblers dodge localisation details - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: CKD imports surged to $1.47 billion in the first nine months of fiscal year 2026, a significant increase from previous years. Local vendors are complaining about low local part use by new auto players, while some assemblers have begun producing parts for their own vehicles and selling them to other assemblers.  The rise in imports is attributed to new models launched with limited localization under the current auto policy, as well as high demand for hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), and battery electric vehicles (BEVs). Experts warn that this trend could hinder Pakistan's industrial ecosystem and limit technological development.

articles.title: Trump evacuated from media dinner after gunshots; supporters say another assassination attempt - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump was hurriedly evacuated from a White House Correspondents’ Association dinner at the Washington Hilton hotel after shots were fired near the main magnetometer screening area. The Secret Service is investigating the incident, which occurred shortly before Trump was scheduled to deliver his speech. One individual is in custody, and law enforcement is assessing the situation.  The president and first lady are safe, as are other protectees including Vice President J.D. Vance and several cabinet members who were present at the event.

articles.title: Trump thought sound of gunman at journalists’ dinner was tray falling | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump initially thought a noise at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner was a tray falling, but quickly realized it was a gunman. The president described the incident as shocking and said he watched to see what was happening before being briefed by officials including Vice President JD Vance, FBI Director Kash Patel, and Acting US Attorney General Todd Blanche.  He praised the Secret Service for apprehending the gunman, who fired on a US agent but was stopped before reaching the ballroom.

articles.title: Thrissur pooram returned, but they didn’t - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thrissur Pooram, a traditional festival in Kerala, has returned with a subdued celebration after the devastating explosion at the Mundathikode firework unit.  The tragedy claimed the lives of several individuals who dedicated their lives to making the festival spectacular. Families are grappling with grief and uncertainty as they mourn the loss of loved ones who were passionate about the Pooram. The absence of their presence is keenly felt, leaving a void that cannot be filled.

articles.title: Measles claims lives of 71 children across country in four months - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan is observing World Immunisation Week from April 24 to 30 with a focus on increasing vaccination rates. The Sindh government has held public awareness activities following the deaths of 71 children, including 40 in the province, due to measles in the first four months of this year.  Dr Raj Kumar, Programme Director EPI, Sindh, highlighted efforts to address vaccine hesitancy and improve coverage, particularly in districts with frequent outbreaks. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) expressed concern over a high number of "zero-dose" children and urged investment in local vaccine manufacturing to reduce reliance on imports.

articles.title: Bomb attack kills 14, injures 38 in Colombia weeks before presidential election - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: At least 14 people were killed and 38 others injured in a highway bomb attack in southwestern Colombia on Saturday. President Gustavo Petro blamed dissident factions of the now-disbanded FARC guerrilla group for the attack, attributing it to Iván Mordisco, Colombia’s most-wanted fugitive.  The bombing occurred in the conflict-hit Cauca department and left multiple vehicles overturned and bodies covered with sheets as rescue crews worked at the scene. Authorities have stepped up military and police deployments across affected areas.

articles.title: ‘Violence must never be the way’: world leaders react to Washington shooting at Trump event | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Leaders from around the world condemned the shooting incident at the White House correspondents dinner, expressing relief that Donald Trump, his wife Melania Trump, and other attendees were unharmed. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, and British Ambassador Christian Turner all offered their well wishes and praised the swift response of law enforcement.  The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, is in custody and being evaluated at a local hospital.

articles.title: CJI bats for structured national registry of former judges willing to serve in ADR - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant called for the creation of a structured national framework to utilize the experience of retired judges in alternative dispute resolution (ADR) mechanisms. He emphasized that their continued engagement should be treated as institutional service with accountability and support, highlighting their potential roles as mediators, arbitrators, legal educators, pre-litigation counsellors, and institution builders. Chief Justice Kant also stressed the importance of ADR systems like mediation, Lok Adalats, and arbitration in ensuring access to justice for millions of Indians.  He urged society to utilize these mechanisms before resorting to court proceedings.

articles.title: Another POL price hike triggers widespread anxiety - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistani government announced a new increase in petrol and diesel prices, prompting widespread criticism from the public, trade unions, and civil society groups.  They argue that repeated price hikes are disproportionately impacting low-income individuals and businesses, exacerbating economic hardship.  A petition has been filed in the Lahore High Court challenging the legality of the recent increases, alleging that they are driven by taxation measures rather than international oil prices. The petitioner demands transparency from the government regarding petroleum pricing and an immediate halt to further price hikes until a transparent mechanism is established.

articles.title: 'Shots will be fired': Karoline Leavitt’s pre-dinner comments go viral after White House shooting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt made a statement about the upcoming White House Correspondents' Dinner that has garnered attention.  She said, "There will be some shots fired tonight in the room," before an incident occurred where armed security personnel shot a suspect who had forced his way into the event. The suspect, identified as Cole Tomas Allen, was apprehended and faces firearm and assault charges. Donald Trump was evacuated from the stage during the incident, which caused panic among guests.

articles.title: ‘Sludge in the system’: myriad problems stymie Labour’s 1.5m new homes pledge | Construction industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK's housing crisis is being exacerbated by a combination of factors, including a skills shortage, rising material costs, and affordability concerns. Despite government pledges to build 1.5 million new homes, the pace of construction remains sluggish.  A lack of affordable housing options and high costs are hindering progress. While planning reforms have been implemented to streamline development processes, they haven't yet addressed underlying issues such as supply chain disruptions and rising material prices. The industry is facing a significant cost of doing business crisis, with many developers struggling to make projects viable. Experts warn that the government needs to address these challenges to achieve its housing targets.

articles.title: Hydrologist backs TUDA plan to revive Avilala tank on lines of Hyderabad’s Tank Bund - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Arun Krishnamurthy, founder of the Environmentalist Foundation of India (EFI), endorsed the Tirupati Urban Development Authority’s (TUDA) plan to conserve and revive the Avilala tank.  The project, which will be executed by the Water Resources Department using TUDA funds, includes restoring the supply channel from Peruru tank to Avilala. The TUDA board, led by chairman Divakar Reddy and vice-chairman R. Govindarao, has approved the necessary sanctions for the work.

articles.title: Trump safe after shooting at White House correspondents dinner; suspect in custody - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A man armed with a shotgun fired at a Secret Service agent near the entrance of the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday night, prompting an evacuation and cancellation of the event. Donald Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, were safely removed from the venue by Secret Service agents after the shooting. The suspect was apprehended and will be arraigned in US capital on Monday.  The incident occurred at the Washington Hilton, a location with a history of high-profile security incidents, including an attempt on President Ronald Reagan's life in 1981. Anthony Guglielmi, a Secret Service spokesman, stated that the service is investigating the shooting. The event was condemned by world leaders such as Asif Ali Zardari and Shehbaz Sharif.

articles.title: Countries with the most millionaires in 2026: The US tops the global list, China and France follow | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The distribution of global wealth in 2026 shows the United States continuing to dominate the list of high-net-worth individuals, holding a lead that remains difficult to close. China follows closely behind, while countries such as France, Japan, and the United Kingdom show similar levels of wealth distribution. Emerging economies like India are showing signs of faster growth, indicating broader economic changes including digital growth, investment flows, and evolving business environments.

articles.title: Ukrainian action thriller billed as Saving Private Ryan for the drone age | Ukraine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Ukrainian war film "Killhouse" is a fictional action thriller that draws inspiration from real-life stories of drone rescues during the ongoing conflict. The film, which features cameos by prominent figures like former military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and US journalist Audrey MacAlpine, depicts the use of drones in warfare and showcases Ukraine's latest technology.  The director, Liubomyr Levytskyi, drew inspiration from a real-life rescue operation where a woman followed a drone to save her unconscious husband. The film was produced with support from Ukrainian intelligence agencies and has been met with positive reception from audiences.

articles.title: Shooter fires five to eight shots at White House dinner, Donald Trump evacuated - what we know so far - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance were evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner after shots were heard. The incident occurred at the Washington Hilton, where guests scrambled for cover as Secret Service personnel swarmed the area.  Both Trump and Vance were reported uninjured. Security agencies apprehended a suspect, but authorities have not released details about the shooting or the suspect.

articles.title: Ashok Kharat case: Oshnology and other deceptions of a godman - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ashokkumar Kharat, a godman, was granted judicial custody after being brought to the Nashik District Sessions Court for charges of sexual assault and forced abortion. The prosecution, led by Shailendra Bagade and Kiran Bendbhar, accused him of these crimes.  The case is ongoing with Kharat appearing via videoconference the following day.

articles.title: Iran war live: Tehran rejects talks under siege, Trump cancels envoys’ trip | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump canceled a planned visit to Pakistan by his envoys, citing that Iran did not make a satisfactory offer for a peace deal. This follows the departure of Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, from Pakistan where he presented mediators with a potential framework for ending the conflict.

articles.title: Person in custody after Trump evacuated in shooting incident at White House correspondents’ dinner | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and members of his cabinet were evacuated from the White House correspondents’ dinner after a shooting incident at the Washington Hilton. The FBI apprehended a suspect near the main magnetometer screening area, and Secret Service agents confirmed that an agent was hit by a bullet but survived. The event was interrupted as journalists ducked for cover, with some reporting mixed messages about whether to stay in the room.  Weijia Jang, president of the dinner, said the event would be rescheduled within 30 days, and Jamie Raskin, a Democratic congressman, stated he saw Secret Service agents throwing people to the ground during the commotion.

articles.title: Iran war jitters to influence policy rate decision - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Experts predict a 100 basis point interest rate hike by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) committee on Monday, driven primarily by concerns over geopolitical instability in the Gulf region. While inflation is currently at 14%, some experts believe a smaller increase of 50 basis points would be sufficient to address the uncertainty.  The decision reflects the SBP's focus on long-term economic impacts and global trends, with Tresmark, a currency tracker, suggesting a preemptive move to protect hot money flows and counter inflation. The interest rate hike will likely benefit exporters and remitters but pose challenges for importers and increase the government's debt burden.

articles.title: Trump White House shooting live updates: 'This is why we need security at ballroom' - Trump says one officer shot by suspect who 'had many weapons' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting incident occurred at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, D.C., prompting an immediate security response and evacuation of President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance. The suspect was apprehended after exchanging gunfire with security personnel near the venue.  The shooting took place outside the main ballroom, but panic spread quickly inside as guests ducked for cover.  President Trump described the incident as a "security breach" and praised the Secret Service's response, stating that the officer who was shot was saved by wearing a bulletproof vest. The suspect has not been identified, and authorities are still investigating the motive behind the shooting.

articles.title: Kavitha’s ‘TRS’ may face ECI scrutiny over acronym similarity - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Election Commission of India (ECI) may reject the proposed name "Telangana Rashtra Sena" for Kalvakuntla Kavitha's new political outfit due to its resemblance to the existing Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS). The ECI scrutinizes party names for potential voter confusion, examining phonetic similarity and visual resemblance. While the BRS is not objecting to the name, some sources suggest that the ECI may approve it if Kavitha has good relations with New Delhi. However, Karthik Reddy, son of a BRS MLA, believes the ECI's decision could be a deliberate tactic to delay registration.

articles.title: Trump evacuated from White House correspondents’ dinner after shots fired | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump was evacuated from the White House correspondents’ dinner in Washington, DC after shots were fired outside the event. The president and first lady were unharmed, but one Secret Service officer was shot during the incident. Trump condemned the suspect as a "thug" who attacked the US Constitution and called for Americans to resolve their differences peacefully.  The Secret Service is assessing the situation and one individual is in custody.

articles.title: Trump says officer saved by bulletproof vest in shooting at White House correspondents’ dinner - follow live | White House correspondents' dinner shooting | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: After a shooting interrupted the White House Correspondents' Dinner, Donald Trump spoke from the briefing room.  The suspect was apprehended and is being evaluated in a hospital, but investigators believe he acted alone. Trump praised law enforcement for their quick response and said the incident highlighted the need for increased security at the White House. The president also expressed his gratitude to those who were present during the attack and assured that the rescheduled dinner would be "better" and "safer."

articles.title: Trump safe after being rushed from White House correspondents dinner, shooter in custody - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, were evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Association dinner after a man armed with a shotgun attempted to breach security. The incident occurred shortly after the suspect fired at a Secret Service agent, who was unharmed.  The event was canceled for the evening, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed his shock and relief that all attendees were safe.

articles.title: Watch: Donald Trump ducks for cover as security rushes to evacuate him after shots heard at White House press dinner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance were evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner after shots were fired inside the Washington Hilton.  The incident triggered panic among guests, who scrambled for cover as Secret Service personnel secured the area.  Both Trump and Vance were reported uninjured. The shooter was apprehended by authorities.

articles.title: UDF will probe “corruption” in the cancellation of DBFOO power supply contracts if it comes to power: V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, leader of the Opposition, called for a probe into alleged corruption behind the cancellation of long-term power supply contracts by the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission and the KSEB. He argued that the decision to cancel these contracts led to unscheduled loadsheddings and increased power costs for the state.  The contracts had guaranteed power at ₹4.29 per unit, but the cancellation resulted in higher costs of ₹6 to ₹12 per unit, causing daily losses of ₹15 crore to ₹20 crore for the KSEB.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of corruption leading to power issues raise concerns about institutional failure.

articles.title: Dramatic scenes as Trump rushed from White House gala | Donald Trump | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump was rushed from a White House gala after dramatic scenes unfolded. The incident occurred during an event celebrating the SAVE Act, a bipartisan bill aimed at addressing issues related to student loan debt.  Details surrounding the circumstances of the rush are currently unclear.

articles.title: Police blocked members of anti-immigration group from Perth dawn service after Anzac Day booing in eastern states | Melbourne | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Western Australian police proactively removed 15 individuals identified as members of "issue motivated groups" from Anzac Day commemorations in Perth following disruptions at ceremonies in Sydney, Melbourne, and Perth. The removals were made to protect the dignity of the commemorations, maintain public safety, and ensure respectful attendance. New South Wales police arrested a 24-year-old man for alleged nuisance behavior during the Sydney dawn service, while Victoria Police reported two incidents of booing at the Shrine of Remembrance.  Indigenous academic Marcia Langton called for those who disrupted ceremonies to be named and banned from future Anzac Day services.

articles.title: Hormuz stays flashpoint amid reopening move - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's military warned of a response to continued US blockade of its ports, while France, Germany, and Turkey expressed interest in de-mining missions in the Strait of Hormuz.  Emmanuel Macron stated his aim is to reopen the strait "in coming days and weeks" with international law guaranteeing freedom of navigation.  The US has blocked Iranian ports to stop its oil exports, leading to energy shortages and a flashpoint in negotiations.

articles.title: From Ronald Reagan to Donald Trump: How Washington Hilton hotel became scene of panic once again - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: During the White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Washington Hilton, shots were fired, prompting a security response. US President Donald Trump was rushed to safety by Secret Service agents after the incident.  The shooter was apprehended and described as "quite an evening" by Trump, who commended the security agencies for their swift action.

articles.title: Raghu Rai death: Renowned photographer passes away at 83 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Raghu Rai, a renowned photographer, passed away on Sunday (April 26, 2026), according to his family.  His career spanned over half a century and he is remembered for his prolific work in photography.

articles.title: Trump live: US president safe after shots fired near correspondents’ dinner | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump and members of his cabinet were evacuated from the White House correspondents' dinner after shots were fired outside the event. Trump confirmed that the shooter has been apprehended, stating that First Lady Melania Trump and Vice President JD Vance are unharmed.

articles.title: Angus Taylor says higher risk of ‘bad people coming from bad countries’ as he singles out Iran | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Angus Taylor, the Liberal leader, doubled down on his immigration policy, stating that some migrants from "bad countries" pose a higher risk of not subscribing to liberal democratic values. He defended his party's preference for the National Party over an independent candidate in the upcoming Farrer byelection, arguing it was the "least worst option". Taylor also refused to criticize Pauline Hanson, who advocates for limiting visas and has called for stricter immigration policies.

articles.title: Four booked for child marriage in Kasaragod - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chandera police have registered a case against the organizers of an alleged child marriage in Kasaragod district.  The case involves Padna panchayat member P.K. Thajuddin, a cleric from Azhikkal Juma Masjid, and Sabir (28), who allegedly married a 16-year-old girl. The Child Marriage Prohibition Officer filed the report after receiving a complaint that the marriage took place on April 13th at the mosque.  The case was directed by a magistrate's court for police investigation.

articles.title: Residents stage protest, seek house sites in Mangalagiri - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Mangalagiri-Tadepalli, led by the CPI(M), staged a protest at the municipal corporation office demanding allocation of house sites and ownership pattas.  The protesters, many carrying applications, accused authorities of delays in implementing promises made to the poor.  Ch. Baburao, CPI(M) state secretariat member, along with district leaders Y. Netaji and Pasham Ramarao, urged for expedited identification of eligible beneficiaries.

articles.title: Vehicles stranded after avalanche hits Srinagar-Kargil highway - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A snow avalanche on the Kashmir-Ladakh national highway caused significant disruptions, stranding several vehicles and leaving one driver missing. The incident occurred near Shaitan Nallah in Sonamarg, Kashmir, where a major avalanche swept into the highway, forcing its closure.  Rescue teams are actively searching for the missing driver while authorities have relocated stranded commuters to safer locations. This follows a similar tragedy on March 28th when seven people lost their lives in an avalanche at the Zojila Pass.

articles.title: Australia news live: Taylor says Coalition preferencing One Nation in Farrer to stop ‘teal policies’; Victoria announces one-off car rego rebate | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Coalition has preferred One Nation ahead of independent Michelle Milthorpe in the upcoming Farrer byelection to prevent "teal policies," according to opposition leader Angus Taylor.  Taylor stated that preferences beyond the National Party are picking the least worst option and he wants people to vote for the Liberal Party and the National Party. He also criticized "teal" policies as existential threats to regional electorates. Meanwhile, Angus Taylor called for a reduction in the use of welcome to country remarks, arguing they have been "devalued" by overuse.  He stated that booing during Anzac Day events is inappropriate and un-Australian.

articles.title: Census 2027: States asked to identify vulnerable areas, keep biased enumerators out - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) has instructed State Directorates to identify vulnerable populations during the ongoing Census exercise, including those affected by communal or political tensions. The RG&CCI emphasized avoiding enumerators with biases towards specific social or religious communities and ensuring all individuals are counted without omission, as any inaccuracies could lead to legal challenges.  The census is being conducted in two phases: Housing Listing and Housing Census (HLO) from April 1 to September 30, followed by Population Enumeration in February 2027. The RG&CCI has also outlined specific guidelines for enumerators, including the preference for teachers and local officials familiar with the area.

articles.title: March to Manipur CM’s house foiled; 22 injured - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: More than 20 people were injured in clashes between protesters and security personnel in Imphal, Manipur, on Saturday (April 25, 2026). The Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (COCOMI), a conglomerate of Meitei civil society organizations, organized the protest demanding the arrest of those involved in the April 7 bomb attack that killed two children.  COCOMI had previously announced a boycott of the ruling BJP and held a rally near the iconic Kangla Fort before meeting with the Chief Minister to submit a memorandum. The incident followed the death of three protesters in Bishnupur, which triggered the protest. In Ukhrul district, an armored vehicle from a paramilitary force rammed barricades set up by locals protesting against inaction against Kuki armed groups.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Clashes with security forces injuring protesters over a bombing is a serious concern.

articles.title: Six persons held in Tiruvannamalai for damaging glass panels at polling booth on poll day - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tiruvannamalai Taluk police arrested six individuals for damaging glass panels at a polling booth in Melpathur village during the election day. The incident occurred after an argument between S. Arunkumar, an AIADMK booth agent, and a group led by K. Arunpandian.  The suspects reportedly assaulted Arunkumar and threw stones at security personnel and voters, injuring S. Kumudhavalli, Sankari, and B. Kala. The individuals were taken into custody and lodged at the Central Prison in Vellore, while an investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Calls to do away with elephants, fireworks in temple festivals get louder in Kerala - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Narayana Guru’s call for the elimination of fireworks and elephant parades in temple festivals is gaining momentum following a recent firecracker accident in Thrissur that claimed 15 lives. Swami Sathchidananda, president of the Sivagiri Madom, advocates for government action to cease dangerous practices like fireworks displays, emphasizing the need for awareness programs.  S. Sreekala, Chairperson of the Kerala State Pollution Control Board (KSPCB), questions the environmental impact of fireworks and suggests exploring green alternatives. R. Venugopal, former Joint Chief Controller of Explosives at the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO), argues that while firework emissions initially appear harmful, they disperse quickly and are generally less damaging than automobile pollution.  Dr. A. Fathahudeen, senior consultant pulmonologist, stresses the need for lung health awareness in light of the recent accident and its potential long-term effects.

articles.title: SSLC results: Yadgir records 91.89 pass percentage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yadgir district has achieved a pass percentage of 91.89%, a significant increase from last year's 62.1%. This improvement, attributed to guidance and support from elected representatives, the district administration, and the zilla panchayat, propelled the district to 31st place in the state ranking table. Despite teacher vacancies, the department utilized available teachers effectively through special classes, overnight sessions, preparatory exams, and group discussions.  The efforts of all stakeholders resulted in a substantial improvement in pass percentage across all years, with girls consistently outperforming boys.

articles.title: 'Women will respond': Congress slams govt over 'delay' in 33% quota; says implement it at once - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ragini Nayak, Congress national spokesperson, criticized the Narendra Modi government for its lack of action on women's reservation in Parliament. She demanded immediate implementation of a 33% quota for women across existing Lok Sabha seats and called out the government's use of technical excuses to avoid addressing the issue.  Vardhan Yadav, Congress Gurugram District President, echoed Nayak's concerns, emphasizing that this is not just a political matter but a social justice issue.

articles.title: India advises nationals in Mali to stay indoors, exercise caution due to security developments - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's Embassy in Bamako issued a security advisory urging all Indian nationals residing in Mali to remain vigilant, exercise caution, and stay indoors due to recent security developments and reported attacks in Kati. The embassy urged citizens to follow instructions from the Malian authorities.

articles.title: Munnar on high UV alert as index hits dangerous levels - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Idukki District Collector Dineshan Cheruvatt issued a high alert for the district due to an alarming UV index of 8, prompting public advisories to avoid direct sunlight and cover exposed skin. The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority (KSDMA) has also directed the Tourism department and the District Tourism Promotion Council (DTPC) to issue warnings to tourists visiting Munnar, where two sunburn incidents were reported on Saturday.  The power generation at the Moolamattom power plant reached near maximum capacity, while water levels in the Idukki reservoir dropped significantly.

articles.title: Download e-Khata online, 13 lakh property records now downloadable - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has launched an online platform for citizens to download their e-Khata, simplifying property services.  Citizens can access the service by logging in with their mobile number and OTP on the https://BBMPeAasthi.karnataka.gov.in portal and downloading their e-Khata instantly. The GBA encourages residents to utilize this digital platform for quick and transparent access to their property records, urging them not to rely on middlemen or visit offices.

articles.title: Governor clears MLC nominations of Azharuddin, Kodandaram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla approved the nominations of Minister for Minority Welfare Mohammad Azharuddin and academic M. Kodandaram to the Legislative Council under the Governor’s quota, ending political speculation. The move clears the way for Mr. Azharuddin's continued service in the Cabinet, with a deadline approaching for him to secure membership in either House of the Legislature.

articles.title: Restoration work at Hindustan Petroleum’s Rajasthan refinery expected to complete in 3-4 weeks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) announced that restoration work at its Balotra refinery-cum-petrochemical complex, which caught fire before its inauguration earlier this week, is progressing and expected to be completed in three to four weeks. The company stated that the crude distillation unit is anticipated to restart in the second fortnight of May, while other secondary units are already nearing completion.

articles.title: Concern over air quality dip in Mysuru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu has updated its commenting platform.  Users must now comment in English and in full sentences, adhering to the publication's community guidelines. The new system allows users to access their older comments by logging into their accounts on Vuukle.

articles.title: Evolution of information centres in modern era highlighted at VIT-A.P. University - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalpakkam Saibaba, a former scientist from the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Energy (IGCAR), spoke at World Book and Copyright Day celebrations organized by VIT-A.P. University.  He discussed the evolution of information centers in the modern era and emphasized the importance of research in nation-building. Saibaba encouraged young minds to utilize educational opportunities provided by institutions and government initiatives for societal betterment.

articles.title: Labourers urge officials to provide basic amenities at Benz Circle - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Laborers in Vijayawada's Benz Circle, a major employment hub for construction and domestic work, face challenges despite their daily presence.  Around 500 individuals arrive by 6 a.m., hoping to find work, but many go without it, leading to an inadequate infrastructure of public amenities like toilets and water facilities.  NTR District Collector G. Lakshmisha has pledged to investigate the situation.

articles.title: 20 years in making: LeBron and Bronny James create NBA playoff history with first father-son alley-oop | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: LeBron James and Bronny James made history during Game 3 of the Lakers-Rockets playoff series with a father-son scoring connection. The play, which saw James make an alley-oop pass to his son for a reverse layup, marked the first time in NBA playoff history that a father and son have combined for a score.  This moment is significant because it reflects the sustained level of performance by James over two decades that allows him to share the court with his son, who entered the league in 2024. The win gave the Lakers a commanding lead in the series.

articles.title: Telangana IAS Transfers Apr 2026 | Major reshuffle; Priyanka Ala is Hyderabad Collector - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana government has announced a major reshuffle of IAS officers, transferring and appointing officials across various departments.  Sanjay Kumar, Special Chief Secretary in several departments, has been transferred to Telangana Bhavan in New Delhi, while M. Dana Kishore will replace him as Special Chief Secretary for the Labour, Employment, Training and Factories (LET&F) Department. Other key postings include B. Viziendira as Secretary to the Social Welfare Department, and Harichandana Dasari, Hyderabad Collector, moving to the LET&F Department.  The reshuffle also saw several collectors being transferred to different districts.

articles.title: ‘I have 3 weeks left in US’: Fired H1-B worker says he is racing against time after job loss - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A foreign worker on an H-1B visa in the United States is facing a critical situation as their visa expires in May and they were recently laid off. The worker, who had previously been laid off twice before, sought advice from Reddit users about how to remain in the country.  Many commenters advised seeking premium processing for their visa application or exploring options like securing a new employer willing to transfer their visa. Others recommended consulting an immigration attorney and paying the $2,800 premium processing fee personally.

articles.title: Family longest held in US immigration detention re-arrested after release | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration re-arrested the El Gamal family, who had been released from detention after a 10-month hold. The family's lawyers say this is in violation of a federal court order that prevented their removal from the United States.  They were detained despite a judge’s order to release them following their return home from detention earlier this week. Senator Dick Durbin condemned the administration's actions, stating they are motivated by xenophobia and not based on any legitimate security concerns.

articles.title: Former KSEB cashier held after evading sentence in graft case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) arrested Sakkeer Hussain, a former cashier at the KSEB sub-engineer office in Tholikkode, for absconding after being sentenced to two years of imprisonment for misappropriating ₹1,37,277 from electricity consumers.  Hussain had been convicted by the Vigilance Court in 2013 and appealed his sentence but both the High Court and Supreme Court dismissed his appeals. He was subsequently arrested by the VACB and remanded to Central Prison.

articles.title: Indian-American responds to MAGA commentator saying Indians are scamming Americans out of jobs: 'You don’t research anything' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sara Gonzales, a Texas MAGA commentator, sparked controversy on X by making claims about Indian professionals in the US tech sector. She compared her family's military service to alleged fraud by Indian workers, prompting backlash from Priya, an NRI user who provided data highlighting the economic and educational contributions of the Indian American community. Gonzales doubled down on her stance, claiming that many Indian immigrants are abusing the legal immigration system. This exchange follows a series of controversial posts from Gonzales about H-1B visas and immigration pathways, including accusations against a company for allegedly discriminating against H-1B visa holders. Her comments have drawn criticism for xenophobic and racist remarks, particularly regarding the growing Indian population in Texas.

articles.title: How serious is the rift in NATO? | NATO News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed anger after European member states declined to join the US-Israeli war on Iran. The US President is considering retaliatory measures against the United Kingdom and Spain.  Experts are assessing the potential impact of these divisions on the future of the NATO alliance.

articles.title: SSLC: Belagavi division tops Karnataka with 95.71 pass percentage - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Belagavi division, comprising nine educational districts, achieved a pass percentage of 95.71 in the SSLC examination, surpassing all other divisions in the state.  Ishwar Ullagaddi, Additional Commissioner of School Education and Literacy, attributed the success to the 'Mission-40' initiative and targeted academic programs. Two students from the division, Prarthana Nagappa Biradar Patil and Soujanya Basavaraj Kandkur, emerged as State toppers with scores of 625 out of 625.  The overall pass percentage in the division has seen a considerable increase compared to the previous year.

articles.title: FBI director Kash Patel 'likely' to be fired, says White House source: 'It’s only a matter of time' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel could be the next senior official to leave the Trump administration, according to a White House source cited in a new report by Politico.  The report suggests growing frustration within the federal agency and concerns about negative coverage surrounding Patel, which is damaging for a senior official's image. The White House has not confirmed any move involving Patel, but his legal and media scrutiny continues to increase. Patel filed a $250 million defamation lawsuit against The Atlantic following an article alleging misconduct, while separate reporting by The Intercept has also drawn attention to past arrests.

articles.title: Explosion in southwest Colombia kills at leat seven, state governor says | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A suspected explosive attack on the Pan-American Highway in Cauca, Colombia killed at least seven people and injured 20 others. Governor Octavio Guzman condemned the attack as an "indiscriminate attack" against civilians and demanded a strong government response.  The incident follows a series of attacks attributed to dissident FARC members who split from the group following a peace agreement in 2016.  Minister of Defence Pedro Sanchez convened a security council in Cali to assess the situation, while President Gustavo Petro blamed a drug trafficker and FARC dissident leader known as Ivan Mordisco for the attack.

articles.title: Trump cancels US envoys' trip to Pakistan for talks on Iran war
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump canceled a planned trip by US officials to Pakistan for talks on the Iran war, citing internal conflicts within Iran's leadership and stating that Iran could easily resolve the issue by calling.  Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, special envoys, were to have joined the delegation, but their trip was called off after Abbas Aragchi, Iranian Foreign Minister, had met with Pakistan's Prime Minister Shebaz Sharif. Despite a ceasefire extension, tensions remain high over the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear ambitions.

articles.title: Key figure in Mandelson vetting scandal will not give evidence before MPs | Peter Mandelson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Emily Thornberry, chair of the Foreign Affairs Committee, requested that Ian Collard, former chief property and security officer at the Foreign Office, provide written answers to questions regarding his role in Peter Mandelson's security vetting.  Collard previously gave evidence to the select committee but declined to appear before the committee on Tuesday. Olly Robbins, former top civil servant at the Foreign Office, testified that Collard briefed him on the vetting findings deeming Mandelson a borderline case and leaning towards recommending clearance denial. Keir Starmer's former chief of staff, Morgan McSweeney, is scheduled to appear before the committee on Tuesday.

articles.title: Woman and child die after getting into ‘difficulty’ in water in west London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Police are investigating the deaths of a woman and her young child who were found unresponsive in Elthorne Park in Ealing, London. The incident occurred around 4:30 p.m. on Saturday, with both victims being recovered from the water and pronounced dead at the scene.  The deaths are not currently being treated as suspicious.

articles.title: Experts discuss preventive care and data-led approach to public health challenges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A webinar hosted by SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) and The Hindu on April 25, 2026, emphasized the need for a shift from reactive care to preventive healthcare in India. The session, part of the Future Career Conversations series, discussed building data-driven systems and developing a skilled public health workforce to address evolving health challenges.

articles.title: It costs $230 out-of-pocket to see a dermatologist. Many Australians go without – despite soaring skin cancer rates | Health | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Patients are increasingly foregoing medically necessary dermatological care due to rising costs, according to a report from Cleanbill. The average cost of a first visit now stands at $230 for adults without concessions, while follow-up appointments cost almost $190.  The report found that the cost of dermatology services rose nationwide by an average of almost $18 in one year, with steeper increases in smaller states. Cleanbill and the Australasian College of Dermatologists have highlighted the limited resources available for training and funding public dermatology clinics, leading to longer wait times and increased out-of-pocket costs for patients.

articles.title: ‘India has its challenges but…’: Ex-Microsoft professional quits the ‘American Dream’ amid visa uncertainty - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Swapnil Sagar, a former Microsoft professional, returned to India after ten years in the United States citing visa uncertainty and job instability as reasons for his decision.  Sagar initially pursued higher education in computer science in the US, working under F-1 and STEM OPT visas before being laid off by Microsoft in 2025. His wife, also on an H-4 dependent visa, was unable to work in the US, further contributing to their decision to return to India.  Despite challenges, Sagar now feels a sense of freedom and closeness to family in his home country.

articles.title: Experts discuss preventive care and data-led approach to public health challenges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A webinar organized by SRM Institute of Science and Technology (SRMIST) in partnership with The Hindu explored the need for a shift from reactive to preventive healthcare in India. The session, part of the Future Career Conversations series, emphasized strengthening preventative systems, building data-driven infrastructure, and developing a skilled public health workforce to address evolving health challenges.

articles.title: Iran’s authorities project hardened stance with more talks on horizon | Conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s authorities are projecting a hardened stance in negotiations with the United States, despite failed attempts at direct talks.  Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, met with Pakistani officials and is headed to Oman before traveling to Russia. Donald Trump has stated that he does not have a rush to reach an agreement with Iranian leadership, claiming they are "fighting like cats and dogs" internally. The US President also criticized the Iranian government for its internet shutdown and called on Iran's leaders to end their internal conflicts.  The Iranian government continues to emphasize unity in opposition to concessions to Trump, while simultaneously calling for citizens to remain united against any perceived threats from the US.

articles.title: Militants and separatists launch coordinated attacks across Mali | Mali | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Islamic militants and Tuareg-led separatists, including the al-Qaida-linked group JNIM, carried out coordinated attacks across several cities in Mali on Saturday. The attacks targeted locations in Bamako, including the international airport and military barracks, as well as other towns like Sevare, Mopti, Kidal, and Gao. The Malian army responded with gunfire and helicopter operations to quell the attackers.  Gen Assimi Goita, leader of the Malian junta, resides in Kati, a town near the main military base that was also targeted by the attacks. The US embassy in Bamako issued a security alert urging citizens to shelter in place.

articles.title: NHAI demolishes top portion of stormwater drain to create more road space in Vellore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) began demolishing the top portion of storm water drains on the Chennai - Bengaluru Highway (NH 48) near Sathuvachari in Vellore to create more road space. NHAI officials cited traffic congestion during rush hour as a reason for the demolition, which will be followed by the construction of new storm water drains at the same level as the existing road.

articles.title: ECI suspends police officials in Bengal; Trinamool alleges strongroom breach - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) has suspended five police officials in West Bengal's Diamond Harbour and deployed 11 new observers following allegations of a strongroom breach during the first phase of the Assembly election. The commission also ordered disciplinary proceedings against the officers for their alleged misconduct and failure to maintain neutrality.

articles.title: Farming is viable only when growers can decide market prices, says Karnataka Minister - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: H.K. Patil, Minister for Law and Parliamentary Affairs, and Tourism, stated that farming will become viable when farmers can set their own market prices instead of selling below production cost. He made this comment at the Global Agri-Tech Summit 2026 in Bengaluru on Saturday. Patil emphasized the need for technology and innovative farming practices to enable farmers to earn well and manage their land as profitable enterprises.

articles.title: Six gold medals to be awarded at BASE convocation on April 27 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar School of Economics (BASE) University in Bengaluru awarded six students with gold medals at its second annual convocation on April 27th.  The six students, including five female students, earned their degrees in economics and financial economics. BASE University will also be presenting 17 rank certificates and 171 degree certificates for the academic years 2023-24 and 2024-25.

articles.title: JD(S) leader alleges denial of ST certificates to Talawar community - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: JD(S) State secretary Shivakumar Natikar alleged that members of the Talawar community are being denied Scheduled Tribe (ST) caste certificates in Kalaburagi and Yadgir districts, despite their recognition as a Scheduled Tribe under the Constitution. He claims authorities have stopped issuing these certificates, contradicting government orders and circulars.

articles.title: Israel airlifts 240 Bnei Menashe members from Mizoram as India maintains security advisory - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Government of India issued an advisory regarding the security situation in Israel amidst the ongoing war in West Asia.  Israel airlifted approximately 240 individuals from Mizoram to Tel Aviv as part of Operation Wings of Dawn, a program sanctioned by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. This operation marks the first time such a large number of members of the Bnei Menashe community have been airlifted to Israel during a period of regional conflict.

articles.title: Tagged Olive Ridley turtles from T.N. reach Sri Lanka Dome, reveal migration patterns - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Environment, Climate Change and Forests Secretary Supriya Sahu announced that Olive Ridley turtles from Tamil Nadu have begun migrating towards the Sri Lanka Dome.  Sahu stated that turtles released from Tamil Nadu's coast have already reached the Sri Lanka Dome, a region known for its high marine life concentration. Turtles migrating from Odisha are also expected to join them in this shared marine hotspot shaped by oceanic processes.

articles.title: T.N. launches third synchronised Nilgiri Tahr survey across Western Ghats - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Forest Department and the Kerala Forest Department have begun a synchronized survey of the Nilgiri Tahr from April 24 to 27. This annual exercise, part of the Project Nilgiri Tahr, aims to assess the species' population across Tamil Nadu's entire range. The coordinated effort ensures accurate estimates by preventing duplication and utilizing shared landscape data within the Western Ghats.

articles.title: Artists get creative at ‘Articulate Gunturian’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vellaturi Krishna Prasad, a painter from Guntur, organized an art exhibition in the city showcasing nearly 300 paintings by artists of various ages and styles. The "Articulate Gunturian" program featured works using diverse mediums like wax crayons, oil pastels, watercolors, and acrylics, reflecting themes including Andhra Pradesh's cultural heritage, women's safety, and wildlife protection.  N. V. Sundarachary, Principal of Guntur Medical College, and Nannapaneni Rajakumari attended the event, encouraging the artists.

articles.title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah pitches Kashmir as ideal shooting destination to South Indian filmmakers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Omar Abdullah, the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir,  promised to create a welcoming environment for filmmakers during an interaction with South Indian filmmakers in Bengaluru. He emphasized the state's scenic beauty and cultural heritage as attractive features for film production, stating his government will extend full support to make filmmaking easier and more accessible.

articles.title: Young musicians shine at Rotary’s Thalir Kala Awards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Rotary Club of Chennai Carnatic (District 3234) hosted the third annual Thalir Kala Awards on Friday at Vani Mahal in T. Nagar. The event featured young classical musicians competing in vocal and instrumental categories, divided into age groups under 12 and 12 to 18 years old. Club president Arun Mahadevan emphasized the importance of preserving Carnatic music as a living heritage for future generations.

articles.title: Youth sentenced to 20 years rigorous imprisonment in POCSO case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old man, Sabanna Kattimani, was sentenced to 20 years in prison for kidnapping and sexually assaulting a minor girl.  Justice Muhammad Mujeer Ullah C.G. found him guilty under the POCSO Act and imposed a fine of ₹1.25 lakh. The investigation was led by Circle Police Inspector Raghavendra H.S. of the Ratkal police station, and the case was prosecuted by Shantveer B. Thuppad, representing the State.  The court also ordered compensation for the victim from the Legal Services Authority.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Sexual assault of a minor is a serious crime and should be treated with utmost urgency.

articles.title: After destroying more than 120 homes, wildfires still a danger, Georgia officials say | Georgia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Two wildfires in southeastern Georgia, one near Brantley County and another near the Florida state line, continued to threaten property and lives on Saturday. Joey Cason, the Brantley county manager, urged residents to evacuate if ordered, while Brian Kemp, Georgia's governor, noted that the Highway 82 fire was the most destructive in state history. The fires were started by a foil balloon hitting power lines and welding sparks respectively, and are both about 10% contained.  The blazes have destroyed over 120 homes and sent smoky haze into surrounding areas, prompting air quality warnings.

articles.title: Tiruvallur sows seeds for greener polling booths, classrooms - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tiruvallur district administration painted six schools green with eco-friendly Khadi Prakritik paint, a non-toxic coating that keeps classrooms cool. The paint, which comprises sustainable ingredients and is safe for children and pets, was used to coat the roofs of the polling booths and cost around ₹7,000 per booth.  The district also created its first green anganwadi using this paint, featuring solar panels, a kitchen garden, and a play area with recycled materials.

articles.title: Arsenal narrowly beat Newcastle to regain Premier League lead over Man City | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Arsenal defeated Newcastle 1-0 in a tense EPL match to regain the Premier League lead from Manchester City.  Eberechi Eze's goal in the first half secured the victory, giving Arsenal a three-point advantage over City, who are playing catch-up after their win against Southampton. The victory was crucial for Arsenal, as they had suffered recent losses and were looking to avoid repeating past mistakes.

articles.title: One police officer dead after Chicago hospital shooting | Chicago | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A Chicago police officer was killed and another critically injured in a shooting at Endeavor Health Swedish hospital on Saturday morning.  The suspect, who has not been publicly identified, was apprehended after opening fire on officers before being transported to the emergency department for treatment. The suspect had already been in custody when they arrived at the hospital and was wanded upon arrival according to the hospital. The incident remains under investigation.

articles.title: Kochi NGO Maithri receives distress calls via AI referrals - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Maithri, a Kochi-based non-governmental organization (NGO) working on suicide prevention, has seen an increase in calls from individuals seeking help through AI-powered applications. The NGO's volunteers have been contacted by users who were initially directed to pre-recorded messages before being connected with Maithri.  Maithri, part of the Befrienders Worldwide organization, is experiencing a surge in calls, prompting them to seek more volunteers to handle the increased demand. Volunteers are needed to provide emotional support and participate in outreach programs.

articles.title: Barcelona on the brink of defending La Liga title after beating Getafe | Football | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Barcelona moved 11 points clear of Real Madrid in the La Liga title race with a 2-0 victory over Getafe. Goals from Fermin Lopez and Marcus Rashford secured the win for Barcelona, who are now on the verge of defending their championship.  The defending champions will need to overcome Osasuna next weekend and hope that Real Madrid fail to beat Espanyol in order to secure their second consecutive Spanish title.

articles.title: President Zardari arrives in China for visit focused on 'economic cooperation, CPEC' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Asif Ali Zardari arrived in China on Saturday for a visit focused on economic and trade cooperation, as well as the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).  He was received by Hu Xusheng, Vice Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Hunan Provincial People’s Congress, and will travel to Changsha from April 25 to 27 before visiting Sanya from April 28 to May 1. The visit is part of a longstanding tradition of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and China, marking the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year.

articles.title: Orbán steps down from Hungarian parliament after landslide defeat
articles.rephrased_article: Viktor Orbán, Hungary's outgoing Prime Minister, announced he would not take his parliamentary seat after his party suffered a landslide defeat. Gulyás Gergely, currently the minister overseeing the prime minister's office, will lead the Fidesz parliamentary bloc.  The new parliament is due to hold its first session on May 9th and will be led by Péter Magyar of the Tisza party, who won a majority in the election. The incoming PM has pledged to reverse Orbán-era changes and restore Hungary's international standing.

articles.title: Macron says EU’s mutual defence clause ‘not just words’ | European Union | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Emmanuel Macron emphasized the significance of Article 42, paragraph 7 of the EU treaty, stating it was not merely words but a concrete mechanism for mutual defense.  He highlighted its effectiveness in response to the drone attack on a British airbase in Cyprus, where several member states provided military aid. António Costa, the European Council president, acknowledged plans to develop a handbook outlining how this clause would be implemented. Macron also criticized the US's approach towards NATO, arguing that Europe should prioritize its own security and not rely solely on the alliance.  He stressed the need for increased cooperation between France and Greece, viewing their strong partnership as a model for the entire EU.

articles.title: eKYC related delay compounds domestic LPG consumer woes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of domestic LPG consumers in Telangana are experiencing difficulties accessing cooking gas refills due to the incomplete e-KYC process.  Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have implemented restrictions on refills and delays in service for those who haven't completed the e-KYC, following an advisory issued earlier. The enforcement of e-KYC is crucial given the impact of the war in West Asia on LPG supply.

articles.title: Officials draw flak over alleged administrative lapses in Kozhikode Corporation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kozhikode Corporation council members criticized officials for alleged delays in clearing bills and administrative lapses during a meeting on Saturday, April 25, 2026. Mayor O. Sadasivan, who chaired the meeting, heard concerns from both ruling front and opposition councillors about recurring inefficiency within the civic body.  Development standing committee chairperson V.P. Manoj raised issues with mismanagement and technical problems in K-SMART during a calling attention motion.

articles.title: Summer travel picks up in Tamil Nadu, but trips get shorter amid rising costs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu residents are opting for shorter, budget-friendly getaways due to rising airfares and global tensions.  Travelers are choosing road trips, camping, and glamping experiences, with astro camping in Hanle being a popular choice. SOTC Travel, Thomas Cook (India) Limited, and Exoticamp report strong travel interest from the region, particularly for Eastbound and Far East destinations like Japan, Vietnam, Singapore, and China.  These trends are also reflected in increased demand for domestic travel within India and the Indian subcontinent.

articles.title: Joy and desire for change as Gaza’s Deir el-Balah holds elections | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Deir el-Balah, Gaza, cast their votes in the first municipal elections since 2006, marking a significant step towards democratic participation after years of conflict and displacement. The election is taking place amidst ongoing challenges, including infrastructure damage from the war and the influx of displaced people. Salama Badwan, a resident, expressed hope for change through peaceful means and a new municipal council capable of addressing the city's needs.  Dunia Badwan, his daughter, highlighted her desire for a more efficient administration that can improve daily life in Deir el-Balah. Despite logistical hurdles like limited resources and access to essential materials, Mohammad Abu Nada, coordinator of the electoral district, emphasized the determination of residents to exercise their right to vote.  The elections are seen as a symbol of resilience and hope for a brighter future in the face of adversity.

articles.title: How one orangutan braved new bridge to unite his split community
articles.rephrased_article: The Sumatran Orangutan Society (SOS) and Tangguh Hutan Khatulistiwa, with government assistance, built a canopy bridge to reconnect two separated orangutan communities in Indonesia's Sumatra.  After two years of inactivity, one orangutan crossed the bridge, potentially signifying a positive change for the primates' health and future.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly elections: Over 50 lakh more voters exercise their franchise this time compared to 2024 Lok Sabha polls - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Over 50 lakh more electors participated in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly election compared to the 2024 Lok Sabha election. This trend reflects a long-standing tradition of higher voter turnout during Assembly elections, likely due to voters' direct impact from government actions and intense political mobilization. The presence of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, along with cash distribution, has also contributed to increased participation.  The Election Commission of India (EC) reported seizures of significant amounts of cash, liquor, drugs, precious metals, and freebies during the election.

articles.title: Reported US CIA agents killed in crash not authorised to operate: Mexico | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mexico’s security cabinet stated that two US citizens killed in a car crash during an anti-narcotics raid were not authorized to operate on Mexican territory. The individuals, who the US embassy described as “embassy personnel,” entered Mexico as visitors and on diplomatic passports, according to the statement.  The incident has raised questions about the extent of US involvement in activities on Mexican soil and whether the government is fully informed of such operations.

articles.title: Rights groups critical as Venezuela prisoner release scheme 'coming to an end'
articles.rephrased_article: Delcy Rodríguez, interim president of Venezuela, announced the end of a prisoner release scheme that has seen nearly 500 political prisoners released under an amnesty law.  Human rights groups, including Foro Penal and Provea, criticized the move as arbitrary and unconstitutional, arguing it lacks legal authority and does not address the underlying issues of repression in the country. While Rodríguez claimed the program was successful, critics argue it is a mere political maneuver to appease the US government, which has supported her administration.

articles.title: Egyptian family of six taken back into ICE custody days after being released | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has re-detained a family of six, the El Gamals, days after their release from a Texas detention facility. The family was on a private jet bound for Egypt due to a court order violation, according to their attorney, Eric Lee.  The case has garnered national attention, as the El Gamals had been detained at the Dilley detention center for 10 months, considered one of the longest detentions for a family under the Trump administration.

articles.title: Goud, Chamala fault Kavitha for targeting CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mahesh Kumar Goud, president of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC), and Chamala Kiran Kumar Reddy, Lok Sabha member, praised K. Kavitha, chief of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi (TRS), for acknowledging the BRS government's alleged looting during its decade-long rule.  Goud questioned her motives for entering politics and Reddy criticized her remarks comparing the Chief Minister to Hitler, asserting that such actions would not garner support from the people of Telangana.

articles.title: In call with Iranian president, PM says Pakistan committed to serving as 'honest and sincere facilitator' - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Saturday, reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to facilitating peace in the region. The phone call followed an Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's visit to Islamabad and a recent round of indirect talks between the US and Iran held in the Pakistani capital.  Both leaders agreed to continue close coordination and expressed confidence in strengthening bilateral ties.

articles.title: The billion-barrel Hormuz oil shock is about to crash demand - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Traders warn that the ongoing closure of the Hormuz Strait, which has disrupted oil supplies for nine weeks, is causing a significant drop in global oil demand. The International Energy Agency estimates a 5.3 million barrel-per-day reduction this quarter and predicts further decline if the closure persists.  The impact is already being felt across various sectors, including airlines and fuel markets like gasoline and diesel, with analysts warning of potential economic recession.  Without a swift resolution to the conflict, oil prices may need to surge significantly to force demand adjustments.

articles.title: Who is Ella Devi? ‘Socialist’ Sri Lankan-American influencer who backs Zohran Mamdani - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ella Devi, an 18-year-old Sri Lankan-American influencer, has sparked debate online for blending left-wing politics with a taste for high-end fashion in New York City.  Devi, who gained attention for supporting NYC mayor Zohran Mamdani, regularly shares outfit videos and political views on TikTok, where she boasts over 34,600 followers. While some users criticize her lifestyle choices, others defend her progressive messaging and political stance.

articles.title: Trump cancels US envoys’ trip after Iran’s Araghchi leaves Pakistan | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump canceled a planned trip for US envoys to Pakistan after Abbas Araghchi, Iran's Foreign Minister, departed the country.  Trump stated that any future talks would be conducted over the phone and suggested that Iran was not serious about diplomacy. Araghchi met with Pakistani officials including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Army chief Asim Munir, and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, sharing Iran's position on ending the war with the US. The situation remains tense as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps continues to block the Strait of Hormuz, impacting global energy markets.

articles.title: Mexico says US agents killed in crash weren't permitted to operate there
articles.rephrased_article: Mexico's security ministry announced that two US agents who died in a car crash last weekend were not authorized to operate within the country. The incident occurred after the agents, reportedly working for the CIA, participated in a raid on suspected drug labs in Chihuahua state.
