Supriya Sahu, Additional Chief Secretary to the Department of Environment, Climate Change and Forests, acknowledged that while such cases are not frequent due to the loris' slow movement, roadkill remains a significant threat. The government is exploring alternative solutions like bunched, insulated overhead cables in areas with river crossings.

articles.title: Roommate arrested after body of University of South Florida doctoral student discovered | Florida | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Hisham Saleh Abugharbeih, a 26-year-old former USF student, was taken into custody after being found in possession of the body of his missing roommate, Zamil Limon.  Limon's remains were discovered on the Howard Frankland Bridge.  Abugharbeih is facing preliminary charges including unlawful moving of a dead body and tampering with evidence.  Nahida Bristy, Limon's missing girlfriend, has not been located. The Hillsborough County Sheriff’s Office continues to search for Bristy while an autopsy will be conducted on Limon’s remains.

articles.title: Hyderabad police launch ‘Coffee with a COP’ outreach to engage youth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Cyberabad Police, in partnership with the Society for Cyberabad Security Council (SCSC), launched a new initiative called "Coffee with a COP" to foster dialogue between law enforcement and young adults. The inaugural session featured students, start-up founders, and corporate employees, led by TGCSB Director Shikha Goel.  Cyberabad Police Commissioner M. Ramesh emphasized the importance of safety in both physical and digital spaces, urging citizens to be vigilant against online fraud. Awareness stalls provided information on traffic management, cybercrime prevention, and women's safety initiatives.

articles.title: Colorado funeral home owner sentenced to 30 years in decomposing bodies case | Colorado | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Carie Hallford, co-owner of a Colorado funeral home, was sentenced to 30 years in prison for her role in a corpse abuse scheme.  Hallford and her then husband Jon Hallford, also pleaded guilty to federal fraud charges related to the scandal which saw them defraud grieving families by promising proper funerary services while leaving their loved ones' remains to decay. The couple collected over $130,000 for funeral services, often returning urns filled with concrete mix instead of ashes.  Jon Hallford was sentenced to 40 years in prison earlier this year. A group of Colorado families affected by the scandal formed Colorado Remembers, a non-profit organization providing support for victims.

articles.title: Birds of Mangalajodi: A visual journey into Chilika’s avian paradise - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Srinivasa Rao Somanchi and his late wife, Dr. Seetha Khambhampati, authored the photographic book "Birds of Mangalajodi," a tribute to the wetlands' birdlife. The book features striking photographs capturing the diverse species found in this significant waterfowl habitat.  The couple spent years documenting the wetlands together, with Mr. Srinivasa Reddy, Fellow of The Royal Photographic Society of Great Britain, praising their dedication and the book's message of passion overcoming age. Wildlife photography enthusiasts will find "Birds of Mangalajodi" invaluable for its insights into capturing birds in their natural habitat.

articles.title: US justice department steps in on behalf of xAI in Colorado regulation case | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US justice department intervened in a lawsuit filed by Elon Musk's xAI, challenging Colorado's new law regulating AI systems. The department argues the law violates the 14th amendment's equal protection guarantee by allowing some discrimination while requiring companies to guard against unintended discriminatory effects.  This intervention escalates the legal battle between xAI and the state of Colorado over state-level AI regulation, with the Trump administration advocating for a uniform national framework.

articles.title: 10 of 26 petitioners caught in Russia-Ukraine crossfire dead; some volunteered, others duped, government tells Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union government informed the Supreme Court that 10 of the 26 individuals who claimed to have been "human-trafficked" to fight in Ukraine are deceased.  Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati stated that the government is pursuing a multi-pronged strategy, including advising young people against traveling to Russia, while acknowledging cases of individuals being misled by agents. The court expressed concern over bringing back the remains from the conflict zone and requested a detailed status report.

articles.title: Trump's envoys Witkoff and Kushner to fly to Pakistan for Iran talks
articles.rephrased_article: Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law Jared Kushner are traveling to Pakistan for peace talks with Iran.  Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baqaei arrived in Islamabad ahead of the talks, stating that no meeting between Iran and the US is planned. The White House has indicated a willingness to engage in diplomacy, while Iran insists on ending the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and addressing breaches of the ceasefire.  Despite public pronouncements, both sides are actively pursuing a path toward de-escalation.

articles.title: Indigenous speakers booed at Anzac Day services as Ben Roberts-Smith attends Gold Coast event | Anzac Day | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Disruptions marred Anzac Day commemorations in Sydney, Melbourne, and the Gold Coast. At Sydney's Martin Place dawn service, a man was arrested for alleged "nuisance" after booing during an Indigenous acknowledgement of country. Uncle Ray Minniecon, who delivered the acknowledgment, urged those responsible to understand that the land is Aboriginal.  Mark Schroffel, president of the RSL Victoria, condemned the behavior as weak-minded and disrespectful. In Melbourne, a similar disruption occurred at the dawn service where Uncle Mark Brown delivered his welcome to country. The Victorian premier described it as "bastardry" while the acting chief of army and deputy prime minister also expressed their disapproval.  Despite these disruptions, many attendees showed support for Anzac Day ceremonies.

articles.title: Israel continues attacks on Lebanon despite extension of ceasefire | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel continued attacks on Lebanon despite the extension of a ceasefire, resulting in casualties.  The Israeli military claimed to have killed six Hezbollah fighters and wounded several civilians in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah responded with rocket fire and drone strikes against Israeli troops. The Lebanese Health Ministry reported two deaths from an Israeli air strike in Touline. United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres welcomed the ceasefire extension, while Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu maintained that Israel would continue to act against threats.

articles.title: The real wall with ears: Ancient Roman walls can hear you from metres away | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ancient Roman structures, like the Pantheon, exhibit a unique acoustic phenomenon known as the whispering gallery effect. This occurs when sound waves are guided along curved surfaces, such as walls and domes, resulting in clear and audible speech over distance. The smooth stone surfaces and carefully shaped interiors of these buildings reflect sound instead of absorbing it, allowing for focused sound transmission. Roman theatres, designed with semi-circular layouts and tiered seating, also demonstrate this principle, enabling performers to be heard clearly by spectators seated far away without the use of modern amplification.

articles.title: Who’s in control of AI? | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ramesh Srinivasan, a professor at UCLA, and Marc Einstein, research director at Counterpoint Research, discussed the recent unauthorized access to one of the world's most powerful AI models.  They emphasized that the breach was not malicious but highlighted concerns about global control of such advanced technology. The discussion also included Adrian Monck, a senior adviser on AI and technology to the United Nations, who offered insights into international efforts to regulate AI development and use.

articles.title: Tips generated by true-crime podcast lead to arrests in unsolved 1982 killing in Louisiana | US crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: State police troopers announced the arrest of four men in connection with the 1982 murder of Roxanne Sharp.  The arrests, made possible by tips generated from a true-crime podcast and advancements in investigative technology, resulted in charges of aggravated rape and second-degree murder against Perry Wayne Taylor, Darrel Dean Spell, Carlos Cooper, and Billy Williams Jr. Covington police had led the initial investigation until 2023 when state police took over. The case remained unsolved for decades due to limited evidence and public cooperation, but a podcast released in early 2025 generated new leads that helped identify and arrest the suspects.

articles.title: Igumdrop: Streamer iGumdrop takes her cooking from Twitch to MasterChef and impresses Gordon Ramsay - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: iGumdrop, a popular Twitch creator known for her food recipes, is competing on the sixteenth season of MasterChef Global Gauntlet.  She impressed judges with her wagyu beef satay in peanut sauce and coconut rice dish, earning a white apron and securing her spot on Team Asia-Pacific. Gordon Ramsay praised her passion and authenticity, while fellow judge Tiffany Derry called her dish "beautiful." iGumdrop's journey from online cooking to a major television platform demonstrates the power of pursuing one's passions.

articles.title: US sending envoys to Pakistan, raising hopes of talks with Iran’s Araghchi | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US President Donald Trump sent envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived for talks.  The US hopes these meetings will lead to a deal, but Iran has not yet committed to new negotiations. Iran’s top diplomat is visiting Pakistan to discuss its proposals for talks with the US, which Pakistan will then relay to Washington. The visit comes amid a fragile ceasefire and growing tensions over control of the Hormuz Strait.

articles.title: Democratic Maine governor vetoes first US state freeze on new datacenters | Maine | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Janet Mills, the Democratic governor of Maine, vetoed a bill that would have imposed a moratorium on large new datacenters in the state. The decision came despite growing local opposition to the electricity-hungry facilities and concerns about their impact on the environment and household energy bills. Mills expressed support for a temporary moratorium but argued that the final version of the bill failed to include an exemption for a key datacenter project in Jay, which would create jobs and generate tax revenue for the town.  The veto has drawn criticism from supporters of the bill who argue it could harm the state's economy and energy future.

articles.title: ‘It was Indian food’: Florida Republican targets Kash Patel, calls FBI director incompetent - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: James Fishback, a Republican gubernatorial candidate in Florida, sparked controversy with a joke comparing FBI Director Kash Patel to a failed food delivery investigation. The comment, made during a campaign appearance and shared on X by commentator Richard Hanania, drew cheers from the audience.  The remarks come amidst political scrutiny of Patel, who has denied allegations of drinking and missed meetings, while The Atlantic stands by its reporting.

articles.title: Real Madrid stunned at Betis as Barcelona have chance to move 11 clear | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Real Madrid were held to a 1-1 draw by Betis, preventing them from closing the gap in the La Liga title race.  Hector Bellerin's injury-time goal salvaged a point for Betis, who moved up to fifth place, while Barcelona remain provisionally eight points ahead of Madrid.  The result leaves Madrid with an uphill battle to catch Barcelona and secure the La Liga title.

articles.title: Shabana Mahmood refuses to rule out sending back failed Afghan asylum seekers | Immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Shabana Mahmood, the UK home secretary, is monitoring discussions between Kabul and European countries regarding a returns program for rejected Afghan asylum seekers. While she hasn't ruled out such a program, it would be a reversal of current policy and shock humanitarian groups. The UN has described Afghanistan as a "graveyard for human rights" with severe restrictions on women and girls, including the exclusion of girls from education and employment.  The UK government is attempting to reduce small boat crossings by Afghans, which have increased significantly in recent years.

articles.title: Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi lands in Islamabad; US officials to also arrive in Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad on Friday for meetings with Pakistani officials, including Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. The visit comes as US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are also expected to travel to Pakistan for talks with Iran.  While the Iranian delegation will meet with high-level Pakistani officials, they have stated that no meeting with the United States is planned.  The development follows a first round of direct US-Iran talks in Islamabad on April 11 and 12, brokered by Pakistan.

articles.title: Ronaldo has three final career dreams he must fulfil before retirement, Messi has already completed the first | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Cristiano Ronaldo, at 41, is aiming for his sixth appearance in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, hoping to secure a final international title and reach the coveted milestone of 1,000 career goals.  Despite facing competition from Lionel Messi, who has already achieved this feat, Ronaldo remains focused on his personal objectives. The Portuguese forward is also considering playing alongside his son, Cristiano Ronaldo Jr., at the senior level, a unique situation in football history.  Ronaldo's current form suggests these goals are achievable as he continues to influence games for Al Nassr and lead Portugal's qualifying efforts.

articles.title: Israel kills at least 12 Palestinians in Gaza amid ‘ceasefire’ | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has killed at least 12 Palestinians in Gaza, including police officers, despite a ceasefire brokered by Donald Trump last year.  The Gaza Ministry of Interior accused Israel of targeting civilian police forces and called for international intervention to end the attacks. Hamas condemned the escalation as part of Israel's "unprecedented bloody, fascist approach" and blamed the failure of the ceasefire on the international community. The Israeli military has continued its attacks despite a truce agreement with Hezbollah, leading rights groups to conclude that the campaign constitutes genocide.

articles.title: Three boys and two men charged over rape of teenage girl in Kent | Crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kent police have charged three boys and two men in connection with the alleged rape of a teenage girl between March 25th and April 19th. Ionut Dobre, 33, was charged with rape, alongside two 16-year-olds and a 15-year-old, all from Gravesend.  Benone Inofte, 46, was also charged with aiding and abetting the rape. The suspects appeared at Medway magistrates court on Friday and will next appear at Woolwich crown court on May 22nd. Both men were remanded into custody while two of the boys were placed in youth detention and the third released to local authority care.

articles.title: Bengaluru firm Shree Bhagavathi Tech Labs to raise ₹50,000 cr to float, fuel 18 startup ventures - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shree Bhagavathi TechLabs, a city-based company owned by the Bhagavathi Devi Temple Trust, announced plans to receive ₹50,000 crore from multiple investors to fund and scale 18 startups across various business sectors.  The investment will support the creation of offices for these ventures within the Central Business District (CBD) areas of Bangalore's pincode 560001 by August 2026. FSTC (Flight Simulation Technique Centre), a pilot training institute, is a key investor in this venture, having been acquired by Adani Defence Systems & Technologies Ltd. last year.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Steady voting push Thoothukudi turnout past 80% - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Brisk polling took place across all six assembly constituencies in Thoothukudi district on Thursday, with an impressive voter turnout of 80.53% as of 9:15 p.m.  Voters formed long queues at polling stations from early morning to exercise their franchise, and polling remained largely peaceful, with minor technical glitches reported at a few locations. The district has a total electorate of 13,88,186 voters across six constituencies.

articles.title: ​Fire and sound: The Hindu Editorial on Kerala’s Mundathikode tragedy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A series of powerful explosions at a makeshift fireworks assembly unit in Kerala, India, killed 15 people and injured over 24 others. The blasts occurred ahead of the annual Thrissur Pooram festival, which is known for its large-scale fireworks displays. The State and the Centre have announced compensation for victims' families and declared it a state disaster to expedite relief efforts.  Multiple inquiries are underway to investigate safety violations and regulatory lapses in the pyrotechnic industry.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Post-SIR electorate drop drives turnout surge; votes remain steady compared to 2021 election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (ECI) reported a significant increase in voter turnout across all 16 Assembly segments in the Chennai district on Thursday, reaching 83.41% compared to the 59.75% recorded in the 2021 Assembly election. This rise was attributed to the reduction in the electorate following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Dindigul district polls 88.98% - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: District Election Officer S Saravanan reported that polling in Dindigul district concluded peacefully with an estimated 88.98% voter turnout.  The seven Assembly constituencies - Dindigul, Natham, Vedasandur, Oddanchatram, Nilakottai, Palani and Athoor - saw brisk voting throughout the day despite scorching temperatures. Young voters were enthusiastically participating in the election process.

articles.title: Madurai Bench orders notice to nine convicts in Sattankulam custodial death case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court issued a notice to nine policemen sentenced to death for the custodial death of trader P. Jayaraj and his son J. Benicks in 2020. The court, hearing the referred trial, ordered the notice to the convicts: then Sattankulam inspector S. Sridhar; sub-inspectors P. Raghu Ganesh and K. Balakrishnan; head constables S. Murugan and A. Saamidurai; and constables M. Muthuraj, S. Chelladurai, X. Thomas Francis, and S. Veilumuthu.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Death sentences for custodial deaths are being challenged, raising concerns about justice.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Tenkasi records 82% voter turnout in incident-free polling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu witnessed brisk and incident-free polling in the Assembly election on Thursday, with voter turnout reaching 82.40%.  The highest turnout was reported in Tenkasi (82.43%), followed by Sankarankovil (SC) (81.52%) and Kadayanallur (81.36%). MDMK general secretary Vaiko cast his vote in his native village, while Home Guards from Karnataka were deployed for security. The votes will be counted on May 4th.

articles.title: Absolute voter increases seen across Tamil Nadu followed spatial patterns - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu recorded an all-time high voter turnout of 85.1% in the recent election, driven by a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise that resulted in the deletion of over 68 lakh electors.  While the absolute number of voters who participated increased, the addition of new voters was lower than previous cycles.  The state-wide aggregate increase also showed distinct constituency-level variations across urban/rural and regional segments.

articles.title: Record turnouts in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu polls a display of citizen power: Supreme Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of India praised the record voter turnout (92.03%) and minimal violence observed during the West Bengal Assembly elections, stating that citizens understand their power in a democracy through voting. Chief Justice Surya Kant emphasized this understanding by saying, "Individually, as a citizen of India, I was very happy to see the percentage of voting."

articles.title: Republican congressman absent over ‘personal health matter’, Johnson says | New Jersey | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mike Johnson, the speaker of the House, confirmed that Tom Kean Jr. is attending to a personal health matter and expects to be back at full capacity soon.  Kean has not voted in the House since March 5th, leaving his absence as another complication for the historically small Republican majority in Congress. This latest development comes amidst a series of resignations and deaths among lawmakers from both parties, including Democrat Eric Swalwell, Republican Tony Gonzales, and Democrat Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick. The Republican majority currently stands at 217 seats plus one independent who caucuses with them, to the Democrats’ 212 seats.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks Bengal poll officers to pursue appeals on SIR exclusion - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court dismissed a petition from over 65 West Bengal poll duty officers seeking to vote in the Assembly elections. The court directed them to pursue their appeals before the Appellate Tribunals, stating that the election is ongoing and cannot be re-held.  The petitioners argued that their exclusion was due to an "AI-driven automated system" employed by the Election Commission of India during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process, a claim disputed by the ECI.

articles.title: FBI chief Kash Patel under scrutiny again over 2005 public urination arrest: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: FBI Director Kash Patel is facing renewed scrutiny after reports surfaced of two past arrests for public intoxication and urination, detailed in a 2005 legal filing. Patel acknowledged the incidents in the document, which was previously disclosed during his early legal career. He stated that both incidents were out of character and apologized for his improper behavior. The resurfacing of these disclosures comes amid a report by the Atlantic alleging Patel's heavy drinking habits and erratic behavior, based on anonymous sources within and around the US government.

articles.title: High school senior identified as person killed in shooting at Lousiana mall | Louisiana | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A high school senior, Martha Odom, was killed and five others were wounded in a mass shooting at the Mall of Louisiana in Baton Rouge.  The incident occurred during an unofficial "skip day" for Ascension Episcopal School seniors, who were present at the mall. The Louisiana attorney general, Liz Murrill, condemned the violence, calling it a "devastating loss of innocent life." Martha was one of three high school seniors from Ascension Episcopal caught in the crossfire.  At least 122 mass shootings have occurred in the US this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive.

articles.title: Kancheepuram district sees over 87% polling - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Voting in the Kancheepuram district of Tamil Nadu was largely peaceful, with 87.39% voter turnout reported by 6 p.m.  Siva of Kuruvimalai in Orikkai attributed the high turnout to the DMK government's promises of pattas and infrastructure improvements. S. Ramesh, an activist from Alancheri near Uthiramerur, raised concerns about the lack of accessible polling booths for residents of five villages who had to travel long distances.  Farmer E. Sureshbabu reported that a protest by farmers demanding Adangal certificates for their land was resolved after assurances from senior officials.

articles.title: D4Vd Court Case: Prosecutors claim 40TB of data linked to D4vd includes child pornography in shocking court update - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd is back in court facing serious charges including murder and abuse of a minor. Prosecutors presented evidence from his phone, cloud accounts, and other devices totaling 40 terabytes, which includes illegal material involving children. They claim this evidence supports their case strongly, but D4vd's legal team insists the evidence will not prove his guilt. The trial continues with more updates expected.

articles.title: Petro becomes first president to visit Venezuela since Maduro abduction | Nicolas Maduro News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gustavo Petro, Colombia's first left-wing president, met with Delcy Rodriguez, Venezuela's interim president, at the Miraflores Presidential Palace in Caracas. The meeting focused on border security and trade issues, as both countries share a significant border.  Petro has been critical of the US abduction of Nicolas Maduro and the ongoing US strikes against alleged drug-smuggling boats in Latin America.

articles.title: ‘What the hell do you say?’: elder son of Rob Reiner speaks out on parents’ murders | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nick Reiner, the son of beloved director Rob Reiner, has been charged with two counts of first-degree murder in connection to the stabbing deaths of his parents.  In a Substack essay, Jack Reiner, Nick's brother, described the devastating impact of their loss and expressed the profound grief he and his family continue to experience. The case has sent shockwaves through Hollywood, as Rob Reiner is a renowned director known for films such as "When Harry Met Sally..." and "The Princess Bride." A preliminary hearing in Nick's case is scheduled for next week.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: A poll boycott and blockade of EVMs in Harur constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of K. Eachambadi village in Harur constituency boycotted the Assembly polls on Thursday (April 23, 2026) due to a proposed relocation of two high school sections to a neighboring Scheduled Caste Colony.  The move sparked a demand for repoll after polling closed following the boycott. The residents also demanded a repoll after the polling was closed.

articles.title: Who is Hisham Abugharbieh? Roommate arrested after USF student Zamil Limon found dead, Nahida Bristy still missing - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hisham Saleh Abugharbieh, a man who was not a student at University of South Florida, has been arrested in connection with the disappearance and death of two students, Zamil Limon and Nahida Bristy.  Abugharbieh barricaded himself inside his residence before surrendering to police. The case began as a missing persons report but escalated into a criminal investigation after authorities discovered links between Abugharbieh and the missing students. Limons' remains were found on the Howard Frankland Bridge, while Bristy remains missing.

articles.title: Trump to again end legal status of people who entered US with CBP One app | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump's administration plans to resume ending the temporary legal status granted to individuals who applied for asylum in the US via the CBP One app, despite a previous court ruling that found his attempt to terminate their status unlawful. The Department of Homeland Security, represented by the US Department of Justice, stated they will issue new termination notices following a memo from CBP's head, Rodney Scott.  The ACLU and Massachusetts Law Reform Institute, representing the individuals whose status is at risk, are urging the court to prevent this action.

articles.title: Mother ends life at Swiss clinic four years after son’s death | Assisted dying | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wendy Duffy, a 56-year-old woman from the West Midlands, died at a clinic in Switzerland after struggling to cope with the death of her son. Ruedi Habegger, founder of the Pegasos clinic, confirmed that Ms. Duffy requested assisted dying and was granted it on April 24th.  Pegasos Swiss Association, a nonprofit organization founded by Mr. Habegger, facilitated the process. The proposed "terminally ill adults (end of life)" bill in England and Wales failed to pass through parliament after facing numerous amendments and opposition.

articles.title: Sally Rooney, Greta Thunberg back Palestine Action before court date | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Sally Rooney, Greta Thunberg, and other prominent figures have signed a letter expressing support for the proscribed group Palestine Action before a UK Court of Appeal hearing. The letter, which bears 132 signatures, opposes genocide and supports Palestine Action's right to exist.  The UK government has appealed the High Court ruling that declared its ban on Palestine Action unlawful. Defend Our Juries, an activist group, argues that the government's appeal is an attempt to silence dissenters and highlights the disproportionate nature of the proscription.

articles.title: Michael B Jordan to take on big-screen adaptation of hit video game Battlefield | Michael B Jordan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Michael B Jordan is producing a big-screen adaptation of the Battlefield video game series, with writer-director Christopher McQuarrie. The project aims for a theatrical release and has been pitched to studios including Apple and Sony.  This follows Jordan's other upcoming projects like "Miami Vice" and "The Thomas Crown Affair." The news comes as video game movies continue to draw audiences at the box office.

articles.title: Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu says he received treatment for prostate cancer | Benjamin Netanyahu News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's Prime Minister, announced that he has successfully completed treatment for early-stage prostate cancer after a tumor was discovered during a routine checkup. The information was published in his annual medical report and revealed that the treatment involved radiation therapy. Aharon Popovtser, director of Hadassah Hospital’s oncology unit, confirmed that Netanyahu's diagnosis is at an early stage and has since been cleared.

articles.title: New US exhibition explores power of monuments – with help from Rocky | Art | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Philadelphia Museum of Art is hosting an exhibition titled "Rising Up: Rocky and the Making of Monuments" to examine the enduring power of monuments. The show, curated by Paul Farber, co-founder of Monument Lab, explores the cultural significance of the iconic Rocky Balboa statue on the museum's steps, which attracts millions of visitors annually.  The exhibition highlights the historical evolution of boxing as a symbol of resilience and triumph, drawing comparisons to ancient sculptures and contemporary artists like Andy Warhol and Jean-Michel Basquiat. The show also includes insights from Sylvester Stallone, who commissioned the bronze statue and views it as a representation of Rocky's journey from poverty to success.

articles.title: Health data of 500,000 UK volunteers listed for sale on Chinese platform, alarm raised | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UK Biobank, a major health research database containing sensitive medical information from nearly 500,000 participants, was briefly listed for sale on a Chinese online marketplace. Ian Murray, the UK Technology Secretary, confirmed that the listings were removed after being flagged by officials and coordinated with Chinese authorities. Experts warn that even though the data was anonymized, it could still be re-identified, potentially jeopardizing public trust in large-scale health research.  The UK Biobank is reviewing its security systems to prevent future breaches.

articles.title: Russian oil exports slump as Ukraine hammers ports and refineries | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine's intensified strikes against Russian oil infrastructure have significantly reduced Russia's oil exports, potentially reaching their lowest levels since 2023.  The US waived sanctions on Russian oil in early March to ease pressure on global crude oil prices, but the waiver has not been effective. The attacks have caused refineries to shut down and oil transhipments to plummet. Ukraine's military intelligence service estimates that Russia lost at least $2.3 billion from March alone due to these strikes.  Russia is now forced to cut crude production by 300,000 to 400,000 barrels a day and has seen its budget deficit increase. Ukraine's air defense capabilities have also been strengthened with the development of mobile fire groups using heavy machine guns mounted on trucks, as well as private companies deploying drones to defend against Russian attacks.

articles.title: Family under longest immigration detention of Trump’s term released | US immigration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Hayam El Gamal and her five children, who had been detained for over 10 months at the Dilley detention center in Texas, were released on Thursday following a judge's order.  The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) criticized the ruling, calling it from an "activist judge" who was releasing the family of a suspected terrorist onto American streets. The family's legal team argued they were unlawfully detained and suffered health issues during their time in custody.

articles.title: Ex-SSP’s son booked for firing on FBR official in Karachi - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: An FBR inspector, Shah Mir Lashari, was shot and wounded by the son of a former senior police officer, Agha Sher, in Clifton after a road accident. The suspect and his associate assaulted the injured officer and his brother, who were traveling in an SUV.  Clifton police have registered an FIR against Agha Sher and his gunman under Pakistan Penal Code sections for assault and attempted murder.

articles.title: Indian-origin couple bags $5 million after selling lottery-won luxury home in Perth: 'I came to Australia...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sanju and Sweety, an Indian-origin couple living in Perth, Australia, have sold their lottery-won beachfront home for $4.899 million, increasing their winnings from the $4.25 million initial prize to over $5 million. The couple initially won the MSWA Lottery Home last year and chose to sell the property instead of moving into it.  The Marmion home features four bedrooms, four bathrooms, a lift, and stunning ocean views.

articles.title: UK assisted dying bill fails after delays but advocates vow to try again | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A UK bill to legalize assisted dying for terminally ill adults was blocked in the House of Lords due to delays caused by more than 1,200 amendments. Lord Charlie Falconer, who sponsored the legislation, accused opponents of "pure obstructionism," while campaigners opposed to the bill expressed relief at its failure.  However, advocates vowed to continue their fight for assisted dying legislation in the next parliamentary session.

articles.title: Top Democrat says DoJ dropped ‘bogus’ Powell investigation to ‘clear the path’ for Trump Fed chair nominee Warsh – live | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Justice Department is ending its criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and his management of ongoing renovations to the central bank. The investigation was dropped after Jeanine Pirro, US attorney for the District of Columbia, directed her office to close it.  Senator Elizabeth Warren criticized the move, stating that it's an attempt to clear the path for Senate Republicans to install President Trump's "sock puppet" Kevin Warsh as Fed Chair. The inspector general will now scrutinize the building cost overruns. Meanwhile, the US Justice Department is strengthening its death penalty policy, including bringing back firing squads and readopting lethal injection protocols.  The department also announced it has rescinded the Biden-era moratorium on federal executions and authorized seeking death sentences against 44 defendants. The White House confirmed that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Islamabad, Pakistan tomorrow for further talks with Iran.

articles.title: Two young men abducted, killed in Bannu’s Domel area - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Militants abducted and killed two young men from the Taus Khel tribe in Bannu, Pakistan, on Thursday night after a confrontation near Painda Khel. The victims were traveling in a car when they were stopped by armed attackers who opened fire, killing one on the spot and taking them to an undisclosed location where one was later executed.  The bodies of both victims were found the following morning at separate locations. The incident has prompted calls for increased security measures from local residents.

articles.title: Four held for two-wheeler thefts, 10 vehicles recovered - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad Police apprehended four individuals, including a juvenile, for their alleged involvement in 10 two-wheeler thefts across the city.  The suspects, Mohammed Riyaz, Syed Ahmed Ali, Mohammed Fardeen, and a 17-year-old juvenile, were arrested on April 23rd at M.M. Pahadi in Attapur after police received credible information. The accused confessed to committing the thefts and recovered vehicles included eight Honda Dio scooters, one Hero Glamour, and one Bajaj Pulsar NS-200.  Further investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Italian Job: Could Pep Guardiola be next Italy boss after World Cup disaster? Big reset being discussed | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pep Guardiola has emerged as a potential candidate for the Italian soccer federation after their recent failure to qualify for the World Cup. The federation is considering a complete rebuild and believes that Guardiola's experience and success could be instrumental in changing the national team's direction.  However, financial considerations pose a significant obstacle, with his current salary at Manchester City being far beyond the federation's budget. While there is support from within the game for Guardiola's appointment, the next steps depend on the federation's decision to pursue him and his own willingness to take on the role.

articles.title: Trump government extends Jones Act waiver by 90 days to dampen oil prices | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump extended a shipping waiver that makes it easier to move oil, fuel, and fertilizer around the US for another 90 days. This move is part of a broader effort by the White House to curb rising energy costs before November's midterm elections. The Jones Act, which requires goods hauled between US ports be moved on US-flagged vessels, has been criticized for slowing delivery times and raising fuel prices.  The extension aims to provide certainty and stability for the economy but is expected to have a minimal impact on lowering gas prices.

articles.title: US veteran lost in Arizona’s wilderness for four days rescued by his own son | Arizona | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Young, a 76-year-old Vietnam War veteran, became lost in Arizona's wilderness for four days after his GPS signal failed. His family reported him missing and search crews combed the area, encountering obstacles like rattlesnakes and mountain lions.  His son, Josh, located his father using a satellite cell phone, leading to a successful rescue by helicopter. Young was dehydrated but otherwise unharmed and expressed gratitude towards the search teams for their efforts.

articles.title: Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi lands in Islamabad; arrival of US representatives expected as well - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian Foreign Minister, arrived in Islamabad on Friday for bilateral consultations with Pakistani officials.  He will meet with Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, as well as other senior leaders. The visit comes amid a second round of US-Iran peace talks expected to take place in Islamabad, with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, representatives from the US government, also traveling to Pakistan on Saturday.  The talks are aimed at addressing outstanding issues between the two countries and promoting regional peace and stability.

articles.title: Four held for two-wheeler thefts, 10 vehicles recovered - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hyderabad Police apprehended four individuals, including a juvenile, for their alleged involvement in a series of two-wheeler thefts across the city. The suspects, Mohammed Riyaz, Syed Ahmed Ali, Mohammed Fardeen, and a 17-year-old juvenile, were arrested at M.M. Pahadi in Attapur on April 23rd after confessing to ten thefts.  The recovered vehicles included eight Honda Dio scooters, one Hero Glamour, and one Bajaj Pulsar NS-200. The Special Crime Team of CCS and Gandhi Nagar police worked with informants and monitored the suspects' social media activity before apprehending them.

articles.title: Peace talks back on? Trump sending envoys to Pakistan to meet Iran FM; Vance on standby - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump is sending senior envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, to Pakistan this weekend for talks with Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi.  The White House hopes the meeting will lead to a deal on Tehran’s nuclear program, but tensions remain high. Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf is not participating, and Vice President JD Vance will stay in the US. The diplomatic initiative underscores Pakistan's role as a facilitator, following an agreement by Trump to extend a ceasefire with Iran.

articles.title: US appeals court rejects Trump’s ban on asylum seekers, teeing up appeal | Migration News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals in Washington, DC ruled that President Donald Trump's asylum ban is unlawful. The ruling found that existing laws, including the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA), grant individuals the right to apply for asylum at the border, and that Trump's proclamation suspending asylum applications was outside his authority.  The decision blocks the order but does not immediately impact its implementation as the White House has announced plans to appeal.

articles.title: Man found guilty over birds of prey dumped outside Hampshire village shop | Crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: James Kempster, a 39-year-old roofer from Totton, was found guilty of possessing two dead wild birds of prey.  He was cleared of criminal damage after DNA evidence linked him to the carcasses of a barn owl and kestrel found alongside 50 dead hares dumped outside a village shop in Hampshire. Adam Cooper, prosecuting, described the incident as a "horror movie scene," while Philip Wilkinson, police and crime commissioner for Wiltshire, suggested the act may have been an intimidation tactic.  The mystery surrounding who left the hares remains unsolved.

articles.title: Kosovo court jails three Serb separatists over 2023 Banjska attack | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Kosovo court sentenced three ethnic Serbs to prison terms for their involvement in a deadly attack on the village of Banjska in 2023.  The attack, which involved heavy weaponry and resulted in the deaths of one police officer and three attackers, was deemed a terrorist act by the judge. Milan Radoicic, a Kosovo Serb businessman with ties to Serbia's ruling party, admitted leading the attack after being identified on drone footage. The incident is seen as part of an ongoing conflict between Serbs who do not recognize Kosovo’s independence and the country's institutions.

articles.title: TikTok and Visa launch debit card to speed payouts to UK creators | TikTok | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: TikTok and Visa have launched a debit card for UK content creators to address cashflow issues associated with earning through the platform's TikTok Live feature. The virtual card, linked to a creator's TikTok account, allows users to access earnings from virtual gifts received during livestreams, which are converted into real money.  The card aims to simplify financial management and provide quicker access to funds for creators who often experience delays in payments through personal bank accounts.

articles.title: Polling percentage of women rises in T.N. this Assembly election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of India (EC) reported that women cast their votes at a higher rate than men in the April 23rd Tamil Nadu Assembly elections.  Women accounted for 85.76% of the electorate's turnout, compared to 83.57% for men. The highest polling percentages were recorded in two constituencies, Karur and Veerapandi, both exceeding 93%.  The EC has secured strongroom security with armed guards and CCTV surveillance for all EVMs and VVPATs.

articles.title: Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi arrives in Islamabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian Foreign Minister, arrived in Islamabad on Friday to meet with Pakistani officials. Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, received Araghchi and discussed regional developments, including the US-Iran ceasefire.  The visit comes as Steve Witkoff, a US Special Envoy on the Middle East, and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's advisor, are scheduled to travel to Pakistan for a second round of talks with Iran. The talks aim to address outstanding issues and advance regional peace and stability.

articles.title: Hunter becomes the hunted: Five elephants crush 75-year-old millionaire trophy hunter to death during hunt | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ernie Dosio, a 75-year-old American millionaire known for his trophy hunting expeditions, died after being trampled by a herd of elephants in Gabon.  Dosio and his guide were tracking a rare antelope when they unexpectedly encountered the group of five forest elephants. The elephants reacted aggressively, charging at close range and fatally crushing Dosio. His guide was injured during the initial charge but survived.

articles.title: Reality check: Israeli ambitions confront US dictates in Iran and Lebanon | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu finds himself in a precarious position as US envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, are leading the negotiations with Iran, while Israel is not included.  Despite repeated calls for war against Iran and its Lebanese ally Hezbollah, Netanyahu has been unable to secure concessions from the US, which appears to be dictating the terms of the ceasefire in Lebanon and Iran. This situation has exposed a growing disconnect between Israel's public expectations and the reality of US influence on the conflict.  Public confidence in Netanyahu's ability to shape outcomes is waning as he faces domestic criticism for failing to translate military achievements into diplomatic gains.

articles.title: Why is this game only legal across Australia one day a year?
articles.rephrased_article: Two-up, a coin toss betting game, is illegal in most of Australia but legal for a few hours on April 25th.  The BBC's Harry Sekulich explores the reasons behind this annual exception and the perspectives of those who support and oppose the practice.

articles.title: TV presenter withdraws claims against Dan Walker after ‘mutual agreement’ with Channel 5 | Channel 5 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Claudia-Liza Vanderpuije has withdrawn her claims against former Channel 5 News co-host Dan Walker, ending a legal dispute that was set to be heard at an employment tribunal.  A mutual agreement between Vanderpuije, ITN, and Channel 5 resolved the case, with Vanderpuije stating she will not repeat or pursue her allegations against Walker. Channel 5 and ITN have both denied the claims made by Vanderpuije, while Walker expressed hope for Vanderpuije's peace of mind.

articles.title: Congress leaders introspect on not aligning with TVK - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress leaders are expressing regret over their decision to not form an alliance with actor C. Joseph Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), believing they missed a chance to rejuvenate the party in Tamil Nadu.  Some members suggest leaving the DMK-led Secular Progressive Alliance immediately and forming an alliance with the TVK if needed to prevent the BJP from coming to power. The TNCC president has demanded an explanation from the Income Tax department after footage showed officials raiding his office, contradicting their claims of no raids.

articles.title: Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi arrives in Islamabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian Foreign Minister, arrived in Islamabad on Friday for bilateral consultations with Pakistani officials.  He was met by Ishaq Dar, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, and other senior officials. The visit comes amid efforts to revive peace talks between the US and Iran, which were mediated by Pakistan. Steve Witkoff, a US Special Envoy on the Middle East, and Jared Kushner, President Donald Trump's advisor, will also be traveling to Islamabad for further discussions.  The Iranian delegation is expected to hold meetings with Pakistani leadership to discuss regional developments and ongoing efforts for peace and stability.

articles.title: US to bring back firing squads as a way of execution? All you need to know - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US Justice Department (DOJ) announced plans to reinstate the firing squad as a method of execution, aiming to expedite the federal death penalty system. The move reverses policies implemented under former President Biden's administration and reflects a shift towards prioritizing capital punishment. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche criticized the previous administration for failing to protect public safety and emphasized the DOJ's commitment to enforcing the law against dangerous criminals.  The department plans to shorten execution timelines, streamline legal procedures, and potentially limit clemency petitions.

articles.title: Israeli attacks on Lebanon may violate international law, UN warns | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations human rights office (OHCHR) has released a report stating that Israeli attacks on Lebanon may violate international humanitarian law. The report, focusing on the first three weeks of the latest escalation between Israel and Hezbollah, cites several instances where Israeli strikes hit residential buildings in Lebanon, killing civilians and potentially violating international law.  The UN also found that Hezbollah rocket fire into Israel lacked precision and damaged civilian infrastructure, possibly breaching international humanitarian law.  The report did not receive immediate comment from the Israeli military or Hezbollah.

articles.title: Somalia piracy: Hijackers seize oil tanker and take 17 crew hostage
articles.rephrased_article: Pirates have hijacked an oil tanker, the Honour 25, carrying 18,500 barrels of oil and 17 crew members off the coast of Somalia. The incident occurred on Wednesday near the Somali coast, with six gunmen overrunning the ship.  The seizure is likely to increase anxiety in Mogadishu, where petrol prices have already tripled since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran. Neither the Somali authorities nor the European Naval Force has released a statement on the hijacking.

articles.title: US millionaire big-game hunter dies after being crushed by elephants | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ernie Dosio, a 75-year-old American millionaire and vineyard owner, died after being crushed by a group of elephants during a hunting expedition in Gabon. The incident occurred last Friday while Dosio was hunting yellow-backed duiker with his guide.  The safari operator confirmed the death, stating that the professional hunter guiding Dosio sustained serious injuries. Officials from the US embassy are coordinating the return of Dosio's remains to California.

articles.title: US won’t give unredacted Epstein documents to UK police without lengthy formal request | Jeffrey Epstein | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: British police are preparing to interview witnesses in Royal and government circles as part of their criminal investigations into Prince Andrew and Peter Mandelson.  The Metropolitan Police and Thames Valley Police, who have both launched full criminal investigations, are seeking the original documents from the Epstein files. The US Department of Justice has stated it will not consider handing over the documents without a formal request.  Formal interviews with witnesses in government circles are expected to begin soon.

articles.title: Israeli police investigate after officers 'cut Palestinian flag' from skullcap
articles.rephrased_article: A British Israeli academic, Alex Sinclair, was detained by Israeli police for wearing a kippah embroidered with an Israeli and Palestinian flag.  Sinclair claims he was ordered to remove the kippah and that it was cut in half when returned to him. The incident has sparked controversy, with the leader of Israel's Democrats Party criticizing the police and the Hebrew University condemning the officers' actions. Israeli police have stated they are investigating the complaint filed by Sinclair and are unable to provide further details at this time.

articles.title: Enrica Lexie owner urges SC for early release of a ₹3 crore bond executed in Kerala HC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Enrica Lexie, a vessel owned by M/s Dolphin Tanker, has requested an early hearing in the Supreme Court for the release of a ₹3-crore bond and other undertakings given in connection with the 2012 case involving the killing of two Indian fishermen. The ship's owner, represented by their authorized power of attorney Robert William, argued for a hearing before April 30th.  The request seeks modification of an order from May 2, 2012 and direction to release or return the bond after the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) ruled in favor of Italy, absolving the two Italian Marines of immunity. The case has a complex history involving multiple court orders and legal proceedings in India and Italy.

articles.title: Citizen taken into custody for likening Tarnol Railway Crossing to Strait of Hormuz - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Pakistan arrested a citizen, Khurram, for allegedly mocking the Tarnol Railway crossing and comparing it to the Strait of Hormuz. The arrest followed a complaint filed by Sub-inspector Shahid Asghar, who alleged that Khurram shared a social media post stating the crossing was comparable to the Strait of Hormuz and could solve all problems if closed.  The incident occurred amidst heightened security measures in the twin cities ahead of anticipated talks between the United States and Iran.

articles.title: How Israel targeted and killed Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Amal Khalil, a Lebanese journalist, was killed while reporting on an Israeli air strike in southern Lebanon during a 10-day ceasefire. This marks the ninth journalist fatality in Lebanon this year and raises questions about accountability for such incidents.  The incident has sparked discussions about the prospects for extending the ceasefire.

articles.title: Zack Polanski calls for ‘nuance’ when discussing antisemitism in rebuke of PM | Antisemitism | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Zack Polanski, leader of the Green Party in England and Wales, criticized Keir Starmer, the Prime Minister, for his handling of antisemitism accusations against the party.  Polanski accused Starmer of playing political games with a serious issue while also expressing concern about recent comments by some Green candidates that appear to sympathize with Hamas or question Israel's right to exist. The Green Party is facing scrutiny over its decentralized structure and internal procedures for vetting members, which have been criticized for allowing the spread of antisemitic views.

articles.title: Mandelson under formal investigation by EU's anti-fraud office
articles.rephrased_article: Lord Mandelson, former European trade commissioner, is under formal investigation by the European Anti-Fraud Office (Olaf) for potential misconduct during his tenure. The investigation stems from allegations of financial impropriety related to his interactions with Jeffrey Epstein, a convicted sex offender, and concerns about his knowledge of an impending €500 billion bailout in 2010. Olaf will examine exchanges between Lord Mandelson and Epstein, as well as any evidence of fraud related to the EU budget. The investigation could lead to sanctions against him but ultimately decisions regarding prosecution or disciplinary action lie with relevant EU authorities.

articles.title: West Bengal election: Modi promises fresh probe into R.G. Kar case after election; Mamata says BJP will get ‘zero’ in many districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a public meeting in Panihati, Kolkata, criticizing the Trinamool Congress and promising protection for women.  He also highlighted the BJP's commitment to ensuring prosperity for women in West Bengal.  Union Home Minister Amit Shah predicted a strong BJP victory, citing anti-incumbency and atrocities on women as key factors.  Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, contesting from Bhabanipur, countered these claims, asserting that the BJP would receive "golla (zero)" in several districts.

articles.title: Minister seeks details on reports of hijacking of tanker with Pakistani crew near Somali coast - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry requested a detailed report on the alleged hijacking of an oil tanker near Somalia, where 11 Pakistani crew members and the Indonesian captain are reported to be hostages. The incident occurred in the Gulf of Aden on April 21st, according to media reports.  The ministry is monitoring the situation and coordinating with relevant departments, including the Foreign Office, while efforts are underway to contact Somali authorities.

articles.title: Trump says royal visit may help steady UK-US ties amid tensions - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump expressed optimism that the upcoming visit by King Charles III and Queen Camilla to Washington could help repair strained relations between the US and UK.  He highlighted his personal relationship with the King, stating he was a "fantastic man" who would be a positive influence on the relationship. While acknowledging underlying tensions over trade, immigration, energy policy, and foreign policy disagreements, Trump believes the visit presents an opportunity to stabilize ties.

articles.title: Alcaraz’s French Open threepeat dream ended by wrist injury | Tennis News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Carlos Alcaraz, the reigning two-time French Open champion, will not play at this year's tournament due to a wrist injury. The 22-year-old Spaniard sustained the injury during the Barcelona Open last week and has decided to prioritize his long-term health over competing in Rome or Roland Garros. Jannik Sinner, who defeated Alcaraz in the Monte Carlo Masters final, expressed disappointment at Alcaraz's absence but hopes for his return at Wimbledon.  Alcaraz's withdrawal leaves the door open for other players to capitalize on his absence.

articles.title: Suicide-related callouts to fire services triple in England in a decade | Mental health | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Samaritans is calling for mandatory suicide prevention training for firefighters in England, citing a threefold increase in callouts over the past decade. The charity argues that firefighters are often among the first responders to suicidal crises and lack formal training on how to intervene effectively.  The fire service attends these incidents when specialized equipment or skills are required, alongside paramedics and police.  Samaritans is urging Fire Minister Samantha Dixon to ensure firefighters receive similar training as police recruits.

articles.title: Three Kosovo Serbs jailed over deadly gun battle and monastery siege
articles.rephrased_article: Kosovo's court sentenced two Kosovo Serbs to life imprisonment and another to 30 years for their roles in a deadly attack on police officers and a monastery in September 2023.  The attack, which involved a lorry blockade, shooting, and barricade situation, left one police officer dead and three others injured. While the court found the men guilty of violating Kosovo's constitutional order and inciting terrorist activities, authorities believe many individuals involved are in Serbia and unlikely to be extradited. The incident has further strained relations between Kosovo and Serbia, with both sides accusing each other of involvement.

articles.title: Two men arrested for misbehaving with women in Yelahanka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Yelahanka Police arrested two men for allegedly misbehaving with women walking on Kogilu Main Road on April 21.  The incident, captured by a car's dashcam, showed the accused riding pillion on a scooter while his accomplice drove. The video went viral and prompted police to register a suo motu case. Yelahanka Police apprehended the suspects and seized their vehicle.

articles.title: White House says Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner to head to Pakistan for talks with Iran - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced that US Special Envoy on the Middle East Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Pakistan for a second round of talks with Iran.  The announcement follows an invitation from Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, who is expected to arrive in Islamabad tonight. Pakistani sources confirmed that a second round of peace talks between the US and Iran are anticipated. The talks come after a ceasefire brokered by Pakistan was reached on April 8th.  Both sides agreed to remain in contact and continue diplomatic efforts.

articles.title: US court blocks Trump order suspending asylum access, cites right to apply - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
articles.rephrased_article: A US appeals court has blocked President Donald Trump’s executive order that suspended asylum access, ruling that immigration laws allow people to apply for asylum at the border. The three-judge panel from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit found that the president does not have the authority to bypass this process and that his attempt to suspend asylum claims was unlawful.  The decision was welcomed by the ACLU, while Judge Justin Walker, a Trump nominee, issued a partial dissent.

articles.title: Trump administration to prioritise seeking death penalty, use firing squads | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration announced plans to expand the use of capital punishment, including the deployment of firing squads. The Department of Justice released a policy document outlining legal arguments for various execution methods and criticized former President Biden's moratorium on federal executions. The administration also called for expanding the federal death row and constructing additional facilities to permit different forms of execution, such as firing squads.  Critics argue that capital punishment is disproportionately applied against minorities and the underprivileged and raises concerns about wrongful convictions.

articles.title: Iran foreign minister to embark on three-nation tour as US peace talks remain stalled | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Abbas Araghchi, Iranian foreign minister, is planning a tour of Pakistan, Russia and Oman to explore the possibility of restarting peace talks with the US and Israel.  He will discuss potential new arrangements for governing the Strait of Hormuz with Oman. While both sides claim time is on their side, neither is willing to back down from its demands. The US, led by Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, is demanding verifiable assurances that Tehran will end its nuclear program and lift its blockade of the strait.  Iran, meanwhile, insists it won't restart talks until the US lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.  The situation has escalated with Iran attacking five ships and capturing two in an effort to enforce the blockade. Pete Hegseth, the US defense secretary, stated that the US navy is prepared to resume major combat operations if ordered by Donald Trump.

articles.title: Iran on the brink: Who is really making decisions?
articles.rephrased_article: Following the opening strikes of Iran's war with the US and Israel, Mojtaba Khamenei, the new supreme leader, has not been seen in public since taking power.  Donald Trump has described Iran's leadership as "fractured" and suggested the US is waiting for Tehran to produce a "unified proposal." While diplomatic channels remain open, Iranian officials have acknowledged that Mojtaba Khamenei may be injured and unable to actively manage the system. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), led by Ahmad Vahidi, appears to be setting the pace of the crisis with its actions in enforcing the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.  Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf has emerged as a prominent figure, stepping into negotiations and addressing the public, but his position is precarious due to a lack of clear authorization from Mojtaba Khamenei.

articles.title: Raghav Chadha and 6 AAP Rajya Sabha MPs join BJP in a major political shift - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Seven members of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in the Rajya Sabha have defected to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), a move that significantly alters the political landscape of the Upper House. The MPs, Raghav Chadha, Sandeep Pathak, and Ashok Kumar Mittal, met with BJP president Nitin Nabin at the party's headquarters on Friday evening.  The AAP has accused the BJP of orchestrating "Operation Lotus" to recruit its members.

articles.title: The boatpeople basti who bothered a barrage - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A hundred and fifty armed policemen, assisted by the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (Pera), demolished a boatpeople settlement in Taunsa Barrage near Kot Addu. The government claims the settlement was encroaching on public land, but residents argue they have lived there for generations and received services from the government.  The demolition comes as part of the Punjab government's "Saaf Suthra Punjab" initiative to improve urban cleanliness and aesthetics through anti-encroachment drives. The project has been criticized for its lack of consideration for informal settlements and their residents, who often find themselves displaced due to the state's failure to provide adequate housing and livelihood opportunities.

articles.title: Iran-Iraq Tanker War redux? Why the Strait of Hormuz crisis is different | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The current US-Iran standoff in the Strait of Hormuz mirrors the 1980s Tanker War, with shipping disruptions and heightened tensions.  US forces have imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, while Iran has closed passage to all vessels. The situation is similar to the 1980s war between Iran and Iraq, where both countries fired on each other's tankers in the Strait of Hormuz seeking to cripple their economies.  However, the current conflict is more about deterrence and signaling than asymmetrical warfare. Iran appears stronger now compared to its position during the Tanker War, as it has shifted its military doctrine from defensive containment to an offensive asymmetric posture. The US and its allies have refused to join in reopening the Strait of Hormuz or participate in minesweeping operations, fearing they will be dragged into the war.

articles.title: Kezia Dugdale, incoming Stonewall chair, says sorry after backlash over JK Rowling remarks | Kezia Dugdale | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kezia Dugdale, the incoming chair of Stonewall, expressed regret after her interview with the Guardian, where she stated "huge respect" for JK Rowling.  Dugdale's comments sparked backlash from both trans advocates and gender-critical feminists. She later issued a statement clarifying that she would never condone harmful behavior towards the LGBTQ+ community, emphasizing her commitment to inclusivity.  Stonewall, which works for the whole LGBTQ+ community, remains committed to trans equality under Dugdale's leadership.

articles.title: Hundreds of wildfires burn across Florida and Georgia
articles.rephrased_article: Florida and Georgia are facing severe wildfires, with hundreds of blazes burning across both states.  The Pineland Road Fire in Georgia, now nearly 30,000 acres, is only 10% contained, while Florida is experiencing one of its worst fire seasons in decades, with over 130 active wildfires.  Dry conditions, high winds, and lack of rain are cited as contributing factors to the difficulty in controlling the fires.

articles.title: ED probes suspected TTI-linked funds routed through foreign bank debit cards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches on April 18 and 19 at six locations in Assam, Chhattisgarh, and other places as part of an investigation into the suspected withdrawal and use of funds through foreign bank debit cards. The agency reported around ₹95 crore of inflow via such cards between November 2025 and April 2026, allegedly bypassing regulatory channels. This probe is linked to The Timothy Initiative (TTI) and associated persons under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).

articles.title: Citizens now able to access district-level records as Nadra revamps its website - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Nadra, Pakistan's National Database and Registration Authority, has launched a revamped website that offers citizens online access to district-level birth and death records, as well as the ability to file right-to-information requests. The redesigned platform includes interactive maps, categorized identity documents, consolidated verification services, and a dedicated RTI portal for tracking information requests.  The initiative aims to enhance digital accessibility, transparency, and public service delivery through modern technology.

articles.title: Five games to go: The Premier League’s unpredictable season turns again | Football | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Premier League title race has shifted dramatically in recent weeks, with Manchester City taking the lead after a string of upsets for Arsenal.  A combination of losses to Bournemouth and Manchester City, coupled with Chelsea's continued struggles, has left the Gunners vulnerable. The author believes that City, despite their recent form, will ultimately prevail due to their superior goal difference and rested squad. However, they acknowledge the unpredictable nature of the league, noting past examples where seemingly insurmountable leads have been overturned.  The final five games will determine the champion.

articles.title: Starmer pledges to bring forward law proscribing Iran’s Revolutionary Guards | UK security and counter-terrorism | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer, the prime minister, pledged to introduce legislation in July that would allow for the proscription of the Iranian Revolutionary Guards (IRGC). This follows a series of arson attacks on Jewish sites in the UK, including a synagogue in Harrow and four ambulances set ablaze. The government will also give powers to address “state-sponsored” groups like the IRGC.  Phil Rosenberg, president of the Board of Deputies of British Jews, welcomed this decision, stating that it was something the community had long called for.

articles.title: 'A dangerous standoff' as Strait of Hormuz blockade continues
articles.rephrased_article: US and Iran are engaged in a standoff at the Strait of Hormuz, with US forces intercepting or turning back vessels traveling to or from Iranian waters.  Iran calls this "piracy" and its top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, insists reopening the strait is not possible while the US maintains its naval blockade.

articles.title: Meta sets up automatic blocking for govt., police-referred content - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, has been complying with censorship orders from Indian authorities, restricting content on its platforms based on local laws. The Sahyog portal, used by police to request takedowns, allows for immediate restriction of access without requiring a formal legal process.  The firm's response is to instantly remove content flagged through this mechanism, even after determining the takedown may be legally improper. Critics argue that this practice creates an "infrastructure of censorship" and undermines free speech, while experts call on Meta to publish all takedown notices and challenge frivolous ones in court.

articles.title: Sindh govt will fulfill its promise to rebuild Gul Plaza, CM Murad says - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah announced that the Sindh government will rebuild the destroyed Gul Plaza, ensuring no increase in the number of shops, as promised.  He also distributed compensation cheques to affected shopkeepers and thanked organizations like the Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industries (KCCI) and the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) for providing temporary business spaces. The government has allocated Rs7 billion for the affected community and is awaiting a court order to begin demolition.  President Asif Ali Zardari expressed his condolences and requested a plan from a Chinese entity that visited Pakistan after the incident.

articles.title: In 2019, a NASA intern scanning star data noticed a tiny glitch and uncovered a world orbiting two suns | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Wolf Cukier, a 17-year-old, discovered TOI-1338 b, a circumbinary planet orbiting two stars, while analyzing data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center. His meticulous observation of an unusual dip in light curves led to further research and the identification of another planet, TOI-1338 c or BEBOP-1c.  This discovery highlighted the importance of human observation in scientific breakthroughs and demonstrated the capabilities of TESS in finding complex exoplanets.

articles.title: UK eases airline penalties as jet fuel shortages threaten flights | Airline industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Airport Coordination Limited has eased penalties for airlines canceling UK flights due to jet fuel shortages, allowing exemptions from the "use it or lose it" rule. The Department for Transport reassured the public that there is no current need to change travel plans and emphasized ongoing monitoring of fuel supply risks. Airlines have lobbied for this change, arguing it will allow them to focus on minimizing disruption rather than protecting takeoff and landing slots.  Despite these changes, airlines are still encouraged to check with passengers before travel and advise them to have insurance.

articles.title: How the Kremlin's internet crackdown is frustrating Russians
articles.rephrased_article: Russian authorities have been implementing stricter internet controls, including blocking access to global messaging apps like WhatsApp and Telegram, and restricting mobile internet in certain areas. Russians report that these measures are negatively impacting businesses and their ability to connect with the outside world.  The Kremlin justifies these restrictions as necessary for public safety, citing the disruption of Ukrainian attack drones by mobile internet blackouts.

articles.title: SC declines to intervene in a plea by Indrani Mukerjea to travel abroad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court declined to grant permission for Indrani Mukerjea, an accused in the murder of her daughter Sheena Bora, to travel abroad. The court instructed Ms. Mukerjea to file an application with the trial court, which will be decided within four weeks.  Ms. Mukerjea was granted bail in May 2022 after spending more than six years in custody. Sheena Bora was allegedly murdered by Indrani Mukerjea, her then-driver Shyamvar Rai, and former husband Sanjeev Khanna.

articles.title: CJP says transferring judge back to SHC would render key constitutional ideals redundant - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi has rejected requests to transfer Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) back to the Sindh High Court (SHC), citing concerns about undermining federalism and equitable representation within the judiciary. The CJP argued that such a transfer would render constitutional ideals redundant and create a temporary administrative arrangement, rather than upholding the spirit of judicial independence enshrined in the Constitution. He emphasized that transfers should be based on justified reasons and adhere to the established procedures outlined in Article 209 for addressing judicial accountability issues.  The CJP also cautioned against setting a precedent where judges could be treated as administratively interchangeable or disposable.

articles.title: Giant Ramesses II statue fragment found in Nile Delta, revealing new clues about ancient Egypt | World News - The Times of India
