He faces five charges of war crimes related to alleged civilian killings during his service in Afghanistan between 2009 and 2012. The Returned and Services League (RSL) welcomes Roberts-Smith's attendance, while a group called the National Workers Alliance is planning a rally in Melbourne on Anzac Day in support of him.  The rally, which calls for the charges against Roberts-Smith to be dropped, has been criticized by some as promoting white nationalism.

articles.title: Epstein housed abuse victims in London flats, BBC reveals
articles.rephrased_article: Jeffrey Epstein housed abuse victims in several London flats after UK police decided not to investigate him.  The Metropolitan Police said they interviewed Virginia Giuffre, who alleged she was trafficked by Epstein, and contacted other potential victims but did not open an investigation. The National Crime Agency (NCA) passed financial intelligence about Epstein's UK transactions to the FBI, including payments for one of his Chelsea flats.  The BBC found evidence that Epstein used the Eurostar to transport women between France and England, and that he paid for at least five women to study in London. Several people who worked for Epstein and his accomplice, Ghislaine Maxwell, have been identified by the BBC. The investigation revealed that British authorities were aware of some of Epstein's activities but did not open an inquiry.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Failure to investigate alleged trafficking is a serious institutional failure.

articles.title: India approves ₹30 billion for Maldives under SAARC swap - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India has approved the first withdrawal of ₹30 billion under its continuing economic and financial assistance to Maldives, marking the first drawdown of the SAARC Currency Swap Framework. The funds are being released following the earlier $400 million withdrawal, which matured on Thursday, April 24, 2026.  The currency swap facility has been instrumental in ensuring financial stability for Maldives since its inception in 2012.

articles.title: Paris Modest Fashion Week: Muslim designers showcase floral dresses and boxy streetwear in Paris
articles.rephrased_article: Paris hosted its first ever Modest Fashion Week, featuring nearly 30 designers showcasing clothing that aligns with religious principles.  The event, held at Hôtel Le Marois, focused on floral dresses, boxy streetwear, and headscarves, reflecting the growing popularity of modest fashion globally. Fatou Doucouré, founder of Soutoura, expressed pride in exhibiting her collection in Paris, highlighting the potential for Muslim women to contribute to any society.  The event also drew attention to the increasing acceptance of religious clothing in France, as young attendees shared their positive experiences and a sense of inclusivity.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump orders US to ‘shoot and kill’ boats laying mines in Hormuz strait; Israel-Lebanon truce extended | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump ordered US military to "shoot and kill" Iranian boats deploying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming US minesweepers are clearing the waterway.  The US president also announced a three-week extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon and stated that the US has “hit about 75% of our targets” in Iran. Trump asserted US control over the strait despite Iranian seizure of two container ships and a US report warning it could take months to clear the waterway of mines.  The situation escalated with the killing of a Lebanese journalist by Israeli forces, prompting international condemnation.  Meanwhile, Iran’s president denied internal divisions within the leadership while its foreign minister emphasized unity and discipline among state institutions.

articles.title: Parts of twin cities remain locked down despite uncertainty over US-Iran talks - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: District administrations in Rawalpindi and Islamabad have yet to decide on reopening closed areas around the Nur Khan Airbase, including roads, markets, and transportation routes. This has caused significant disruptions for residents, with Metro Bus, electric bus services, and goods transport suspended since April 19th. Residents are facing difficulties accessing essential supplies like water, food, and electricity, with Iesco resuming power cuts despite claims of no outages due to heightened security measures. The Oil Tankers Contractors Association has called for a two-to-three hour window for fuel supply during which tankers can replenish stations under official supervision.

articles.title: West Bengal election 2026: Record turnout of over 92% in first phase amidst isolated incidents of violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: West Bengal registered a record voter turnout of 92.03% in the first phase of Assembly elections on April 23, 2026.  The high turnout was attributed to the election being seen as a fight for voting rights and the potential implementation of the National Register of Citizens (NRC). Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated voters and praised the Election Commission of India (ECI) for ensuring a peaceful election. Despite the record turnout, isolated incidents of violence were reported across different districts, including clashes between supporters of political parties and attacks on BJP candidates.  The second phase of polling will be held on April 29th.

articles.title: Rosenberg: Kremlin's tightening grip on internet fuels public discontent
articles.rephrased_article: Kremlin officials have tightened control of Russia's internet, restricting access to global messaging apps and mobile internet.  This crackdown is causing public discontent as people are struggling with disruptions to their businesses and daily lives. President Vladimir Putin acknowledges the disruption but insists it is necessary for national security. While he claims these measures will be lifted once the need disappears, many Russians feel that this is a new normal.  The situation has sparked protests and calls for change, with some even questioning the future of Russia's internet landscape.

articles.title: Largest-ever ban on toxic chemicals in EU hit by ‘extremely frustrating’ delays | Pollution | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: European Commission has faced criticism for its failure to implement the "restrictions roadmap" aimed at phasing out hazardous substances, with delays exceeding legal deadlines in regulating seven groups.  The delay, according to a report by ClientEarth and the European Environmental Bureau, has resulted in nearly 100,000 tonnes of extra chemical pollution from six groups, including lead in ammunition and fishing tackle. Green groups allege that the Commission is the "chief roadblock" to its own roadmap and claim "unlawful delays," despite previous progress on restricting substances like Pfas in firefighting foam and lead in PVC plastics.

articles.title: Infosys shares fall 4% after Q4 results. What Morgan Stanley, other top brokerages are saying - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Infosys reported a 13.4% increase in revenue for Q4FY26, reaching Rs 46,402 crore.  Operating margin remained stable at 21%, but profit after tax rose 28% to Rs 6,654 crore. Revenue growth was driven by a 6.6% sequential increase in dollar revenue. However, analysts like Jefferies and Morgan Stanley expressed concerns about the company's weak FY27 revenue guidance of 1.5% to 3.5%, citing headcount reduction and lower net new deal wins. Despite these concerns, some analysts like Motilal Oswal maintained a Buy rating on Infosys shares due to its strong fundamentals and potential for growth in the AI-driven market.

articles.title: US soldier allegedly bet on Maduro operation using intel - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A US soldier, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, faces charges for allegedly using classified information to bet on outcomes related to the US operation to capture former Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro.  Van Dyke, a member of the US Army, is accused of making over $400,000 through online prediction markets like Polymarket. The Department of Justice has stated that insider trading has no place on Polymarket and cooperated with their investigation. Polymarket flagged Van Dyke's activity to the Department of Justice.  The case highlights concerns about conflicts of interest related to the Trump administration's actions, including betting on events like the Iran-Iraq war and cryptocurrency investments by members of the family.

articles.title: Despite heat, senior citizens step out to vote in large numbers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Despite Election Commission of India efforts to facilitate postal voting for super senior citizens and persons with disabilities, many elderly individuals chose to vote in person.  Stephen, a 103-year-old resident, cast his vote at the polling station due to his desire to fulfill his democratic duty. Others like Easwari, a 102-year-old woman, also voted in person despite their age. However, some elderly voters faced difficulties such as long queues and transportation challenges. Consumer activist T. Sadagopan questioned why those above 80 were not classified as super senior citizens, while the Income Tax Department and Government of India had already done so.  A.M. Rajagopalan, a former printer and publisher of The Hindu, and H.V. Hande, a former Minister, also voted despite their advanced age.

articles.title: White House memo claims mass AI theft by Chinese firms
articles.rephrased_article: The White House has issued a memo outlining concerns about "industrial-scale campaigns" by foreign entities, primarily based in China, to steal American AI technology through a process called "distillation."  Michael Kratsios, Director of Science and Technology Policy, stated the administration will work with US AI firms to combat these attacks, sharing information about tactics employed and developing best practices for identifying and mitigating them. China's US embassy responded by claiming its development is a result of dedication and international cooperation, not malicious exploitation.  The memo did not detail specific plans but acknowledged the growing sophistication of detection methods and warned that foreign entities relying on such fragile foundations should be wary of their AI model integrity.

articles.title: Revealed: UK oil refinery owner moved Russian loans to offshore subsidiary where sanctions did not apply | Essar Energy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Following Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Essar, an Indian-owned conglomerate with ties to the Russian state bank VTB, shifted billions of dollars in loans from Cyprus to Mauritius, a tax haven.  Despite sanctions imposed on VTB and its chief, Andrey Kostin, Essar claimed it complied with UK sanctions law. However, experts and lawmakers are questioning whether this move circumvented sanctions regulations and call for investigations by the UK authorities. The Cypriot government is also examining the legality of these transactions.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential sanctions evasion by an Indian company raises concerns about financial misconduct.

articles.title: SW Solar shares fall 2% after Q4 revenue declines 23%; net profit balloons 143% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Sterling and Wilson, a major MEP and EPC contractor, reported a 23% year-on-year decline in revenue to Rs 1,946 crore for the fourth quarter of FY26. Revenue fell 7% from the previous quarter to Rs 2,092 crore. The company's total expenses decreased by 24% year-on-year to Rs 1,844 crore. SWREL returned to profitability after reporting a loss in Q3FY26 and achieved record quarterly PAT and 4.5 GW execution for FY26.  The company has a strong order book of Rs 11,813 crore for FY27, with growth expected from wind and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects.

articles.title: Israel, Lebanon extend ceasefire as Iran peace talks stall - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump extended a ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon for three more weeks, while the US remains at a standstill in negotiations with Iran.  The truce extension came despite recent Israeli strikes in Lebanon and rocket fire from Hezbollah. The US president stated that he is not in a rush to end the war with Iran, emphasizing that "the clock is ticking" for the Islamic republic. Meanwhile, tensions remain high as Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, citing retaliation for the ongoing conflict.  The US Navy continues to operate in the region, including the arrival of a third aircraft carrier, while Israel's Defense Minister calls for the elimination of the Khamenei dynasty.

articles.title: Telangana SEEEPC Survey: What does it show about caste inequality? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A new government report from Telangana, India, challenges long-held assumptions about social disadvantage by using a novel Composite Backwardness Index (CBI) to measure caste-based inequality. The SEEEPC Survey 2024, conducted on a massive scale and covering 97% of the state's population, reveals that Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) face a systemic form of disadvantage far exceeding incremental differences in income.  This groundbreaking study provides a stark contrast to traditional measures of economic inequality.

articles.title: US government watchdog to investigate Epstein files release
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) inspector general is launching an investigation into whether the agency is complying with a law requiring the release of files related to Jeffrey Epstein. The investigation will examine the identification, collection, and production of responsive material related to Epstein, as well as guidance and processes for redacting and withholding material consistent with the law.  The DoJ has released millions of files since the Epstein Files Transparency Act was signed by President Donald Trump in 2025, but some have criticized the agency's handling of the case and its potential to protect powerful individuals.

articles.title: Actor felt ‘mocked’ by Rebel Wilson’s wife in Instagram post referencing Finding Nemo, court hears | Rebel Wilson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Charlotte MacInnes, lead actress in the film "The Deb", is suing Rebel Wilson for defamation over social media posts alleging she made a sexual harassment complaint and retracted it to advance her career.  MacInnes claims Wilson's wife Ramona Agruma-Wilson mocked her testimony with an Instagram post referencing Dory from "Finding Nemo," causing her emotional distress. The trial continues as both Wilson and Agruma-Wilson are expected to testify.

articles.title: Silver dips Rs 2,300, gold at Rs 1.51 lakh as oil surge, Iran war uncertainty raise inflation worries. What’s next? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran released footage of commandos boarding a cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions. MCX silver futures fell while gold futures declined slightly.  Analysts predict continued volatility in both metals due to fluctuations in the dollar index, crude oil prices, and uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran peace deal. They advise waiting for stability before taking fresh positions.

articles.title: Pakistan repays $3.45bn to UAE, confirms central bank - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's central bank confirmed the repayment of a $3.45 billion deposit to the United Arab Emirates, completing the return of all funds provided in 2019.  The country repaid $1 billion to the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development on April 23 and $2.45 billion last week, according to the State Bank of Pakistan. This repayment comes amid concerns about near-term financing gaps and pressure on foreign exchange reserves. The move is seen as a cost to uphold national dignity despite drawing down reserves.

articles.title: Iran Nuclear Issue: Iran admits 'strategic mistake' over nuclear issue at negotiation table in Pakistan - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Nabavian, a member of Iran’s parliamentary national security and foreign policy committee, criticized the decision to discuss Iran's nuclear program during recent negotiations in Pakistan, calling it a "strategic mistake."  Donald Trump, former US president, asserted that he was not in a rush to reach an agreement with Iran and warned that time was working against Tehran. He also stated that any deal would only be finalized if it aligned with US interests and those of its allies.

articles.title: Watch: Manipur sees little respite despite a change of guard under the BJP | The Hindu Editorial - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Home Ministry and the BJP are calling for increased cooperation to quell tensions in the country. They suggest a more proactive role by the Home Ministry and an effort by the BJP to involve all political actors in easing the situation. The strategy also includes empowering security agencies to target hardline elements engaging in violence.

articles.title: Woman killed by bear in Polish forest, son and local government say
articles.rephrased_article: A 58-year-old woman was killed by a bear in the Bieszczady region of Poland while collecting antlers. Her son witnessed the attack and called for help, but emergency services were delayed due to difficult terrain and lack of phone reception. The incident is believed to have occurred near the town of Płonna, where Poland has around 100 brown bears.  The woman's death marks a rare fatal encounter between humans and bears in the country.

articles.title: Oil rises above $106 per barrel as US, Iran deadlocked in Strait of Hormuz | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged above $106 per barrel on Friday morning as heightened tensions between the US and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz escalated. Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to destroy Iranian boats laying mines in the waterway, following the Pentagon's seizure of a second Iranian-flagged tanker for violating sanctions. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps captured two foreign cargo ships in the strait, citing security concerns over vessels operating without permits. Shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has been significantly reduced as a result of these actions, with only nine vessels transiting on Wednesday compared to 15 on Monday.

articles.title: Anthony Albanese accused of ‘caving to gas companies’ as Labor set to reject new export tax | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor is poised to reject a proposed 25% gas export tax in the upcoming budget, despite calls from David Pocock, an independent senator. The government has opted against pursuing this tax, citing concerns about global oil supply and diplomatic efforts to secure fuel from Asian allies.  However, less dramatic changes like reforms to the petroleum resources rent tax or a windfall profits tax are still under consideration. Anthony Albanese argues that gas corporations already pay substantial taxes and emphasizes Australia's role as a reliable gas supplier. The decision has drawn criticism from some who argue it allows gas companies to profit excessively during the energy crisis.

articles.title: Pharma stocks buck market weakness as Dr Reddy's gains - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Dr Reddy's Laboratories, Piramal Pharma, and Cipla saw significant gains on Thursday, with the Nifty Pharma Index rising 2.4% while the broader Nifty declined 0.8%.  Analysts suggest this rally is driven by anticipation of a successful approval for Dr Reddy's Laboratories' Semaglutide generic filing in Canada, which is expected around May. Other companies in the Semaglutide value chain also experienced significant increases, including OneSource Specialty Pharma and Shaily Engineering Plastics.  Pharma shares are gaining popularity due to their defensive positioning amid market uncertainty.

articles.title: CJP Afridi openly opposes Judicial Commission of Pakistan meeting for judges’ transfer - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi has expressed his opposition to the scheduled meeting of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) to consider the transfer of five judges from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to other high courts.  He believes that allowing such transfers would set a dangerous precedent, erode public confidence in the judiciary's independence and stability, and be "punitive" in nature. Justice Afridi previously supported the transfer of three judges to the IHC under Article 200 but now argues that these proposed transfers violate constitutional principles and the spirit of judicial independence.  The JCP is scheduled to meet on April 28th to consider the CJP's concerns.

articles.title: Trump reclassifies state-licensed medical marijuana as a less-dangerous drug - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump’s acting attorney general, Todd Blanche, signed an order reclassifying state-licensed medical marijuana as a Schedule III drug. This change, while not legalising marijuana for medical or recreational use under federal law, shifts regulation from the highly controlled Schedule I to a less strict Schedule III. The move also grants tax breaks and eases research barriers for licensed medical marijuana operators.  This policy shift represents a major advancement in cannabis policy and is seen as a significant step towards legitimizing medical marijuana programs across the country.

articles.title: The Karur stampede is yet to fade from the memory of the voters at Velusamypuram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Velusamypuram, the site of a deadly political rally tragedy in September 2025, saw brisk polling on Thursday.  Voters were grappling with the lingering impact of the stampede that claimed 41 lives, including nine children, while awaiting answers about the cause and those responsible. C. Joseph Vijay, president of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), was accused in the case but voters largely refrained from discussing it during the election process.  The polling station at Velusamypuram recorded 81.31% turnout with almost four hours remaining before closing.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article highlights a deadly tragedy with unanswered questions about responsibility.

articles.title: Singer D4vd found with 'significant amount' of child sex abuse images - prosecutors
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, has been accused of possessing "a significant amount" of child sex abuse images on his phone and iCloud account when he was arrested for the death of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Police discovered these images during their investigation into how Rivas Hernandez died in Burke's Tesla, which had been towed to a Hollywood tow yard after a foul odor was reported.  The singer has pleaded not guilty to murder and other charges, including continuous sexual abuse of a child and the mutilation of remains. The case is ongoing with two court hearings scheduled for next week.

articles.title: India voices anger after Trump shares comments calling it a ‘hellhole’ | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump posted inflammatory comments on Truth Social calling India a "hellhole," sparking criticism from India's foreign ministry, which called the remarks "uninformed, inappropriate and in poor taste."  Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State, is scheduled to visit India next month. Congressman Ami Bera condemned Trump's post as "offensive, ignorant and beneath the dignity of the office he holds," while the Hindu American Foundation expressed concern over the potential for increased xenophobia.

articles.title: Global cues weigh on Dalal Street as oil spike fuels investor worries - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty and Sensex experienced losses on Thursday, falling 0.8% and 1.1%, respectively.  Analysts attributed the decline to profit-taking following a recent rally and concerns over elevated crude prices and the ongoing West Asia conflict. The VIX, India's volatility index, also rose, indicating caution among traders.  However, some analysts believe the market may consolidate within a specific range in the near future.

articles.title: CJP Afridi openly opposes Judicial Commission of Pakistan meeting for judges’ transfer - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Justice of Pakistan (CJP) Yahya Afridi has expressed his opposition to the scheduled meeting of the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) to consider transferring five judges from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to other high courts.  He argues that allowing such transfers would set a dangerous precedent, eroding public confidence in the judiciary's independence and stability. Justice Afridi previously supported similar transfers under Article 200 of the Constitution but now expresses concern about the potential consequences for judicial integrity. The JCP is scheduled to meet on April 28th to discuss the matter.

articles.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei awaiting prosthetic leg after strike, suffered severe facial burns: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran's Supreme Leader, is facing health challenges following a bomb attack and has limited physical mobility. This situation has led to a power vacuum with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) increasingly influencing decision-making processes.  Analysts suggest that Khamenei's authority has diminished, with decisions presented as "fait accompli," while communication with him is restricted to sealed letters. The evolving power structure, characterized by board-style leadership and increased IRGC influence, raises concerns about the future of diplomacy between Iran and the United States.

articles.title: Torn fisherfolk families in Thangachimadam turn to the polls as a last resort - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fisherfolk in Rameswaram and nearby areas cast their votes despite the ongoing arrests of fishermen by Sri Lankan Navy, expressing a sense of helplessness and resignation.  Tamilarasi, a mother whose son is imprisoned in Sri Lanka, and Rayappan, another fisherman who experienced imprisonment, voted believing that their ballots could bring about relief to the long-lasting issue of arrests. They recognized the significance of their vote as a tool for influencing the system that puts politicians in power.

articles.title: Meta says it will cut 8,000 jobs as AI spending soars
articles.rephrased_article: Meta announced it will cut 8,000 jobs as part of a company-wide restructuring plan. The Meta CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, has stated that the increased focus on artificial intelligence (AI) is driving this decision.  The layoffs are expected to be Meta's largest since 2023 and follow similar actions by other tech giants like Amazon, Oracle, Block, and Snap. These companies have cited AI investment as a key driver for their workforce reductions.

articles.title: ‘If you buy Kyle, you get Kyle’: Sandilands’ lawyer defends sacked Kiis FM shock jock in Sydney court | Australian media | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kyle Sandilands and his former partner Jackie “O” Henderson are suing ARN Media for over $80 million each, claiming breach of contract after their dismissal from the Kiis FM breakfast show.  Sandilands' lawyer argued that the alleged misconduct was contractual and monetized, while ARN Media claims Sandilands repeatedly berated colleagues and audience members on air. The court will hear the case separately, with Justice Angus Stewart presiding over both cases.

articles.title: IT majors see strong deal pipeline but revenue momentum cools in Q4 - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Infosys, HCL Technologies, and TCS reported weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue, with TCS marking its first annual decline since going public. Analysts had anticipated a drop of under 1% in each case, but the IT giants' topline growth has now fallen to mid-single digits.  This raises concerns about AI disruption and deflation within the industry, prompting investors to question whether stock valuations have adequately reflected these risks. The trailing price-earnings (P/E) multiples of these companies have been declining for a decade, further adding to investor anxiety.

articles.title: Trump rules out N-option amid Hormuz struggle - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to destroy any vessels laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, citing "total control" over the strait.  The move followed a successful seizure of an Iranian tanker off Sri Lanka and heightened tensions with Iran. The Pentagon also announced the boarding of a sanctioned Iranian oil tanker in the Indian Ocean, while Iran received its first revenue from tolls imposed on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, a third US aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, bringing the total number to three.  The Senate voted against a motion to advance a war powers resolution that would have limited Trump's ability to continue hostilities beyond the timeframe allowed under US law.

articles.title: One killed, five injured in shooting at Mall of Louisiana food court - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting at the food court of Mall of Louisiana in Baton Rouge left one person dead and five injured on Friday afternoon.  The incident stemmed from a confrontation between two groups, according to Baton Rouge Police Chief TJ Morse, who confirmed that five people were taken into custody.  Desire Batton, a worker at a clothing store, said shoppers and employees fled the scene as gunfire erupted. The mall will remain closed for the rest of the day.

articles.title: How Visakhapatnam zoo keeps animals cool as temperatures rise - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park (IGZP) is implementing its annual summer management plan to ensure animal comfort amidst rising temperatures.  The zoo, spread across 625 acres of forested hills and the Bay of Bengal, uses water sprinklers, shade structures, adjusted diets, and modified routines to maintain a comfortable environment for all animals within their enclosures. The park's staff carefully monitors each species' needs and implements tailored strategies to ensure animal well-being during the summer months.

articles.title: US soldier charged after winning $400,000 betting on removal of Venezuela's Nicolas Maduro
articles.rephrased_article: A US special forces soldier, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, has been arrested for allegedly betting on the removal of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro before it was publicly known.  The US Department of Justice (DOJ) alleges that Van Dyke used classified information to profit from his bets on the outcome of Operation Absolute Resolve, a military operation that captured Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores. The Polymarket platform, where Van Dyke allegedly placed his bets, referred the matter to the DOJ for investigation. Van Dyke faces charges including unlawful use of confidential government information and commodities fraud.

articles.title: Iran war live: Lebanon truce extended; Trump says time not on Tehran’s side | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump extended the ceasefire in Lebanon for three weeks, hoping to bring together Israeli and Lebanese leaders.  He stated he has no pressure to end his war with Iran, claiming time is limited for Tehran. The death toll from Israel's ongoing conflict with Gaza has reached 72,568 with 172,338 injured according to the Gaza’s Health Ministry.

articles.title: US soldier involved in Maduro raid charged over alleged bets on capture | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a US soldier involved in the January capture of Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro, has been arrested for allegedly cashing in over $400,000 on wagers about the politician's removal from office. Van Dyke is facing charges of commodities and wire fraud, unlawful use of confidential government information for personal gain, and is accused of using his position to profit from a military operation. The Department of Justice (DoJ), FBI, and Polymarket have all played roles in the investigation.  The case highlights concerns about insider trading within prediction markets and raises questions about potential conflicts of interest among government employees.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu elections 2026: Over 84% voter turnout in the State, highest in its electoral history - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu recorded its highest polling percentage in an Assembly election, reaching 84.69% on April 23, 2026. Over 4.85 crore people cast their votes across all 234 constituencies. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar commended voters in both West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, noting it was the highest percentage of polling in those states.

articles.title: Watch: Above 92% turnout in Bengal, 85% in Tamil Nadu amid poll violence | Above the Fold | 23.04.2026 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu reports on key election trends in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, highlighting shifts ahead of the polls. The publication also covers political tensions in the United States over birthright citizenship and rising tensions in West Asia around the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, West Bengal's campaign landscape has seen a significant change.

articles.title: Book release controversy: SSUS to initiate inquiry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS)'s Vice-Chancellor, Ciza Thomas, cancelled the release of a biography of Chattampi Swamikal due to incomplete printing. The Kerala Governor, who was scheduled to release the book, directed Thomas to investigate and take action.  The university is now conducting an inquiry into the mix-up involving the printing and release of the work.

articles.title: Analysis: Why there is a ‘Pawar play’ over political legacy in Baramati - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sharad Pawar's legacy in Baramati, Maharashtra, is being challenged after the death of his nephew, Ajit Pawar.  The constituency, long dominated by the Pawar family, faces uncertainty as younger generations seek their own political paths. The BJP seeks to capitalize on this shift while the NCP and its allied party, NCP (SP), grapple with internal divisions.

articles.title: Nepal’s customs duty is the outcome of a ‘pre-existing provision’, will not affect ‘household goods’: India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nepal's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) responded to protests against new customs duty regulations imposed on travelers from India. The MEA stated that the duty is a pre-existing provision and will not affect families carrying household goods.  The new rule, implemented in mid-April by Prime Minister Balendra Shah, requires travelers with goods worth over one hundred Nepali rupees to pay customs duty.

articles.title: Bombay HC pulls up NIA for delays in 2006 Malegaon blast investigation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bombay High Court quashed charges against four individuals accused in the 2006 Malegaon bomb blasts, citing insufficient evidence provided by the National Investigation Agency (NIA). The court's decision was made by a Division Bench of Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and Justice Shyam C. Chandak, who ruled that there was not enough material to proceed against Rajendra Chaudhary, Dhan Singh, Manohar Ram Singh Narwaria, and Lokesh Sharma.

articles.title: Revanth, Uttam to meet CBI Directorfor expediting Kaleshwaram probe - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and Irrigation Minister N. Uttam Kumar Reddy plan to meet the CBI Director to urge for expedited investigation into alleged irregularities in the Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project. The High Court upheld the constitution of the Justice P. C. Ghose Commission, finding no fault with its findings or legal validity.  The Ministers will consult senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi before deciding whether to appeal to the Supreme Court.

articles.title: NHRC issues notices to Centre, States over poor adoption of NCERT, SCERT textbooks in private schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) has issued notices to the Centre and States seeking explanations regarding inspections or audits into allegations that private schools are substituting government-prescribed textbooks with those from private publishers. The complaint alleges this practice burdens families financially, prompting the NHRC's inquiry.

articles.title: Trump shares right-wing anchor’s rant against Indians, MEA terms it ‘inappropriate’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Centre responded to derogatory remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump about India and Indian immigrants, calling them "uninformed, inappropriate, and in poor taste." The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) spokesperson stated that the comments do not reflect the reality of the India-U.S. relationship and expressed concern over the amplified views shared by Mr. Trump.  The U.S. Embassy did not clarify or backpedal on Mr. Trump's statements, further fueling criticism from Indian politicians and experts who called for a stronger response from the government.

articles.title: Business houses in Tamil Nadu pause for election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article:
Tamil Nadu businesses largely shut down on election day, 2026, to allow employees to vote. The banking and real estate sectors were closed, while Credai, the Confederation of Real Estate Developers Associations of India, granted a full day leave for workers.  IT firms and industrial estates housing MSMEs saw varying degrees of closure, with essential businesses remaining operational. 
Cognizant, an IT firm, closed its offices in Tamil Nadu to enable employees to vote.

articles.title: Visakhapatnam sees record participation for State football selections - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Visakhapatnam emerged as the top-performing district in Andhra Pradesh for football league selections, with 232 children participating in district-level trials. The Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP) conducted the trials at the Indira Priyadarshini Stadium to identify teams for upcoming State-level competitions.  The selection process included Under-15 and Under-21 categories for both boys and girls, with a strong presence from schools and parents. A total of 64 players were selected to represent Visakhapatnam at the State-level competitions in Anantapur.

articles.title: Pandalam family member criticises Kerala for stance in Sabarimala entry dispute - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A senior representative of the Pandalam royal family, who claims to be the foster family of Lord Ayyappa, argued before the Supreme Court on Thursday that the State of Kerala has not taken a strong stance against petitions questioning the age-old rituals and beliefs at the Sabarimala temple.  K. Radhakrishnan, representing the royal family, cited past instances where the state had failed to address similar demands for investigations into the Makaravilakku festival.

articles.title: Polling booth agent arrested for damaging EVM in Tiruvannamalai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Venkatesan, a 47-year-old polling booth agent from Kilpalur village, was arrested in Kalasapakkam Assembly constituency for allegedly damaging an EVM machine at a polling booth. The incident occurred around 10:00 AM when Venkatesan reportedly became upset after observing voters being directed to cast their votes for the AIADMK's "Two Leaves" symbol.  Police apprehended him before he could cause further damage.

articles.title: Tempers rise on second day of stir as Telangana RTC calls for temporary driver applications - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: TGSRTC workers continued their strike on Thursday, with one worker attempting suicide in protest of delayed absorption into the government. E. Venkanna, chairman of the RTC Joint Action Committee, condemned the incident and demanded better treatment from the Telangana government. The committee also accused police of preventing peaceful protests and called for intervention by Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy.  The corporation ran all its hire buses and electric buses to maintain service, but this proved inadequate as they were unable to meet demand.

articles.title: Kerala fireworks tragedy: body parts found as search intensifies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police recovered a severed, charred human head from a paddy field near the Mundathikode blast site in Thrissur.  The remains were found during an extensive search operation involving multiple agencies and personnel, including cadaver dogs and drone surveillance. Over 14 body parts were recovered, with four individuals still unaccounted for. Authorities are investigating the cause of the explosion and have collected DNA samples from relatives of the missing persons to identify them. The investigation is ongoing, with inconsistencies in witness statements being examined.

articles.title: US soldier charged with using Polymarket to bet on Nicolas Maduro abduction | Government News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: An active-duty US soldier, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, has been charged with using the prediction market platform Polymarket to bet on the abduction of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro. Prosecutors allege that Van Dyke used classified military information for personal gain, earning over $400,000 from his bets. The FBI and the Department of Justice are investigating this case as a breach of public trust.  The US government has taken steps to regulate prediction markets in recent years, but concerns remain about potential insider trading by government officials.

articles.title: BJP claiming ‘fake credit’ for raising land acquisition compensation for farmers; law made by UPA govt, says Congress - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress party alleged that the Madhya Pradesh government was falsely claiming credit for doubling land acquisition compensation, a provision enacted by the UPA government under former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh in 2013. The state cabinet approved an increase to double the market price of land acquired for farmers, with Chief Minister Mohan Yadav calling it a "major decision in the interest of farmers."

articles.title: US professors sue university over arrest during pro-Palestine protest | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Emory University professors Noelle McAfee, Emilio Del Valle-Escalante, and Caroline Fohlin filed a lawsuit against the university alleging it violated its own free speech policies by calling in police to disperse a 2024 pro-Palestine protest. The suit argues that the university failed to protect students and staff during the arrest of 28 individuals, including the professors who were observers at the event. Emory University maintains that it acted appropriately and responsibly to ensure safety on campus.  The lawsuit demands financial compensation for legal fees and punitive damages.

articles.title: Residents near Katpadi boycott polls after relocation of polling booth - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Residents of Balekuppam village in Vellore district boycotted elections on Thursday, protesting the relocation of a polling booth and lack of civic amenities. They hoisted black flags to signify their opposition and expressed dissatisfaction with the existing polling booth's distance from the village's Scheduled Caste settlement. The boycott was part of a wider movement against the proposed changes.

articles.title: Record turnout in WB & Tamil Nadu polls despite violence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu has migrated to a new commenting platform. Users can access their older comments by logging into their accounts on Vuukle.  All users must abide by the community guidelines for posting comments, which are in English and must be in full sentences.

articles.title: Bengaluru garbage tender: Contractor moves Karnataka High Court for probe alleging 9-15% bribe demand by two IAS officers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A private contractor, S.N. Balasubramaniam, has filed a petition in the High Court of Karnataka alleging that two senior State officials demanded illegal gratification ranging from 9% to 15% of the annual bid amount for awarding a Solid Waste Management (SWM) tender package in Bengaluru city. The petition was filed by the contractor's company, Nelaanjanaa Enterprises, and its representative organization, the Bangalore Mahanagara Swachahte Matthu Lorry Malikara Hagoo Guthigedarara Sangha.

articles.title: RTC driver succumbs after immolation bid, tension prevails in Warangal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Shankar Goud, a 54-year-old driver for the Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC), died from burn injuries sustained in an attempted self-immolation during the ongoing RTC employees' strike. The incident occurred at the Narsampet depot and prompted tension in the town and Warangal. Goud was rushed to a local hospital before being transferred to MGM Hospital in Warangal.

articles.title: Lisa Gill appointed Chief Justice of A.P. High Court - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: President Droupadi Murmu appointed Justice Lisa Gill as the Chief Justice of the Andhra Pradesh High Court, effective April 25th.  This appointment follows the retirement of current Chief Justice Dhiraj Singh Thakur on April 24th. Justice Gill, who was previously a puisne judge of the High Court, will assume the role upon the incumbent's departure.

articles.title: NOTA loses ground as electors in Tamil Nadu lean towards new political alternatives - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: NOTA, an option allowing voters to reject all candidates, did not see a significant surge in support during the recent elections.  While some voters chose NOTA, there was little public discussion about its popularity. Introduced in 2013 after a Supreme Court ruling, NOTA allows voters to formally reject all candidates on electronic voting machines.

articles.title: Two Scheduled Tribe couples exercise their franchise for the first time this election - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Masi and Govindammal, a couple from the Scheduled Tribe community in Konai village, cast their first votes on Thursday at the age of over 40 and 50 respectively. The pair had previously been trapped in bonded labor for six years in Salem district before receiving their voter IDs recently.

articles.title: Troubled waters: A.P., T.N. fishermen embroiled in a row - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fishermen from Cuddalore, Tamil Nadu, and Karaikal, Puducherry released four mechanised boats seized by fishermen in Nellore district, Andhra Pradesh. The dispute over the boats, which have been at the center of a long-standing conflict between the two states for almost four decades, has fueled concerns about inadequate maritime patrols.

articles.title: US-Israeli war on Iran will push 30 million back into poverty, UN warns | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United Nations has warned that the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran will push more than 30 million people back into poverty, due to disruptions in fuel and fertilizer supplies. Alexander De Croo, administrator of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), stated that even if the conflict ends immediately, these effects would persist for months, leading to increased food insecurity and energy shortages.  The disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route for Middle Eastern fertilizers, has already impacted crop yields and will further exacerbate global food security concerns.

articles.title: Recent hits give Malayalam film industry a shot in the arm - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hashir, Alan, Ajin, and Vinayak, all social media influencers, who starred in the Malayalam film "Vaazha II: Biopic of a Billion Bros," achieved their dream of storming the cinema after their January reel went viral. The movie, which cost ₹13 crore to produce, became a massive box-office hit, raking in ₹150 crore in less than 10 days.

articles.title: How bad is Lamine Yamal’s injury? Will he make Spain’s World Cup opener? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lamine Yamal, a 18-year-old Spanish forward, suffered a hamstring injury during a Barcelona match against Celta Vigo on April 22nd. The injury is expected to keep him out for several weeks, raising questions about his availability for Spain's World Cup opener on June 15th.  Barcelona confirmed the injury and stated that Yamal will be available for the World Cup. Lamine Yamal was instrumental in Spain's Euro 2024 victory and helped Barcelona win La Liga last season.

articles.title: A season to try and understand the people’s pulse - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sonia Gandhi made her debut election speech in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu on January 11, 1998, amidst a backdrop of political tension and the legacy of Rajiv Gandhi's assassination.  During the campaign, voters expressed their support for Congress through slogans like "Zindabad," while others displayed strong emotional ties to parties like the AIADMK, exemplified by an elderly woman who identified with the party's symbol despite its opposition.

articles.title: ACLU, Amnesty lead 120 rights groups issuing US World Cup ‘travel advisory’ | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) and Amnesty International, along with over 120 other civil society groups, issued a travel advisory for foreigners attending the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States. The advisory warns of “deteriorating human rights” and calls on FIFA to use its leverage to push for meaningful policy changes and guarantees that will ensure visitor safety.  The White House responded by calling the advisory "scare tactics" driven by liberal activists. The advisory cites concerns about immigration enforcement, racial profiling, suppression of speech, increased surveillance, and conditions in US detention facilities as potential risks. It recommends precautions such as securing electronic devices and brushing up on “know your rights” resources.

articles.title: BJP women cadre accuse Congress of blocking quota bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana BJP organized a women's protest march on Thursday evening, criticizing the Congress party for its perceived "hypocritical and anti-women stance" on women's reservation in legislatures. The march, which began at Domalguda and culminated in a public meeting at Indira Park, saw thousands of women party workers and supporters participate, with senior leaders like N. Ramchander Rao, G. Kishan Reddy, Bandi Sanjay Kumar, K. Laxman, D.K. Aruna, Eatala Rajender, Yeleti Maheswar Reddy, and Malka Komuraiah taking part.

articles.title: Italy slams Trump envoy proposal of taking Iran’s place in World Cup 2026 | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Paolo Zampolli, an Italian-American US envoy for global relations, suggested that Italy replace Iran in the 2026 World Cup.  Zampolli made the proposal to both Donald Trump and FIFA President Gianni Infantino. However, this suggestion was met with strong opposition from Italian officials, including Andrea Abodi, the Sports Minister, who stated that it is "not appropriate" for a team to be selected based on political considerations.  The idea has also been rejected by fans and other football figures in Italy.

articles.title: Congress questions EC notice to Kharge, alleges ulterior motives - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress officials have written to the Election Commission of India, questioning the issuance of a show-cause notice to party president Mallikarjun Kharge. They allege ulterior motives and a casual, routine manner in the notice's issuance. The letter, addressed to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and two other commissioners, also notes that two notices with the same reference number and date were issued but signed by different officials, leaving ambiguity about their status.

articles.title: Decapitating cartels? Mexico leans into ‘kingpin strategy’ but at a cost | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following the arrest of Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a surge in violence and disappearances has plagued Mexico.  The Sinaloa Cartel experienced a power struggle that led to increased homicides, femicides, and missing person reports. Activists like Maria Isabel Cruz, who works with Sabuesos Guerreras, have observed the rise in violence as a direct consequence of targeting cartel leaders alone. While pressure from the United States has driven Mexico's current president, Claudia Sheinbaum, to continue the "kingpin strategy," critics argue that it fails to address the root causes of the problem and only serves to appease US demands.  The strategy has also been criticized for failing to dismantle the criminal market, which continues to thrive due to high demand in the United States. The violence has extended beyond Sinaloa, impacting neighboring states like Sonora and Durango, and even seen an increase in femicides.

articles.title: KSRTC issues summer advisory for drivers, conductors - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) has issued a summer advisory to its drivers and conductors, urging them to prioritize staff welfare during the hot months. The advisory recommends carrying sufficient drinking water, consuming light food, and frequently drinking fluids to prevent fatigue, dehydration, and heat-related illnesses. The corporation also suggests keeping Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) on hand and consuming hydrating foods like buttermilk, coconut water, and fruits.

articles.title: US reclassifies some marijuana products as less dangerous drug | Drugs News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States Department of Justice reclassified state-licensed medical marijuana as a less dangerous drug, moving it from Schedule I to Schedule III on the federal government’s five-tier drug classification system. This change allows for research into the safety and efficacy of marijuana while maintaining that it does not legalize recreational or medical marijuana under federal law. The move reflects a broader trend away from heavy penalization of marijuana possession and aligns with growing acceptance of its use in states across the country.

articles.title: DoJ inspector general to audit department’s compliance with Epstein Files Transparency Act | Jeffrey Epstein | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US Department of Justice’s office of the inspector general (OIG) announced an audit of the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act. The audit will evaluate the justice department's processes for identifying, redacting, and releasing records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.  The review will also assess the department's guidance and processes for withholding material as required by the act. Pam Bondi, former attorney general, was subpoenaed by the House oversight committee regarding her handling of the Epstein investigation. However, the committee has been informed that Bondi will not be appearing for a scheduled deposition due to her removal from office.

articles.title: Anagha from Tirthahalli is second topper in SSLC exam-1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anagha K.S. of Vagdevi School in Tirthahalli achieved the second-highest score (624/625) in the SSLC examination, while Kruthi P.S. of Priyadarshini High School secured the third rank with a score of 623/625.  The district of Shivamogga recorded a pass percentage of 96.56%, placing it ninth in the state and marking an improvement from last year's fifth position. The students, who achieved high marks, expressed gratitude for their teachers and parents' support.

articles.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teenager in occupied West Bank raid | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces shot and killed a 15-year-old Palestinian teenager in Nablus, West Bank, during a raid. The incident occurred as the teenager was exiting the city with other Palestinians after being questioned by Israeli soldiers.  The Israeli military stated that the teenager was shot while throwing stones at their forces, but Palestinian officials say they are unaware of the reason for the shooting. This incident follows a surge in settler violence across the occupied Palestinian territory since October 2023, resulting in numerous deaths and destruction.

articles.title: Trump administration pushes DoJ to pursue denaturalization cases – report | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is reportedly pushing the Justice Department to pursue hundreds of denaturalization cases, aiming to strip citizenship from foreign-born US citizens. The department has identified 384 individuals who will be targeted in the coming weeks and plans to assign civil litigators across 39 regional offices to file these cases. Experts warn that this initiative could divert resources from other legal areas and raise concerns about its potential for political bias, similar to past instances where denaturalization was used to target activists and immigrants with flimsy evidence.  The US government can request the removal of citizenship status if someone illegally obtained it through fraud or misrepresentation.

articles.title: Bengaluru: Mental health session held for north-east division police personnel - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police officers and staff from four police stations in the north-east division participated in a special session on mental health and stress management. The session, led by Wazeera Begum, focused on key psychological challenges faced by police personnel, including occupational stress and unpredictable duty hours. Participants were trained in techniques to manage stress, improve decision-making skills, and build emotional resilience.  The program emphasized the importance of teamwork and peer support within the force, concluding with a message encouraging all personnel to prioritize their mental health.

articles.title: Iran dismisses Trump’s claim of leadership rift, says nation is ‘one soul’ | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf all rejected President Donald Trump's claims of a leadership rift in Tehran. They emphasized the nation's unity and obedience to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.  Iran maintains that diplomatic talks with the US are stalled due to American blockades on its ports, not disagreements within its government.

articles.title: LaGuardia firefighter heard ‘stop’ before crash but didn’t know who it was for, report says | New York | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: National Transportation Safety Board investigators determined that a fire truck collided with an Air Canada jet at LaGuardia airport on March 22nd, killing both pilots. The crash occurred after the fire truck crossed the runway despite warnings from air traffic controllers and a lack of functionality in the ASDE-X system which was supposed to prevent such incidents.  The incident involved a convoy of vehicles responding to an odor report in a United Airlines jet, with numerous flights arriving at LaGuardia during the busy night.

articles.title: State may witness close contests in many constituencies - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's high voter turnout has raised questions about the closeness of this year's election results.  The 2016 contest, with a margin of victory of just one percentage point between the ruling AIADMK and the DMK-led coalition, serves as a precedent for potential close races in 2023. The People's Welfare Front, Pattali Makkal Katchi, and Bharatiya Janata Party contested independently in 2016, contributing to a wider margin of victory for the AIADMK.  This year, the presence of C. Joseph Vijay, founder of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam, is expected to influence the outcome.

articles.title: Milei administration in Argentina blocks journalist access to Casa Rosada | Freedom of the Press News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The administration of Javier Milei, Argentina's president, has restricted access to the presidential palace, the Casa Rosada, for journalists.  Milei accused two journalists from the Argentinian channel TN of illegal espionage and threatened to silence them. The head of Argentina’s Secretariat of Communication and Press, Javier Lanari, stated that the decision was a preventive measure in response to a complaint filed by the Military Household. This action is part of a broader trend of restrictions on journalists under Milei, with critics citing a decline in press freedom since his presidency began.  Reporters Without Borders (RSF) and PEN International have both expressed concern about these policies.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Blocking press access and threatening journalists is a serious threat to freedom of the press.

articles.title: At least one dead and five people injured in Louisiana mall shooting, police say | Louisiana | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A shooting at the Mall of Louisiana in Baton Rouge left one person dead and five others injured. Police responded to reports of gunfire around 1:22 pm, finding two groups arguing before opening fire on each other.  The incident prompted a large police presence, with Baton Rouge Mayor Sid Edwards stating that authorities are seeking suspects with assistance from the FBI and ATF. Several people were taken into custody, and officials urged anyone with video footage to come forward.

articles.title: Telangana RTC strike | A transport system stuck in breakdown mode - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana State Road Transport Corporation (TGSRTC) has once again halted operations at its Mahatma Gandhi Bus Station (MGBS) due to a strike by its workers. The 32-demand strike, which began on April 22nd, is centered around the absorption of 40,000 employees into government service. This marks the second time in six years that public transport has been disrupted in Telangana, with the crisis persisting despite a change in political power.

articles.title: Meta lines up layoffs while Microsoft offers buyouts | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Meta announced it will lay off approximately 8,000 workers, representing about 10% of its workforce. The company cited the need for efficiency and investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure as reasons for the cuts. Microsoft, meanwhile, is offering voluntary buyouts to 8,750 US employees, or 7% of its workforce. This move comes amid a similar industry trend driven by increased spending on AI development and operations. Both companies are seeking to streamline operations and reduce costs while maintaining productivity.

articles.title: US justice department watchdog to review release of Jeffrey Epstein files – live | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice's watchdog announced an investigation into the DOJ's compliance with a law mandating the release of late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's investigative files. Yechiel Leiter, Israel's US-born ambassador, met with Lebanese counterpart in the Oval Office and thanked Trump for brokering a ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon.  Donald Trump announced that the ceasefire will be extended by three weeks. The president also said he would not use a nuclear weapon against Iran.

articles.title: US boards ship carrying Iran oil as Trump threatens mine-laying boats
articles.rephrased_article: The US Navy boarded a sanctioned ship carrying Iranian oil in the Indian Ocean, marking another naval move against Iran. President Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to "shoot and kill" any boats laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran claimed one US ship interception earlier this week was piracy. The blockade imposed by the US on maritime traffic entering and leaving Iranian ports has resulted in the return of 33 vessels to port.  Despite a ceasefire request from mediator Pakistan, Trump maintains his stance that Iran is "getting no business" while claiming the Strait of Hormuz is under complete US control.

articles.title: Indian-origin restaurant owner in North Carolina arrested for attempt to murder wife, daughter called 911 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mathivanan Pothiyappan, owner of the closed CholaNad Indian restaurant in North Carolina, is facing charges of attempted first-degree murder and assault on a female after a domestic violence incident with his wife. The incident occurred earlier this month when Pothiyappan chased his wife following an argument and threatened to kill her.  Pothiyappan was initially released on bond but later arrested again after the attempted murder charge was filed, with conditions including no contact with family and surrendering his passport.

articles.title: Thousands call on UK ministers to cut ties with US tech giant Palantir | Palantir | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Over 200,000 people have signed petitions calling for the UK government to end contracts with Palantir, a US tech company whose software is used by various organizations including ICE and the Israeli military.  Wes Streeting, the health secretary, has faced pressure to cancel its £330 million patient data contract with the NHS, while Matthew McGregor, from 38 Degrees, argues that Palantir's technology should not have access to sensitive UK data. The company is defending itself against criticism by using memes and social media posts, but faces continued calls for action from groups like Zack Polanski of the Green party and Jolyon Maugham of the Good Law Project.

articles.title: US sanctions Cambodian senator over purported scam network links | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Treasury Department announced sanctions against Cambodian Senator Kok An and 28 associates for their alleged involvement in a scam network that defrauds US citizens. The department accuses An of using his political influence to protect these fraudulent operations, which entice vulnerable Americans into transferring their savings through investment scams.  The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) stated that the fraudsters lure victims with promises of high returns and then steal their funds outright.

articles.title: ‘My body feels like lead’: Heat is making pregnancy a nightmare in Karachi - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: In Karachi, Pakistan, rising temperatures are exacerbating health issues for pregnant women and newborns.  Asiya, a 21-year-old expecting her third child, experiences debilitating heat exhaustion due to the city's intense summer heat, compounded by power outages and lack of ventilation in her home. This is not an isolated case; Savera, another young mother, faced similar challenges during her baby's first weeks after birth.  Rubina Hussain, a gynaecologist at Ziauddin University, highlights the disproportionate impact of heat on pregnant women, leading to dehydration complications and increased risks for preterm births and low birth weights. Grassroots organizations like Mama Baby Fund are stepping in to address these issues, providing essential care and resources to vulnerable communities like those on Baba Island, where residents face extreme heat, limited access to clean water, and inadequate healthcare infrastructure.

articles.title: Karnataka tobacco crop size cut to 56 million kg for 2026–27 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tobacco Board of Karnataka has significantly reduced the state's tobacco crop size for 2026-27 to 56 million kg, down from the earlier projection of 90 million kg. The decision was made at a meeting in Guntur on April 20th, influenced by geopolitical factors and market conditions driven by high tobacco yields in countries like Zimbabwe, Brazil, and Tanzania.

articles.title: Watch: 'Tomato juice' thrown at Iran's exiled crown prince Reza Pahlavi in Germany - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran's last Shah, was splashed with tomato juice in Berlin on Thursday while leaving a news briefing. The incident occurred shortly after he criticized the US-Iran ceasefire extension and called for more support from European countries for Iranian democracy advocates. Pahlavi claimed that the ceasefire assumes Tehran will change its behavior but believes diplomacy has been given enough chance.  Police detained the suspected attacker, whose identity was not disclosed.

articles.title: Foreign Office unit tracking Israel’s potential breaches of international law closes due to cuts | Foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Foreign Office has closed its international humanitarian law cell due to budget cuts, ending funding for the Conflict and Security Monitoring Project run by the Centre for information Resilience (CIR). The closure follows a review by Olly Robbins, the former permanent secretary who was dismissed last week.  This decision is part of a wider restructuring at the Foreign Office that has led to the closure of several teams, including the IHL cell, despite the ongoing violations of international law and atrocities committed in various regions. Critics argue this move undermines Britain's commitment to upholding international law and its obligations under arms export criteria.

articles.title: Will complex EU loan deal intensify conflict? | TV Shows | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine has received a multibillion-dollar loan from the European Union, despite ongoing conflict with Russia. The deal comes as Moscow benefits from increased oil revenue, potentially bolstering its war efforts.  The agreement's long-term viability is uncertain due to existing mistrust between the parties and the potential for escalation.

articles.title: KSE-100 plunges below 170,000-mark as bears maintain control of PSX - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX)'s benchmark index, KSE-100, experienced a significant drop of 2,405.93 points on Thursday, closing at 169,173.37 points after losing 1.4 percent. The decline was attributed to global market sentiment influenced by tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and uncertainty surrounding US-Iran peace talks. Topline Securities noted that trading activity remained subdued with volumes reaching 1.321 billion shares and turnover at Rs. 30.8 billion.

articles.title: 19-year-old worker kills newborn minutes after delivery in factory toilet in Bengaluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old woman, an operator at the Foxconn facility in Devanahalli, allegedly killed her premature newborn baby by slitting his throat and disposing of the body inside a factory toilet on Wednesday. The incident has shocked authorities in Bengaluru.

articles.title: Top 10 largest gold mines in the world: US, Uzbekistan, Russia and other global mining countries revealed | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The global gold mining industry saw production levels remain substantial in 2025, with Nevada Gold Mines, Muruntau, Olimpiada, Kazzinc Consolidated, and Grasberg among the largest producers.  Despite output fluctuations, Nevada Gold Mines remained the world's largest gold mining operation, while Muruntau in Uzbekistan took second place. Other notable mines included Olimpiada in Russia, Blagodatnoye in Russia, Detour Lake in Canada, Kibali in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Ahafo in Ghana.

articles.title: Baby died after NHS trust failed to warn mother of ‘unsafe’ home birth, coroner finds | NHS | The Guardian
articles.sentiment_target: Royal Free London NHS foundation trust
articles.rephrased_article: An inquest concluded that Poppy Hope Lomas, a seven-day-old baby, died from lack of oxygen in the 30 minutes before her birth after an unsafe home birth that went against medical advice. The senior coroner Andrew Walker found that Royal Free London NHS foundation trust failed to address "an accumulation of risk factors" despite agreeing to support Lomas's mother with the home delivery.  The inquest also highlighted concerns about the use of phrases like "out of guidance" instead of "against medical advice," prompting recommendations for improved communication and consent forms regarding risks associated with unsafe home births.

articles.title: War-driven demand boosts profits for weapons and aircraft manufacturers | Military News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, and RTX Corporation saw their first-quarter earnings impacted by geopolitical conflicts driving increased demand for defense products.  While Boeing reported a reduced loss, citing strong sales of F-35 fighter jets and space travel contributions, Lockheed Martin fell short of analyst expectations due to delays in the F-16 program and supply chain issues. Northrop Grumman experienced higher revenue driven by increased demand for its B-21 bomber and missile systems. RTX Corporation, parent company of Raytheon, also saw a boost in revenue due to increased demand for air and missile defense systems.

articles.title: KSE-100 plunges below 170,000-mark as bears maintain control of PSX - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX)'s benchmark index, KSE-100, experienced a significant decline on Thursday, dropping over 2,400 points.  Topline Securities attributed the losses to heightened geopolitical tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, including reports of vessel seizures and blockades, as well as uncertainty surrounding peace talks between Islamabad and Iran. Trading activity remained subdued with volumes at 1.321 million shares and turnover at Rs. 30.8 billion.

articles.title: Stalin commends people of T.N. for record voter turnout - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister M.K. Stalin commended the high voter turnout of 84.69% in Tamil Nadu, which he described as a testament to the people's sense of responsibility and peaceful election process.  He praised voters for their dedication despite the scorching heat and emphasized that this was an election for a generation. Mr. Stalin concluded by stating that Tamil Nadu will win on May 4th.

articles.title: N3On: Streamer N3on admits paying $1.4 million to clippers to make his content go viral - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: N3on, a popular streamer on Kick and YouTube, has revealed that he spends around $1.4 million to hire "clippers" who create short clips from his live streams for social media sharing. These clippers are part of a network of individuals in countries like India and Nigeria who are paid based on the views their clips receive. N3on believes this strategy is crucial to his online growth, as viral clips can significantly increase viewership even if the live stream itself doesn't have many viewers.

articles.title: ‘Toxic’ views of Reform UK candidates raise questions about party’s vetting | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A number of Reform UK candidates have been criticized for making offensive comments, including one who called for a “white Britain” and another who complained about “constant kowtowing to the black community.”  These remarks have raised doubts about the party's vetting processes. Nigel Farage, the Reform leader, has defended the party's vetting procedures, but Labour is using these comments in an upcoming election broadcast to highlight what they see as toxic views within the party.

articles.title: Pope decries migrants and refugees being treated ‘worse than house pets’ | Human Rights News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Leo condemned the mistreatment of migrants and refugees, stating they are often treated worse than house pets.  He emphasized that countries have a right to control their borders but urged wealthier nations to help develop countries where migrants originate, preventing them from leaving in search of better lives. Pope Leo also criticized the killing of Iranian protesters by the Iranian government, calling it unjust and condemning all actions that take human life. He defended his decision to visit authoritarian leaders' countries, stating the Vatican maintains diplomatic relations with those governments and works behind the scenes to promote justice.

articles.title: Iran's economy looks set to withstand US naval blockade - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: US naval blockade of Iranian ports is likely to impact Iran's oil output in the coming weeks, but analysts say it may not lead to a complete economic collapse.  The US imposed the counter-blockade in response to Iran's Strait of Hormuz blockade, aiming to force peace talks. However, experts predict that Iran will experience storage capacity limitations within a month or two and may be forced to reduce production. While some analysts believe this could lead to financial strain on Iran, others suggest its resilience and ability to withstand previous sanctions make it unlikely to compromise easily.  The situation remains fluid as the US and Iran continue negotiations and economic pressures mount.

articles.title: Pahalgam, a year on: Resilience falters, tourism struggles - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The 2025 attack on the Baisaran meadow in Pahalgam, Kashmir, has significantly impacted tourism and livelihoods. The incident resulted in the closure of several tourist destinations, including Baisaran, Dabyan, and Chandanwari, leading to job losses for locals who relied on tourism-related businesses.  The Jammu and Kashmir Cable Car Corporation (JKCCC) is planning a cable car project connecting the meadow with the Yatri Niwas hotel to attract pilgrims during the Amarnath Yatra. Security measures have been intensified in Pahalgam, including facial recognition technology at tourist destinations. The attack has also led to a decline in tourism footfall and financial hardship for hotels and businesses that relied on the influx of visitors.  Mehraj Din Wani, an ATV owner, expressed concerns about the long-term impact on local livelihoods.

articles.title: US identifies 384 foreign-born Americans who will soon lose citizenship: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Donald Trump administration is intensifying its efforts to denaturalize individuals who obtained US citizenship through fraudulent means.  Matthew Tragesser, a Justice Department spokesman, stated that the department is pursuing the highest volume of denaturalization referrals in history from the Department of Homeland Security. The plan involves assigning civil litigators across 39 regional offices to file denaturalization cases against identified individuals.
