The assessment found that rural areas were most severely impacted, with agriculture being the hardest hit sector.  The ILO recommended a package of recovery measures, including cash-for-work programs and skills training, to help restore livelihoods in flood-affected areas. Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain acknowledged the severe impact on livelihoods, particularly for self-employed workers, daily wage earners, small farmers, and vulnerable households. He pledged support from his ministry, along with provincial governments, social partners, and development partners, to ensure targeted employment recovery programs are implemented.

articles.title: Archaeologists find world’s oldest beer receipt and decode the surprising message written on it | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Researchers from the National Museum of Denmark and the University of Copenhagen have identified what may be the world's oldest known beer receipt, dating back 4,000 years. The clay tablet, part of a cuneiform collection, details supplies delivered by a man named Ayalli to workers in the Sumerian city of Umma. This discovery highlights how early writing systems were used to manage trade and labor, offering insights into everyday life during that period.  The inscription records 16 liters of high-quality beer and 55 liters of ordinary beer, suggesting it was likely used as wages or rations for workers in the ancient city. The findings challenge popular notions about early writing, emphasizing its practical applications beyond literature and royal decrees.

articles.title: EU court rules Hungary’s LGBTQ law violates human rights | LGBTQ News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The European Court of Justice ruled that Hungary's 2021 anti-LGBTQ legislation violates EU law, deeming it contrary to the bloc’s values and principles. The ruling, hailed as a landmark decision, was launched by the European Commission alongside 16 member states and the European Parliament.  The court found the legislation infringed on Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU), impacting the rights of transgender and non-heterosexual individuals. The Hungarian government has been urged to implement the decision.

articles.title: Middle East crisis live: US-Iran talks in doubt as JD Vance’s Pakistan trip reportedly on hold | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: JD Vance's trip to Islamabad has been halted after Iran failed to meet US negotiating terms.  The White House is awaiting a signal that Iran's negotiators are willing to sign a deal. President Trump expressed his intention to resume bombing Iran as the ceasefire nears its end, stating he believes it would be a better attitude and that the US is in a strong negotiating position. The US will host ambassador-level talks with Israel and Lebanon on Thursday, but the objective remains unclear.  Iran has arrested over 3,600 people for alleged involvement in the war. A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah has been in place since April 8th, but tensions remain high.

articles.title: T.N. government extends ban on mayonnaise for another year - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government extended a one-year ban on the manufacture, processing, and sale of mayonnaise made with raw eggs, citing health risks associated with foodborne illnesses like Salmonella. The order, issued by the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration, is based on the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and aims to prevent potential contamination from bacteria such as Salmonella typhimurium, Salmonella enteritidis, Escherichia coli, and Listeria monocytogenes.

articles.title: Around 3.3 million jobs may have been affected by 2025 floods in Pakistan: ILO - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The International Labour Organisation (ILO), a specialized UN agency, has assessed the impact of the 2025 floods in Pakistan and estimates that approximately 3.3 million jobs may have been affected. The assessment found that rural areas were most impacted by employment losses, with agriculture being the hardest hit sector.  Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development Minister Chaudhry Salik Hussain stated that targeted recovery measures are needed to help communities rebuild their lives and income sources. The ILO Country Director for Pakistan Geir Tonstol emphasized the need for timely measures to support decent work and income recovery, while also advocating for a revived World of Work Crisis Response Strategy for future disaster responses.

articles.title: 'Release these women': Trump's offer to Iran for 'good start to negotiations' after military warning - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump urged Iran to release eight women facing execution, stating it would be a "great start" to negotiations.  Trump expressed his desire for the release and warned of potential military action if talks fail. While both sides are expected to resume ceasefire talks in Pakistan, neither has confirmed the meeting's details. Trump stated he opposes extending the truce and emphasized Iran must negotiate.

articles.title: Israeli sexual violence helping push Palestinians from West Bank: Report | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A new report from the West Bank Protection Consortium reveals at least 16 cases of conflict-related sexual violence attributed to Israeli settlers and soldiers in the occupied West Bank. The report, "Sexual Violence And Forcible Transfer In The West Bank: How The Exploitation Of Gender Dynamics Drives Displacement," found that threats of sexual violence are a major reason for Palestinians leaving their homes.  The consortium interviewed 83 Palestinians from across ten communities and found that over 70% cited these threats as the decisive factor in their decision to leave. Israeli soldiers were often present during these incidents but failed to intervene or investigate, according to the report. This has led rights groups to condemn the recent reinstatement of five soldiers accused of sexual assault despite an ongoing internal military inquiry into their conduct.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The report details sexual violence as a tool for displacement, a serious human rights abuse.

articles.title: Martin Scorsese’s film about Pope Francis to receive world premiere in Vatican City | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Martin Scorsese's documentary, "Aldeas, The Final Dream of Pope Francis," had its world premiere in the Vatican today as part of events commemorating the first anniversary of Pope Francis' death.  The film, co-directed by Scorsese and Johnny Shipley and Clare Tavernor, features an in-depth interview with the late pope and outlines Scholas Occurrentes, an organization founded by Francis while he was Archbishop of Buenos Aires, which promotes social integration through arts and technology. The screening comes amid heightened tensions between the US government and the papacy following Pope Leo's criticism of the US and Israel's attack on Iran.

articles.title: APPSC candidates for Assistant Professor posts demand justice over stalled recruitment - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Assistant Professor candidates who qualified the 2017-18 examination have accused the State government of discrimination in the handling of recruitment-related court proceedings. They allege that the interview process was abruptly halted without explanation, and that previous government affidavits supporting legal challenges to the recruitment notifications led to cancellation of the process. The association leaders also claim officials failed to present key information regarding reservation rules and University Grants Commission (UGC) guidelines.  They are urging Minister for Education Nara Lokesh to intervene and ensure justice for qualified candidates.

articles.title: Notification declaring local holiday in Rawalpindi on April 22 is fake: DC - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Rawalpindi's Deputy Commissioner Hassan Waqar Cheema refuted a fake notification claiming a local holiday for April 22, urging the public to rely on official sources.  This follows similar dismissals of fake notifications by Islamabad's DC Irfan Nawaz Memon, who also addressed closures in anticipation of US-Iran talks scheduled in Islamabad.

articles.title: US embassy workers killed in Chihuahua, Mexican president says she had no idea what they were doing - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Claudia Sheinbaum, the president of Mexico, stated that she was unaware of a joint operation involving US officials in Chihuahua that resulted in the deaths of two individuals. César Jáuregui, the Chihuahua Attorney General, confirmed that four officials died after their car crashed into a ravine while returning from an operation to destroy clandestine drug labs. The identities of the deceased US officials have not been released but were reported by the New York Times as members of the CIA.  Ronald Johnson, the US ambassador to Mexico, expressed condolences for the deaths and highlighted the risks faced by those working in security efforts.

articles.title: What’s the bill to rebuild Gaza, and who will pay? | Gaza | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A new report by the United Nations and European Union estimates that rebuilding Gaza will require $71 billion over 10 years. The report highlights the need for restoring essential services, with about a third of the total cost allocated to this purpose.  The report raises questions about how Gaza will be rebuilt and who will ultimately bear the financial burden.

articles.title: UK agriculture deal with EU will not remove all red tape, peers told
articles.rephrased_article: The House of Lords heard that a new agriculture agreement with the EU may benefit sales of Scottish shellfish, such as langoustines and oysters. Although the agreement will not erase all Brexit paperwork, it is expected to have "modest" impact on the UK economy and could reduce trade barriers.

articles.title: APPSC candidates for Assistant Professor posts demand justice over stalled recruitment - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Assistant Professor candidates who qualified the 2017–18 examination have accused the State government of discrimination in recruitment proceedings. articles.title: Iran foreign ministry spokesperson says Tehran yet to decide on participating in talks with US in Islamabad - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has not yet decided whether to participate in peace talks with the United States in Pakistan.  The Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baghaei, criticized US actions against Iranian vessels and questioned Washington's commitment to diplomacy. Meanwhile, Pakistani officials are awaiting a formal response from Iran regarding its participation in the second round of talks. The ceasefire between the US and Iran, which was supposed to expire on Tuesday, has been extended until Wednesday evening.  US President Donald Trump expressed confidence in securing a favorable deal with Iran, but also indicated his willingness to resume attacks if no agreement is reached.

articles.title: $97 million wine fraud scheme: UK citizen sentenced to 10 years in US for defrauding 140 people worldwide - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: James Wellesley, a UK citizen, was sentenced to 10 years in prison for his role in a multi-million dollar fraud scheme that tricked investors into funding a fake fine wine business.  The scheme defrauded over 140 victims worldwide of more than $97 million. Wellesley, who used aliases "Andrew Fuller" and "Andrew Templar", was ordered to forfeit $1 million and restitution will be determined at a later date. The FBI stated that Wellesley spoiled the reputation of the prestigious wine industry and his co-conspirator, Stephen Burton, is awaiting sentencing for his role in the scheme.

articles.title: The US exit from Syria, explained | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States has withdrawn its troops from Syria, ending a decade-long presence.  This decision comes as power dynamics shift on the ground and Kurdish forces grapple with new realities. The future of Syria remains uncertain amidst regional tensions and fragile negotiations.

articles.title: Albanians in UK scapegoated by rightwing media and politicians, says ambassador | Immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Uran Ferizi, the Albanian ambassador to Britain, criticized Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, for singling out Albanians in parliament when discussing immigration issues. He argued that negative portrayals of Albanians in media and by politicians have negatively impacted the community, including workers, families, and schoolchildren.  Ferizi cited examples of discrimination against Albanian individuals in workplaces and social settings, citing a case where an Albanian woman was asked about her background at a work function after being labeled as "criminal" due to news reports. He also criticized selective statistics used by media outlets that amplify negative narratives about Albanians, particularly when elections are approaching.

articles.title: EU credibility is on the line over Israel, says Spanish foreign minister | Russia-Ukraine war | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Spanish foreign minister warned that the European Union risks losing credibility if it doesn't apply consistent principles to Israel's actions in the Middle East, particularly its ongoing conflict with Palestinians. The minister urged a unified stance, citing human rights clauses in the EU-Israel agreement and criticizing violence in Gaza, the West Bank, and Lebanon.

articles.title: Govt actively pursuing diversified capital markets strategy, finmin tells EU envoy - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met with EU Ambassador Raimundas Karoblis to discuss Pakistan's efforts to strengthen its capital markets and attract foreign investment.  The meeting focused on the recent successful upsizing of a Eurobond transaction, which signals improved economic fundamentals. The finance minister emphasized the government’s commitment to sustainable financing and highlighted upcoming opportunities for international issuances and innovative financing instruments. Aurangzeb also accepted an invitation to participate in the high-level EU–Pakistan Business Forum, where he will deliver a keynote address on "Pakistan Rising: Incentives, Reforms, and the Next Investment Frontier."

articles.title: 'Thought I had understanding with Xi': Trump says ship seized by US had 'gift from China' for Iran - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced that the US seized a ship on Monday, calling it a "gift from China" and stating it contained items he deemed "not very nice."  He made these remarks while discussing tensions with Iran, including his threat to bomb Iranian bridges.  Trump also stated that he does not want to extend the current ceasefire with Iran and expects a "great deal" with the country.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Government college, fair price for betel leaves prominent demands in Paramathi Velur constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Paramathi Velur constituency in Tamil Nadu is known for its agricultural activities, particularly sugarcane cultivation and jaggery production. Residents are advocating for improved facilities, including a government college and a knowledge center, as well as better prices for betel leaves.  A. Kumaraguru, S. Sridhar, M. Rajendran, and other residents have voiced their concerns to the local representatives, who are preparing for a four-cornered contest in the upcoming election.

articles.title: Decision on EU’s €90bn loan for Ukraine ‘due in next 24 hours’ after Zelenskyy says oil pipeline repaired – Europe live | Europe | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The EU's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, says a positive decision on the €90 billion loan for Ukraine could be reached within 24 hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that all necessary steps have been taken. The Druzhba pipeline transporting oil to Hungary and Slovakia has been repaired and can resume operations.  Hungary's outgoing and incoming prime ministers suggested that Ukraine should stop political games and restart the pipeline, while Slovakia's prime minister also recommended this sequence of events. articles.title: Israeli soldiers and settlers kill 11 Palestinians across Gaza, West Bank | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli soldiers and settlers have killed at least 11 Palestinians across Gaza and the occupied West Bank, according to Palestinian officials. In Gaza, a series of attacks by Israel resulted in the deaths of seven Palestinians, including a child who died from injuries sustained days earlier.  In the West Bank, four Palestinians were killed in an attack on an al-Mughayyir school by Israeli settlers and another was killed during a raid on the Jenin refugee camp by Israeli forces. The violence has continued despite a ceasefire announced in October.

articles.title: SC to function with minimal staff on Wednesday; no judicial work to be conducted at FCC for 2nd consecutive day - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan will operate with minimal staff at its Islamabad headquarters on Wednesday, while the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC) in Islamabad will remain closed for a second consecutive day due to security measures related to anticipated US-Iran peace talks. The Supreme Court issued a notification stating that only essential personnel would be present and those working remotely would stay connected with their supervisors.  The FCC also announced the cancellation of its cause list on Wednesday, citing similar security concerns.

articles.title: 'Make it hard for them to live, procreate': Greg Bovino says there are 100 million illegals in US and 'they all need to go' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Greg Bovino, a former US Border Patrol commander, has called for drastic measures to deter undocumented immigration. He suggests making it difficult for these individuals to live, work, and procreate in the United States, urging them to self-deport.  Bovino's comments come after his controversial tenure under President Trump and a recent incident involving ICE agents that led to the deaths of two US citizens. His views have drawn criticism for their potential to incite violence and promote racial hatred.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Powerloom weavers caught in a web of woes in Aruppukottai constituency - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The DMK candidate, K.K.S.S.R. Ramachandran, is facing a challenge in the Aruppukottai Assembly constituency from AIADMK's S. Sethupathy and other candidates like K. Manimaran (Naam Tamilar Katchi), K. Raghupathi (Puthiya Tamilagam) K. Karthik Kumar (TVK) and Dharmaraj (AIPTMMK).  The traditional weaving industry in the region is facing issues such as a lack of effluent treatment plants, frequent raids under the Handlooms Act, and limited marketing opportunities. The town's infrastructure has seen improvements with new roads and drainage facilities, but farmers are concerned about shrinking agricultural land due to pollution from nearby towns.

articles.title: Blue Origin rocket grounded after satellite 'mishap'
articles.rephrased_article: Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket was grounded after a failed launch of an AST SpaceMobile satellite, causing the company to halt its planned dozen launches this year. The FAA ordered an investigation into the incident, which resulted in the satellite not reaching its intended orbit. Dave Limp, Blue Origin's chief executive, stated that the failure was due to insufficient thrust and that the company is working with the FAA to determine corrective actions.

articles.title: Death of Sydney’s ‘birdman’ described as ‘beyond tragic’ by Albanese government | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Federal and state housing ministers expressed deep concern over the death of a young homeless man in Sydney's Hyde Park, highlighting gaps in services for non-resident individuals with expired visas.  The death of Bikram Lama, who came to Australia seeking better opportunities, has brought attention to the challenges faced by those without residency status who are unable to access crucial support systems like housing and healthcare. Clare O’Neil, federal housing minister, emphasized the need for collaboration between government agencies and community organizations to prevent such tragedies.  Rose Jackson, New South Wales housing and homelessness minister, acknowledged the gaps in services for non-residents but pledged to work with advocates to address them. Both City of Sydney and St Vincent's have been advocating for increased support for this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Iran’s World Cup participation depends on team’s safety in the US: Minister | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s team is preparing for the FIFA World Cup, but its participation hinges on the government guaranteeing the players' safety in the US. articles.title: Health minister says medicine stocks sufficient to meet demand for next 5 to 6 months - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

articles.title: 'Military raring to go': Trump outlines US response if Iran fails to make deal before truce ends - The Times of India

Trump expressed his disapproval of extending the ceasefire beyond its deadline.

articles.title: Summer showers bring relief to residents in Kerala; heat, humid weather to continue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Isolated spells of heavy rain brought much-needed relief from the sweltering summer heat to parts of Kerala on Tuesday, with some areas experiencing rainfall exceeding 5 cm.  The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts isolated showers will continue for the next four days due to a trough/wind discontinuity running from North Chhattisgarh to the Comorin area. While these showers offer respite, the oppressive heat and humidity are expected to persist in most of the state, with temperatures exceeding 40°C in some areas.

articles.title: Nigeria monarch's abduction in Kwara: Police arrest miners
articles.rephrased_article: Police in western Nigeria have arrested 42 suspected illegal miners as part of an investigation into the abduction of Oba Salman Olatunji Aweda, the ruler of the Olayinka community. articles.title: Uber driver Michael was assaulted by passengers. He says the platform’s response added insult to injury | Industrial relations | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Uber drivers are facing unfair deactivations, leading to financial hardship and concerns about worker safety. The situation has prompted complaints to the Fair Work Commission and calls for greater transparency and accountability from Uber.  The company claims to prioritize driver and rider safety but faces criticism for its automated system that deactivates drivers without proper investigation.

articles.title: Rabbi accused of war crimes selected for Israel’s national celebration | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rabbi Avraham Zarbiv, a controversial figure accused of war crimes in Gaza, has been selected to light one of the torches at Israel's Independence Day ceremony. articles.title: Tata Investment Q4 Results: Profit jumps 69% YoY to Rs 64 crore; co declares Rs 3.4 dividend - The Economic Times

articles.title: Health minister says medicine stocks sufficient to meet demand for next 5 to 6 months - Pakistan - DAWN.COM

articles.title: New update on Indian-origin man who changed name to remain in US: Judge revokes citizenship of Gurdev Singh Sohal - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Justice filed a civil denaturalization complaint against Gurdev Singh Sohal, who changed his identity to obtain US citizenship in 2005. articles.title: Police suspect wider links in baby selling racket in Krishna District - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Krishna district police are investigating a child kidnapping and selling ring that was busted on April 17th. The investigation is focusing on potential links to other cases, financial details, contacts with staff at hospitals and maternity homes, and the role of an auto driver involved in the operation.  Police are also monitoring the movements of previously arrested suspects.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Child kidnapping and selling is a serious crime indicating institutional failure.

articles.title: Iran sees mass redundancies from war with US and Israel
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has experienced a massive wave of redundancies across various sectors following the conflict with the US and Israel.  The Deputy Work and Social Security Minister stated that two million people have lost their jobs, while other reports indicate widespread layoffs in manufacturing, retail, import/export, and the digital sector. The Iranian government's internet blackout since the war has also negatively impacted the tech and digital sectors, costing the economy over $1.8 billion.  The conflict has disrupted supply chains, leading to factory closures and job losses in industries like car manufacturing and steel production.

articles.title: Carney names broad team to advise on tense US-Canada trade talks | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Mark Carney, Canada's prime minister, has established a 24-member advisory committee to prepare for upcoming trade negotiations with the United States. The committee includes former Conservative leaders Erin O’Toole and Lisa Raitt, as well as former provincial premiers PJ Akeeagok and Jean Charest, and former Canadian high commissioner to the United Kingdom Ralph Goodale.  The committee will meet on April 27th, with the prime minister emphasizing the need to diversify away from reliance on the US. articles.title: Nigeria charges six people with ‘terrorism’, treason over 2025 coup plot | African Union News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Nigeria has charged six military officers with "terrorism" and treason for allegedly plotting to overthrow President Bola Tinubu. The suspects, including a retired major-general and a serving police inspector, were arrested in 2025 over alleged acts of indiscipline and breaches of service regulations.  The government initially denied the existence of a coup plot but later announced that the military would try several officers for planning to overthrow the government.

articles.title: 76% of UK universities report drop in Indian students as international enrolments fall 31% ahead of new visa rules | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: UK universities are experiencing a decline in international student enrollments, particularly from India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. articles.title: ‘Not a personal attack’: gun lobby targets marginal Labor seats at NSW election over post-Bondi reforms | New South Wales politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian Recreation Union (ARU), a gun users' group, plans to campaign against Labor candidates in the 2027 New South Wales election who support current firearm laws enacted after the Bondi terror attack. The ARU has not disclosed any formal campaign support to either the Liberal or National parties.

articles.title: Mass trial for 486 alleged MS-13 gang members begins in El Salvador
articles.rephrased_article: A mass trial of 486 suspected members of the MS-13 gang has begun in El Salvador, with the attorney general's office claiming they committed over 47,000 crimes between 2012 and 2022. UN experts have criticized the use of mass trials for undermining the right to defense and presumption of innocence.  The trial comes amidst a controversial state of emergency in El Salvador that has led to thousands of arrests, but human rights groups argue it has resulted in arbitrary detentions. The attorney general's office claims the MS-13 structure has instilled fear and grief in Salvadorean families and charges them with crimes including femicide, disappearances, and rebellion.

articles.title: Pakistan says formal response from Iran regarding participation in 2nd round of talks ‘still awaited’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that a formal response from Iran regarding its participation in the second round of peace talks with the United States is still pending.  The ceasefire between the US and Iran, which was supposed to end on Tuesday evening, has been extended to Wednesday evening. US President Donald Trump expressed confidence in achieving a favorable deal with Iran, but also indicated his willingness to resume attacks if a deal isn't reached soon. Meanwhile, Iranian officials have criticized what they perceive as US inconsistencies and violations of the ceasefire agreement.

articles.title: Why is the EU under pressure to suspend its trade agreement with Israel? | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: European Union foreign ministers are meeting to discuss the bloc's relationship with Israel and whether or not to suspend its trade agreement.  Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia have requested a reconsideration of the suspension, arguing that the EU must uphold human rights commitments. However, countries like Germany, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are reluctant to take drastic steps, making full suspension unlikely in the near future. The debate stems from growing unease over Israel's conduct in the occupied Palestinian territories, including its treatment of Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank.  The EU-Israel Association Agreement, which grants Israel preferential access to EU markets, is at the heart of the controversy due to a human rights clause that critics argue justifies suspension. The agreement has been called into question by numerous governments, human rights groups, and citizens who have condemned Israel's actions.

articles.title: Indian man living in US on student visa convicted of scamming elderly man posing as federal staff - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Venkateswara Chagamreddy, a 27-year-old Indian man on a student visa in Texas, was convicted of defrauding a 79-year-old Vietnam veteran in Delaware County. The victim was tricked into transferring gold to Chagamreddy after being told his identity had been stolen and he needed to cooperate with federal authorities.  Chagamreddy acted as a courier for the scam, traveling across states to collect gold from victims and delivering it to co-conspirators. Evidence presented at trial showed that Chagamreddy was in contact with numerous elderly individuals who were targeted by the scheme.

articles.title: Timor-Leste parliament questions president over proposed resort’s links to ‘scam’ empire | Timor-Leste | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Timor-Leste’s opposition has raised concerns about the foreign investment in a proposed cryptocurrency resort, questioning how prime beachfront real estate was obtained and why a Chinese businessman received a diplomatic passport. Fretilin MP Florentino Ximenes da Costa criticized the involvement of Prince Group, a Cambodian conglomerate accused by US authorities of running scams, and urged President José Ramos-Horta to explain his decision to grant diplomatic credentials to Lin Xiaofan. The opposition called for an investigation into how the resort obtained land near the airport and whether local actors were involved.

articles.title: Role of US officials killed in Mexico crash under scrutiny
articles.rephrased_article: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has ordered an investigation into the role of two US officials in a counter-narcotics operation that resulted in their deaths. The officials, described as "instructor officers" from the US embassy, were traveling back from destroying illegal drug labs when their car crashed and exploded.  Sheinbaum stated that neither she nor senior members of the federal security team had been informed about any joint US-Mexican operations. She emphasized Mexico's sovereignty and stressed that intelligence sharing with the US does not include joint operations on Mexican soil without prior approval at the federal level.

articles.title: Candidates wrap up last-minute efforts to woo voters as campaigning draws to a close in northern districts of T.N. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Candidates from various political parties across Tamil Nadu concluded intense campaigning for the April 23 Assembly elections in Cuddalore, Villupuram, and Kallakurichi districts.  Chief Minister M.K. Stalin and AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami addressed rallies in the three districts.  Sitting Ministers M.R.K. Panneerselvam and C.V. Ganesan, along with former minister C.Ve. Shanmugam and DMDK general secretary Premallatha Vijayakant, are among those vying for political positions. The Election Commission (EC) has instructed all outsiders, including party workers and functionaries, to leave the constituencies immediately.

articles.title: Trump says he opposes extending Iran ceasefire amid talks uncertainty | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated he opposes extending a ceasefire with Iran, which is set to expire by the end of Wednesday.  He believes Iran has no choice but to attend talks in Pakistan and accept a "great" deal, despite uncertainty surrounding the negotiations. The US president also threatened military action against Iran, claiming it would hurt them militarily if they continue their defiance.

articles.title: Pakistan says formal response from Iran regarding participation in 2nd round of talks ‘still awaited’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar stated that a formal response from Iran regarding its participation in the second round of peace talks with the United States is still awaited.  The ceasefire between the US and Iran, which was supposed to expire on Tuesday, April 21st, has now been extended until Wednesday evening. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar urged both sides to consider extending the ceasefire and engage in dialogue. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump expressed confidence in a favorable deal with Iran, while also threatening renewed attacks if no agreement is reached soon.  The US delegation is expected to arrive in Islamabad for the second round of talks, but an official announcement from Iran regarding its participation has not been made.

articles.title: Groww's Ishan Bansal sees structural shift in derivatives participation post regulatory changes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bansal, the CEO of a financial services company, reported that FY25 regulatory changes impacted F&O revenues, which were lower last year but rebounded in the current quarter due to heightened volatility. The company's equity derivatives penetration has decreased from 18% to nearly 10%, but growth is expected through increased customer numbers and activity levels as younger investors adopt derivatives alongside equities.  He noted that while the recent Securities Transaction Tax (STT) increase hasn't significantly impacted trading volumes yet, the long-term impact remains unclear. Bansal also highlighted the company's focus on expanding segments like margin trading facility (MTF), commodities, and wealth management, which are expected to contribute more to revenue in the future.

articles.title: Chinese national arrested for photographing US ‘doomsday’ plane without permission, says it was for ‘personal collection’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tianrui Liang, a 21-year-old Chinese national, was arrested at New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport on April 7th for violating federal law by photographing restricted military aircraft at Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska.  The FBI investigation began after a witness reported seeing Liang near the base with a telescopic lens and he later admitted to taking photographs of several aircraft, including the E-4B, often referred to as the "doomsday plane."  Liang claimed his images were for personal collection but investigators believe he was aware of the restrictions. He had plans to continue photographing military sites, including at Tinker Air Force Base in Oklahoma.

articles.title: Student allegedly jailed in China for six years after taking part in pro-democracy protests in Australia | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian government has been urged to take stronger action to protect Chinese international students from political repression following the alleged imprisonment of a student who participated in pro-democracy protests.  Human rights advocates, including Maya Wang, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch, argue that China's focus on suppressing activism within its borders has shifted overseas, targeting students who migrate to democratic countries. Universities Australia and the Department of Education have declined to comment on whether existing guidelines would be updated to address political repression against students.  Shadow home affairs and immigration minister Jonno Duniam expressed concern over the case and called for stronger safeguards against foreign interference in universities.

articles.title: Israeli soldiers punished over vandalism of Jesus statue in Lebanon
articles.rephrased_article: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) announced that two Israeli soldiers involved in the vandalism of a Jesus statue in Lebanon will face 30 days of military detention. The soldiers, who have not been named, were also removed from combat duty. Six other soldiers present at the scene but who did not intervene will be dealt with separately. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu expressed his "stunned and saddened" reaction to the incident.

articles.title: Documentary illuminates ‘Rasanishpathi’ through Kathakali - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Harish K.M., a Professor of Sound Engineering at the Film and Television Institute of India, Pune, has released a one-hour documentary titled "Rasanishpathi" exploring the concept of Rasa through the lens of Kathakali performance. The film, which features visuals by Manesh Madhavan and sound design by Madhu Apsara, follows two young women undergoing intensive training in Kathakali.  The documentary was screened at Kairali Sree Theatre in Kozhikode recently, with Harish expressing his happiness to present the work and its reception.

articles.title: Pakistan races against time to get Iran back to US talks as truce end nears | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan is racing against time to convince Iran to rejoin talks with the United States aimed at ending their war.  The US has recently taken actions that have injected skepticism into Islamabad's peacemaking efforts, despite Pakistani officials remaining cautiously hopeful. The situation is further complicated by public statements from Iran, which insists it will not negotiate under threat and demands an end to the US naval blockade of its oil exports.  US President Donald Trump has set firm red lines for Iran, including a halt to uranium enrichment and surrender of existing stockpiles. A second round of talks is expected to begin on Wednesday, but Iran's delegation's attendance remains uncertain. The outcome of these negotiations could have devastating consequences for both countries.

articles.title: Nigeria coup plot: Six people charged with treason over attempt to overthrow President Tinubu
articles.rephrased_article: Nigeria's Attorney General filed treason charges against six individuals, including a retired major general and a serving police inspector, for allegedly attempting to overthrow President Bola Tinubu in a coup last year. The defendants are accused of conspiring with one another to levy war against the state and destabilize the country.  The charges also include terrorism and money laundering, with prosecutors alleging that the defendants had prior knowledge of the alleged plot but failed to inform authorities. Col Mohammed Alhassan Ma'aji, who was arrested alongside other accomplices, is believed to have led the coup attempt.

articles.title: Kremlin forcing big firms to join ‘witch-hunt’ against internet rebels, claims report | Russia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Russian companies, including T-Bank, Sberbank, Yandex, and VKontakte, are actively collecting data on VPN users through their apps.  The investigation by RKS global, an advocacy group for internet freedoms, found that 22 of these apps detect VPN usage and retain the data in their servers. This new level of surveillance raises concerns about privacy and potential criminal penalties for VPN users in Russia. Authorities are increasingly using VPN data to track and prosecute individuals who circumvent online controls imposed by the Kremlin.

articles.title: Azerbaijan says it is ready to supply LNG to Pakistan - Business - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: SOCAR, Azerbaijan's state energy company, is prepared to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Pakistan upon request. The agreement between SOCAR Trading and Pakistan LNG Limited (PLL) allows for direct purchases of LNG under an accelerated procedure.  Pakistan faces a growing energy shortfall due to declining domestic production and global price fluctuations.

articles.title: Two-sun planets keep disappearing: Here’s why scientists point to Einstein | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's Kepler Space Telescope discovered several circumbinary planets, which orbit two stars simultaneously.  These planets disappear from observation due to orbital precession, a slow rotation of their orbits caused by the gravitational influence of the two stars. Einstein's theory of relativity explains this phenomenon as massive bodies can "curve" space-time, altering the motions of other bodies in their vicinity. This curvature causes oscillations in a planet's orbital plane, leading to temporary visibility changes and eventual disappearance from observation until their orbits align again.  Scientists are now able to forecast these events using Einstein's theories and advanced technology.

articles.title: International delegates to visit T.N. for observing polling process on April 23 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delegates from 17 countries, including representatives of their foreign missions in New Delhi and the International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (IDEA), will visit Tamil Nadu on April 22nd and 23rd to observe the polling process. The International Election Visitors’ Programme (IEVP) is a flagship program of the Election Commission of India aimed at international cooperation and engagement with other countries' election management bodies.  The delegates will witness the dispatch and distribution centers, district control rooms, media monitoring centers, and actual polling on April 23rd.

articles.title: Shot by Israeli forces, Hala, 18 and Mohammad, 13 fight for their lives | Child Rights | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Hala Salem Darwish, an 18-year-old bride-to-be in Gaza, and Mohammad Saber al-Sheikh, a 13-year-old boy in the West Bank, remain hospitalized after being shot in the head by Israeli snipers.  Hala was preparing dinner when she was shot near a UNRWA clinic, while Mohammad was playing football when he was struck during an Israeli raid on the Jalazone refugee camp. The shootings highlight the persistent violence faced by Palestinian youth across the occupied Palestinian territory.  The incidents come amid a surge in Israeli violence against Palestinians, including the killing of 16-year-old Mohammad Majdi al-Jabari in Hebron and attacks that have resulted in the deaths of at least seven Palestinians, including a child. International humanitarian organizations have reported that Israeli soldiers are using sexual abuse to pressure Palestinians into leaving their homes.

articles.title: Unprecedented ruling finds Hungary's anti-LGBTQ laws in breach of EU values
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union's top court ruled that Hungary's anti-LGBTQ laws violate EU values and breach its rules. The ruling, considered historic in its symbolism, found the law interfered with rights such as freedom of expression and discrimination based on sex or sexual orientation.  The Hungarian government, led by Viktor Orbán, passed the legislation in 2021, arguing it protected children from harmful influences. The ruling comes after a change in leadership following a recent election, with new Prime Minister Péter Magyar promising to reverse the law and adopt a more pro-European approach.

articles.title: ‘The witches are back’: first look at Practical Magic 2 as Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman return for spooky sequel | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, Academy Award winners, are reprising their roles as sisters Sally and Gillian in the sequel to "Practical Magic".  Joining them are Joey King and Maisie Williams. The film's release is scheduled for September 18th.  The sequel will feature a more moody aesthetic but will also include elements from the original film such as the return of the beloved midnight margaritas.

articles.title: Trump says US in a ‘very, very strong’ position for Iran talks, expects ‘great deal’
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump stated that the US is in a strong negotiating position with Iran and expects to resume attacks if a deal isn't reached soon.  The two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran, which was set to expire on Wednesday, has been extended to Thursday evening. Pakistan urged both countries to consider extending the ceasefire and continue dialogue. Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with US Chargé d’Affaires Natalie Baker to discuss regional peace.  A US delegation is expected in Islamabad for a second round of talks between Washington and Tehran, which have yet to yield an agreement.

articles.title: 'China helping prop up Iran's regime': Nikki Hailey says ship seized by US linked to chemical shipments for missiles - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The United States seized an Iranian-flagged cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming it was headed to Iran with chemical shipments for missiles. China denied the claim, stating the ship was a "foreign container" vessel and that it rejected any false association or speculation.  US Central Command said the vessel failed to respond to repeated warnings over six hours and was operating in breach of a US-enforced blockade. Iran strongly condemned the action, calling it "armed piracy."

articles.title: Centre directs DPR revision for Kerala’s semi-high-speed rail to align with broad gauge standards - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Union Railway Ministry has asked Kerala's State government to revise the Detailed Project Report (DPR) for its long-delayed semi-high-speed rail project, SilverLine. The ministry is directing the use of broad gauge tracks instead of standard gauge tracks, citing the Railway Board's development of standards and specifications for a semi-high-speed BG corridor based on its ongoing Sarkhej–Dholera project in Gujarat.

articles.title: Palestine weekly wrap: Coordinated attacks and evictions in Gaza, West Bank | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli airstrikes, settler violence, and evictions continue to escalate in the West Bank and Gaza.  Palestinian casualties have risen significantly since October 2023, with over 72,553 deaths reported since then. Israel has been accused of ethnic cleansing tactics against Palestinians, including attacks on civilians, demolitions, and evictions. The US and Hamas are engaged in diplomatic talks that have yielded little progress.  The Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for the full military occupation of Gaza, while settlers continue to attack Palestinian villages and steal livestock.

articles.title: Zelensky says failure of US envoys to visit Kyiv is 'disrespectful'
articles.rephrased_article: Zelensky expressed disappointment over the lack of official visits by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, US envoys, to Kyiv despite their trips to Moscow.  He acknowledged complex logistics but emphasized the importance of continued cooperation with the US, noting that attention shifted towards the Middle East following the US-Israel war with Iran.  Despite ceasefire talks gaining momentum in autumn 2025, key issues like Ukraine's demand for Russian territory and Moscow's insistence on a "regime change" remain unresolved, leaving the negotiations at a stalemate. The ongoing war has resulted in significant casualties and destruction across Ukraine since its full-scale invasion in 2022.

articles.title: George Ariyoshi, first US governor of Asian American descent, dies aged 100 | Hawaii | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: George R Ariyoshi, Hawaii's first Asian American governor, died at age 100 on Sunday night.  He served as governor from 1973 to 1986 and was a three-term elected official who led the state during a period of significant growth. Josh Green, current governor, praised Ariyoshi's "quiet strength and integrity" and his dedication to public service. Ariyoshi was born in Honolulu and overcame personal challenges to become a lawyer and later a governor. He is survived by his wife, Jean Hayashi Ariyoshi, and children Lynn, Donn, and Ryozo.

articles.title: Thunderstorm forecast in 18 Telangana districts on April 22 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm forecast for 18 districts in Telangana on Wednesday, April 22, 2026. The weather will be partly cloudy in Hyderabad and its surrounding areas with light to moderate rain or thundershowers possible in the evening or night.  Hyderabad is expected to have maximum temperatures around 38℃ and minimum temperatures around 27℃.

articles.title: Uk Unemployment Rate: UK unemployment rate falls to 4.9% as wage growth hits slowest pace since 2020 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UK’s unemployment rate unexpectedly fell to 4.9% in the three months to February, but wage growth slowed to its weakest pace in over five years at 3.6%. Liz McKeown, director of economic statistics at the Office for National Statistics, noted an increase in economic inactivity.  Yael Selfin, chief economist at KPMG UK, cautioned that sustained higher costs could weigh on hiring in the months ahead, despite signs of stabilizing in February. The International Monetary Fund has warned that the energy shock could hit the UK harder than other advanced economies.

articles.title: Ofcom probing Telegram over child sexual abuse material concerns
articles.rephrased_article: Ofcom, the UK media regulator, has launched an investigation into Telegram over concerns it may be failing to prevent child sexual abuse material (CSAM) from being shared on its platform. The probe follows evidence suggesting CSAM is present and being shared on the messaging service.  Ofcom stated that while progress has been made in tackling CSAM on smaller platforms, this issue extends to large platforms as well. Suzanne Cater, director of enforcement at Ofcom, emphasized the importance of addressing child sexual exploitation and abuse, stating that these firms must do more to protect children or face serious consequences under the Online Safety Act.
articles.civic_flag_reason: CSAM is a serious crime and its presence on a platform should be urgently addressed.

articles.title: Liberals and Nationals to preference One Nation in blow to Michelle Milthorpe in Farrer byelection | Farrer byelection 2026 | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Liberals and Nationals have agreed to preference One Nation candidate David Farley ahead of independent Michelle Milthorpe in the Farrer byelection. This strategy could significantly impact the outcome of the race, as both parties are seen as frontrunners.  Milthorpe's campaign is supported by the Climate 200 fundraising vehicle and seeks to distance herself from the teal independent movement. One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has been facing increased scrutiny for her party's decision to re-hire a convicted rapist as campaign manager, but she maintains that the move was necessary.

articles.title: Rising stars on Dalal Street: 15 stocks with up to 50% upside potential, do you own any? - Solid bets | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: SBI Securities has named 16 stocks as its "rising star" recommendations, suggesting potential for significant upside. The brokerage predicts a range of gains from 18% to over 50%, with some stocks showing impressive three-year growth.  The list includes companies like APL Apollo Tubes, Star Cement, and Lumax Auto Technologies, among others.

articles.title: Clean electricity meets all new demand, curbing fossil fuels, says Ember | Energy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ember, a leading think tank, reports that low-emissions energy sources met all new global electricity demand in 2025 for the first time, leaving no room for fossil fuels to grow. Solar and wind power led this shift, generating 75% and almost all of the remaining demand respectively. The International Energy Agency also found a slowdown in oil and gas demand in 2025, suggesting a potential decline in fossil fuel reliance. However, some analysts remain skeptical, arguing that repeated shocks to the fossil fuel market will not render it obsolete.

articles.title: SC notifies SOPs to ensure uninterrupted functioning during ‘unforeseen public holidays’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan has implemented new standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure uninterrupted judicial functioning during unforeseen public holidays. The measures, including prioritizing urgent cases and reducing pendency, were announced in response to security arrangements for anticipated US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad this week.  These SOPs also include the issuance of weekly and proposed monthly cause lists, along with an automated case fixation system to enhance transparency and improve case flow management.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly polls: Musiri residents flag water, roads and livelihood issues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Musiri, an agriculturally fertile constituency in Tiruchi district, faces challenges ahead of the upcoming State Assembly elections. Residents cite concerns about groundwater depletion, irrigation planning, road connectivity, water supply, and the future of cottage industries, despite agriculture and banana cultivation remaining key to livelihoods.

articles.title: 'I have nothing left': Indian-origin man who lost wife, daughter in Air India crash faces deportation from UK - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammadmiya Sethwala, a 28-year-old Indian-origin man, is fighting to remain in the United Kingdom after his application for compassionate grounds was rejected.  Sethwala's wife and two-year-old daughter were among the 241 people killed on Air India Flight 171 in June 2025. His dependent visa expired earlier this year, and subsequent attempts to secure a new visa have failed. Sethwala is seeking to challenge the Home Office decision in court, with his legal team arguing for leniency based on exceptional humanitarian circumstances.

articles.title: Madonna offers reward for return of missing Coachella costume
articles.rephrased_article: Madonna offered a reward for the return of several vintage costume pieces stolen from her after her Coachella performance. The missing items, including a purple jacket, corset, and dress, are particularly significant to the singer as she wore them during a 20-year-old performance. The Indio Police Department is investigating the disappearance, but there's no evidence suggesting theft.

articles.title: Labor to tighten child NDIS eligibility to curb spending as Queensland MP warns change is ‘failing kids’ | Disability | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor is implementing changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) to curb its growth and address concerns about fraud. Mark Butler, the health minister, announced new eligibility rules for children under 18 and mandatory character checks for service providers. This move has drawn criticism from state governments, particularly Queensland, which accuses Labor of neglecting responsibilities to families reliant on long-term care. The changes are intended to bring the NDIS back to its original goal of supporting people with permanent disabilities while addressing concerns about waste and fraud within the scheme.

articles.title: Tata Steel shares jump 12% so far in April. Here’s why Nomura stays bullish on India’s steel sector - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nomura maintains a bullish outlook on the Indian steel sector, citing improving domestic price momentum despite global headwinds. The brokerage believes large blast furnace-based steel players are better positioned than smaller gas-based DRI producers due to their ability to substitute LPG usage with alternatives. Nomura has reiterated its 'Buy' ratings on Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Jindal Steel, and Lloyds Metals, while setting a target price of Rs 220 for Tata Steel shares.  Despite slight corrections in Indian steel prices last week, they remain near elevated levels.

articles.title: Is China a winner of the Iran war or facing economic risks? | Business and Economy | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: China's economy grew by 5 percent in the first quarter, exceeding expectations despite geopolitical tensions.  While this strong start is attributed to increased investment in high-tech industries and green energy, weak domestic demand and structural risks remain a concern. Beijing is actively addressing these challenges through strategic investments, potentially mitigating economic vulnerabilities arising from the ongoing Iran war.

articles.title: Pakistan Navy conducts successful test of locally developed air-launched cruise missile: ISPR - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan Navy successfully tested its indigenously developed ‘Taimoor’ air-launched cruise missile, demonstrating precision strike capability and operational readiness. The test, which was lauded by President, Prime Minister of Pakistan, Chief of Defence Forces, and other high-ranking officials, strengthened the nation's multi-dimensional coordinated strike posture in the conventional domain. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also congratulated the scientists and engineers on this significant milestone.

articles.title: Hours to go before stir, Telangana govt to hold talks with RTC JAC - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana State government is attempting to de-escalate a potential bus strike by the RTC Joint Action Committee, which represents employee unions, with talks scheduled for 5 pm on Tuesday.  The strike, set to begin Wednesday morning, remains in effect according to RTC JAC office bearer Thomas Reddy. The strike's impact will be felt by lakhs of bus users as TGSRTC services could be significantly disrupted.

articles.title: Indian Student Killed In Canada: Killer of Indian student Kartik Vasudev in Canada found guilty, judge says schizophrenia no excuse for random murder - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Richard Edwin, a Toronto man, was found guilty of first-degree murder in the deaths of two men, Kartik Vasudev and Elijah Eleazar Mahepath.  The killings occurred two days apart in 2022 and both victims died from multiple gunshot wounds.  Edwin's mental disorder diagnosis did not prevent him from being found guilty as he was deemed capable of understanding the wrongfulness of his actions. The judge stated that Edwin conducted internet searches related to violence, gunfights, and vulnerable organs, indicating a planned and deliberate nature to the murders.

articles.title: John Ternus' challenges as new Apple boss - AI, Trump and product launches
articles.rephrased_article: Apple vice president of hardware, John Ternus, is expected to become the next CEO after Tim Cook, who has been in charge for 16 years.  Ternus, known as a "product guy," has a history with Apple dating back to his early days at the company. He expressed interest in working closely with development teams and emphasized the importance of user experience. Ternus faces challenges such as navigating AI's rapid evolution and building a strong relationship with the US president.  His leadership style will be crucial for Apple's future success, especially in the face of growing public expectations for authenticity from powerful figures.

articles.title: ‘We were terrified they were going to kill us’: fishers who survived US boat strike speak out | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A group of Ecuadorian fishermen aboard the Don Maca fishing vessel were attacked by drones and detained by a US-flagged patrol boat. The attack occurred approximately 200 miles north-west of the Galápagos Islands, where the crew was fishing when they were targeted.  The crew claims that their phones were confiscated and photos/videos of the attack were deleted, while they were subjected to intimidation and threats by US personnel before being transferred to a Salvadorian patrol boat. The incident has been condemned as an extrajudicial killing by legal experts and rights groups. The Pentagon and the White House have not responded to requests for comment.  The crew was eventually returned to Ecuador but remains traumatized by the experience.

articles.title: Rebel Wilson labelled ‘nuts’ by PR team she allegedly hired to attack colleague, court hears | Rebel Wilson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rebel Wilson is facing a lawsuit from Charlotte MacInnes, the lead actor in her film "The Deb," over social media posts accusing MacInnes of making a sexual harassment complaint against co-producer Amanda Ghost.  A crisis PR firm, The Agency Group, allegedly created websites attacking Ghost, claiming she was a sex trafficker. Texts between agency staff referred to Wilson as “fucking nuts,” and evidence suggests Wilson ordered the creation of these sites. The trial continues.

articles.title: Nifty bears regret not buying the dip. Will Trump hand them a second chance? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Trump, Iran, and the Strait of Hormuz are at the center of a potential escalation in Middle East hostilities, which could benefit sidelined investors. Despite market uncertainty, analysts like CA Rudramurthy BV, MD at Vachana Investments, believe the market is close to a bottom and recommends buying on dips.  They cite factors such as retail and HNI buying, slowing FII selling, and attractive valuations as reasons for optimism. However, experts caution against aggressive investments until clarity emerges regarding earnings season and geopolitical developments.

articles.title: ECP halts Senate by-election for Murad Saeed’s vacant seat - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) halted the by-election for the vacant Senate seat previously held by Murad Saeed after a petition challenged the legality of his de-notification. The ECP issued a stay order, adjourning the case until May 7th to address the legal ambiguity surrounding Saeed's disqualification from his Senate seat.  The ECP cited an anti-terrorism court's March 7 order disqualifying Saeed for his conviction in the May 9 GHQ attack case and subsequently de-notified him on March 25th.

articles.title: Donald Trump: ‘Then lots of bombs start going off’: Donald Trump explains what will happen when US-Iran ceasefire expires - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump warned of a potential escalation in the Iran conflict if the current ceasefire expires without a deal, stating that "lots of bombs start going off" would result from renewed hostilities. Trump emphasized that the US delegation will travel to Islamabad for further talks with Iran, but uncertainty remains about their participation.  The two-week ceasefire is set to expire soon, and Trump expressed confidence in his negotiating team while suggesting a potential decrease in oil prices if a deal is reached.

articles.title: Kenya’s John Korir, Sharon Lokedi win Boston Marathon on record-breaking day | Athletics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: John Korir of Kenya broke the Boston Marathon course record, finishing in 2 hours, 1 minute, 52 seconds.  He achieved this feat in a Kenyan sweep as his compatriot Sharon Lokedi defended her title with a time of 2 hours, 18 minutes, and 51 seconds. The top three men beat the previous record set in 2011 by Geoffrey Mutai.  Lokedi's victory marked the fastest finish in the race's 130-year history, while Jess McClain of the United States placed fifth.

articles.title: The Onion launches new effort to turn Infowars into parody website
articles.rephrased_article: The Onion, a satirical publication, has proposed a licensing agreement to parody Alex Jones' Infowars media company. The proposal requires approval from a judge and would allow The Onion to publish its own content on Infowars' platforms.  This follows a previous attempt by The Onion to buy Infowars outright, which was rejected by another judge. Jones, who faces liquidation of his assets due to defamation lawsuits related to the Sandy Hook school shooting, has indicated he will oppose the new proposal.

articles.title: Music executive behind K-pop group BTS faces arrest in South Korea | South Korea | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: South Korean police are seeking to arrest Bang Si-Hyuk, the chair of HYBE, for alleged investor fraud. The investigation, which began in November, centers around accusations that Bang misled investors about HYBE's plans for an IPO and induced them to sell shares to a private equity fund before the company went public.  Bang’s legal team expressed regret over the arrest request but pledged continued cooperation with the investigation.

articles.title: Adani Power shares zoom nearly 40% in just 13 sessions. Should you book profits now? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Adani Power, India's largest private thermal power producer, is experiencing strong bullish momentum in its share price. The stock has recently broken out of a consolidation phase with expanding volumes and positive momentum across the Adani Group.  Traders are encouraged to hold existing long positions and view dips as buying opportunities. Analysts anticipate rising power demand due to the receding western disturbance that disrupted March's peak, which will benefit companies like Adani Power and NTPC.

articles.title: ECP halts Senate by-election for Murad Saeed’s vacant seat - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) halted the by-election for the vacant Senate seat previously held by Murad Saeed after a petition challenged the legality of his de-notification. The ECP issued a stay order and adjourned the case until May 7, following arguments that Saeed had not taken the oath of office despite being elected senator in July 2025.  The ECP's decision came after Saeed was disqualified from his Senate seat on March 26 due to his conviction in a May 9 case.

articles.title: Ishowspeed: IShowSpeed’s Caribbean tour schedule: Start date and countries revealed - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: IShowSpeed is launching a Caribbean Islands Tour starting April 25, 2026. The tour will feature IShowSpeed and his younger brother, Jamal, visiting multiple islands including Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Dominica, and more.  The timing of the tour coincides with St. Thomas Carnival in the U.S. Virgin Islands, potentially giving IShowSpeed a large audience during the event. The tour follows an African trip that IShowSpeed described as changing him, and is part of his growing global appeal through travel-focused videos.

articles.title: Usain Bolt hopes Australian sprint sensation Gout has strong support system | Athletics | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Usain Bolt advised Australian sprint sensation Gout to surround himself with a strong support system to stay focused on his track and field career.  The 18-year-old, who has already earned comparisons to the Jamaican sprinting great, is set to make his Diamond League debut in Oslo on June 10th. Bolt, who holds the world record in the 200m and 100m, emphasized the importance of avoiding distractions that come with success in track and field.

articles.title: Fannie Masemola: South Africa's police boss charged in connection with controversial health contract
articles.rephrased_article: Fannie Masemola, the chief of South Africa's police, has been formally charged with failing to properly oversee a controversial $21 million health contract. The case stems from an investigation into alleged corruption involving police officers and politicians.  The tender awarded to businessman Vusimuzi "Cat" Matlala's company Medicare24 Tshwane District was cancelled in 2025 after allegations of collusion, and Masemola is the only officer not charged with corruption. The case will proceed on May 13th, alongside other senior police officers and Matlala who have been accused of wrongdoing.

articles.title: Sam Neill says New Zealand goldmine supporters have threatened him with violence | New Zealand | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sam Neill, a New Zealand actor, has received threats of violence from supporters of a controversial goldmine project in Central Otago.  The Bendigo-Ophir mine, proposed by the Australian mining company Santana Minerals, is opposed by environmental groups like Sustainable Tarras, who fear it will damage the region's natural beauty and tourism industry. The project has sparked controversy due to its potential environmental impact and fast-track approval process under a controversial government law.  The threats against Neill come amidst growing opposition to the mine, including from Shane Jones, New Zealand’s resources minister, who has been criticized for his "drill, baby, drill" rhetoric.

articles.title: Sensex jumps 1,200 points in three days ahead of Iran war ceasefire expiry. 4 key factors - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 experienced significant gains today, adding over Rs 8 lakh crore to the market capitalisation.  Investor optimism was fueled by hopes of a resolution in the US-Iran conflict, with Brent crude prices hovering near $95 per barrel and oil prices declining due to expectations of increased trade through the Strait of Hormuz. FIIs softened their selling pressure after three consecutive days of net purchases. However, concerns remain regarding bond yields and the weakening rupee.

articles.title: Young doctor shot dead near Karachi’s Mehran Hotel - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A young doctor, Dr Sarang Memon, was fatally shot in a suspected targeted attack near the Mehran Hotel in Karachi on Monday night.  Dr Memon and his wife, also a doctor, were traveling in a rickshaw when suspects in a car intercepted them and opened fire. The victim died from multiple gunshot wounds at the Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre shortly after being transported there. The DIG South stated that the attack was likely personal in nature, and police are investigating.

articles.title: Kier Starmer: 'Felt political pressure': Sacked UK official blames Starmer’s office over Mandelson US appointment - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Olly Robbins, former head of the Foreign Office, testified before the House of Commons Foreign Affairs Committee that he felt political pressure to expedite Peter Mandelson's appointment as Britain’s ambassador to Washington despite security concerns.  Robbins stated that the vetting agency considered Mandelson a "borderline case" and was leaning toward recommending against giving him security clearance, but the Foreign Office approved it anyway. Prime Minister Keir Starmer acknowledged the appointment was a mistake and placed responsibility on Foreign Office officials for failing to inform him about the security concerns.

articles.title: Spain, Slovenia, Ireland push EU to debate Israel pact suspension | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Spain, Slovenia, and Ireland have urged the European Union to discuss suspending its association agreement with Israel due to alleged human rights violations. The three countries, citing a proposed Israeli law that would impose the death penalty on Palestinians convicted in military courts, as well as the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, argue that Israel is breaching the 1995 agreement and international law. They call for "bold and immediate action" from the EU and say all options should remain on the table.

articles.title: Japan loosens arms export rules in break from post-WW2 pacifism
articles.rephrased_article: Japan's government announced the relaxation of decades-old restrictions on its arms exports, allowing it to sell lethal weapons to more than a dozen countries. This move comes amidst heightened tensions in the region and follows a gradual shift away from Japan's pacifist post-World War II policy.  The decision has been met with concern from China, which views it as "reckless militarization," while South Korea urged Japan to uphold its pacifist constitution while contributing to regional peace.

articles.title: US ‘restricts intelligence sharing with South Korea’ after minister identified suspected nuclear site | South Korea | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: South Korea’s unification minister, Chung Dong-young, disclosed information about a suspected North Korean nuclear site in Kusong, prompting the US to partially restrict intelligence sharing with Seoul.  The restrictions began early this month and followed protests from US officials concerned about sensitive information being leaked. The US has not confirmed the restrictions publicly, but South Korea's defense ministry maintains close cooperation with the US continues despite the incident. President Lee Jae Myung defended his minister, stating that the information was widely reported in academic papers and media prior to Chung’s remarks.

articles.title: Diplomatic flurry as US-Iran truce deadline nears - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A US delegation is expected to arrive in Islamabad today, Tuesday, for the second round of peace talks with Iran, while Tehran has indicated its openness to attending.  President Donald Trump extended the ceasefire by a day but said further extension was unlikely without a deal. The two-week truce ends on Wednesday evening. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian criticized US signals as "unconstructive" and called for an end to the war with Iran. Meanwhile, diplomatic efforts intensified with calls between Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, President Xi Jinping, and President Emmanuel Macron.  The situation remains tense with heightened security measures in Islamabad ahead of the talks.

articles.title: Burj Al Arab Hotel Closed: Dubai’s Burj Al Arab hotel shutting down for 18 months for major refurbishment since 1999 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Burj Al Arab, Dubai's iconic sail-shaped luxury hotel, is set for a 18-month closure beginning soon for a major refurbishment. Jumeirah, the owner of the hotel, has announced phased upgrades led by Paris-based interior architect Tristan Auer. The closure period may shift slightly depending on work progress and guests with existing bookings will be relocated to nearby hotels.  The move is unusual in Dubai's hotel scene as large-scale refurbishments for such iconic properties are rare.

articles.title: Canadian woman killed in shooting at Mexico's ancient pyramids
articles.rephrased_article: A gunman opened fire at the ancient Teotihuacán pyramids in Mexico, killing a Canadian woman and injuring several others, including citizens from Colombia, Russia, and Canada.  President Claudia Sheinbaum of Mexico expressed her condolences and instructed officials to investigate the incident. Anita Anand, Canada's foreign minister, confirmed the death of a Canadian tourist and the wounding of another. The gunman took his own life after the attack. Despite the tragedy, authorities have assured that security measures are being taken for the upcoming World Cup in Mexico City.

articles.title: Jewish man among first charged in pro-Palestinian slogan crackdown that reminds some of 1970s Queensland | Queensland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Heydt, a 73-year-old Jewish clinical psychologist, was arrested in Brisbane for displaying a T-shirt with the phrase "Jews for a free Palestine from the river to the sea" and chanting it.  He is one of 25 people charged under new Queensland laws prohibiting two expressions frequently chanted by pro-Palestinian demonstrators. Zac Karaniki, a Palestinian Australian student, was also arrested for holding a banner displaying one of the banned phrases. The laws have been criticized by some as reminiscent of police repression under former Queensland Premier Joh Bjelke-Petersen and are seen by others as necessary to prevent incitement to violence.  Jason Steinberg, president of the Queensland Jewish Board of Deputies, argues that the phrase is not a peaceful slogan but has been used by terrorists since the 1960s.

articles.title: ICICI up, HDFC down after Q4 show; analysts positive on both - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ICICI Bank closed at ₹1,356.2, gaining 0.7%, while HDFC Bank fell 0.6% to ₹795.45. The Nifty 50 ended little changed at 24,364.85. Analysts remain positive on both banks, with Bloomberg consensus suggesting an average upside of 33% for HDFC Bank and 24% for ICICI Bank.

articles.title: Algeria’s ex-minister of industry jailed in high-profile corruption case | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ali Aoun, former Algerian Minister of Industry and Pharmaceutical Production, was sentenced to five years in prison for corruption.  Aoun was convicted alongside several other officials, including his son, who received a six-year sentence. The case involved accusations of irregular sales of metal waste and the unlawful awarding of industrial contracts. Abdelmadjid Tebboune, Algerian President, has launched an ongoing anticorruption drive targeting senior officials, including those from the previous regime.

articles.title: Diplomatic flurry as US-Iran truce deadline nears - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A US delegation is expected to arrive in Islamabad today, while Iran also appears open to sending negotiators for the second round of peace talks.  The ceasefire between Iran and the US expires on Wednesday evening, with President Trump expressing skepticism about an extension unless a deal is reached.
