The money was found in two separate incidents, with one individual carrying ₹10 lakh to her relative's house in Vellore for an emergency and another individual found with ₹1.21 lakh in cash near Walajah town. The seized cash was handed over to the district treasury and is under investigation.

articles.title: Tornadoes and heavy winds destroy homes and roads across US midwest | US weather | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Severe weather, including reported tornadoes, caused widespread damage across the upper Midwest on Friday. The National Weather Service is conducting surveys to determine the extent of the damage.  Homes and buildings were damaged in Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Illinois, with some residents trapped in their basements. Marathon County Sheriff Chad Billeb stated that this was the most extensive damage he had seen in his 34 years as a law enforcement officer. The Community Foundation of North Central Wisconsin partnered with the United Way chapter of Marathon county to assist those whose homes were damaged.

articles.title: Visakhapatnam prepares for first international cruise departure - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cordelia Cruises is launching international sailings from Visakhapatnam, marking a significant step in Andhra Pradesh's efforts to establish the port city as a cruise tourism hub. The ship will begin with domestic voyages before transitioning to international routes, including stops in Kuala Lumpur and Singapore.  The 14-day voyage, starting July 15th, is expected to attract more cruise liners and generate revenue through an 18% GST on cabin sales. Officials believe this initiative will establish a sustainable cruise circuit linking Chennai, Visakhapatnam, and Southeast Asian destinations.

articles.title: UK seeks EU deals on steel and EVs in push for closer economic ties | Brexit | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The UK government is seeking to secure deals on steel and electric vehicles with the EU as it seeks to upgrade its post-Brexit economic relationship.  Nick Thomas-Symonds, Cabinet Office minister, stated that these sectors need to be discussed this year due to upcoming trade restrictions. The EU has imposed tariffs on steel imports in response to Chinese overcapacity, which will affect British industry. While the UK and EU are exploring deeper economic ties, a summit is planned for the summer with an agenda focused on food, youth mobility, and energy.  The future of these negotiations remains uncertain.

articles.title: Lok Adalat to help settle UKP land acquisition cases - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vijayapura District Legal Services Authority will hold a Lok Adalat to assist farmers affected by the Upper Krishna Project (UKP) from April to July. The disposal of cases will take place in First and Third Additional Courts in Vijayapura, with sessions scheduled for 12:30 p.m. to 1:30 p.m. in April and May and from 4:45 p.m. to 5:45 p.m. from June to July.  Farmers who have legal issues related to land acquisition or compensation can participate in the Lok Adalat for swift case settlement based on mutual agreement.

articles.title: Woman arrested after car driven into pedestrians in central London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 29-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after a car hit pedestrians in central London early Sunday morning.  The incident injured three people, including a man in his 50s with life-changing injuries and a woman in her 30s with minor injuries. The driver is being held by police while DCI Alison Foxwell urges anyone who witnessed the collision to come forward.

articles.title: Trump says US representatives heading to Islamabad, will be ‘there tomorrow evening for negotiations’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump announced that US representatives would be in Islamabad for a second round of talks with Iran, stating he hoped they would accept a "very fair and reasonable" deal.  The talks, brokered by Pakistan, were intended to address the impasse over the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran closed on Saturday, citing the ongoing US blockade of Iranian ports. Despite this, both sides remained in a standoff with Iran accusing the US of violating the ceasefire agreement and inflicting collective punishment on its population.  The talks are being closely watched by regional powers and international organizations as they attempt to de-escalate tensions between the two countries.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Nanguneri constituency, a dry agrarian region with no dearth of caste issues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A tri-corner contest is expected in the Nanguneri Assembly segment of Tamil Nadu, where Congress, Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam and the newly formed Tamilaga Vetri Kazhagam are vying for victory.  The constituency has historically been a stronghold of the Indian National Congress until 1971 when the DMK took control, with subsequent wins by the AIADMK.

articles.title: Punjabi TV host in Canada sentenced to 5.5 years in jail for smuggling 108 kg of meth in duffel bags from US - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sukhvinder Kaur Sangha, a 47-year-old Punjabi radio and TV host in Canada, was sentenced to 5.5 years in prison for smuggling methamphetamine from the US in 2021.  Sangha pleaded guilty to importing drugs estimated at $1 million to $10 million and her lawyer argued she was forced into the crime by a threat against her teenage son. The prosecutor sought a longer sentence, highlighting the need to deter similar crimes.

articles.title: Why do gray whales keep dying in San Francisco's waters?
articles.rephrased_article: Scientists are investigating the reasons behind a high mortality rate of gray whales in San Francisco Bay, with researchers noting that many are undernourished and dying from a combination of dwindling prey availability, climate change, and human-caused factors.  The bay is attracting these whales due to their long migration routes, but they are also being struck by ships, leading to increased concern for the species' future. US Coast Guard officials have implemented safety measures to protect whales in the busy harbor, while wildlife experts hope that the bay can be a safe haven for gray whales as they continue their journey.

articles.title: Italian lawyers could win ‘wild west-style bounties’ if immigration clients go home | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Giorgia Meloni’s far-right government in Italy has proposed a controversial bonus scheme for lawyers who successfully encourage immigrant clients to return home. The plan, which would allocate €246,000 this year and double funding for 2027 and 2028, has drawn criticism from legal professionals and opposition parties who argue it undermines judicial independence and incentivizes lawyers to prioritize state interests over their client’s rights.  The measure is part of a broader effort by the government to curb irregular immigration, following a referendum defeat on judicial reforms.

articles.title: Does Israel’s ‘Yellow Line’ violate the Lebanon ceasefire? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The recent ceasefire in Lebanon has been met with concerns that Israel's "Yellow Line" military zone could become a permanent occupation.  Israel claims the line is necessary to combat Hezbollah, while Lebanon and Hezbollah reject it as an illegal occupation of sovereign territory. Despite the ceasefire, Israeli forces have continued to carry out demolitions, artillery shelling, and land-clearing operations in violation of the agreement.  Analysts argue that the ceasefire's wording leaves room for interpretation regarding Israel's right to self-defense, while Hezbollah has vowed to remain vigilant against any violations. The situation is further complicated by ongoing Israeli attacks on Lebanese villages and communities near the "Yellow Line", raising fears that the truce could be a tactic to legitimize occupation.

articles.title: Iran warns Hormuz will stay shut unless US lifts siege on its ports | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has threatened to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed unless the US lifts its restrictions on Iranian ports. This action comes as overlapping ceasefires with Israel and Lebanon, along with the US, are nearing expiration, raising concerns about renewed conflict.  Iran claims this is a "US siege" on its ports, halting most traffic through one of the world's key oil chokepoints.

articles.title: Does the world need new leaders? Varsha Gandikota & Naledi Pandor | TV Shows | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Progressive International General Coordinator Varsha Gandikota-Nellutla and Naledi Pandor, Chair of the Board of Trustees at the Nelson Mandela Foundation, discussed power dynamics in the international order on the latest episode of Reframe.  They explored whether the Global South can unite to counterbalance the US and emphasized the importance of international solidarity, drawing parallels with South Africa's fight against apartheid.

articles.title: JioBlackRock Mutual Fund: HDFC Bank, ITC and Infosys among top 10 stock holdings in March - Portfolio check | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JioBlackRock Mutual Fund, a new entrant in the mutual fund industry, held significant positions in several prominent Indian companies. The fund's top holdings included HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, representing around 7.05% and 4.89% of its equity AUM respectively.  The fund also invested heavily in Bharti Airtel, Reliance Industries, Larsen & Toubro, State Bank of India, Infosys, Mahindra & Mahindra, ITC, and MCX.

articles.title: Iran war: 10 frequently used words and their meanings | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US-Israel war on Iran has caused significant disruption to global energy flows, with the Strait of Hormuz being a key point of contention.  Iran, the US, and Israel have used various terms to describe their actions in the conflict. Shahed drones are low-cost weapons used by Iran. The Tomahawk cruise missile is a long-range weapon developed by the United States. The Bab al-Mandeb strait connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and is a crucial trade route.  The Epic Fury operation is a joint military campaign launched by the US and Israel against Iran.  Ayatollahs, high-ranking clerics in Shia Islam, have played a significant role in both religious and political life in Iran.  Kharg Island, Iran's primary oil export terminal, has been targeted by military operations.

articles.title: Mcap of 8 of top-10 most valued firms surges by Rs 1.87 lakh cr; Airtel biggest winner - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The BSE Sensex and the NSE Nifty experienced notable gains last week, rising 1.21% and 1.25%, respectively. This uptrend was driven by easing geopolitical tensions and improved risk sentiment, fueled in part by optimism surrounding a potential US-Iran peace agreement.  Key market players saw their valuations increase significantly, with Bharti Airtel, LIC, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), and Reliance Industries leading the charge.

articles.title: Pope Leo tells Angola during huge Mass to ‘build hope’ | Religion News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Leo XIV addressed tens of thousands of Angolan faithful, urging them to overcome divisions and corruption stemming from their war-scarred past. During a landmark tour of Africa, the first US-born pope also spoke out against resource exploitation and called President Donald Trump’s threat to end Iran's civilization "unacceptable."  He emphasized the need for hope and building a future free from poverty and suffering.

articles.title: Trump tests his luck with the religious right amid feud with pope and AI Jesus posts | Donald Trump | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's recent social media posts depicting himself as Jesus Christ have sparked criticism from some Christian groups, including those on the right. Trump, who has a strong base of support among white evangelicals, is facing backlash for his actions and statements.  Experts suggest that while Trump's support among white evangelicals may endure in certain regions, Catholic voters could be more influential in competitive races across the country. The Republican party's success in these elections will likely hinge on their ability to maintain or gain support from white Catholics.

articles.title: Watch: Obama and Mamdani sing with children in New York
articles.rephrased_article: Barack Obama and Zohran Mamdani, the mayor of New York City, met for the first time on Saturday at a child care center in the Bronx. They sang to preschoolers, including a rendition of "Wheels on the Bus" and a K-pop song called "Soda Pop."  Obama joked that he felt old after singing with the children, while Mamdani said they discussed the administration's vision for the city.

articles.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nilesh Jain of Centrum Finverse and Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking analyzed the Indian stock market, suggesting a positive outlook with support shifting higher to around 24,000.  The volatility index has softened, hovering near the 17 mark, lending further support to the bullish sentiment.  European markets also closed in green, with the UK's FTSE 100 and Germany's DAX closing higher between 0.73% and 2.18%.

articles.title: H-1B visa fraud: Two Indian-origin men plead guilty in California; hired people for non-existent posts - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Two Indian-origin men, Sampath Rajidi and Sreedhar Mada, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit H-1B visa fraud. They submitted false petitions to the USCIS, claiming they were hiring for the University of California, while knowing these positions did not exist.  They then provided these fraudulent visas to other clients, gaining an unfair advantage over competing firms and depleting available H-1B visas. Both men face a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of the H-1B visa system for personal gain is a serious concern.

articles.title: Peru says presidential election results due by mid-May after delayed count | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Peru's presidential election results will not be finalized until mid-May after a review of over 15,000 challenged ballots. Keiko Fujimori, the right-wing candidate, leads with 17% of the vote, while Roberto Sanchez and Rafael Lopez Aliaga are vying for second place. The delay has been met with criticism from some candidates who allege fraud without providing evidence.  The European Union's election observer mission stated that the vote met democratic standards despite challenges.

articles.title: Hamnet-era mourning jewel from celebrated painting rediscovered after 400 years | Art | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A heart-shaped mourning pendant, depicted in a 17th-century portrait of Sir Thomas Aston at the Deathbed of His Wife, has been rediscovered after four centuries. The pendant, made to commemorate the death of Aston's son Robert in 1634, was found by the current owners of the painting and identified by historian Martyn Downer.  The pendant is valued at £650,000 and reflects its rarity as a piece of 17th-century memento mori jewelry. The Manchester Art Gallery hopes to reunite the pendant with its original artwork.

articles.title: Alec Baldwin to face civil trial over Rust film set shooting
articles.rephrased_article: Alec Baldwin is facing a civil trial over the 2021 shooting on the set of the film Rust, after a judge ruled that his lawsuit could proceed.  The lawsuit, filed by lighting technician Serge Svetnoy, alleges Baldwin was negligent in leading up to the incident where a live round was fired from his prop gun, killing cinematographer Halyna Hutchins and injuring director Joel Souza.  A civil trial date has been provisionally set for October 12th.

articles.title: Where’s the Indian mutual fund sector going ahead? 6 big trends to watch out for - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Large-cap equity AUM has declined while Mid and Small Cap have grown, demonstrating a shift in investor preference. Multi-Asset Allocation funds (MAAFs) have seen significant growth fueled by gold and silver performance, surpassing traditional hybrid funds. SIP inflows have reached ₹32,087 crore, exceeding total equity inflows of recent years, indicating a sustained increase in long-term savings.  Mid Cap gained market share due to strong returns and investor confidence, while Large Cap lost ground as its return gap widened compared to benchmarks. MAAFs are attracting investors seeking diversification and exposure to precious metals.

articles.title: Humanoid robots race past humans in Beijing half-marathon, showing rapid advances - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Honor, a Chinese smartphone brand, and other robotics companies showcased their rapidly advancing humanoid robots in the inaugural Beijing half-marathon.  The robots, equipped with advanced AI and liquid cooling technology, outpaced human runners by significant margins, setting new world records for autonomous navigation and speed. Spectators were impressed by the robots' athleticism and potential to reshape industries like manufacturing. While economically viable applications are still in development, the race highlighted the growing capabilities of these machines and China's ambition to become a global leader in robotics.

articles.title: Canadian man Germanpreet Singh wanted for firing gun with intent in Calgary; police warn public not to approach - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Calgary Police Service are searching for 22-year-old Germanpreet Singh, also known as 'Garry,' who is wanted on a warrant for discharging a firearm with intent. The offense carries significant prison time if proven in court and authorities urge the public not to approach him. Anyone who sees Singh should immediately contact emergency services. The investigation remains ongoing.

articles.title: Trump says US negotiators to head to Pakistan for Iran ceasefire talks | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced that US negotiators will travel to Islamabad, Pakistan for a second round of talks aimed at ending the US-Israel war on Iran. The announcement follows last weekend's failed negotiations in which Vice President JD Vance led the US delegation.  Trump accused Iran of violating a ceasefire by firing bullets in the Strait of Hormuz and threatened severe repercussions if they do not accept the proposed deal.

articles.title: Bank bosses called to meeting with Reeves over impact of Iran war on UK economy | Economics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Chancellor Rachel Reeves has summoned the CEOs of HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest, and Santander to discuss mitigating the economic impact of the ongoing crisis in the Middle East. The meeting will focus on protecting vulnerable borrowers from rising mortgage rates, with an update on the government's mortgage charter and support for 1.6 million customers whose fixed-rate deals expire by year-end.  The escalating conflict has led to soaring energy prices and increased mortgage rate hikes, potentially impacting over one million UK households. The meeting could also prompt banks to provide insights into consumer behavior in response to the crisis.

articles.title: Rat poison found in HiPP baby food jar in Austria, police say
articles.rephrased_article: HiPP, a German baby food company, has issued a recall of its entire range of purées sold in jars at Spar supermarkets in Austria after rat poison was found in a sample. The Austrian police are investigating the incident and believe at least one more poisoned jar is in circulation.  The company claims the recall is due to a criminal act being investigated by authorities, not a product defect.  HiPP has also removed its baby food from stores in other countries as a precautionary measure. Spar has removed the brand's baby food from its stores across Austria and other European countries.

articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Congress, CPI(M) question delay in poll data publication - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V.D. Satheesan, leader of the Opposition in Kerala, and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) have requested an explanation from the Election Commission of India regarding the delay in releasing the complete election data for the April 9, 2026, Kerala Assembly elections.  The request was made to the Chief Election Commissioner of India.

articles.title: Kerala poll: Deputy CM debate resurfaces as IUML asserts eligibility for post - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Syed Munawwarali Shihab Thangal, president of the Muslim Youth League, stated that the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) is eligible for the Deputy Chief Minister position if the United Democratic Front (UDF) forms a government in Kerala. He cited past examples of former party leaders holding the post, but emphasized that the IUML will not claim or negotiate it.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Omalur constituency residents seek cold storage facility for marigold - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Omalur constituency, located 15 km from Salem, has been a stronghold for the AIADMK, winning eight elections since 1977.  The DMK has won twice, while other parties like the Congress and PMK have also secured victories in the past. Agriculture is a major industry in Omalur, with marigold cultivation prevalent in certain areas.

articles.title: Virginia’s redistricting vote ‘a critical step’ for the swing state | Virginia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Glenn Youngkin warned conservative activists that Virginia's congressional map referendum is the most important election in the state's history, as it could allow Democrats to win all but one seat in the November midterm elections. The question before voters is whether to replace the current maps with a new version that could be more favorable to Democrats.  Polls show a narrow lead for the side in favor of redistricting, despite concerns from some Democrats about undermining their stated focus on bolstering democratic norms.  The referendum has been fueled by national redistricting battles instigated by Donald Trump, who aims to preserve Republican control of Congress, and is seen as a response to his efforts in other states. The outcome could have implications for the 2024 presidential election.

articles.title: Operating nuclear plants was ‘lifetime commitment’: Experts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's new SHANTI Act, enacted in 2025, aims to increase the country's nuclear power capacity from 8.7 gigawatts (GW) to 100 GW by 2047. The act allows private companies to operate nuclear power plants and attract foreign investment. Former regulators of the nuclear energy establishment and policy veterans have emphasized the need for long-term commitment and financial security in managing waste, claims related to radiation exposure, and decommissioning nuclear power plants.

articles.title: Four feared dead in major accident on NH-50 in Karnataka’s Vijayanagara district - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A multiple-vehicle collision involving a lorry, bus, car, and motorcycles on National Highway 50 near Danapur in Vijayanagara district resulted in at least four fatalities and numerous injuries.  The incident began when the garlic-laden lorry, allegedly driven recklessly, struck two motorcycles, injuring three people before continuing to collide with other vehicles and motorcycles. The bus was hit from behind by the lorry, leaving 25 passengers injured. Police Superintendent S. Jahnavi oversaw rescue operations at the scene.

articles.title: Scooty-riding girl robbery suspect injured in ‘encounter’ - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Lahore arrested Adnan Yousaf, the prime suspect in a mobile phone snatching incident, after he was injured during an attempt to flee from police.  The suspect had been involved in the crime two days prior and was tracked using geofencing and human intelligence. The suspect's accomplice escaped the scene but was later apprehended. Chung police registered a case against both suspects, with police claiming hundreds of CCTV camera footages were reviewed to trace the incident.

articles.title: The GCC has unity, it now needs joint defence and development | GCC | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) is pursuing a balanced diplomatic policy to de-escalate the conflict between the United States, Israel and Iran.  GCC members are unified in their opposition to aggression and destabilization, calling for regional security arrangements, new energy routes, and economic integration projects. The GCC stresses that any attempt to control the Strait of Hormuz is a violation of international law and will be met with firm action. The GCC also calls for a just and comprehensive resolution on the Palestinian question based on the Arab Peace Initiative and a unified Gulf foreign policy.

articles.title: Falling fertility, debt and AI: is the US headed toward a population crisis? | US economy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US fertility rate is falling, hitting a record low of 1.57 in 2025, below the replacement level of 2.1 children per woman needed to maintain a stable population. This trend, coupled with an aging population, is straining social security and Medicare budgets, leading to rising public debt.  Falling fertility rates are not unique to the US; they are occurring globally, contributing to rising public debt in countries like China and across the OECD. While some propose solutions such as government incentives or increased investment in childcare, experts argue that these measures won't address the root cause of the problem: a lack of innovation and economic growth to support an aging population.

articles.title: ‘No one could ever call me anti-women’: Tharoor shares details of conversation with Rijiju - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor and other opposition MPs met with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju after the Lok Sabha adjourned sine die.  Tharoor stated that Rijiju conceded that no one could ever call him anti-women, highlighting the importance of women's representation in Parliament and institutions. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill to implement 33% reservation for women in legislatures was defeated in the Lok Sabha on Friday after failing to secure a two-thirds majority. The bill proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats to 816 by 2029, following a delimitation exercise based on the 2011 Census.

articles.title: Traffic restored on Karakoram Highway following landslide as heavy rainfall lashes GB - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Karakoram Highway (KKH) was reopened on Sunday after being blocked for nearly 20 hours due to a landslide near Lachi in Kohistan.  The Astore Valley road remains closed due to landslides, impacting thousands of passengers traveling between Gilgit-Baltistan and other areas. The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) had warned of heavy rainfall and thunderstorms in the region from April 16-19. The PMD advised authorities to take precautions against potential landslides.

articles.title: Australia and Japan sign contracts for $7bn warships deal | Military News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Australia and Japan signed contracts for the first three of 11 warships as part of a $7 billion defense deal, deepening their military cooperation. The contract was signed by Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles and Japanese Defence Minister Koizumi Shinjiro, with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries building three stealth frigates in Nagasaki Prefecture and Austal constructing eight in Western Australia.  The first Japanese-built warship is scheduled to be delivered in 2029, entering service in 2030. This deal reflects the growing security concerns shared by Australia and Japan, particularly China's rising influence in the region.

articles.title: Nathalie Baye, prolific star of French and Hollywood cinema, dies aged 77 | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nathalie Baye, a renowned French film star, has died at the age of 77 from Lewy body dementia.  She was known for starring in over 80 films and winning four César awards, including three consecutive wins from 1981 to 1983. Baye's career included international roles such as playing Leonardo DiCaprio's mother in "Catch Me If You Can" and a French aristocrat in the Downton Abbey sequel, "A New Era."  She also worked with filmmakers like Xavier Dolan and had a notable relationship with rock and roll singer Johnny Hallyday.

articles.title: Minister launches PM Surya Ghar Utsav in Banganapalle - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for Roads and Buildings BC Janardhan Reddy inaugurated the 'PM Surya Ghar Utsav' in Banaganapalle town, Andhra Pradesh. The initiative provides free solar electricity to SC and ST families, with Andhra Pradesh offering a 100% subsidy.  The scheme aims to alleviate financial burdens on middle-class families and promote renewable energy. During a separate review meeting, Janardhan Reddy directed officials to ensure drinking water availability throughout the summer season and address any potential groundwater depletion issues.

articles.title: Security beefed up as Islamabad braces for arrival of ‘foreign delegations’ - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad’s Red Zone and Extended Red Zone are closed to all traffic due to the anticipated arrival of foreign delegations, including security officials from the United States and Iran.  The move comes as both countries prepare for potential peace talks. Rawalpindi district administration has also suspended public and goods transport until further directives. The Islamabad police and administration have asked hotels, hostels, inns, and guest houses to close their premises until further orders.

articles.title: Humanoid robot breaks half marathon world record in Beijing | Science and Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A humanoid robot from Honor, a Chinese smartphone maker, broke the men’s world record at a Beijing half-marathon, finishing in 50 minutes and 26 seconds. The robot's impressive performance surpassed the current world record of 57:20 held by Ugandan runner Jacob Kiplimo. Spectators were impressed by the robot's speed and agility, with some expressing concerns about the potential impact of rapid technological advancements on human jobs.  The event aimed to showcase the growing popularity of humanoid robots in China and their potential applications in various fields.

articles.title: Canadian astronaut’s bon mots help heal wounds from French language row | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jeremy Hansen, a Canadian astronaut on the NASA Artemis II mission, spoke French during the journey to the moon. This marked the first time the language was spoken en route to the lunar surface and sparked widespread praise for Hansen's efforts.  His decision to speak French, following a recent controversy surrounding Air Canada CEO Michael Rousseau, highlighted the importance of cultural representation and respect for languages beyond one's native tongue.

articles.title: War reparations - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has demanded compensation from the US for damages inflicted on its civilian infrastructure during the recent conflict. International law experts argue that the US is liable to pay reparations, citing numerous attacks on schools and healthcare facilities, including a devastating strike on a school in Minab that killed over 175 people. The Iranian Red Crescent reports at least 763 schools and 316 health centers have been targeted by the US-Israeli coalition.  The article suggests the US should address these claims to demonstrate sincerity in pursuing a lasting deal with Iran.

articles.title: ‘A little tacky’: Trump reviews his own McDonald’s moment - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of experienced journalists, provides global news and diverse perspectives to its readers. The organization is dedicated to accuracy, depth, and timeliness in delivering international affairs coverage.  They strive to keep readers informed about the ever-changing world.

articles.title: Security tightened as Islamabad braces for arrival of foreign teams in run-up to anticipated US-Iran talks - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad Police closed the Red Zone and Extended Red Zone to all traffic due to expected foreign delegations for potential peace talks between the United States and Iran. The closures, effective Sunday, also included Murree Road.  The Islamabad police and administration requested hotel, hostel, inn, and guest house closures until further orders. Public and heavy transport were suspended in both Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

articles.title: Vodafone incentivised security staff to fine its own franchisees | Vodafone | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Vodafone has been accused of unfairly fining its franchisees, leading to a high court claim by 62 former franchisees alleging the company "unjustly enriched" itself. The telecoms group implemented a policy that incentivized its security staff to increase fines levied on franchisees, with some penalties reaching £10,000 for a mistake costing Vodafone just £7.08. Vodafone has acknowledged flaws in the program and made goodwill payments but maintains that fines are not intended to generate profit and are designed to discourage poor customer outcomes. The company continues to contest the high court claim.

articles.title: Indian heritage spirits Mahua and Goan Feni debut in UK market | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mahua and Feni, traditional Indian spirits, have entered the UK market through Maharaja Drinks. The retailer launched a new range featuring three Feni variants and one Mahua spirit, made using small-batch distillation methods and natural ingredients.  The move aims to bring authentic native flavors to a wider audience while appealing to the Indian diaspora in the UK.

articles.title: Fire razes 200 homes in Sabah, leaving hundreds homeless | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A fire in Sandakan district, Sabah, Malaysia destroyed approximately 200 homes, displacing over 445 people. Jimmy Lagung, the district's fire and rescue chief, attributed the rapid spread of the blaze to strong winds and low tide conditions. Datuk Walter Kenson, head of the Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee, stated that the affected homes are no longer safe to live in.  Anwar Ibrahim, Malaysia's Prime Minister, confirmed federal government coordination with Sabah authorities for basic assistance and temporary relocation efforts.

articles.title: Bulgaria votes as pro-Russian former president leads in the polls | Bulgaria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Bulgarians are voting in their eighth parliamentary election in five years, with Rumen Radev, the former president and frontrunner for the pro-Russian Progressive Bulgaria party, promising to address corruption and instability.  Radev's campaign has been boosted by social media campaigns and promises of stability, appealing to voters weary of repeated elections and a small group of veteran politicians seen as corrupt. Bogomil Bardarski, a 72-year-old metalworker, expressed the desire for political unity and action, while Boyko Borissov's GERB party trails in second place.  Voter interest appears to be high, with polls suggesting a turnout of nearly double that of previous elections.

articles.title: Security tightened as Islamabad braces for arrival of foreign teams in run-up to anticipated US-Iran talks - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad Police closed the Red Zone and Extended Red Zone to all traffic until further orders due to expected foreign delegations for potential peace talks between the US and Iran. The move also included a closure of Murree Road, as well as requests for hotels, hostels, inns, and guest houses to close their premises.  The Islamabad and Rawalpindi district administrations suspended public and goods transport until further directives.

articles.title: London synagogue targeted in another attempted arson attack; Sadiq Khan vows strict action - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Community Security Trust (CST) reported an attempted arson attack at the Kenton United Synagogue in north-west London on Saturday night.  Minor smoke damage was caused, but there were no injuries or significant structural damage.  London Mayor Sadiq Khan condemned the attack and vowed to prosecute perpetrators. Ephraim Mirvis, the Chief Rabbi of the UK, called it "cowardly" and warned of a sustained campaign of violence against Jewish communities in the UK. This incident follows a string of suspected antisemitic attacks in north-west London, including one on a Jewish charity building and another targeting a synagogue with petrol-filled bottles.

articles.title: Displaced Lebanese families return home despite Israeli attacks | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands of displaced Lebanese families have begun returning to their southern homeland despite ongoing Israeli shelling and home demolitions near the border.  While a 10-day truce between Lebanon and Israel has allowed for inspections, many residents find their homes destroyed or damaged beyond habitation, leading them to be hesitant about staying.  Hezbollah, a senior official warned that this is a temporary truce and Israeli treachery could erupt at any time. Local authorities report nearly 2,300 deaths caused by Israeli attacks and over one million displaced people, primarily from southern Lebanon and Beirut's southern suburbs.

articles.title: Zelensky condemns US extension of Russian sanctions waiver
articles.rephrased_article: Zelensky condemned the US decision to extend a waiver allowing Russia to sell oil despite Western sanctions. The US argues that the move eases energy supply concerns, but Zelensky stated that every dollar spent on Russian oil funds the war in Ukraine.  The Ukrainian leader cited Russia's "shadow fleet" of tankers and its ability to generate revenue from oil sales to support its military operations.

articles.title: Rat poison found in baby food jar in Austria after product recall | Austria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: HiPP baby food has been recalled in Austria after rat poison was found in a sample of the product. The police in Burgenland said that jars with specific characteristics, such as a red circle sticker and damaged lids, may have been tampered with.  The HiPP company stated that this incident appears to be an external criminal act affecting their distribution channel. Customers are advised not to consume the affected products and should contact Spar Austria for refunds.

articles.title: Chhattisgarh Vedanta power plant blast: Death toll rises to 24 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A blast at the Vedanta power plant in Chhattisgarh's Sakti district has tragically claimed 24 lives, with one more fatality reported on Sunday.  Vedanta Ltd. workers were injured when a steel tube carrying high-pressure steam exploded, leaving several others critically burned. Anil Agarwal, chairman of Vedanta Group, and Devendra Patel, plant head, are among eight to ten individuals named in an FIR filed by police for causing death by negligence.  The incident is under investigation by both the police and state authorities.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale harm to citizens due to industrial negligence is reported casually.

articles.title: Healers who kill - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan is facing a growing HIV epidemic, with outbreaks occurring in multiple regions.  Dr Zafar Mirza, former SAPM on health, has warned of a generalized AIDS epidemic in Pakistan, citing rising cases and the failure to address unsafe injection practices. Dr Fatima Mir, a Karachi-based paediatric infectious disease specialist, highlights the lack of public awareness and enforcement against syringe reuse as contributing factors to these outbreaks. Despite existing policies aimed at addressing these issues, such as the National Injection Safety Policy and the Prime Minister's Programme for Prevention and Control of Hepatitis, progress has been slow.  The article emphasizes that while single-use injection equipment reuse is a major concern, other transmission pathways like reused blades and contaminated blood transfusions also pose significant risks.

articles.title: PM Modi speaks with Andhra Pradesh Deputy CM Pawan Kalyan; enquires about his health - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inquired about the health of Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, who underwent surgery on Saturday, April 18, 2026.  Mr. Kalyan expressed gratitude to PM Modi for his concern and well wishes for a speedy recovery.

articles.title: A new Pakistan - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's diplomacy to end the war between Iran and the US has been successful, leading to a shift in its strategic role on the global chessboard. The country is now seen as a swing state, capable of balancing interests with both China and the US, potentially becoming a long-term peace broker in West Asia. This opportunity requires Pakistan to diversify its security doctrine, moving away from an India-centric approach and embracing a more multi-faceted strategy, including mediation and regional security provision.  This will require adjustments to its defence hardware and strategic software.

articles.title: Bihar CM slams opposition over women's quota bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary criticized the opposition parties for their refusal to support an amendment to the women's reservation bill, calling it a "black day" and vowing retaliation. Sanjay Saraogi, state party president of the BJP, announced that the party's women's wing would hold a protest on April 20th against the opposition's stance. The amendment, which grants 33% reservation to women in Parliament, was passed by an overwhelming majority in 2023 but faced opposition from non-NDA parties who were wary of its link with delimitation.

articles.title: Iran, US still ‘far’ from breakthrough amid Strait of Hormuz impasse | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran and the United States have made progress in negotiations but remain far from a deal, according to Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.  Despite "progress," Ghalibaf stated that many gaps and fundamental points remain. The future of Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz are key sticking points. Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian criticized President Donald Trump, accusing him of depriving Tehran of its rights.  The US has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, which Ghalibaf called "ignorant" and "foolish." The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) reimposed restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz in response to the blockade.  Mediators are pushing for another round of peace talks, but no date has been set.

articles.title: Michigan gas station clerk saves teen from alleged kidnapper after she whispers ‘help’ | Michigan | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 16-year-old girl was kidnapped at gunpoint while waiting for her school bus in Hamtramck, Michigan, on April 13th. The girl's abduction led to a rescue partially attributed to convenience store employee Abdulrahman Abohatem, who noticed the girl's distress and intervened when she mouthed the word "help" to him.  Abohatem alerted authorities after confronting the kidnapper at a Sunoco gas station, leading to the arrest of Donald Fields, a 48-year-old registered sex offender. The girl was reunited with her family and praised for her courage in seeking help.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Election 2026: At least 404 candidates in T.N. have serious criminal cases against them: Report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: At least 404 candidates in the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections have declared serious criminal cases against them, according to a report released by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and Tamil Nadu Election Watch (TNEW).  The report analyzed affidavits of 3,992 candidates, revealing that 118 out of 170 from the AIADMK, 92 out of 231 from the TVK, and 70 out of 175 from the DMK have declared such cases.  Jayaram Venkatesan, State Coordinator of Arappor Iyakkam, stated that despite Supreme Court directives, political parties continue to nominate candidates with criminal records.
articles.civic_flag_reason: High number of candidates with criminal cases raises concerns about justice and representation.

articles.title: Reform UK’s Richard Tice allegedly failed to pay £100,000 in corporation tax | Richard Tice | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Richard Tice, deputy leader of Reform UK, has been accused of failing to pay almost £100,000 in corporation tax between 2020 and 2022. The Sunday Times reported that he ran four shell companies which allegedly did not pay any tax on profits during this period.  The newspaper also stated that these companies received dividends from Tice's property investment firm and passed the money to his parent company, Tisun Investments Ltd, before transferring £1,113,000 to Reform UK.

articles.title: Naidu to anchor NDA’s Tamil Nadu push with rallies and roadshows - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, will embark on a two-day campaign tour in Tamil Nadu for the upcoming elections as part of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA)'s outreach effort.  He will visit various cities including Coimbatore, Hosur, Thalli, Chennai, Madurai, and Sattur, engaging with voters and party supporters. The tour aims to energize party cadre, strengthen voter engagement, and reinforce the NDA’s development-oriented narrative.

articles.title: JioBlackRock Mutual Fund: HDFC Bank, ITC and Infosys among top 10 stock holdings in March - Portfolio check | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: JioBlackRock Mutual Fund, a new entrant in the mutual fund industry, held significant positions in several major Indian companies. The top holdings included HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, with allocations of 7.05% and 4.89%, respectively.  The fund also had substantial investments in Bharti Airtel, Reliance Industries, Larsen & Toubro, State Bank of India, Infosys, Mahindra & Mahindra, ITC, and MCX.

articles.title: Police investigate attempted arson attack at north-west London synagogue | London | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Metropolitan police are investigating an attempted arson attack at a synagogue in Harrow, north London. The incident caused minor smoke damage but no injuries or significant structural damage. The Community Security Trust, which monitors antisemitism and provides protection for Jewish communities in the UK, is working with the police to identify those responsible. This follows a string of similar incidents targeting Jewish property in the area over the past month.

articles.title: Delhi weather updates: Delhi faces poor air quality amid rising temperatures - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi experienced a minimum temperature of 21.7 degrees Celsius on Sunday, April 19th, 2026, slightly below the average for this time of year.  The India Meteorological Department predicts partly cloudy skies with a high of 40 degrees Celsius. The air quality in Delhi was recorded as 'poor' at 9 a.m., with an AQI of 238 according to the Central Pollution Control Board.

articles.title: Jubilant Foodworks and Godrej Industries - Physicswallah and Jubilant Foodworks among 9 midcap stocks that may get demoted to smallcap in AMFI rejig | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) may demote nine midcap stocks to the smallcap segment in its semi-annual review scheduled for H2 CY26.  Nuvama Institutional Equities predicts that these companies include Kaynes Technology, SJVN, Global Health, Physicswallah, K.P.R. Mill, Cholamandalam Fin Holdings and CRISIL, Jubilant Foodworks, and Godrej Industries.  The changes are based on the anticipated increase in the largecap cut-off to approximately Rs 1.04 lakh crore and the midcap threshold to around Rs 31,500 crore.

articles.title: Late bloomer Salman Mirza sets sights on 2027 World Cup - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Salman Mirza, a left-arm pacer, has set his sights on representing Pakistan at the 2027 ODI World Cup. After breaking into the national T20I setup in 2025, he has established himself as a reliable performer with impressive performances against South Africa and Bangladesh.  He credits his journey to hard work, perseverance, and adapting to professional cricket after initially playing tape-ball cricket during his youth. Salman believes that Pakistan's white-ball setup is moving in the right direction and is excited about the prospect of representing his country at the 2027 World Cup.

articles.title: Actor Parthiban moves Madras High Court seeking ‘no caste, no religion’ certificate - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Parthiban, a well-known Tamil actor, has filed a writ petition in the Madras High Court seeking a direction to consider his application for a 'no caste, no religion' certificate.  The case stems from controversy surrounding his introduction of himself as a "Naidu boy" during the promotion of a Telugu film. Parthiban claims he was born without a birth certificate and has renounced religious and caste identities but obtained certificates for his children based on their community. He argues that the caste system is unique to Hinduism and seeks a timely resolution from the authorities, citing a previous High Court ruling in favor of similar applications.

articles.title: Market Trading Guide: Buy Shipping Corporation and Power Grid on Monday for short-term gains of up to 29% - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nilesh Jain, Vice President, Head of Technical and Derivative research at Centrum Finverse, suggests a buy-on-dips approach for the market, citing support around 24,000 and potential upside to 24,700.  He notes positive momentum indicators and a softening volatility index as supportive factors. Kunal Kamble, Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza Portfolio, recommends buying Shipping Corporation with an upside target of 29% and Power Grid with an upside target of 9%.  Both stocks have broken out from consolidation patterns, indicating bullish sentiment.

articles.title: Ministers rally around Keir Starmer as leadership questions grow over Mandelson saga – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article:
Keir Starmer would have withdrawn Peter Mandelson's appointment as US ambassador if he had known the peer failed security vetting, according to Liz Kendall, his science and technology secretary.  Kendall stated that Starmer would not have continued with the appointment regardless of the timing, emphasizing that the prime minister has made "the right calls" on major issues facing the country. She also refuted claims that Starmer's poor judgment was the root of the issue, stating that the failure to inform him about Mandelson's security clearance concerns was a serious mistake.  
 
 Kendall further stated that Starmer is a man of integrity and would not have proceeded with the appointment despite any perceived embarrassment. She also criticized Sir Olly Robbins for failing to inform Starmer or the foreign secretary about the vetting advice against Mandelson's appointment.

articles.title: ED conducts raids at residences of senior cop, businessman in Kolkata over ‘money laundering’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted raids on the premises of Kolkata Police Deputy Commissioner Shantanu Sinha Biswas and another individual, Joy Kamdar, as part of a money laundering investigation into an alleged criminal syndicate in West Bengal. The raids were carried out under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) at two locations belonging to Biswas, including his residence in Ballygunge and one site associated with Kamdar, Managing Director of Sun Enterprise.

articles.title: Defence stocks breakout: Should you book profits or buy the dip? Anand James answers - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Nifty ended in the green for the second consecutive week, with analysts predicting a potential target of 25,600.  While the Nifty Smallcap 250 index has surged 15% this month and is showing strong momentum, some experts recommend a cautious approach due to overbought conditions. The Defence sector is performing well, with several stocks breaking out from consolidation zones. Analysts suggest buying opportunities on dips in select stocks like TI, Tilaknagar Industries, and IGIL.

articles.title: Rawalpindi’s Ring Road to open without Thalian interchange - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab government has decided to complete the Rawalpindi Ring Road by May, using a two-way carriageway for its functionalization.  A senior official of the divisional administration stated that work on the Thalian interchange project will not commence immediately and is planned for after the completion of the Ring Road. Deputy Project Director of Rawalpindi Ring Road Ashfaq Sulheri confirmed that the Rs5 billion Thalian interchange project would be constructed later, with the National Highway Authority (NHA) working to expand the service road to accommodate traffic demand.

articles.title: Queen Elizabeth Ii Biography: Queen Elizabeth II’s private papers opened for first official biography project | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anna Keay, chief executive of The Landmark Trust, has been appointed to write the first official biography of Queen Elizabeth II.  The project will grant her unprecedented access to personal letters, documents and records held within the Royal Archives. This decision marks a rare moment of transparency within the British Royal Family, as the archive material will span key moments from her accession in 1952 through periods of profound political and social transformation. The biography is expected to take several years to complete and will be produced with the cooperation of the Royal Household.

articles.title: Bodies of 50 infants dumped at Trinidad graveyard
articles.rephrased_article: Trinidad and Tobago police discovered the bodies of at least 50 infants and six adults dumped in a graveyard, with preliminary investigations suggesting an unlawful disposal of unclaimed corpses.  The discovery has been described as "deeply troubling" by police commissioner Allister Guevarro, who stated that those found responsible will be held accountable. The incident comes amidst ongoing concerns about crime in the country, which remains a challenge despite efforts to reduce it through security measures.

articles.title: PM Modi to address the nation tonight at 8:30 p.m. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the nation tonight at 8:30 p.m. following the defeat of a bill to implement women's reservation in legislatures in the Lok Sabha. The bill, which aimed to increase seats for women in parliament and state assemblies by 2029, was voted down despite support from 298 members.  The opposition parties opposed the bill, requiring a two-thirds majority that the ruling BJP-led alliance failed to achieve.

articles.title: 13 penny stocks plunge up to 70% in CY26. Are you affected? - Taking Stock | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ACE Equity has identified 13 penny stocks with market capitalizations below Rs 1,000 crore and share prices under Rs 20 that have experienced declines of 40% to 70% in the first half of 2026. The targeted screening approach focuses on actively traded penny stocks with a minimum trading volume of 5 lakh shares. These stocks often attract investors seeking quick gains but carry significant risks due to low liquidity, high volatility, and limited transparency.

articles.title: India LPG consumption slides 13% amid West Asia conflict - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India's LPG consumption fell by 13% in March due to supply disruptions caused by the West Asia conflict. The Oil Ministry's Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) reported a decrease of 8.1% in domestic household LPG sales and almost 48% in non-domestic sales.  To address the shortfall, the government directed refineries to divert feedstock from petrochemical production to boost LPG output, resulting in an increase in domestic production. Despite the March decline, India's overall LPG consumption for the fiscal year ended March 2026 grew by 6%.

articles.title: 11 gold ETFs offer up to 59% return since last Akshaya Tritiya. Do you own any? - Auspicious occasion | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Gold ETF, Aditya Birla Sun Life Gold ETF, and ICICI Prudential Gold ETF led the pack in returns for investors buying gold during Akshaya Tritiya, with returns ranging from 59.42% to 58.98%.  Several other Gold ETFs, including Zerodha Gold ETF, Kotak Gold ETF, and DSP Gold ETF, also saw significant gains since the last Akshaya Tritiya. Experts suggest that gold remains a valuable asset for portfolio diversification, especially during uncertain economic times.

articles.title: Kamala Harris: Kamala Harris says Donald Trump was ‘pulled into’ Iran war by Netanyahu, calls it distraction over ‘Epstein files’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kamala Harris, former US Vice President, criticized Donald Trump's foreign policy during an event hosted by the Michigan Democratic Women’s Caucus.  She alleged that Trump was "pulled into" the ongoing conflict with Iran by Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, and used the situation to distract from domestic controversies. Harris further accused Trump of being “the most corrupt, callous and incompetent” administration in US history and argued that his actions have weakened America's global influence.

articles.title: PM Modi speech row: Congress leader in Kerala moves ECI against PM Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anil Akkara, an All India Congress Committee (AICC) member from Kerala, filed a complaint with the Election Commission of India (ECI) alleging that Prime Minister Narendra Modi violated the Model Code of Conduct by using Doordarshan for politicking during the Tamil Nadu and West Bengal Assembly elections.  He argued that Modi's address on April 18, 2026, concerning women's reservation and delimitation bills, which require constitutional amendments, constituted a misuse of his official position and violated election protocols. Akkara requested legal action against Modi and the Doordarshan authorities for alleged violations of the Representation of the People Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, and other relevant laws.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Potential abuse of state-owned media for political gain during elections.

articles.title: Don’t trust the hype: Why earnings quality matters more than broker calls in today’s volatile market - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Thornton O’Glove, a veteran investor, emphasizes the importance of focusing on earnings quality over mere headline numbers. He warns that analysts, often incentivized to maintain positive coverage, may overlook negative signals in company performance.  In today's volatile market environment, where liquidity is tightening and growth expectations are uncertain, investors need to scrutinize financial statements for red flags like non-recurring gains masking weak operations or divergent cash flow from earnings. O’Glove advocates for independent analysis over consensus thinking, urging investors to delve deeper into company narratives and track trends across multiple quarters to make informed investment decisions.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia arrests over 14,000 illegal residents in week-long crackdown, thousands deported | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Interior conducted a week-long crackdown on illegal residents, resulting in the arrest of 14,487 individuals. The arrests were made between April 9 and April 15, with violations including residency law breaches (7,911), border security regulations (3,588), and labor law violations (2,988).  Authorities have deported 12,554 people and referred others to secure travel documents. The ministry also intercepted illegal entrants and arrested individuals aiding violators.

articles.title: Three women held in Sialkot for beggary in KSA - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) arrested four individuals, including three women from Islamabad, at Sialkot airport for engaging in organized begging in Saudi Arabia. The group arrived from Saudi Arabia via Oman and admitted to the activity after being questioned by immigration officials.  They had obtained visas and tickets through an agent, Muhammad Siddique Akbar, who facilitated their travel for Rs250,000 per person. The FIA will seek the deportation of the main agent involved in the beggary racket in Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh CM wishes Pawan Kalyan speedy recovery - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed his well wishes for the speedy recovery of Deputy Chief Minister K. Pawan Kalyan, who underwent surgery at a private hospital in Hyderabad on April 18th, according to a statement from the Jana Sena Party.  The surgery was performed due to a serious condition that arose during Kalyan's administrative duties on April 17th. Doctors advised him to rest for at least a week and take necessary precautions.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh implements advanced unified command system under Jal Jeevan Mission - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Uttar Pradesh's government has launched a statewide SCADA-enabled monitoring framework integrated with advanced automation technologies under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM).  The system, managed through the Unified Command and Control System (UCCS), will monitor water supply parameters like quality, distribution efficiency, and asset performance across rural areas using approximately 0.7 million IoT-enabled sensors. The initiative aims to ensure regular water supply in adequate quantity and prescribed quality for the state's estimated 17 crore population.  The system is expected to improve service delivery at the grassroots level by providing real-time insights and facilitating automated grievance redressal, according to Anurag Srivastava, Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) for the Namami Gange & Rural Water Supply Department, Uttar Pradesh.

articles.title: 13 penny stocks plunge up to 70% in CY26. Are you affected? - Taking Stock | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: ACE Equity identified 13 penny stocks with market capitalizations below Rs 1,000 crore and share prices under Rs 20 that have experienced declines of 40% to 70% in 2026.  The screening strategy targets low-priced, actively traded penny stocks known for their high volatility and potential for manipulation. Investors should be aware of the risks associated with these investments before entering the market.

articles.title: Wife of ‘facilitator’ held in Nokundi FC headquarters suicide blast case - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces in Quetta have arrested the wife of an alleged facilitator of a female suicide bomber who targeted the Frontier Corps (FC) headquarters last year.  The arrest of Rahima Bibi, the wife of the alleged facilitator, provided key leads in the investigation. Officials believe that her husband facilitated the attack and later fled to Afghanistan with an unidentified woman and her children. The suspect's husband allegedly used his wife's identity to obtain a SIM card and maintain contact with terrorists.  Babar Khan Yousafzai, the aide of home department affairs, stated that this case highlights how terrorist groups are exploiting women for their activities.

articles.title: Trinidad and Tobago police uncover 56 bodies, mostly children, at cemetery | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Trinidad and Tobago police discovered 56 bodies, mostly children, abandoned at a cemetery in the town of Cumuto. The discovery has prompted an investigation into potential unlawful disposal of unclaimed corpses. Police Commissioner Allister Guevarro acknowledged the disturbing nature of the find and pledged to uncover the truth with urgency and sensitivity.  The police service is working alongside specialized units including homicide experts to determine the origin of the remains and any associated breaches of law or procedure.

articles.title: Mark Carney Visit Gurdwara Sahib Ottawa: Watch: Canada PM Mark Carney celebrates Sikh Heritage Month, joins community service at Ottawa gurdwara - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney visited Gurdwara Sahib Ottawa on Saturday as part of Sikh Heritage Month 2026 celebrations. He emphasized the significance of the Sikh community in Canada, noting its second-largest population globally.  The month features cultural and community events across the country, including an exhibition titled "Baaghi ja Badshah" exploring Sikh history and a celebration of Vaisakhi with performances highlighting Sikh values.

articles.title: Scams have grown more sophisticated, but people are fighting back
articles.rephrased_article: Scammers are becoming increasingly sophisticated, targeting individuals with elaborate schemes. Victims like Kirsty, a woman in the UK who lost £80,000 to a Nigerian scammer posing as an English businessman, fall prey to these international scams.  The Global Anti-Scam Alliance reports that global fraud losses have surpassed half a trillion dollars annually, and romance scams such as Kirsty's rose by 20% between 2024 and 2025. The UK government has stated that 70% of scams originate from overseas criminal gangs, while the UN Office on Drugs and Crime highlights the challenges posed by lawless areas where law enforcement struggles to operate.  To combat this growing problem, a joint agreement was signed between nations at the Global Fraud Summit in Vienna, aiming to disrupt fraud networks and enhance victim support. However, there is still a need for greater international cooperation and collaboration between governments, tech companies, and law enforcement agencies to effectively tackle these evolving scams.

articles.title: Explained: India tried to pass 33% reservation for women, it failed. Here’s why - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The 131st Amendment Bill, part of the delimitation package, was defeated in the Lok Sabha. Parliament members voted against the bill, which aimed to amend electoral boundaries and voting rights. The defeat is a significant development in the ongoing debate surrounding electoral reforms.

articles.title: 11 gold ETFs offer up to 59% return since last Akshaya Tritiya. Do you own any? - Auspicious occasion | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Tata Gold ETF, Aditya Birla Sun Life Gold ETF, and ICICI Prudential Gold ETF led the pack in returns for investors during Akshaya Tritiya, with gains ranging from 59.42% to 58.98%.  Several other gold ETFs like Zerodha Gold ETF, Kotak Gold ETF, and DSP Gold ETF also saw significant returns, highlighting the appeal of investing in gold during this auspicious occasion. Experts recommend allocating a portion of your portfolio to gold for its potential as a hedge against inflation and economic uncertainty.

articles.title: Real Sociedad upset Atletico Madrid to win fourth Copa del Rey title | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Real Sociedad defeated Atletico Madrid 4-3 on penalties to win their fourth Copa del Rey title in Seville.  After a dramatic match that ended 2-2 after extra time, Unai Marrero made two crucial saves in the shootout, securing victory for the Basque side. This marks a significant turnaround for Real Sociedad, who were hovering above relegation before winning the trophy under new manager Pellegrino Matarazzo.  Atletico Madrid, meanwhile, will focus on their Champions League campaign with a last-four matchup against Arsenal.

articles.title: United Airlines Emergency Landing: ‘Possible security issue’: United Airlines flight diverted, passengers evacuated via emergency slides in Pittsburgh - watch - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to New York was diverted to Pittsburgh International Airport on Saturday after crew members detected a "beeping noise" during the flight, prompting them to treat it as a potential bomb threat.  The aircraft landed safely with no injuries reported and authorities conducted a thorough search of the plane, passengers, and luggage. The FBI, bomb squad, and other law enforcement agencies cleared the aircraft after finding no explosive device.

articles.title: Chernobyl's last wedding: The couple who married as a nuclear disaster unfolded
articles.rephrased_article: On April 26, 1986, a wedding in Pripyat was disrupted by the Chernobyl nuclear disaster. Iryna Stetsenko and Serhiy Lobanov, who were looking forward to married life in the newly built Soviet city, witnessed the explosion of reactor four at the nearby power plant. Despite official attempts to downplay the incident, radiation levels rose, forcing them to evacuate their home and flee to Berlin. The couple's wedding was a somber affair, with the growing realization that a tragedy had unfolded casting a shadow on their celebration.  Decades later, they continue to grapple with health issues stemming from the disaster, but remain united in their love.

articles.title: Vice-President embarks on two-day visit to Sri Lanka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vice-President of India C.P. Radhakrishnan began a two-day official visit to Sri Lanka on April 19, 2026.  During his trip, Radhakrishnan met with President Anura Kumara Disanayaka and Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya, as well as members of the Indian-origin Tamil community. The Vice-President also addressed the Indian diaspora in Colombo, where he virtually handed over houses to beneficiaries from Tamil communities under the Indian Housing Project.  This visit is expected to further strengthen ties between India and Sri Lanka.

articles.title: Can Sensex, Nifty extend gains on Monday? Oil prices, 5 factors to guide Dalal Street this week - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Indian stock markets are experiencing a recovery fueled by optimism surrounding the potential resolution of the Iran-US conflict and positive economic indicators.  The Strait of Hormuz is now open, Brent crude prices dropped significantly, and major banks reported strong quarterly earnings. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, and Yes Bank all saw significant profit increases. The Indian rupee has strengthened against the US dollar, and foreign investors remain net buyers of Indian equities.  The near-term outlook for the market remains positive, with analysts expecting continued momentum based on improving sentiment and a potential breakout above resistance levels.

articles.title: Titanic life jacket worn by survivor sold for £670,000 ($906,000) at UK auction | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A life jacket worn by Laura Mabel Francatelli, a first-class passenger on the Titanic, sold at auction for £670,000 ($906,000), exceeding its estimated value. The flotation device, signed by other survivors from the same lifeboat, was purchased by an anonymous bidder and is expected to reflect continued public interest in the Titanic story.  The sale also included a seat cushion from one of the Titanic's lifeboats, which was purchased by owners of Titanic museums in the United States.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election: flames of DMK’s black flag protest burnt down BJP’s saffron flag, asserts Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M.K. Stalin, president of the DMK, compared his burning of a copy of the Constitution Amendment Bill to its defeat in Parliament on April 17th, stating that the flames of the protest had extinguished BJP's saffron flag.  While campaigning for candidates in Tiruppur district, he sang a song from Rajnikanth's film "Rajadhi Raja," emphasizing Tamil Nadu's strength and resilience.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly Elections 2026 | Pattas, startups and safety top priority in Saidapet, says TVK’s Arul Prakasam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Arul Prakasam, candidate for the Saidapet Assembly Constituency, has pledged to prioritize issuing land titles (pattas) if elected.  He stated that TVK will deliver pattas within 100 days to six months, highlighting a long-standing demand from residents and contrasting it with other parties' promises without action.

articles.title: In a first, migratory honey bees get ‘warm womb’ to stay back in winters in Kashmir - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: CSIR-IIIM, in collaboration with beekeepers, has developed protocols and scientific interventions to allow honey bee colonies to survive sub-zero temperatures in Jammu and Kashmir. This innovation eliminates the need for physical hive migration to warmer regions, reducing mortality rates by 30%. The initiative also resulted in the production of the first mono-floral apple honey in Kashmir.

articles.title: BJP will never understand the self-respect of Telangana: Ponnam Prabhakar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ponnam Prabhakar, the Welfare Minister of Telangana, criticized the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for comparing the state's struggle for independence to the partition of India and attempting to undermine its political existence through a "ridiculous" delimitation process.  He accused BJP leaders of being "Betrayers of Telangana" for justifying the remarks made by Tejasvi Surya, a BJP MP, in Parliament.

articles.title: North Korea conducts fresh missile tests at sea; South Korea on alert - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles into the sea on Sunday, prompting South Korea, Japan, and the US Indo-Pacific Command to express concern.  The launches were detected by Japan's Defence Ministry who lodged a protest with Pyongyang, while the US Indo-Pacific Command stated that there is no immediate threat to US personnel or territory. The South Korean presidential office will convene an emergency meeting to assess the situation.

articles.title: Daylight bank heist in Singrauli: One accused held; M.P. police launch manhunt in four States - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kamlesh Kumar, an accused in a bank robbery of over ₹15 crore in Madhya Pradesh's Singrauli, was arrested by the Railway Protection Force (RPF) near Aurangabad's Nabinagar station on Saturday. Kumar was found in suspicious condition and questioned before being apprehended.  Cash worth ₹15 lakh and some gold were recovered from him.

articles.title: Pakistan returned $2bn to UAE, says its central bank - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's central bank returned $2 billion in debt to the United Arab Emirates, following a request from the UAE government. The move comes after Saudi Arabia deposited $2 billion, part of a $3 billion aid package, with the SBP earlier this week. The funds were held as a safe deposit pending the resolution of international tensions and are now being returned.

articles.title: APTF members stage protest in Ongole demanding to resolve teachers’ issues - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh Teachers’ Federation (APTF) president Chennupati Manjula led a protest at Prakasam Bhavan in Ongole, demanding the government address issues facing teachers and employees in the state's education sector.  Manjula stated that dharnas are being held across 28 district centers, highlighting the Coalition government's failure to fulfill election promises regarding long-pending employee and teacher concerns after two years in power.

articles.title: With 60 Kirk-themed bills, 20+ US states seek to promote his ideology - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Charlie Kirk, a conservative activist, has inspired numerous state-level tributes and bills promoting his ideology.  In Kansas, a new law allows college students to sue their schools for free speech violations in the name of Kirk. In Tennessee, a bill encourages the inclusion of "the positive impacts of religion" in American history courses.  These laws are among over 60 proposed tributes to Kirk across 20 states, reflecting his influence on conservative legislation.

articles.title: MP Rashid’s party moves bail application to attend ailing father in Srinagar; NC’s Farooq Abdullah demands release - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Awami Ittehad Party (AIP) filed an interim bail application for jailed party chief Engineer Rashid to visit his critically ill father in Srinagar.  Dr. Farooq Abdullah, president of the National Conference (NC), also demanded Rashid's release, emphasizing the humanitarian aspect of the situation. Several legislators and leaders from various parties visited the hospital where Rashid's father is being treated.

articles.title: With 60 Kirk-themed bills, 20+ US states seek to promote his ideology - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Charlie Kirk, a conservative activist who was killed while speaking at a Utah university last year, is the driving force behind several new laws in multiple states. Kansas enacted a law allowing college students to sue their schools for free-speech violations, and Tennessee passed legislation encouraging teachers to include "the positive impacts of religion" in American history courses.  These are among over 60 Kirk-themed bills proposed in 20 states seeking to promote his ideology.

articles.title: Chenchu women oppose relocation from Amrabad Tiger Reserve - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chenchu women from the Amrabad Tiger Reserve are protesting against a proposed relocation order, arguing that their traditional foraging practices and livelihoods would be severely disrupted. They claim they have not received forest pattas or housing assistance, and fear losing access to essential resources like water and electricity. The women, who are classified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG), argue that the government's offer of compensation and rehabilitation packages is insufficient and that their rights will be jeopardized if they are forced to relocate. They have presented their concerns to the Prajavani program in Hyderabad, demanding the preservation of their traditional way of life within the forest.
