Sridhar Babu, Minister for IT and Industries of Telangana, urged the defense industry, research laboratories, and scientists to collaborate with the state government to build a strong aerospace ecosystem in Hyderabad. He highlighted the region's existing infrastructure, talent pool, and dedicated aerospace clusters, noting that over 1,500 firms contribute to global aerospace supply chains within Telangana.

articles.title: Opposition defeated an attack on the Constitution, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition, hailed the defeat of the Constitution Amendment Bill concerning women's reservation as a victory for the Indian Constitution. He argued that the bill was not a genuine attempt to empower women but a political maneuver aimed at altering India's electoral framework. The bill failed to garner the necessary two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha.

articles.title: From ultra left to campaigner for Tamil Brahmins - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. S. Pandiarajan, a Madurai lawyer, experienced a rift with the CPI(ML) in the 1980s after being passed over for leadership despite his long-standing commitment.  He alleges that he was told his Brahmin heritage disqualified him, prompting his departure from the party. He believes this caste discrimination was unique to Tamil Nadu and contradicts the party's stated principles of inclusivity.

articles.title: US Congress passes 10-day extension of surveillance law amid Republican infighting | US Congress | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Congress voted to extend a controversial warrantless surveillance law, Section 702, for 10 days after Republican infighting stalled plans for a longer renewal.  The extension was passed by both chambers of Congress despite opposition from privacy advocates and dissenting lawmakers who argued the bill did not address their demands for a warrant requirement for Americans' communications collected under the program.  Jim McGovern (D-MA) criticized the late-night vote as a "shameful midnight smash-and-grab attempt" to steal away Americans' privacy rights.

articles.title: Nine killed as van carrying Malappuram schoolteachers plunges off Valparai cliff - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nine members of a 12-person excursion group from Pang in Kuruva panchayat, Malappuram district, were killed when their van crashed off a cliff at Valparai in Tamil Nadu. The incident occurred on Friday afternoon, with the remaining members transported to hospitals for treatment. Three critically injured individuals were transferred to a hospital in Coimbatore for advanced care.

articles.title: Yogeeshgouda Goudar’s sister celebrates conviction - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vinay Kulkarni, a former Congress MLA, and 16 others were sentenced to life in prison for the murder of BJP zilla panchayat member Yogeeshgouda Goudar in 2016.  The victim's sister, Akkamahadevi, expressed relief at the verdict after ten years of waiting.

articles.title: Starmer was kept in dark about Mandelson’s vetting by two other top civil servants | Peter Mandelson | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer was kept uninformed about a security vetting failure involving Peter Mandelson, the prime minister's former chief of staff, and two other top civil servants.  The head of the Foreign Office, Olly Robbins, was forced out after failing to inform Starmer that Mandelson had been cleared despite UK Security Vetting (UKSV) recommending against it. The Cabinet Secretary, Antonia Romeo, and Catherine Little, the permanent secretary at the Cabinet Office, were aware of the vetting failure since March but delayed informing Starmer.  The issue has sparked concerns about whether the government is being run by civil servants rather than ministers.

articles.title: When a star madean impact on the poll outcome in Tamil Nadu - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's political landscape has long been intertwined with the film industry, as evidenced by past electoral contests. In the 1990s, Jayalalithaa, then Chief Minister of AIADMK, and M. Karunanidhi, leader of the DMK-led coalition, engaged in a fierce rivalry.  Rajinikanth, known for his charisma, entered this volatile political environment during that period.

articles.title: Chaturvedi’s grumbling over defeat of Women’s Bill’ flies in the face of her party’s stand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shiv Sena UBT leader Priyanka Chaturvedi criticized the defeat of the Women’s Reservation Bill in the Lok Sabha, expressing her opposition to its inclusion with the Delimitation Bill. Sanjay Raut, a Shiv Sena UBT MP, stated that the party opposed the bill because it was presented as a means for the BJP to advance their own agenda. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis condemned the opposition's actions, calling them hypocritical and stating that they prioritized politics over progress.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The defeat of the Women's Reservation Bill raises concerns about institutional failure to advance women's rights.

articles.title: Police say no evidence found of reported gang-rape in Epsom | Surrey | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Surrey police have stated they have not found any evidence of a rape reported on April 11th in Epsom, prompting protests from the community. The investigation is ongoing, and police are reviewing CCTV footage, interviewing witnesses, conducting forensic investigations, and doing house-to-house inquiries.  The force has acknowledged the speculation surrounding the lack of suspect information, particularly regarding ethnicity, but clarified that this is due to limited information about the incident and potential suspects.

articles.title: It’ a red-letter day, says Revanth; KTR blames BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Following the defeat of the Women's Reservation Bill in Parliament, Congress and Bharatiya Rashtra Samithi (BRS) leaders praised opposition parties for uniting to block the controversial legislation.  Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, and A. Revanth Reddy led the charge against the bill, with K. T. Rama Rao blaming the BJP for its failure. Bandi Sanjay accused the Congress of using the bill to weaken southern India, while N Ramchander Rao criticized the bill's defeat as a setback for women's empowerment.

articles.title: Chinese researcher on J-1 visa pleads guilty to smuggling E. coli bacteria into US disguised as women’s underwear - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Youhuang Xiang, a Chinese researcher working in the United States, pleaded guilty to smuggling E. coli into the country.  He admitted to concealing bacterial DNA in a shipment falsely labeled as women's underwear and was sentenced to over four months in prison. FBI Director Kash Patel warned that such actions pose serious risks and are an example of exploiting US visa privileges for illegal activity. The case follows similar incidents involving foreign researchers attempting to smuggle biological materials into the country, including Chinese nationals at a University of Michigan laboratory and a Russian-born Harvard researcher who brought frog embryos without permits.

articles.title: India fails to pass bill to boost women’s representation after delimitation row | India | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian government failed to pass a bill increasing female representation in parliament after accusations of using it as a cover for electoral map redrawing. The bill, requiring a two-thirds majority, was opposed by the opposition who argued it was an attempt to manipulate the electoral process and unfairly benefit certain states.  This failure marks the first time in 12 years that a constitutional amendment proposed by Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) government failed to pass parliament.

articles.title: United Opposition defeated bid to harm Constitution: Kharge - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and other opposition leaders celebrated the defeat of a bill seeking to redraw India's political map based on the 2011 Census. Kharge thanked opposition parties for their united effort, while K.C. Venugopal, another Congress leader, expressed willingness to support the government if it implements women's reservation immediately.  D. Raja, CPI general secretary, and John Brittas, a CPI(M) MP, criticized the bill as a ploy by the Modi government to manipulate elections for political gain.

articles.title: Protests erupt after Epsom church assault claim, police find no proof - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Surrey Police are investigating an alleged assault near a church in Epsom, but have found no evidence to support the claim despite extensive inquiries. The investigation began after a young woman reported feeling followed while leaving a venue late on Saturday night.  The incident sparked online speculation and protests, with demonstrators calling for greater transparency from authorities. Surrey Police have increased patrols in the area and urged residents to rely on verified updates during the ongoing investigation.

articles.title: Watch: Constitution Amendment Bill, part of delimitation package, defeated - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Lok Sabha rejected the Constitution Amendment Bill on women's quota, while Sri Lanka’s Power and Energy Minister resigned amidst controversy.  Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, easing global shipping concerns. The Supreme Court flagged illegal sand mining in Madhya Pradesh.

articles.title: Three in court over attempted arson attack at Persian media company in London | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Oisin McGuinness, Nathan Dunn, and a 16-year-old boy appeared in court on Friday charged with arson with intent to endanger life after an attempted firebombing of the offices of Volant Media, the parent company of Persian news channel Iran International. The incident occurred at approximately 8:30 pm on Wednesday, when officers responded to reports of an ignited container thrown towards the site in Wembley.  The suspects fled the scene in a black four-wheel-drive vehicle and no injuries were reported.

articles.title: ADG visits NCC units in Kozhikode, Malappuram - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Major General Arun C.G., the newly appointed Additional Director General (ADG) of the National Cadet Corps (NCC), Kerala and Lakshadweep Directorate, conducted a two-day official review of NCC units in the region. During his visits to Kozhikode and Malappuram districts, he inspected various establishments, interacted with officers, staff, and cadets, and emphasized the importance of leadership engagement in reinforcing core values and mission. The visit was part of efforts to highlight the significance of leadership within the NCC.

articles.title: Julius Malema: What next for South African opposition firebrand?
articles.rephrased_article: Julius Malema, leader of the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), has been sentenced to five years in prison for unlawful firearm possession and public discharge.  He will appeal the conviction but not the sentence, meaning he can continue as a member of parliament until the appeals process is complete. Political analysts believe this could benefit his political career by garnering sympathy and strengthening his party's position.

articles.title: Nursery worker jailed for three years over death of 14-month-old boy in her care | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kimberley Cookson, a 23-year-old nursery worker, was sentenced to three years and four months in prison for gross negligence manslaughter after the death of 14-month-old Noah Sibanda. Deborah Latewood, owner of the Fairytales Day Nursery where the incident occurred, received a suspended six-month sentence for health and safety offenses. The nursery was fined £240,000 for corporate manslaughter and failure to comply with health and safety regulations. CCTV footage showed Cookson restraining Noah face-down with a blanket while attempting to put him to sleep, leaving him unchecked for two hours before his death.  Noah's parents expressed their grief and anger at the nursery's negligence.

articles.title: South stood united, made its voice heard and democracy prevailed: T.N. CM Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The BJP-led Union government's attempt to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha through a Bill that included 33% reservation for women in the House failed in the Lok Sabha.  DMK president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M. K. Stalin stated that the South stood united, made its voice heard, and democracy prevailed. He emphasized that delimitation should strengthen the Union, not weaken it, and called for fairness and consultation in any future attempts at reform.

articles.title: Is Mandelson vetting scandal the final straw for Starmer? –The Latest | Keir Starmer | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer expressed his shock and disapproval at learning that Peter Mandelson had been cleared for the US ambassador role despite initial security concerns.  The revelation, confirmed by a Guardian investigation, came after Mandelson was initially denied clearance due to a background check. The Foreign Office overruled this decision.

articles.title: BJP to take to streets over defeat of women’s quota Bill in Lok Sabha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: BJP national president Nitin Nabin announced that the party and its allies would take to the streets to protest the defeat of the Constitutional Amendment Bill on women's reservation and the Delimitation Bill.  Following the Bills' failure in the Lok Sabha, a meeting was held by J. P. Nadda, the Leader of the House in the Rajya Sabha.  Nabin criticized the Congress for betraying women's rights and vowed to mobilize public support against the opposition. Women MPs from the NDA protested outside Parliament.

articles.title: Record number of Rohingya refugees died at sea last year, UNHCR says | Refugees News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The UNHCR reported that nearly 900 Rohingya refugees died or went missing at sea in 2025, marking the deadliest year on record for maritime movements in South and Southeast Asia.  This tragic trend highlights the perilous journeys undertaken by Rohingya fleeing persecution in Myanmar, with thousands attempting to reach Malaysia or Indonesia despite limited opportunities and ongoing conflict. The UNHCR hopes increased awareness of this crisis will lead to solutions to prevent further loss of life.

articles.title: Daniel Kinahan arrested in Dubai over serious organised crime
articles.rephrased_article: Daniel Kinahan, a suspected Irish crime boss, was arrested in Dubai on April 15th after an extradition warrant issued by the Irish courts.  The US government imposed sanctions on him in 2022 for his alleged involvement with the Kinahan organized crime cartel. The arrest follows an investigation into his alleged role in an international criminal network and is part of efforts to combat cross-border crime. Dubai police say they arrested the Irish national after intensive search and surveillance operations, based on a judicial file from Irish authorities detailing his crimes and involvement.

articles.title: Four Maoists killed in exchange of fire with security forces in Jharkhand - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jharkhand Police and the 209 COBRA Battalion conducted a joint operation in the forest region between Hazaribagh and Chatra, resulting in the deaths of four Maoists.  The deceased included Shahdev Mahto, a regional committee member with a ₹15 lakh reward; Ranjit Ganjhu, a zonal committee member with a ₹10 lakh reward; Natasha, a sub-zonal committee member with a 17-case record; and Budhan Karmali, an area commander with a ₹1 lakh reward.  The operation also recovered weapons and other items of daily use, according to the police who claim it has neutralized the Maoist squad active in the region. The police have appealed for remaining militants to surrender.

articles.title: 'No money is changing hands': Trump rejects $20 billion Iran 'nuclear dust' deal claim - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump announced major breakthroughs in the US military mission against Iran, claiming the suspension of Tehran's nuclear program and the reopening of the strategic Strait of Hormuz.  He stated that Iran's nuclear ambitions have been effectively shut down, and a broader deal to end the conflict is close to completion. Trump also indicated that talks on a lasting agreement would likely take place over the weekend. He asserted that the US will secure "nuclear dust" from Iran without financial exchange and that negotiations with Iran are progressing well.

articles.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary launches self-enumeration phase of Census 2027 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary launched the self-enumeration phase of Census 2027 from the Chief Minister’s Secretariat, urging citizens to participate in the process. The initiative will be conducted digitally from April 17th to May 1st and includes a House Listing Operations (HLO) phase from May 2nd to May 31st. Mr. Choudhary emphasized the importance of accurate data for good governance and development plans, while former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar also completed his self-enumeration.  The web-based platform allows citizens to enter their family details online at their convenience.

articles.title: Boston Marathon 2026: Check latest expected race conditions, date, route and weather forecast | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Boston Athletic Association (B.A.A.) is hosting the 130th Boston Marathon on Monday, April 20th, with over 30,000 runners expected to participate. The race follows its established route from Hopkinton to Boston, covering a distance of 26.2 miles and passing through eight Massachusetts towns before finishing on Boylston Street at Copley Square.  The event is anticipated to generate more than $509 million for the Greater Boston area, while 193 non-profit organizations are involved through the Bank of America Boston Marathon Official Charity Program. The marathon will be held alongside other events in Boston, including a baseball game between the Detroit Tigers and the Boston Red Sox.

articles.title: Constitution Amendment Bill, part of delimitation package, defeated - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Opposition defeated a Constitutional Amendment Bill that aimed to redistribute Lok Sabha seats based on the 2011 census to expedite women's reservation. The bill, which received 298 votes in favor and 230 against, fell short of the two-thirds majority needed for passage. Union Home Minister Amit Shah argued that the bill was necessary to address population growth and uphold the "one person, one vote, one value" principle.

articles.title: Sunita Williams to run 130th Boston Marathon, returning after barefoot teen run and historic space marathon | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sunita Williams, a former NASA astronaut and Needham, Massachusetts native, will participate in the 130th Boston Marathon on Monday, April 20.  The marathon, which stretches 26.2 miles from Hopkinton to Back Bay, is expected to feature over 30,000 runners from around the world. Williams, who holds the record for the most spacewalking time by a woman, will receive the Patriots’ Award from the Boston Athletic Association during the race.  The event is known for its challenging conditions and diverse participants, including elite runners, amateur athletes, and charity participants.

articles.title: Jacinta Allan wants voters to see Victoria’s 12-year-old Labor government as ‘new and united’. Can she cling to power? | Victorian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Jacinta Allan, the Victorian premier, reshuffled her cabinet on Wednesday, attempting to present a fresh image for her long-serving government.  The move followed resignations of several ministers and left the new cabinet almost unrecognizable from its predecessor. Allan appointed four backbenchers to fill the vacancies, including Luba Grigorovitch, who was chosen by the right faction despite concerns about her past support for former union boss John Setka. The reshuffle also saw promotions for MPs close to Allan, but it did not fully address leadership challenges within the party.  The government faces numerous external challenges, including a high court ruling on election donations and ongoing issues with fuel supply.

articles.title: Tipra Motha scores massive win in TTAADC polls; BJP suffers defeat - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tipra Motha, led by royal scion Pradyot Kishore Manikya, secured a landslide victory in the Tripura Tribal Areas Autonomous District Council (TTAADC) elections, winning over three-quarters of seats. The party won 24 out of 28 seats, while the BJP garnered only four.  The BJP's unexpected defeat surprised them after they had invested heavily in campaigning for months.

articles.title: Row over anti-Islam US influencer granted UK visa approval, calls out British leaders: 'England belongs to...' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Valentina Gomez, a US-based far-right influencer, has been granted a UK Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) despite facing criticism for anti-Islam content.  She is scheduled to speak at Tommy Robinson's "Unite the Kingdom" rally in London on May 16th and her appearance has drawn condemnation from activists and commentators who question why she was granted permission to enter the UK.  The controversy comes amid tensions over a planned pro-Palestine march on the same day as the rally, raising security concerns due to past violence at similar events.

articles.title: NSW should think twice before banning ‘globalise the intifada’ after court struck down anti-protest law, legal expert says | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Minns government should reconsider its plan to ban the phrase "globalise the intifada" after a landmark court ruling that limits attempts to control speech and protests. The New South Wales Court of Appeal struck down an anti-protest law, finding that suppressing all protests to protect social cohesion was not legitimate under the constitution. Constitutional expert Anne Twomey suggests any future attempts by the government to restrict political expression should focus on preventing violence rather than simply causing distress or offense.  The court's decision could have significant implications for future attempts to ban political slogans and regulate protests, potentially impacting charges against protesters involved in the anti-Herzog rally.

articles.title: House approves short-term extension of surveillance law in blow to Republicans’ long-term plan – US politics live | US Congress | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The House of Representatives voted to extend a controversial surveillance law, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), until April 30th. The decision came after unanimous consent and followed bipartisan opposition to five-year and 18-month renewals.  Republicans joined Democrats in voting for the short-term extension, with some Democrats expressing concerns about warrantless surveillance and its potential impact on American privacy. The law allows the government to collect communications of foreigners living outside the country without a warrant, raising concerns from critics who argue it enables the US government to spy on Americans.  The move comes amidst ongoing tensions between the Trump administration and congressional Democrats over surveillance practices.

articles.title: Balen Shah: Nepal's Government Launches Historic Probe into Assets of Former Leaders and Officials | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The newly formed Balendra Shah government in Nepal has established a five-member judicial panel to investigate the assets of public officials from 2006 to the current fiscal year. The inquiry will encompass former kings, presidents, prime ministers, and senior bureaucrats, including figures like former president Ram Baran Yadav and PM Sher Bahadur Deuba. Rajendra Kumar Bhandari, retired Supreme Court judge, heads the commission, which is expected to examine assets based on evidence and legal standards. While the Nepali Congress supports the probe, concerns have been raised about its potential politicization and lack of permanent legal framework.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Investigating past leaders' assets for potential corruption is a positive step.

articles.title: The three clocks of the Iran war | Opinions | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump, facing a precarious political position with midterm elections looming, is racing against time to secure a resolution in the Iran conflict. Iran, meanwhile, aims to outlast him by enduring the war's consequences until November. Benjamin Netanyahu, seeking to maintain public support and advance his regional ambitions, prioritizes prolonging the conflict indefinitely. The three protagonists are locked in a battle of wills, each operating on a different political clock with their own unique deadlines.  The outcome will be determined by who can best navigate this complex geopolitical landscape and secure an advantageous "morning after."

articles.title: On this day: Modern snooker was invented in 1875 in India by Sir Neville Chamberlain, a bored British officer | International Sports News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sir Neville Chamberlain, serving with the 11th Devonshire Regiment, in India in 1875, adapted a game of black pool by introducing additional colored balls and a different sequence of play. He named this new version "snooker" and it was not until 1938 that he formally identified himself as its originator. The game spread organically from officers' clubs to billiards halls and eventually gained structure with the Billiards Association and Control Club establishing standardized rules in 1919.  The introduction of the professional World Snooker Championship in 1927 solidified the sport's competitive framework, with figures like Joe Davis becoming key players. Television exposure in the 1960s brought snooker to a wider audience and contemporary stars such as Ray Reardon, Alex Higgins, Steve Davis, and Dennis Taylor further popularized the game.

articles.title: Birmingham is awash with local election candidates – but will result be a ‘coalition of chaos’? | Birmingham | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming local elections in Birmingham are expected to be a chaotic and fragmented affair, with no single party predicted to win an overall majority. Paul Tilsley, the Lib Dem candidate for the seat, believes this will lead to a "bugger's muddle" as opposing factions struggle to form a coalition.  Akhmed Yakoob, an independent candidate running on a platform of change and outsider status, is hoping to capitalize on Labour's perceived failures. Shahid Butt, another independent candidate with a controversial past, has also entered the race. The Green party and Reform are vying for voters disillusioned with mainstream parties, while John Cotton, the leader of Birmingham City Council, emphasizes the importance of electing "serious people" capable of working together to address the city's challenges.

articles.title: Indian-origin politician Charishma Kaliyanda in Australia slams Liverpool mayor for doxxing her address: 'Completely unacceptable' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Charishma Kaliyanda, an Indian-origin Labor MP, accused Liverpool mayor Ned Mannoun of doxxing her after her home address was shared on social media during a heated by-election campaign.  Kaliyanda stated that the incident put her safety at risk and called it "completely unacceptable" and "potential criminal conduct." While Mannoun deleted the original post, he apologized for its publication. The row escalated into a tense clash at a pre-polling station, with police called to intervene after verbal arguments between candidates.

articles.title: IIT Palakkad expands academic, research initiatives - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: IIT Palakkad has launched several new initiatives to enhance its technological capabilities and research opportunities. The institute established a Department of Materials and Metallurgical Engineering, will introduce a BTech program in Materials Engineering starting in 2026-27, and set up the Madhava Supercomputing Facility in collaboration with C-DAC, Pune.  The facility is designed to support advanced computational research and enhance interdisciplinary research capabilities at the institute. Additionally, a 500 MHz Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectrometer has been established to strengthen scientific instrumentation facilities.

articles.title: Islamabad administration denies claims regarding closure of transport terminals - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad and Rawalpindi administrations have refuted reports of transport terminal closures, stating that all bus terminals in both cities are open and operating as usual.  Islamabad's Deputy Commissioner Irfaz Nawaz Memon and the Islamabad Traffic Police confirmed this, urging citizens to rely on verified information from official channels. Rawalpindi's Deputy Commissioner Hassan Waqar Cheema also stated that all types of transport were operational in the district.

articles.title: Extraemily Controversy: ExtraEmily under fire for alleged viewbotting after viral clip - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A controversy erupted on social media after a clip from ExtraEmily's Twitch stream showed a website labeled "ViewBot.ai," sparking speculation that she may have used a viewbotting service to artificially inflate her viewer count. The incident spread to Reddit's r/LivestreamFail community, where users debated the validity of the claims. While moderators initially attributed the appearance of the website to a redirect, some users disputed this explanation and pointed out inconsistencies in its design. Fellow streamer Mizkif expressed doubt about viewbotting, stating he did not see evidence of artificial inflation based on ExtraEmily's typical viewer numbers.  The controversy remains unresolved as ExtraEmily has yet to address the allegations.

articles.title: Decisions on Karnataka leadership rests with Congress high command: Home Minister G. Parameshwara - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Home Minister G. Parameshwara stated that decisions regarding leadership in the Karnataka government will be made by the Congress high command. He dismissed claims of helplessness from former minister K.N. Rajanna, emphasizing that all 224 legislators are eligible for ministerial positions.  He also highlighted ongoing police reforms including technological upgrades and the e-beat system, as well as efforts to address technical challenges in recruitment.  Parameshwara acknowledged the court's verdict on Vinay Kulkarni's sentence but emphasized that the law applies equally to all.

articles.title: Islamabad administration denies claims regarding closure of transport terminals - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad and Rawalpindi administrations have refuted reports of the closure of transport terminals in both cities.  Islamabad's Deputy Commissioner Irfaz Nawaz Memon confirmed that all bus terminals are open, with inter-city transport operating as usual. The Islamabad Traffic Police also clarified that no shutdown orders were issued and urged citizens to rely on verified information. Rawalpindi's Deputy Commissioner Hassan Waqar Cheema similarly stated that all types of transport are operational in the district.

articles.title: Uae: UAE introduces first-ever weight loss pill Foundayo, here’s how much it may cost and where to get it | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The UAE has approved Foundayo (orforglipron), a once-daily oral obesity pill developed by Eli Lilly, marking the country as one of the first globally to offer a needle-free alternative to injectable weight-loss treatments. The drug, which belongs to a class of medications known as GLP-1 receptor agonists, works by helping patients feel full earlier and reducing hunger signals, leading to weight loss.  However, Foundayo is not intended for casual or cosmetic use and will be available only through prescription under strict medical supervision. Doctors across the UAE are expected to follow clear eligibility guidelines before recommending the drug, which has been shown in clinical trials to help patients lose up to 12.4% of their body weight over a period of time.  The pill is expected to be available in UAE pharmacies starting May 2026 and will likely be priced competitively within the existing range for GLP-1 treatments.

articles.title: Man arrested for defrauding victims of ₹24 lakh in digital arrest scam - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gajarla Avinash, a 26-year-old man from Jagtial district, was arrested by the Cyberabad Police for his involvement in an international "digital arrest" scam that defrauded Indian citizens of ₹24 lakh.  The accused had travelled to Cambodia under false pretenses and used impersonation tactics to threaten victims into transferring money through mule bank accounts. The investigation is ongoing to identify additional victims, trace the funds, and apprehend other members of the cybercrime network.

articles.title: Olly Robbins is just the latest: a guide to the high-profile exits under Starmer’s tenure | Labour | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Olly Robbins, the top civil servant at the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), has left his position.  This follows a string of high-profile resignations since Keir Starmer took office as prime minister.  Angela Rayner, deputy prime minister from July 2024 to September 2025, resigned after breaching the ministerial code over her underpayment of stamp duty on her seaside flat. Josh Simons, a Cabinet Office minister, also resigned in February 2026 following accusations of falsely linking reporters to a “pro-Kremlin” network.  Tulip Siddiq, economic secretary to the Treasury from July 2024 to January 2025, stepped down after an investigation into her ties to her aunt, the ousted prime minister of Bangladesh accused of corruption.

articles.title: Islamabad administration denies claims regarding closure of transport terminals - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Islamabad and Rawalpindi administrations have refuted reports of transport terminal closures, stating that all bus terminals in both cities are open as usual.  Islamabad's Deputy Commissioner Irfaz Nawaz Memon and the Islamabad Traffic Police confirmed inter-city public transport is operating normally with no shutdown orders issued. The Rawalpindi Deputy Commissioner Hassan Waqar Cheema also assured that all private, public, and goods transport are operational in the district.

articles.title: Indian man converted from Hinduism to Christianity denied asylum in Australia; tribunal says no risk of harm on return - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old Indian man who converted to Christianity and sought asylum in Australia was denied refugee status by the Immigration and Protection Tribunal. The tribunal found that his claims of persecution from family members were not credible, citing inconsistencies in his account and a lack of attempts to seek help from authorities.  The tribunal also ruled that there was no evidence he would face escalating harm upon returning to India, nor any indication he could not relocate safely within the country.

articles.title: Sasken Tech to hire 100 people for CoE in Hyderabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sasken Technologies opened a center of excellence (CoE) in Hyderabad, India, to support advanced engineering programs for global customers. The CoE will focus on next-generation engineering across connected devices, 5G-led platforms, IoT solutions, embedded systems, and digital product engineering. Nirmala Datla, Chief Data Science and Engineering Officer at Sasken Technologies, will lead the Hyderabad CoE.  The company plans to hire 100 engineers initially for the facility.

articles.title: Bulgaria elections: Who’s running and what’s at stake? | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bulgaria will hold a snap parliamentary election on April 19th, following political instability and widespread corruption protests. Rumen Radev, former president of the Progressive Bulgaria party, is running for prime minister, along with former Prime Minister Boyko Borissov from the GERB-UDF party.  The election comes amidst deep divisions and a desire for stability after seven national elections in the past four years. The outcome could significantly impact Bulgaria's foreign policy, particularly its relationship with the European Union and Russia. While Radev has pledged to combat corruption and restore order, his pro-Russian stance may complicate relations with Brussels.  The election is expected to draw over 3.3 million voters, who are concerned about economic challenges and political instability.

articles.title: Keir Starmer says it is unforgivable he was not told Mandelson failed vetting | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer expressed his anger and disappointment over the revelation that Peter Mandelson failed security vetting before being appointed ambassador to Washington.  He stated he was not informed of this failure, nor were any ministers, and insists he will provide full transparency in parliament on Monday. Starmer has faced calls for resignation from Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservative party, and Ed Davey, leader of the Liberal Democrats, who have called for an investigation into the situation by the Commons privileges committee.

articles.title: Andhra University journalism department holds Veeksha 2026 photo exhibition for centenary - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra University's Department of Journalism and Mass Communication celebrated its centenary year with the photography exhibition Veeksha 2026. The event, held at T.L.N. Sabha Hall on April 17, 2026, featured a blend of contemporary student work and archival photographs dating back to the 1930s.  Vice-Chancellor G.P. Raja Sekhar inaugurated the exhibition as part of the university's centenary celebrations. C.M. Vinaya Kumar, Head of the Department, highlighted the significance of this year's exhibition in reflecting on the department's history and its engagement with visual storytelling.

articles.title: Nigeria News: Nigeria Faces Brutal Heatwave Amid Rising Fuel Costs Due to Iran War | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Azeez Akanni, a clothier in Lagos, Nigeria, is among millions struggling with the country's intense heatwave exacerbated by rising fuel prices. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) reports that temperatures have been consistently high, reaching record highs of 44C in Sokoto and 38C in Abuja.  This has led to increased use of generators, which contribute to greenhouse gas emissions and worsen air quality. While many traders continue to operate outdoors despite health warnings, the heatwave poses a significant threat to public health, potentially increasing malaria transmission as well as the cost of living. The approaching rainy season offers some relief but also brings its own challenges.

articles.title: Govt. wants to change India’s electoral map, Opposition will defeat the Bill, says Rahul Gandhi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, criticized the Indian government's proposed Constitution Amendment Bill as a "panic reaction" aimed at altering electoral maps and denying representation to southern, northeastern, and smaller states. He called it an "anti-national act" and stated that the Opposition would defeat the attempt to "attack the nation state".  Gandhi urged the government to implement the 2023 Women's Reservation Act instead. The three Bills introduced for amendments in the women's quota law and setting up a delimitation commission were debated in the Lok Sabha.

articles.title: Candace Owens: "What was the threat": Candace Owens accuses Erika Kirk of “fake footage” cover-up after low turnout sparks controversy - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Candace Owens has criticized the Turning Point USA event featuring Vice President JD Vance, alleging that organizers manipulated footage to portray a higher turnout than actually occurred.  Owens claims the event was sparsely attended and cites evidence of edited visuals from Fox News, suggesting the organization used old footage to mask low attendance. She also questioned the timing of Erika Kirk's sudden absence, raising concerns about whether security concerns were genuine or if they were an attempt to control the narrative.

articles.title: Assembly Elections 2026 LIVE: Abhishek Banerjee says BJP supporters abused TMC woman worker - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, a senior TMC leader, alleged that BJP supporters abused a woman party worker in West Bengal.  Mamata Banerjee, the Chief Minister of West Bengal, accused the BJP-led NDA Government of using the proposed amendment to the women’s quota law as a front for the Delimitation Bill. The Income Tax Department conducted searches at the residences and election offices of Debasish Kumar, a senior TMC leader, and associates of former Minister V. Senthilbalaji.  The five states will vote on April 23rd and 29th with results announced on May 4th.

articles.title: Indian-origin Karishma Vijay wins UK reality show The Apprentice, secures Lord Sugar’s £250,000 investment | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Karishma Vijay, an Indian-origin entrepreneur, won the 2026 edition of the UK reality show The Apprentice, securing a £250,000 investment from Lord Alan Sugar. The final saw Vijay and fellow finalist Pascha Myhill compete in developing brand and advertising campaigns for their business ideas.  Vijay plans to use the investment to grow her beauty brand, Kishkin, which she hopes will become a successful company with young girls eager to purchase it.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election: Biryani caterers work around fuel shortages, inflation for Tiruchi’s political meetings - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu’s Legislative Assembly elections have been impacted by the war in West Asia, which has increased the cost of LPG gas and firewood.  This has strained the traditional relationship between politics and biryani, as caterers are facing delayed payments from political parties. Many caterers in Tiruchi are now turning to outsourcing orders to master cooks from nearby towns due to financial difficulties.

articles.title: Dubai News: Watch: Dubai Police seize vehicles, impose Dh50,000 fines for reckless stunts during rain | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dubai Police seized multiple vehicles and imposed strict penalties after drivers engaged in reckless stunts during recent rainfall, turning public roads into dangerous zones.  The incidents occurred in mid-April 2026, prompting Brigadier Jumaa Salem bin Suwaidan, Acting Director of the General Department of Traffic, to issue a warning that such behavior violates traffic laws and poses a direct threat to public safety. Dubai Police emphasized a zero-tolerance approach toward reckless driving, particularly during adverse weather conditions, with penalties including vehicle impoundment, black points, fines, and release fees reaching up to Dh50,000.  The crackdown aims to maintain road discipline across the emirate, urging motorists to slow down, maintain safe distances, and ensure their vehicles are roadworthy.

articles.title: MK Stalin stands exposed after PM Modi’s assurance on delimitation: Edappadi Palaniswami - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Edappadi K. Palaniswami, leader of the opposition AIADMK, dismissed M.K. Stalin's protest against the Delimitation Bill as "unnecessary melodrama."  He argued that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah had clarified their position on delimitation, assuring no injustice would be done to any state.  Palaniswami questioned the need for such protests when clear assurances were given.

articles.title: Noida protests: Workers in India demand hike in minimum wage - but it's not as simple
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of factory workers in Noida, India, have been protesting for higher wages and improved working conditions. The protests, which began a week ago as mostly peaceful demonstrations, have escalated into violent clashes with police using tear gas and making arrests.  Uttar Pradesh's government has announced temporary wage increases but many workers feel these are insufficient. Experts point to inconsistent enforcement of labor laws and the lack of union representation in many sectors as contributing factors to the growing discontent. The protests highlight a broader struggle for fair pay within India's vast informal sector, where wages have not kept pace with rising living costs.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Violent clashes between workers and police over insufficient wage hikes signal potential abuse of power.

articles.title: Uk Man Tattoo Masterpieces: UK man’s Marvel obsession stuns the world with over 60 tattoo comic masterpieces, securing the Guinness World Record title | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Tom Radford, a UK man, has been recognized by Guinness World Records for having the most Marvel-based tattoos with 63 designs. His collection began in 2007 with a Spider-Man tattoo and evolved over time into a cohesive theme.  Radford's interest in tattoos started as random imagery but grew to include characters from across the Marvel universe, all done by tattoo artist Andy Walker over a decade. Radford also pays tribute to Stan Lee through his dog, Stanlee.

articles.title: Bomb threat call to Uppal Metro Station turns out to be hoax - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Uppal police responded to a bomb threat received at the Hyderabad Metro Station on Friday, April 17th, 2026.  Police teams conducted thorough checks with assistance from the bomb disposal squad and dog squad after confirming the call was a hoax. The station later participated in a mock drill as part of an awareness exercise following the incident.

articles.title: Starmer says it is ‘staggering’ and ‘unforgivable’ he was not told Mandelson failed vetting – UK politics live | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Keir Starmer faced calls to resign after revelations that Peter Mandelson failed security vetting but was cleared by the Foreign Office.  Starmer acknowledged he wasn't told of the decision, sparking criticism from various MPs and opposition leaders. The prime minister has said he will address parliament on Monday with all relevant facts. Stephen Flynn, an SNP leader, urged Starmer to resign while others like Diane Abbott and Zack Polanski called for his removal.  The Foreign Office's top civil servant, Olly Robbins, was effectively fired after the decision to clear Mandelson was overruled. The story dominated news coverage across various media outlets.

articles.title: Rupee touches one-week high on report of RBI plan to ease oil refiners' dollar bids - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The rupee strengthened to its strongest level since April 10, reaching 92.7250 per dollar, as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) implemented measures to support the currency against high energy prices and weak capital flows. The central bank urged state-run oil refiners to utilize a special credit line for foreign exchange needs while curbing spot dollar purchases.  These actions have helped boost the rupee by about 2.5% since its record low in late March, according to analysts.

articles.title: Quote Of The Day: Quote of the day by John F. Kennedy: “If we cannot end now our differences, at least we can help make the world safe for diversity. For, in the final analysis, our most basic common link is that we all inhabit this small planet. We all breathe the same air. We all cherish our children's future. And we are all mortal.” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: John F. Kennedy, the 35th President of the United States, delivered a famous quote during his 1963 commencement speech at American University that emphasizes the importance of unity and coexistence despite political differences.  The quote, "If we cannot end now our differences, at least we can help make the world safe for diversity," highlights the need to work together to create a more respectful and peaceful world.  This message remains relevant today as societies become increasingly interconnected, emphasizing the shared humanity that binds people across cultures and ideologies.

articles.title: Parliament special sitting LIVE: Opposition will defeat the Bill, Rahul Gandhi says amid din - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla announced that voting on three bills to amend the women’s quota law and set up a delimitation commission will be held at 4 p.m. on Friday, April 17, 2026. Union Home Minister Amit Shah assured Parliament that southern states' representation in the House would not decrease if the Women's Reservation Act is implemented with increased strength of the House post delimitation. The Women’s Reservation Act 2023, which mandated a 33% quota for women in legislatures, came into effect on April 16, 2026.

articles.title: Myanmar News: Aung San Suu Kyi's Sentence Reduced: Still Imprisoned Amid Ongoing Political Turmoil in Myanmar | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi's sentence has been reduced by one-sixth, cutting her 27-year term to approximately 22 years.  The reduction comes despite her remaining in detention at an undisclosed location. The amnesty, announced by President Min Aung Hlaing, also included the commutation of death sentences and life imprisonment for other prisoners. Suu Kyi was not among those released, and her whereabouts remain unknown. This is the third amnesty in six months since the 2021 coup.

articles.title: Waaree Renewable shares rocket 12% as Q4 revenue soars 131%, profit up 66%. Check details - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Waaree Energies reported strong financial performance in the fiscal year 2026, with a significant increase in revenue and profitability. The company's EBITDA grew by 106.21% to Rs 641.10 crore, while its profit after tax surged 109% to Rs 478.65 crore. Waaree Energies attributed this growth to a strong momentum in India's renewable energy sector, with solar capacity additions increasing significantly to over 44 GW during the year.  The company also highlighted its robust order book and expanding bidding pipeline.

articles.title: Ancient ‘Machine Gun’: Traces of legendary multi-shot weapon found in Pompeii | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Adriana Rossi, a lead researcher, and her team used advanced laser scanning to discover ballistic signatures on the northern fortification walls of Pompeii. The unique patterns suggest the use of a polybolos, an ancient machine gun-like weapon, during the siege of Pompeii in 89 BCE by Lucius Cornelius Sulla. This discovery provides evidence for the revolutionary mechanics of the polybolos, which could continuously fire until its magazine was exhausted and had a flat-link chain mechanism that allowed for rapid reloading.  The findings are published in MDPI.

articles.title: Three charged with arson on Persian language media offices
articles.rephrased_article: Three men, Oisin McGuinness, 21, and Nathan Dunn, 19, both from Watford, and a 16-year-old boy from north London, have been charged with arson with intent to endanger life following an attempted attack on the offices of Volant Media in Park Royal. The incident occurred on Wednesday evening when an ignited container was thrown towards the building but landed in a car park where it extinguished.  The three men are due to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court, while McGuinness faces additional charges of dangerous driving.

articles.title: Radhakishan Damani-backed VST Industries shares jumps 15% as Q4 profit doubles to Rs 116 crore - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: VST Industries reported a significant increase in net profit and revenue for Q4 FY26, with profits jumping 120% year-on-year to Rs 116.7 crore. Revenue from operations rose by 52% to Rs 689 crore compared to the previous year. The company attributed its strong performance to market demand and operational efficiencies, leading to a 61% increase in EBITDA to Rs 450 crore.  This positive financial performance has bolstered investor confidence in VST Industries as a stock to watch.

articles.title: Muslims Dead In Philippine: Philippine Forces Eliminate 10 Muslim Militants in Major Disruption to Insurgency | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Philippine forces killed 10 suspected Muslim militants in a clash with Dawlah Islamiya-Maute, a group linked to the Islamic State, in Lanao del Sur province. The fighting began when police and army troops attempted to arrest the group's leader for murder and other crimes.  The military seized weapons and explosives during the hour-long battle, while no government casualties were reported. Army 1st Infantry Division commander Maj. Gen. Yegor Rey Barroquillo Jr. stated that the operation was a "decisive blow" towards achieving lasting peace in the region.

articles.title: Rapper d4vd arrested on suspicion of murdering 14-year-old girl | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: d4vd, a 21-year-old rapper, was arrested on suspicion of murdering 14-year-old girl Celeste Rivas. Police found Rivas's dismembered body in the trunk of a Tesla registered to d4vd last year. The LA County District Attorney’s office will review the case for formal charges.  The rapper's lawyers claim he is innocent and that evidence will prove it.

articles.title: Silver gains Rs 1,500, gold at Rs 1.53 lakh as investors eye Iran war peace talks. Key levels to watch today - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: MCX silver futures rose 0.5% to Rs 2,50,086 per kg on Thursday, while gold futures were little changed at Rs 1,53,079 per 10 grams. Global gold prices remained steady and were set for a fourth consecutive weekly gain, with spot gold unchanged at $4,789.67 per ounce.  Manoj Kumar Jain, of Prithvi Finmart, predicts both metals will remain volatile in the near term due to fluctuations in the dollar index, crude oil prices, and potential US-Iran peace talks. He recommends a buy-on-dips strategy for gold and silver.

articles.title: Woman stranded in Dusseldorf after return UK flight blocked over Home Office admin error | Home Office | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Liza Tobay, a German woman living in the UK for 15 years, was separated from her two-year-old daughter at Edinburgh Airport after a Home Office error flagged her immigration status.  The mistake led to Tobay being denied boarding on a connecting flight from Munich to Edinburgh and left her stranded in Dusseldorf. The grassroots campaign group the3million criticized the Home Office's reliance on a digital immigration verification system, arguing that it is prone to errors and delays in resolving issues.

articles.title: BJP using women as shield for electoral ambitions: DMK’s Kanimozhi in Lok Sabha - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kanimozhi, leader of the DMK, criticized the government's move to amend the 2023 women's reservation law before implementing the principal Act, calling it an "election rescue strategy" and a trap designed to link the two. She argued that the proposed delimitation exercise is being used by the BJP as a means to suppress women's representation in Parliament. Kanimozhi also challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing him of attempting to silence opposition with his "kaala teeka" remark and comparing it to the dark goddess Kali.  Her party, along with other Tamil Nadu leaders, protested against the bill by wearing black clothes and burning copies of the delimitation bill.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article alleges manipulation of a women's rights law for electoral gain.

articles.title: Watch: How is the US Navy enforcing blockade amid Hormuz deadlock - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US Central Command (CENTCOM) released video footage showing the US Navy escorting a merchant vessel in the Gulf of Oman.  The USS Michael Murphy (DDG 112) communicated with the vessel, informing its crew that it would be escorted to its next port of call. The US Navy maintains its maritime enforcement activity in regional waters and states it is prepared to sustain the operation as long as necessary.

articles.title: Gold ETFs deliver up to 61% returns since last Akshaya Tritiya. Should you hold or book profits after the rally? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have delivered impressive returns since the last Akshaya Tritiya, with an average return of 59.63%.  Analysts attribute this rally to geopolitical tensions, central bank buying, inflation fears, and a softer US dollar. While some experts caution against overexposure to gold due to its volatility, others believe it remains a strategic diversifier for long-term investors. Despite recent gains, the sustainability of this rally is debated, with some suggesting that a correction may be imminent.  Experts recommend a disciplined approach, such as staggered entry and maintaining an asset allocation framework, rather than chasing short-term price movements.

articles.title: Harivansh elected Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha unopposed - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Harivansh, a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha, was elected unopposed as Deputy Chairman on Friday, April 17, 2026.  President Droupadi Murmu had nominated him to fill the vacancy created by the retirement of former Chief Justice of India Ranjan Gogoi. The election followed a special sitting of Parliament and consultations with opposition leaders. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge congratulated Harivansh, highlighting his experience and contributions to the Rajya Sabha.

articles.title: Fans react as Sykkuno admits infidelity and takes streaming break - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sykkuno, a popular streamer, has admitted to infidelity in a public statement following allegations that surfaced earlier this year. His girlfriend remains with him despite the accusations and many fans have reacted with shock and mixed opinions on social media. Sykkuno apologized for his actions, stating he will be taking a break from streaming and the internet to focus on personal growth and rebuilding his relationship.

articles.title: High conviction picks! Bharti Airtel, Kotak Bank, 3 other stocks with up to 70% upside potential - Bullish Bets | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nifty is trading at a 12% discount to its 15-year average PE, with valuations approaching levels seen during significant events like GST implementation and demonetisation. Bharti Airtel, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Fortis Healthcare, CESC, and Apeejay Surender Park Hotels have received target price upgrades from various brokerage firms, highlighting potential for growth in the Indian market.

articles.title: 'Building castles in the air': Iran mocks Trump’s 'will get free oil, free Hormuz' claim amid deadlock - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran state media mocked Donald Trump's claims of a successful negotiation, dismissing them as unrealistic.  The media shared a poetic message referencing "building castles in the air," highlighting their skepticism about Trump's assertions regarding a deal with Iran. Despite ongoing ceasefire and peace talks held in Pakistan failing, Trump claimed that Iran is ready to hand over its enriched uranium stockpile.

articles.title: France arrests suspect over 1982 attack on Jewish restaurant | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mahmoud Khader Abed Adra, also known as Hicham Harb, a man suspected of organizing the 1982 deadly attack on a Jewish restaurant in Paris, was arrested and placed in custody in France after being surrendered by Palestinian authorities.  The handover followed France's recognition of Palestinian statehood and is linked to the extradition request filed by French antiterrorism prosecutors last year. The attack resulted in six deaths and 22 injuries, and two other suspects are already in French custody.

articles.title: ‘Parent’s worst nightmare’: Sydney childcare worker faces 137 child abuse charges relating to multiple centres | Australia news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A former childcare employee in his 30s, who was initially charged with eight counts of online child abuse material offences, has been hit with an additional 129 charges after investigators uncovered more victims.  The Australian federal police (AFP) examined over 2.4 million electronic files on the man's devices to establish the scope of his alleged offending across multiple childcare centers. The Sydney man appeared in Parramatta local court, facing a total of 137 charges, including production of child abuse material and filming a person engaged in a private act without consent.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Child abuse is a serious crime and the scale of alleged offenses is alarming.

articles.title: 12 lakh people in Telangana opt for ‘No Caste’ in SEEEPC Survey-2024 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nearly 12 lakh people in Telangana opted for the "No Caste" option in the Telangana Socio Economic, Educational, Employment, Political and Caste Survey (SEEEPC) 2024, representing 3.4% of the state's population. The Independent Expert Working Group (IEWG) report found that despite identifying as caste-neutral, a significant portion of this group still holds caste certificates, suggesting potential institutional or societal pressures to disclose caste information.  The report also noted that individuals in this category hold higher percentages of government jobs and private professional jobs compared to the state average.

articles.title: HDFC Life Insurance shares tank 4% on Q4 results. What are Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited reported a 4% year-on-year rise in profit after tax to Rs 496 crore for the March quarter. Net premium income grew 9% YoY, indicating steady momentum despite a challenging environment. The company will issue equity shares to HDFC Bank, aiming to improve solvency and support growth plans.  Morgan Stanley maintains an Overweight rating on HDFC Life with a target price of Rs 745, while Goldman Sachs also retains its Buy rating with a target price of Rs 735. Nomura maintained a Neutral stance with a lowered target price to Rs 725.

articles.title: UK: Church in Wales approves bill for same-sex marriage blessings with majority backing | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Church in Wales approved a bill making same-sex marriage blessings permanent, with a two-thirds majority vote from its governing body. The decision was made after years of discussion and feedback, with supporters emphasizing inclusivity and the need to address past harm inflicted on LGBT individuals. However, some members expressed concerns about potential divisions within the Church and questioned the move's alignment with traditional teachings.  The change follows the appointment of Cherry Vann as Archbishop of Wales in July 2025, who has advocated for greater diversity within the Church.

articles.title: Revanth’s hybrid model for delimitation enters national discourse - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A hybrid model for delimitation, proposed by Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, has sparked a political debate in Parliament between the BJP and the Congress.  The model seeks to balance population-based representation with economic performance indicators like Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP). Tejasvi Surya, a BJP MP, criticized the model as "foolish" and argued that GSDP is too volatile for delimitation. However, Congress leaders defended the model, claiming it aims to ensure fairness for states with controlled population growth while contributing significantly to the national economy.

articles.title: Wipro shares crack 4% after Q4, Rs 15,000-crore buyback. What Goldman Sachs, other brokerages are saying? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Wipro's Q4 FY26 revenue increased 8% year-on-year to Rs 24,236 crore.  However, the core IT services segment saw limited growth with revenue rising just 0.6% quarter-on-quarter and 2.1% year-on-year. Morgan Stanley downgraded its rating on the company, citing weak performance and a continued decline in revenue. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs maintained a Sell rating, pointing to further revenue contraction and valuation discount compared to peers.  Despite these challenges, Nomura retained a Buy rating, highlighting strong deal wins and potential for growth driven by AI-led transformation.

articles.title: UK: Church in Wales approves bill for same-sex marriage blessings with majority backing | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The Church in Wales approved a bill on Wednesday (15 April) to permanently bless same-sex marriages, marking a significant step towards greater inclusivity. The decision was supported by lay members (48 to eight), clergy (32 to seven), and bishops who voted unanimously. While some expressed concerns about potential divisions, the move reflects the Church's commitment to reflecting modern society and follows Archbishop Cherry Vann's appointment in July 2025.

articles.title: Chelsea vs Manchester United: Premier League – teams, lineups, start | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Chelsea host Manchester United in a crucial Premier League match this Saturday.  Chelsea are looking to close the gap on Manchester United, who are currently third, and could secure a Champions League spot with a win. The Blues have struggled recently, but manager Liam Rosenior is confident his team can turn their form around. Manchester United face a tough task without key players like Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire.  The match will be a tight one, with both teams vying for the top five spots.

articles.title: Inside Andhra’s millet push that is turning women into entrepreneurs - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: In Andhra Pradesh, the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty (SERP), in partnership with the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) and Vishalakshi Innovations for Sustainable Value Chain (VISV), is training women to run millet-based enterprises.  The three-day training program at SVR Industries in Pendurthi focuses on recipes, business planning, and market access, aiming to help women transition from cooking for their families to creating marketable products. The initiative includes hands-on sessions on preparing a range of millet dishes, as well as providing support for setting up mobile "plug and play" millet carts.  The program aims to empower women entrepreneurs by building sustainable livelihoods through the cultivation, processing, and sale of millets.

articles.title: D4vd arrested on suspicion of killing teen girl whose body was found in his Tesla | US crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd, a 21-year-old R&B singer, has been arrested in connection with the death of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez whose body was found in his Tesla.  The Los Angeles Police Department discovered the dismembered body at a tow yard in Hollywood after receiving reports of a foul odor emanating from the vehicle. The Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office will review the case and determine if charges are filed.

articles.title: Russia hits Ukraine with missiles & drones, 17 dead - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Russia launched a massive attack on Ukraine, targeting Kyiv and other major cities with over 40 ballistic and cruise missiles and more than 650 drones. The attacks resulted in at least 17 deaths and numerous injuries, with Ukraine's air defense reporting heavy damage to residential areas in Dnipro, Odesa, Kharkiv, and Zaporizhzhia.  President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the casualties during a visit to the Netherlands and discussed potential anti-ballistic air defense systems with Ukrainian officials.

articles.title: Logistics firms enter last mile for IPO delivery, rev up for Rs 9,000 crore issues - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Several logistics companies, including Skyways Air Services, CJ Darcl Logistics, Leap India, Caliber Mining & Logistics, Shiprocket, Horizon Industrial Parks and Yatayat Corporation India Ltd, have filed draft red herring prospectuses (DRHPs) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi). These companies are expected to raise approximately ₹8,000-9,000 crore over the next few quarters, driven by increasing demand from e-commerce, manufacturing, and infrastructure sectors.  This surge in IPO activity reflects confidence in the logistics sector's growth potential, with companies seeking capital for expansion and improved balance sheets.

articles.title: Annatto seed growers pitch for government support - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Pallala Suryanarayana Reddi, a 38-year-old tribal farmer, recounts his childhood memories of playing with annatto seeds.  He now cultivates the seeds for a living in Papikonda National Park, where he harvests them from shrubs along the Pamuleru stream.  Reddi explains that the natural red color from grinding and splashing the seeds was once a source of fun for him and his friends.

articles.title: War brings US close to net crude exporter for first time since WWII - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: US crude oil exports surged to a seven-month high of 5.2 million barrels per day last week, nearing a record high and contributing to the country's first net export status since World War II. This surge was driven by increased demand from Asian and European buyers seeking alternative supplies after disruptions caused by the Iran war. While this trend is positive for the US economy, analysts warn that the country is approaching its export capacity.

articles.title: Global Markets: Asian stocks dip as traders await ceasefire news - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The MSCI Asia Pacific Index closed lower on Friday, ending a three-day rally.  President Donald Trump expressed optimism about securing a permanent ceasefire with Iran, which led to a decline in crude oil prices and a slight increase in gold prices. Investors are awaiting progress in talks that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ease pressure on economies after oil prices surged following the conflict's onset. While markets have reached record highs, economists warn that they may be underestimating the war's economic toll.

articles.title: Vem Narender Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vem Narender Reddy and Abhishek Manu Singhvi, both from Telangana, were sworn in as Rajya Sabha MPs on Thursday.  After the oath-taking ceremony, Reddy met with Sonia Gandhi to express his gratitude for her selection.

articles.title: Singer D4vd arrested in connection to murder of missing teen
articles.rephrased_article: D4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, has been arrested in connection with the death of missing teen girl Celeste Rivas Hernandez. The Los Angeles Police Department announced his arrest on Thursday and he is being held without bail.  The case will be presented to the District Attorney's office on Monday. Authorities found the 14-year-old's remains in a Tesla car registered to Burke's address in Texas in September, but no cause of death has been released. The case had been under investigation by a grand jury since December and was fueled by online speculation about D4vd's connection to the teen.

articles.title: Delimitation will turn Tamils into second-class citizens, says CM Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: DMK president and Chief Minister M.K. Stalin criticized the BJP-led NDA government's Delimitation Bill, stating it would diminish Tamil Nadu's status within the country.  He warned that if MPs lack a voice, citizens will lose their own.  Stalin urged the public to raise their voices against the bill and hold the BJP accountable for its actions.

articles.title: Schools in Ernakulam shine in CBSE Class X exams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Schools under the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) in Ernakulam district achieved high pass rates in Class 10 examinations.  Bhavan’s Vidya Mandir, Elamakkara led with 205 distinctions, followed by Bhavan’s Adarsha Vidyalaya, Kakkanad and other schools like Vidyodaya School, Thevakkal and Toc H Public School, Vyttila.  The results demonstrate strong performance across the district.

articles.title: In manifestos, political parties in Tamil Nadu firm on moving education back to State list, retaining two-language formula - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Several political parties in the state, including DMK, AIADMK, NTK, and VCK, have reiterated their demand to bring education back into the State list. They also emphasized the continuation of the two-language formula currently practiced in the state. This demand echoes from previous elections as well.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Cleanliness, safety, housing top agenda of many women candidates in Chennai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: AIADMK, PMK, and BJP have fielded women candidates in the Chennai municipal elections.  The AIADMK has nominated former ministers B. Valarmathi, S. Gokula Indira, and Porkodi Armstrong, while PMK has selected M. Thilagabama and BJP has chosen Tamilisai Soundararajan to represent their constituencies.

articles.title: T.N. Assembly election 2026: Cases filed against DMK, AIADMK candidates for alleged distribution of ₹8,000 coupons and ₹10,000 tokens - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court agreed to hear two writ petitions on Friday, April 17th. One petition accuses numerous DMK candidates of distributing ₹8,000 coupons during the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, while another targets AIADMK candidate Royapuram Mano alias R. Manohar for distributing ₹10,000 tokens in Chennai. The court will hear both cases if they are numbered by the end of the day.

articles.title: Delimitation exercise: Tourism Minister, TNCC president protest in Tamil Nadu's Salem - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R. Rajendran, Minister for Tourism, and K. Selvaperunthagai, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president, participated in a protest against the Delimitation Bill by hoisting a black flag in Salem on Thursday. The duo led a group of DMK supporters who raised slogans against the Union government and demanded the bill's withdrawal.  They then proceeded to burn a copy of the bill at the Salem District DMK office.

articles.title: Citizens demand all-day park access amid rising heat in city - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Citizens in South Bengaluru have urged MLA C.K. Ramamurthy to keep public parks open during the day, citing climate and health concerns.  The HeatWatch Foundation, an NGO working on extreme heat adaptation, joined residents in petitioning Ramamurthy after several parks were closed between 11 a.m. and 4 p.m., despite a 2024 order mandating park access from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.

articles.title: High Court dismisses Karti Chidambaram’s writ for speedy disposal of plea to de-freeze salary account - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court dismissed a writ petition filed by Congress MP Karti P. Chidambaram, preventing the court from directing the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) to expedite his plea for salary account de-freezing. Justices S.M. Subramaniam and K. Surender stated that such a direction would pressure the tribunal to prioritize cases over a systematic judicial process.

articles.title: Cashew farmers in Pudukottai struggle amid falling prices and low yields - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cashew farming in Pudukottai district, Tamil Nadu, is experiencing a downturn due to shrinking profit margins and declining production. The area affected by the 2018 Cyclone Gaja has resulted in significant losses for farmers who are still struggling to recover.  The region accounts for nearly 5,000 acres of cashew cultivation, with trees taking several years to yield fruit and remaining productive for decades.

articles.title: Creeping risk: The Hindu Editorial on industrial accidents and neglect of risks - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Boiler explosions, like the recent incident in Sakti, Chhattisgarh, are often caused by a gradual build-up of issues such as overpressure and scaling.  These incidents share similarities with other industrial disasters in India, including the Visakhapatnam gas leak and the Neyveli blast, highlighting systemic failures in boiler safety regulations. The current regulatory framework, which focuses on fabrication standards rather than continuous monitoring, has been criticized for failing to adequately address transient thermal and pressure imbalances that can lead to explosions.  The lack of surprise government inspections and a focus on "ease of doing business" have contributed to these issues, as evidenced by the exploitation of contract labor and inadequate safety measures in some facilities.

articles.title: LPG autorickshaws wait in queues as several bunks go dry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Retail outlets in and around Chennai city are experiencing long queues for auto liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) as demand surges.  State-run oil marketing companies (OMCs) are seeing increased sales, with some bunks going dry due to high volume. Balasubramanian of the CITU Auto Thozhilalargar Sammelanam stated that this shortage is impacting 40,000 families who rely on LPG for their livelihood and face significant delays in obtaining fuel.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Spat between Centre and State takes a toll on quality of higher education - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu government's efforts to improve higher education quality have been hampered by a long-standing ideological battle between the DMK and the BJP at the Centre.  This has resulted in numerous challenges, including the prolonged vacancy of vice-chancellors at public universities due to disagreements between the Governor and the state government. The state Assembly passed a bill to abolish the NEET exam twice, only to have it rejected by the President.  The DMK government's attempt to dispense with the requirement for candidates to qualify in NEET was met with opposition from the BJP.

articles.title: Department of Justice investigating Eric Swalwell amid sexual assault allegations | House of Representatives | The Guardian
